translation: 当人们介入纠正机器人时，他们不仅通过如何纠正其行为，还通过何时选择介入来提供信息。现有的从修正中学习的方法主要集中在比较新轨迹与机器人最初预期的行为，从而低估了干预前机器人行为的上下文信息。在这项工作中，我们研究了如何将干预前和干预后的行为转化为偏好对，用于学习近似人类潜在奖励的价值函数。我们通过将修正后的行为与被取代的行为进行比较来构建干预后偏好，并通过导致干预的状态之间的的时间关系来构建干预前偏好。我们通过两项下游任务评估了学习到的价值表示：目标 inference（推理）和修正 forecasting（预测）。我们的结果表明，干预后偏好对目标推理特别有效，而干预前偏好则提供了强大的修正预测性能。结合这两种信息源在两项任务中都表现出强劲的性能，即使在推广到训练中未见过的参与者时也是如此。这些发现表明，人类纠正的“何时”和“如何”都为从纠正交互中学习价值表示提供了互补的信息。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种利用人类干预的时机与修正方式（通过时间偏好）来学习机器人价值函数的新方法，显著提升了机器人的目标推理和修正预测能力。
ai_comments: 该论文巧妙地利用了人类干预机器人的“时间维度（when）”和“方式维度（how）”来构建偏好对，这为从人类修正中学习（LfC）开辟了新的视角。通过结合干预前后的行为，提升了目标推理和修正预测的泛化能力。
motivation: 现有的从修正中学习的方法主要集中于将新轨迹与机器人原本的意图进行比较，从而低估了干预前机器人行为的上下文信息，而人类不仅通过如何纠正，还通过何时干预来提供重要信息。
method: 提出利用前置和后置干预行为转化为偏好对来学习逼近人类潜在奖励的价值函数。通过比较修正后的行为与被取代的行为构建后置干预偏好，通过导致干预的状态间的时间关系构建前置干预偏好。
results: 实验表明，后置干预偏好对目标推理特别有效，而前置干预偏好则提供了很强的修正预测性能；结合两种信息在两项任务上都表现出色，且对未见过的参与者具有良好的泛化能力。
conclusion: 本研究证明了人类修正中的时间选择和修正方式结合能够提供互补的信息，从而有效地学习价值函数，并在目标推理和修正预测任务中表现出优异的性能和泛化能力。

title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study
authors: Sayed Amir Karim
abstract: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. We study two things. First, a small learned projection W: R^1024 -> R^d (d in {11, 32}), trained by a deterministic recipe on a declared set of cases, that suppresses the trap: for the declared cases, HN@10 = 0.0000 (no trap in the top-10) in all twelve (domain, pool-size) settings across four independent domains (legal, medical, patent, financial) and pools up to 100,000, while the correct paraphrase is retained for 93-99% of cases, under exact nearest-neighbour search. Second, a boundary-conditioned accelerator that serves the projection at that scale: an acceleration of spectral graph retrieval (SpectRAG) that replaces a dense eigendecomposition with a boundary-value solve, holding HN@10 = 0.0000 at n = 100,000 in every domain and retrieving the ~300-query suite in 0.6-1.1 s (~2-4 ms per query on average). Because the lens's output is the stored representation (a few floats per document), a hardened, specialised index per domain or tenant is ~90x smaller and dimension-proportionally faster than the full embedding, making many small declared indexes a practical alternative to one large vector store. The claim is scoped to the declared cases on the measured pools, with no probabilistic bound; the correct-answer rate drops for a reworded query against an unchanged corpus (about 0.79, trap suppression still holding). A projection transfers only partly to other domains, which we report in full. The recipe, lenses, trap sets and evaluation harness are released under AGPL-3.0; the accelerator's implementation is a reserved commercial component, and every HN number is reproducible under exact search.
comment: Comments 27 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Code, lenses, trap sets and data: https://github.com/pelloran-inc/pelloran-safety-lens (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24345474)
zh_title: 基于谱加速的语义反转感知检索的小型学习投影：一项四领域实证研究
translation: 稠密嵌入检索器可能会发生对抗性失效：当一个查询由文档A回答，却被与A仅有微小意义改变的近副本B（“陷阱”）反转时，在5000的候选池中，E5-Large-v2的原始余弦相似度使B在82-100%的查询中排在Top-10。我们研究了两件事。首先，一个小型学习投影 W: R^1024 -> R^d（d在{11, 32}中），通过在声明的案例集上的确定性配方训练以抑制陷阱：对于声明的案例，在跨越四个独立领域（法律、医疗、专利、金融）的全部十二种（领域、池大小）设置以及高达100,000的池中，HN@10 = 0.0000（Top-10中无陷阱），同时在精确最近邻搜索下，93-99%的正确复述得以保留。其次，一个边界条件加速器，用于在该规模下提供投影服务：谱图检索（SpectRAG）的一种加速，用边界值求解代替了稠密特征分解，在n = 100,000的每个领域中保持HN@10 = 0.0000，并在0.6-1.1秒内检索约300个查询的套件（平均每个查询约2-4毫秒）。由于透镜的输出是存储的表示（每个文档几个浮点数），每个领域或租户加固的专用索引比完整嵌入小约90倍，并且维度成比例地更快，使得许多小型声明索引成为单个大型向量存储的实用替代方案。该声明的范围限于测量的池上的声明案例，没有概率界限；对于未改变的语料库，重新表述的查询的正确答案率下降（约为0.79，陷阱抑制仍然保持）。投影仅部分转移到其他领域，我们对此进行了全面报告。配方、透镜、陷阱集和评估工具包在AGPL-3.0下发布；加速器的实现是一个保留的商业组件，每个HN数字都可在精确搜索下重现。
tldr: 本文提出了一种小型学习投影与谱加速方法，有效解决了稠密检索中的语义反转“陷阱”问题，大幅提升了高精度领域检索的鲁棒性与效率。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一种小型学习投影方法，有效解决了稠密检索中由于微小语义变化导致的对抗性失效问题（即“陷阱”文档问题），并通过边界条件加速器实现了高效的大规模检索。这对于提高法律、医疗、专利和金融等高精度领域的检索鲁棒性具有重要意义。
motivation: 稠密嵌入检索器容易受到对抗性攻击的影响（即查询被文档A回答，却被与其仅有微小意义改变的近副本B捕获），导致检索结果出现严重偏差。
method: 提出了一种小型学习投影（W: R^1024 -> R^d, d在11和32之间），通过确定性配方在声明的案例集上进行训练；同时开发了一种基于边界值求解的谱图检索加速器（SpectRAG）。
results: 在四个独立领域（法律、医疗、专利、金融）和最高达100,000的池规模下，所提方法实现了HN@10 = 0.0000（前10个结果中无陷阱），正确复述的保留率为93-99%，并且加速器将检索时间缩短至每查询约2-4毫秒，索引体积减小了约90倍。
conclusion: 小型学习投影结合谱加速器能够有效抑制检索中的语义反转“陷阱”，在保持极高准确率的同时显著减小索引体积并提升检索速度。

title: CrossCheck II: A Compiler Plugin for Certified Cost Bounds of Real-Time C and C++ Code, and its Evaluation
authors: Luca Dall'Olio
abstract: We describe a plugin for the Clang compiler that bounds the cost of C and C++ functions intended for real-time use, and rejects at compile time the functions that allocate, throw, call through pointers, or contain a loop or a recursion for which no bound is found. Loops are bounded by affine ranking potentials synthesized with an SMT solver through Farkas' Lemma, or by logarithmic ones, recursion by depth and size potentials, and callees are analyzed in the calling context in which they are used. For functions in a linear fragment, the plugin emits a cost certificate that a checker, compiled from a Lean~4 definition proved sound in a companion paper, validates with integer arithmetic only; the bound then depends neither on the analyzer nor on the solver. On the 29 kernels of the TACLeBench collection, without annotations, the plugin bounds 142 of 220 loops in the calling contexts of the programs, 131 of them exactly as the benchmarks' flow facts, and 161 of the 165 bounded functions receive a certificate that the checker accepts, 152 of them also validated against an independent description of the source. On the CMSIS-DSP library for Cortex-M (786 functions), with assumed input ranges, it bounds 616 functions. We compare the loop bounds with loop counts observed by running the kernels and with five existing analyzers (LLVM's ScalarEvolution, KoAT2, CoFloCo, Infer and oRange), and the plugin with KoAT2 and CoFloCo on the C programs of the Termination and Complexity Competition: without annotations, 147 of 553 programs receive a certified bound that holds for all inputs, where the two tools bound 288 and 264. Loop bounds, exported annotations and the checker program are also tested on random programs and on mutated certificates.
comment: 23 pages. Companion of "CrossCheck I" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24444576), which holds the theory and the Lean proofs. Code, benchmarks and Lean formalization: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24425070
zh_title: CrossCheck II：一个用于实时C和C++代码认证成本界限的编译器插件及其评估
translation: 我们描述了一个用于Clang编译器的插件，该插件用于界定实时使用的C和C++函数的成本，并在编译时拒绝那些分配内存、抛出异常、通过指针调用、或者包含无法找到界限的循环或递归的函数。循环通过基于Farkas引理的SMT求解器合成的仿射排序势（affine ranking potentials）或对数势来定界，递归通过深度和大小势来定界，被调用函数在其使用的调用上下文中进行分析。对于线性片段中的函数，该插件发出一个成本证书，该证书由从Lean 4定义编译而来的检查器进行验证（该定义在随附论文中已被证明是可靠的），且仅使用整数算术；因此该界限既不依赖于分析器也不依赖于求解器。在TACLeBench集合的29个内核上（无需注释），该插件在程序的调用上下文中界定了220个循环中的142个，其中131个与基准测试的流事实完全一致，165个有界函数中有161个收到了检查器接受的证书，其中152个还对照了源码的独立描述进行了验证。在Cortex-M的CMSIS-DSP库（786个函数）上，假设了输入范围的情况下，它界定了616个函数。我们将循环界限与运行内核观察到的循环计数以及五个现有的分析器（LLVM的ScalarEvolution、KoAT2、CoFloCo、Infer和oRange）进行了比较，并在终止与复杂度竞赛（Termination and Complexity Competition）的C程序上将该插件与KoAT2和CoFloCo进行了比较：在没有注释的情况下，147个（共553个）程序收到了适用于所有输入的认证界限，而另外两个工具分别界定了288和264个。循环界限、导出的注释和检查器程序也在随机程序和变异证书上进行了测试。
tldr: 本文介绍了CrossCheck II，一个基于Clang编译器的插件，能够自动为C和C++代码计算实时成本界限，并通过Lean 4生成的形式化检查器验证成本证书，确保结果不依赖于分析器或求解器本身。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了CrossCheck II，这是一个用于C和C++代码的Clang编译器插件，创新性地结合了静态分析、SMT求解以及Lean 4定理证明器生成的Certified Cost Bounds（带证书的成本界限），保证了结果的可靠性。实验证明了其在实际基准测试和大型库（如CMSIS-DSP）上的有效性。
motivation: 为了确保实时C和C++代码的成本（如执行时间或资源消耗）在安全范围内，同时克服传统成本分析器缺乏形式化安全保证、依赖复杂分析工具和求解器可信度的问题。
method: 基于Clang编译器的插件，利用SMT求解器通过Farkas引理合成仿射排序势（affine ranking potentials）或对数势来界定循环，利用深度和大小势来界定递归，并在Lean 4中生成经过可靠性证明的独立检查器来验证成本证书。
results: 在TACLeBench的29个内核上无需注解成功界定了165个函数中的161个证书，其中152个通过了独立描述验证；在CMSIS-DSP库中界定了616个函数；在Termination和Complexity Competition的C程序中为147个程序生成了全局有效的证书。
conclusion: CrossCheck II成功地将自动化成本分析与形式化验证相结合，通过Lean 4生成的验证器为线性片段的代码提供了独立于分析器和求解器的安全证书，在实际嵌入式和实时代码中表现出色。

title: Directed brain-body graphs across timescales
authors: Luís A. Alexandre, Karolina Finc
abstract: Simultaneous brain and body recordings combine signals sampled at very different rates with processes that act on timescales from milliseconds to minutes. Placing all signals on one time grid can distort the directed relationships estimated from them. Unmeasured common influences can also make one signal appear to drive another. We introduce rate-matched Granger causality (RMGC), which estimates directed predictive relationships without a common sampling grid. Each relationship receives a robustness value, the strength of the weakest common influence found within a specified class that can reproduce it. A neural extension tests for nonlinear relationships. In a controlled benchmark, RMGC recovered more true relationships than four established methods and an autoregressive model on a common grid (92\% at a false-positive rate of 5\%). Given the same signal features, the common-grid model matched this recovery but had more than twice the false-positive rate, and it reversed the relationship from respiration to heart rate. The robustness value never overstated the strength of the driver behind a spurious relationship, even for drivers outside the searched class. It separated true from spurious relationships better than predictive strength did. In overnight sleep recordings and two awake datasets, many brain--heart relationships could be reproduced by common drivers no stronger than measured respiration. Robustness values only partly identified those that appeared when respiration was omitted, particularly during wakefulness. Surrogate analyses showed elevated background rates in one awake dataset. The approach applies to other signals recorded at different rates or as events, provided that influences act with a delay.
zh_title: 跨时间尺度的有向身心图谱
translation: 同步的大脑和身体记录结合了以非常不同的速率采样信号以及作用于从毫秒到分钟时间尺度的过程。将所有信号放在一个时间格网上会扭曲从中估计的有向关系。未测量的共同影响也会使一个信号看起来像是在驱动另一个信号。我们引入了率匹配格兰杰因果关系（RMGC），它在没有共同采样网格的情况下估计有向预测关系。每个关系都会收到一个鲁棒性值，即指定类别内可以重现它的最弱共同影响的强度。神经扩展测试非线性关系。在受控基准测试中，RMGC比四个成熟的方法和一个通用网格上的自回归模型恢复了更多的真实关系（在5%的假阳性率下为92%）。给定相同的信号特征，通用网格模型与这种恢复相匹配，但假阳性率是其两倍以上，并且它逆转了从呼吸到心率的关系。鲁棒性值从未夸大虚假关系背后的驱动因素强度，即使对于搜索类别之外的驱动因素也是如此。它比预测强度更好地分离了真实关系和虚假关系。在夜间睡眠记录和两个清醒数据集中，许多脑-心关系可以通过不强于测量呼吸的共同驱动因素来重现。鲁棒性值只是部分识别了省略呼吸时出现的关系，特别是在清醒状态下。替代分析显示了一个清醒数据集中的背景率升高。该方法适用于以不同速率记录或作为事件记录的其他信号，前提是影响具有一定的延迟。
tldr: 本文提出了一种率匹配格兰杰因果关系（RMGC）方法，无需统一采样网格即可准确估计不同采样率的大脑与身体信号之间的定向因果关系，并有效抑制虚假关联。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一种率匹配格兰杰因果关系（RMGC）方法，能够有效解决多模态脑机接口和身心生理信号记录中采样率不一致及未观测到共同影响所导致的虚假因果关系问题，通过引入鲁棒性值提升了因果推断的可靠性，具有重要的理论和应用价值。
motivation: 同时记录的大脑和身体信号具有不同的采样率和时间尺度，将其强行放到统一时间格网上会导致定向关系估计扭曲，且未测量的共同影响也会造成虚假因果关系，因此需要一种不依赖共同采样网格且能处理共同影响的方法。
method: 引入了率匹配格兰杰因果关系（RMGC），在没有共同采样网格的情况下估计定向预测关系，并利用鲁棒性值量化共同影响的强度，同时开发了用于测试非线性关系的神经扩展。
results: 在受控基准测试中，RMGC比四个传统方法和一个通用网格自回归模型恢复了更多的真实关系，且假阳性率更低（在5%的假阳性率下达到92%的恢复率）；在实际睡眠和清醒数据集应用中，成功识别并区分了真实与由呼吸等共同驱动引起的虚假脑-心关系。
conclusion: 该研究所提出的RMGC方法及其鲁棒性度量，为分析跨时间尺度的异构身心信号提供了一个准确且抗干扰的强大工具。

title: Taxi: Analyzing Agents at (Real) Scale
authors: Guy Dar
abstract: In this technical report, we present Taxi -- a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale. Taxi scales to millions of steps efficiently. This is made possible by a combination of scalable analysis methods. Taxi relies primarily on clustering to generate a taxonomy over steps for a structured overview of the data, and provides full SQL access for engineers and automated agents to ask complex questions. Clustering and querying are best used together in a hybrid pipeline guided by a coding agent. Taxi also includes an experimental integration of Jev-style decision models: models that map state and bounded questions directly to typed, probabilistic decisions. They add low-cost semantic routing and evaluation where embeddings or literal queries alone are insufficient. In addition, Taxi provides an extensible ecosystem, including built-in evaluators and daily reports. To accommodate growth, Taxi is designed to be modular, hackable, and easy to plug-and-play for individuals and teams.
zh_title: 出租车：大规模分析代理
translation: 在本技术报告中，我们提出了Taxi——一个用于大规模调试、聚类和监控代理的系统。Taxi能够高效地扩展到数百万个步骤。这得益于一系列可扩展的分析方法的结合。Taxi主要依靠聚类来生成步骤的分类，从而对数据进行结构化概览，并提供完整的SQL访问权限，供工程师和自动化代理提出复杂问题。聚类和查询最好在由编码代理指导的混合管道中结合使用。Taxi还包括对Jev风格决策模型的实验性集成：这些模型将状态和有界问题直接映射到类型化、概率化的决策。它们在仅靠嵌入或字面查询不足的情况下，提供了低成本的语义路由和评估。此外，Taxi还提供了一个可扩展的生态系统，包括内置的评估器和每日报告。为了适应增长，Taxi被设计成模块化、易于修改，并且易于个人和团队进行即插即用。
tldr: Taxi是一个用于大规模调试、聚类和监控代理的系统，通过可扩展的分析方法实现，结合聚类和SQL查询，并集成了Jev风格的决策模型，提供可扩展的生态系统。
ai_comments: 该论文介绍了一个名为Taxi的创新系统，它有效地解决了大规模代理分析的挑战。该系统结合了聚类、SQL查询和Jev风格决策模型等多种技术，提供了一个全面而可扩展的解决方案。其模块化设计和易于集成性是该系统的关键优势，使其能够适应各种应用场景。然而，报告中未详细说明Jev风格决策模型的具体实现细节及其在不同复杂场景下的性能表现。
motivation: 在真实尺度上分析代理的需求，以进行调试、聚类和监控。
method: 结合可扩展的分析方法，主要依赖聚类生成步骤的分类，并提供SQL访问以进行复杂查询。还集成了Jev风格的决策模型，用于语义路由和评估。
results: Taxi能够高效地扩展到数百万个步骤，通过聚类提供结构化数据概览，并通过SQL提供复杂查询能力。Jev风格的决策模型提供了低成本的语义路由和评估。
conclusion: Taxi是一个为大规模代理分析设计的、可扩展的、模块化的系统，通过结合聚类、SQL查询和决策模型，为工程师和自动化代理提供了强大的工具。

title: The Fingerprinting Paradox: Why Sensitivity Undermines Black-Box Model Integrity Verification
authors: Shahinul Hoque, Farhin Farhad Riya, Jinyuan Sun, Fnu Suya
abstract: Black-box integrity verification aims to detect unauthorized modifications to outsourced models using only prediction APIs. Existing frameworks seek to improve verification efficiency through sensitive fingerprints: queries whose predictions are more likely to change under tampering than those of genuine inputs. We show that this sensitivity can also help dishonest providers recognize verification queries and selectively conceal tampering. We prove that excess sensitivity relative to genuine inputs lower-bounds statistical distinguishability. We evaluate five integrity verification frameworks across three model architectures, three datasets, and three adversarial knowledge settings. When the deployed framework is known, our fingerprint detectors achieve AUCs at least 0.989, and selective filtering makes all five frameworks require significantly larger estimated query budgets than genuine inputs, reversing their intended efficiency advantage. A query-efficiency advantage remains marginally in a small subset of evaluated settings with poor detection transfer. We further design verification methods under stronger concealment constraints but find that reduced detectability comes with losses in sensitivity or fingerprint-generation success. Our results expose a sensitivity-detectability tension and show that sensitivity alone does not ensure efficient black-box verification against adaptive malicious providers.
zh_title: 指纹识别悖论：为什么敏感性会破坏黑盒模型完整性验证
translation: 黑盒完整性验证旨在仅通过预测API来检测外包模型的未经授权的修改。现有的框架试图通过敏感的指纹：其预测在被篡改时比真实输入更可能发生变化的查询，来提高验证效率。我们表明，这种敏感性也可以帮助不诚实的提供者识别验证查询并选择性地隐藏篡改。我们证明，相对于真实输入的过度敏感性会降低统计区分度的下限。我们评估了跨越三个模型架构、三个数据集和三个对抗性知识设置的五个完整性验证框架。当部署的框架已知时，我们的指纹检测器的AUC至少为0.989，并且选择性过滤使得所有五个框架都需要比真实输入显著更大的估计查询预算，从而逆转了它们预期的效率优势。在检测转移性较差的一小部分评估设置中，查询效率优势仍然存在。我们进一步在更强的隐藏约束下设计了验证方法，但发现可检测性的降低伴随着敏感性或指纹生成成功率的损失。我们的结果揭示了敏感性-可检测性之间的权衡，并表明仅靠敏感性不能确保针对适应性恶意提供者的有效黑盒验证。
tldr: 提高验证查询的敏感性以检测篡淆，反而可能帮助恶意提供者识别并隐藏篡改，从而削弱了模型的完整性验证。
ai_comments: 这项研究揭示了一个重要的悖论，即用于增强模型完整性验证的方法本身可能成为被利用的弱点。研究结果强调了在设计安全验证机制时，需要仔细权衡效率和鲁棒性，并考虑对抗性攻击者的适应性。未来研究可以探索更先进的、不易被识别的验证技术。
motivation: 现有的黑盒模型完整性验证框架试图通过使用对篡改更敏感的“指纹”查询来提高效率，但这种敏感性也可能被恶意提供者利用来识别和隐藏篡改。
method: 证明了过度的敏感性会降低统计区分度，并在不同模型、数据集和知识设置下评估了五个完整性验证框架。设计了在更强隐藏约束下的验证方法，并分析了敏感性和可检测性之间的权衡。
results: 当部署框架已知时，指纹检测器的AUC至少为0.989，但选择性过滤使得所有框架的估计查询预算都显著增加。在检测转移性差的设置中，查询效率优势仅略微存在。更强的隐藏约束会导致可检测性下降，并伴随着敏感性或指纹生成成功率的损失。
conclusion: 敏感性本身并不能保证针对适应性恶意提供者的有效黑盒验证，因为敏感性与可检测性之间存在内在的权衡。

title: MADlibs: Analyzing the Distribution of Generative Music
authors: Matthew Keating, Noah Schaffer, Michael Casey, Nikhil Singh
abstract: What music can a text-to-music model actually make? The answer to this question has consequences for individual creators, communities, and musical culture more broadly. We introduce MADlibs, a framework to measure the expressive support of state-of-the-art music generators: the subset of musical behaviors they will actually produce across the space of prompts. We first develop strategies for generating musical prompts using natural language processing methods and existing caption corpora. Then, we use a set of MIR techniques to study the corresponding output spaces in terms of interpretable and qualitatively meaningful elements like key, beat, tempo, instrumentation, and dynamics. We find that text-to-music models are not interchangeable instruments for the same prompt space. Rather, each model has learned idiosyncratic properties that constrain the regime of music reachable via prompting it, for example, defaulting to certain tempi, failing to produce silences, or oversampling canonical band arrangements. Because users interact with these systems one prompt at a time, these biases are often invisible in practice yet cumulatively shape what AI-assisted music sounds like, risking the production of a new auditory monoculture hidden behind the promise of universal describability. We thus urge the MIR community to further study and responsibly steer population-level properties of music generation models.
translation: 现今的文本到音乐模型究竟能创作出什么样的音乐？这个问题的答案将对个人创作者、社群乃至更广泛的音乐文化产生深远影响。我们引入了MADLIBS，一个用于衡量最先进音乐生成器表达支持能力的框架：即在所有可能的提示空间中，它们实际会产生的音乐行为子集。我们首先开发了使用自然语言处理方法和现有标题语料库生成音乐提示的策略。然后，我们利用一套MIR技术，从可解释的、具有定性意义的元素（如调性、节拍、速度、乐器和动态）的角度研究相应的输出空间。我们发现，文本到音乐模型并非同一提示空间中可互换的乐器。相反，每个模型都学会了独特的属性，这些属性限制了通过提示它们可达到的音乐范围，例如，默认采用某些速度、无法生成静默、或过度采样典型的乐队编排。由于用户一次只通过一个提示与这些系统交互，因此这些偏见在实践中通常是看不见的，但它们会累积地塑造AI辅助音乐的声音，从而有可能在普遍可描述性的承诺背后，产生一种新的听觉单一文化。因此，我们敦促MIR社群进一步研究并负责任地引导音乐生成模型的群体属性。
tldr: MADLIBS框架分析了文本到音乐模型的音乐生成能力，发现不同模型具有独特的、限制性的生成属性，可能导致音乐的单一化。
ai_comments: 这项研究揭示了当前文本到音乐模型在生成音乐时存在的潜在偏见，并提出了一个量化分析框架。研究强调了这些偏见可能对音乐多样性产生的长远影响，并呼吁社区关注负责任的AI发展，这一点非常有价值。然而，研究中提到的“MIR技术”具体指哪些技术并未详细说明，可以进一步阐述。
motivation: 评估文本到音乐模型实际能生成的音乐类型，以及这对创作者、社群和音乐文化的影响。
method: 开发了使用自然语言处理和现有标题语料库生成音乐提示的策略，并利用MIR技术分析输出的音乐属性（如调性、节拍、速度、乐器、动态等）。
results: 文本到音乐模型并非可互换的工具，每个模型都有其独特的、限制性的生成属性，例如偏向特定速度、无法生成静默、或过度使用标准乐队编排。这些偏见会累积起来，影响AI辅助音乐的整体风格，可能导致“听觉单一文化”。
conclusion: 文本到音乐模型具有隐藏的、累积性的偏见，可能导致音乐的单一化。MIR社群应进一步研究并负责任地引导音乐生成模型的群体属性。

title: Below the Stopwatch: Checking the Performance Claims of Coding Agents in the Kernel
authors: Yuvraj Sehgal, Sneh Patel, Mahsa Panahandeh, Naser Ezzati-Jivan
abstract: Coding agents open many pull requests (PRs) that claim to make software faster. Most such claims also give a reason, such as "cache the result" or "read the file once". A stopwatch can show that code got faster, but not that it got faster for the stated reason. We present Below, a pipeline that checks these reasons at the kernel level. From 1,343 runtime-performance PRs in the AIDev dataset, Below extracts the mechanism each PR claims and maps it to the kernel and hardware signals that must change if the claim is true. A build agent that never sees the claim rebuilds the code before and after each PR. Below then measures both versions with plain timing runs, hardware counters and LTTng kernel traces. Most claims are not measured: 57.3% of the PRs offer only reasoning or no evidence, and only 31.4% state an effect size. Of 82 analyzed PRs, 32 ran faster, 28 showed no clear change and 22 ran slower. The expected signal of the claimed mechanism appeared in 34 PRs (20 in kernel-trace signals alone), and 42 PRs also changed their output. Kernel signals move about 1.7 times as often for a faster PR's claimed mechanism as for mechanisms it did not claim; the instruction count barely separates them (1.15 times).
comment: Short paper for the AGENT 2027 workshop at ICSE 2027. 5 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables
zh_title: 秒表之下：检查内核中编码代理的性能声明
translation: 编码代理会打开许多拉取请求（PR），声称能使软件运行得更快。大多数此类声明都给出了原因，例如“缓存结果”或“只读取一次文件”。秒表可以显示代码是否运行得更快，但无法证明其是否因所述原因而变快。我们提出了Below，一个在内核层面检查这些原因的流水线。Below从AIDev数据集中提取了1,343个运行时性能相关的PR，并识别出每个PR声称的机制，并将其映射到如果声明为真时必须改变的内核和硬件信号。一个从不看到声明的构建代理在每个PR之前和之后重建代码。Below然后使用普通计时运行、硬件计数器和LTTng内核跟踪来测量两个版本。大多数声明都没有得到衡量：57.3%的PR仅提供推理或无证据，只有31.4%的PR说明了效果大小。在分析的82个PR中，32个运行速度更快，28个没有明显变化，22个运行速度变慢。声称的机制的预期信号出现在34个PR中（20个仅在内核跟踪信号中），42个PR的输出也发生了变化。与未声称的机制相比，运行更快的PR的声称机制的内核信号移动的频率大约是1.7倍；指令计数几乎无法区分它们（1.15倍）。
tldr: 该研究引入了一个名为Below的工具，用于验证编码代理（如GitHub Copilot）声称的软件性能提升的真实性和原因。研究发现，大多数PR（Pull Request）的性能声明缺乏实际证据，并且实际性能提升与声称原因之间的关联性不强。
ai_comments: 这项研究非常有价值，因为它揭示了AI驱动的代码优化中一个重要的潜在问题：缺乏可验证性。许多AI生成的代码优化声称能提升性能，但实际效果和原因往往难以证实。Below工具的提出为解决这一问题提供了一个具体的方法。然而，该研究也存在一些局限性，例如分析的数据集可能无法完全代表所有类型的代码和性能优化场景，并且内核层面的信号分析可能需要专业知识。未来的工作可以扩展到更多的编程语言和应用领域，并探索更自动化的信号解释方法。
motivation: 许多编码代理声称能通过优化代码来提升软件性能，但这些声称往往缺乏充分的验证，尤其是在性能提升的原因方面。本研究旨在开发一种方法来核实这些性能声明及其背后的原因。
method: 研究提出了一种名为Below的流水线，该流水线在内核层面检查编码代理提出的性能提升声明。Below从AIDev数据集中提取了1,343个运行时性能相关的PR，并识别出每个PR声称的优化机制。然后，它将这些机制映射到内核和硬件信号，这些信号应在声明为真时发生变化。一个独立的构建代理在不了解声明内容的情况下，对每个PR的前后版本进行代码构建。接着，使用普通计时运行、硬件计数器和LTTng内核跟踪来测量两个版本的性能。
results: 在分析的82个PR中，32个PR的实际运行速度更快，28个PR没有明显变化，22个PR运行速度变慢。声称的机制预期的信号在34个PR中出现（其中20个仅在内核跟踪信号中体现）。42个PR的输出也发生了变化。与未声称的机制相比，声称的机制在运行更快的PR中，其对应的内核信号改变的频率大约是1.7倍；而指令计数在这两者之间的区分度较低（1.15倍）。研究还发现，57.3%的PR仅提供推理或无证据，31.4%的PR未说明效果大小。
conclusion: 本研究发现，编码代理提出的性能提升声明普遍缺乏充分的验证和证据支持。许多声明未能提供可衡量的效果大小，并且实际性能变化与声称的优化机制之间的关联性较弱。Below工具能够帮助更可靠地评估这些声明，揭示了当前代码优化声明中存在的问题。

title: Ground, Guide, Act: Improving VLA Spatial Generalization with Multimodal Foundation Models
authors: Guangting Zheng, Shaoxuan Wang, Yu Yuan, Zhipeng Tang, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models effectively learn action policies from robot demonstrations, but struggle to generalize to changes in object positions and task goals. General multimodal foundation models (MFMs) offer complementary scene understanding and spatial reasoning, but remain slow and unreliable for direct fine-grained control. To understand how MFMs can improve VLA spatial generalization, we conduct a systematic capability analysis across multiple VLA architectures using atomic-stage interventions, revealing that many failures stem from poor target grounding and global spatial routing, while local manipulation skills remain largely usable. Based on these findings, we propose MFM-VLA, a selective collaboration framework in which an MFM provides target grounding and spatial guidance, controllers execute free-space motion, and the VLA retains control over fine-grained manipulation. We fine-tune the VLA with action-chunk-level dense geometric captions and perturbed-state recovery data to improve local guidance following and recovery from unfamiliar handoff states. A development-calibrated capability router selects between direct VLA execution and MFM-assisted execution to avoid unnecessary intervention. Across LIBERO-PRO, ALOHA-Sim-PRO, RoboCasa365, and real-world chemistry tasks, MFM-VLA improves success rates by 14.9, 74.0, 3.6, and 30.9 percentage points, respectively, over the corresponding base VLA. The project page is available at https://tom-zgt.github.io/MFM-VLA
zh_title: 地面、引导、行动：利用多模态基础模型提高VLA空间泛化能力
translation: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型能有效地从机器人演示中学习动作策略，但在物体位置和任务目标发生变化时，其泛化能力会受到限制。通用的多模态基础模型（MFM）提供了互补的场景理解和空间推理能力，但在直接进行细粒度控制时速度较慢且不可靠。为了理解MFM如何改进VLA的空间泛化能力，我们通过原子阶段干预，对多种VLA架构进行了系统的能力分析，结果表明许多失败源于目标定位不准和全局空间路径规划不佳，而局部操作技能在很大程度上仍然可用。基于这些发现，我们提出了MFM-VLA，一个选择性协作框架，其中MFM提供目标定位和空间引导，控制器执行自由空间运动，VLA模型则保留对细粒度操作的控制。我们使用动作块级别的密集几何描述和扰动状态恢复数据对VLA模型进行微调，以提高其对局部引导的遵循能力以及从不熟悉的状态转移中恢复的能力。一个经过开发校准的能力路由器负责在直接VLA执行和MFM辅助执行之间进行选择，以避免不必要的干预。在LIBERO-PRO、ALOHA-Sim-PRO、RoboCasa365以及现实世界的化学任务中，MFM-VLA的成功率分别比相应的基线VLA模型提高了14.9%、74.0%、3.6%和30.9%。项目主页可在https://tom-zgt.github.io/MFM-VLA找到。
tldr: MFM-VLA框架通过多模态基础模型（MFM）增强了视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在机器人任务中的空间泛化能力，解决了目标定位和空间导航问题，并在多个基准测试中显著提高了成功率。
ai_comments: 该研究通过结合多模态基础模型（MFM）和视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型，有效地解决了机器人任务中的空间泛化难题，展示了混合模型的强大潜力。然而，框架的复杂性和能力路由器的效率仍有待进一步研究和优化。
motivation: 现有的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在处理物体位置和任务目标的变化时泛化能力不足。虽然通用的多模态基础模型（MFM）在场景理解和空间推理方面表现出色，但它们在精细控制方面速度慢且不可靠。本研究旨在探索MFM如何提升VLA模型的空间泛化能力。
method: 提出了一种名为MFM-VLA的选择性协作框架。在该框架中，MFM负责目标定位和空间引导，控制器处理自由空间运动，而VLA模型则专注于精细操作。为了增强局部引导和处理不熟悉的状态，VLA模型使用了动作块级别的密集几何描述和扰动状态恢复数据进行微调。此外，还引入了一个能力路由器，用于在直接VLA执行和MFM辅助执行之间进行选择，以避免不必要的干预。
results: 在LIBERO-PRO、ALOHA-Sim-PRO、RoboCasa365和现实世界的化学任务中，MFM-VLA的成功率分别比相应的基线VLA模型提高了14.9%、74.0%、3.6%和30.9%。
conclusion: MFM-VLA通过将MFM在目标定位和空间引导方面的优势与VLA模型在精细操作方面的能力相结合，显著提高了机器人任务的空间泛化能力。

title: Geometric Control Analysis of an Internally Actuated Flying Wing
authors: Jonathan Becker, Ella M. Atkins
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous geometric accessibility and controllability analysis for a fixed-wing Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) actuated solely by an internal moving mass, a momentum wheel, and external thrust. This configuration eliminates traditional control surfaces, which in turn reduces the combinatorial set of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) studies necessary for high-fidelity modeling of flight through unsteady flow fields. Using Lie bracket computations and the strong Lie Algebra Rank Condition, it is shown that the full nonlinear dynamics are generically small-time locally accessible, with singular configurations explicitly characterized and shown to be immediately escapable by direct mass actuation. The stronger property of small-time local controllability is shown to hold for the attitude subsystem at equilibrium points, using Sussmann's condition. A key contribution is the explicit treatment of the time-varying inertia tensor via the Huygens-Steiner Theorem, which introduces nontrivial coupling between the control vector fields. The momentum wheel provides direct yaw authority that, combined with inertia variation from the moving mass, generates a full-rank accessibility Lie algebra. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (MPC) is derived with consideration of flight envelope constraints and is applied to track different trajectories under unperturbed and perturbed flow field conditions.
comment: Submitted to IEEE TCST for review
zh_title: 内部驱动飞翼的几何控制分析
translation: 本文对一种仅由内部移动质量、动量轮和外部推力驱动的固定翼无人机系统(UAS)进行了严格的几何可及性和可控性分析。这种配置消除了传统的控制面，从而减少了高保真模拟飞行通过非稳态流场所需计算流体动力学(CFD)研究的组合集。利用李括号计算和强李代数秩条件，证明了在一般情况下，完整的非线性动力学在小时间范围内是可及的，并明确表征了奇异构型，且表明可以通过直接的质量驱动来立即摆脱这些构型。利用Sussmann的条件，证明了在平衡点处，姿态子系统具有小时间局部可控性这一更强的性质。一项关键的贡献是通过Huygens-Steiner定理对随时间变化的惯性张量进行了显式处理，该定理在控制向量场之间引入了非平凡的耦合。动量轮提供了直接的偏航控制能力，结合来自移动质量的惯性变化，生成了全秩的可及性李代数。在考虑飞行包线约束的情况下，推导了一个非线性模型预测控制器(MPC)，并将其应用于在无扰动和扰动流场条件下跟踪不同的轨迹。
tldr: 该论文分析了一种仅通过内部移动质量、动量轮和外部推力驱动的固定翼无人机系统的几何可达性和可控性。研究表明，该系统在小时间尺度上是可控的，并提出了一种考虑飞行包线约束的非线性模型预测控制器。
ai_comments: 该研究在理论上对内部驱动飞翼的控制可达性和可控性进行了深入分析，并提出了实用的MPC控制器。然而，实际应用中如何精确建模和控制内部移动质量的动态特性，以及在极端气象条件下的鲁棒性仍是未来研究的重点。
motivation: 消除传统控制面，减少高保真建模所需的计算流体动力学(CFD)研究数量，并分析内部驱动飞翼的几何可达性和可控性。
method: 使用李括号计算和强李代数秩条件来分析可达性；使用Sussmann条件分析姿态子系统的可控性；利用Huygens-Steiner定理处理随时间变化的惯性张量；推导非线性模型预测控制器(MPC)。
results: 证明了完整的非线性动力学在一般情况下是小时间局部可达的，并明确了奇异构型；证明了姿态子系统在平衡点处具有小时间局部可控性；通过移动质量产生的惯性变化和动量轮提供的偏航控制，实现了全秩可达性李代数；MPC控制器能够跟踪不同轨迹，即使在扰动流场条件下也是如此。
conclusion: 该内部驱动飞翼系统在小时间尺度上是可控的，并且通过所提出的MPC控制器可以有效地跟踪轨迹。

title: A dataset of clinically similar image pairs from citation-linked case reports for medical image retrieval
authors: Guy Shmueli, Keno K. Bressem, Tom Hope
abstract: Retrieving images of patients clinically similar to a given patient can support diagnosis, teaching and research. Training and evaluating retrieval systems requires knowing which images of different patients show the same finding, and existing datasets are small or narrow in scope. We construct PMC-PaIR, a dataset of 86,144 pairs of clinically similar images from 56,013 open-access PubMed Central case reports, which often document rare or challenging presentations. We develop an approach that follows citations, which often link case reports of similar patients. To determine what two linked cases share clinically, it prompts large language models to generate and answer hierarchical questions, from modality to diagnosis and findings, and to match images by caption using the answers. Experts find the pairs highly accurate, and this question-guided approach finds twice as many correct pairs as direct matching. Fine-tuning BiomedCLIP on PMC-PaIR improves retrieval in all modality, anatomy and diagnosis categories tested, for image-only queries and image queries with a short text naming the finding. We release the dataset and the automated pipeline, which can extend PMC-PaIR as new case reports are published.

title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
authors: Kunyang Li, Chaoyang Wang, Mubarak Shah, Yuzhang Shang
abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements. Our multimodal agent autonomously researches products through web and image search and translates its findings into selling-point-driven storyboards that guide a frozen video generator. To achieve this, we develop a dedicated data construction pipeline that yields two training datasets, AdProducer-SFT and AdProducer-RL, and train the agent through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with joint optimization of storyboard- and video-level rewards. We further introduce AdCreation-Bench, comprising 305 advertising briefs across eight domains, with two complementary metrics: PG-Score for product correctness and creative execution, and Ad-Score for overall advertising effectiveness assessed by an independent judge. Experiments demonstrate that AdProducer improves the PG-Score of MiniMax H3 from 17.3 to 51.3 and generalizes to Veo 3.1 without additional training, improving its score from 28.0 to 35.9, with consistent gains in Ad-Score, VideoScore2, and human evaluations. Code, models, and data are released.

title: Linear-Time Optimal Leaf Roots beyond 3-Leaf Powers
authors: Daniela Ceban, Christian Rosenke
abstract: A $k$-leaf power for an integer $k \geq 2$ is a graph $G$ that permits a $k$-leaf root, a tree $T$ with leaf set $V(G)$ such that, for all distinct vertices $x,y \in V(G)$, their distance in $T$ is at most $k$ if and only if $xy$ is an edge of $G$. Constructing such trees is motivated by the reconstruction of phylogenetic trees from similarity data. For every fixed $k$, Lafond [ACM Trans. Algorithms 2023] showed that $k$-leaf powers can be recognized in polynomial time. Recently, Dupré la Tour, Lafond, and Ndiaye [SODA 2026] proved that the problem becomes NP-complete when $k$ is part of the input and that deciding whether a graph is a $k$-leaf power for some $k$ is NP-complete as well. Le and Rosenke [J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 2024] proposed a different algorithmic perspective by studying \emph{optimal leaf roots} of graphs $G$, that is, the $k$-leaf roots of $G$ with minimum possible $k$. This smallest $k$-value is called the \emph{leaf rank} of $G$. They showed that optimal leaf roots of chordal cographs, a class of unbounded leaf rank, can be constructed in linear time. However, chordal cographs do not even contain all $3$-leaf powers. This paper extends linear-time optimal-leaf-root construction to three natural superclasses of the $3$-leaf powers, the $(\text{bull},\text{gem})$-free, the $(\text{bull},\text{dart})$-free, and the $(\text{dart},\text{gem})$-free chordal graphs. Except for the latter case, which follows from known results, our methods are based on structural decompositions of bull-free chordal graphs. In particular, the relevant $(\text{bull},\text{gem})$-free graphs decompose into chordal cographs attached to a tree, while the $(\text{bull},\text{dart})$-free case reduces to trees and powers of paths.
comment: Appears in the Proceedings of the 52nd International Conference on Current Trends in Theory and Practice of Computer Science (Sofsem 2027)

title: Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis
authors: Andreas Martin Lisewski
abstract: Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunkštis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compresses true $Π_1^0$ statements about $ζ(s)$ into $\mathsf{ZFC}$ derivations of bounded length $L_0$. Assuming classical logic and $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$, Gödel--Carnap diagonalization over bounded zeta-encoded provability yields a contradiction. The self-referential result converts a digital encoding framework with any uniform proof-compression principle for RH into an immediate non-constructive refutation of RH. Given that, with human input and computer assistance, $\mathsf{RH}$ has been formally verified in the Lean theorem prover strictly within constructive logic, this contradiction does not refute $\mathsf{RH}$. Instead, it falsifies $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$. We conclude by isolating the exact proof-theoretic obstruction---Pudlák's lower bound on bounded reflection proofs---showing why the analytic regularity of $\mathsf{RH}$ cannot compress logical self-reference, and exposing the limits of applying the Law of Excluded Middle to uncomputably bounded searches.

title: CRAB-H: Task-Centric Certification for Healthcare Autonomous Systems
authors: Tord Johan Eide, Einar Holt
abstract: This paper introduces CRAB H as a task-centric certification methodology for healthcare autonomous systems. CRAB H extends the ARC governance architecture by introducing the task as a first-class governance object, represented through Task Requirement Profiles TRP H. Each profile defines the cognitive capabilities, governance constraints, evidentiary requirements, and operational assumptions necessary for the safe execution of a specific healthcare activity. Rather than asking whether a robot achieves a sufficiently high benchmark score, CRAB H asks whether demonstrated capabilities satisfy the requirements of the task. Certification becomes a comparison between demonstrated capability and required capability. A reliability-gated assurance allocation mechanism routes cognitive dimensions that cannot be reproducibly evaluated to LEA operational requirements rather than discarding them. Governance integrity is preserved: unreliable dimensions are governed, not ignored. The Capability Margin is defined as the threshold-based conjunction of per-dimension compliance determinations, not as a subtracted scalar preserving non compensatory governance logic appropriate for safety-critical healthcare deployment

title: PromptSMC: Enabling Particle Exploration in Flow Matching via LLM-Based Prompt Rejuvenation
authors: Wenyi Lian, Zheng Zhao, Thomas B. Schön
abstract: This paper is concerned with prompt-image alignment at inference time through exploration of generative trajectories and dynamical prompt rejuvenation. We leverage sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), to offer a gradient-free and principled framework for this purpose through reward-guided trajectory selection. More specifically, we introduce LLM-based prompt rejuvenation, allowing for efficient particle exploration in SMC samplers along the diffusion time in flow matching models. The proposed method, PromptSMC, retains the selected latent states and uses a pretrained LLM to dynamically revise the prompts of duplicated particles under semantic-preservation constraints. These revised prompts induce alternative conditional velocity fields, allowing particles to explore different continuations from a shared intermediate state. The method further uses a reward model to evaluate each particle's alignment with the original prompt, and the resulting scores guide particles through resampling. PromptSMC thus integrates prompt-based exploration with reward-guided sampling, achieving faithful prompt-image alignment without additional noise injection, model training, or reward gradients. Our experiments and ablation studies across multiple benchmarks and backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of the method for text-to-image flow matching. Code is available at https://github.com/shermanlian/PromptSMC.

title: Pearl: TEE-Enabled Fair Ordering with Minimal Replication
authors: Vian Robotin, Jérémie Decouchant, Shaokang Xie, Dakai Kang, Mohammad Sadoghi
abstract: Recent research has investigated fair transaction ordering in blockchain consensus. An orthogonal line of work has demonstrated that equipping replicas with trusted execution environments (TEEs) enables more efficient consensus protocols with only $2f{+}1$ replicas. In this work, we bridge these two areas and demonstrate that two key fair-ordering properties, ordering linearizability and $γ$-batch-order fairness with minimal batching, cannot be implemented in partially synchronous networks with $2f{+}1$ replicas, even when the replicas are equipped with TEEs. We show that Byzantine replicas can circumvent TEE protections by manipulating the timing of transaction submissions to the enclave, thereby biasing the resulting ordering indicators. However, we prove that assuming a synchronous network allows both properties to be implemented with a reduced replica count. We propose two mechanisms: one uses absolute TEE-attested timestamps to guarantee ordering linearizability in a system of $n \ge 2f{+}1$ replicas, and the other uses TEE-maintained relative sequence numbers to guarantee $γ$-batch-order fairness when $n > \frac{2γf}{2γ-1}$. Ultimately, we integrate these mechanisms into a synchronous lane-based consensus algorithm, achieving strong fair-ordering properties and superior performance while requiring fewer replicas than representative state-of-the-art baselines.

title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
authors: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li, Zhixiang Lu, Haolin Yang, Jianxu Chen, Yifan Lu, Di Fan, Yutong Xie
abstract: Spatial reasoning agents increasingly rely on external tools, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation, to answer questions that a multimodal large language model (MLLM) cannot resolve from pixels alone. Tool access, however, shifts the bottleneck to orchestration: the agent must decide which tools to call, in what order, and how to interpret their outputs, yet a stateless agent repeats the same mistakes across tasks. We ask whether a frozen tool-using agent can improve its orchestration from its own interaction history, without parameter updates. We present SpatialCraft, a self-evolving framework that maintains two forms of external knowledge: Experiences, condition-action tactics distilled by contrasting rollouts of the same task, and Skills, multi-step procedures with explicit activation and termination conditions. Three designs couple the two streams. Experiences can be anchored to a Skill, appearing only while it is active rather than once per task. A Contrastive Utility Score estimates each Experience's effect by randomly withholding it across rollouts of the same task, separating its contribution from task difficulty, and Experiences with consistently positive utility are consolidated into the Skills they support. Across five spatial benchmarks and four backbones, SpatialCraft achieves the best accuracy in all 20 settings, showing that a frozen agent can learn to orchestrate spatial tools from its own experience.

title: Transferable, Time-Parallel Graph Dynamics via Space-Time Factorization
authors: Wencong Yang, Chaopeng Shen, Abdolmehdi Behroozi
abstract: Time-parallel neural operators (FNO and successors) have transformed PDE surrogates on regular grids. Mesh-based operators (MeshGraphNets, Transolver) extend operator learning to irregular geometries, but jointly learning across diverse topologies while retaining non-recurrent temporal evaluation remains challenging. We propose space-time factorization: partition the model into local temporal operators (learned, graph-independent) and a spatial mixer that propagates information across nodes without graph-dependent learned parameters. This structural condition lets the same parameters run on unseen graphs; non-recurrent instances also admit time-parallel evaluation. Accurate zero-shot transfer further depends on controlling three information leaks (graph-dependent weights, graph-specific features, and graph-correlated training distributions) and on suitable task physics and training coverage. The protocol applies to two distinct spatial-mixer families, fixed-spectral and learned-attention. We validate the principle in three domains. For floodwave propagation in river networks, a 27K-parameter model trained on the Yangtze transfers zero-shot to the Mississippi with median NSE 0.998 in boundary-conditioned operational evaluation, training 5.5x faster than a stabilized recurrent baseline. On cross-geometry Navier-Stokes, the three-seed SepFNO mean relative vorticity error on five unseen targets falls by about 28% from 5 to 12 training geometries, with a consistent single-run SepTransolver trend. On cross-city traffic forecasting, zero-shot transfer reaches within 12.9% of an oracle trained on the target city. Across settings, cross-geometry error decreases with both the number of training geometries and their relatedness to the test, at a rate depending on the spatial mixer. This opens the path to pooled-data, foundation-style models for graph dynamics on irregular topologies.

title: Which Way Is Up? Rotated Photos Silently Hurt Multi-View 3D Foundation Models
authors: Yukun Shi, Minglun Gong
abstract: Multi-view 3D foundation models estimate camera poses and 3D points from a set of photos in one forward pass. Many cameras store a portrait shot sideways, with an orientation tag telling viewers how to turn it, and this tag can be ignored, lost or wrong. We measure how rotated photos affect five such models on three datasets. A few rotated photos lower camera pose accuracy for every model, and the sideways photos already in a standard benchmark do the same. Even the most robust model still loses accuracy. The failure is also silent: the models' confidence does not reliably flag it, and most official image loaders ignore the tag. The fixes we test each correct only part of the problem. These findings call for orientation checks in reconstruction pipelines and benchmarks.

title: SwiftLoop: Selective Refinement for Adaptive Implicit Reasoning in Looped Transformers
authors: Tianyi Zhao, Ke Wan, Chen Chen
abstract: Looped Transformers advance implicit chain-of-thought reasoning through recurrent latent refinement. However, existing looped reasoners typically employ fixed-depth recurrence, updating all latent positions at every iteration and incurring redundancy when further refinement is unnecessary. We introduce \textsc{SwiftLoop}, an inference-time framework for selective recurrent refinement through position-wise freezing, enabling adaptive computation allocation across both recurrent depth and active width. SwiftLoop learns lightweight freezing policies through hindsight-guided supervision derived from two complementary criteria: K/V reusability at the internal representation level and functional impact at the output level. At inference time, these policies guide adaptive freezing based on observed hidden states. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SwiftLoop achieves favorable accuracy--computation trade-offs over fixed-loop inference and adaptive baselines, with measured inference acceleration. Beyond implicit reasoning, we further demonstrate its applicability to recurrent prompt prefilling in general looped models.

title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design
authors: Santiago A. Cadena, Andrea Merlo
abstract: In high-dimensional, PDE-constrained design, interpolating between known feasible solutions can reveal trade-offs without repeating expensive optimization campaigns. In stellarator design for fusion energy, direct interpolation of plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints even when both endpoints are feasible. Learned latent representations can capture nonlinear relationships among design variables, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design. We introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. Geometric benchmarks show the benefit of regularizing latent interpolants. In stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, compared with 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct interpolation of boundary parameters. Ablations show that both ingredients are needed for this gain. Beyond interpolation, latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, while self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On the ConStellaration benchmark, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely. After low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the benchmark's high-fidelity feasibility test. We release code and over 600k designs for stellarator generation, surrogate training, and front-filling evaluation. These results support feasibility-aware latent learning for exploring constrained design trade-offs.

title: Embodied Neuro-symbolic AI: Making Robot Behavior Auditable, Safe, and Scalable
authors: Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Jonathan Francis, Alessandro Oltramari
abstract: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) end-to-end systems have driven major progress in robot learning, yet they still face persistent barriers to dependable real-world deployment. In practice, these models often exhibit brittle generalization under distribution shift (i.e., novel objects, layouts, lighting, or contact conditions), limited physical and causal reasoning, and inconsistent fine-grained motor control. Critically, many VLA pipelines offer limited ways to express and audit what a robot must not do, making it difficult to provide assurance in safety-critical settings. These limitations constrain scalability, maintainability, and trust when robots move beyond controlled demonstrations. We propose Embodied Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI: a deployment-oriented paradigm that integrates learned perception, planning and control with explicit, machine-readable background knowledge and formal constraints. By combining knowledge-guided perception, constraint-aware symbolic planning, and hybrid learning, Embodied NeSy AI enables robots to reason about their environment, adapt to new tasks, and provide auditable, machine-checkable compliance with safety and operational requirements, thus supporting scalable, trustworthy robot deployment.

title: Evaluating Frontier-Model Agent Skills with Open-Weight Models in a Science Gateway
authors: Komal Thareja, Mats Rynge, Anirban Mandal, Ewa Deelman
abstract: Scientific analyses that span many jobs and computing sites depend on workflow management systems to run reliably, but writing a production workflow requires expertise in such a system, which many domain scientists do not have. Coding agents can supply this expertise when they are guided by skills and packaged procedures for recurring tasks. We wrote skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow management system with a frontier model, and the PegasusAI Studio science gateway offers them to scientists through a chat interface. New users without frontier-model credits need an open-weight model, served at no cost on research cyberinfrastructure, but skills written for a frontier model may not work with an open-weight solution. This paper presents a method for adapting such skills. An evaluation harness drives the real gateway as a user would, scores the workflows the agent builds, and feeds recurring failures back to the frontier model that maintains the skills. We evaluated 21 open-weight models on 17 tasks. The five highest-scoring models are close in quality after one trial per task, and their median response times differ twelvefold. In repeated trials with the best of the three open-weight models, we repeated scores of 0.76 on workflow building against 0.82 for Claude. The harness led to five changes to the initial skills. We also identify challenges in evaluating agents within operational systems: evaluation failures can be mistaken for model failures, and agents can circumvent experimental controls within their privilege domain. In a controlled ablation, an initially significant effect disappeared when the restrictions were properly enforced.

title: GDD: A Remote Sensing Image Deepfake Detection and Manipulation Localization Dataset
authors: Jacob Arndt, Philipe Dias, Debvrat Varshney, Sudarshan Srinivasan, Dalton Lunga
abstract: Verifying image authenticity is a critical need for a variety of applications and decision-making in the remote sensing (RS) domain, yet it is becoming more challenging as advancements in generative AI enable producing increasingly realistic synthetic overhead data. However, existing RS deepfake benchmarks prioritize sheer volume at the expense of visual realism and diversity, while also lacking rigorous out-of-distribution (OOD) testing protocols to evaluate real-world robustness. To address this, we introduce the Geospatial Deepfakes Dataset (GDD), a benchmark for RS deepfake detection and manipulation localization. Rather than relying on uncurated, redundant synthetic generation, GDD comprises images across diverse modern generative models and real image sources, alongside manipulations from diffusion inpainting, splicing, and copy-move operations. Crucially, GDD establishes an OOD evaluation protocol for deepfake detection comprising unseen real image sources and generative models. We benchmark five deepfake detectors and two localization models across intra- and cross-dataset regimes and reveal that detectors trained on high-volume, uncurated benchmarks overfit to dataset-specific artifacts, whereas training on GDD yields superior cross-dataset generalization despite its compact scale. This benchmarking also exposes critical failure modes in current state-of-the-art methods. Combined, GDD and its evaluation protocol establish a high-quality standard for developing and stress-testing detection and localization models in this safety-critical RS domain. The dataset is publicly available.

title: Trust-Region Optimization for Performative Prediction without Response Modeling
authors: Siqi Du, Miaolan Xie, Roy Dong
abstract:
Performative prediction studies learning problems in which deployed decisions change the distribution of future data. Existing methods often impose structure on the population response, which limits their applicability when a fixed model class poorly captures that response. Generic black-box optimization avoids response modeling but does not exploit the known loss function.
  We introduce Performative Trust-Region Optimization (PTRO), which bridges these two approaches by optimizing performative risk without specifying or fitting a response model while still exploiting the known loss. The key idea is sampling from the current population to evaluate the known loss at nearby decisions, and use additional deployments only to estimate the effect of population response. This gives a local approximation of performative risk without committing to a model of how the population responds. PTRO then uses a trust-region mechanism to determine and adapt how far this local information can be trusted.
  Under moment-bounded losses and suitable smoothness and estimator-accuracy conditions, we establish high-probability convergence to an $ε$-stationary point of the performative risk in $O(ε^{-2})$ iterations, with $O(d^{3}ε^{-4})$ samples per iteration, where $d$ is the decision dimension and $q\geq2$ is the loss-moment order.
  Experiments illustrate methods built around a specified response model can be more sample-efficient when their structural assumptions are accurate, whereas PTRO remains effective as the population response is poorly captured by a fixed model class. Ablations further show that both exploiting the known loss and adaptive trust-region updates are important for controlling the accuracy and efficiency.

title: Reading Between the Layers: Where Representation Quality Lives, and What Geometry Reveals
authors: Arnesh Batra, Aniket Khandelwal, Arush Gumber, Krish Thukral, Kushagra Agrawal, Dev Sharma
abstract: Representation quality in pretrained text foundation models is not concentrated at the final layer, yet practitioners routinely probe it there because layer selection without labels has remained an open problem. We present a large-scale empirical study of where layer quality lives across 25 models spanning four architectural families and four pretraining strategies, evaluated on 13 datasets across classification, pair classification, semantic textual similarity, and multiple-choice question answering. Peak probing layers depend systematically on pretraining strategy and architecture: masked encoders peak in late-middle layers, sequence-to-sequence models shift their peak with task type, contrastive sentence encoders concentrate signal at the final layer under CLS and last-token readouts but peak early under mean pooling, and decoder-only models exhibit distinct phase structure tied to depth. We distill these findings into the Stable Geometry Index (SGI), a closed-form, fully label-free selector with no fitted coefficients combining power-law fit quality, effective-rank capacity, spectral stability, and a weak depth prior. Across 383 evaluation groups SGI improves over the last-layer baseline and lifts Hit@3 from 0.39 to 0.52, recovering 40% of the gap to the oracle without using any labels, and exceeds a supervised ELMo-style layer mix on the matched subset despite using strictly less information. Our ablations also reverse a common assumption in the spectral-decay literature: power-law fit quality is a stronger predictor of layer quality than the exponent's proximity to one.

title: HyMTS: A Multiscale Tensor Factorization-Based Network for Hyperspectral Image Restoration
authors: Lei Xu, Fahad Sohrab, Moncef Gabbouj, Mehmet Yamac
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) restoration has been explored using deep learning techniques recently. Because hyperspectral images have strong spectral and spatial redundancy, the underlying clean signal is usually represented in a low-dimensional spectral subspace and locally low-rank spatial structures. Existing methods primarily explore dense attention or feature mixing across spectral bands. In this work, we propose HyMTS, a hyperspectral restoration network with a backbone built on the Multi-scale Tensorial Summation (MTS) factorization operator. HyMTS provides a natural architectural mechanism for exploiting a low-rank prior, embedded directly in the network operator rather than imposed via an auxiliary loss or a constraint on the reconstructed output. Specifically, HyMTS stacks a unified block that couples factorized layers with input-adaptive layers, capturing both local and global dependencies across the spectral and spatial dimensions. Extensive experiments without auxiliary data on standard benchmarks for Gaussian and real-noise denoising and single-image super-resolution show that HyMTS efficiently achieves superior or comparable performance to various state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Measuring Counterfactual Credit in a Replayable Wildfire-Suppression Benchmark
authors: Alireza Moghaddasi
abstract: In cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, learned critics are usually evaluated by how well they predict the team's return. Yet predicting a team's return and assigning credit to individual actions are distinct tasks. To test credit directly, we introduce FLARE (Fireline Learning Agents in a Replayable Environment), a stochastic wildfire suppression benchmark in which any moment of a fire can be replayed with different actions under the same random events. Replaying one step measures the immediate effect of each agent's suppression, which we call simulator credit and use for training. Replaying to the end of the episode measures the effect of each action, which we use for grading critics. In a comparison over eight seeds with multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO), simulator credit reduces the interquartile mean burn score (each cell's burning time, capped and averaged over the map; lower is better) from 26.6% with shared reward to 20.9%. Learned credit from a centralized COMA-style critic does no better than the shared reward. Four trained critics predict the team's return well, yet the credit they assign is 9 to 42 times larger than the credit measured by replay. The critics also give heterogeneous agents nearly identical action rankings. These results show that a good fit to the team's return is a weak test of a critic's credit.

title: ModernELECTRA: Replaced-Token Detection with Boundary-Window Reconstruction for Compact Encoders that Classify and Embed
authors: Mykhailo Shtopko, Ihor Stepanov, Dmytro Vodianytskyi, Oleksandr Lukashov
abstract: ELECTRA-style replaced-token detection (RTD) is a sample-efficient objective for pre-training text encoders, and RTD-trained models such as DeBERTaV3 are strong on classification benchmarks. The same models, however, are known to be poor backbones for embedding tasks such as retrieval and semantic similarity: the binary "original vs. replaced" signal does not ask the final layer to retain the token identity and contextual content that dense representations rely on. We introduce ModernELECTRA, a pre-training recipe that keeps RTD as the main objective and adds a lightweight auxiliary task, boundary-window reconstruction. For every token, we sample a window of 3-12 tokens that strictly contains it and reconstruct the token's original identity only from the discriminator's hidden states at the two window boundaries. The task costs one small FFN at training time and is discarded afterwards, yet it forces every final-layer state to carry information about its neighbourhood. Combined with a frozen, separately pre-trained generator, a temperature curriculum for hard negatives and a 512-to-8192 length curriculum, we train two compact encoders: EdgeCoder-31M, an 8-layer English model, and EdgeCoder-Multilingual-61M, a 16-layer model covering 46 languages, each on about 1T tokens. They reach 86.0 and 85.1 on GLUE. The English model outperforms Ettin-Enc-32m (83.5) and MiniLM-L12 (84.6) on GLUE while matching them on MTEB English v2 (51.1), and the multilingual model outperforms the 2.3x larger mmBERT-small on GLUE and Multilingual MiniLM and mDistilBERT on XTREME over the languages it covers. We also describe FlashDeBERTa, our open-source fused implementation of DeBERTa's disentangled attention that stores no $n \times n$ score matrix: at 4096 tokens it is 10x faster and uses 93% less memory than the reference implementation, and it loads existing DeBERTa checkpoints unchanged.

title: TokenJoule: Energy Modeling for Distributed Training and Inference of LLMs
authors: George Karfakis, Lime Yao, Joyjit Kundu, Debjyoti Bhattacharjee, Puneet Gupta
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) scale, energy dictates operating cost, cooling, and cluster capacity across training and inference. Early hardware design-space exploration (DSE) requires predicting energy before silicon exists, yet performance models miss hidden component work while prior energy predictors calibrate to deployed GPUs. We present TokenJoule, an open-source analytical tool that derives device kernel sequences, tiled compute, shared-memory staging, cache residency, and collective traffic, pricing activity directly with component energies. With zero workload fitting, TokenJoule achieves 3.3-6.6% activity error (151 A100/H100 runs) and 3.0-6.8% A100 energy error, guiding parallelism, memory packaging, and 3D-DRAM chip co-design.

title: Near-Zero Forgetting Is Not Enough: Out-of-Distribution Robustness in Continual Learning of Pretrained VLAs
authors: Adrià Ruiz, Bartłomiej Twardowski, Tinne Tuytelaars, Sergi Masip
abstract: Recent work shows that pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit near-zero forgetting in specific continual learning settings with experience replay. However, robustness to domain shift of learned tasks remains unexplored. In this work, we study the robustness of Pi0 fine-tuned with experience replay under out-of-distribution (OOD) data using the LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks. While the in-domain (ID) setup achieves near-zero catastrophic forgetting, OOD performance on previous tasks quickly collapses. Specifically, we show that during the continual learning process, the OOD capabilities of the model degrade, following a shared representational pattern across domain shifts, which is also visible behaviorally in the two simpler suites. Representational analysis shows that drift concentrates in the multimodal and action features. Linear probes indicate that OOD features still retain task-relevant information, but appear unreadable, consistent with representation misalignment. These findings suggest that even when ID stability remains intact, severe OOD forgetting can still occur, accompanied by representational drift during continual learning.
comment: Presented at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Robot Learning at Deployment (Learn@Deploy). Project page: https://adrrp.github.io/vla-ood-robustness

title: How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective
authors: Thomas Pethick
abstract: Recurrent-depth models are trained with truncated backpropagation, yet it remains unclear why this works. We show that input injection, commonly used in recurrent-depth models, is exactly Halpern iteration, and that a slowly vanishing stepsize provably converges with a backpropagation window polylogarithmic in the depth. The guarantees require a Lipschitz operator, which for SwiGLU leads to a weight constraint in both row and spectral norm, while only a row norm constraint for gates. Based on these constraints, we develop an optimizer tailored to each parameter group, Sparrow, which provides a drop-in replacement of Muon/MuonH with no overhead, that speeds up training even beyond recurrent models.

title: Synthetic Augmentation for Data-Scarce Object Detection: Allocation, Dose, and Filtering Across Six Datasets
authors: João Félix, Atabak Dehban, Rodrigo Ventura
abstract: Robotic perception for capturing uncooperative orbital objects and inspecting variable industrial products must often operate with limited labelled imagery. We examine a modular synthetic-augmentation pipeline, evaluating generation planning and post-generation filtering as separate interventions, with computational cost as a design constraint. Across six object-detection datasets, FLUX.1-Fill with class-specific LoRA adaptation produced dataset-dependent dose effects; the validation-selected augmentation improved mAP@50:95 on four datasets and reduced it on two. Filtering did not yield consistent gains, and FID, KID, precision, recall, and LPIPS did not consistently track detector changes. The results do not establish that image quality alone identifies useful samples. They motivate standardised evaluation and inexpensive candidate-utility measures that could identify useful samples before detector retraining, reducing repeated training cost.
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to European Robotics Forum 2027

title: Optimal Signaling Mechanisms for One-round Matching Markets
authors: Varsha Dani, David G. Harris, Thomas P. Hayes, Seth Pettie
abstract:
Signaling mechanisms are used in various types of matching markets so that applicants may credibly signal interest in firms. They have been observed to improve outcomes in job markets and dating markets, and proven to improve outcomes in several stylized theoretical models.
  In this paper we develop optimal signaling mechanisms for a simple one-round matching market consisting of $n$ applicants and $n$ firms. We consider a much richer space of signals than have been used previously, in theory or practice, and also consider randomized signaling mechanisms, which have not been systematically studied.
  For each $k \geq 1$, we determine the optimal deterministic and randomized signaling mechanisms in which applicants signal $k$ firms. In the limit as $k\to \infty$, our deterministic mechanism guarantees that in expectation, $\approx 75.4504\%$ of the applicants receive job offers, and this is optimal. Likewise, for $k \to \infty$, our randomized mechanism guarantees that $\approx 78.197\%$ of the applicants receive offers, which is also optimal.
  The optimal $k$-signal randomized mechanism is non-constructive, and has a rather complex description. We describe some simple randomized signaling mechanisms whose efficiency surpasses that of the limiting optimal deterministic mechanism. Finally, we also discuss incentive-compatibility for the firms to follow the mechanism.

title: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management
authors: Malay Phadke, Chirath Hettiarachchi
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) requires lifelong insulin therapy, and reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for automated dosing in the UVA/Padova simulator. However, the decisions of RL controllers remain difficult to interpret. We present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework for evaluating pretrained insulin-dosing policies without retraining. Each policy uses 60 minutes of continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and administered-insulin history, sampled every 5 minutes, to recommend insulin. We use SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to compare the importance of CGM and insulin-history inputs and summarize insulin-history attributions over three 20-minute windows motivated by insulin-on-board. We assess whether these attributions correspond to policy-output sensitivity through targeted input replacement and compare temporal rankings with TimeSHAP. In all 80 patient-policy-mask-size cases, replacing the highest-attribution inputs changes the normalized insulin recommendation more than replacing the lowest-attribution or random inputs. The highest-attribution insulin-history window is also the most output-sensitive in 115 of 120 patient-policy-scenario configurations, and KernelSHAP and TimeSHAP select the same top window in 111 of 120. Applying XRL4T1D to PPO and G2P2C across 20 virtual patients, we find that both controllers rely predominantly on CGM history, especially G2P2C. However, the distribution of insulin-history importance across recent, middle, and older windows varies by cohort, explainer, and analysis settings, without a consistent separation between controllers. Global feature-attribution rankings remain stable under the tested observation corruptions. These results show why attribution fidelity, temporal reproducibility, and controller-comparison robustness should be assessed separately.
comment: 23 pages, 7 figures. GenAI for Health Workshop at NeurIPS 2026

title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion
authors: Simon Weber, Mateo de Mayo, Je Hyeong Hong, Carl Olsson, Daniel Cremers, Ronald Clark
abstract: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFree-SfM, a complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose a simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play a central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements.

title: PatientFlowSynth: Evaluating FHIR Agents with Matched Patient Charts
authors: Anthony Cuturrufo, Ratul Ghosh, Devashish Khatwani, Krishnaram Kenthapadi
abstract: Agents that search patient charts must classify claims from retrieved records, including cases with missing or conflicting evidence. In Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), status fields can change how those records should be interpreted. PatientFlowSynth provides 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients and 18 templates that hold the patient, question, and retrieval program fixed across chart variants representing four evidence states. Re-executing the program verifies each variant's reference answer, evidence sets, and search requirements. Strict success requires a completed response with correct labels and citations exactly matching an accepted evidence set retrieved during the episode. Where required, a tool response must also show a complete search at the specified scope. In a study using GPT-5.6 Luna and 225 synthetic patients (3,600 matched pairs), explicit Encounter-status guidance increased strict success from 40.7% to 51.3% (+10.6 percentage points; 95% patient-bootstrap confidence interval, 8.4 to 12.8). Among cases whose primary reference label was insufficient evidence, label agreement fell from 49.2% to 29.3%. A prespecified two-model replication reproduced both changes. Failed retrieval can mask interpretation errors by producing a correct insufficient-evidence label without examining the relevant records. Additional model comparisons showed that the benefit of guidance was model-dependent. Retrieval, citation, and classification should be evaluated separately.

title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
authors: Zhanwen Chen, Tianchun Wang
abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Compared with Agent S3, Chronotope reduces median end-to-end latency by 85.5% for a 27B model, expanding its performance envelope to 100% Live success at an 8-second deadline versus 0%. Chronotope enables real-time GUI control through compact interaction history, knowing when to preserve, revise, or replace actions, and an overall efficient architectural design that obviates verbose reflection, reasoning, and grounding calls.

title: Your Codec, Your Generator: Idempotent Generative Compression without Retraining
authors: Raz Haim, Assaf Shocher
abstract: We introduce an image compression framework with three properties: (i) adaptation of pretrained codecs without retraining or fine-tuning, (ii) cycle-consistent recompression, even of already-encoded images, and (iii) decoding with independently chosen generative priors. We wrap the frozen encoder with non-learned operations so that every continuous latent has a preimage, yielding a surjective pseudo-invertible neural network. A nonlinear right inverse built from the pretrained decoder satisfies $E'(D'(E'(x)))=E'(x)$. To extend consistency to quantized bitstreams, the receiver searches for a continuous latent that reproduces both the transmitted main symbols and entropy side information. A successful search and an exact correction preserve both streams under deterministic coding; the final reconstruction is checked through the actual coding path. The encoder's pseudo-inverse enables a nonlinear counterpart of back-projection. In the linear case, back-projection has the closed-form solution $x'=x+A^\dagger(y-Ax)$, giving the closest reconstruction to $x$ satisfying $Ax'=y$. Our nonlinear formulation enforces the transmitted code on proposals from an independently chosen generative model. Adjusting the starting noise controls the prior's influence without changing that code. Experiments show small first-pass quality changes, higher retained quality than trained consistency codecs over 50 recompressions, also under 8-bit storage, and decoder-side control of the perception-distortion trade-off. Decoupling the codec from its prior lets the receiver adopt future generators without retraining or re-encoding.

title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
authors: Khalid Akhmouch, Eric Jauer
abstract: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is selected by greedily minimizing the Sliced Wasserstein distance between the empirical signature distributions of the candidate subset and the full dataset, a criterion for which we establish a convergence guarantee for random coresets. We validate SOTS on a real-world, highly imbalanced industrial I&C testing dataset, where SOTS-Greedy exceeds 95% of full-dataset accuracy using only 30% of the training data, outperforming standard coreset baselines at most budgets. This advantage generalizes to public UEA regular multivariate time series benchmarks specifically when class-discriminative information is purely geometric.

title: Fast Anatomy-Aware Diffeomorphic Augmentation for Brain MRI
authors: Tonmoy Hossain, Alexandra G. Roberts, Mark Olchanyi, Jonathan Williams Ramirez, Stefan Brandstätter, Juan Eugenio Iglesias
abstract: Data augmentation is essential for training deep learning models that are generalizable, particularly when training data are limited. In brain MRI, augmentation methods that synthesize anatomically diverse images without relying on large cohorts are particularly attractive, especially when training supervised models for scans with a specific resolution or MRI contrast. While conventional random nonlinear fields offer a simple means of achieving such diversity, they fail to capture the underlying spatial dependencies among morphological changes across brain regions. To address this limitation, we introduce BrainAug, an anatomy-aware augmentation framework that generates diverse, anatomically coordinated deformations without relying on population imaging data. BrainAug constructs an anatomical graph encoding spatial proximity and bilateral correspondence between brain regions, then incorporates these relationships into a probabilistic model designed to sample correlated regional volume changes. These sampled variations are translated into diffeomorphic transformations, enabling substantial structural changes while preserving anatomical topology. Combined with contrast-agnostic image synthesis, BrainAug generates training images with independently varying anatomy and appearance. Evaluations across eight brain MRI datasets demonstrate stronger segmentation generalization across diverse populations, while registration experiments show improved alignment under substantial morphological differences.

title: ECLIPSE: Embedding-Centered Foundation-Model Federated Knowledge Transfer for Data-Free Edge Intelligence
authors: S. Kawa Atapour, S. Jamal Seyedmohammadi, Maryam Hosseini, S. Mohammad Sheikholeslami, Jamshid Abouei, Konstantinos Plataniotis, Arash Mohammadi
abstract: Foundation Models (FMs) are envisioned to become an integral component of intelligent federated edge networks because of their strong representation and generalization capabilities. However, their integration into resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive edge environments remains challenging. This challenge is particularly pronounced in data-free settings, where no shared, public, or server-accessible reference dataset is available to establish a common reference space for aligning distributed knowledge. To address this challenge, we propose ECLIPSE, which is an embedding-centered FM-based federated knowledge transfer framework developed for data-free edge intelligence. ECLIPSE enables edge intelligence capitalizing on a server-hosted FM without sharing raw data, local models, or a public reference dataset. It establishes a shared embedding reference space through which edge devices encode their local task knowledge. Only the resulting embeddings are transmitted to the server for alignment and aggregation. Using the aggregated embeddings, the server constructs a task-aware surrogate dataset through an embedding-guided generative process. This surrogate dataset is then used to adapt the server-hosted FM to the downstream task. The adapted FM is subsequently distilled into a lightweight global model and distributed to the edge devices.
