Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configuration, and analyze performance and interaction trajectories across models and tasks. Adaptive observation yields substantial gains on fine-grained action understanding, with benefits also extending to Video-MME-v2. Even under the same observation interface, gains differ substantially across models; interaction traces reveal corresponding differences in evidence seeking and the reliability of answer revision. The benefits also vary across tasks for the same model, ranging from substantial improvements to limited gains and regressions. Together, these findings support an account in which harness effectiveness depends on the alignment between opportunities for informative observation and the model's ability to turn interaction into reliable revisions. They motivate video harnesses that coordinate perception and reasoning, matching observational autonomy to task demands and model capabilities.

title: topAC99: A compact MATLAB implementation of filter-free Allen--Cahn topology optimization with matrix-free field transfer
authors: Run Du
abstract: This paper presents topAC99, a self-contained, toolbox-free 99-line MATLAB kernel for filter-free Allen--Cahn topology optimization via the Augmented Lagrangian method on structured quadrilateral meshes. The software architecture combines three compact numerical components: (i) a lumped nodal discretization with a 7-line Kronecker-sum 5-point Laplacian that enforces homogeneous Neumann conditions at width-invariant sparse memory cost; (ii) matrix-free node-to-element averaging and adjoint backpropagation via two-dimensional convolutions (conv2); and (iii) an inlined 18-line 1D-dual bisection Method of Moving Asymptotes (MMA) solver for signed sensitivities. Benchmarks from 60x40 to 300x200 meshes (121,002 degrees of freedom) against convolution- and PDE-filtered SIMP baselines show that Allen--Cahn residual and adjoint evaluations add only 0.7%--1.2% per-step overhead while converging in 78--92 iterations on fine grids. Minimal-line extensions to a symmetric force inverter compliant mechanism and a passive-deck highway arch bridge further demonstrate the versatility of the 99-line kernel.

title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
authors: Shanmuga Venkatachalam, Quinn Jacobson, John Paul Shen
abstract: Spiking neural networks for multimodal audio-visual classification reach high accuracy by adopting deep-learning machinery: multi-stage convolutional or transformer encoders trained end-to-end with surrogate-gradient backpropagation through time. These prior works typically rely on full-precision (32-bit) parameters and do not treat hardware efficiency as a primary design objective. In this paper, we propose NeuTNN-AV, a much simpler hardware-amenable multimodal substrate built on the recently proposed NeuroAI Temporal Neural Network (NeuTNN) and demonstrate that it can match or outperform state-of-the-art SNN baselines with a fraction of their synapse counts. NeuTNN neurons carry multiple active dendritic segments. Each input line spikes at most once (temporal coding) and every weight is learned via a local reward-modulated spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP) rule. All weights are 4-bit integers and inference uses only comparisons and additions. On CREMA-D, it reaches 78.6% with 2.34M synapses establishing a new state-of-the-art SNN accuracy, against 77.14% for MISNet-XL (31M parameters). On UrbanSound8K-AV, NeuTNN reaches 98.82% with 1.38M synapses, against 96.85% for SMMT (9.99M parameters) and 98.96% for MISNet-XL (31M parameters). Weight memory is 23-106x smaller than the spiking baselines, and the measured synaptic energy per inference is two to three orders of magnitude lower. Furthermore, the proposed NeuTNN learns CREMA-D in a single pass with 73.8% accuracy and demonstrates rapid online continual learning by adapting to unseen actors from a few dozen clips.

title: Barrier-Based Safety Filtering for Quadrotor Flight in Cluttered Environments Under Acceleration Limits
authors: Andi Rahmadiansah
abstract: Accurate trajectory tracking alone does not guarantee safe quadrotor flight when the reference passes near obstacles or the available control authority is limited. This paper presents a safety-filtered trajectory-tracking framework for a quadrotor operating at a fixed altitude in obstacle-cluttered environments. A nominal tracking controller is combined with high-order control barrier constraints and an acceleration-constrained quadratic program. The safety filter preserves the nominal acceleration whenever it is admissible and modifies it only when the prescribed obstacle clearance is threatened. The analysis establishes nominal exponential tracking, forward invariance of the safe region under compatible initial conditions and continued quadratic-program feasibility, and bounded tracking error during safety intervention. Numerical experiments using an idealized planar translational model with single and multiple stationary circular obstacles show minimum clearances of $0.000$--$0.001$~m under the safety filter, compared with $-1.594/-1.421$~m under nominal control. Tracking RMSE increases from $0.618$ to $0.950$~m across reference-speed scales $0.6$--$1.6$, illustrating the effect of reference speed on tracking accuracy under safety constraints. Additional tests examine how acceleration limits affect control effort and feasibility. These findings inform safety-filter design for UAV trajectory tracking under limited control authority.

title: Toward Database-Native Genomics: A Vision for Declarative Genomic Analysis
authors: Dhruv Aron, Danial Saleem, James Christopher Sorenson III, Xiangyao Yu
abstract: In recent years, numerous advancements in relational database management systems (RDBMS), including cloud-native and GPU-native paradigms, have resulted in highly competitive RDBMS performance for analytical workloads. At the same time, the field of genomics has evolved into a data-intensive domain owing to the advent of next-generation sequencing; however, current genomic analysis workflows are often file-based, fragmented, and reliant on disparate tools, limiting their expressiveness, usability, performance, and scalability. This work argues for an incremental adoption of RDBMS and declarative SQL querying in genomic analysis, particularly tertiary analysis. By translating common tasks from widely-used tools like SAMtools and BEDtools into SQL queries executed in DuckDB, we demonstrate that off-the-shelf RDBMS can match or exceed the performance of existing tools while offering significant improvements in expressiveness and usability. We identify current limitations and propose practical paths forward, aiming to position relational databases as a foundational platform for modern bioinformatics workflows.

title: Open-OmniCoach: Evidence-Enhanced Trajectory Learning for Omni Video Agents
authors: Weisong Liu, Xiangtai Li, Haochen Wang, Haiquan Wen, Zhaoxiang Zhang
abstract: Training capable omni video agents requires more than diverse question-answer pairs: agents must learn to reliably find, connect, and correct task-relevant evidence in omni-setting. However, we argue that existing data pipelines provide limited control over task-relevant evidence and weak supervision for these capabilities. In this work, we present Open OmniCoach, a new framework for evidence-seeking omni video agents. It contains a high-quality dataset, OmniCoach-240K, and a new agentic reinforcement learning (RL) method, Step-Level Evidence-Guided Policy Optimization (SEPO). For the former, OmniCoach-240K comprises 248.2K interaction trajectories, including 230.7K multi-span trajectories and 17.4K reflection trajectories. We design a three-stage data pipeline by leveraging both fine-grained omni-evidence and the agent's own errors. Meanwhile, compared with other RL baselines, SEPO provides turn-level credit based on improvements in evidence coverage and temporal localization. Applying both trajectory data and the SEPO method, we obtain Open OmniAgent models. The resulting models outperform the baselines across multiple video and audio-visual understanding tasks by significant margins, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Open OmniCoach framework. In particular, Open OmniAgent-30B improves average accuracy over Qwen3-Omni by 6.3 percentage points across nine benchmarks, with gains of 12.2 and 13.3 points on LVOmniBench and LVBench, respectively.
comment: 24 pages. Project Page: https://open-omnicoach.github.io , Code: https://github.com/Open-OmniCoach/omnicoach , Models & Data: https://huggingface.co/Open-OmniCoach

title: Cheap Memory Costs Future Compute: Co-Designing Persistent KV and GPU Execution for Efficient Streaming Video Diffusion
authors: Jian Yang, Zhizhuo Kou, Qiyuan Zhu, Han Chen, Sirui Han, Yike Guo
abstract: Block-causal video diffusion generates long videos block by block, conditioned on a persistent key-value (KV) cache. After each block is denoised, an extra noise-free ($t=0$) forward pass writes its clean KV into the cache; once distillation and speculative early exit make denoising cheap, this clean KV update dominates the runtime. Reusing stale KV shortens the update, but stale memory corrupts the conditioning of later blocks and inflates their denoising steps, so the saved compute reappears downstream. We present SAMR (Step-Aware Memory Reconstruction), a training-free method for frozen causal video DiTs that refreshes only part of the cache and reconstructs the rest without DiT forwards. Our key observation is that, once rotary position phases are removed, motion-aligned historical KV and the in-flight KV a token holds at its exit step are complementary estimates of its clean KV. SAMR debiases in-flight KV with offline-calibrated per-head affine maps in Pre-RoPE space, fuses the two estimates, and reserves true $t=0$ refreshes for tokens flagged by an attention-readout error proxy, all executed by tile-aligned, synchronization-free Triton kernels. On 48-second LongLive-1.3B videos, SAMR reduces DiT latency by 20.9% and principal FLOPs by 30.7% relative to dense KV updates, lowers downstream denoising steps, and improves final-quarter PSNR over token reuse by 1.61 dB (1.14 dB on held-out VidProM-16). The reconstruction also transfers to frozen Self-Forcing-DMD-1.3B: zero-shot, it reduces reuse-induced step inflation ($2.47 \to 2.30$ steps/token) and improves late PSNR by $+0.33$ dB, and a one-time training-free calibration recovers the diagnostic score that zero-shot transfer lowers ($89.62 \to 91.10$).

title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
authors: Zheng Sun, Zhuo Li, Zhihao Li, Hengyi Sim, Ge Wang, Ziyue Zhu, Mingkai Jia, Fei Chen
abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. Our key observation is that a single real demonstration simultaneously specifies scene geometry, defines the terminal success criterion, and serves as a physical reference trajectory for verifying world fidelity---all decoupled from the source robot's kinematics. We present {RESET}: we reconstruct a contact-rich world and derive a frozen read-only criterion from one demonstration ({R}ebuild); check that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency ({E}xamine); evolve modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence ({S}elf-improve); deploy frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls ({E}xecute); and share the verified world and criterion with unseen robots without new demonstrations ({T}ransfer). On 8 manipulation tasks, each rebuilt from one real demonstration, RESET achieves 97% average success on unseen layouts in simulation, whereas zero-shot code reaches 27%, per-task fine-tuned pi0.5 policies 31%, and Diffusion Policy 50%; injecting reconstruction defects shows that practice tolerates many reconstruction errors, that geometric errors can still stall or mislead it, and that the check flags most of them while physical randomization covers the rest. Without any target demonstrations, 3 heterogeneous robots acquire the same task skills in the shared world: a robot with similar arms copies 95% of its skill functions unchanged from the source robot, while robots with different arms and hands write their own. In real-robot experiments, the resulting programs run on 4 robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials.

title: PreWAM: Exploring the Design of Latent Future Prediction for World-Action Modeling
authors: Wan Chi, Sen Li, Zihang Cui, Chuqin Huang, Yunlong Wang, Nanshan Deng, Yanjun Huang
abstract: World-action models combine action generation with future prediction, allowing visual transitions to serve as supervision for policy learning. Our controlled study of prediction spaces shows that spatially structured semantic features support better overall generalization under visual perturbations and make motion information more readily recoverable from learned predictive representations. Building on these observations, we introduce PreWAM, a world-action model that organizes future supervision around state changes in a prediction space defined by pretrained DINO features. Specifically, Residual World Prediction jointly learns source-relative changes and their resulting future states to emphasize dynamic information while preserving future-state semantics. Temporal-Scale Prediction conditions world queries on temporal distance to capture both short-term local motion and longer-horizon state evolution. These predictive objectives jointly shape a shared vision-language backbone with action supervision during pretraining and downstream policy learning. Experiments across the LIBERO benchmark family, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic manipulation demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved generalization and robustness under diverse distribution shifts.

title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
authors: Kai Zeng, Ruichuan An, Zhen Fang, Xi Fang, Han Lyu, Moran Li, Yingchen Yu, Yifan Dai, Bohan Zeng, Quanqing Xu, Zhengzhou Zhu, Wentao Zhang
abstract: Knowledge-intensive video generation remains challenging because prompts often omit the facts, appearances, and temporal relationships required for accurate generation. While search-based workflows can retrieve missing evidence, manually designed strategies limit adaptive planning, and conventional training suffers from costly video-level feedback and coarse trajectory-level credit assignment. In this paper, we present Loupe, a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to construct evidence-grounded temporal video prompts with reference images. We further introduce Rubric-Based Credit (RBC), which leverages prompt-specific factual, visual, and temporal requirements to evaluate intermediate search and planning decisions before video rendering. Building on RBC, RBC-SFT reweights assistant-token learning by step quality, while RBC-GRPO incorporates step-level credits alongside a final planning reward, without rendering videos during RL. To address the lack of dedicated search-oriented evaluation, we construct Search-VBench, which contains 150 held-out prompts across seven categories. Experiments show that Loupe improves all four evaluation dimensions across three video generators, raising the overall score of MiniMax-H3 from 32.80 to 70.67 and outperforming an untrained search workflow. Ablation experiments show that full RBC training outperforms standard SFT followed by trajectory-level GRPO by 5.27 points. Human evaluations and results on Sci-VBench and KIVI-Bench further demonstrate improved generation quality, scientific grounding, factual precision, and helpfulness. Our project page is available at https://zengkaiya.github.io/Loupe/.

title: MIFLOW: Dynamic Recent-Behavior Priors for Reference-Calibrated Online Flow-Policy Reinforcement Learning
authors: Chenhao Wang, Haonan Ma, Wenjie Zhang, Yifan Wang, Mingbin Gao, Yuan-Ye Zhang, Wenjing Hong
abstract: Flow-based policies provide expressive action distributions for continuous-control reinforcement learning. In online actor-critic learning, off-policy value estimates can be unreliable in poorly covered action regions, where expressive policies may shift probability mass toward critic-favored actions. We propose MIFLOW, which calibrates online flow-policy learning with a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions. Inspired by canalization as a qualitative analogy for path-dependent stabilization, we use the prior as a moving density reference for value-guided policy improvement. MIFLOW uses the approximate recent-action log-density in a dimension-normalized correction to both actor updates and critic targets. This correction increases the cost of low-density actions while keeping them available. Across six MuJoCo continuous-control tasks and five random seeds, MIFLOW achieves competitive mean return curves and higher late-training mean returns than the evaluated baselines on several tasks. In a Walker2d-v4 case study, MIFLOW shows a lower proportion of actions assigned low density by the learned reference, both overall and among high-Q actions. Prior-family and prior-buffer comparisons show task-dependent differences in returns and prior-defined diagnostics. These results support dynamic recent-behavior priors for reference calibration in the evaluated settings. The diagnostics measure how sampled actions align with the learned reference. True action support and critic extrapolation error remain unmeasured in these experiments.
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the 2026 IEEE 38th International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI)

title: Beyond Average Gains: Probing the Equity--Vulnerability Tension in Structured Visual AI for Learning
authors: Mingyuan Li, Duan Wang, Erick Purwanto, Yihong Wang
abstract: Open-ended conversational AI requires learners to formulate questions, organize learning paths, and track changing problem states. Structured visual interfaces may ease these demands, but higher average ratings do not establish that support is experienced consistently across learner backgrounds and devices. We conducted a randomized study of graph-algorithm learning, comparing VisualCodeChat (VCC), which combines predefined learning stages, conversational explanations, and dynamic algorithm visualizations, with a standard text-based chatbot. We analyzed 282 post-task questionnaires from university students. In unadjusted comparisons, VCC received significantly higher usability and perceived effectiveness ratings. We detected no significant between-condition differences in efficiency, satisfaction, or post-use emotion. Exploratory within-condition analyses identified differences associated with prior chatbot experience: infrequent users reported lower adoption and learning-management ratings in the standard AI condition, while uncomfortable prior chatbot experiences were associated with lower interaction and layout ratings in the VCC condition. These findings suggest that improving the average interaction experience is only part of making AI-supported learning inclusive. Future evaluations should examine whether learners with different prior experiences can obtain guidance, recover from difficulties, and demonstrate understanding independently across devices.

title: Beyond Expert Replay: Cross-Instruction Anchoring for Continual Vision-Language-Action Learning
authors: Ziyang Chen, Dehua Chen, Shaoguang Wang, Xu Yan, Hao Huang, Tao Chen
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models need to continually acquire new manipulation skills while retaining the ability to follow previously learned instructions. Experience replay (ER) can mitigate catastrophic forgetting, but retaining only a small number of historical expert frames per task leaves many old-instruction responses without direct supervision. Under limited replay, we observe a structured failure mode in which an earlier instruction can trigger a subsequently learned, competing goal. To address this gap, we propose Cross-Instruction Anchoring (XIA), which supplements expert replay with instruction-conditioned response preservation. At each task boundary, XIA freezes the previous policy as a teacher and matches its responses to old instructions paired with current observations. This extends supervision beyond stored historical examples without requiring additional expert replay data. Experiments across multiple VLA architectures and three LIBERO suites demonstrate improved success rates and reduced forgetting compared with ER under identical historical expert-data budgets. Additional RoboCasa and real-world experiments further support the effectiveness of XIA.
comment: 19 pages, 12 figures, 10 tables, including supplementary material

title: OrangeTree: A Linear and Tree-based Time Series Forecasting Model Supporting Multiple Input and Output Lengths
authors: Yiqi Tang, Zhichen Lai, Yuxuan Yang, Dalin Zhang, Jinpeng Chen, Gang Chen, Huan Li
abstract: Time series forecasting (TSF) models suffer from a critical rigidity: the inability to handle Multiple Input and Output Lengths (MIOL) within a single architecture. Current workarounds, such as padding or autoregression, often incur computational redundancy or suffer from error accumulation. We propose OrangeTree, a linear and tree-based architecture that decouples model parameters from sequence lengths. It employs a Segment Tree Encoder and an Inverse Tree Decoder to translate multi-length input history into multi-length output predictions within a unified framework. Crucially, a Range Weighter and a Feature Fuser bridge these components, dynamically selecting and fusing relevant ranges into optimal contexts for forecasting. Experiments on six benchmarks confirm OrangeTree achieves the SOTA performance. In MIOL settings, it matches the accuracy of length-fixed models without substantial accuracy degradation or a substantial increase in inference latency typical of heuristic methods. Code is available at https://github.com/Tang-Yiqi/OrangeTree.

title: TQ-HQNet: A Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for Cross-Domain Learning on Heterogeneous Data
authors: Abdur Rasool, Saba Aslam, Hui Chen, Chayut Bunterngchit
abstract: Hybrid quantum neural networks are a promising direction for noisy intermediate-scale quantum computing, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by poor trainability, rigid circuit design, and weak robustness across heterogeneous real-world tasks. This paper proposes TQ-HQNet, a Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for cross-domain learning on heterogeneous data. The proposed framework combines three mechanisms: 1) adaptive latent compression to map domain-specific features into qubit-compatible representations, 2) trainability-aware search over compact variational circuit candidates, and 3) hybrid fusion of multiple shallow quantum experts to improve robustness without increasing qubit cost excessively. TQ-HQNet is evaluated on four public datasets spanning neurological screening, phishing detection, financial direction prediction, and DNA sequence classification. Across all domains, the proposed model consistently improves over a fixed hybrid quantum baseline, with balanced-accuracy gains of +0.280, +0.170, +0.071, and +0.060, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm that gains arise from trainability-aware compact circuit selection and expert fusion, not circuit scaling. Although classical baselines outperform on some tasks, fixed-split results show consistent improvements over the fixed hybrid reference. These analyses support the practical role of compact selection and fusion, with repeated-split and hardware-aware studies left for future work.

title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
authors: Ruixiao Shi, Fu Feng, Yucheng Xie, Jing Wang, Xin Geng
abstract: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

title: ReJEPA: Bounded Predictive Regulation for Latent World Models
authors: Fangzhou Lin, Yuping Wang, Shuo Xing, Yang Chen, Yuwen Heng, Xin Li, Wenbin He, Yuhan Yao, Zhengzhong Tu, Liu Ren
abstract:
Latent world models learn representations by predicting future states in an abstract embedding space rather than reconstructing raw pixels. When training across multi-frame sequences, however, not all frames and spatial regions are equally informative or predictable. We argue that forcing a world model to minimize every prediction error may be unnecessary and harmful. Under standard $L_2$ loss, unbounded gradients force the encoder and predictor to overfit noisy or transient frames at the expense of core physical structure, while amplifying gradient conflict with representation regularizers. Conversely, $L_1$ loss bounds large gradients, but its constant gradient magnitude near zero disrupts the local smoothness required for planning. We resolve this tension with \textbf{ReJEPA}, a bounded predictive regulation principle that combines bounded gradients for large errors with smooth quadratic behavior near zero, instantiated simply via the element-wise $\log\cosh$ loss.
  As a drop-in training replacement across Temporal Straightening, LeWorldModel, and V-JEPA~2.1, $\log\cosh$ consistently outperforms $L_2$, a curvature-matched quadratic control, $L_1$, and Smooth-$L_1$ baselines without altering architectures or inference procedures. Notably, the gains grow with environmental complexity, scaling from simple navigation to contact-rich manipulation and real-world autonomous driving on NAVSIM. Probing and geometric analyses confirm that relaxing the penalty on extreme errors yields representations that better capture physical states and align with the true planning cost landscape.

title: HiGS: A Hierarchical Architecture for Fast Differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting
authors: Dawid Pająk, Martin Bisson, Rodolfo Lima, François Trudel
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) makes one screen tile the cell of partitioning, the cell of rasterization, and the unit of parallel work. Partitioning favors large tiles and rasterization small ones, and with one unit per tile the densest tiles set the frame time. We present Hierarchically Tiled Gaussian Splatting (HiGS), a unified architecture for rendering and reconstruction that gives each role its own granularity: Gaussians are partitioned over coarse macro-tiles, rasterized over the fine render tiles within them, and processed in bounded depth-sorted batches. A dense region issues more batches instead of one longer unit, so frame time follows the work in a view rather than its densest tile. The same batches carry reconstruction: compositing supplies the transmittance and color needed to differentiate each one independently, leaving optimizer memory traffic as the dominant training cost. We fuse the optimizer into the backward pass, halve the parameters and moments it stores and updates directly, and defer appearance updates outside the view. HiGS renders scenes faster than every published method we evaluate, by the widest margin on views with uneven load, and reconstructs them faster and in less memory, at equal image quality and with exact front-to-back alpha compositing.

title: Meta-Amortized Cognitive Modeling
authors: Jerry M. Huang, Lukas Schumacher, Niek Stevenson, Mischa von Krause, Stefan T. Radev
abstract: Cognitive modeling is highly iterative. Researchers repeatedly revise model structures, parameterizations, covariates, and experimental designs as theories evolve and data accumulates. Amortized Bayesian inference with neural networks provides rapid estimation for individual models, but every revision requires new simulations and training. Here, we introduce CogFormerV2, a meta-amortized framework that enables researchers to specify, revise, and fit cognitive models with a single network, carrying amortization across an entire space of models all at once. Trained once in about a day on a single GPU, it delivers accurate, well-calibrated posteriors across more than 14.6 billion model configurations spanning binary, multi-alternative, and continuous decisions, with varying parameter sets, covariate structures, trial counts, and contamination levels. It can fit empirical data from distinct behavioral tasks and extends to new models through continual learning and representation transfer. Released as an open-source interactive application, CogFormerV2 provides a reusable infrastructure for meta-amortized inference in cognitive modeling, while carrying the potential to accelerate computational modeling workflows at large.
translation: 认知建模是高度迭代的。随着理论的发展和数据的积累，研究人员反复修改模型结构、参数化、协变量和实验设计。使用神经网络的摊销贝叶斯推断为单个模型提供了快速估计，但每次修订都需要新的模拟和训练。在此，我们引入了CogFormerV2，一个元摊销框架，使研究人员能够用一个单一的网络指定、修订和拟合认知模型，一次性在整个模型空间中进行摊销。它在单个GPU上训练约一天后，能在超过146亿种模型配置上提供准确、校准良好的后验估计，涵盖二元、多选和连续决策，具有不同的参数集、协变量结构、试验计数和污染水平。它能拟合来自不同行为任务的经验数据，并通过持续学习和表示迁移扩展到新模型。CogFormerV2作为一个开源交互式应用程序发布，为认知建模中的元摊销推断提供了一个可重用的基础设施，同时有潜力加速大规模的计算建模工作流程。
tldr: CogFormerV2是一个元摊销框架，通过一个单一网络实现了认知模型的快速指定、修订和拟合，解决了传统摊销贝叶斯推理每次模型修改都需要重新模拟和训练的问题。
ai_comments: CogFormerV2的创新之处在于提出了“元摊销”的概念，将摊销推理的能力从单个模型扩展到整个模型空间，极大地提高了认知建模的效率和灵活性。其能够处理数十亿种模型配置的能力，以及对新模型的适应性，预示着计算建模工作流程的重大加速。作为一个开源工具，它有望对认知科学和计算建模领域产生广泛影响。
motivation: 认知建模是一个高度迭代的过程，每次模型结构、参数、协变量或实验设计的修订都需要新的模拟和训练，这使得个体模型的摊销贝叶斯推断效率低下。
method: 本文引入了CogFormerV2，一个元摊销框架。它使用一个单一的神经网络，能够一次性在整个模型空间中进行摊销，从而实现认知模型的指定、修订和拟合。
results: CogFormerV2在单GPU上训练一天后，能在超过146亿种模型配置上提供准确、校准良好的后验估计，涵盖二元、多选和连续决策，以及不同的参数集、协变量结构、试验计数和污染水平。它能拟合来自不同行为任务的经验数据，并通过持续学习和表示迁移扩展到新模型。
conclusion: CogFormerV2提供了一个可重用的元摊销推理基础设施，有望加速计算建模工作流程，使研究人员能够在一个单一网络中指定、修订和拟合认知模型。

title: Rethinking Universal Time Series Foundation Models from Unified Representations to Shared Dynamics (UniTFU)
authors: Shuxin Li, Yingjie Zhou, Le Zhang, Jingyuan Xia, Shengxi Li, Ce Zhu, Anderson Rocha
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) have attracted increasing attention in cross-domain forecasting. Existing works mainly rely on large-scale pre-training and general modeling paradigms. However, the former heavily relies on the diversity and domain coverage of pre-training data. Meanwhile, the latter learns unified representations across heterogeneous domains without explicitly identifying the temporal regularities shared among them, limiting robust cross-domain generalization. This work explores cross-domain generalization by characterizing commonalities in recurring local dynamics across domains, rather than relying solely on implicitly learned temporal representations. To capture such cross-domain commonalities, we propose Time Series Foundation Units (TFUs) as reusable building blocks discovered from multi-scale temporal segments, each characterizing a recurring local dynamic pattern shared across domains. Building on TFUs, we develop a unified time series foundation model (UniTFU) that explicitly reuses and composes shared temporal regularities across domains for forecasting. Experiments on seven public datasets show that UniTFU substantially outperforms existing TSFMs in cross-domain forecasting and can efficiently adapt to target-domain dynamics by updating its reusable components with limited target data. UniTFU also achieves strong forecasting performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.
zh_title: 从统一表示到共享动态：重新思考通用时间序列基础模型 (UniTFU)
translation: 时间序列基础模型（TSFMs）在跨域预测中受到了越来越多的关注。现有工作主要依赖大规模预训练和通用建模范式。然而，前者严重依赖预训练数据的多样性和域覆盖范围；同时，后者在异构域之间学习统一表示，而没有显式识别它们之间共享的时间规律，从而限制了强大的跨域泛化能力。本工作通过表征跨域循环局部动态中的共性来探索跨域泛化，而不是仅仅依赖隐式学习的时间表示。为了捕捉这种跨域共性，我们提出了时间序列基础单元（TFUs），作为从多尺度时间片段中发现的可复用构建块，每一个单元都表征跨域共享的循环局部动态模式。基于TFUs，我们开发了一个统一的时间序列基础模型（UniTFU），它显式地复用和组合跨域共享的时间规律来进行预测。在七个公共数据集上的实验表明，UniTFU在跨域预测方面大大优于现有的TSFMs，并且可以通过用有限的目标数据更新其可复用组件，高效地适应目标域动态。与最先进的方法相比，UniTFU还取得了强大的预测性能。
tldr: 通过引入可复用的跨域共享局部动态单元（TFUs），本文提出的UniTFU模型克服了传统时间序列基础模型的局限，实现了卓越的跨域预测与高效适应。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了UniTFU，通过发现和复用跨域共享的局部动态模式（TFUs），克服了传统时间序列基础模型过度依赖隐式统一表示和大规模预训练数据的局限性，在跨域预测和少样本适应方面展现出色的性能和高效性。
motivation: 现有的时间序列基础模型主要依赖大规模预训练以及在异构域间学习隐式统一表示，但忽视了显式识别跨域共享的时间规律，导致鲁棒的跨域泛化能力受限。
method: 提出了时间序列基础单元（TFUs）作为从多尺度时间片段中发现的、可复用的构建块，用于表征跨域共享的局部动态模式，并据此开发了统一的时间序列基础模型（UniTFU）进行显式的规律复用和组合预测。
results: 在七个公共数据集上的实验表明，UniTFU在跨域预测方面显著优于现有的时间序列基础模型，且仅需少量目标数据更新可复用组件即可高效适应目标域动态，表现出与最先进方法相比极强的预测性能。
conclusion: UniTFU通过显式建模跨域共享的局部时间动态，有效提升了时间序列基础模型的跨域泛化能力和少样本适应效率，为设计更具解释性和鲁棒性的TSFMs提供了新的范式。

title: DUALingo: A Dual-Hand Instruction-Guided Dataset for Affordance Grounding on 3D Objects
authors: Ming-Lun Lee, Yi-En Li, Feng-Dian Su, Ming-Han Lee, Kun-Ru Wu, Krzysztof Czarnecki, Yu-Chee Tseng
abstract: Affordance grounding localizes where an agent should interact with an object to perform a task. Many everyday manipulation tasks, however, require bimanual affordance, in which two hands assume complementary and cooperative roles to accomplish a shared goal. Existing 3D affordance datasets primarily ground single interaction regions, and manually annotating dual-hand, cooperative contacts does not scale. To address this gap, we introduce DUALingo, a large-scale dataset for task-conditioned, role-aware bimanual 3D affordance grounding on diverse everyday objects. DUALingo represents each task as two cooperative, hand-agnostic roles, each grounded as a heatmap on the object surface. It contains 271K free-form tasks on 71K objects, generated by a fully automated pipeline of open-weight foundation models without human labeling. Expert ratings and a validated LLM judge confirm the quality of the resulting annotations. Trained on DUALingo, existing 3D affordance models learn to ground both cooperative roles from natural-language instructions, with the best-performing model achieving a more than threefold improvement in aIoU over the zero-shot baseline, from 10.3 to 37.8. Robotic manipulation demonstrations illustrate the actionability of the predicted bimanual affordances in performing cooperative tasks. These results position DUALingo as a scalable foundation for learning everyday bimanual affordances. Project page: https://nycu-pair-labs.github.io/DUALingo/
zh_title: DUALingo：用于3D物体可供性定位的双手指令引导数据集
translation: 可供性定位确定了智能体在执行任务时应与物体交互的位置。然而，许多日常操作任务需要双手可供性，即两只手承担互补和合作的角色来完成共同的目标。现有的3D可供性数据集主要定位单一交互区域，且手动标注双手合作接触点无法扩展。为了填补这一空白，我们推出了DUALingo，这是一个用于在各种日常物体上进行任务条件化、角色感知的双曼式（bimanual）3D可供性定位的大规模数据集。DUALingo将每个任务表示为两个协同的、与手无关的角色，每个角色在物体表面上都被定位为一个热图。它包含在71K个物体上的271K个自由形式任务，由开源基础模型的全自动管道生成，无需人工标注。专家评分和经过验证的LLM评判证实了所得标注的质量。在DUALingo上训练后，现有的3D可供性模型学会了根据自然语言指令定位两个协同角色，表现最好的模型在aIoU上的表现比零样本基线提高了三倍以上，从10.3提高到37.8。机器人操作演示说明了预测的双曼式可供性在执行协同任务时的可操作性。这些结果将DUALingo定位为学习日常双手可供性的可扩展基础。
tldr: 本文推出了DUALingo——一个大规模、全自动生成的双手协同3D可供性数据集，显著提升了机器人根据语言指令进行双臂协同操作的能力。
ai_comments: DUALingo通过完全自动化的流程构建了一个大规模的双手协同3D可供性数据集，解决了以往数据集难以扩展且局限于单手操作的痛点，对双臂机器人操作的发展具有重要推动作用。
motivation: 现有的3D可供性数据集主要局限于单手交互区域，而许多日常操作任务需要双手协同（双臂配合），手动标注双人合作接触点成本高且难以扩展，因此需要一个大规模的、任务条件化的、角色感知的双手3D可供性数据集。
method: 提出了一种完全自动化的流程，利用开源基础模型生成271K个自由形式的任务和71K个对象的可供性标注，无需人工标注，并将其表示为对象表面上的两个协同、与手无关的角色热图。
results: 在DUALingo上训练后，现有的3D可供性模型能够根据自然语言指令准确 grounding 双手协同角色，表现最好的模型在aIoU指标上比零样本基线提升了三倍以上（从10.3提高到37.8），并且在机器人双臂协同操作演示中验证了预测可供性的实际可行性。
conclusion: DUALingo通过自动化流程成功构建了一个大规模的双手协同3D可供性数据集，显著提升了现有3D可供性模型在自然语言指令下的双角色定位能力，并在机器人操作中验证了其有效性。

title: Decompose, Verify, Evolve: Physically Grounded Shape Decomposition
authors: Wenchao Ma, Rui Yu, Fan Zhu, Jiachen Liu, Sharon X. Huang
abstract: Shape decomposition represents 3D objects as a compact set of geometric primitives for interpretable modeling and simulation. However, existing decomposition methods are trained primarily for geometric fidelity, without explicit constraints on physical plausibility, and can therefore produce disconnected parts or physically unstable reconstructions. We present PhysDec, an agentic framework that draws on a pretrained vision-language model's semantic understanding and commonsense reasoning to predict material-aware primitive decompositions from a few images. Within this framework, PhysDec-Loop is an agentic pipeline that reasons about part structure and materials, using a reference 3D point cloud for geometric feedback and physical verifiers to guide iterative refinement. Through self-evolution, we further develop another agentic pipeline, PhysDec-Evolved, which learns from prior corrections to predict primitive decompositions from images without point-cloud feedback or a correction loop at inference. Experiments show that PhysDec-Loop improves geometric fidelity, physical plausibility and visual quality over geometry-focused baselines, while PhysDec-Evolved approaches its performance at substantially lower inference cost.
zh_title: 分解、验证、演化：物理基础的形状分解
translation: 形状分解将3D对象表示为一组紧凑的几何原语，以实现可解释的建模和仿真。然而，现有的分解方法主要针对几何保真度进行训练，没有明确的物理合理性约束，因此可能产生不连贯的部分或物理不稳定的重建。我们提出了PhysDec，一个基于代理的框架，利用预训练的视觉语言模型的语义理解和常识推理能力，从几张图像中预测出考虑材料的原始分解。在该框架内，PhysDec-Loop是一个基于代理的流程，通过参考3D点云进行几何反馈和使用物理验证器来指导迭代细化，从而推理部件结构和材料。通过自我演化，我们进一步开发了另一个基于代理的流程PhysDec-Evolved，它从先前的校正中学习，无需在推理时进行点云反馈或校正循环即可预测原始分解。实验表明，与仅关注几何的方法相比，PhysDec-Loop在几何保真度、物理合理性和视觉质量方面有所提升，而PhysDec-Evolved的性能接近于它，但推理成本却大大降低。
tldr: 本研究提出了PhysDec框架，通过结合视觉语言模型和物理验证，实现了对3D物体进行物理可信的形状分解，并提出了两种方法：PhysDec-Loop（迭代优化）和PhysDec-Evolved（无需反馈的预测），后者在保证性能的同时降低了推理成本。
ai_comments: 该研究解决了现有形状分解方法在物理合理性方面的不足，提出了一种新颖的结合了视觉语言模型和物理验证的框架。PhysDec-Loop的迭代优化和PhysDec-Evolved的自我演化两种策略的提出，为形状分解任务提供了更灵活和高效的解决方案。特别地，PhysDec-Evolved在降低推理成本方面的优势使其在实际应用中具有更大的潜力。然而，该方法对输入图像的数量和质量可能存在依赖性，以及其在处理复杂拓扑结构物体时的泛化能力仍有待进一步验证。
motivation: 现有形状分解方法主要关注几何保真度，缺乏物理合理性约束，可能导致分解结果不连贯或物理不稳定。
method: 提出PhysDec框架，利用预训练的视觉语言模型进行语义理解和常识推理，从图像预测材料感知的原始形状分解。PhysDec-Loop是一个迭代细化流程，结合了3D点云的几何反馈和物理验证器。PhysDec-Evolved则通过自我演化，无需点云反馈或校正循环即可进行预测。
results: PhysDec-Loop在几何保真度、物理合理性和视觉质量方面优于仅关注几何的方法。PhysDec-Evolved的性能接近PhysDec-Loop，但推理成本显著降低。
conclusion: PhysDec框架能够实现物理基础的形状分解，并且通过迭代优化和自我演化，能够生成更优的分解结果，同时降低了推理成本。

title: Learning When a Robot Should Ask For Help: Adaptive Intervention Requests in Human-Robot Teaming
authors: Yanran Jiang, Cécile Paris, Dana Kulić, Leimin Tian
abstract: Robots operating in complex environments occasionally encounter situations where autonomous navigation fails. Requesting and receiving a timely intervention from their human supervisor can be critical for failure prevention or recovery. However, requesting help too frequently or at inappropriate times can increase operator workload and reduce team efficiency, while delayed requests may lead to prolonged downtime or unrecoverable failures. In addition to alert timing, the human, robot and task context also influences the intervention outcomes. This paper proposes an algorithm for learning to generate adaptive human intervention requests during human-robot teaming. A help-seeking policy is trained via offline reinforcement learning based on past intervention helpfulness and autonomous progress. This learned alert policy enables a robot to selectively request human help when the intervention outcome is likely to be beneficial. We evaluate the proposed policy in different task environments and user expertise levels in simulation, followed by evaluation in a physical user study. Our findings demonstrate that the learned policy improves exploration efficiency, reduces unnecessary alerts, and enhances novice user support without compromising expert performance in real-time human-robot teaming missions.

title: TANDEM: Temporal Anchor Densification With Reliability-Aware Memory for Lightweight Sparse Depth Completion in Endoscopic Robotic Navigation
authors: Weikuan Qiu, Jiale Hou, Chongzhao Xu, Jinlian Ma
abstract: For endoscopic robotic surgery, accurate dense depth perception serves as a foundational capability, which enables navigation, instrument localization, and tissue interaction. However, endoscopic video lacks reliable metric depth, while metric measurements obtained via tracking, time-of-flight sensing, or instrument contact only cover a small fraction of pixels in each frame, rendering sparse depth completion an urgent and unsolved challenge. In this work, we propose Temporal Anchor Densification with Reliability-Aware Memory (TANDEM), a causal sparse depth completion framework for endoscopic video. It adopts a lightweight design and leverages the video stream: past measurements re-projected into the current view recover the metric evidence unavailable within a single sparse frame. To keep this evidence interpretable, accurate, and efficient, an explicit memory scores each re-projected measurement with analytic re-observation, age, and motion-parallax factors without overriding current measurements. A compact network then reconstructs depth via reliability-weighted gradient integration and a frequency-gated reference prior. We evaluate TANDEM on the C3VD colonoscopy and StereoMIS laparoscopy datasets. With only 5.58 M parameters, TANDEM reduces the root mean square error by 11.7% and 32.0%, respectively, compared with the strongest baseline, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy. It also remains accurate under pose errors of the magnitude reported for endoscopic pose estimation. Code will be released at https://github.com/Wk-cpu-art/TANDEM upon acceptance.
comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, 2026. 11 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables
zh_title: TANDEM：面向内窥镜机器人导航中轻量级稀疏深度补全的带可靠性感知记忆的时序锚点致密化方法
translation: 对于内窥镜机器人手术来说，精确的密集深度感知是一项基础能力，它能够实现导航、器械定位和组织交互。然而，内窥镜视频缺乏可靠的度量深度，而通过追踪、飞行时间传感或器械接触获得的度量测量只能覆盖每一帧中极小一部分像素，这使得稀疏深度补全成为一个紧迫且尚未解决的挑战。在这项工作中，我们提出了TANDEM（Temporal Anchor Densification with Reliability-Aware Memory），这是一个针对内窥镜视频的因果稀疏深度补全框架。它采用轻量级设计并利用视频流：重新投影到当前视图的过去测量结果可以恢复在单个稀疏帧中无法获取的度量证据。为了保持这些证据的可解释性、准确性和高效性，显式记忆通过解析重观察、年龄和运动视差因子对每个重新投影的测量进行评分，而不会覆盖当前的测量。随后，一个紧凑的网络通过可靠性加权梯度积分和频率门控参考先验来重建深度。我们在C3VD结肠镜和StereoMIS腹腔镜数据集上对TANDEM进行了评估。在仅有5.58M参数的情况下，与最强的基线相比，TANDEM的均方根误差分别降低了11.7%和32.0%，并达到了最新的最优（SOTA）准确率。在内窥镜位姿估计报告幅度的位姿误差下，它依然保持准确。代码将在接收后于 https://github.com/Wk-cpu-art/TANDEM 发布。
tldr: 提出了一种名为TANDEM的轻量级、基于时序记忆的稀疏深度补全框架，有效解决了内窥镜机器人导航中深度感知稀疏且不可靠的难题。
ai_comments: 该论文针对内窥镜机器人手术中稀疏深度补全这一具有挑战性的任务，提出了TANDEM框架。其核心创新在于设计了带可靠性感知记忆的时序锚点致密化方法，通过显式记忆对历史测量值进行多维度评分，并结合轻量级网络实现了高精度的深度重建。模型参数量小且对位姿误差具有鲁棒性，在公开数据集上取得了显着的性能提升，展现出极高的临床应用潜力。
motivation: 内窥镜视频缺乏可靠的度量深度，而通过追踪、飞行时间传感或器械接触获取的度量测量只能覆盖每个帧的一小部分像素，因此轻量级稀疏深度补全在内窥镜机器人导航中是一个 urgent 且未解决的挑战。
method: 提出TANDEM因果稀疏深度补全框架，利用视频流将过去重新投影的测量值与当前视图结合；采用显式记忆基于解析重观测、年龄和运动视差因子对重新投影的测量进行评分；通过紧凑的深度重建网络利用可靠性加权梯度积分和频率门控参考先验进行深度重建。
results: 在C3VD结肠镜和StereoMIS腹腔镜数据集上，TANDEM在仅有5.58M参数的情况下，相比最强的基线模型，均方根误差（RMSE）分别降低了11.7%和32.0%，达到了SOTA精度，并且在内窥镜位姿估计误差下依然保持准确。
conclusion: TANDEM是一个高效、轻量且具备强鲁棒性的内窥镜视频因果稀疏深度补全框架，通过结合可靠性感知记忆和轻量化网络，在多个数据集上实现了SOTA的准确性，对内窥镜机器人导航具有重要意义。

title: Symmetry-reduced High-index Saddle Dynamics for Saddle Point Search under Continuous Symmetries
authors: Yuanshen Lin, Jianyuan Yin, Lei Zhang
abstract: For energy invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points may form critical manifolds, leading to degeneracy of the Hessian. In such cases, the ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) may include symmetry directions, making it difficult to locate saddle points of a prescribed Morse index. To address this issue, we propose symmetry-reduced HiSD (SR-HiSD) by formulating the quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lifting the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space. Under suitable regularity and Morse--Bott assumptions, we establish local exponential stability of the quotient HiSD equilibria associated with the prescribed index and instability of equilibria associated with critical points of different indices. We further prove local convergence of the SR-HiSD position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit. Numerical algorithms with direction updates restricted to the horizontal space are developed. Numerical experiments on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau--Brazovskii model demonstrate reliable searches for saddle points of the prescribed index and the construction of solution landscapes, together with improved computational efficiency in large-scale problems.

title: Shuttle: Dependency-Attributed Workflow Evolution for Smart Contract Auditing
authors: Yue Xue, Yi Rong, Ziqiao Kong, Ronghui Gu, Dan She, Yuannan Yang, Zhiju Yang, Yuqiang Sun
abstract: In LLM-based smart contract auditing, detection quality depends on both model capability and workflow design. While coding agents can revise workflows from execution feedback, unconstrained rewrites rarely yield stable gains. Cross-function vulnerabilities require multi-step state tracking and boundary reasoning that coarse pipelines miss. End-to-end outcomes hide which step lost a clue, so direct rewrites regress existing hits or discard valid edits under coarse aggregate scoring. Repeatedly iterating on a small project set also adds case-specific heuristics that bloat prompts and hurt generalization. We present Shuttle, a constrained workflow-evolution system, and LucidScan, the auditing framework it evolves. Shuttle centers on provenance-graph attribution: it expands each run into an instance-level dependency graph, locates the node where a clue was lost via forward search, and traces existing hits backward into a protected set. After evaluating a merged batch, Shuttle drops dragging edits via a node-level provenance ledger, falling back to cache-reusing local re-runs only when early-round edits overlap on the same node. For localized bottlenecks, Shuttle generates edits under task decomposition, progressive refinement, and generality blind review. On 10 training projects, Shuttle evolves LucidScan from $G_0$ (28.7% per-project average C/H/M recall) to $G_8$ (82.1%). On 13 held-out validation projects under the same model, average recall rises from 28.6% ($G_0$) to 70.3% ($G_8$), above Pashov and Codex Security. In an anonymized live public audit contest with 896 researchers (Nov. 2026), the evolved scanner tied for #1 in High-severity recall (6/8, 75.0%), ranked #2 in scored H/M clusters (34/72, 47.2%) with 92.9% validity (78/84), and finished #3 overall.

title: Scoring What Matters: Exact Feedback Reduction for Language Model Comparison
authors: Hui Zhang, Haoda Yue, Bicheng Deng, Yuanchao Zhu, Jun He, Rui Qian
abstract: Comparing language-model checkpoints requires estimating performance differences, yet evaluation pipelines can pay to score responses whose contributions cancel from those differences. We introduce Contrast-Aware Feedback Acquisition (CAFA), a sampler-agnostic method that identifies which scores a requested linear report needs before acquiring feedback. CAFA groups identical scoring inputs and aggregates their report coefficients, removing queries beyond ordinary caching while preserving the fully scored result. For a fixed response bank and an otherwise unrestricted scalar scorer, we characterize necessary and sufficient query sets for exact recovery of sample means, either alone or jointly with ordinary sample covariances. On controlled updates, CAFA removes 55.8% and 90.1% of the scoring inputs remaining after caching for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, respectively, averaged over four generation repetitions. Across three online group relative policy optimization (GRPO) trajectories, Independent Star sampling with CAFA achieves 46.1-51.3% lower recorded generation-plus-feedback cost than independent autoregressive sampling with caching at a common empirical precision threshold (RMS MCSE $\leq 0.04$). This is a post hoc comparison of completed runs on a fixed budget grid. All 504 evaluated report cells reproduce the fully scored means and covariances to numerical precision. We provide a modular implementation supporting existing response banks, versioned caches and external scorers.

title: (No) Separation of Concerns: Philosophical Concerns about Agent Ethics and Implications for SE Practitioners
authors: Marc Cheong, Sebastian Baltes, Joanne Byrne, Haoyu Gao, Raula Gaikovina Kula, Sarita Rosenstock, Christoph Treude, Mansooreh Zahedi
abstract: The use of AI agents in software engineering (SE) are commonplace, with differing levels of autonomy, a myriad of capabilities, and ability to perform a variety of tasks. Philosophers have begun to examine the ethics of such agents, and SE researchers or practitioners could benefit from them; on the other hand, SE practitioners currently explore most of these concerns through the lens of principlism. We bridge this gap by reviewing the philosophical literature on AI agents indexed in PhilPapers, and translating its ethical concerns into a research agenda for SE researchers and into implications for teams that use coding agents. A systematic mapping study of PhilPapers -- a major philosophy index and open access archive -- yielded 33 peer-reviewed papers by professional philosophers published since 2023. We coded these papers thematically, with cross-disciplinary review of the emerging themes, resulting in eight themes and 85 codes. From these, we derive seven research questions for SE, covering developers' reliance on agents, responsibility for agent-written code, ethical constraints in agent configurations, and benchmark design. For practitioners, we derive five implications: decide which choices an agent must refer to a human, keep agent-written pull requests small enough to review, pair configuration-file instructions with checks, watch for changes to tests, and record who approved what. We argue that ethical concerns cannot be separated from SE concerns into a module of their own: they arise inside code review, configuration, evaluation, and requirements work, and addressing them requires cross-disciplinary work.
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, submitted for consideration to AGENT-2027

title: Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Unlearning
authors: Fangzhou Lin, Shuo Xing, Xin Li, Wenbin He, Zhengzhong Tu, Liu Ren
abstract: Large language model unlearning aims to remove the influence of designated training data while preserving unrelated model capabilities. Existing likelihood-based methods commonly optimize against fixed forget sequences, providing only negative supervision on what the model should not generate and overlooking the states visited by the evolving unlearned policy. We introduce Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation (CPSD), a new unlearning framework that constructs an explicit knowledge-reduced target distribution and distills it along the model's own trajectories. Given a student rollout, a frozen reference model evaluates each token under a plain context and a privileged context containing the forget information. CPSD treats the resulting distributional shift as a knowledge-associated direction and reverses it to obtain a counterfactual unlearning target. The student is then trained to match this target at every rollout position while retaining its utility on unrelated data. We further introduce a privacy-enhanced variant that combines distributional unlearning with lightweight sequence-level suppression. Experiments under OpenUnlearning show that CPSD improves the forgetting-utility trade-off over NPO across TOFU forget-set sizes and Llama models ranging from 1B to 8B parameters. On MUSE-News, the privacy-enhanced variant improves all reported knowledge, memorization, privacy, and utility metrics over NPO.

title: Native Block-Quantized Matrix Multiplication and Explicit K/V Residency with Dual-View Access for LLM Inference on RISC-V Vector Processors
authors: Weiying Wang, Yuanyang Xiang, Zhiwei Zhang
abstract: Some key execution states in large language model inference persist across multiple instructions and are difficult to express and exploit within RVV semantics centered on individual operations. We define specialization boundaries according to data-state lifetimes and propose Quantized Block Streams (QBS) and Attention/KV Context (AKV) while preserving RVV programmability. QBS organizes native-block format processing, block traversal, integer computation, and ordered FP32 accumulation into a unified execution process, whereas AKV maintains local K/V residency and supplies operand views aligned with the computation direction while leaving Attention arithmetic on RVV. Cycle-accurate RTL evaluation shows that QBS achieves geometric-mean speedups of 35.68x and 51.34x for projection Compute and Matmul, respectively, while AKV achieves a 1.45x geometric-mean speedup over Tiled RVV for Decode Attention. Compared with the baseline, the complete design increases total area by 12.65%; on the evaluated projection workloads, throughput per area and energy efficiency improve by 46.63x and 19.78x, respectively. Further evaluation demonstrates applicability across multiple block-quantization formats and across models with different Attention organizations.

title: CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies
authors: Jiahao Wang, Xiaoxuan Chen, Aijun Yang, Xiaohua Wang
abstract: A tool call can fail even when the operation behind it is correct, because the receiving tool parses delimiters, dates or record layouts under a configuration the agent cannot inspect. Compiling a tool-use policy for such a tool requires both calibration, which evaluates candidate calls on candidate configurations, and search over the evaluated calls. The two share one compilation budget: calibrating everything first postpones any improved policy until the end, while re-solving every partially known model delays the next useful query. A call becomes usable as soon as its effects are known on the configurations that reach it. We present CAPE, a training-free compiler built on this observation. It maintains an executable policy at all times, directs calibration to the calls that can improve this policy, and tightens bounds only where doing so ends calibration early. Returned policies preserve every configuration the initial policy completes, and CAPE certifies optimality when its executable and optimistic values meet. On CSV and JSON workflows built from 64 requests, CAPE reaches the independently computed optimum in 502 of 504 compilations while taking 22.0% less compilation time than eager exact search. On larger CSV families it returns policies with higher completion at similar compilation time, and it raises completion by 15.38 to 34.66 percentage points over an LLM that revises its serialization from error feedback.

title: Beyond the Last Loop: Reinforcement Learning with a Teacher Extrapolated from the Model Itself
authors: Linghua Zhang
abstract: Looped language models apply one shared transformer stack several times per token, and every loop can be read out through the shared language-model head. Post-training them with verifiable rewards is hard: the outcome reward carries one bit per response, spreading it over loops trains intermediate loops on tokens sampled from the last loop, and distillation needs either a teacher that ignores the reward or an external, larger model. We observe that a looped model already contains a teacher stronger than its last loop: the next-token distribution extrapolated from the first loop through the last. ELGO (Extrapolated-Loop Group-relative Optimization) adds to GRPO a dense per-token distillation term towards this distribution. The teacher is computed from an anchor copy of the model, which stays frozen and is replaced by the current model once the student's KL to the teacher falls below a threshold, so the teacher improves with the student without chasing its own extrapolation. The outcome reward splits probability between correct and incorrect responses, and the teacher decides which tokens are preferred inside a response. Between refreshes the objective is KL-regularised RL anchored at the teacher, whose optimum tilts the teacher by the reward. On Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, ELGO raises the average avg@8 over five math benchmarks from 62.32 with GRPO to 64.20 and is the best compared method on every benchmark, while spreading the reward over loops falls below the base model.
zh_title: 超越最终循环：利用自模型外推教师进行强化学习
translation: 循环语言模型（Looped language models）在每个token上多次应用同一个共享的Transformer层栈，并且每个循环都可以通过共享的语言模型头读出。使用可验证奖励对其进行后训练非常困难：结果奖励在每个响应上仅包含一个比特的信息，将其分摊到各个循环会导致中间循环基于从最后一个循环采样的token进行训练，而知识蒸馏则需要一个忽略奖励的教师模型或者外部更大模型。我们观察到，循环模型自身已经包含了一个比其最终循环更强的教师：即从第一个循环到最后一个循环外推得出的下一个token分布。ELGO（外推循环组相对优化）在GRPO的基础上，针对该分布添加了一个逐token的密集蒸馏项。教师分布由模型的锚点副本计算得出，该副本保持冻结状态，并在学生与教师的KL散度降至阈值以下时被当前模型替换，从而使教师随着学生共同提升而不会追逐自身的外推。结果奖励在正确与错误响应之间分配概率，而教师则决定响应内部更偏好哪些token。在两次刷新之间，优化目标是以教师为锚点的KL正则化强化学习，其最优解通过奖励对教师进行倾斜。在Ouro-1.4B-Thinking上，ELGO将五个数学基准的avg@8平均分从GRPO的62.32提高到64.20，并且在每个基准上都是最优的比较方法，而将奖励分摊到各循环的方法则落后于基座模型。
tldr: ELGO利用循环语言模型自身循环演进外推出的更强分布作为自蒸馏教师，并结合强化学习，显著提升了循环模型的推理性能。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地发现循环语言模型（Looped LM）内部各循环步骤演进中蕴含着超出最终循环能力的'外推'分布，并巧妙将其作为无须外部大模型的自蒸馏教师。结合强化学习与自更新锚点机制，不仅解决了稀疏奖励在循环步数上的分配难题，还实现了显著的性能增益，为循环架构模型的后训练提供了极具启发性的新范式。
motivation: 使用可验证奖励对循环语言模型进行后训练十分困难：结果奖励针对每个响应只有1比特信息，若将奖励直接分摊到中间循环会导致偏差，而传统蒸馏则需要外部大模型或忽略奖励的教师模型。
method: 提出ELGO（外推循环组相对优化）方法，在GRPO的基础上增加逐token的密集蒸馏项，目标指向从第一轮到最后一轮循环外推得出的更强token分布；该教师分布由冻结的锚点模型生成，当学生模型与教师的KL散度低于阈值时动态刷新锚点，实现学生与教师的协同进化。
results: 在Ouro-1.4B-Thinking模型上，ELGO在五个数学基准测试上的avg@8平均得分从GRPO的62.32提升至64.20，且在所有基准上均取得最优表现；相比之下，将奖励直接分摊到各循环的方法性能甚至低于基座模型。
conclusion: ELGO成功证明了利用循环模型内部外推教师提供密集蒸馏监督是可行的，能够在强化学习中显著优于传统奖励分配策略和标准GRPO基线。

title: MELODI: Similarity-Identity Decoupling for Lightweight Ranking
authors: Quoc Phong Nguyen, Vuong Le, Volodymyr Vaskovych, Julien Monteil
abstract: For latency-constrained candidate ranking, we propose a similarity-identity decoupling framework that separates target-history compatibility from target-only information. We study two orders for computing pooled similarity, similarity-then-pool and pool-then-similarity, and identify linearity of the similarity operator in its history argument, for each fixed target, as sufficient for their equivalence, justifying the cheaper pool-then-similarity form. We instantiate the framework as multi-head efficient lightweight operator for decoupling identity and similarity (MELODI), whose similarity branch combines target-conditioned multi-head history pooling with a single residual-free cross layer that is linear in its pooled-history input and whose identity branch is problem-dependent. On public benchmark datasets, MELODI matches or surpasses the evaluated target-aware and target-agnostic baselines. On two large-scale industrial datasets, its area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), normalised discounted cumulative gain (NDCG), and recall values are equal to or higher than those of the evaluated target-aware baselines. Processor measurements show lower latency than the evaluated candidate-conditioned baselines at large candidate counts, further reduced by request-local history reuse.
zh_title: MELODI：用于轻量级排序的相似度与身份解耦方法
translation: 针对受延迟限制的候选排序场景，我们提出了一个相似度-身份解耦框架，该框架将目标-历史兼容性与纯目标信息分离开来。我们研究了计算池化相似度的两种顺序——“先相似度后池化”与“先池化后相似度”，并证明在每个固定目标下，相似度算子对其历史参数的线性性质足以保证两者等价，从而论证了采用计算成本更低的“先池化后相似度”形式的合理性。我们将该框架实例化为解耦身份与相似度的多头高效轻量算子（MELODI），其相似度分支结合了目标条件多头历史池化与一个在其池化历史输入上呈线性的单层无残差交叉层，其身份分支则因问题而异。在公开基准数据集上，MELODI 达到或超越了所评估的目标感知和目标无关基线。在两个大规模工业数据集上，其精确率-召回率曲线下面积（AUPRC）、归一化折损累计增益（NDCG）和召回率指标均等于或高于所评估的目标感知基线。处理器实测显示，在大候选数量下，其延迟低于所评估的候选条件基线，且可通过请求局部历史重用进一步降低。
tldr: 提出了一种相似度-身份解耦的轻量级排序模型 MELODI，通过理论推导采用高效的“先池化后相似度”架构，在大候选规模下以显著更低的延迟实现了媲美或超越重度基线的排序性能。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于通过数学推导证明了在特定线性条件下“先池化后计算相似度”与“先计算相似度后池化”等价，从而在理论层面支撑了轻量化设计的合理性。其重要性体现在工业界重排序与召回阶段对超低延迟和高精度的极致要求，该方法在兼顾精度的同时极大降低了计算开销，具备很强的工业落地价值。局限性在于其表现高度依赖历史表征与相似度算子的线性假设，对更复杂非线性交互的建模能力可能受限。
motivation: 针对受延迟严格限制的候选排序场景，解决在高效捕捉目标物品与历史交互的兼容性信息的同时降低计算延迟的难题。
method: 提出相似度-身份解耦框架（MELODI），将目标-历史兼容性与纯目标信息分离；指出当相似度算子对其历史参数为线性时，“先池化后相似度”与“先相似度后池化”等价，从而采用更轻量的先池化计算模式；相似度分支结合目标条件多头历史池化与单层无残差交叉层，并结合请求局部历史重用技术降低延迟。
results: 在公开基准数据集上，MELODI 达到或超过了评估的目标感知和目标无关基线；在两个大规模工业数据集上，其 AUPRC、NDCG 和 Recall 均等于或高于所评估的目标感知基线；处理器实测显示在大候选集场景下延迟显著低于候选条件基线，且支持通过历史重用进一步降低。
conclusion: MELODI 成功实现了在保持甚至超越重度目标感知基线性能的同时，大幅削减了低延迟场景下的排序延迟，是一种高效实用的轻量级排序解决方案。

title: Beyond "AI Can Make Mistakes": How Risk Communication Shapes Trust and Decision Confidence for LLMs in Health Information Seeking
authors: Jiawei Zhou, Mengting Tu, Shravika Mittal, Sowmya Krishna, Q. Vera Liao, Munmun De Choudhury
abstract: Adoption of LLMs for health information has outpaced public understanding, but whether risk communication can work as a corrective remains unknown. In a preregistered experiment (N=500), we compared a standard disclaimer against structured risk communication varying in contextual relevance and mechanistic explanation. Without intervention, users understanding LLMs less reported higher trust and confidence in deciding when to rely. Structured risk communication significantly reduced trust, more so with health-specific framing, but did not improve confidence in reliance decision. Risk disclosure was associated with higher decision confidence among those with stronger AI knowledge, but lower confidence among those less preferring analytical thinking. Effects were also task-dependent: disclosure shifted preferences for medical queries and impairment assistance, while LLMs remained preferred for emotional companionship regardless of exposure. These findings demonstrate that risk communication can narrow trust gaps across AI-literacy levels, but turning disclosure into judgment requires adapting to usage context and users' prior knowledge.
zh_title: 超越“AI会犯错”：风险沟通如何塑造健康信息检索中大语言模型的信任与决策信心
translation: 大语言模型（LLM）在健康信息方面的应用已经超过了公众的理解水平，但风险沟通是否能作为一种纠正机制仍然未知。在一项预注册实验（N=500）中，我们比较了标准免责声明与在情境相关性和机制解释上有所不同的结构化风险沟通。在没有干预的情况下，对LLM理解较少的用户报告了更高的信任度以及对何时依赖它的决策信心。结构化风险沟通显著降低了信任度，特别是采用健康特定框架时，但并未提高依赖决策的信心。风险披露与AI知识较强的用户更高的决策信心相关，但与较少偏好分析思维的用户的较低决策信心相关。效果还具有任务依赖性：披露改变了对医疗查询和障碍辅助的偏好，而无论是否暴露于披露，LLM仍然是情感陪伴的首选。这些发现表明，风险沟通可以缩小不同AI素养水平之间的信任差距，但要将披露转化为判断，需要适应使用情境和用户的先验知识。
tldr: 结构化风险沟通可以降低对健康类大语言模型的盲目信任并缩小素养差距，但其对决策信心的影响取决于任务类型、使用情境及用户的AI知识水平。
ai_comments: 本研究通过预注册实验深入探讨了风险沟通在健康领域大语言模型应用中的作用，创新性地发现结构化、情境相关的风险提示能够有效缩小不同AI素养人群之间的信任差距，但也凸显了信任与决策信心之间的复杂关系，强调未来AI风险沟通需要因人、因场景而异。
motivation: 尽管大语言模型在健康信息领域的应用迅速普及，但公众对其理解滞后，且风险沟通能否作为纠正机制尚不明确，因此需要探究风险沟通如何塑造用户对健康领域大语言模型的信任和决策信心。
method: 采用预注册实验方法（N=500），对比了标准免责声明与随情境相关性和机制解释变化的结构化风险沟通效果。
results: 结构化风险沟通显著降低了用户信任（特别是结合健康特定框架时），但并未提高对何时依赖AI的决策信心；风险披露对决策信心的影响因用户的AI知识水平和分析思维偏好而异，且效果具有任务依赖性。
conclusion: 风险沟通可以缩小不同AI素养人群之间的信任差距，但要将风险披露转化为精准的决策判断，必须根据使用情境和用户的先验知识进行定制化调整。

title: DraftKV: Protecting Persistent Worlds through Hierarchical Streaming Retrieval
authors: Xiaoling Zhou, Haopeng Li, Yufa Zhou, Rui Ding, Yu Li, Jun Lin, Enze Xie, Chunhua Shen, Xuan Shen
abstract: Interactive video world models enable action- and camera-controlled exploration, yet struggle to maintain consistent spatial geometry and appearance when revisiting previously explored locations. Historical KV caches help auto-regressive video diffusion models maintain long-term consistency, but their retrieval and attention computation introduce substantial latency as history grows. We propose DraftKV, a training-free framework that retrieves historical KV caches based on geometric grounding and query-conditioned relevance, while combining CPU offloading with tile-wise streaming attention to reduce GPU memory usage and inference latency. Theoretically, we show that draft relevance reproduces the mean branch of full-resolution block relevance exactly, so its deviation is confined to the $β$-weighted max branch, and we bound retrieval utility loss in terms of the measured Top-K selection overlap. We further show that draft relevance cannot distinguish blocks with similar pooled descriptors regardless of camera pose, motivating geometric grounding before refinement. Then, we introduce streaming CG-Attention, which overlaps CPU-to-GPU KV transfers with attention computation through tile-wise streaming, hiding transfer latency while maintaining bounded GPU memory usage. Experiments across diverse model families show that DraftKV achieves superior generation quality and consistency while achieving $3.27\times$ end-to-end speedup and 42.2% peak GPU memory reduction over other CPU-offloaded KV cache retrieval methods. Notably, DraftKV enables high-quality interactive world generation with historical KV retrieval on a single H100 GPU using SolarWM-33B.
comment: Includes supplementary material. Code and project page are available online
zh_title: DraftKV：通过分层流式检索保护持久世界
translation: 交互式视频世界模型能够实现动作和相机控制的探索，但在重访先前探索的位置时，难以保持空间几何和外观的一致性。历史KV缓存有助于自回归视频扩散模型维持长期一致性，但随着历史增长，其检索和注意力计算会引入大量延迟。我们提出了DraftKV，一个无需训练的框架，它基于几何定位和查询条件相关性检索历史KV缓存，同时结合CPU卸载和分块流式注意力来减少GPU内存使用和推理延迟。理论上，我们表明草稿相关性精确重现了全分辨率块相关性的均值分支，因此其偏差仅限于β加权的最大分支，并且我们根据测量的Top-K选择重叠来限制检索效用损失。我们进一步表明，无论相机姿态如何，草稿相关性都无法区分具有相似池化描述符的块，这促使在细化之前进行几何定位。然后，我们引入了流式CG-Attention，它通过分块流式处理将CPU到GPU的KV传输与注意力计算重叠，从而隐藏传输延迟，同时保持GPU内存使用量受限。跨不同模型家族的实验表明，DraftKV实现了卓越的生成质量和一致性，同时比其他CPU卸载的KV缓存检索方法实现了3.27倍的端到端加速和42.2%的峰值GPU内存减少。值得注意的是，DraftKV使得在单个H100 GPU上使用SolarWM-33B进行高质量的交互式世界生成成为可能。
tldr: DraftKV是一个无需训练的框架，通过几何定位和查询条件相关性检索历史KV缓存，并结合CPU卸载和分块流式注意力，显著减少了交互式视频世界模型的延迟和GPU内存使用，同时提高了生成质量和一致性。
ai_comments: DraftKV的创新点在于其无训练的框架设计，巧妙地结合了几何定位、查询条件相关性检索和流式注意力机制来优化KV缓存的使用。这不仅解决了长期一致性带来的性能瓶颈，还在理论上提供了严谨的分析。其通过CPU卸载和分块流式处理隐藏传输延迟的策略，对于实时交互式应用具有重要意义，在单GPU上实现高质量世界生成更是展现了其工程上的卓越性。
motivation: 交互式视频世界模型在重访已探索位置时，难以保持空间几何和外观的一致性。虽然历史KV缓存有助于自回归视频扩散模型维持长期一致性，但随着历史增长，其检索和注意力计算会引入大量延迟和内存消耗。
method: 本文提出了DraftKV，一个无需训练的框架。它基于几何定位和查询条件相关性检索历史KV缓存，并通过结合CPU卸载和分块流式注意力来减少GPU内存使用和推理延迟。理论上，DraftKV证明了其草稿相关性能够精确重现全分辨率块相关性的均值分支。此外，论文引入了流式CG-Attention，通过分块流式处理将CPU到GPU的KV传输与注意力计算重叠，从而隐藏传输延迟并保持GPU内存使用量受限。
results: 实验表明，DraftKV实现了卓越的生成质量和一致性，相比其他CPU卸载的KV缓存检索方法，端到端速度提升了3.27倍，峰值GPU内存减少了42.2%。值得注意的是，DraftKV使得在单个H100 GPU上使用SolarWM-33B进行高质量的交互式世界生成成为可能。
conclusion: DraftKV通过创新的分层流式检索机制，有效解决了交互式视频世界模型中长期一致性维护所带来的延迟和内存问题，显著提升了生成性能和效率。

title: User-Adaptive Fusion of Multiple Foundation Models for Recommender Systems
authors: Sunwoo Kim, Hyunjin Hwang, Geon Lee, Kyungho Kim, Kijung Shin
abstract: Can recommender systems benefit from combining a collection of foundation models within and across modalities? While different foundation models may capture complementary aspects of item metadata, we find that naively combining their representations yields only marginal gains over using a single foundation model. We make a key observation: the users who benefit vary across foundation models. Motivated by this observation, we introduce UF2O, a user-adaptive approach for fusing multiple foundation models for recommendation. In a nutshell, UF2O models the contribution of each foundation model as user-specific by maintaining separate recommendation views and adaptively combining their scores for each user. By performing fusion at the score level, UF2O can also fuse heterogeneous foundation models without directly aligning their representation spaces. Extensive experiments that jointly combine four foundation models on four datasets show that UF2O outperforms existing fusion approaches in both static and sequential recommendation settings, with improvements of up to 7% over the strongest fusion baseline. The code, datasets, and supplementary materials for our work are available at https://github.com/kswoo97/UFFO.
zh_title: 用户自适应融合多个基础模型用于推荐系统
translation: 推荐系统能否受益于在模态内部和跨模态结合一系列基础模型？虽然不同的基础模型可能捕捉物品元数据的互补方面，但我们发现，简单地结合它们的表示只比使用单个基础模型带来微小的增益。我们做了一个关键的观察：受益的用户在不同的基础模型之间是不同的。受这一观察的启发，我们引入了UF2O，一种用于融合多个基础模型以进行推荐的用户自适应方法。简而言之，UF2O通过维护单独的推荐视图并为每个用户自适应地组合它们的评分，将每个基础模型的贡献建模为用户特定的。通过在评分层面执行融合，UF2O还可以融合异构基础模型，而无需直接对齐它们的表示空间。在四个数据集上联合组合四个基础模型的广泛实验表明，UF2O在静态和序列推荐设置中均优于现有融合方法，比最强的融合基线提高了多达7%。我们的工作代码、数据集和补充材料可在 https://github.com/kswoo97/UFFO 获取。
tldr: UF2O是一种用户自适应方法，用于融合多个基础模型以改进推荐系统，通过为每个用户自适应地组合不同基础模型的评分来显著优于现有方法。
ai_comments: 这项工作提出了一种新颖的用户自适应融合策略，解决了简单结合基础模型表示效果不佳的问题。通过在评分层面进行融合，UF2O能够处理异构模型，这增强了其实用性。其核心创新在于识别并利用了用户对不同基础模型的偏好差异，为推荐系统中的多模型融合提供了一个有效且可扩展的框架。潜在的局限性可能在于用户特定贡献模型的复杂性和计算开销。
motivation: 现有研究发现，简单地结合基础模型的表示只会带来微小的增益，而不同用户从不同基础模型中受益。基于这一观察，作者提出了用户自适应的融合方法。
method: UF2O通过为每个基础模型维护单独的推荐视图，并为每个用户自适应地组合它们的评分来建模每个基础模型的用户特定贡献。它在评分层面进行融合，从而能够融合异构的基础模型，而无需直接对齐它们的表示空间。
results: 在四个数据集上联合组合四个基础模型的广泛实验表明，UF2O在静态和序列推荐设置中均优于现有融合方法，比最强的融合基线提高了多达7%。
conclusion: UF2O通过用户自适应的评分级融合，有效结合了多个异构基础模型，显著提升了推荐系统的性能，证明了用户特定融合策略的有效性。

title: MALET & Katalina: A Large-Scale Dataset and Static Analysis of macOS Malware
authors: Godwin Attigah, Obinna Igbe
abstract:
While malware on platforms such as Windows and Android has been extensively studied, the macOS ecosystem remains comparatively understudied. To address this gap, we present MALET, a large-scale public dataset for macOS malware analysis. MALET contains 44{,}804 malicious Mach-O binaries and 44{,}457 samples with zero antivirus detections on VirusTotal. From the undetected set, we further identify 25{,}835 high-confidence benign samples using conservative, heuristic-based filtering. We also introduce Katalina, an open-source static analysis framework that extracts macOS-specific structural features and indicators of potential behavior at scale.
  Using MALET, we perform, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale static characterization of macOS malware. Our analysis reveals macOS-specific traits, including widespread misuse of security entitlements, abuse of native scripting interfaces, and irregularities in code-signing infrastructure. We find that 93.0\% of malicious samples are unsigned, demonstrating that unsigned code continues to execute in practice through user-mediated approval mechanisms. Among CA-signed malware, 28.4\% (816 samples) were associated with certificates that were later revoked, including samples publicly attributed to DPRK-linked threat actors, as reflected in antivirus labels and threat intelligence reports. Finally, we identify significant detection instability: in 185 structurally identical malicious samples, antivirus engines failed to provide consistent detections for 77.2\% (143 samples). Together, these results highlight persistent blind spots in macOS malware detection and motivate improved approaches to certificate abuse analysis, similarity-based clustering, and platform-specific defense mechanisms. Based on these insights, we outline concrete steps to advance the state of macOS malware analysis and defense.
zh_title: MALET & Katalina：一个大规模macOS恶意软件数据集与静态分析
translation:
尽管Windows和Android等平台上的恶意软件已被广泛研究，但macOS生态系统相对研究不足。为了弥补这一空白，我们提出了MALET，一个用于macOS恶意软件分析的大规模公共数据集。MALET包含44,804个恶意Mach-O二进制文件和44,457个在VirusTotal上零杀毒检测的样本。从这些未检测到的样本中，我们使用保守的、基于启发式的过滤方法进一步识别了25,835个高可信度的良性样本。我们还介绍了Katalina，一个开源静态分析框架，用于大规模提取macOS特有的结构特征和潜在行为指标。
利用MALET，我们进行了我们所知的第一项大规模macOS恶意软件静态特征分析。我们的分析揭示了macOS特有的特征，包括普遍滥用安全授权、滥用原生脚本接口以及代码签名基础设施中的不规范行为。我们发现93.0%的恶意样本未签名，这表明未签名代码通过用户批准机制在实践中持续执行。在CA签名的恶意软件中，28.4%（816个样本）与后来被撤销的证书相关联，包括公开归因于与朝鲜相关的威胁行为者的样本，这反映在杀毒软件标签和威胁情报报告中。最后，我们识别出显著的检测不稳定性：在185个结构相同的恶意样本中，杀毒引擎对77.2%（143个样本）未能提供一致的检测。总而言之，这些结果突出了macOS恶意软件检测中持续存在的盲点，并促使人们改进证书滥用分析、基于相似性的聚类以及平台特定的防御机制。基于这些见解，我们概述了推进macOS恶意软件分析和防御现状的具体步骤。
tldr: 本研究介绍了MALET，一个大规模macOS恶意软件公共数据集，以及Katalina，一个开源静态分析框架。利用这些工具，研究人员首次对macOS恶意软件进行了大规模静态分析，揭示了macOS特有的恶意软件特征、检测盲点，并提出了改进防御方法的建议。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过提供第一个大规模的macOS恶意软件公共数据集MALET和开源静态分析框架Katalina，对macOS安全研究做出了重大贡献，填补了该领域长期存在的空白。其研究结果，特别是关于未签名恶意软件的普遍性、证书滥用以及杀毒软件检测不一致性的发现，对于理解macOS当前的安全状况至关重要。识别macOS平台特有的恶意软件特征对于指导未来的防御策略具有极高的价值，为推进macOS恶意软件分析和防御提供了坚实的基础。
motivation: macOS生态系统中的恶意软件研究相对不足，与Windows和Android平台相比存在研究空白。缺乏大规模的macOS恶意软件数据集和有效的静态分析工具来深入理解其特性。
method: 1. 构建了MALET：一个大规模的macOS恶意软件公共数据集，包含44,804个恶意Mach-O二进制文件，其中44,457个样本在VirusTotal上检测数为零，并进一步识别出25,835个高可信度的良性样本。2. 引入了Katalina：一个开源静态分析框架，用于大规模提取macOS特有的结构特征和潜在行为指标。3. 利用MALET数据集，进行了首次大规模的macOS恶意软件静态特征分析。
results: 1. 揭示了macOS特有的恶意软件特征，包括普遍滥用安全授权、滥用原生脚本接口以及代码签名基础设施中的不规范行为。2. 发现93.0%的恶意样本未签名，表明未签名代码通过用户批准机制在实践中持续执行。3. 在CA签名的恶意软件中，28.4%（816个样本）与后来被撤销的证书相关联，包括与朝鲜威胁行为者相关的样本。4. 识别出显著的检测不稳定性：在185个结构相同的恶意样本中，杀毒引擎对77.2%（143个样本）未能提供一致的检测。
conclusion: 这些结果突出了macOS恶意软件检测中持续存在的盲点，并促使人们改进证书滥用分析、基于相似性的聚类以及平台特定的防御机制。基于这些见解，本文概述了推进macOS恶意软件分析和防御现状的具体步骤。

title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes
authors: Seonghwan Park, Min-Gyu Park
abstract: Hands grasp objects with soft skin. A fingertip flattens against a mug, and a palm curves around a bottle. Yet hand-object datasets and estimators represent the hand as a rigid articulated mesh, which hovers above or penetrates the object where skin would press against it. Existing refiners keep the mesh rigid and adjust only the pose, trading pose accuracy for physical plausibility. We ask whether a rigid hand can instead touch the object as skin does while staying close to its original pose. We lift annotated or estimated rigid hands to contact-consistent meshes through an optimization that (i) slightly adjusts the joints and wrist to bring the fingers onto the object, (ii) deforms the skin so that penetrating regions settle onto the surface, and (iii) keeps this deformation consistent over time. Since deformation reaches only skin already near the object, we further train a lightweight head on the lifted annotations to predict where an estimated hand should touch and steer the deformation there. Unlike existing refiners, the lift more than doubles the skin lying on the object surface for three published estimators while barely changing the pose. Guidance from the learned head further improves grasp stability by closing contact gaps that the estimate leaves open. Existing hand-object datasets and estimators can thus adopt contact-consistent hands without changing the hand model or retraining the estimators.
zh_title: 超越刚性手：将皮肤变形为接触一致的手部网格
translation: 手用柔软的皮肤抓握物体。指尖会压平在马克杯上，手掌会环绕瓶子。然而，手物数据集和估计器将手表示为刚性铰接网格，这使得皮肤应该压在物体上的地方悬浮或穿透物体。现有的细化器保持网格刚性，仅调整姿态，以姿态准确性换取物理合理性。我们提出一个问题：刚性手能否像皮肤一样接触物体，同时保持接近其原始姿态？我们通过一个优化过程将注释或估计的刚性手提升为接触一致的网格，该过程包括：(i) 微调关节和手腕以使手指接触物体；(ii) 变形皮肤使穿透区域落在表面上；(iii) 保持这种变形随时间一致。由于变形仅限于已经靠近物体的皮肤，我们进一步在提升后的注释上训练了一个轻量级头部，以预测估计的手应在哪里接触并引导变形。与现有细化器不同，这种提升使三个已发表估计器在物体表面上的皮肤接触面积增加了一倍多，同时几乎不改变姿态。学习到的头部的引导通过弥补估计遗留的接触间隙，进一步提高了抓握稳定性。因此，现有的手物数据集和估计器可以采用接触一致的手，而无需改变手部模型或重新训练估计器。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种优化方法，可以将刚性手部网格提升为接触一致的网格，使皮肤与物体接触，同时保持姿态接近原始估计，显著提高了手部与物体接触的物理真实性。
ai_comments: 这项工作的创新之处在于它通过引入皮肤变形来解决手物交互中长期存在的物理真实性问题，而不是仅仅依赖于姿态调整。它提供了一种即插即用的解决方案，使得现有手物模型能够更容易地实现更真实的接触，这对于提高虚拟现实、机器人抓取和动画的真实感具有重要意义。其方法的有效性体现在显著增加接触面积而不牺牲姿态准确性。
motivation: 现有的手物数据集和估计器将手表示为刚性铰接网格，导致手部皮肤在与物体接触时悬浮或穿透物体。现有细化器仅调整姿态，牺牲姿态准确性以换取物理合理性，无法实现皮肤的真实变形。
method: 该方法通过一个优化过程将注释或估计的刚性手提升为接触一致的网格。该优化过程包括：(i) 微调关节和手腕以使手指接触物体；(ii) 变形皮肤使穿透区域落在表面上；(iii) 保持这种变形随时间一致。此外，训练了一个轻量级头部来预测估计的手应在哪里接触并引导变形。
results: 与现有细化器相比，该方法使三个已发表估计器在物体表面上的皮肤接触面积增加了一倍多，同时几乎不改变姿态。学习到的头部的引导通过弥补估计遗留的接触间隙，进一步提高了抓握稳定性。
conclusion: 现有的手物数据集和估计器可以采用接触一致的手，而无需改变手部模型或重新训练估计器，从而显著提升了手物交互的物理真实性。

title: VLG-Drive: Unifying Vision-Language and Geometric Priors for Autonomous Driving
authors: Junge Zhang, Jie Zhu, Yanqi Jia, Xiangyu Xu, Zixun Huang, Wenbin He, Xin Li, Jiachen Li, Liu Ren
abstract: A driving planner needs both scene semantics, which vision-language models (VLMs) provide, and spatial structure, which geometric foundation models recover from visual history. We present VLG-Drive, which keeps both models frozen and trains only a fusion interface and a planner from trajectory labels. At each camera-grid cell, the interface fuses the paired VLM and geometry features into one joint token through a geometry-anchored residual, and a command-conditioned planner reads these tokens to predict the ego trajectory. VLG-Drive achieves 31.78 EPDMS on NavHard under perturbed initial states, the highest among the compared methods, and 88.27 PDMS on NavTest from cameras alone. Pointwise fusion outperforms independent VLM and geometry streams on both benchmarks. In closed-loop driving on 420 HUGSIM scenarios, VLG-Drive outperforms all compared planners. These results indicate that a lightweight planner trained on fused features of frozen vision-language and geometric foundation models is an effective alternative to adapting either model for planning.
zh_title: VLG-Drive：统一视觉-语言与几何先验的自动驾驶
translation: 自动驾驶规划器既需要视觉-语言模型（VLMs）提供的场景语义，又需要几何基础模型从视觉历史中恢复的空间结构。我们提出了VLG-Drive，它保持两个模型冻结，仅利用轨迹标签训练一个融合接口和一个规划器。在每个相机网格单元处，该接口通过几何锚定的残差将成对的VLM和几何特征融合成一个联合Token，并且命令条件规划器读取这些Token来预测自车轨迹。在受扰动初始状态下的NavHard测试中，VLG-Drive取得了31.78的EPDMS，是对比方法中最高的；在仅通过相机的NavTest测试中取得了88.27的PDMS。逐点融合在两个基准上均优于独立的VLM和几何流。在420个HUGSIM场景的闭环驾驶中，VLG-Drive优于所有对比规划器。这些结果表明，在冻结的视觉-语言和几何基础模型的融合特征上训练轻量级规划器，是适应这两类模型进行规划的有效替代方案。
tldr: 提出VLG-Drive，通过轻量级接口融合冻结的视觉-语言模型与几何基础模型特征，实现了优异的自动驾驶轨迹规划性能。
ai_comments: 该论文巧妙地结合了视觉语言模型（VLM）的语义理解能力和几何基础模型的空间结构恢复能力，通过冻结基础模型、仅训练轻量级融合接口和规划器的方式，在保持计算高效的同时显著提升了自动驾驶的规划性能。这为利用大模型进行具身智能/自动驾驶提供了一种极具实用价值的范式。
motivation: 自动驾驶规划器既需要视觉-语言模型（VLM）提供的场景语义，又需要几何基础模型从视觉历史中恢复的空间结构。然而，直接适配这些大模型成本高昂且复杂，因此需要探索一种更有效的方法来统一这两种先验。
method: 提出VLG-Drive，保持视觉-语言模型（VLM）和几何基础模型冻结，仅训练一个融合接口和一个基于轨迹标签的规划器。在每个相机网格单元处，通过几何锚定的残差将成对的VLM和几何特征融合成一个联合Token，最后由命令条件的规划器读取这些Token预测自车轨迹。
results: VLG-Drive在NavHard基准测试中（受扰动初始状态下）取得了31.78的EPDMS（对比方法中最高），在NavTest基准测试中仅通过相机就取得了88.27的PDMS。逐点融合在两个基准上均优于独立的VLM和几何流。在420个HUGSIM场景的闭环驾驶中，VLG-Drive优于所有对比规划器。
conclusion: 基于冻结的视觉-语言模型和几何基础模型特征，通过轻量级融合接口和命令条件规划器进行训练，是端到端自动驾驶的一种高效且性能优异的替代方案。

title: Perception Is Enough, at the Right Scale: Scale-Adaptive Token Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Yifeng Lin, Liuxiang Qiu, Yunfeng Chen, Tiesong Zhao
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models must process continuous streams of visual observations, and the resulting computational cost limits real-time robotic control. Token pruning reduces this cost, but a fixed semantic scale of perceptual representation can overlook information needed at different stages of manipulation. We show that perceptual semantics can guide effective token selection without relying on internal attention when the selection scale adapts to the scene's evolving semantic structure. Based on this observation, we introduce TauPrune-VLA, a training-free method that controls the scale of the retained perceptual representation through a single perception temperature $τ$. To adapt this scale as manipulation proceeds, TauPrune-VLA updates $τ$ online using trends in perceptual semantics, with robot-state changes and action magnitude regulating the adjustment strength. While these semantics evolve over the course of manipulation, they remain relatively stable between consecutive frames.
