By flexibly composing and extending available skills, SkillHarness adapts to unseen terrain and task combinations without retraining the locomotion policies. The framework further incorporates execution feedback and retrospective decision revision to improve skill selection and avoid inappropriate skill switching. We evaluate SkillHarness across diverse terrain configurations, perceptual disturbances, and multi-obstacle traversal tasks to assess its adaptability and reliability in long-horizon traversal.
zh_title: 技能马具：用于长距离遍历的即插即用技能的执行感知协调
translation: 跨越复杂地形需要机器人协调各种运动技能，同时适应看不见的障碍物和不断变化的环境。尽管感知强化学习能够实现敏捷的运动，但传统的跨地形运动依赖于固定的策略，限制了适应性和技能的可扩展性。感知干扰和不可靠的技能转换进一步挑战了鲁棒的执行。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了SkillHarness，一个执行感知协调框架，它集成了灵活的、即插即用的运动技能库。为了增强遍历鲁棒性，我们引入了一种感知强化学习方法，该方法在保留任务相关环境参考的同时不断更新本体感受反馈，从而降低了对感知波动的敏感性。视觉语言引导的Harness通过事件触发推理、几何可行性验证和执行阶段约束来协调导航和技能执行。通过灵活地组合和扩展可用技能，SkillHarness可以在不重新训练运动策略的情况下适应看不见的地形和任务组合。该框架还结合了执行反馈和回顾性决策修订，以改进技能选择并避免不恰当的技能切换。我们在各种地形配置、感知干扰和多障碍物遍历任务中评估了SkillHarness，以评估其在长距离遍历中的适应性和可靠性。
tldr: SkillHarness是一个执行感知协调框架，通过即插即用技能库和感知强化学习来提高机器人跨越复杂地形的能力，即使在存在干扰和不可靠技能转换的情况下也能适应新环境和任务。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种名为SkillHarness的先进框架，用于解决机器人长距离地形遍历中的复杂性。该方法通过结合即插即用技能库和执行感知协调，在提高机器人适应性和鲁棒性方面取得了显著进展。特别是，感知强化学习的应用以及事件触发推理和回顾性决策修订等机制，展示了在应对现实世界挑战方面的潜力。然而，该研究可能需要进一步探讨在极端或高度不可预测的环境中的可扩展性和计算效率。
motivation: 传统的机器人跨越复杂地形的方法依赖于固定的策略，这限制了它们适应性和技能的可扩展性，并且容易受到感知干扰和不可靠的技能转换的影响。
method: SkillHarness框架集成了即插即用运动技能库，并采用感知强化学习方法，该方法在保留任务相关环境参考的同时不断更新本体感受反馈。它使用视觉语言引导的协调器，通过事件触发推理、几何可行性验证和执行阶段约束来协调导航和技能执行。该框架还包括执行反馈和回顾性决策修订，以改进技能选择。
results: SkillHarness在各种地形配置、感知干扰和多障碍物遍历任务中得到了评估，证明了其在长距离遍历中的适应性和可靠性。
conclusion: SkillHarness通过其执行感知协调框架，有效地提高了机器人跨越复杂地形的能力，并且无需重新训练运动策略即可适应新的地形和任务组合。

title: Wind-Aware Trajectory Planning for Deformable Aerial Formations
authors: Haozhe Wang, Xun Huang
abstract: Coordinated aerial transport in dense urban environments requires drone formations to navigate confined spaces and adapt to spatially varying winds around buildings. Formation deformation enables passage through narrow spaces but changes individual drone velocities and the local winds they encounter, coupling formation motion with aerodynamic effects. We propose Family-Air, a wind-aware trajectory-family planner that constructs a virtual tube as shared collision-free flight space and jointly optimizes formation-center motion, deformation, and timing. A shared affine transformation represents a continuous trajectory family, incorporating spatially varying wind and deformation-induced velocities into a unified air-relative motion objective. The optimization enforces virtual-tube containment, inter-drone separation, and kinematic feasibility. Simulations across four urban wind-field scenarios demonstrate the importance of local wind-deformation coupling. Flight simulations further show improvements in trajectory tracking accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of wind-aware trajectory-family planning for coordinated aerial transport in complex urban environments.
zh_title: 面向可变形空中编队的风感知轨迹规划
translation: 在密集的城市环境中进行协同空中运输需要无人机编队能够穿越狭窄的空间并适应建筑物周围空间变化的風。编队变形能够使编队通过狭窄空间，但会改变单个无人机的速度以及它们遇到的局部風，从而将编队运动与空气动力学效应耦合起来。我们提出了一种名为Family-Air的风感知轨迹族规划器，它构建一个虚拟管道作为共享的无碰撞飞行空间，并联合优化编队中心的运动、变形和时间。共享的仿射变换表示连续的轨迹族，将空间变化的風和变形引起的风速变化纳入统一的空速运动目标。优化过程强制执行虚拟管道约束、无人机间安全距离和运动学可行性。在四种城市風场场景下的仿真表明，局部風与变形的耦合很重要。飞行仿真进一步显示了轨迹跟踪精度的提高。这些结果证明了风感知轨迹族规划在复杂城市环境中进行协调空中运输的潜力。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为Family-Air的风感知轨迹规划方法，用于在城市环境中协调无人机编队进行空中运输。该方法通过构建虚拟管道来优化编队中心的运动、变形和时间，同时考虑了空间变化的風和变形引起的风速变化。仿真结果表明，该方法能有效处理城市环境中的复杂风场，提高轨迹跟踪精度。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的风感知轨迹规划方法，名为Family-Air，专门用于解决复杂城市环境中无人机编队的空中运输问题。研究亮点在于其能够同时考虑空间变化的風和编队变形对空气动力学的影响，并通过构建虚拟管道来确保飞行安全和效率。方法上的创新在于使用共享仿射变换来统一表示轨迹族，并将风和变形引起的风速变化纳入统一的运动目标。仿真结果也令人信服地展示了该方法在提高轨迹跟踪精度方面的优势。然而，实际部署中的鲁棒性、计算复杂度以及对风场预测精度的依赖性有待进一步验证。
motivation: 城市环境中无人机编队进行空中运输需要克服狭窄空间和空间变化的風的挑战。编队变形虽然有助于通过狭窄空间，但会改变无人机的速度和局部風，从而将编队运动与空气动力学效应耦合起来。
method: 提出了一种名为Family-Air的风感知轨迹规划方法，该方法构建一个虚拟管道作为共享的无碰撞飞行空间，并联合优化编队中心的运动、变形和时间。使用共享的仿射变换表示连续的轨迹族，将空间变化的風和变形引起的风速变化纳入统一的空速运动目标。优化过程强制执行虚拟管道约束、无人机间安全距离以及运动学可行性。
results: 在四种城市風场场景下的仿真表明，局部風与变形的耦合很重要。飞行仿真进一步显示了轨迹跟踪精度的提高。
conclusion: 风感知轨迹族规划在复杂城市环境中的协调空中运输具有潜力。

title: Blaming the Machine, Billing the Victim? How Mock Jurors Reassign Fault from Generative AI Systems and Respond to Liability Cliffs in Tort
authors: Tin Trung Nguyen, Jiannan Xu, Bao Kham Chau, Hal Daumé III, Zubin Jelveh
abstract: Generative AI complicates tort liability attribution when people blame a generative AI system that cannot itself bear legally relevant fault. We investigate where this blame goes when fault must be allocated among legal persons, and whether American discontinuous apportionment doctrines influence mock jurors' factual findings of fault. Such doctrines include Contributory negligence, Joint and several liability, and their 50% or 51% variations, all of which have a fault-percentage threshold or a "cliff" where the victim-entitled compensation (or a defendant's liability) jumps to zero (or to all compensatory damages). Our pre-registered human subjects experiment (N=199 Prolific participants) shows that as many U.S. mock jurors (36%) blame the AI system itself, the AI blame often "leaks" to the victim or to the AI user (in 27% to 73% of our AI-blaming records, depending on how leakage is calculated). Although mock jurors rarely change their blame assignment from one side of the liability cliff to the other, these participants do not acknowledge the legal doctrine or its monetary consequence when explaining their changes. Our empirical results illustrate how a narrow doctrinal exception in tort, carving out "joint and several liability" for those deploying or using Generative AI without reasonable care, might mitigate the impact of blame leakage on victims' deserved compensation without introducing significant jury nullification risks.
comment: Under review at an AI Governance conference
zh_title: 责怪机器，账单给受害者？模拟陪审员如何在侵权法中将生成式AI系统的过错重新分配并应对责任断崖
translation: 生成式AI使侵权责任归属变得复杂，当人们指责一个本身无法承担法律相关过错的生成式AI系统时。我们调查了当过错必须在法律主体之间进行分配时，这种指责的去向，以及美国的非连续分摊原则是否会影响模拟陪审员对过错的事实认定。这些原则包括协同过失、连带责任及其50%或51%的变化形式，所有这些都有一个过错百分比阈值或“断崖”，受害者有权获得的赔偿（或被告的责任）会骤降至零（或跃升至全部赔偿性损害赔偿）。我们的预注册人类受试者实验（N=199名Prolific参与者）表明，多达36%的美国模拟陪审员将过错归咎于AI系统本身，AI的指责往往会“泄漏”给受害者或AI用户（占我们AI指责记录的27%到73%，取决于泄漏的计算方式）。尽管模拟陪审员很少在责任断崖的一侧到另一侧改变他们的过错指派，但这些参与者在解释其改变时并未承认该法律原则或其金钱后果。我们的实证结果说明了侵权法中一个狭窄的法理例外——为那些在没有合理注意的情况下部署或使用生成式AI的人分割出“连带责任”——如何能够减轻责任泄漏对受害者应得赔偿的影响，同时又不会引入显著的陪审团废止权风险。
tldr: 论文通过实验发现，公众在面对生成式AI引发的损害时会将对AI的指责“泄漏”给受害者或用户，并对侵权法中的责任断崖及救济途径进行了实证探讨。
ai_comments: 该论文结合实验法探讨了生成式AI侵权责任分配中模拟陪审员的归责倾向及责任断崖（liability cliff）的影响，对AI时代的法律规制研究具有重要的创新价值和实践意义。
motivation: 生成式AI无法承担法律上的过错，这使得侵权责任归属变得复杂。论文旨在研究当必须在法律主体间分配责任时，对AI系统的指责最终流向何处，以及美国的不连续分配原则（如责任断崖）是否会影响模拟陪审员对事实过错的认定。
method: 采用了预注册的人类受试者实验方法（N=199），研究模拟陪审员对生成式AI引发的侵权案件中的过错归属与责任断崖的反应。
results: 高达36%的美国模拟陪审员将责任归咎于AI系统本身，且这种AI指责经常“泄漏”给受害者或AI用户（占AI指责记录的27%到73%不等）。尽管陪审员很少在责任断崖的两侧改变过错归属，但他们在解释改变时并未明确承认相关法律原则或其金钱后果。
conclusion: 本研究表明，生成式AI系统的介入会导致责任向受害者或用户“泄漏”，传统的责任断崖规则虽然在金额上有突变，但陪审员的判罚变化并未明确显现对法律条文的意识。引入特定的责任分配例外规则或可有效缓解受害者补偿不足的问题。

title: A User-Item Aware Encoding Framework for Short Video
authors: Weihui Deng, He Liu, Bin Wang, Xiaocheng Li, Deliang Fu, Zhen Wang
abstract: Traditional encoding methods from the Professional Generated Content (PGC) era face significant challenges due to two unique characteristics of user-generated short videos: massive daily uploads (reaching hundreds of millions) and heterogeneous content-consumer relationships (varying video quality and diverse consumer contexts). To address these challenges, we propose UIAE (User-Item Aware Encoding), a novel multiple bitrate ladder group encoding method comprising three key components: 1) Establishing user-item relationships via rule-based or DNN-based models; 2) Developing local optimization models maximizing Quality of Experience (QoE) for sub-populations based on contextual consumption patterns; 3) Deriving globally optimal encoding strategies through hierarchical model integration. Experimental results demonstrate that the UIAE framework adaptively adjusts encoding outcomes for distinct user groups with varying context profiles, ensuring optimal QoE for end viewers. We have deployed the UIAE method into the online pipeline, handling tens of millions of video transcoding tasks daily.
comment: Accepted to ICASSP 2026 (ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE Int. Conf. on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing). Author's preprint version, 5 pages, 4 figures, 1 table
zh_title: 面向短视频的用户-项感知编码框架
translation: 传统PGC（专业生成内容）时代的编码方法由于用户生成短视频的两个独特特征而面临严峻挑战：海量每日上传（达到数亿）和异构的内容-消费者关系（视频质量不同且消费者情境多样）。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了UIAE（用户-项感知编码），一种新颖的多比特率阶梯组编码方法，包含三个关键组成部分：1）通过基于规则或DNN（深度神经网络）的模型建立用户-项关系；2）开发最大化基于情境消费模式的子群体体验质量（QoE）的局部优化模型；3）通过分层模型集成推导出全局最优编码策略。实验结果表明，UIAE框架能够为具有不同情境特征的区分用户群体自适应地调整编码结果，确保最终用户的最佳QoE。我们已将UIAE方法部署到在线流程中，每日处理数千万的视频转码任务。
tldr: 提出了一种名为UIAE的用户-项感知编码框架，通过用户-项关系、局部优化和分层模型集成来解决海量用户生成短视频的编码挑战，以最大化用户体验。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的用户-项感知编码框架（UIAE），有效解决了短视频领域面临的独特编码挑战。通过结合用户行为、内容特征和消费情境，该方法在提升用户体验方面取得了显著成效，并成功进行了实际部署，具有重要的理论和应用价值。未来可以进一步探索更精细化的用户群体划分和更动态的编码策略。
motivation: 传统PGC编码方法难以应对用户生成短视频的海量上传和异构内容-消费者关系等挑战。
method: UIAE框架包括三个部分：1）建立用户-项关系；2）开发最大化子群体体验质量（QoE）的局部优化模型；3）通过分层模型集成推导出全局最优编码策略。
results: 实验表明，UIAE框架能够为具有不同上下文特征的不同用户群体自适应地调整编码结果，确保最终用户的最佳QoE。该方法已成功部署并处理大量视频转码任务。
conclusion: UIAE框架通过考虑用户-项关系和消费情境，能够有效地为用户生成短视频实现自适应编码，从而优化用户体验。

title: Self-Orthogonal Minimal Codes from n-to-1 Mappings
authors: Qin Du, Ziling Heng, Jun Zhang
abstract: Self-orthogonal codes are central to the construction of quantum error-correcting codes, and minimal codes yield secret-sharing schemes whose access structures are read off from the supports of their codewords. A code that is both self-orthogonal and minimal therefore serves both purposes at once, so that a single family of codes can produce a quantum code and a secret-sharing scheme simultaneously. Linear codes arising from n-to-1 mappings over finite fields are a natural source of such codes and have attracted considerable attention recently, yet their parameters and weight distributions remain difficult to determine: for most high-degree functions the Walsh spectra cannot be computed directly, and it is precisely these weights on which the analysis of minimality and self-orthogonality rests. We address this difficulty through the algebraic theory of skew polynomial rings. Using the right greatest common divisor of skew polynomials, we determine the dimensions of the kernel spaces of the linearized polynomials associated with the n-to-1 mappings, which in turn yield the weight distributions of the corresponding codes. With this method we treat two newly constructed families of n-to-1 functions together with one known family, and obtain the exact weight distributions of the resulting codes; we further prove that all of these codes are minimal and self-orthogonal. Each family therefore simultaneously yields a quantum error-correcting code and a secret-sharing scheme, with explicitly determined parameters and access structures. This work offers a new perspective for determining the parameters of linear codes derived from n-to-1 mappings.
translation: 自正交码在构造量子纠错码方面起着核心作用，而最小码则产生其访问结构可从其码字支撑中读出的秘密共享方案。一个同时是自正交和最小的码因此可以同时服务于这两个目的，使得单一的码族可以同时产生量子码和秘密共享方案。源自有限域上n-to-1映射产生的线性码是这类码的自然来源，并引起了相当大的关注，但它们的参数和权重分布仍然难以确定：对于大多数高次函数，Walsh 谱无法直接计算，而这正是分析最小性和自正交性所必需的。我们通过斜多项式环的代数理论来解决这一困难。利用斜多项式的右最大公约数，我们确定了与n-to-1映射相关的线性化多项式的核空间维度，这反过来又产生了相应码的权重分布。利用这种方法，我们处理了两个新构造的n-to-1函数族以及一个已知的函数族，并获得了所产生码的精确权重分布；我们进一步证明了所有这些码都是最小且自正交的。因此，每个族都同时产生一个量子纠错码和一个秘密共享方案，并明确确定了参数和访问结构。这项工作为确定源自n-to-1映射的线性码的参数提供了一个新的视角。
tldr: 通过使用代数理论中的斜多项式环，我们解决了确定线性码的参数和权重分布的难题，特别是那些源自n-to-1映射的码。我们成功地计算了两个新构造的n-to-1函数族和一个已知函数族产生的码的权重分布，并证明了它们是最小且自正交的，从而可以同时用于量子纠错码和秘密共享方案。
ai_comments: 该研究巧妙地利用代数理论中的斜多项式环来解决确定线性码参数的难题，特别是那些源自n-to-1映射的码。通过精确计算权重分布并证明其最小和自正交的性质，该方法成功地实现了同时构造量子纠错码和秘密共享方案的目标。这为设计更高效的编码方案提供了新的思路和工具，但其在实际大规模应用中的计算复杂度和效率仍需进一步评估。
motivation: 线性码源自n-to-1映射，它们同时具有自正交和最小码的性质，可用于构造量子纠错码和秘密共享方案。然而，确定这类码的参数和权重分布非常困难，因为对于高次函数，其 Walsh 谱难以直接计算，而这正是分析最小性和自正交性所必需的。
method: 利用斜多项式环的代数理论，通过右最大公约数来确定与n-to-1映射相关的线性化多项式的核空间维度，进而得到相应码的权重分布。对两个新构造的n-to-1函数族和一个已知函数族进行了分析。
results: 成功确定了三个n-to-1函数族产生的码的精确权重分布，并证明了所有这些码都是最小且自正交的。每个码族都同时产生一个量子纠错码和一个秘密共享方案，其参数和访问结构已明确确定。
conclusion: 通过代数理论中的斜多项式环，我们提出了一种新方法来确定源自n-to-1映射的线性码的参数和权重分布。该方法成功应用于三个函数族，证明了它们产生的码是最小且自正交的，从而实现了同时构造量子纠错码和秘密共享方案的目标。

title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
authors: Zeming Fei, Hongming Fei, Yi Xu, Xiaoyang Wang, Ying Zhang
abstract: Request-derived authorizers such as Progent protect LLM agents from prompt injection by deriving what an agent may do from the user's request. Their guarantee rests on attribution: the request is taken to be what the user said. Compaction breaks it. At every automatic compaction we observed, Claude Code and Codex placed a model-written summary of earlier turns as a user message, so the compactor's quotation of the user, documents and injected text reads as the user speaking. Because a policy frozen at the first request lets the agent finish few later tasks, we let Progent derive its policy for each request, and find that what it grants then follows what the compactor wrote. Even a payee the user stated is not safe: when an attacker's notice states another account as plain data and the user asks to pay the rent, the policy derived from a frontier compactor's summary admits the notice's account in 91% of cases, and the one derived from the user's own words in none. The cause is general: we prove that an authorizer that cannot see who wrote which bytes cannot treat a forged record differently from the legitimate one it imitates by more than the two are distinguishable, and that the bound is tight. Frontier compactors bear this out: they mark injected instructions, which have no legitimate twin, but rarely injected data, which does. What a compactor keeps, and how it marks it, is a security parameter. The fix follows from attribution: the authorizer credits only what the user said, authenticated on arrival and carried verbatim across the boundary, while the agent still reads the summary. We prove that it then receives exactly that text or nothing, so an attacker can block the policy but cannot shape it, and adaptive attacks on our implementation confirm it. In 40 attacked AgentDojo episodes re-run with the fix, no attacker action completes while the agent reads the summary.
zh_title: LLM Agent 授权跨越上下文压缩
translation: 请求派生的授权程序（例如Progent）通过从用户请求中推导出代理可能执行的操作来保护LLM代理免受提示注入的侵害。它们的保证基于归因：请求被视为用户所说的内容。压缩破坏了这一点。在我们观察到的每次自动压缩中，Claude Code和Codex都将早期对话的机器生成的摘要作为用户消息插入，因此压缩器对用户、文档和注入文本的引用被视为用户在说话。由于在第一次请求时固定的策略允许代理完成一些后续任务，因此我们让Progent为每个请求推导其策略，并发现当时授予的内容遵循了压缩器的写入内容。即使是用户指定的收款人也不安全：当攻击者的通知将另一个账户作为纯数据陈述，而用户要求支付租金时，从前端压缩器的摘要推导出的策略允许在91%的情况下接受通知中的账户，而在用户自己的话中推导出的策略则为0%。原因是普遍的：我们证明，无法区分字节来源的授权程序，其允许的范围与被模仿的合法记录相比，不会超过两者之间的可区分性，而且这个界限是精确的。前端压缩器证实了这一点：它们标记了注入的指令，这些指令没有合法的对应物，但很少标记注入的数据，因为它们有合法的对应物。压缩器保留的内容以及它的标记方式是一个安全参数。解决方法源于归因：授权程序仅信任在到达时经过身份验证并逐字传递到边界的内容，而代理仍然读取摘要。我们证明，它随后接收到的文本要么是该文本，要么是什么都没有，因此攻击者可以阻止该策略，但不能塑造它，我们实现中的自适应攻击也证实了这一点。在用修复方法重新运行的40次AgentDojo情节的攻击中，没有攻击者的行为在代理读取摘要时完成。
tldr: 上下文压缩技术会破坏LLM Agent的安全机制，因为模型生成的摘要会被误认为是用户输入，导致安全漏洞。研究提出了一种新的授权方法，通过验证用户输入来源来解决此问题，并证明了其有效性。
ai_comments: 这项研究揭示了LLM Agent在上下文压缩过程中一个关键的安全漏洞，并提供了一个有效的解决方案。然而，实际部署中，如何高效且准确地验证信息来源，以及处理各种复杂的交互场景，仍然是需要进一步探索的挑战。此外，对于不同压缩策略和不同模型的影响也需要更深入的分析。
motivation: 现有的LLM Agent安全机制（如Progent）依赖于用户请求的归因，但上下文压缩技术会破坏这一假设，导致安全漏洞。
method: 提出了一种新的授权方法，该方法允许Progent为每个请求动态推导策略，并只信任用户明确提供的数据。通过在AgentDojo环境中进行攻击性测试来验证该方法的有效性。
results: 在91%的情况下，攻击者可以利用上下文压缩的摘要将付款账户更改为攻击者指定的账户。新提出的安全机制在40次攻击测试中成功阻止了所有攻击。
conclusion: 上下文压缩技术对LLM Agent的安全构成了严重威胁。通过严格验证用户输入来源并仅信任用户明确提供的数据，可以有效解决这些安全问题。

title: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy
authors: Zeming Fei, Hongming Fei, Jingwen Chen, Xiaoyang Wang, Prosanta Gope, Biplab Sikdar, Ying Zhang
abstract:
Coding agents let plugins and remote services answer permission prompts, and Claude Code documents that such an answer cannot override the operator's deny rules. However, we show that this guarantee, checked one decision at a time, fails over a whole run, because an answer to one permission prompt can rewrite the policy that every later answer is checked against. For example, a remote service with no access to the operator's files approves an unrelated command and attaches an update that deletes the deny rule protecting the project's secrets. The agent then reads the secrets in that session and the next, even inside the vendor's strict sandbox. The root cause is that Claude Code checks only updates that add or replace allow rules. Relays that forward such deletions already exist, including the vendor's own Remote Control. In effect, the right to answer a prompt has become the right to administer the policy. Worse, the deletion leaves the same records as a local edit by the operator, so Claude Code cannot tell who wrote a rule.
  More generally, what a runtime records decides what it can safely delegate. A runtime that cannot tell who wrote a rule can accept only updates that keep every currently denied call denied, whereas, to protect every party's restrictions, a runtime that records who wrote each rule can let each party remove only the restrictions proven to be its own. We prove that these two bounds are tight. They correctly predict whether the operator's restrictions survive in all thirteen permission designs across ten agent systems, including predictions we wrote down before running Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, and Goose. Enforcing the bounds at the shared update step blocks the attack. A survey of 2,227 fetched marketplace plugins finds only two that send policy updates.

title: MoGe-4D: Efficient, Flexible, and Unified Dense 4D Reconstruction and Tracking
authors: Ruicheng Wang, Linlin Xin, Sicheng Xu, Jianfeng Xiang, Zelong Lv, Yu Deng, Yue Dong, Guangzhong Sun, Tong Zhang, Jiaolong Yang
abstract: Reconstructing dynamic scenes from RGB video requires reasoning about both 3D geometry and motion across viewpoints, yet existing methods either split reconstruction and tracking into fragmented pipelines or face prohibitive dense spatiotemporal decoding costs. We introduce MoGe-4D, a feed-forward framework that unifies geometry and motion prediction via ordered queries of paired allocentric and egocentric dynamic point maps. Each query maps source pixels to a target time simultaneously in both camera frames, resolving relative camera pose in closed form while flexibly serving depth, dynamic registration, and dense 3D tracking. For efficient dense querying, MoGe-4D decouples scene modeling from query decoding: a high-capacity context encoder caches coarse global spatiotemporal features once, while a lightweight query encoder rapidly decodes dense point maps at flexible resolutions. Furthermore, as supervising dense 4D queries demands continuous 3D correspondences whose raw trajectory storage is prohibitive, we introduce RigIDTrack, a synthetic data pipeline and dataset that compresses surface dynamics into rigidity-regularized affine bodies, recovering exact arbitrary-frame 3D trajectories with $\sim15\%$ storage overhead over RGB-D video. Across diverse benchmarks, MoGe-4D achieves state-of-the-art dense 3D tracking, matches dedicated 3D foundation models in reconstruction, and runs substantially faster than prior 4D baselines.

title: What to Change, What to Keep: Experience-Evolving Agents for Video Recasting
authors: Shiying Zhang, Yuxia Zhu, Huaze Xue, Shengqi Dang, Yizhen Wu, Yijie Li
abstract: Video recasting aims to transform the entities and environments of existing videos into new visual worlds while preserving their essential actions and interactions. However, achieving coherent transformations remains challenging, as coordinated edits can disrupt the original event structure. In this paper, we introduce RecastAgent, an experience-guided agentic framework for source-conditioned video recasting that operates under frozen model weights. Our framework employs an Experience-Guided Planner to choose edit prompts and input video states under qualitative visual critique, allowing the agent to build upon partial progress or backtrack to preserve source structure. Across tasks, an Experience Accumulation module distills completed trajectories into conditional, evidence-linked principles that record both an editing strategy and its scope of validity. We additionally construct a benchmark of 67 source videos with 134 paired-specification tasks across six creative categories for evaluation. Experiments demonstrate that RecastAgent outperforms single-pass and agentic rewriting baselines across Bernini and Ditto. Furthermore, accumulated experience improves performance on held-out test videos and transfers zero-shot to external benchmarks like FiVE-Bench and VE-Bench.
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. The first three authors contributed equally to this work. Supplementary material is not included in this version
zh_title: 什么该改变，什么该保留：经验演化的视频重铸代理
translation: 视频重铸旨在将现有视频中的实体和环境转换为新的视觉世界，同时保留其基本动作和交互。然而，协调编辑可能会破坏原始事件结构，因此实现连贯的转换仍然是一个挑战。在本研究中，我们提出了一种名为RecastAgent的经验引导代理框架，用于源条件视频重铸，该框架在冻结模型权重的情况下运行。我们的框架采用经验引导规划器，在定性视觉评估下选择编辑提示和输入视频状态，使代理能够建立在部分进展的基础上或回溯以保留源结构。在整个任务中，经验积累模块将完成的轨迹提炼成条件化的、与证据相关联的原则，记录编辑策略及其有效范围。我们还构建了一个包含67个源视频和134个配对规范任务的基准，涵盖六个创意类别用于评估。实验表明，RecastAgent在Bernini和Ditto上均优于单通道和代理重写基线。此外，积累的经验提高了在未见过的测试视频上的性能，并且能够零样本迁移到FiVE-Bench和VE-Bench等外部基准。
tldr: 本研究提出了一种名为RecastAgent的经验引导代理框架，用于视频重铸，能在保持原有动作和交互的同时，将视频内容转换为新的视觉世界。该框架使用经验引导规划器和经验积累模块，能够在冻结模型权重的情况下进行视频编辑，并能从过去的编辑经验中学习，提高性能并实现零样本迁移到新基准。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的代理框架RecastAgent，用于解决视频重铸中的挑战。通过经验引导和积累，该方法在冻结模型权重的情况下实现了有效的视频转换，并展示了良好的泛化能力。其构建的基准测试也为该领域的研究提供了有力的支持。
motivation: 视频重铸旨在将现有视频中的实体和环境转换为新的视觉世界，同时保留其基本动作和交互。然而，协调编辑可能会破坏原始事件结构，因此实现连贯的转换仍然是一个挑战。
method: 提出了一种名为RecastAgent的经验引导代理框架，用于源条件视频重铸。该框架使用经验引导规划器（Experience-Guided Planner）来选择编辑提示和输入视频状态，并能在冻结模型权重的情况下进行操作。经验积累模块（Experience Accumulation module）将完成的轨迹提炼成条件化的、与证据相关联的原则，记录编辑策略及其有效范围。
results: RecastAgent在Bernini和Ditto数据集上超越了单通道和代理重写基线。此外，积累的经验提高了在未见过的测试视频上的性能，并且能够零样本迁移到外部基准，如FiVE-Bench和VE-Bench。
conclusion: RecastAgent通过经验学习和引导，有效地解决了视频重铸中的挑战，实现了更连贯和高质量的视频转换，并展示了良好的泛化能力。

title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation
authors: Indra Agustian, Ruvita Faurina
abstract: Solar filaments are cool, dense chromospheric plasma structures held by magnetic field lines above polarity inversion lines. Their destabilization triggers coronal mass ejections and severe space weather hazards. Segmenting individual filaments from ground-based GONG H-alpha observations (2048 x 2048 pixels) is challenging due to low contrast, turbulent fibrils, delicate barb structures, and annotator boundary variance. In this technical report, we describe SolarFilNet-V4, a targeted segmentation framework developed for the MAGFiLO 1.0 benchmark (Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026). Our method couples a lightweight Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions (k=15) and dual-frequency feed-forward blocks (DFFN) to follow extended flux ropes while capturing thin central spines. A shallow full-resolution convolutional branch operating at 1024 x 1024 preserves high-frequency edge details and mitigates transformer downsampling. We train the network using multi-task supervision over masks, centerline spines, barb boundaries, and pixel-contrastive representations. At test time, we apply 8-fold dihedral test-time augmentation (D4), bilinearly upscale predictions to the native 2048 x 2048 grid, and apply an activity-adaptive post-processing routine that calibrates morphological joining parameters for quiet versus active solar disks. On the official benchmark, SolarFilNet-V4 achieves an out-of-fold validation Panoptic Quality of 0.4340 and a Public Leaderboard score of 0.380. The model contains 15.46M parameters and requires 224.34 GFLOPs per forward pass, reducing parameter count by 36.8% compared to standard ResNet-34 U-Net baselines.
comment: 4 pages, 1 figure, IEEE format, Technical Report for Kaggle Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026. Source code and model: https://github.com/indraagustian/SolarFilNet-V4-Kaggle2026
zh_title: 太阳丝网V4：用于太阳丝网分割的多尺度Transformer视觉与物理信息自适应后处理
translation: 太阳丝网是磁力线束缚在极性反转线上方的冷、密 chromospheric 等离子体结构。它们的失稳会触发日冕物质抛射和严重的空间天气灾害。从地面 GONG H-alpha 观测（2048 x 2048 像素）中分割单个丝网由于对比度低、纤维湍流、精细的刺结构以及标注者的边界差异而具有挑战性。在本技术报告中，我们描述了 SolarFilNet-V4，一个为 MAGFiLO 1.0 基准（太阳丝网分割挑战 2026）开发的定向分割框架。我们的方法将一个轻量级的金字塔视觉 Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) 主干与各向异性曲线条卷积 (k=15) 和双频前馈块 (DFFN) 相结合，以跟踪延长的磁力绳，同时捕捉细小的中心刺。一个在 1024 x 1024 分辨率下运行的浅层全分辨率卷积分支保留了高频边缘细节，并减轻了 transformer 的下采样。我们使用掩膜、中心线、刺边界和像素对比度表示的多任务监督来训练网络。在测试时，我们应用 8 折 dihedral test-time augmentation (D4)，将预测双线性上采样到原始的 2048 x 2048 网格，并应用一个活动自适应后处理例程，该例程校准了安静或活跃太阳盘的形态连接参数。在官方基准测试中，SolarFilNet-V4 实现了 0.4340 的离群验证集全景质量 (Panoptic Quality) 和 0.380 的公共排行榜分数。该模型包含 15.46M 参数，每次前向传播需要 224.34 GFLOPs，与标准的 ResNet-34 U-Net 基线相比，参数量减少了 36.8%。
tldr: 该论文提出了SolarFilNet-V4，一种用于太阳丝网分割的新型框架，结合了Transformer和卷积网络，并通过物理信息自适应后处理提高了精度，在MAGFiLO 1.0基准测试中取得了优异的成绩，同时减少了参数量和计算量。
ai_comments: 该研究在太阳丝网分割领域取得了显著进展，提出的SolarFilNet-V4模型在结合Transformer和CNN方面表现出色，并且通过多任务学习和自适应后处理提高了分割精度。然而，其计算复杂度（224.34 GFLOPs）对于实时应用可能仍需进一步优化。
motivation: 太阳丝网的分割对于理解可能引发空间天气事件的日冕物质抛射至关重要，但由于其低对比度、复杂的结构和标注不一致性，分割任务具有挑战性。
method: SolarFilNet-V4框架结合了轻量级金字塔视觉Transformer（PVT-v2-B1）骨干网络、各向异性曲线条卷积和双频前馈网络（DFFN），并利用一个浅层全分辨率卷积分支来保留高频细节。训练采用多任务监督（掩膜、中心线、刺边界、像素对比度表示）。在测试时，采用8折 dihedral test-time augmentation（D4），双线性上采样预测，并应用活动自适应后处理来校准形态连接参数。
results: SolarFilNet-V4在MAGFiLO 1.0基准测试中取得了0.4340的验证集全景质量（Panoptic Quality）和0.380的公共排行榜分数。该模型拥有15.46M参数，每次前向传播需要224.34 GFLOPs，与标准的ResNet-34 U-Net基线相比，参数量减少了36.8%。
conclusion: SolarFilNet-V4通过结合先进的深度学习架构和物理信息后处理，成功解决了太阳丝网分割的挑战，并在基准测试中取得了最先进的性能，同时实现了更高的效率。

title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
authors: Henry Castillo, Yanchen Liu, Claudio Mayrink Verdun, Dylan Hadfield-Menell
abstract: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. These models repurpose a single input channel for both instructions and data, leading to common failure modes where the model mistakenly treats data as instructions such as intentional jailbreaks and unintentional in-context alignment drift. To correct this, we propose a pretraining method and architecture that separates the two from the very start, producing Mancelle-3B. An encoder processes high-level semantic features of upcoming text with cross-attention that prevents the token stream from writing back into this control channel. During pretraining, the model learns to rely on these features to predict the next token, turning the channel into an effective handle for steering the model. Mancelle-3B steers more strongly than prompt- and activation-based methods on comparable open models while maintaining fluency, and it withstands adversarial black-box and soft-prompt counter-steering that defeats those baselines. We reproduce this against a more controlled baseline with Mancelle-400M. Our results show that robust control can be built into language models if we do so early and intentionally.

title: SplatTok: Data-Driven Compression of 3D Gaussian Splats with Scene-Level Tokens
authors: Sai Karthikey Pentapati, Shashank Nelamangala Sridhara, Birendra Kathariya, Peng Yin, Guandao Yang, Alan C. Bovik
abstract: 3D Gaussian splats enable real-time rendering but require substantial storage. Existing compression methods either encode the primitives of a given splat or optimize a compact representation independently for each scene. Yet a Gaussian splat is only one realization of a scene: different arrangements of primitives can produce nearly identical rendered views. We exploit this freedom on the decoding side with SplatTok, a learned scene-resynthesis codec. Trained across thousands of real-world scenes, a transformer encodes an existing splat into compact, spatially anchored latent tokens, and a shared decoder synthesizes a new set of standard Gaussian primitives without preserving correspondence to the input. The representation is learned through rendering supervision rather than primitive reconstruction. At compression time, a quantization-aware latent search refines only the scene code, keeping the networks frozen, and closes most of the encoder's remaining error. On standard benchmarks, using only renders of the input splat for the latent search, without the original training images, SplatTok matches the PSNR of the feed-forward codec FCGS with 4 to 6.5 times smaller files, compressing input splats about 75 to 110 times. With the training images, it exceeds the PSNR of the per-scene method HAC++ with 13 to 41% smaller files. A single model trained on DL3DV generalizes to unseen scenes with millions of Gaussians and supports multiple target rates without retraining.

title: Who gets the information? An $α$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection
authors: Zhenzhi Tang
abstract: Recent information-theoretic filters for multi-label feature selection disagree on how to distribute relevance over labels: some amplify features that inform a few labels, others balance what every label receives. We show these choices are implicit social welfare functions. Treating labels as agents whose utility is the information they receive, we propose FLIC, which greedily maximises the $α$-fair welfare of per-label information coverage. A single parameter $α$ moves from utilitarian ($α=0$) through proportionally fair ($α=1$) to max-min selection ($α\to\infty$), and a dozen published relevance terms lie on this axis, most as special cases, first-order approximations or limits. The objective is monotone submodular for every $α\ge0$ whenever each label's information is, so greedy selection is a $(1-1/e)$-approximation; this fails for $α<0$, and the max-min limit is inapproximable. Fano's and the Hellman-Raviv inequalities tie raw coverage to the Bayes Hamming loss and normalised coverage to per-label relative error. FLIC uses bias-corrected, label-wise conditional information and has no relevance-redundancy trade-off parameter. On 22 data sets, FLIC is the best of 14 information-theoretic filters on seven of nine metrics, winning 86 of 117 pairwise comparisons significantly and losing none significantly. Among 17 methods it ranks first on ranking loss, coverage and macro-AUC with two classifiers and has the best mean rank (narrowly with ML-kNN), while three embedded methods lead on Hamming loss, one-error and micro-F1.
comment: 25 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Supplementary material is provided as an ancillary file

title: Seeing Is Not Reaching: Instruction Shortcuts Override Visual Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Qing Zhang, Xuesong Li, Zhaoyuan Yang, Changlin Song, Xinyu Tian, Jing Zhang
abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are expected to inherit visual grounding from vision-language models, yet often reach for an object's training location after it has been moved. Across six VLAs, we identify two shortcuts: a scene shortcut, where the arm follows the scene's original task despite a new instruction, and an instruction shortcut, where the instruction retrieves the requested object's training location. In $π_{0.5}$, the instruction shortcut persists even though object-name attention follows the moved target. We call this Seeing Is Not Reaching. To determine whether this grounding is unused or overridden, we separately mask an image-mediated grounding pathway and a direct instruction-to-action pathway. Masking the grounding pathway eliminates reaches to moved targets, whereas masking the direct pathway increases them. Thus, grounding already guides action but is often overridden by the instruction shortcut, which acts through the direct pathway. We introduce Pathway-Separated Guidance (PSG), which amplifies grounding and suppresses the shortcut without training or external target locations. On LIBERO-PRO Object under Position perturbations, PSG raises the target-reaching rate from 22.0% to 52.6% and task success from 16.6% to 40.8%, while largely preserving performance on the original tasks.
comment: 31 pages, including supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/QZhang2111/psg

title: When the Miner is the Generator: Rethinking the Separation Axiom in LLM-Driven Data Mining
authors: Xi Chen, Mengke Li
abstract: The theoretical foundation of data mining implicitly relies on an unstated premise, the Separation Axiom (SA), which assumes that mining tools and the data being analyzed are epistemologically independent. However, this premise is increasingly challenged by the emergence of LLM-driven AI agents that actively participate in data generation. We argue that this shift leads to a new epistemic failure mode, which we term ontological self-reference, where discovered patterns may reflect the inductive biases of the tools rather than the underlying structure of the data. This raises fundamental concerns about the credibility of knowledge discovery and the risk of self-reinforcing epistemic loops, where inferred patterns may reflect model-internal biases rather than the underlying structure of the data. We therefore call for a rethinking of the data mining paradigm in the era of large language models, grounded in an SA-aware theoretical foundation and extended to system-level epistemic safeguards. We argue that such a shift is necessary to conceptually rearm the discipline, preventing future knowledge discovery from collapsing into self-justifying algorithmic echo chambers.

title: ArEssays: Towards Robust Arabic Handwritten Text Understanding in Educational Settings
authors: Hamdy Mubarak, Anas Madkoor, Ehsaneddin Asgari, Majd Hawasly
abstract:
Automated understanding of handwritten Arabic student essays remains challenging due to script complexity and high variability
  in children's writing. We introduce ArEssays, a large-scale dataset of authentic essays from primary to secondary students
  across Egypt, with both verbatim transcriptions and linguistically corrected versions. We benchmark 34 vision-language and OCR
  models, including fine-tuned systems, and find large performance gaps on real student handwriting. We release the dataset,
  training pipelines, and results to support research in Arabic OCR, document understanding, and educational NLP.

title: FlashSegmentator: High-Throughput TotalSegmentator Inference without Loss of Accuracy
authors: Yosuke Yamagishi, Tomohiro Kikuchi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe
abstract: Purpose: To develop, evaluate, and publicly release FlashSegmentator, an open-source inference pipeline that increases the throughput of TotalSegmentator without retraining or loss of segmentation accuracy. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study used public datasets: 73 CT examinations from the TotalSegmentator test split (median age, 65 years; 37 male, 35 female, one unknown), 30 abdominal CT examinations from the Beyond the Cranial Vault (BTCV) dataset, 512 training-split CT examinations for concurrent-process analysis, and 55 MRI examinations. FlashSegmentator adds static-shape compilation, pipelining, batched sliding-window inference, and GPU postprocessing. Throughput was compared with the reference implementation (including its lower-resolution modes) and FastSegmentator on GH200, A100, and T4 GPUs. Dice agreement was tested with two one-sided tests (margin, +/-0.01). Results: FlashSegmentator processed 3782, 1810, and 270 examinations per hour on the GH200, A100, and T4 (57.7, 33.9, and 6.4 times the reference implementation and 3.20, 2.50, and 1.22 times compiled FastSegmentator). Dice scores were equivalent for all 117 structures on every GPU (mean difference <= 1.2 x 10^-5; P < .001) and at the examination level on BTCV. In contrast, the lower-resolution modes of the reference implementation processed 181 and 213 examinations per hour on the A100 but reduced mean Dice by 0.116 and 0.241. On MRI, throughput increased 94-fold with all 50 structures equivalent. Estimated A100 cloud cost per 10,000 examinations decreased from 997 to 29 US dollars. Conclusion: FlashSegmentator increased the throughput of TotalSegmentator on data center and entry-level GPUs without loss of segmentation accuracy compared with the reference implementation.
comment: 19 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables; supplementary material included. Code: https://github.com/yamagishi0824/FlashSegmentator

title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
authors: Zifei Wang, Wei Wen, Qiang Ji, Qian-Wen Zhang, Ruizhi Qiao, He Liu, Xing Sun, Qiang Lin
abstract: Multimodal retrieval must match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools and memory. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. We present OmniEVIE, a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64 (9,472 bytes, or 8.82 GiB per million records), providing a mean vector, 1-bit signs, and int8 multi-vectors for coarse, middle, and final search while localizing each hit to a page region or video interval. Training, merging, indexing, and retrieval are co-designed: all tasks share one retrieval format, a three-grade evidence check removes false negatives, dynamic sampling follows the baseline-teacher gap, candidates are compressed with ST-HAC during training to match the index, stage-wise and specialist models are merged by parameter block, and a saliency gate with a noise floor refines query scoring. Trained on public datasets, OmniEVIE scores 60.68 (full d=2048 sequence) and 60.06 (K128 x d64 int8 index) on MMEB-V3 (190 tasks), 77.96 on MMEB-V2 (78 tasks), and 62.96 on ViDoRe V3 (48 tasks). On 1M and 5M records, a single-thread query takes 54.2 ms and 120.2 ms (11.1x and 25.3x faster than exact 4096-d single-vector search; 236x and 532x faster than full int8 MaxSim). Video is encoded directly from frames without a parsing model: on QVHighlights (1,083 queries), the peak falls inside the labeled segment for 78.0% of queries and the returned span (18% of video length) intersects it for 94.3% vs. 44.9% random. Weights and code: https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B and https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE.

title: Parity-check matrices and their MDS or NMDS properties for several classes of non-GRS type linear codes
authors: Zhonghao Liang, Chenlu Jia, Qunying Liao
abstract: Parity-check matrices and weight distributions are important for understanding the structure and performance of linear codes. However, obtaining explicit expressions for them is often challenging. In recent years, numerous families of non-GRS type linear codes have been constructed, motivated by applications in coding theory and cryptography. For many of these codes, explicit parity-check matrices remain unavailable, hindering further investigation of their duality properties, decoding methods, and weight distributions. In this paper, we first develop a method for constructing parity-check matrices using code extensions and Cramer's rule, and then apply this method or through direct constructions to obtain explicit parity-check matrices for column-twisted generalized Reed--Solomon codes (TGRS), modified GRS codes and so on. Second, we introduce the $(Ł,¶)$-twisted generalized Roth--Lempel (TGRL) code $\C_{k,\ell}(Ł,¶,\A_{m\times m},\B)$, obtain explicit parity-check matrices for three subclasses through direct constructions, and establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $\C_{k,\ell}(Ł,¶,\A_{2\times 2},\B)$ with the most general $Ł$, $¶$, and $\B$ to be maximum distance separable (MDS). For one-column TGRS codes, we prove that they are either MDS or near MDS (NMDS), furthermore, establish a necessary and sufficient condition for them to be NMDS, and determine the weight distribution of a family of these NMDS codes using subset sums in finite abelian groups. Finally, basing on known results for non-GRS properties of TGRS codes, we establish sufficient conditions for these codes considered in this paper to be non-GRS from the perspective of punctured codes.

title: EvoSearch: Self-Evolving Active Perception for Wide-Area Geospatial Search
authors: Zhenghao Xie, Jing Xiao, Zihao Yu, Wanyi Yu, Liang Liao, Gui-Song Xia, Mi Wang
abstract: Geospatial search is fundamental to resource surveys and environmental monitoring, requiring the discovery of relevant evidence across large geographic areas and multiple spatial scales. Existing active perception methods adaptively select observation locations and scales to improve search efficiency, yet their search trajectories become increasingly long and costly as the search area expands. A key limitation is that final-answer correctness alone provides little guidance on which observations to retain and when to stop, hindering efficient wide-area search. To address this challenge, we propose EvoSearch, a self-evolving active perception framework that co-evolves the perception policy and exploration program to compress search trajectories while preserving answer quality. Specifically, quality-cost comparisons between completed branches from shared evidence train the policy to acquire useful observations, avoid redundant ones, and stop when sufficient evidence is available. Execution feedback from the updated policy then guides exploration-program revision, adapting experience generation to the policy's changing observation needs. We further introduce GeoSearchBench, a benchmark for evaluating search quality and visual processing efficiency through relational search and region search. Experiments demonstrate that EvoSearch shortens search trajectories and substantially reduces visual processing while maintaining overall search quality, supporting scalable active perception for wide-area geospatial search.

title: XMind: Thinking Twice via Cross-Memory Reasoning for LLM-Based Autonomous Driving
authors: Zuyi Guo, Xianjie Dai, Lei Yang, Xiaocong Zhao, Jingguang Li, Kitae Jang, Heye Huang
abstract: Memory-augmented large language model (LLM) driving agents can reuse past experience, yet previously learned corrections often fail to transfer when traffic conditions change. A key limitation is that existing memories mainly record observed outcomes, providing little evidence about alternative actions. We introduce XMind, a training-free framework that enables LLM-based driving to "Think Twice" through cross-memory reasoning. XMind integrates working memory of recent traffic states with episodic memory of critical risk events. The agent first makes an initial decision from the current context and then cross-checks it against retrieved historical experience. If a conflict arises, it makes a second decision guided by the retrieved evidence. To construct reliable episodic memory, XMind evaluates alternative actions through counterfactual rollouts under perturbed traffic conditions and stores the verified outcomes as structured risk capsules. These capsules are retrieved by jointly matching spatial risk patterns and scenario semantics. Across closed-loop highway simulations, XMind achieves success rates of 83.3-93.3%, exceeding the strong baseline by 6.6 percentage points on average. Evaluation on K-Risk further demonstrates lower decision risk on unseen real-world high-risk interactions. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of working memory, risk-text retrieval, and counterfactual verification. Code is available at https://github.com/xiangxiangliuwo/XMind

title: Vx: A Programming Language for Scalable, Maintainable and Secure Systems
authors: Aditya Kumar
abstract: A program for a modern machine runs on several kinds of chips. Its memory spaces, links and capacities are invisible to the compilers of today. So a host that reads device memory, a working set that does not fit, or a data race shows up only when the program runs. Vx is a systems programming language that puts these facts in the program text. A machine is a source file of declarations. A value's type says which memory it lives in. Apart from one stated exception, a function's signature is the whole contract that its callers see. A flag lists the code and the facts that the compiler trusts without a proof. This report is a tour of the language at one commit. It describes six design principles, the core language, and the features that serve three qualities. Vx is scalable because one program text runs across machines, cores and GPU threads. With an option, the compiler also checks its function bodies in parallel. It is maintainable because a signature is the contract of a function and most diagnostics have codes. The output of the parallel compiler does not depend on the number of threads. It is secure because safe code has ownership, borrow, race and placement checks, and in safe code, a file or a socket of the standard library opens only with a right. For every feature, the report gives its status and the evidence for it. It also lists where the implementation does not yet meet the design.

title: NativeDrive: Native Multimodal Foundations for Autonomous Driving
authors: Zehua Fan, Qi Jiang, Wei Li, Kai Tang, Yue Jiang, Yujian Li, Bailin Li, Feng Gao, Yan Wang, Kun Zhan
abstract: Autonomous driving requires semantic understanding and fine-grained scene perception for precise action prediction. Vision-language-action models (VLAs) inherit semantic priors, but low-dimensional action labels provide limited structural supervision. Some studies extend VLAs with visual generation tasks or adopt video-based world-action models (WAMs), but both approaches introduce appearance-reconstruction overhead, which is less relevant to planning. Native multimodal models offer an alternative to unify understanding and generation within one backbone. On this basis, we propose NativeDrive, a native encoder-free multimodal driving framework adapting the unified backbone for policy learning and introduce a dense supervision task tailored to driving. The Native Action Interface reuses the understanding expert's token-prediction interface for the discrete policy and adapts the generation expert for continuous policy. Driving Semantic Editing reuses the generation expert's editing capability for dense scene-structure supervision during training, while inference runs only the selected planning policy. NativeDrive achieves competitive planning performance among unified understanding-and-generation models on NAVSIM v1 and v2, with ablations validating its components' effectiveness. Code will be released.
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables, including supplementary material

title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation
authors: Pengyu Hou, Mingfei Han, Haihong Hao, Xiaolong Wu, Bo Dong, Xiaojun Chang, Salman Khan, Bin Shi
abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to relate past experience, current spatial state, and future motion while following natural-language instructions. Recent approaches improve these capabilities through long-horizon memory, state-aware reasoning, and future prediction, yet these components are often modeled separately, leaving navigation state evolution insufficiently connected across time. We argue that camera pose provides a natural geometric representation for bridging past, present, and future states. Based on this insight, we propose PoseVLN, a pose-aware VLN framework that jointly learns navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. PoseVLN organizes visual memory and the current observation in an episode-relative coordinate frame, and jointly predicts the next K navigation actions together with a local $Δ$Pose over the same horizon. The predicted $Δ$Pose is composed with the current trajectory-level pose to obtain the future pose state, which is recursively propagated throughout navigation, forming a continuous geometric state evolution from past memory to future motion. Experiments on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE Val-Unseen splits demonstrate the effectiveness of explicitly modeling geometric state evolution, with PoseVLN outperforming the strongest compared baselines by 2.6 and 2.9 percentage points in success rate, respectively, using only single RGB observations.
comment: 26 pages, 6 figures, including appendix. Project page: https://houpengyu123.github.io/PoseVLN/

title: Beyond Autoregression: Diffusion Language Model is All Analog In-Memory Computing Need
authors: Yuanuo Feng, Yubing Ye, Yizhe Chen, Wenshuai Yao, Ngai Wong, Wenyong Zhou, Wang Kang
abstract: Analog in-memory computing (AIMC) enables energy-efficient language-model inference, but hardware non-idealities perturb matrix--vector multiplications and degrade generation quality. Autoregressive (AR) models are especially vulnerable: each token is committed to the causal context at birth, so perturbation-induced errors cascade. We study diffusion language models (DLMs), which iteratively refine a masked sequence, as an alternative paradigm. Across scale-matched model pairs and open checkpoints, DLMs degrade more gracefully than AR counterparts under persistent weight perturbations. Controlled analyses rule out cross-round noise averaging and support delayed token commitment and progressive context resolution as the mechanism. A larger denoising-step budget further shrinks the clean--noisy gap, a DLM-specific latency--robustness knob. We perform large-scale simulation tests across diverse datasets and models using a noise model calibrated from real silicon measurements. Furthermore, on a 16-chip 28nm eFlash AIMC cluster, hybrid on-board measurements show DLMs tolerate $1.4$--$3\times$ larger weight noise, making diffusion-based generation a promising paradigm for noise-resilient AIMC inference.
comment: Accept by Design, Automation and Test in Europe Conference(DATE2027)

title: FaceNet versus VGG Features in Wasserstein Distortion for Face Image Compression
authors: Xinyu Wang, Jona Ballé
abstract: Wasserstein distortion (WD) compares local statistics of deep features and has been used to optimize learned image codecs for perceptual quality, but existing WD objectives rely on features from networks trained for generic image classification, such as VGG. We ask whether features from a face recognition network better reflect the perceived quality of compressed faces. In the Cool-Chic codec, we replace the VGG features in a WD-based objective with intermediate feature maps of FaceNet, and compare the two objectives on 20 LFW face images at a matched average bitrate of about 0.15 bits per pixel. In a preliminary pairwise human study, FaceNet-based reconstructions were preferred in 72.5% of judgments and by a majority of participants on 16 of the 20 images. These results suggest that the choice of feature network inside WD affects the perceived quality of face images, and that face recognition features are a promising direction for face-aware perceptual compression.

title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study
authors: Tim d'Hondt, Oleksii Furman, Damian Kwolek, Jan Poręba, Maciej Zieba, Mykola Pechenizkiy
abstract: Many applications of machine learning on tabular data need both a classifier and a generator of realistic records. The default is to train two separate models, whereas a single joint model promises both from one set of weights. Several families of tabular deep learning models can be turned into such a joint model, which raises the question of which joint model is preferable at which computational budget. In this empirical study, we introduce and compare joint models based on four state-of-the-art tabular data modeling families (energy-based models, probabilistic circuits, tabular foundation models and tabular diffusion models) against measured FLOPs and wall-clock time, on 29 classification datasets. Methods are evaluated based on two defined aggregate scores that take into account different aspects of prediction and generation. We then also compare these joint models with every pair of a separate classifier and generator at different computational budgets, to see when a joint model may be a defendible choice against the regular practice of keeping a separate classifier and generator. We find that the best joint model is a probabilistic circuit at the smallest budgets and, beyond that, a tabular foundation model that generates column by column using a regressor (TabICL). Compared with pairs of separate models, this study finds a joint model is rarely preferable but often very close to the best pair, without the hassle of training and maintaining two separate models.

title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining
authors: Boning Zhang, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu
abstract: Learning latent actions from unlabeled video sequences offers a promising way to acquire reusable action representations without relying on embodiment-specific control annotations. However, existing latent-action pretraining approaches commonly couple the modeling of visual transitions with action inference, directly mapping paired observations or derived transition cues into latent action codes. This formulation leaves two distinct tasks entangled: characterizing the relational structure of an observed transition and abstracting it into a compact action representation. We propose RELACT, a relation-first framework that explicitly separates transition relation modeling from predictive action abstraction. RELACT first constructs a structured relation representation $R$ that captures how visual elements and their interactions evolve across observations. It then infers a compact, state-conditioned stochastic latent action $U$, whose predictive effects are learned through action-conditioned latent dynamics. The resulting action representation can be grounded in native control spaces for model-based planning or used to supervise downstream embodied policies. Extensive experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain image-goal navigation, goal-conditioned manipulation, and downstream policy adaptation demonstrate improved predictive action representations and consistent gains in planning and control, supporting the effectiveness and generality of relation-first latent action pretraining.

title: ST-SfM: Spatio-Temporal Structure-from-Motion for Initialising 4D Gaussian Splatting
authors: Harshit, Sami Brandt
abstract: Dynamic Gaussian splatting is usually initialised either with random points or with a structure-from-motion (SfM) cloud of the first frame. Neither says anything about what moves, where and when. We introduce ST-SfM, a sparse spatio-temporal SfM for synchronised, calibrated multi-camera video that splits the scene into two branches. Static structure is detected once per camera on a temporal-median image, gated for temporal stability and matched along epi-polar lines. Motion is detected as space-time interest points (STIPs) in the video volume, described with HOG3D and matched only between candidates that agree both epipolarly and in time. Union-find tracks that refuse inconsistent merges are triangulated with RANSAC over all view pairs, giving static 3D points and dynamic 4D points (x, y, z, t) with sub-frame times. We use ST-SfM derived sparse 4D cloud to initialise 4D Gaussian splatting. In comparison with random initialisation on N3DV scenes we get improvements in PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS.

title: Relational Bottleneck Models
authors: Shin'ya Yamaguchi, Kosuke Nishida
abstract: Achieving both interpretable and high-performance inference is a key challenge in deep learning. While Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) provide inherent interpretability, they are constrained by task-specific training and rely on isolated visual concepts that fail to capture higher-order visual semantic relationships. Conversely, Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate zero-shot capabilities through Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. However, standard CoT lacks a strict causal dependency between the generated rationale and the final output, compromising faithfulness. To bridge this gap, we propose Relational Bottleneck Models (RBMs), a novel training-free framework that transforms any off-the-shelf LVLMs into inherently interpretable models in a plug-and-play manner. RBMs consist of two stages: (i) Structured Rationale Generation (SRG), which explicitly models semantic interactions between visual concepts as subject-predicate-object triplets, and (ii) Rationale-Grounded Decoding (RGD), which enforces a strict causal dependency between the rationales and the final output. RGD aggregates rationale-conditional next-token distributions via an importance-weighted product-of-experts strategy, strictly excluding the image inputs from the decoding context. Extensive zero-shot evaluations across diverse benchmarks and LVLM backbones demonstrate that RBMs achieve superior interpretability while improving task performance over CBM baselines, entirely without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Disentangling Visual Dynamics for World Model Planning
authors: Yuhong Shi, Yihan Guo, Jie Wei, Jianyi Liu, Jingwen Fu
abstract: Visual world models enable planning through predictive latent states. However, entangled agent and exogenous dynamics can obscure task progress. Disentangling visual dynamics for planning requires addressing two challenges: 1) suppressing cross-factor interference while retaining useful information; and 2) linking factors to task-relevant signals, since stability alone does not ensure meaningful planning distances. Therefore, we introduce FactorWorld, a disentangled visual dynamics framework for world model planning. To separate agent and exogenous dynamics, we propose a Counterfactual Consensus Residual Factorizer (CCRF) guided by bidirectional counterfactual pairs. CCRF separates shared context from dynamic residuals, combining average and worst-partner constraints to suppress interference with state and motion supervision to retain useful information. To translate these factors into planning decisions, we introduce semantic routing to refine full-representation task predictions for state estimation, trajectory scoring, and task-adapted planning. Experiments on MiniGrid, MetaDrive, and CARLA show improved bidirectional factor stability across two backbones. On MiniGrid, factor routing raises mean SR from 78.80% to 82.40%. Across four continuous control tasks, including Push-T, FactorWorld achieves mean success rates ranging from 91.67% to 100% across tasks. These results demonstrate that combining decoupled visual dynamics with explicit tasks can significantly improve the planning capabilities of world models.

title: Concurrent Visibility: Higher-Order Concurrency with First-Order Store
authors: Iwan Qu{é}merais, Guilh{è}me Jaber, Ken Sakayori, Davide Sangiorgi
abstract: We propose an Operational Game Semantics for a (call-by-value) concurrent higher-order language with first-order store (references may contain other references or first-order values such as integers or booleans; however they may not store higher-order values such as functions). We adapt the game-semantic notion of visibility, which semantically captures the absence of higher-order references and developed for sequential higher-order languages, to a concurrent setting. We thus define a complete-trace preorder, and prove it sound for the contextual preorder, by introducing a synchronization-based composition of semantic configurations and establishing an observational adequacy result. We also prove completeness for the subset of the language in which functions return first-order values. In contrast to the case of sequential visibility, in the labeled transition semantics we have to account for the presence of multiple active threads with possibly different visibilities, and of a tree-like structure for managing the dependencies among the threads so created. Moreover, we have to reason on families of traces, rather than single traces, as in concurrent setting the order among certain actions cannot be enforced.

title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
authors: Yujie Zhao, Anthony L. Hu, Zimeng Huang, Zhijing Wu, Luobin Wang, Richard Li, Shrivas Sudharsan, Henrik I. Christensen, Jishen Zhao
abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol that continuously advances environment time during model inference and control-interface delays, paired with time-sensitive metrics. Evaluating over 30 methods, we find that the best-performing approach is the trained VLA, yet it achieves only 8.3% temporal success even on Easy-level tasks, with persistent challenges in generalization and transfer. These findings reveal fundamental limitations in current robotic systems and highlight the need to jointly optimize physical competence, temporal reasoning, and execution latency.

title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
authors: Kaipeng Fang, Yuhao Wang, Ji Zhang, Yunsong Zhou, Jingkuan Song, Lianli Gao
abstract: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments with diverse start poses, yielding a wide and well-defined boundary that can be communicated to the agent through a simple handoff protocol. Second, Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement retrains the policy on curated successful system rollouts, extending the boundary toward earlier stages of each task and allowing the agent to hand over sooner with fewer language-model calls. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo, our system outperforms the strongest baseline by over 26 percentage points, reaching 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, while further reducing its API cost and execution time by 41.3% and 37.5%, respectively. These results suggest that the key to robust agent-policy orchestration lies not only in improving either component individually, but also in explicitly shaping the boundary between them.

title: MYSTIQUE: Few-Shot Facial Identity Transfer with Performance Preservation
authors: Shihan Cheng, David Hyde, Junting Deng, Michael Bao, Paul Debevec, Roshni Cooper, Soshi Shimada
abstract: In visual effects, identity transfer replaces the identity in a driving image with that of a target person, while preserving the expression, lighting, pose and scene of that image. Paired ground truth is rarely available, so many methods are trained by self-reconstruction, where the model can learn a shortcut by copying identity cues from the driving image. This shortcut causes identity leakage at inference, where the driving image shows a different person. Our key observation is that leakage can enter through any input that reads the driving image. We therefore present MYSTIQUE, a diffusion-based identity transfer method that takes identity from a set of the target's photos and reads expression, lighting and scene through separate streams. It learns to disentangle identity from the other streams through multi-stage training, with disentanglement strategies at their inputs: a random block mask whose boundaries do not follow the face outline, self-augmentation, which randomly changes the face shape in the expression input and keeps its expression, and face randomization, which replaces the person in the expression and lighting inputs while the ground truth stays the driving image. At inference, we also warp the lighting input onto the face shape of a first pass, which reduces face-shape leakage through the lighting stream. Since face-recognition scores and human judgments each have limits, we evaluate identity with both, together with face-shape metrics on rendered faces of known shape. In a user study, raters judge MYSTIQUE's results more like the target than those of each compared method. Among these methods, MYSTIQUE also recovers the target's face shape most accurately, and its recognition score gains the most as more photos of the target are given.

title: The Insertion-Deletion Distance of Linear Codes under Random Coordinate Permutations
authors: Hengfeng Liu, Chunming Tang, Zhengchun Zhou
abstract: We study the maximum insertion-deletion (insdel) distance attainable by permuting the coordinates of a fixed $[n,k]_q$ linear code. Exploiting the connection between common subsequences of codewords and noncrossing matchings in the related bipartite graphs, we establish probabilistic lower bounds under random coordinate permutations over large alphabets. In particular, if the maximum symbol multiplicity among nonconstant codewords is $O(n/q)$, a uniformly random coordinate permutation yields insdel distance at least $2n-O(n/\sqrt q)$ with high probability for sufficiently large $q$. Furthermore, for projective linear codes satisfying the same symbol multiplicity condition, we show that the maximum attainable insdel distance is $2n-Θ(n/\sqrt q)$. As an application, for $[n,k]_q$ MDS codes containing the all-one vector, random coordinate permutations yield insdel distance at least $2n-O(\sqrt{kn})$ with high probability whenever $(k-1)(\log q)^2=o(n)$. In particular, for full-length Reed--Solomon (RS) codes, we obtain the lower bound $2q-O(\sqrt{kq})$ with high probability for $k=o(q/(\log q)^2)$, substantially improving previously known lower bounds while allowing a wider range of dimensions. Finally, we give explicit constructions of full-length RS codes over square fields, attaining the order-optimal insdel distance $2q-Θ(\sqrt q)$.

title: Can You Find the Edit When Nothing Looks Wrong? A Paired Benchmark for Text-Driven Image Manipulation Localization Beyond Semantic Abnormality
authors: Peiyu Zhuang, Jianquan Yang, Zhuoying Cai, Yi Jiang, Yingquan Chen, Xinle Wang, Zeqin Yu, Dongdong Lin, Ruitao Xie, Kaige Li, Xiaochun Cao
abstract: Instruction-driven image editing can alter a photograph while keeping the result coherent with the scene. Existing benchmarks lack matched plausible and anomalous edits of the same target, making it difficult to measure how localization performance changes with semantic plausibility. We construct a paired benchmark by generating semantically plausible and anomalous replacements of the same target in each source photograph. Both edits use the same editor, language, and generation settings. We estimate a separate mask for each output and retain pairs with sufficient mask overlap, enabling direct comparison of localization performance under the two semantic conditions. The release contains 47,747 bilingual triplets from 6,500 photographs, spanning four editors, three source domains, and six intended violation types. Across nine public localizers, editor-averaged IoU is lower on plausible edits in 26 of 27 model-dataset comparisons. This gap persists under pixel-change controls and region-size analyses. These findings reveal a semantic-plausibility shortcut: localization often weakens when an edited result looks ordinary. The benchmark provides a controlled setting for measuring this gap and developing localizers that remain effective on plausible edits.

title: Motion Chain of Thought: Disentangling Motion Semantics from Visual Appearance for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Xiangkai Ma, Xinyi Wang, Junjie Wang, Sheng Xu, Mingyang Li, Yue Ma, Han Zhang, Yuzheng Zhuang, Wenzhong Li, Zhihao Yuan
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding action generation. However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions. This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening the predictive capability of world evolution modeling for action generation. We propose PILOT (Physical Inference for Latent Optimized Trajectories), whose core Representational Deduction (RD) bridges this gap by integrating motion chain-of-thought (CoT) guidance as a native model capability. Specifically, RD aims to encourage the action branch to explicitly model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as CoT in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectory. Experiments demonstrate that RD not only improves the success rate and generalization ability of WAMs in complex robotic manipulation tasks but also enhances the model's physical interpretability by decoupling high-level motion semantics from low-level trajectory details. Furthermore, the abundant state transition supervision signals introduced by RD effectively alleviate the sparse supervision in action generation, supporting data-efficient real-robot adaptation with reduced demonstration sets.

title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
authors: Jiajie Zhang, Yankai Xiang, Changhao Chen
abstract: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $π_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
authors: Xiaoyang Fan, Yufan Cai, Zhe Hou, Jin Song Dong
abstract: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted guidance in ascending order of the sum of its priority and trigger-strength ranks, which can surface high-risk guidance with weaker triggers. VerClin outperforms direct generation and Top-5 RAG on HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Professional. On the LLMEval-Med subset, it outperforms direct generation and ties Top-5 RAG. Component analyses further examine semantic closure, example-guided refinement, specialty screening, and constraint-conditioned delivery.

title: SkillCore: Internalizing Generalizable Skills via Scaffolding-Removed Fine-Tuning
authors: Yi Liu, Changqing Ai, Peijie Dong, Xiankun Lin, Yongkang Yang, Zhezheng Hao, Xilin Xia, Hande Dong, Qiang Lin, Qiang Xu
abstract: Runtime skills can improve agents' problem-solving capabilities by providing procedural guidance for tasks such as code review and debugging. However, these benefits reach only a minority of users, as most do not proactively invoke skills in practice. We argue that such generalizable procedures should become part of the model's capabilities rather than remain optional external add-ons, making them directly available without explicit skill loading. To this end, we present SkillCore, a data pipeline and supervised fine-tuning recipe for internalizing generalizable skills. We transform real agent trajectories by removing skill-loading scaffolding while preserving the task context and subsequent agent actions, thereby supervising direct execution without external skill content. To preserve access to task-specific skills that provide genuinely external information, we mix these scaffold-removed trajectories with a small proportion of skill-native trajectories that preserve supervision for skill invocation. On a held-out skill-free evaluation, SkillCore improves task completion quality over the base Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-72B models by 54.4% and 24.8%, respectively, while preserving task-specific skill invocation on a separate probe and general coding performance on SWE-bench Verified.

title: Seldon TFM family: Seldon-Mini, Seldon and Seldon+
authors: Stanislas Angebault, Nicolas Atienza, Nicola Cancedda, Aziz Fouché, Salomé Gobbi, Ekaterina Iakovleva, Nicolas Makaroff, Arthur Nahmias, Paul Novello, Alexandre Pasquiou
abstract: We introduce Seldon, a family of tabular foundation models. Our classifier Seldon+ ranks first among 15 models on TabBench, our benchmark of 124 classification datasets, and on its variant with missing values. In our own runs of public benchmarks, it also ranks first on BeyondArena IID classification and TabBench-Bio, and second on TabArena classification. The open-weight models Seldon-Mini (27M parameters) and Seldon (213M parameters) both lie on the TabArena Pareto front of Elo against inference time: no entry is both more accurate and faster. On TabArena, Seldon ranks fourth and Seldon-Mini seventh among 109 leaderboard entries, and on the IID track of BeyondArena, Seldon ranks second among 42 entries. Seldon-Mini and Seldon handle both classification and regression, use an architecture similar to those of Kumo-Tabular, TabFM and TabPFN-3.5, and are trained on synthetic tables only.
comment: Technical report. 18 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables. Models: https://huggingface.co/Neuralk-AI/seldon and https://huggingface.co/Neuralk-AI/seldon-mini

title: CaveBench: Benchmarking Abductive Physical Reasoning from Internal Observations
authors: Guanxin Lin, Chen Yang, Shenxiang Zeng, Honghui Zhu, Xin Li, Wenbo Deng, Jiansheng Fan, Chen Wang
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are advancing in physical reasoning, but whether they can understand external physical drivers from internal observations remains an open question. Existing benchmarks have not specifically targeted this setting. To this end, we introduce CaveBench, a benchmark for abductive physical reasoning from internal observations. Models receive apparatus descriptions and internal images while the external controls remain hidden, and must infer the operations responsible for the observed responses. CaveBench spans 20 apparatus scenes in five physical domains and contains 10,200 simulated episodes, split into 9,000 training, 1,000 validation, and 200 test episodes. Questions span one to six events and require the complete control set at every event, testing whether an explanation accounts for the entire process. Synchronized observations and control records provide the inputs and reference answers. Evaluating 27 VLM configurations yields six-event exact-match accuracies of 68.0% for the strongest closed-source model and 12.5% for the strongest open-weight model. Seven adaptation baselines show that single-event gains need not improve complete sequences. Error analysis identifies failures in visual identification, physical inference, evidence integration, and action composition, specifying where current models struggle to connect internal phenomena with their external causes.
comment: 50 pages, 47 figures, 13 tables, including the appendix. Guanxin Lin and Chen Yang contributed equally. Chen Wang is the corresponding author. Project page: https://pier-lab.github.io/CaveBench/

title: TimeTravelContainer: A Live Forking Sandbox for Stateful Agent Exploration
authors: Zizheng Guo, Yanqing Zhang, Nathaniel Pinckney, Cunxi Yu, Brucek Khailany
abstract: LLM agents that drive stateful tools (e.g., interactive shells, design environments, simulation engines) frequently need to clone, backtrack, and parallelize live sessions to support exploration. However, cloning a live session today requires serializing the tool's in-memory state to disk or relaunching from scratch, both prohibitively slow for interactive exploration. Existing agent sandboxes based on microVMs or kernel patches either serialize full guest memory to storage or require privileged deployment, limiting use on shared compute farms, personal computers, and other restricted environments. We present TimeTravelContainer (TTC), a rootless container runtime that live-forks an entire running container, including processes, memory, filesystem, and network, with copy-on-write (CoW) semantics. Because the bulk of a tool session's memory is typically read-only after the fork point, clones share it automatically and only diverged pages consume additional memory.
