title: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory
authors: Shuguang Chen, Salman Paracha
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on external memory to retain and reuse information across interactions. Existing memory systems treat memory as a record of the past and evaluate it by fidelity to the conversation. However, the value of memory lies in whether it improves the agent's response. A memory system decides what to memorize and what to serve before that response exists, and fidelity checks neither decision against it. Faithful memory can therefore fail to improve the response. We instead view memory as a prediction problem and present \textbf{\emph{\leto{}}}, a memory system for LLM agents that focuses on the utility of memory to the future rather than on its fidelity to the past. Because future requests are unknown, \emph{\leto{}} preserves access to conversation details through memory indexing, allowing information to remain available through its sources. When a request arrives, memory replay draws on this index to anticipate and supply the context the agent needs beyond what the request explicitly states. The utility of the served context remains uncertain until the response is generated, motivating a utility loop that uses response outcomes to refine future memory selection. We evaluate our system against six memory systems on five benchmarks across three scenarios. In personalization, it outperforms the strongest compared memory system by 16.3 percentage points in accuracy on PrefEval and by 3.1 points in task completion on PERMA. For long-horizon tasks, it achieves the best overall performance on MemoryArena averaged over five environments with a gain that increases with the chain depth. In long-context understanding, it is on par with retrieval over the raw history while serving fewer context tokens.

title: MESSI: Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration for Physics-Based Character Control
authors: Xiaogang Peng, Jiaqi Zou, Lei Zhong, Sirui Xu, Huaizu Jiang
abstract: Physics-based soccer characters must perform diverse motor skills and transition smoothly between them, such as dribbling into a shot. However, skills that perform well in isolation may fail when executed sequentially, as preceding behaviors can leave the character and ball in unfamiliar states. We present MESSI (Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration), a framework that enables multiple soccer skill transitions through shared adaptation while preserving the original skill policy outside transitions. MESSI first trains eight task-competent experts using motion priors and task rewards, then distills them into a unified, skill-conditioned Transformer. Rather than retraining individual experts for different transitions, we train a shared, context-conditioned low-rank adapter on the frozen student through online reinforcement learning. Activated upon skill switching, the adapter helps the target skill handle unfamiliar entry states, while a learned exit mechanism determines when to return control to the original student. By disabling the adapter during native skill execution, MESSI preserves the original student policy by construction. Experiments across individual skills, skill transitions, and continuous skill chains demonstrate substantial improvements over direct switching, including an increase in dribbling-to-shooting success from 19.8% to 61.8%.

title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
authors: Xuanchen Liu, Hejun Zhang, Boxuan Dong, Ying Wu, Heshuai Li, Wen Gao, Yonghong Tian, Weihao Yu
abstract: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies, every mirror condition reduces aggregate success rates: averaged over the three conditions, the drop ranges from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points across policies, and it reaches 62.5 points on the mirrored tabletop. Because a mirror is also a physical obstacle, we compare it against geometrically matched non-reflective panels; 50--88\% of mirror-specific failures occur without recorded robot--panel contact, so direct collisions alone do not explain the degradation. Trajectory and contact analyses instead reveal recurring behaviors consistent with phantom targeting of reflected objects and spatial mislocalization of real ones. Targeted diagnostics further characterize grasping near reflections, policy-dependent pushing progress, and physical-target interaction under main-camera occlusion. Real-robot experiments with $π_{0.5}$ and FastWAM also show lower overall success rates under the upright-mirror and mirrored-tabletop conditions. These findings reveal a shared vulnerability to reflective environments across diverse robot policies and motivate reflection-aware evaluation of embodied intelligence. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/robodojo-mirror.

title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
authors: Neda Ghafouri
abstract: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions. But how reliably can these judges recognize clinically dangerous mistakes, especially when an agent appears to have completed its task successfully? We investigate this question using MedAgentBench by introducing controlled clinical errors into verified agent trajectories. The experiments include 416 faulty trajectories, eight error categories, and six open-weight LLM judges. By comparing each faulty trajectory with its correct counterpart, we measure whether judges genuinely recognize errors rather than simply flagging more actions as unsafe. The findings show that access to clinical evidence significantly improves judge reliability. When shown only the final answer, judges cannot distinguish errors that leave it unchanged, while flagging 56% of correct trajectories. With full trajectory information, the ability to distinguish unsafe actions from correct ones reaches a score of 0.75, and providing actual EHR responses improves discrimination by 0.39. Surprisingly, including the agent's reasoning does not improve overall performance and reduces detection of incorrectly reported clinical values by 0.18, which remain the hardest errors to detect. MedGemma performed worse than the general-purpose model and was the only judge to miss potentially dangerous medication overdoses. We also find that the benchmark's original grader accepts all 38 trajectories with an intentionally skipped laboratory check, while combining LLM judges with a rule-based checker informed by the full EHR record detects 97% of injected faults.

title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation
authors: Jiawei Weng, Rui Zhang, Saining Zhang, Changjian Pan, Yuanbo Lyu, Jiarui Guo, Yongzhi Li, Guolin Liu, Jialu Liu, Jiankun Wang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li, Zhiheng Li, Jiaying Wan, Junhao Chen, Weiqing Xiao, Jingrun Du, Wenyi Li, Weiyi Lin, Zenan Meng, Hu Wei, Lin Qu, Zongzheng Zhang, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li
abstract: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition. Its reported inventories comprise 1,010,386 asset records: 524,611 rigid assets in 1,212 categories (RFW-R), 402,410 articulated assets in 531 categories (RFW-A), and 83,365 jointly verified deformables in 485 categories (RFW-S). These taxonomies contribute 2,228 dataset--category entries. RFW-R couples category-guided generation with collision geometry, composed physical properties, and interaction annotations; RFW-A uses reusable agent-authored procedural generators with explicit part and joint structure; RFW-S uses structure-aware simulation representations, calibration, and independent testing. A common interface preserves physical requirements specific to each asset type for retrieval and scene assembly. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that RFW-R provides broader asset coverage and stronger scene-fulfillment capabilities than existing datasets. Across five RoboTwin tasks, using 100 demonstrations per task for each asset source, policies trained on RFW-R achieve macro success rates of 71.2% in clean settings and 41.8% under randomization, exceeding the strongest baseline by 15.8 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively. RFW-W provides a scalable and unified asset foundation for generating physically grounded, task-conditioned embodied worlds.

title: Training Lightweight Gaze Models without Target Gaze Annotation: What Makes a Good Teacher?
authors: Scott J. Lewis, Di Fu
abstract: Model-generated labels offer a scalable route to training lightweight vision models, but what makes a model a good teacher, and can we tell before training a student? We study this in gaze target estimation, where interactive robots need models that are both accurate and efficient. In a controlled comparison of eleven supervision conditions, we vary only the source of gaze-point labels, keeping the student, training protocol and 361k training samples fixed, across three video datasets, two student sizes and three seeds; every student is evaluated against human annotation. Three findings emerge. First, imperfect model-generated labels can replace human annotation: Gaze-LLE, never trained on the target datasets' gaze annotation, trains students that match annotation-trained ones on ViT-Tiny and are significantly more accurate on ViT-Small (average distance error 0.187 vs 0.196), and the ViT-Tiny student runs 32$\times$ faster than its teacher on a laptop CPU. Second, apparent competence can conceal unreliable supervision: given another person's face centre in the prompt, InternVL3 and Qwen3-VL return it on 93.4% and 81.1% of test samples, and a copy-the-coordinate baseline matches InternVL3's labels and students. Without that coordinate, both models fall far behind the specialist. Third, good teachers can be identified before training: validation label error ranks student test error (Spearman's $ρ= 0.91$), and ten annotated clips single out the two specialist teachers in 95% of draws. These findings give practical principles for assessing supervision, exposing shortcuts and selecting teachers for lightweight models.

title: RePix-VFI: Re-rendering Observed Pixels for Video Frame Interpolation with Generative Priors from One-Step Diffusion
authors: Dayeon Kim, Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim
abstract: Multi-frame video frame interpolation (VFI) aims to reconstruct dense video from sparse keyframes, requiring accurate intermediate motion and faithful appearance. As temporal gaps grow, flow-based methods can retain observed textures but misplace them under ambiguous motion, whereas iterative latent-diffusion models can synthesize plausible content but incur substantial sampling costs and may alter details during reconstruction with a variational autoencoder (VAE). We present RePix-VFI, named for Re-rendering observed Pixels, a multi-frame VFI framework that couples draft-conditioned one-step video diffusion with reconstruction from observed keyframes. A pretrained video diffusion model refines a flow-rendered draft of the whole window in a single forward pass. For each target frame, our generative readback matches its two bounding keyframes to the generated prediction using an optical-flow estimator. The resulting correspondences guide re-rendering of original keyframe RGB pixels outside the VAE. A lightweight appearance fusion head combines these renderings with generated appearance. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in reconstruction and perceptual quality. On SNU-FILM at $\times$8 and $\times$16, RePix-VFI achieves the highest PSNR and the lowest LPIPS, FloLPIPS, and tOF among the compared methods, exceeding the best evaluated diffusion-based baseline by 1.71 and 1.48dB in PSNR, respectively. It also runs 32--42$\times$ faster than the state-of-the-art multi-frame VFI diffusion model.

title: E-MAPS: Event-Based Promptable Video Segmentation with Memory-as-Prompt
authors: Adonay Demewez Gebremedhin, Mohamad Alansari, Wessam Shehieb, Muzammal Naseer, Hasan AlMarzouqi, Sajid Javed, Naoufel Werghi
abstract: RGB-based video object segmentation (VOS) remains brittle under fast motion and adverse illumination. Event cameras preserve signal under blur and challenging exposure, but provide little evidence when motion slows. Interaction can restore object state for subsequent propagation, yet promptable event methods merely address single windows. We formalize event-based Promptable Video Segmentation (ePVS), where prompts at arbitrary windows initialize, correct, or introduce objects and predictions. We present Event Memory-As-Prompt Segmentation (E-MAPS), which transfers a pretrained promptable segmenter to event streams and learns propagation and correction. Event-to-Token (E2T) aligns recurrent event features with pretrained representations while preserving prompt-conditioning priors. Memory-Aware Prompting (MAP) converts object-conditioned history into sparse prompts, allowing memory and user inputs to share one decoder pathway efficiently. We construct Event-View Masklets (EViM) from 206K aligned RGB-event pairs and 620K masks for two-stage representation transfer and native event-video learning, and establish three training-disjoint benchmarks. E-MAPS leads prompt-once and interactive ePVS across all three benchmarks while being more efficient. It further demonstrates strong performance on zero-shot object tracking benchmarks. Project page: https://github.com/adonaydem/emaps-wacv

title: PORTA: Systematic Discovery of Vulnerabilities in Identity Brokers
authors: Zixu Zhou, Xiangyu Guo, Ilya Grishchenko, David Lie
abstract: Identity brokers such as Keycloak, Vault, and Dex translate authentication proofs from an upstream identity provider into sessions for downstream services. Due to their central role in authentication and trust mediation, a single vulnerability in a broker compromises every downstream service behind it. In fact, recent incidents have demonstrated that even widely adopted platforms are not immune to such issues, highlighting the critical need for systematic analysis. To build such an analysis, this work first defines invariants for broker operation. These invariants are not completely covered by existing authentication specifications, primarily because brokers are unique in their duality, i.e., acting simultaneously as a relying party and an identity provider. The invariants capture the properties that identity brokers must uphold throughout their workflows, as all 60 previous CVEs we consider violate at least one invariant. Within these workflows, we further define high-level action categories. Equipped with this information, our automated tool PORTA leverages a large language model (LLM) to generate API invocation sequences corresponding to the high-level action categories, and oracle assertions aligned with the specified invariants. PORTA identifies 33 previously unreported security vulnerabilities in seven popular open-source brokers. We study these novel vulnerabilities and trace them to eight recurring patterns. We responsibly disclosed all discovered vulnerabilities: 29 have been confirmed, 14 patched, and 19 assigned CVE numbers, with 10 CVEs rated as critical.
comment: In Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security CCS26

title: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
authors: Ce Zhang, Junyi He, Tianshi Ming, Jinxi He, Jianshu Zhang, Xiyuan Yang, Jianuo Zhu, Yicheng Tao, Xiyu Luo, Minghao Fu, Jiahui Zhu, Kehan Guo, Yunzhong Xiao, Jingyang Lin, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Katia Sycara, Yaqi Xie
abstract: Despite strong performance on standard benchmarks, video reasoning models remain vulnerable to visual degradation, raising concerns about their reliability in safety-critical scenarios. Existing benchmarks address this concern in part by simulating visual degradation or probing model reasoning with challenging questions, leaving open how well models handle naturally degraded video and whether they can make the simpler judgments that matter for safe driving. To this end, we introduce GRAPE-Bench, which jointly evaluates video reasoning across visual degradation conditions and question difficulty. It combines a synthetic set spanning twelve corruption types across daily-life and driving videos with real-world footage of driving at night or in rain, snow, or fog. Each video is paired with three progressively challenging questions, from fundamental judgments with potential safety implications to demanding reasoning stress tests. Across open-weight and frontier models, we observe ranking reversals between synthetic and real-world conditions and level-specific weaknesses obscured by overall accuracy. Synthetic-data fine-tuning improves Qwen3.5-9B's real-world accuracy from 76.7% to 81.1%, while clean-privileged on-policy distillation reaches 80.4% in a separate reasoning-enabled setting. Through preference steering, we further demonstrate continuous control over a frozen model's trade-off between safety-relevant judgments and challenging reasoning, with little change in overall accuracy. Together, GRAPE-Bench provides a unified testbed for evaluating, improving, and controlling video reasoning under degraded visual conditions.

title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
authors: Yifan Duan, Lihuan Li, Chao Xue, Siyuan Zheng, Du Yin, Flora D. Salim
abstract: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations. These methods do not use the localization result to select the text for mode diagnosis. To address this limitation, we propose RecordRoute, which couples comparative localization with local diagnosis. Specifically, it represents each record with word and character features and learns to rank records through comparisons within each trajectory. The selected record supplies the actor and step, while its text and metadata drive mode prediction. On controlled-injection Who&When Pro, RecordRoute outperforms StepFinder and ASCon on all four official metrics. With actor and step predictions fixed, local diagnosis reaches 77.47% pooled joint accuracy versus 69.28% for full-trace diagnosis. On natural failures from TraceElephant and CatchBench POST, it outperforms these baselines and three open LLMs in localization.

title: Blockchain-IoT Convergence for Spatiotemporal Data Systems: Challenges, Solutions, and Research Gaps
authors: Natalia Chaudhry, Muhammad Murtaza Yousaf
abstract: Blockchain in conjunction with the Internet of Things (IoT) is changing the management of spatiotemporal data in a way that has never been possible before now. In the process of gathering geospatial and time-stamped data from a large network of IoT devices, data authenticity, accuracy, and timely processing are major issues. Spatiotemporal indexing in a blockchain environment is necessary for ensure quick data retrieval; supporting real time data processing requirement. Blockchain with its decentralized consensus mechanism is a possible solution for preventing data fabrication, unauthorized access, and single point of failure in IoT based spatiotemporal applications. This paper aims to describe how Blockchain and IoT indexing can be combined to enhance the spatiotemporal data management (specifically indexing and querying of data). Literature solutions will be reviewed and compared to highlight challenges and insights for future blockchain-integrated IoT in resilient spatiotemporal data ecosystems.

title: PAC-style Bounds on the Conditional Validity of Conformal Predictors
authors: Nicolo Colombo
abstract: Conformal prediction sets are guaranteed to be marginally valid over the attribute space, but local coverage can diverge from the user-defined target $1-α$. Constructing conditionally valid prediction sets with finite calibration data is impossible for a general data-generating distribution. We derive PAC-type probabilistic lower bounds on the input-conditional coverage of any conformal predictor, without assumptions on the data distribution. They are based on the Markov and Cantelli inequalities and adapt to both calibration-marginal and calibration-conditional setups. A tighter, model-dependent Cantelli bound depends on the variance of the conditional coverage and is estimable from data using a fully non-asymptotic Hoeffding argument. The results suggest conditional-coverage variance as a scalable and theoretically motivated empirical measure of conditional validity.

title: Best Arm Identification with Unknown Post-Action Context Distribution
authors: Amir Mohammad Abouei, Mohammad Shahverdikondori, Emad Emamjomeh, Negar Kiyavash
abstract: We study best arm identification (BAI) with post-action context in the fixed-confidence setting. After choosing an action, the learner observes a post-action context together with a reward whose distribution depends only on this context. Incorporating such intermediate information can substantially reduce the sample complexity of identifying the best arm. While Shahverdikondori et al. (2026a) analyzed the case where the distribution of contexts given actions is known, we address the more challenging and practically relevant case where this distribution is unknown. We derive an instance-dependent sample complexity lower bound and propose a Track-and-Stop algorithm that matches it asymptotically with access to an optimization oracle. Our stopping rule uses a new concentration inequality that jointly controls uncertainty in the context distributions and reward means, removing the factor of two incurred by separate concentration bounds. Implementing the algorithm generally requires solving nonconvex optimization problems. We propose a convex relaxation with instance-dependent approximation guarantees, including asymptotic tightness on hard Gaussian instances. Experiments demonstrate that exploiting post-action context reduces the sample complexity relative to baselines that ignore it, even when the context distributions are unknown.

title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
authors: Zhiyuan Dong, Carlos Mundo-Levano, Daniel L. Lau, Gonzalo R. Arce
abstract: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes with the closed-form score elsewhere, which proves essential for stability at scale. A closed cosine-form observation operator turns missing-node recovery into linear-Gaussian guidance with stabilized posterior sampling. On hypergraphs of up to 500 nodes, our model beats a clique-expansion baseline by margins growing from $2\times$ to $27\times$ in covariance error, matches the graph-spectral statistics of the data better than the graph-basis model itself, and reaches the finite-sample estimation floor on data rotated off the t-spectral axes. Posterior sampling reduces missing-node NMSE to 0.28-0.64 (classical baselines 0.87-1.1) at conservative coverage, and cuts the framework's own denoising baseline by up to $3.6\times$.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027

title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment
authors: Shivank Rajput, Himanshu Singh, A. V. Subramanyam
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries append optimized suffixes to otherwise benign looking prompts to bypass safety alignment. Existing optimization-based GCG-style attacks can be effective, but they are expensive at inference time, and suffer from poor transfer. We present, SALSA, a generative framework that learns a distribution over jailbreak suffixes from optimization-derived attack corpora. Once trained, the model supports efficient sampling-based attacks. On open-source targets, it achieves attack success rates comparable to state-of-the-art optimization baselines, while reducing generation time from 3.46s to 0.04s per prompt. In black-box transfer, it remains highly effective against proprietary systems, including 99% ASR on GPT-3.5-Turbo, and reaches 45% ASR on the substantially harder GPT-4o, more than doubling the strongest baseline at an equal sampling budget. We further offer an intuition for why generative sampling can preserve high attack success, when the learned suffix distribution is close to the distribution of optimization outputs. Overall, our results show that learning adversarial suffix distributions yields a scalable, and practically efficient foundation for continuous LLM vulnerability discovery.

title: High-Performance Algorithms for Computing the V-BLAST Permutation
authors: Tomer Pelleg, Haim Avron, Sivan Toledo
abstract: We propose two novel and efficient algorithms for computing a column permutation called V-BLAST or an approximation of it. The V-BLAST column permutation is used in a QR factorization that is part of an integer/discrete least-squares solver. The overall solver is part of the receiver in advanced communication systems that transmit multiple symbols simultaneously. Two classes of efficient algorithms for computing the exact V-BLAST permutation have been proposed in the literature. The first, based on a sequence of Givens rotations, is unfortunately highly sequential. The other, based on a sequence of downdating operations on a pseudo-inverse, has a shorter critical path, but is unlikely to be numerically stable. The new algorithms that we propose are inspired by the similarity between V-BLAST and rank-revealing QR factorizations. Our first algorithm uses Householder reflections, is numerically stable, and has a short critical path. It is unable, however, to efficiently exploit cache memories. We rectify this with a randomized algorithm that computes an approximation to the V-BLAST permutation and has a short critical path and can effectively exploit cache memories. We prove approximation properties of the randomized algorithm and demonstrate experimentally that both algorithms are faster than existing ones, both when tested in isolation and when tested within an integer least-squares solver.

title: SHARPnP: Self-Supervised and Plug-and-Play Hyperspectral Super-Resolution from Real Noisy Unaligned Camera Measurements
authors: Mohamad Jouni, Brayan Monroy, Jorge Bacca, Mauro Dalla Mura
abstract: Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise. Low-cost RGB cameras provide fine visible details to guide NIR reconstruction, but introduce spatially varying cross-camera misalignment. Supervised fusion methods require relatively large datasets of clean, high-resolution hyperspectral images, are sensitive to sensor noise, and generalize poorly across new sensors. We introduce SHARPnP, an interpretable, flexible framework coupling registration and reconstruction for RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy, unaligned measurements without clean references. We adapt a pretrained registration model via a cross-view loss backpropagated through a fixed plug-and-play fusion module. Temporal and recorrupted pairs enable reference-free self-supervision on noisy inputs. At test time, we calibrate cross-camera radiometry and refine alignment. Plug-and-play fusion employs sequential three-band denoising. On the REAL benchmark, SHARPnP outperforms supervised fusion baselines at $4\times$, $8\times$, and $16\times$ on clean inputs and at $4\times$ under Gaussian noise ($σ=5/255, 10/255$). On native RGB-HSI snapshot measurements, it reconstructs all 51 VIS-NIR bands, beyond the conventional 31-band VIS setting, without high-resolution references.

title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
authors: Sabrine Aroua, Osama Arouk, Pegah Alizadeh
abstract: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles. This survey introduces a technique-agnostic taxonomy of RAN decision-making organized around four complementary capabilities: Representation and Reasoning, Prediction and Simulation, Adaptive Control, and Decision Synthesis. These capabilities are defined by their roles in the control process, independently of the techniques used to implement them. Through this perspective, we examine representative AI and model-based approaches, including foundation models, world models, reinforcement learning, and optimization. We then apply the taxonomy to representative RAN control solutions across slow, medium, fast, and cross-timescale applications to identify which capabilities they implement and how these capabilities are combined in hybrid AI systems. We also review datasets, benchmarks, simulators, digital twins, and experimental platforms according to their support for the decision-making process and reproducible evaluation. The review highlights a gap between the availability of resources for closed-loop experimentation and the standardization of tasks, metrics, and evaluation protocols needed for meaningful comparisons.Finally, we identify research directions for hybrid AI in AI-native RAN, including capability integration, multi-agent and cross-timescale coordination, constraint handling, and reproducible closed-loop evaluation. A curated list of surveyed works and evaluation resources is available at https://github.com/pegahani/Hybrid-AI-RAN-Survey.

title: Linear Probes Can Guide: Training-Free Control of Representation Generators
authors: Pengwei Wang, José Morano, Botond Fazekas, Hrvoje Bogunović
abstract: Representation-space generative models, such as Representation Autoencoders (RAEs), leverage pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) primarily to accelerate training and improve sample fidelity. Yet VFMs are more than reconstruction tokenizers, as they feature rich representation spaces that are highly organized and linearly readable. We observe that this removes a key obstacle of post-hoc guidance: by linearity of expectation, a clean probe applied to an ideal denoiser's prediction yields the exact posterior mean of the probe scores at any noise level. This regime, which we call Semantic Mean-Space, turns semantic guidance into a Bayesian linear inverse problem, bypassing the need for training-time conditioning. With this foundation, we propose LiSM, a unified framework for Linear Guidance in Semantic Mean-Space. To validate the framework, we developed and adapted different solvers, and characterized them based on how they estimate probe-space uncertainty and propagate the correction through the representation. In addition, we propose Fit-Path, a solver designed to achieve strong global and local control. Our results in four control setups (class, attributes, foreground, and keypoints) show that LiSM methods, and Fit-Path in particular, provide effective, lightweight control across global and local tasks, outperforming noise-aware and pixel-space guidance.

title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
authors: Steffen Urban
abstract: We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference. Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%. We design four evaluation protocols that differ in the input and task description given to the LLMs and analyze their responses. In the first two protocols the LLMs are given the float and the 4-bit RTN network and are told that the accuracy has dropped significantly. In the last two they receive only the float network and the task to quantize it, which tests whether they apply an optimization on their own or fall back to plain RTN. Our analysis shows that a frontier LLM can recover most of the lost accuracy. Given one answer per layer, Opus 5.5 raises the accuracy of the 4-bit network to 77.95% by balancing the rounding errors within each 3x3 kernel, reasoning over the integer weights without tools. This is 3.5 pp below the float network and 2.8 pp below AdaRound, which learns the rounding from calibration data. Given only the float network, the LLMs name error-cancelling corrections but do not apply them and fall back to plain RTN, at most with mildly clipped scales, which still lifts Fable 5.2's quantized network to 70.0%. We analyze in detail what the LLMs did and why it works. Code and prompts can be found at https://github.com/urbste/weight-space-programming-ptq
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures. Code and prompts on GitHub (weight-space-programming-ptq): https://github.com/urbste/weight-space-programming-ptq

title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
authors: Hao Wu, Sipeng Chen, Weikai Li, Tianyi Chen, Qiancheng Yang, Hang Zhou, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang, Xiao Luo
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring. In this scenario, comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods becomes challenging because LLM rankers lack a standard item-classification head. Their scores may depend on option labels, prompts, generation procedures, and the available user and item evidence. Existing methods derive uncertainty from different sources and apply it at different stages of the recommendation process. Some methods evaluate an issued ranking, whereas others use uncertainty to change the ranking itself, making direct comparison difficult. Here we introduce a fixed-ranking benchmark which evaluates eight heterogeneous UQ signals as record-level monitors under a shared output contract. We evaluate these signals across four recommendation datasets and two LLM backbones under a shared fixed-ranking protocol. From the results, we draw three main observations. First, UQ method ordering changes across backbones even on the same reference instances. Second, ranking-aligned Top10Mass provides the strongest scalar Error@10 detection in several evaluation conditions, reflecting effective cutoff-aligned monitoring, while its advantage narrows for popularity-tail targets. Third, scalar UQ signals are weak at identifying which control has the larger clipped NDCG@10 difference, whereas source-specific signals, including Perturbation Rank Instability and simple listwise distances, provide stronger paired-control agreement, reflecting their sensitivity to the two controlled evidence sources. These findings motivate us to evaluate ranking-failure detection, robustness across recommendation conditions, and responses to controlled evidence changes as distinct properties of UQ.
comment: 27 pages, 5 figures. Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 11/2026. Reviewed on OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=GXDe6REdu3

title: At the Limit: Autonomous Vehicle Drifting under Generative Policies
authors: Jie He, Meixun Qu, Cheng Hu, Lei Xie, Ezio Bartocci, Radu Grosu
abstract: Autonomous drifting requires agile control despite tire-force saturation and highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics. We propose an online reinforcement learning method for flow policies that combines stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling for exploration with value-based policy optimization. This method supports both training from scratch and fine-tuning a policy pretrained on expert demonstrations. After training, control actions can be generated using either SDEs or ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Experiments on circular and eight-shaped drifting in an F1TENTH digital twin platform show that both training strategies can achieve effective real-time drift control, with tighter tracking, higher success rates, and better robustness under noisy conditions.

title: A Bernstein-Type Variance-Adaptive PMW Mechanism for DP Query Release
authors: Mohamed Aniss Benstaali, Habib Louafi, Naima Bessah
abstract: Private Multiplicative Weights (PMW) is a central mechanism for the differentially private release of adaptive linear statistics over a finite universe. Its classical analysis uses a fixed multiplicative-weights learning rate and does not exploit the local variance of the current hypothesis. This paper presents PMW-Bernstein, a variance-adaptive refinement in which the update step is determined by the relationship between the privately estimated query error and the variance under the current hypothesis. The mechanism retains the standard PMW privacy architecture based on Sparse Vector screening, Gaussian numerical measurements, sequential composition, and post-processing. Through a potential-based analysis, we prove a one-step progress bound that yields a global weighted energy bound, recovers the classical $O(1/α2)$ update regime in general, and establishes an $O(1/α)$ update regime under a Bernsteintype condition on updated rounds. Controlled simulations over synthetic finite-universe distributions and query workloads show that the adaptive rule reduces the number of updates in the low-variance regime, remains competitive in the high-variance regime, and succeeds within the prescribed update budget in the heterogeneous regime where the fixed-step baseline fails.

title: When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes
authors: Gendo Kumoi
abstract: Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) combine binary classifiers by the sum decoder, which totals probabilities, or the product decoder, which totals log-likelihoods. In the noiseless setting, where the binary classifiers output the true posteriors, we ask on which code matrices each decoder always agrees with the Bayes-optimal (MAP) class. For the sum decoder the answer is known: the code must be equidistant (James and Hastie, 1998). We answer the question for the product decoder. Two classes are compared through the votes of the columns on which they differ: the sum decoder decides by their sample mean, the product decoder by an M-estimator with influence function artanh, and each vote is the MAP margin plus a bias determined by the other classes alone. Our main theorem states that the product decoder is MAP-consistent if and only if, for every class pair, the columns on which the two classes differ are matched with the columns obtained by swapping the two classes (or their complements), and equivalently if and only if the code is a union of n-vs-Rest codes. Efficient equidistant codes are therefore excluded: Hadamard codes ($M\ge 8$), which meet the Plotkin bound with $M-1$ columns, have no such pairs, and for the Sylvester type the reversal margin can be at least a constant 0.0182 independent of $M$. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. On six real datasets with estimated probabilities, the product decoder is slightly more accurate when each column is calibrated, and the sum decoder is better when the calibration error differs across columns; in either case the decoders disagree only near ties.
comment: 17 pages, 4 figures. Lean 4 formalization of all theorems in the ancillary files

title: Spectrify: Framework for Hyperspectral Image Generation Using Computer Graphics
authors: Yasin Mamedov, Daniil Vladimirov, Sofiia Dorogova, Bakhtiyar Khalfin, Egor Ershov
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) record the full spectrum of light at every pixel, so projecting an HSI through a camera's spectral sensitivities gives that camera's RAW image, and one HSI can supply training data for hyperspectral reconstruction and camera-pipeline methods. Real HSIs, however, are slow and expensive to capture, and the largest datasets hold only about 1,000 images. High-level vision commonly replaces scarce real data with images rendered from 3D scenes. Low-level tasks, however, need physically correct spectra, which requires spectral rendering with a measured spectrum for every material in a scene, and existing spectral renderings cover only a handful of scenes, mostly with a simplified image formation model. We present Spectrify, a framework that converts 3D scene datasets into HSIs, together with a library of reflectance spectra labeled by material and compiled from close-range hyperspectral datasets and spectrophotometer measurements. In Spectrify, spectra follow the material: each object receives a physically based optical model and measured reflectance spectra or optical constants from its material category, each lamp an emission spectrum of its type and the sky a modeled daylight spectrum, and Mitsuba 3 path-traces the full light transport of each scene per wavelength. We show that a hyperspectral reconstruction network trained only on our synthetic HSIs generalizes to unseen real datasets better than networks trained on the largest real HSI datasets on most test sets, and that assigning spectra by material category instead of by color alone improves this transfer on every test set. RAW images projected from our HSIs are also useful training data for color constancy, performing on par with existing synthetic RAW generators. We release the 4,500 rendered HSIs, the code of Spectrify and its material-labeled reflectance library.
comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables; includes supplementary material

title: Latent Merger: Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs
authors: Yanlai Yang, Minki Kang, Divyam Madaan, Sung Ju Hwang, Mengye Ren
abstract: Recent work proposes hypernetworks that convert a document into a low-rank parameter update (LoRA) in a single forward pass, enabling fast injection of new knowledge into a frozen LLM. However, storing separate LoRA adapters for each document can be unsustainable in streaming settings. In this paper, we study the problem of composing hypernetwork-generated LoRAs using two representative systems, Doc-to-LoRA and SHINE. We show that hypernetwork-generated LoRAs have a geometry sharply different from directly fine-tuned LoRAs. They exhibit greater spectral concentration and stronger cross-document alignment than next-token prediction and QA fine-tuned adapters, which are diffuse and nearly orthogonal across documents. Guided by this observation, we propose latent-space LoRA merging. We compose the intermediate hypernetwork latents and then decode the merged latent through the frozen LoRA-generation head. We show that latent-space merging techniques consistently improve over weight-space and factor-space baselines while preserving a single fixed-rank adapter. These results support latent-space composition as a promising mechanism for combining hypernetwork-generated LoRAs under a fixed output-rank budget.

title: $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS Allocations
authors: Zehan Lin, Shengxin Liu, Biaoshuai Tao, Xiaowei Wu, Yuhao Zhang
abstract: We study maximin share (MMS) allocations of $m$ indivisible items among $n$ agents with additive valuations. We prove that for both goods and chores, the optimal MMS approximation factor converges to $1$ as $n$ grows. In particular, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large $n$, and any $m$, we give polynomial-time algorithms that compute a $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for goods and a $(1+\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for chores. Furthermore, both algorithms can be implemented using a polynomial number of bundle comparisons.

title: Approximate MMS allocations for large number of agents
authors: Uriel Feige, Vadim Grinberg
abstract: We consider allocation of indivisible items to agents with non-negative additive valuations, under the maximin share (MMS) fairness benchmark. We prove that for every $ρ< 1$, there exists some $n_ρ$ such that every allocation instance with $n \ge n_ρ$ agents has a $ρ$-MMS allocation. This was explicitly stated as a conjecture in a recent paper of the authors, where it was shown to hold if the number of items is at most $(2 - ε)n$ (and $n \ge n_{ρ, ε}$). We build on some techniques from that earlier paper, including the construction of $\textit{ordinal MMS}$ allocations that give $n - O(\log^2 n)$ agents their full MMS. Among the new techniques that we introduce is the definition of $\textit{block-matchings}$ between the MMS partitions of two agents, and a proof that if the number of item types is small, then block-matchings of small width necessarily exist.

title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
authors: Erfei Cui, Shengjia Zhao, Yan Qin, Kaixuan Wang, Junming Chen, Ping Luo, Tianxing Chen
abstract: Progress in embodied foundation models is largely measured by task success, while the physical safety of their decisions remains underexamined. Safety evaluations centered on rule following and binary judgments do not adequately assess whether embodied models understand environmental hazards and make safe decisions. We introduce EmbodiSafety, comprising 1,092 snapshot tasks and 540 trajectory tasks across 844 visual scenarios to assess safety over short and long horizons. Six response modes cover direct execution, refusal, clarification, constrained execution, autonomous recovery, and human escalation. Distinguishing recovery from human intervention makes the boundary of safe autonomy an explicit evaluation target. Our protocol assesses mode correctness, risk identification, and actionable handling, with complete decision accuracy requiring all applicable checks to pass. Claude-Opus-5.5 achieves the highest complete decision accuracy among reference models, reaching 56.1% on snapshots and 61.5% on trajectories. We further develop a data construction pipeline and curate 40k examples for safety alignment. Supervised training on this corpus raises the complete decision accuracy of Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B.

title: Local Indices Are Not Enough: Synchrony and Global Information in Bandit Algorithms
authors: Aakash Gore, Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan
abstract: Standard index-based stochastic bandit algorithms such as KL-UCB and Thompson Sampling achieve optimal $O(\log T)$ regret over a horizon $T$. The former uses the global timestep to construct each arm's index, while the latter samples each arm's belief distribution at every timestep. The necessity of global information and synchronous index updates for achieving optimal regret has not been examined yet. In this paper, we investigate the fundamental limits of asynchronous local index algorithms---those that recalculate an arm's index only upon pulling it, using solely that arm's own reward history and a local randomness budget. We prove that no such algorithm can achieve $O(\log T)$ regret across all bandit instances. We then analyse the functional equations arising from asynchronous updates, and show that the achievable regret lies in a sub-polynomial, super-polylogarithmic regime. We propose an asynchronous local index policy whose regret upper bound also lies in this regime. Turning to synchronous local algorithms, which sample every arm's index at all timesteps as in Thompson Sampling, we show that a locally determined randomness budget per arm suffices to retain $O(\log T)$ regret, demonstrating that synchrony, albeit with some randomness, is essential to the optimality of Thompson Sampling.

title: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement
authors: Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng
abstract: Answers from generative AI chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) now arrive at very different speeds: reasoning models deliberate before replying, while response caches can return a stored answer at once. Blind preference votes, which rank these models, are read as judgments of their text, and if delivery matters, faster answers are expected to gain. Research on the labor illusion and on how text appears on screen suggests instead that an answer which unfolds as it is written is credited over the same answer shown at once. We test these accounts with three sources of variation in natural use. First, compar:IA, a French government chatbot arena, answered repeated prompts, by a random draw, either with a fresh answer streamed as it was written or with a stored earlier answer from the same model, shown at once. Within the same prompt, a replay lowered an answer's chance of winning a decisive blind vote by 25.8 percentage points. The same stored text won 57% of its decisive votes when streamed and 29% when replayed, and voters called it less complete, more superficial and more often incorrect when replayed. Second, provider congestion slowed streamed answers. In 324,029 conversations, slower answers earned no detectable net credit in the vote, but a slower first exchange made visitors less likely to ask a follow-up question. Third, in 4,378,514 WildChat replies from everyday ChatGPT use, replies slowed by congestion made users less likely to continue. Delivery moved blind votes, in the direction opposite to the one the arena's designers expected, while waiting cost follow-up questions that a comparison between two answers cannot register when both are slow. The results bear on how AI services cache and stream answers, how they budget latency, and how preference leaderboards evaluate models.

title: Understanding Clipping In Zeroth-Order Optimization
authors: Saket Gollapudi, Elisa Bertino, Sewoong Oh
abstract: Zeroth-order optimization has emerged as a resource-efficient alternative to Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) when fine-tuning LLMs, thanks to the inherent low dimensionality of the loss landscape. It relies on a two-point estimate of the gradient that only accesses the function value and not the gradient, bypassing the resource-heavy backpropagation. Recently, it was accidentally discovered that per-sample clipping can improve the performance of the trained model, while running a differentially private version of zeroth-order optimization \cite{zhang2024dpzero} with a very large privacy parameter $ε$ (corresponding to very little privacy). In this paper, we systematically investigate this phenomenon and demonstrate that ($i$) the optimal choice of learning rate $η$ is inversely proportional to the clipping threshold $c$, satisfying $ηc =$ constant; ($ii$) clipping drives the zeroth-order optimization to a different solution with higher test accuracy; and ($iii$) this phenomenon is only observed with per-sample clipped zeroth-order optimization and not other zeroth-order alternatives that also provide robust estimates of the gradient. Further analyses with artificially injected label noise reveals that clipping leads to more robust predictions, which stems from the implicit down weighting of hard-to-fit training examples. Our code is available at https://github.com/SewoongLab/ClipZero
zh_title: 理解零阶优化中的裁剪现象
translation: 由于损失固有的低维性，零阶优化已成为微调大模型时替代随机梯度下降（SGD）的资源高效方法。它依赖于梯度的两点估计，仅需访问函数值而无需梯度，从而避开了资源密集型的反向传播。最近，人们偶然发现，在运行具有非常大隐私参数 $\varepsilon$（对应极少隐私）的差分隐私零阶优化版本时，每样本裁剪可以提高训练模型的性能。在本文中，我们系统地研究了这一现象并证明了：($i$) 学习率 $\eta$ 的最优选择与裁剪阈值 $c$ 成反比，满足 $\eta c = \text{常数}$；($ii$) 裁剪驱使零阶优化走向具有更高测试准确率的不同解；以及 ($iii$) 这种现象仅在每样本裁剪的零阶优化中观察到，而在其他同样提供稳健梯度估计的零阶替代方法中没有。通过注入人工标签噪声的进一步分析表明，裁剪会导致更稳健的预测，这源于对难以拟合的训练样本的隐式降权。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/SewoongLab/ClipZero 获取。
tldr: 本文揭示了零阶优化中每样本裁剪能够提高模型测试准确率和鲁棒性的内在机制，发现学习率与裁剪阈值存在反比关系，且该效果源于对难训练样本的隐式降权。
ai_comments: 该论文首次系统性地研究了零阶优化中样本裁剪（per-sample clipping）现象，揭示了其在提升模型测试准确率和鲁棒性方面的独特作用，为大语言模型的高效微调提供了新的理论视角。
motivation: 近期研究无意中发现，在运行具有极宽松隐私参数的差分隐私零阶优化时，每样本裁剪（per-sample clipping）能够意外提升训练模型的性能，本文旨在系统性地研究并解释这一现象。
method: 系统性地理论与实验分析，研究学习率与裁剪阈值的关系，探究不同零阶梯度估计替代方法的表现，并利用人工注入标签噪声进行进一步分析。
results: 发现最优学习率 $\eta$ 与裁剪阈值 $c$ 成反比（满足 $\eta c = \text{常数}$）；裁剪引导零阶优化走向具有更高测试准确率的不同解；该现象仅存在于每样本裁剪的零阶优化中；裁剪通过隐式降低难以拟合的训练样本的权重，从而提高预测的鲁棒性。
conclusion: 样本裁剪通过隐式下权重难以拟合的样本，能够显著提升零阶优化的泛化能力和鲁棒性，而学习率与裁剪阈值之间存在常数乘积的Scaling关系。

title: U-Statistics-Powered LLM Reasoning
authors: Shijin Gong, Kai Ye, Victor Chernozhukov, Xinyu Zhang, Chengchun Shi
abstract: Since its introduction by DeepSeek, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted for training large reasoning models and agents, spurring a proliferation of its variants. Yet the group size, a crucial hyperparameter in these GRPO-type algorithms, remains largely chosen by trial and error. Exploiting the U-statistic structure of GRPO's policy gradient, we recast the selection of the group size as a classical statistical problem of variance ratio estimation. This problem is particularly challenging when the denominator of the ratio is small, rendering naive plug-in estimators unstable. To address this challenge, we propose a pessimistic ratio estimator that accounts for the denominator's estimation uncertainty. We characterise the statistical properties of this estimator across three sample-size regimes. Empirically, using %a jackknife-based pessimistic rule on synthetic tasks from Reasoning Gym and real-world benchmarks covering both mathematical reasoning and code generation, we show that our adaptive group size selection reduces the mean squared error of the resulting policy gradient and improves policy optimisation over fixed-group-size baselines, with modest additional computational cost.
translation: 自DeepSeek引入以来，群组相对策略优化（GRPO）已被广泛应用于训练大型推理模型和智能体，并催生了其众多变体。然而，群组大小作为这些GRPO型算法中的一个关键超参数，在很大程度上仍然是通过试错法选择的。利用GRPO策略梯度中的U统计量结构，我们将群组大小的选择重构为一个经典的方差比估计统计问题。当比率的分母很小，导致朴素的插件估计器不稳定时，这个问题尤其具有挑战性。为了解决这一挑战，我们提出了一种悲观比率估计器，该估计器考虑了分母的估计不确定性。我们描述了该估计器在三种样本量情况下的统计特性。在经验上，通过在Reasoning Gym的合成任务以及涵盖数学推理和代码生成的真实世界基准上使用基于jackknife的悲观规则进行自适应群组大小选择，我们表明我们的方法降低了所得策略梯度的均方误差，并改进了相对于固定群组大小基线的策略优化，且额外计算成本适中。
tldr: 针对GRPO算法中群组大小选择的试错问题，本文利用U统计量结构将其转化为方差比估计问题，并提出一种悲观比率估计器，通过自适应群组大小选择有效降低策略梯度的均方误差并改进策略优化。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于将GRPO算法中群组大小的选择从经验试错转化为一个严谨的统计问题（方差比估计），并提出了一个理论上更稳健的悲观比率估计器。这种将统计学工具应用于深度学习超参数优化的方法具有重要意义，可能为其他类似问题提供新的解决思路。其贡献在于提高了GRPO算法的效率和稳定性。
motivation: GRPO-type算法中群组大小这一关键超参数通常通过试错法选择，效率低下且不稳定。
method: 本文利用GRPO策略梯度中的U统计量结构，将群组大小的选择重构为方差比估计的统计问题。为解决分母较小时朴素估计器不稳定的挑战，提出了一种悲观比率估计器，以考虑分母的估计不确定性。该估计器在三种样本量情况下的统计特性被表征。经验上，使用基于jackknife的悲观规则进行自适应群组大小选择。
results: 自适应群组大小选择降低了所得策略梯度的均方误差，并改进了策略优化，优于固定群组大小的基线方法，且额外计算成本适中。该方法在Reasoning Gym的合成任务以及涵盖数学推理和代码生成的真实世界基准上均得到了验证。
conclusion: 本文提出的基于U统计量的自适应群组大小选择方法，通过解决GRPO算法中群组大小选择的挑战，有效提高了策略梯度的稳定性和策略优化的性能，且计算成本可接受。

title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges
authors: Hamin Koo, Chanjoo Jung, Fangzhao Wu, Jaehyung Kim
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated evaluators in evaluation and training pipelines, their judgements are often affected by systematic biases that conflict with human preferences. Although prior work has identified various biases and proposed methods for detecting and mitigating them, less attention has been paid to using human preferences to inform bias identification and mitigation. Moreover, these approaches rely heavily on pre-discovered bias lists, overlook bias strength, and depend on costly interventions. In this work, we propose HUB-J, an integrated framework based on human-derived bias factors that detects, quantifies, and mitigates biases in LLM-as-a-Judge systems. Our approach leverages human-LLM judgement disagreement cases to automatically discover interpretable bias factors, and utilizes agreement cases to quantify bias strength through controlled input modifications and resulting shifts in model decisions. Finally, building on these quantified biases, we introduce a lightweight, training-free regression-based mitigation strategy that estimates the influence of each bias factor on model judgments and corrects bias-influenced decisions by removing its estimated effect. Empirical results show that HUB-J uncovers both known and novel bias factors, reveals meaningful differences in model susceptibility, and consistently reduces bias-driven decision flips while generalizing across models.
zh_title: 审计法官：LLM法官中的人类偏见发现、量化和缓解
translation: 虽然大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被部署为评估和训练管道中的自动化评估器，但它们的判断经常受到系统性偏见的干扰，而这些偏见与人类偏好相冲突。尽管先前的工作已经识别出各种偏见并提出了检测和缓解方法，但利用人类偏好来指导偏见识别和缓解的关注较少。此外，这些方法严重依赖于预先发现的偏见列表，忽略了偏见的强度，并依赖于昂贵的干预措施。在本研究中，我们提出了HUB-J，一个基于人类衍生的偏见因素的集成框架，用于检测、量化和缓解LLM作为裁判系统中的偏见。我们的方法利用人类-LLM判断不一致的案例来自动发现可解释的偏见因素，并利用一致的案例来通过受控的输入修改和由此产生的模型决策变化来量化偏见强度。最后，基于这些量化的偏见，我们引入了一种轻量级的、无需训练的基于回归的缓解策略，该策略估计每个偏见因素对模型判断的影响，并通过消除其估计的影响来纠正受偏见影响的决策。实证结果表明，HUB-J能够揭示已知和新颖的偏见因素，揭示模型敏感性的有意义的差异，并在跨模型泛化能力的同时，一致地减少了由偏见驱动的决策翻转。
tldr: 本研究提出了HUB-J框架，利用人类偏好来识别、量化和缓解大型语言模型（LLM）作为裁判系统中的偏见，通过分析人类与LLM判断不一致的案例来发现可解释的偏见因素，并量化偏见强度，最后提出一种无需训练的回归方法来减轻偏见。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的HUB-J框架，通过整合人类偏好来解决LLM裁判系统中的偏见问题，这在现有研究中是一个重要的进展。该方法在偏见发现、量化和缓解方面都展现出有效性，并且提出了一种创新的、无需训练的缓解策略，具有很高的实用价值和潜在的应用前景。然而，对于“成本高昂的干预措施”的具体含义以及HUB-J的缓解策略在不同类型和复杂度的偏见上的普适性，还需要进一步的探讨和验证。
motivation: 现有方法在利用人类偏好来指导LLM偏见识别和缓解方面关注不足，并且依赖于预先发现的偏见列表，忽略了偏见的强度，并依赖于成本高昂的干预措施。
method: HUB-J框架利用人类-LLM判断不一致的案例自动发现可解释的偏见因素，利用一致的案例通过控制输入修改量化偏见强度，并提出一种轻量级的、无需训练的基于回归的缓解策略来估计和消除每个偏见因素对模型判断的影响。
results: HUB-J能够发现已知和新颖的偏见因素，揭示模型敏感性的显著差异，并在跨模型泛化能力的同时，一致地减少了由偏见驱动的决策翻转。
conclusion: HUB-J框架能够有效地识别、量化和缓解LLM裁判系统中的偏见，并优于现有方法。

title: Making History-Independence-Preserving LL/SC Writable
authors: Dante Bencivenga, Philipp Woelfel
abstract: A randomized implementation of $m$ LL/SC objects for $n$ processes, with at most $k$ outstanding LL() operations each, uses $O(kn + m)$ CAS and FAID objects [Bencivenga, Habashi, and Woelfel, DISC 2026], achieves constant expected step complexity, and preserves quiescent history independence for algorithms such as [Hagit Attiya, Michael A. Bender, Martín Farach-Colton, Rotem Oshman, and Noa Schiller, STOC 2025]. Unlike some other LL/SC algorithms, such as [Anderson and Moir, WDAG 1995; Jayanti and Petrovic, PODC 2003; Jayanti, Jayanti, and Jayanti, DISC 2023; Hagit Attiya, Michael A. Bender, Martín Farach-Colton, Rotem Oshman, and Noa Schiller, PODC 2024], this algorithm does not support an unconditional write operation. We show how to add a (randomized) wait-free write operation without affecting the asymptotic step or space complexity of the implementation.
zh_title: 可写且保持历史独立性的LL/SC
translation: 一个针对n个进程、每个进程最多k个未完成LL()操作的m个LL/SC对象的随机化实现，使用了O(kn + m)个CAS和FAID对象[Bencivenga, Habashi, and Woelfel, DISC 2026]，实现了常数期望步数复杂度，并为[Hagit Attiya, Michael A. Bender, Martín Farach-Colton, Rotem Oshman, and Noa Schiller, STOC 2025]等算法保持了静态历史独立性。与[Anderson and Moir, WDAG 1995; Jayanti and Petrovic, PODC 2003; Jayanti, Jayanti, and Jayanti, DISC 2023; Hagit Attiya, Michael A. Bender, Martín Farach-Colton, Rotem Oshman, and Noa Schiller, PODC 2024]等其他LL/SC算法不同，该实现不支持无条件写入操作。我们展示了如何添加一个（随机化的）无等待写入操作，而不影响该实现的渐进步数或空间复杂度。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种改进的LL/SC（Load-Linked/Store-Conditional）对象实现方法，通过添加一种随机化的无等待写入操作，在不影响渐进复杂度的前提下，使其支持写入操作，并保持历史独立性。
ai_comments: 该研究的创新之处在于成功地为LL/SC对象实现添加了写入功能，这对于构建更复杂的并发算法具有重要意义。通过随机化和无等待的设计，有效地解决了现有方法的局限性，并保持了良好的性能和历史独立性。
motivation: 现有LL/SC实现不支持无条件写入操作，而添加写入操作对于某些算法至关重要。
method: 通过添加一种随机化的无等待写入操作来增强LL/SC对象的实现。
results: 成功添加了无等待写入操作，同时保持了渐进的步数和空间复杂度。
conclusion: 该研究成功地为LL/SC对象实现添加了无等待写入操作，解决了现有方法的局限性，并保持了历史独立性。

title: SUPRA: Synthesizing Amyloid PET from MRI and Plasma Biomarkers with an Explicit Regional SUVR Prior
authors: Hanwen Li, Fadi Deek, Zhi Wei, Ruixiang Tang, Feng Liu, Bharat Biswal, Michal Schnaider Beeri, Auriel Willette, Chenxi Yuan
abstract: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) quantifies brain amyloid-$β$ as a standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), but is costly and not widely available. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is routine, and plasma biomarkers such as phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) are becoming practical. Synthesizing amyloid PET from MRI alone is ill-posed, because brain anatomy reveals little about amyloid burden. We present SUPRA (SUVR prior-guided amyloid synthesis), which divides this task between MRI and plasma biomarkers. A regression maps the plasma panel to regional SUVR levels, painted onto the subject's MRI segmentation as an explicit prior. A 3D network then adds a residual correction guided by MRI. The output is in absolute SUVR, and the model also runs on p-tau217 alone. On the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort (111 test pairs), SUPRA reaches a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 23.4 dB, against at most 20.7 dB for four published models, and rank correlations of 0.56 to 0.67 with true SUVR in the composite cortex, an early-accumulation region and the striatum, against at most 0.24. In a second, cognitively unimpaired cohort with other plasma platforms (143 test pairs), it reaches 22.8 dB and 0.32 to 0.61, against at most 21.4 dB and 0.20. Its area under the curve for amyloid positivity is 0.91 and 0.82, against at most 0.63. Ablations show that plasma supplies the amyloid information and the network the image quality. Combining MRI with a blood test yields synthetic amyloid PET that is realistic and tracks burden across regions.
zh_title: SUPRA：利用显式区域SUVR先验从MRI和血浆生物标志物合成淀粉样蛋白PET
translation: 淀粉样蛋白正电子发射断层扫描（PET）以标准化摄取值比率（SUVR）量化脑内淀粉样蛋白-$\beta$，但其成本高且普及率低。结构磁共振成像（MRI）较为常规，而磷酸化tau 217（p-tau217）等血浆生物标志物正变得日益实用。仅从MRI合成淀粉样蛋白PET是一个不适定问题，因为脑解剖结构几乎无法反映淀粉样蛋白负担。我们提出了SUPRA（SUVR先验引导的淀粉样蛋白合成），它将这一任务分配给MRI和血浆生物标志物。回归模型将血浆面板映射到区域SUVR水平，并作为显式先验绘制在受试者的MRI分割上。随后，3D网络在MRI的引导下添加残差修正。输出结果为绝对SUVR，且该模型也可单独运行于p-tau217。在阿尔茨海默病神经影像主动追踪（ADNI）队列（111对测试对）中，SUPRA的峰值信噪比（PSNR）达到了23.4 dB，而四个已发表模型最高为20.7 dB；在复合皮层、早期累积区和纹状体中，其与真实SUVR的秩相关系数为0.56至0.67，而最高为0.24。在第二个使用其他血浆平台的认知未受损队列（143对测试对）中，其PSNR达到了22.8 dB，相关系数为0.32至0.61，而对比模型最高分别为21.4 dB和0.20。其淀粉样蛋白阳性的曲线下面积（AUC）为0.91和0.82，而最高为0.63。消融实验表明，血浆提供了淀粉样蛋白信息，而网络提供了图像质量。将MRI与血液检测相结合，可产生逼真且能追踪各区域负担的合成淀粉样蛋白PET。
tldr: 该论文开发了SUPRA模型，通过融合MRI和血浆生物标志物，能够高效、准确地合成淀粉样蛋白PET图像，大幅超越现有仅依赖MRI的方法。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将血浆生物标志物与结构MRI相结合，利用显式区域SUVR先验解决了仅从MRI合成淀粉样蛋白PET的不适定性问题。实验结果在多个队列上显著优于现有方法，具有极高的临床应用价值。
motivation: 淀粉样蛋白PET成本高且普及率低，而单独从结构MRI合成PET由于脑解剖结构无法充分反映淀粉样蛋白负担而属于不适定问题，因此需要引入血浆生物标志物来提供淀粉样蛋白信息。
method: 提出SUPRA模型，通过回归将血浆生物标志物面板映射为区域SUVR水平，作为显式先验涂抹在受试者的MRI分割上，随后利用3D网络由MRI引导添加残差修正。
results: 在ADNI队列中，SUPRA的峰值信噪比达到23.4 dB（优于现有模型的20.7 dB），复合皮层等区域的秩相关系数达到0.56至0.67（优于最高0.24），且在淀粉样蛋白阳性分类上的曲线下面积（AUC）达到0.91。在第二个队列中也表现出一致的优越性。
conclusion: 结合MRI和血浆生物标志物（如p-tau217）的SUPRA模型能够合成逼真的淀粉样蛋白PET图像，并准确追踪不同脑区的病理负担，显著优于现有基于MRI的方法。

title: On the Creation of Object-Centric Event Logs from Patient Journeys
authors: Saimir Bala, Neven Borak, Maximilian König, Anjo Seidel, Zeinab Soleimani, Lorenzo Famiglini, Lev Petrov, Jonas Witt, Mathias Weske
abstract: Interactions between patients and health systems as well as conditions that individuals experience during a disease are represented in patient journeys. Therefore, patient journeys are important assets to investigate how care is being provided, and how health systems can be designed to better suit the needs of patients. While there is initial work on patient journeys from a process mining perspective with traditional case notions, object-centric process mining techniques have yet to be covered. This is unfortunate, since due to the rich structure of objects and their relationships, object-centric process mining approaches are particularly promising in this context. This paper addresses this gap by investigating object-centric event log (OCEL) generation from patient journeys. Based on a list of challenges and requirements, the paper presents an approach for the creation of OCELs from patient journey data. The approach is evaluated on a synthetic patient cohort provided by our industry partner.
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to PODS4H @ ICPM. Replication package: https://github.com/mama-neven/OCEL-patient-journeys-replication-package

title: The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers
authors: Gendo Kumoi, Hideki Yagi, Manabu Kobayashi, Shigeichi Hirasawa
abstract: Error-correcting output coding (ECOC) builds a multi-class classifier from binary classifiers. We study the excess error rate of ECOC over the Bayes (MAP) classifier when each binary classifier outputs a posterior estimate whose log-odds is corrupted by Gaussian noise. Recasting decoding as a test over a Gaussian channel, we derive an upper bound from the union and Chernoff bounds and a lower bound from the nearest competing category and the Mills ratio. The bounds show that a large Hamming distance is both necessary and sufficient for reducing the excess error rate. The excess error rate stays bounded away from zero, by a constant that depends on the two largest posteriors and the noise level but not on the number of categories $M$, whenever the distance between the code words of the two most probable categories is bounded; for equidistant codes this distance is $d_{\min}$. Conversely, it is at most $M-1$ times a factor that is exponentially small in the minimum distance $d_{\min}$, and it vanishes whenever $κ\,d_{\min}-\ln(M-1)\to\infty$ for an explicit $κ$ (for general codes, under a posterior condition). For $n$-vs-rest codes with $n\geq2$, the upper and lower exponents coincide asymptotically, which determines the reliability function of ECOC in closed form. The results extend to correlated Gaussian noise with the Hamming distance replaced by an effective distance; when noise is shared at the level of categories, the effective distance stays bounded and the excess error rate does not vanish for any code. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. In a semi-synthetic setting, the measured decay agrees with the predicted exponent. On ResNet-50 features of CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet-1k, the excess error over a log-likelihood decoding reference decreases with $d_{\min}$ and, for larger $M$, levels off at a moderate distance, while codes with $d_{\min}=1$ degrade as $M$ grows.
comment: 27 pages, 2 figures. Lean 4 formalization of all theorems in the ancillary files
zh_title: 带噪声二元分类器的纠错输出码的可靠性函数
translation: 纠错输出编码（ECOC）从二元分类器构建多类分类器。我们研究了当每个二元分类器输出的对数几率被高斯噪声干扰时，ECOC相对于贝叶斯（MAP）分类器的过错率。通过将解码重述为高斯信道上的检验，我们从联合界和切尔诺夫界推导出上界，并从最近竞争类别和Mills比率推导出下界。这些界限表明，大的汉明距离是降低过错率的必要和充分条件。当两个最可能类别的码字之间的距离受限时，过错率会保持一个不为零的常数界限，该常数取决于两个最大后验概率和噪声水平，而与类别数M无关；对于等距码，该距离为$d_{\min}$。相反，它最多是$M-1$乘以一个关于最小距离$d_{\min}$指数级小的因子，并且当$κ\,d_{\min}-\ln(M-1)\to\infty$时（对于一般码，在后验条件下），它会消失。对于$n$-vs-rest码，当$n\geq2$时，上界和下界指数渐近一致，从而可以确定ECOC的可靠性函数，并给出闭式解。这些结果可以扩展到相关的分母噪声，其中汉明距离被有效距离取代；当噪声在类别层面共享时，有效距离保持有界，并且对于任何码，过错率都不会消失。所有定理都在Lean 4中进行了机器验证。在一个半合成设置中，测量的衰减与预测的指数一致。在CIFAR-10/100和ImageNet-1k的ResNet-50特征上，相对于对数似然解码参考的过错会随着$d_{\min}$的增加而减少，并且对于较大的M，会在一个中等距离处趋于平稳，而$d_{\min}=1$的码会随着M的增加而退化。
tldr: ECOC的过错率可以通过汉明距离来控制，但当两个最可能类别的码字距离受限时，过错率会有一个不为零的常数界限。
ai_comments: 该研究深入探讨了ECOC在噪声环境下的理论性能极限，并提供了量化分析和实验验证。其理论推导严谨，并考虑了多种噪声和编码场景，具有较高的学术价值。然而，实际应用中噪声模型的选择和参数调整仍是挑战。
motivation: 研究当二元分类器输出的对数几率受到高斯噪声干扰时，ECOC的过错率相对于贝叶斯（MAP）分类器的表现。
method: 将解码重述为高斯信道上的检验问题，并利用联合界和切尔诺夫界推导出上界，利用最近竞争类别和Mills比率推导出下界。
results: 较大的汉明距离是降低过错率的必要和充分条件。当两个最可能类别的码字距离受限时，过错率会有一个不为零的常数界限。对于n-vs-rest码，上界和下界指数渐近一致，从而可以确定ECOC的可靠性函数。结果可以扩展到相关的分母噪声，并对噪声共享到类别级别的情况进行了讨论。
conclusion: 汉明距离是控制ECOC过错率的关键因素，较大的最小汉明距离可以确保过错率的有效衰减。

title: FOL-Proof: Verifying LLM Text-to-Logic Translations via Deterministic Semantics
authors: Yisrael Clark, Guy Katz
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate natural-language statements into first-order logic (FOL) to improve reasoning. However, LLMs are prone to errors, and so a semantically unfaithful FOL formula could corrupt downstream reasoning. We present FOL-Proof, a semantic firewall pipeline that validates LLM-generated FOL translations against independently derived linguistic interpretations. FOL-Proof operates by deterministically obtaining a pool of candidate translations via semantic analysis tools, such as the English Resource Grammar and Minimal Recursion Semantics; then applying an SMT solver to check each derived reading for logical equivalence to the LLM-generated formula. If the translation is faithful it is accepted; otherwise, it is rejected, or optionally repaired via repeated invocations to the LLM. The procedure is conservative: incomplete search, unsupported constructions, or inconclusive checks yield abstention rather than false rejection. We evaluated FOL-Proof on established benchmarks (ProofWriter, RuleTaker and PrOntoQA), and also on a new adversarial benchmark (LongFaithCheck). Our experiments show that FOL-Proof attains near perfect selective accuracy, while direct LLM judges and round-trip baselines show substantially worse performance.

title: Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for Linear Swap Regret in Polyhedral Games
authors: Vasilis Pollatos, Alberto Marchesi
abstract: We study linear swap regret in self-play against all affine self-maps of each player's strategy polytope. Efficient adversarial bounds for this class scale as $\sqrt{T}$. On compact polytopes given by linear inequalities, our deterministic uncoupled dynamics achieve $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\mathrm{poly}(D)T^{1/3})$ cumulative regret, where $D$ is the binary length of the game description. The bound is independent of the number of vertices. In perfect-recall $n$-player extensive-form games with at most $M$ terminal sequences per player, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(n^2M^4\log T)$ regret against all linear deviations, extending the logarithmic trigger-regret bound of Anagnostides, Farina, and Sandholm [AFS23]. This class can strictly contain the trigger deviations [FP23] and consists exactly of the deviations implementable by untimed communication (UTC), in which a player interleaves moves with mediator queries along a separate feasible path [ZFS24]. The proof combines optimistic log-barrier learning on a compact matrix lift with stability of the Gordon fixed point, using treeplex geometry in extensive form.

title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
authors: Yufeng Huang
abstract: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference. We develop a new quantization method, Shifter Quantization (SQ), that reconstructs native-width integer operands by appending and shifting shared bits. To further extend the efficiency, we develop a special variant of SQ, Shifter Integer (SHI), to use INT4 kernels. We show that SQ and SHI formats perform better than standard groupwise quantization in quality, as measured by projection error and KL divergence, and in inference speed, as measured during decoding and prefill. For low precision like 2-bit quantization, SQ2 and SHI2 achieve 2.71-3.77x the 4,096-token prefill throughput of llama.cpp on a Q2_K checkpoint and reduce WikiText-2 KL by 6.6-7.8%. For mid precision like 4-bit quantization, SQ4 achieves 1.43-2.47x the prefill throughput of NInfer's groupwise-integer baselines across the tested models and prompt lengths, with 24-40% lower KL than the NInfer baselines. For high precision like 8-bit quantization, SQ8 achieves 27.4% higher batch-one prefill throughput and 72.7% lower KL than vLLM's online FP8.

title: Who decides the norms in TCS? Analysing the composition of the STOC 2027 committees and of the Simons Institute "AI+TCS" working group
authors: Guillaume Munch-Maccagnoni
abstract: A working group organised by the Simons Institute released a report last September containing recommendations aiming to increase the usage of LLMs in theoretical computer science (TCS), including introducing them for communication and evaluation. Most of these recommendations were enacted by the STOC 2027 programme committee and the ACM SIGACT executive committee (as the steering committee of STOC). The composition of the Simons Institute working group is analysed along two axes: country of affiliation, and ties with industry (i.e. affiliated with or funded by). The results show an overwhelming representation of researchers from US institutions and private companies, and a large over-representation of researchers with ties to AI/Big Tech companies (in the present or the recent past). The composition of the STOC 2027 and 2026 programme committees is analysed in terms of country of affiliation. The results show a large over-representation in 2027 of researchers from US institutions/companies, and large under-representation of researchers from EU and Asian institutions, as compared to 2026. The composition of the ACM SIGACT extended executive committee is analysed along the same two axes as the Simons Institute working group: country and industrial ties. The results show the same overwhelming representation of researchers from US institutions/companies, and a large representation of researchers with ties to AI/Big Tech companies.
comment: 6 pages of main text and 6 figures

title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
authors: Nasser Alkhulaifi, Direnc Pekaslan, Christian Wagner
abstract: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth. This discards valuable information about the ambiguity of the underlying data (e.g., span boundary disagreement and type confusion), leading to brittle systems that fail unpredictably when faced with uncertainty in inputs. Therefore, this work presents a proof-of-concept for uncertainty-aware ER that treats uncertainty as native data that should be preserved and exploited throughout ER pipelines. We (i) capture uncertainty signals in the NER stage and (ii) leverage these signals into the EL stage to improve candidate retrieval under ambiguity. Using a BERT-based NER model augmented with two auxiliary span-boundary prediction heads, we apply Monte Carlo (MC) dropout at inference time to derive three mention-level proxy signals: the MC-averaged start-boundary probability, the MC-averaged end-boundary probability, and De Luca-Termini fuzzy entropy computed over the Begin-Inside-Outside (BIO) predictive distribution. These signals are used to adapt the fuzzy cutoff in candidate generation (CG) for EL. Because CG is treated as a blocking step, we evaluate retrieval recall. On the AnnoCTR dataset linked to the MITRE ATTCK knowledge base, the boundary-aware and dual-signal fuzzy linking approaches improve Recall@10 from 0.6186 to 0.7966. The contribution lies not in an end-to-end optimised ER pipeline but in establishing uncertainty preservation as a viable and beneficial component of ER pipelines, enabling downstream EL to make better-informed decisions under uncertainty.
comment: This paper has been accepted for oral presentation at the 19th International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence (ICAART 2027)

title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset
authors: Dominique Regli, Brian C. Williams
abstract: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also surpassing technical limitations of other sensing modalities. However, radar-based activity recognition remains constrained by the limited availability of large-scale datasets. We introduce the Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) dataset to addresses the gaps identified in existing work: 1) it expands the scale of available data by providing over eight hours of annotated recordings in which a person performs eight distinct activities; 2) it overcomes room configuration limitations by recording from five different locations in a two-bedroom, two-bathroom apartment; and 3) it extends beyond primitive actions to focus on high-level ADLs. In addition to the dataset, this paper introduces practical guidance for future ADL dataset construction. We conducted a detailed analysis of how ADLs are prioritized across academic research, health survey tools, and clinical trials to identify clinically significant ADLs. Furthermore, we provide our experimental design, data collection and annotation strategies, post-processing pipeline for forming the R-ADL dataset from raw data, and baseline results on standard machine learning architectures. The R-ADL dataset serves as a valuable resource for advancing ADL recognition systems as we continue building larger and more diverse datasets.

title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
authors: Guangyuan Wang, Chengran Li, Minchen Luo, Jichen Feng, Mengdi Wang, Yifan Zhang
abstract: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. Across 9,136 attempts by four coding agents, the difficulty lies in stored state. Feedback that points to the first state mismatch raises acceptance over output-only feedback in all 12 agent--task cells of a matched study, by 25.0 to 46.9 percentage points, and halves the agent-hours per accepted design. Regraded on new sequences and conditions, 45 of 69 accepted designs fail within the 32 steps their tests required. More than a third of attempts to speed up a correct design end without one. An overall score ranks Sol 5.6 and Fable 5.1 above Astra 6 and Opus 5.5, and both halves of the instances give this order in all 200 random splits. Hardware agents therefore need debugging feedback that exposes stored state, and their benchmarks need final tests well beyond the development cases.

title: Coverage of THz Networks in Presence of Blockages and Scattering
authors: Kaushlendra Pandey, Aman Pandey, Afaq A. Lone, Harpreet S. Dhillon, Abhishek K. Gupta
