In this arXiv update, we shortened the abstract and corrected the placement of Figures 3 and 4. The results and conclusions are unchanged. Reproduction code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23695034

title: NPUFHE: An Efficient CKKS Execution System for Ascend NPUs
authors: Ke Chang, Jian Wang, Xuan Xu, Yijing Zong, Jiqiang Liu
abstract:
Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation directly on encrypted data, but its substantial computational cost hinders adoption in privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Neural processing units (NPUs) already deployed in AI infrastructure provide a practical platform for FHE acceleration. However, after mapping the number theoretic transform (NTT) to matrix multiplications on Ascend NPUs, modular arithmetic and representation conversion on the Vector backend still incur substantial overhead at stage boundaries. Evaluation-key material of key switching also increases storage and data-transfer costs, and whole-limb task assignment causes tail load imbalance.
  We present NPUFHE, an end-to-end CKKS execution system optimized for Ascend NPUs. To reduce modular recovery and twiddle costs in NTT, we propose Boundary-Optimized NTT, which eliminates intra-axis modular recovery, compiles intra-axis twiddle factors into matrix constants, and introduces two-level folded modular recovery at axis endpoints. To alleviate evaluation-key storage and transfer pressure, we design Compact Shoup encoding, which halves the key representation through local coefficient recovery. Finally, we propose Cost-Aware Parallel Tiling to mitigate tail load imbalance caused by whole-limb task assignment. It uses a cost model to adaptively partition tail tasks and smooth stepwise latency increases.
  We integrate the above designs into OpenFHE. On one Ascend 910B4, full-packing CKKS bootstrapping with real evaluation keys takes 0.95 s, encrypted CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 inference with bootstrapping requires 9.87 s per image, and encrypted MNIST inference achieves an amortized latency of 19.81 ms per image. The peak NTT throughput of NPUFHE reaches up to $184.22\times$, $2.04\times$, and $4.46\times$ that of OpenFHE on CPU, TensorFHE, and CROSS, respectively.

title: Seeing vs. Knowing: Counterfactual Supervision and Correction for 3D-Aware Object Editing
authors: Jian Zahng, Zhijun Zhang
abstract: Rotating, translating, or rescaling an object in a photograph requires revealing unseen surfaces, preserving visible appearance, and updating shadows and reflections. Reconstructed 3D assets, rendered at the target pose as a 3D state, provide explicit geometric guidance, but their imperfect textures may conflict with the photograph, while standard paired training does not explicitly teach the editor which source to trust. To address this, we propose counterfactual state supervision, which constructs controlled photo--state conflicts through hidden-surface repainting, hidden geometry with re-rendered shadows and reflections, and visible-surface texture replacement. This teaches the editor to follow the 3D state for unseen content while preserving photograph-visible appearance. However, learning this distinction does not ensure that it is maintained during sampling. We therefore introduce symmetric counterfactual correction, which uses state-side and photo-side twins, which share the photograph and the state respectively, to construct directed latent perturbations toward condition-inconsistent targets and train recovery toward the target specified by the current condition. Both strategies operate only during training, requiring no architectural changes or additional inference steps. Experiments on OBJect and SpatialEdit-Bench demonstrate strong spatial editing performance and content preservation, while controlled ablations show improved source selection and sustained responsiveness to conditioning during sampling.
zh_title: 看见与知晓：用于三维感知对象编辑的反事实监督与校正
translation: 在照片中旋转、平移或缩放对象需要揭示未见表面、保留可见外观并更新阴影和反射。重建的三维资产在目标姿态下作为三维状态渲染，提供了明确的几何指导，但其不完美的纹理可能与照片冲突，而标准的成对训练并未明确教会编辑器信任哪个来源。为解决此问题，我们提出了反事实状态监督，通过隐藏表面重绘、带有重新渲染阴影和反射的隐藏几何以及可见表面纹理替换来构建受控的照片-状态冲突。这教会编辑器在处理未见内容时遵循三维状态，同时保留照片中可见的外观。然而，学习这种区分并不能确保其在采样过程中得到保持。因此，我们引入了对称反事实校正，它使用状态侧和照片侧的“孪生”样本，分别共享照片和状态，以构建指向条件不一致目标的定向潜在扰动，并训练模型恢复到当前条件指定的目标。这两种策略仅在训练期间操作，无需架构更改或额外的推理步骤。在OBJect和SpatialEdit-Bench上的实验表明，该方法具有强大的空间编辑性能和内容保留能力，而受控的消融实验显示，源选择得到改善，并且在采样过程中对条件的响应性得以持续。
tldr: 该论文提出了反事实监督和校正方法，以解决三维感知对象编辑中三维资产与照片之间的冲突，确保未见内容遵循三维指导，同时保留可见照片外观。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于明确地通过构建受控的反事实场景来解决“看见与知晓”的冲突。这种方法使编辑器能够鲁棒地处理不完美的三维资产，并确保编辑过程的一致性，这对于实现更逼真的三维感知图像操纵具有重要意义。
motivation: 在照片中旋转、平移或缩放对象需要揭示未见表面、保留可见外观并更新阴影和反射。虽然重建的三维资产可以提供明确的几何指导，但其不完美的纹理可能与照片冲突，且标准的成对训练未能明确指导编辑器信任哪个来源。
method: 本文提出了反事实状态监督，通过隐藏表面重绘、带有重新渲染阴影和反射的隐藏几何以及可见表面纹理替换来构建受控的照片-状态冲突，从而教会编辑器在处理未见内容时遵循三维状态，同时保留照片中可见的外观。此外，为确保在采样过程中保持这种区别，引入了对称反事实校正，利用状态侧和照片侧的“孪生”样本，分别共享照片和状态，以构建指向条件不一致目标的定向潜在扰动，并训练模型恢复到当前条件指定的目标。这两种策略仅在训练期间操作，无需架构更改或额外的推理步骤。
results: 在OBJect和SpatialEdit-Bench上的实验表明，该方法具有强大的空间编辑性能和内容保留能力。受控的消融实验显示，源选择得到改善，并且在采样过程中对条件的响应性得以持续。
conclusion: 通过反事实状态监督和对称反事实校正，该方法有效地解决了三维感知对象编辑中三维资产与照片之间的冲突，从而在编辑过程中实现了更好的源选择和一致性。

title: Social Interaction Breaks Replicate Independence in Controlled-Clone LLM Agents
authors: Yandan Zheng, Haoran Luo, Anh Tuan Luu
abstract: Multi-agent LLM evaluations and social simulations create many agents from one model and treat them as independent replicates, even after the agents interact. This assumption remains untested with matched controls. We introduce SocCogEval, a controlled-clone assay for Social Cognitive Transfer (SCT). Clones share the base model, system prompt, and decoding parameters and differ only in a private brief, and a factorial protocol separates the brief, 30 rounds of interaction, and initialization noise. On Qwen3-122B-FP8, interaction with the briefs held fixed raises off-topic BFI-10 response-profile drift by $\barΔ=+0.917$ and $+0.912$ in two topically disjoint scenarios (exact $p=0.0008$ and $0.0039$). The drift is larger than under the brief alone, persists under temperature-zero re-probing, and stays positive without typed memory extraction in exploratory tests. Matched solo generation reproduces part of it, and social interaction remains highest. Across five more model variants, every scenario-averaged interaction contrast is positive. Each interacting population is therefore one replicate, and treating its agents as independent requires paired no-interaction controls.
zh_title: 社交互动打破了受控克隆LLM智能体中的复制独立性
translation: 多智能体LLM评估和社交模拟从一个模型创建许多智能体，并将它们视为独立的复制品，即使智能体已经交互。这一假设在有匹配对照的情况下仍未经测试。我们引入了SocCogEval，一个用于社交认知转移（SCT）的受控克隆实验。克隆智能体共享基础模型、系统提示和解码参数，仅在私有简介上有所不同，并且一个因子协议分离了简介、30轮交互和初始化噪声。在Qwen3-122B-FP8上，简介固定时的交互在两个主题不相干的情景中分别使偏离主题的BFI-10响应概况漂移增加了$ arΔ=+0.917$和$+0.912$（精确$p=0.0008$和$0.0039$）。这种漂移比单独简介下的更大，在零温度重新探测下依然存在，并且在探索性测试中没有类型化记忆提取的情况下保持正值。匹配的单独生成复制了部分漂移，但社交互动导致的漂移仍然最高。在其他五个模型变体中，每个情景平均的交互对比都是正向的。因此，每个交互群体都是一个复制品，将智能体视为独立个体需要配对的无交互对照组。
tldr: 在多智能体LLM评估中，即使智能体相互作用后，将其视为独立的复制品是未经检验的假设。本研究引入了SocCogEval，一个受控克隆实验，发现社交互动显著增加了偏离主题的响应漂移，表明每个交互群体是一个复制品，智能体并非独立。
ai_comments: 本文通过引入创新的受控克隆实验（SocCogEval），首次系统性地检验了多智能体LLM评估中一个关键但未经测试的假设。其发现对理解LLM智能体的行为及其在复杂社会模拟中的应用具有重要意义，提醒研究人员在设计和解释多智能体LLM实验时，必须考虑智能体间交互导致的依赖性，并建议采用无交互对照组来确保评估的准确性。
motivation: 多智能体LLM评估和社交模拟中，智能体通常被视为独立的复制品，即使它们已经相互作用。然而，这种假设在有匹配对照的情况下尚未经过测试。
method: 研究引入了SocCogEval，一种用于社交认知转移（SCT）的受控克隆实验。克隆智能体共享基础模型、系统提示和解码参数，仅在私有简介上有所不同。采用因子协议分离简介、30轮互动和初始化噪声。在Qwen3-122B-FP8模型上进行测试，并通过BFI-10响应概况漂移来衡量影响。
results: 在Qwen3-122B-FP8上，固定简介的互动使偏离主题的BFI-10响应概况漂移在两个不相干情景中分别增加了+0.917和+0.912（p=0.0008和0.0039）。这种漂移比单独简介下的更大，在零温度重新探测下依然存在，并且在探索性测试中没有类型化记忆提取的情况下保持正值。匹配的单独生成复制了部分漂移，但社交互动导致的漂移最高。在其他五个模型变体中，每个情景平均的互动对比都是正向的。
conclusion: 每个交互群体都是一个复制品，将智能体视为独立个体需要配对的无交互对照组。

title: SparQ4D: Learning to Act through Sparse 4D Queries
authors: Siyuan Xie, Jinxi Xiao, Ran Ji, Yikai Liu, Mingxi Li, Xuebing Li, Ye Shi, Yuxiang Gao, Jiayuan Gu
abstract: Successful manipulation requires a policy to understand where things are and how they will move, yet action demonstrations leave this spatiotemporal structure implicit. While explicit 4D supervision has proven effective, reducing the cost of dense 4D prediction remains challenging. This paper introduces SparQ4D, a lightweight yet expressive decoder that efficiently injects holistic 4D scene understanding into policies and improves success rates. At its core is a query-based decoder attached to a pretrained policy, which casts many spatialtemporal tasks into one unified interface (e.g. depth, 2D/3D point motion, multi-view correspondence, and hand-eye relations). This design enables efficient training and inference without sacrificing expressivity: the policy learns rich 4D structure from a small number of sampled queries during training, while the decoder can be removed at inference with zero additional overhead. Across multiple backbones, simulated environments, and real-world settings, SparQ4D achieves state-of-the-art manipulation performance, outperforming competing methods while training up to $5\times$ faster. Probing analyses further reveal that this 4D structure is recoverable from the policy.
zh_title: SparQ4D：学习通过稀疏4D查询进行行动
translation: 成功的操作需要策略能够理解物体的位置和运动，但动作演示将这种时空结构隐含化。尽管显式的4D监督已被证明是有效的，但降低密集4D预测的成本仍然具有挑战性。本文提出了SparQ4D，一种轻量级但表达能力强的解码器，能够有效地将整体的4D场景理解注入策略并提高成功率。其核心是一个基于查询的解码器，附加在预训练的策略上，将许多时空任务统一为一个接口（例如，深度、2D/3D点运动、多视图对应和手眼关系）。这种设计能够在不牺牲表达能力的情况下实现高效的训练和推理：策略在训练期间从少量采样查询中学习丰富的4D结构，而在推理期间可以移除解码器，无需任何额外开销。在多个基线、模拟环境和真实场景中，SparQ4D实现了最先进的操作性能，超越了竞争方法，同时训练速度提高了5倍。探测性分析进一步表明，这种4D结构可以从策略中恢复。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为SparQ4D的轻量级解码器，用于将4D场景理解融入策略，提高了操作成功率。它通过在训练时使用少量采样查询来学习4D结构，并在推理时移除解码器以实现零额外开销。SparQ4D在多个基线、模拟和真实环境中均取得了最先进的操作性能，且训练速度提高了5倍。
ai_comments: SparQ4D在解决操作任务中的4D场景理解问题上取得了显著进展，通过其轻量级和高效的设计，有效降低了对密集4D监督的需求。其核心创新在于将4D理解任务统一为查询接口，并实现了训练和推理的高效分离。然而，未来研究可以进一步探索其在更复杂、动态环境中的鲁棒性，以及可解释性。
motivation: 动作演示将时空结构隐含化，而显式的4D监督成本高昂，因此需要一种能够有效降低密集4D预测成本的方法，并将4D场景理解注入策略。
method: SparQ4D是一种基于查询的解码器，附加在预训练策略上，将多种时空任务统一为一个接口。它在训练时使用少量采样查询学习4D结构，并在推理时移除解码器。
results: SparQ4D在多个基线、模拟环境和真实场景中都达到了最先进的操作性能，超越了现有方法，并且训练速度提高了5倍。分析表明，策略可以恢复4D结构。
conclusion: SparQ4D是一种轻量级且高效的4D场景理解方法，能够显著提升策略在操作任务中的性能，同时降低训练成本，并且其学习到的4D结构可以从策略中恢复。

title: Sánchez, Feijóo, or Abascal? Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X of the Leaders of the Three Main Parties of the 29N General Election in Spain
authors: Víctor Yeste, Candida Maria Greco, Paolo Rosso, Andrea Tagarelli
abstract: Source cues are central to political communication, yet reception studies with large language model (LLM) personas as synthetic audiences have not tested whether personas respond to who speaks and not only to what is said. With Spain's general election of 29 November 2026 in mind, we run a speaker-attribution experiment using 1,075 anonymised X posts by the leaders of PSOE, PP and VOX on four topics (the economy and employment, household costs, immigration and corruption) and 791 distinct value-grounded, LLM-generated personas. Each post was assigned to 300 topic-selected persona profiles, 150 grounded in the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map and 150 in Moral Foundations Theory, under four conditions: no author, Sánchez, Feijóo or Abascal, yielding 322,470 complete persona-post quartets. Naming any leader lowered support for identical text, with the penalty for Abascal nearly twice as large as those for Sánchez and Feijóo. The penalty follows the persona's elicited left-right self-placement (ideological congruence): left personas spare Sánchez and right personas spare Feijóo, although ideology was never in the message-evaluation prompt. Corruption posts were penalised under every name, whereas on other topics the ideologically closest leader generally produced little or no penalty. The leader order matches public opinion in 48 CIS barometers (2022-2026) in all three groups and the sign of all twelve differences, but fits barometers before the model's 2024 knowledge cutoff better than recent ones. Our findings demonstrate that LLM personas evaluate political speakers through systematic, value-congruent priors: however, while they replicate human candidate rank-orders across survey barometers, this alignment is ordinal rather than quantitative, highlighting their utility for controlled source-effect experiments though not as substitutes for empirical public opinion surveys.
comment: 27 pages, 7 figures, 34 tables. Code and configuration: https://github.com/VictorMYeste/spanish-political-communication

title: Trajectory Visibility at First Sight
authors: Mohammad Ali Abam, Mohammad Ghodsi, Seyed Mohammad Hussein Kazemi
abstract:
Let $P$ be a simple polygon with $n$ vertices, and let two moving entities $q(t)$ and $r(t)$ travel at constant (possibly distinct) speeds $v_q$ and $v_r$ along line-segment trajectories $τ_q$ and $τ_r$ inside $P$. We study the first-visibility time $ t^* = \min\bigl\{\,t \ge 0 \mid \overline{q(t)\,r(t)} \subseteq P\,\bigr\}, $ the earliest moment at which the segment joining $q(t)$ and $r(t)$ lies entirely within $P$. Prior work by Eades et al.~\cite{swat2020,eeades-phd} focused on the decision version of this question in a simple polygon. They gave a one-shot decision algorithm running in ${O}(n)$ time. For a stationary entity and a moving one, they gave a data structure with ${O}(n \log n)$ preprocessing time and ${O}(n)$ space that answers decision queries in ${O}(\log n)$ time. For two moving entities, after ${O}(n \log^5 n)$ preprocessing time, they built a data structure of size ${O}(n \log^5 n)$ with ${O}(n^{3/4}\log^3 n)$ query time. Variants for polygonal domains with holes or when entities cross the boundary of $P$ lie beyond our scope.
  In this work, we go beyond decision to compute $t^*$ exactly under three models for a simple polygon $P$. When both trajectories are fixed in advance, we preprocess $P$ in ${O}(n)$ time and space and answer each query $(v_q, v_r)$ in ${O}(\log n)$ time. If one trajectory $τ_r$ is fixed while $τ_q$ is given as a query, we build a structure in ${O}(n \log n)$ time and space that computes $t^*$ in ${O}(\log^2 n)$ time per query. When neither trajectory is known in advance, we develop a data structure with ${O}(n^{1+\varepsilon})$ expected preprocessing time and ${O}(n)$ space that achieves ${O}(n^{1/2}\,\text{polylog}(n))$ expected query time for any fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.

title: PROPS: Can Visual Generators Keep the Current Look of a Prop?
authors: Xiangzhao Hao, Dianyi Wang, Keyan Zhou, Yiqian Zhang, Zefeng Zhang, Bailin Li, Kun Zhan, Junchi Yan
abstract: Many generation tasks draw the next image from a visual history, such as storyboards, illustrated stories and multi-turn editing. A new request often states what happens next without restating how earlier objects look. Instead of recovering an object's current look from the history, generators often redraw it from the request alone or bring back an outdated look, and the error can carry into later steps. We call this failure prop drift. Existing evaluations rarely isolate it, because similarity to the history rewards copying and a judge that sees a single history cannot tell a look recovered from that history from one the generator happens to prefer. We introduce PROPS, a benchmark of 2,257 pairs of twin histories that end on the same request but show one prop in two different looks. A pair passes only if the generator draws the matching look on each side and carries out the request, so a look preferred by the generator or the judge passes at most one side. All 34 open and closed systems we test show prop drift, and even systems that carry out the requested action on most sides often lose the current look of the prop. Swapping the planners and editors of agents further shows that both history understanding and image generation limit agent performance. We also build PROPS-Train, 80,250 training chains in four tracks whose targets recover an earlier state or carry scripted changes forward, and fine-tuning on it clearly improves all four tested models. Both datasets will be publicly released.
zh_title: 比例: 视觉生成器能否保持道具的当前外观？
translation: 许多生成任务从视觉历史中抽取下一张图像，例如故事板、插画故事和多轮编辑。新的请求通常说明接下来会发生什么，而不重述早期物体外观的样子。生成器与其从历史中恢复物体的当前外观，不如常常仅根据请求重新绘制它，或者带回过时的外观，并且错误会延续到后续步骤。我们将这种失败称为道具漂移。现有的评估很少将其孤立出来，因为与历史的相似性会奖励复制，而只看到单一历史的裁判无法区分从该历史中恢复的外观与生成器碰巧偏好的外观。我们引入了PROPS，一个包含2,257对孪生历史的基准测试，这些历史以相同的请求结束，但展示了一个道具在两种不同的外观下。一对只有当生成器在两侧都画出匹配的外观并执行请求时才算通过，因此生成器或裁判偏好的外观最多通过一侧。我们测试的所有34个开放和封闭系统都表现出道具漂移，即使是那些在大多数情况下执行了请求动作的系统，也常常会丢失道具的当前外观。交换代理的规划器和编辑器进一步表明，历史理解和图像生成都会限制代理的性能。我们还构建了PROPS-Train，包含四个轨道上的80,250个训练链，其目标是恢复早期状态或将脚本化更改向前推进，并且在其上进行微调可以明显改善所有四个被测模型。两个数据集都将公开发布。
tldr: 生成模型经常无法保持物体在视觉历史中的一致外观，导致“道具漂移”。PROPS是一个新的基准测试，用于评估和解决这个问题，它包含成对的历史记录，并要求模型匹配特定的外观。测试表明所有模型都存在道具漂移问题，但使用PROPS-Train数据集进行微调可以显著提高模型性能。
ai_comments: PROPS基准测试的创新之处在于其“孪生历史”设计，巧妙地解决了现有评估方法难以分离“道具漂移”和模型偏好的问题。通过强制模型在匹配外观和执行指令之间取得平衡，能够更准确地衡量模型的真实能力。PROPS-Train数据集的构建也为解决这一问题提供了有效的训练资源。然而，需要注意的是，数据集的规模和多样性可能仍然是未来研究需要考虑的因素，以确保模型在更广泛的场景下都能保持良好的性能。
motivation: 许多生成任务需要根据视觉历史生成新图像，但现有的生成器常常无法准确恢复或保持历史中物体的一致外观，这种现象被称为“道具漂移”，并且现有评估方法难以单独检测此问题。
method: 引入PROPS基准测试，包含2,257对“孪生”历史记录，这些记录在同一请求下结束，但展示了一个道具在两种不同外观下的情况。通过要求生成器在两侧都画出匹配的外观并执行请求来评估模型。还构建了PROPS-Train数据集，包含80,250个训练链，用于微调模型。对34个现有系统进行了测试，并分析了规划器和编辑器对模型性能的影响。
results: 所有测试的34个开放和封闭系统都表现出道具漂移现象。即使是能够执行请求动作的系统，也常常会丢失道具的当前外观。将代理的规划器和编辑器进行替换后发现，历史理解和图像生成能力都会限制代理的性能。使用PROPS-Train数据集进行微调，可以显著提高所有四个被测模型的性能。
conclusion: 道具漂移是当前视觉生成模型普遍存在的问题，现有评估方法不足以检测。PROPS基准测试和PROPS-Train数据集提供了一种有效的方法来评估和解决道具漂移问题，并且通过微调可以显著提升模型性能。

title: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
authors: Jiarui Guo, Jinkai Zhang, Yuanhong Yu, Yongchen Zai, Futang Zhu, Ruizhen Hu, Sida Peng, Xiaowei Zhou
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. Multi-session evaluation demonstrates that the constructed memory can be reused, while deployment on a real quadruped robot further shows the system's applicability. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav-1.5/

title: Differential Proteomics to Symbolic Rules: An Audit of SHAP Guidance in Lung Adenocarcinoma
authors: Surajit Das
abstract:
We tested whether SHAP improves protein-based Horn rules for distinguishing lung adenocarcinoma from adjacent-normal tissue. CPTAC supplied 213 samples (111 tumour, 102 adjacent-normal) from 111 patients, including 102 matched pairs. Per-protein effects and tests used the same complete pairs with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Sparse logistic regression used five stratified patient-grouped outer folds, with preprocessing and tuning confined to training data and feature selection repeated within inner folds. A separate five-fold patient-grouped evaluation of inductive logic programming used training-derived evidence and discretisation.
  Of 9,518 proteins passing quality control, 378 differed in abundance (40 up, 338 down) at FDR below 0.05 and an absolute mean paired log-ratio difference of at least 1. Classifier ROC-AUC, average precision, accuracy and balanced accuracy were 0.9997, 0.9998, 0.9906 and 0.9906, respectively. On the original held-out rule splits, accuracy and F1 were 0.9765 and 0.9774, respectively. One clause appeared in two folds and the others appeared once.
  On common folds across all 111 patients, F1 was 0.9600 with SHAP, 0.9910 without SHAP and 0.9909 for L1 logistic regression. The inclusive SHAP cutoff retained all 100 ranked proteins per audited fold. Absolute logistic-regression coefficients reproduced the SHAP-guided candidate sets, clauses and held-out predictions in both the all-patient and paired-only analyses. A single-protein threshold reproduced full-rule predictions in the paired-only cohort.
  SHAP guidance did not improve held-out F1 on the common folds. Diagnostic utility, early detection, prognosis and generalisability beyond this cohort remain unestablished. Biomarker and clinical claims require independent validation, rule-stability testing under repeated resampling and further biological annotation.

title: One Size Doesn't Fit All: Input Adaptive Class Activation Mapping for Improved Visual Explanations
authors: Ayesha Sahar, Tahir Mustafa Madni, Tehseen Zia, David Windridge, Uzair Iqbal Janjua, Waleed Umar
abstract: Despite their widespread use in tasks such as image classification, object detection and semantic segmentation, the limited interpretability of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) can undermine trust and hinder adoption in safety-critical applications. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods seek to address this by providing human-understandable explanations for model predictions. Class Activation Maps (CAM) constitute one such widely used XAI technique for visualizing discriminative regions. However, existing CAM methods may exhibit limitations in channel weighting, localization, and adaptability across network architectures potentially resulting in noisy or imprecise explanations. To address these issues, we propose ADAPT-CAM, a gradient-based, parameter-adaptive CAM framework. The method combines first-order gradient energy with activation-weighted second-order curvature to derive channel contributions. It further incorporates adaptive local contrast normalization and knee-guided soft channel selection to refine the resulting explanations. Importantly, key parameters are estimated independently for each input, allowing the framework to adapt to variations in feature representations across network architectures. We validate ADAPT-CAM on ImageNet and Oxford 102 Flowers across CNN and ViT architectures. Quantitative results demonstrate competitive or superior performance against established CAM methods across multiple evaluation metrics. In parallel, qualitative comparisons illustrate its ability to highlight discriminative image regions. Further parameter analysis and ablation experiments examine the behaviour and contributions of the individual adaptive components. These findings demonstrate the applicability of ADAPT-CAM across different architectures and datasets.

title: Packing Stern into L2: GPU-Accelerated Primal-Shortened ISD for High-Codimension Binary Goppa Key Recovery
authors: Raullen Chai, Xinxin Fan
abstract:
Primal-Shortened Information-Set Decoding (ISD) with quadratic polar lifting recently pushed TII McEliece Track-2 key recovery to $mt=126$ (TII-228, $2{,}463$ CPU core-hours), with over $99\%$ of runtime spent harvesting weight-$(2t+1)$ codewords. Porting MiniMax's Mode-6 Stern sampler directly to one block per SM leaves $1.0\text{-}1.5\text{ GB}$ of hash tables active and stalls on global memory. We pack $128$ syndrome bits into one $16$-byte ulonglong2 without left-triple indices (lossless for $mt \le 145$, and extended to $mt \le 192$ via truncated range pre-filtering), share $G \in \{4, 8\}$ cooperative tables inside GPU L2 cache, batch $64G$ random systematic reductions per launch, and widen the shortening prefix $n'$ to cut modeled GPU-hours by $34\%\text{-}47\%$.
  Across five Track-2 challenges ($mt = 108 \to 153$), every recovered private key passes both the official SageMath checker and a standalone pure-Python verifier. Eight Modal L40S GPUs solve TII-228 ($mt=126$) in $18.9\text{ min}$ ($2.15$ GPU-hours, $3.0\times$ faster in wall-clock than MiniMax's EPYC cluster). We further recover keys for the previously undocumented challenges TII-237 ($mt=135$, $22.1$ L4 GPU-hours), TII-235 ($mt=144$, $39.62$ L40S GPU-hours, $17.97\text{ s}$ lift), and TII-185 ($mt=153$, $140.4$ L40S + $\approx 60$ L4 GPU-hours, $39.01\text{ s}$ lift). These results do not demonstrate practical recovery against Classic McEliece parameters ($mt \ge 768$).

title: Policy-intrinsic Demonstration Curation
authors: Sunjae Jeong, Geunhyeok Yu, Dowoon Lee, Hyoseok Hwang
abstract: Fine-tuning a robot policy for a new target task requires target demonstrations, but only a few are available. Demonstrations of other tasks can fill this gap, and demonstration curation selects the useful ones among these candidates. Retrieval-based curation selects the candidates that are most similar to the target demonstrations. Since it does not use the policy, any candidate that looks similar receives a high score. Performance-aware curation therefore estimates the effect of each candidate on the policy. However, this requires training on the candidates and takes a long time. We propose a third branch, policy-intrinsic curation, which uses the policy and still takes little time. It estimates this effect with forward passes of the pretrained policy and needs no training. We instantiate this branch with PICKER (Policy-Intrinsic Curation from Known Errors). It selects the candidates on which the policy makes errors that agree with those on the target demonstrations. PICKER reaches success rates comparable to those of performance-aware curation and takes about as long as retrieval-based curation. Its selection is also stable across seeds.
comment: 15 pages (including 1 page of references and 6 pages of appendices), 5 figures, 7 tables

title: OmniSLAM: Evidence-Authorized Revision of Persistent Object Maps
authors: Haoxiang Jie, Yaoyuan Yan, Zhiyou Heng, Liang Li, Zhaosong Li, Lifeng Liu
abstract: A new surface observation can extend an object map while contradicting an earlier object assignment. Treating both updates as a single merge can join unrelated objects; keeping all earlier assignments leaves fragmented objects unresolved. We present a revision module that makes these decisions separately. Historical merges require shared-mask evidence to outweigh separate-object explanations across views, including after removal of any one observation. New measured points are assigned through local competition among object seeds supported by image masks. On two preselected KITTI-360 windows, the method improves mean building/car instance AP50:90 from 17.259 to 18.762. On four further spatial holdouts, AP rises from 20.263 to 23.171, although unconditional revision reaches 23.251. Controlled comparisons attribute the gains to protecting existing identities, consolidating selected fragments, and assigning new points locally. The results also show where conservative merge decisions suppress useful updates. A garage recording demonstrates the same revision module on LiDAR--inertial--visual mapping outputs.

title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
authors: Kanghui Tian, Shuai Dong, Yuhan Zhu, Congcong Wang, Ji Zhao, Tianxiang Jiang, Zhixiong Zhang, Shengyuan Ding, Yi Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao
abstract: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student that predicts clicks directly from screenshots at native resolution. The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision. At inference, the same decision head selects a visual token, and a lightweight pixel head predicts the click within it, all in one forward pass. A click-aligned loss encourages pixels inside the target box to score above those outside. Across four benchmarks, PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B achieves 83.8% mean accuracy, the highest among the evaluated single-forward grounders, with a mean latency of 0.43 s per target.

title: De Novo Generation of Odorant Molecules with Targeted Olfactory Receptor Activation Patterns
authors: Kexin Zhang, Manhao Guan
abstract: Odor perception arises from a combinatorial code in which each molecule activates a specific subset of olfactory receptors (ORs), and the resulting activation pattern determines the perceived smell. We present a framework for de novo generation of molecules predicted to match target multi-receptor activation profiles. We first construct a panoramic binding matrix over 20 ORs, then cluster it to discover representative activation patterns, and finally formulate a structured selectivity loss, combining pairwise ranking, distribution matching, and complexity constraints, to steer a molecular generator via reinforcement learning. Across nine target profiles of varying complexity, our method achieves high predicted selectivity within 18000 oracle calls and provides the largest gains on profiles that are rare under the prior, especially broad-spectrum and sparse-activator targets.

title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments
authors: Yi-Fei Cao, Tianxin Huang, Hanbo Xie, Jian-Qiao Zhu
abstract: A Large Language Model (LLM), its harness, and the test-time compute budget jointly determine its behavior. Consequently, the same underlying model, embedded in different agentic workflows or allocated different amounts of test-time compute, can exhibit markedly different performance. Psychologists face an analogous challenge when evaluating human performance: the same person may behave differently under different incentives and levels of deliberation. Psychological tasks therefore provide an ideal testbed for studying such behavioral variation. However, when adapted to LLMs, these tasks are typically text-transcribed, replaying fixed, language-rendered experiments as static prompts. This format is ill-suited to agent evaluation, where actions can alter future observations and task states. Conversely, although dynamic environments are prevalent in the evaluation of LLM agents, they rarely ask whether the resulting behavior is human-like. Here, we bridge this gap by transforming psychological tasks into dynamic environments in which agents can interact and by using a learned human-policy model to evaluate how compatible the resulting behavioral trajectories are with human behavior. Across these environments, we find that this compatibility varies with an LLM's agentic configuration and the psychological task, and that memory raises it mainly by making choices more predictable rather than more human-like. These findings motivate a more holistic evaluation of LLM agents in psychology-inspired environments, accounting for both the backbone model and its agentic scaffold.

title: ConsisX: Cross-View Consistency Thinking in 3D for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Yunhe Zhang, Long Gao, Yuedong Fu, Gang He, Li Xu, Chang Wu, Yuqi Zhu, Pengyu Li
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models integrate visual perception and language understanding from vision-language models (VLMs) with action prediction for robotic manipulation. Although multi-view observations provide complementary scene information, VLMs model cross-view interactions based on 2D feature similarity, which can lead to physical inconsistency in the form of cross-view incorrect association between distinct entities and cross-view information fragmentation about the same entity. To address these challenges, we propose ConsisX, a novel VLA framework that integrates cross-view association and entity coherence to enable cross-view consistency thinking in 3D for physically consistent robotic manipulation. Specifically, Cross-View Association Modeling (CAM) is proposed to introduce cross-view spatial proximity constraints in a shared 3D space to reduce cross-view incorrect association. Entity Coherence Organization (ECO) is designed to organize cross-view local information into coherent 3D entity evidence, thereby addressing cross-view information fragmentation. Consistent Action Conditioning (CAC) is introduced to condition action prediction on task-relevant 3D entity evidence for cross-view consistent action execution. Experiments on 3 real-world manipulation tasks and 4 simulation benchmarks establish ConsisX as an effective and competitive framework for robotic manipulation.

title: SVUBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
authors: Yuxuan Liang, Bohan Zhang, Haiyang Yu, Bocheng Hu, Ke Niu, Xu Li, Zhengtao Yao, Yan Wen, Haotian Chen, Xiaolei Chen, Jiacong Wang, Zhe Liu, Jingqun Tang, Benlei Cui, Fan Shi, Xiangyang Xue
abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to interpret unfolding events, respond timely, and retrieve relevant historical evidence. To systematically evaluate these capabilities, we introduce SVUBench, a comprehensive proactive streaming video benchmark comprising 12,131 questions and 62,881 answer points across ten proactive tasks spanning Perception, Understanding, and Reasoning. Constructed through model-assisted annotation and human verification, SVUBench introduces two complementary interaction modes. Basic evaluates sustained proactive responses from video onset, while Trajectory requires historical recovery and continuous response updates following task activation during streaming. A Duration-Scaled Challenge further evaluates these capabilities across four video duration tiers. We develop the Proactive Response Score (PRS) with task-adaptive answer windows to jointly assess answer correctness, response timeliness, historical consistency, and content quality. Extensive experiments and analysis reveal the strengths and limitations of existing models, highlighting directions for advancing proactive streaming video understanding.

title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
authors: Jiawei Guo, Yu Huang, Dijiang Dong, Yue Liu, Peiran Ren, Wei Shen
abstract: Precise language control requires embodied models to follow instructions governing both task outcomes and execution. Although recent methods train policies to follow increasingly detailed commands, existing benchmarks often assess instruction following alongside perception, planning, and generalization to unfamiliar scenes. Higher task success therefore offers limited evidence of closer adherence to instructions. We introduce RoboInF, a benchmark measuring how reliably manipulation policies adapt their behavior to changes in an instruction. For each of eight tasks, six to twelve expert-validated instruction branches vary the requested goal, procedure, or manipulation detail while holding the initial scene and robot state fixed. Task-specific checkers verify the terminal goal and use recorded trajectories, contacts, and event sequences to assess compliance throughout execution. The accompanying RoboInF-4K dataset pairs 4,242 expert demonstrations with simulator-derived annotations of motion and contact. We evaluate leading manipulation policies ($π_{0.5}$ and OpenWAM) and inference-only agents (GPT-6 Astra and Qwen3.8-Flash). All four models exhibit a gap between task completion and faithful execution, indicating substantial room for fine-grained instruction following.

title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
authors: Yuxi Wang, Yufei Liu, Chengkai Jin, Qingyue Chen, Wenqi Ouyang, Tianyi Wei, Kerui Ren, Siyuan Huang, Zhiqi Shen, Hongsheng Li, Xingang Pan
abstract: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras. In this work, we propose ViDiHand2, a geometry-driven framework that reformulates VDM-based hand depth estimation from direct regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving. Specifically, we introduce Fine-Grained Geometric Lifting and Clip-Level Ray Fitting, which recover metric depth by enforcing geometric consistency between pixel-aligned 2D joints and the metric structure of MANO hands, while leveraging temporal observations across the clip. Since the lifting relies on these 2D joints, to improve robustness under occlusion and image truncation, we further develop Confidence-Gated Fusion to adaptively combine geometrically lifted joints with MANO predictions according to localization confidence. Finally, we enhance the VDM backbone to better capture spatial-temporal representations and produce the per-frame 2D joint and MANO predictions that both steps rely on. Extensive experiments on seven public datasets demonstrate that ViDiHand2 consistently outperforms 18 baselines, reducing in-the-wild absolute joint error by 42% and detection failures by 8.82x compared with the best baseline on each metric, while running at 57 FPS. The project page is available at https://vidihand2.github.io/.

title: Vasicek Graph Diffusion Model
authors: Junyi Tang, Chang Liu, Kun Zhan
abstract: Diffusion-based graph generation models progressively transform Gaussian noise into structured graphs through stochastic dynamics. We observe that the effectiveness of this transformation is fundamentally determined by the evolution of the diffusion trajectory. Existing graph diffusion models often suffer from excessive uncertainty during diffusion and delayed growth of the signal-to-noise ratio, causing useful structural information to emerge only in the later stages of generation. To address this issue, we propose the Vasicek Graph Diffusion (VGD), a graph diffusion process derived from the Vasicek dynamics. The key insight of VGD is data-anchored mean dynamics with a closed-form solution, which analytically establishes a continuous transition from Gaussian noise to the target graph distribution. Unlike conventional graph diffusion processes that rely predominantly on stochastic evolution, VGD introduces a data-anchored drift that continuously steers the latent state toward the target distribution throughout diffusion. As a consequence, VGD maintains a smoothly evolving uncertainty while rapidly increasing the signal-to-noise ratio throughout diffusion, allowing informative graph structures to emerge much earlier during generation. Extensive experiments on multiple graph generation benchmarks demonstrate that VGD outperforms existing diffusion-based graph generative models in terms of generation quality and structural fidelity.

title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data
authors: Merel Kuijs, Till Richter, Rushin H. Gindra, Korbinian Traeuble, Christian Matek, Rebeka Luknárová, Tingying Peng, Fabian J. Theis
abstract: Modeling multimodal data from partially paired samples is critical for advancing domains like biomedicine, where vast unimodal datasets and foundation models exist but paired data remains scarce. Existing fusion methods rely on large-scale paired datasets, limiting their use in scenarios with incomplete pairing. We introduce CAMEO, an adversarial learning-based modality fusion framework that integrates modalities from small, partially paired datasets. Combining any pre-trained unimodal encoder with a cross-modal latent alignment mechanism, CAMEO learns shared representations requiring only minimal paired samples. Evaluated on computational pathology tasks such as niche classification and cell type composition prediction, CAMEO achieves superior data efficiency, outperforming contrastive approaches like CLIP in low paired-data regimes, and highlighting the benefits of adversarial alignment when paired annotations are scarce. To facilitate further research, we additionally release a fully annotated HuggingFace dataset comprising three organs and paired image and gene expression modalities. By extending fusion methods to address limited pairing and small-scale datasets, we provide a framework that advances multimodal learning and broadens its applicability to real-world biomedical problems.

title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
authors: Da Xiao, Qingye Meng, Shengping Li, Xingyuan Yuan
abstract: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

title: Optimising VLM Harnesses to Localise Errors in Generated Videos
authors: Ankit Yadav, Nikhil Cherian Kurian, Arpit Garg, Lingqiao Liu
abstract: Identifying subtle errors in generated videos is an important step toward automated video generation, where errors must be detected to assess and refine generated clips. Recent work shows that pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) can localise such errors, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the workflow used: choices about which frames to inspect, which tools and model calls to make, and how to combine predictions can lead to substantially different results. We study VLM harnesses for video error localisation. Instead of relying on manually designed harnesses, we propose Harness Search and Merge (HSM), an algorithm that automatically constructs them by searching over executable evaluation programs. An LLM orchestrator refines candidate harnesses independently on random training subsets, records findings in a memory, and constructively merges complementary candidates. We evaluate HSM on Spotlight, a recently proposed benchmark for localising errors in generated videos. HSM achieves 0.234 $\pm$ 0.012 F1, exceeding the strongest benchmark strategy (0.173 $\pm$ 0.016), and retains its lead on an unseen video generator (0.213 $\pm$ 0.008 versus 0.140 $\pm$ 0.003). On IPV-Bench, it achieves strong localisation performance with lower false-alarm rates than existing optimisation baselines. Together, these results show that searching over complete VLM harnesses can outperform existing evaluation strategies, transfer to an unseen video generator, and reduce false alarms on real videos.

title: LimeTree: Linear-Memory Graph Neural Networks over Tree-Graphs for Resource-Efficient Language Modeling and Context Extrapolation
authors: Elisabeth Fink
abstract: The search for computationally efficient alternatives to the Transformer has yielded numerous architectures in recent years; however, most exhibit severe weaknesses in associative recall-such as key-value (KV) retrieval-and length extrapolation, where even standard Transformers struggle. This paper introduces LimeTree, a linear-complexity architecture in both memory and compute for sequence modeling. By integrating synthetic KV retrieval tasks directly into standard language modeling training, LimeTree achieves strong perplexity alongside reliable recall. Two variants were evaluated on WikiText-103 and PG-19 under strict compute constraints. On WikiText-103, LimeTree reaches a token-level perplexity of 19 in just 6 hours on four Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs, while maintaining 100\% KV retrieval accuracy even when extrapolating from a training context length of 512 to an evaluation length of 16,384. On PG-19, the model achieves a token-level perplexity of 10.84 in 35.5 hours on a single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU with minimal hyperparameter tuning. These results position LimeTree as a competitive linear-complexity alternative to Transformers, combining superior perplexity and training throughput with robust in-context retrieval and length extrapolation.

title: Fairness-optimized interlacing knots for even-degree periodic B-spline interpolation
authors: Shutao Tang, Zixuan Zhao
abstract: Interpolating an ordered set of points by a B-spline curve is a fundamental operation in computer-aided geometric design. Most of the literature addresses open curves, where the Schoenberg--Whitney condition characterizes a nonsingular collocation matrix and averaging is the standard way to choose the knot vector. Periodic B-spline interpolation has received much less attention, and the open-curve algorithms cannot be transferred directly. No theoretical criterion is available for choosing the knots, and the few existing constructions, such as the shifting and energy methods, remain empirical, with neither a theoretical guarantee nor a supporting analysis. This paper addresses this gap for even degrees. We prove that for every even degree $p\ge2$ the periodic collocation matrix is nonsingular whenever the domain knots and the interpolation parameters interlace, in either of two admissible orderings, for arbitrarily nonuniform parameters. Rather than singling out one knot vector, this sufficient condition delimits an $n$-parameter family of admissible knot vectors and provides the theoretical foundation for knot selection that periodic interpolation has lacked. It also explains why the empirical shifting method is solvable, previously justified only by an incorrect diagonal-dominance argument. We then exploit the remaining freedom to place the knots by fairness optimization, which preserves admissibility at every iterate and leads to the methods Opt-R and Opt-L. On four closed shapes with irregularly distributed points these methods achieve a fairness comparable to the shifting and energy methods, improve on them in several cases, and offer guarantees that no empirical construction provides.

title: Token Pruning Needs a Protected Sink Token: Coherent Spatial Aggregation in Vision Transformers
authors: Julian Wyatt, James Willoughby, Allison Clement, Irina Voiculescu
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are a predominant architecture for computer vision, with token reduction emerging as a popular paradigm to improve their efficiency. Prior work compares reduction algorithms, but not how models respond to them, nor how their response changes with model depth. We propose Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact on the prediction when tokens are explicitly removed during the forward pass. Applying MCTP to recent pretrained models, we observe that most, such as DINOv3, maintain a similar ranking of token importance at every depth (high Coherent Aggregation), while SigLIP 2 does not. This coherence requires predictions to survive pruning, which depends on keeping high-norm "sink" tokens: prefix tokens are kept by design, while prefix-free SigLIP 2 forms them on patch tokens, which pruning may remove. We show that in removing DINOv3's prefix tokens, its predictions and coherence collapse, while protecting only 5 tokens for SigLIP 2 cuts the token impact outside the object's bounding box by up to 62%. Beyond this, MCTP offers a post-hoc method to evaluate how a pretrained ViT responds to pruning, and suggests that token reduction methods should keep "sinks".

title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
authors: Yihong Luo
abstract: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the trainable policy velocity onto rollouts from a behavior distribution. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect online self-consistency. This behavior--policy mismatch breaks baseline invariance and injects baseline-induced gradient drift, destabilizing training. To resolve this issue, we propose Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching (iTDM), taking the infinitesimal limit of Trajectory Distribution Matching toward a time-local reward-guided target via the posterior-score identity to yield a sample-level gradient anchored at the behavior velocity without learning an additional reward-tilted target score. Tracking this velocity with an online auxiliary denoiser guarantees exact baseline invariance at the auxiliary optimum, effectively suppressing baseline drift across both online and offline RL. Extensive experiments across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment show that iTDM achieves state-of-the-art in-domain and out-of-domain performance across group-wise online/offline RL and pairwise offline RL. Notably, on the challenging GenEval2 benchmark, iTDM converges nearly 3\times faster than competing methods while scaling smoothly to 0.87 without collapse. Furthermore, iTDM scales effectively to the 5.6B FLUX.3 model, achieving better performance across both in-domain and unseen metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM

title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
authors: Xuanlei Zhao, Hailun Xu, Kai Wang, Yang Luo, Yingxuan Ren, Zirui Zhu, Yuxuan Lou, Kun Xu, Yan Wang, Kanchan Sarkar, Yang You
abstract: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity. Attending to all earlier loops also lets layers skip intermediate ones, so we restrict each layer to a residual window of the latest W loops, forcing every loop to build incrementally on recent ones. Across 6 pretrained LLMs from 3 model families and 9 benchmarks, LoopRes delivers significant and consistent gains: at 2x compute, it improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base by 29.1% over SFT, more than doubling the gain of the state-of-the-art baseline. The gains hold on larger models up to 30B and across all three families. More importantly, from 1.7B to 8B, LoopRes scales more steeply than SFT as compute grows, reaching a higher ceiling while needing less compute on long outputs. These results establish LoopRes as an effective looping approach, delivering both better performance and better test-time scaling.

title: Treatment Effects in Extreme Regimes
authors: Ahmed Aloui, Ali Hasan, Yuting Ng, Miroslav Pajic, Vahid Tarokh
abstract: Understanding treatment effects in extreme regimes is important for characterizing risks associated with different interventions. This is hindered by the unavailability of counterfactual outcomes and the rarity and difficulty of collecting extreme data in practice. To address this issue, we propose a new framework based on extreme value theory for estimating treatment effects in extreme regimes. We quantify these effects using variations in tail decay rates of potential outcomes in the presence and absence of treatments. We establish algorithms for calculating these quantities and develop related theoretical results. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on various standard synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets.

title: Modern Self-Supervised Vision Transformers Are Pareidolic
authors: Zihang Lin, Huaiyuan Qin, Liangli Zhen, Qing Guo, Jun Liu, Yew-Soon Ong, Hongyuan Zhu
abstract: In human perception, pareidolia is the tendency to perceive a meaningful pattern, such as a face, in a random or ambiguous stimulus. We find a similar phenomenon in modern self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs): on white noise, which contains neither objects nor spatial structure, a few directions of their features still form spatially coherent patterns across the patches, imposed by the features themselves. We call this behavior pareidolia, and the span of these directions the pareidolic subspace. On natural images, it holds most of the feature variance in DINOv2 and DINOv3 but little in DINO. This excess explains why DINOv2 and DINOv3, despite stronger dense features, fall far behind DINO in object emergence, the hallmark ability of self-supervised ViTs to identify the patches of an object on their own. Our experiments further show that scaling down their pareidolic subspaces steadily restores their ability to discover objects, so their object emergence is hindered rather than lost. These findings naturally lead to a training-free calibration: Pareidolic Subspace Calibration (PSC) measures the pareidolic subspace only on a noise input and then calibrates the features of natural inputs by scaling its directions down to the variance level of the remaining directions. Across diverse object emergence tasks, PSC improves DINOv2 and DINOv3 by up to 31.7 CorLoc on object discovery, 30.2 maxF on saliency detection and 59.9~$\mathcal{J}$ on video object segmentation. To identify the cause of pareidolia, we trace it block by block and find that it forms in the middle blocks of every self-supervised model we examine but stays strong to the last block only in models trained with a patch-level loss; controlled training confirms that an image-level loss alone lets it fade.

title: Quickly excluding an apex-forest
authors: Jędrzej Hodor, Hoang La, Piotr Micek, Clément Rambaud
abstract: We give a short proof that for every apex-forest $X$ on at least two vertices, graphs excluding $X$ as a minor have layered pathwidth at most $2|V(X)|-3$. This improves upon a result by Dujmović, Eppstein, Joret, Morin, and Wood (SIDMA, 2020). Our main tool is a structural result about graphs excluding a forest as a rooted minor, which is of independent interest. We develop similar tools for treedepth and treewidth. We discuss implications for Erdős-Pósa properties of rooted models of minors in graphs.

title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Zien Wang, Yuhao Pan, Yunfeng Fan, Nan Cheng, Xin Xia, Wenchao Xu
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce WeaveVLA, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context. A learned-query readout summarizes the updated graph representations into compact relational tokens, which condition the action expert alongside the original vision-language context. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages spatial structure preservation. We instantiate WeaveVLA on StarVLA-GR00T and $π_{0.5}$, achieving over 98% average success on LIBERO with both backbones. On LIBERO-Plus, WeaveVLA improves success from 74.9% to 82.0% and from 85.7% to 87.8%, respectively, with additional improvements on CALVIN D$\rightarrow$D. On three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based variant improves average success from 55.6% to 70.0% under standard conditions and from 33.3% to 53.3% under OOD perturbations, surpassing the $π_{0.5}$ baseline in both settings.

title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
authors: Chen Wang, Jiahui Huang, Riccardo de Lutio, Alex Trevithick, Bryan Chu, Jiawei Ren, Laura Leal-Taixé, Shengyu Huang, Lingjie Liu, Haithem Turki
abstract: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one. To overcome both, we propose Lyris, a long video generation framework that never leaves the video model without an anchor: a persistent point-cloud memory where the scene has been observed or generated, and a 3D layout that a vision-language model authors where it has not. Our key insight is that the interface between the two models can be surprisingly coarse. A layout of one labeled 3D box per object is simple enough for a vision-language model to author (and for a user to edit), yet expressive enough for a video model to follow once rendered along the camera path. We demonstrate walkthroughs of over three minutes and 50 meters from a single photo, passing through doorways into rooms it never shows. When evaluated on minute-long round trips across four datasets, Lyris outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a wide margin, reducing camera error by 3.8x and improving consistency upon return by 22% on average.

title: A Steerable Deep Network for Model-Free Diffusion MRI Registration
authors: Gianfranco Cortés, Xiaoda Qu, Baba C. Vemuri
abstract: Nonrigid registration is vital to medical image analysis but remains challenging for diffusion MRI (dMRI) due to its high-dimensional, spatio-angular dependence. We present a novel, geometric deep learning framework for model-free, nonrigid registration of raw dMRI data. We formulate registration in the native spatio-angular acquisition space under the joint action of 3D roto-translations, $\mathrm{SE}(3)$. Central to our framework is the equivalence between equivariant spatio-angular convolutions and 3D steerable convolutions on spherical-harmonic coefficient fields, which we exploit to construct an $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant U-Net. A by-product of this design choice is freedom from having to augment the data with roto-translated versions of itself. We also formulate a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss between water-displacement distributions, evaluated in Fourier space as a weighted sum of squared signal differences, and extend it with a local contrast correction that reduces to a local correlation. In controlled comparisons, including a known deformation of real tissue, the raw signal yields markedly more accurate alignment than fractional anisotropy under the same optimizer. On held-out HCP subjects and on a held-out clinical-grade cohort (AOMIC) from a different scanner, our method improves anatomical overlap over ANTs SyN on fractional anisotropy, mrregister on fODFs, DDMReg and SynthMorph, without estimating any derived representation, and the steerable network matches a conventional U-Net with fewer parameters while being unaffected by grid rotations of its inputs. This work establishes a foundation for data-driven, geometry-aware dMRI registration directly in the acquisition space.

title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
authors: Rishabh Batra
abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.
translation: 最近的一系列工作已确立EFI对作为量子密码学的“最小”假设。近来，Cavalar等人[CCC+26]证明了EFI对等价于非均匀可扩展单副本伪随机态生成器（1PRS），并获得了EFI对的非均匀元复杂性刻画。我们消除了他们构造中的非均匀性，并证明了EFI对等价于可扩展1PRS。作为推论，我们获得了EFI对的首个均匀元复杂性刻画。结合Batra和Jain[BJ24]所证明的统计可验证单向态生成器与承诺之间的等价性，这给出了经典单向函数、承诺和伪随机生成器之间等价关系的量子类似物。

title: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
authors: Aleksa Milojević, Patryk Morawski, János Pach, Ankan Sadhu, Benny Sudakov, Gábor Tardos, Istvan Tomon, Ji Zeng
abstract:
A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. Recently, using AI tools, we discovered that a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich essentially resolves this conjecture, with the implicit constant depending superexponentially on $k$.
  In this paper, we greatly improve this bound, showing that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. Our proof is purely combinatorial, based on a geometric charging scheme and Erdős-Szekeres type arguments. We also construct $k$-quasiplanar graphs on $n$ vertices with $Ω(k^{8/7}n)$, disproving the widely held belief that the right order of magnitude is $Θ(kn)$.

title: Randomized Forward Mode of Automatic Differentiation For Optimization Algorithms
authors: Khemraj Shukla, Yeonjong Shin
abstract: Reverse mode automatic differentiation (AD) computes a gradient in a single sweep, but at a memory cost that grows with the length of the computational graph. That cost becomes the binding constraint when the graph is long, as in parameter identification governed by differential equations or in training on memory-limited hardware. We study a randomized forward mode gradient (RFG) as an alternative to backpropagation in precisely this regime. RFG is a random gradient estimator built from the directional derivative along a random vector, a quantity that forward mode AD computes without storing a tape. Replacing the gradient with RFG yields a class of optimization algorithms; for RFG-based gradient descent (GD) and Polyak's heavy ball (PHB) methods, we establish convergence results on quadratic functions. The analysis reveals that using random vectors from a probability distribution with the smallest kurtosis yields the fastest rate of convergence. Computational experiments demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithms and verify the theoretical findings, including beyond quadratic functions. We further characterize when RFG is computationally preferable to backpropagation. Since the variance of RFG grows with the parameter dimension $d$ while the memory required by the reverse mode grows with the length $\ell$ of the computational graph, the relevant figure of merit is the ratio $\ell/d$. We confirm this by measurement against reverse mode with checkpointing. For a physics-informed neural network, where $d$ is large and $\ell$ short, RFG is not competitive. For parameter identification governed by differential equations, where a handful of coefficients is recovered from a long time integration, RFG requires one to three orders of magnitude less memory. The price is a larger iteration count, which leaves its time to solution comparable to or worse than a well-tuned reverse mode.

title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
authors: Ge Zhong, Charith Jayasekara, Nisal De Silva, Muhammad Usman, Muhammad Aamir Cheema, Chetan Arora
abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification with a known ideal success fraction, under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.

zh_title: 噪声幅度放大中的可观测频谱框架：停止稳定性与校正
translation: 噪声幅度放大的停止规则通常依赖于特定信道的成功概率公式，这限制了它们在不同噪声机制间的迁移。我们开发了一个可观测频谱框架，用于具有已知理想成功分数的平稳噪声标准幅度放大，并在显式的主导模式、频谱分离和残余控制条件下。在此类别中，第一个放大波瓣具有阻尼振荡的主导分量和有界非主导贡献。我们推导了频率偏移、阻尼和可观测相位偏移如何使主导峰值位移，并建立了采样间隙准则，以保持理想的整数停止深度、认证重新校准或选择稳健的候选窗口。在单目标Grover搜索中，频率和阻尼误差的停止坐标敏感性与搜索空间大小成正比，而相位偏移则与其平方根成比例；残余模式可以独立地逆转相邻深度的排序。分析构造、电路仿真、有限次推断和校准导出的设备类轨迹检验了这些预测及其操作限制。对于一个64元素的搜索，事后采样集检查选择深度五而非六，成功概率从0.595增加到0.626。由此产生的理论将可观测频谱动态与条件整数停止保证联系起来，而无需单独的微观信道解决方案。
tldr: 本文提出了一种可观测频谱框架，用于解决噪声幅度放大中停止规则对特定信道依赖的问题，并提供了在存在噪声时保持理想停止深度的标准和校正方法。
ai_comments: 这篇论文提出了一种创新的方法，通过可观测的频谱动态来处理噪声幅度放大中的停止问题，避免了对特定信道模型的依赖，这对于量子算法在实际噪声硬件上的实现具有重要意义。其引入的采样间隙准则和对不同误差敏感性的分析，为噪声环境下的鲁棒量子计算提供了理论基础和实用指导。
motivation: 现有的噪声幅度放大停止规则通常依赖于特定信道的成功概率公式，这限制了它们在不同噪声机制间的迁移性。
method: 开发了一个可观测频谱框架，用于具有已知理想成功分数的平稳噪声标准幅度放大，并满足显式的主导模式、频谱分离和残余控制条件。推导了频率偏移、阻尼和可观测相位偏移如何影响主导峰值，并建立了采样间隙准则以保持理想的整数停止深度、认证重新校准或选择稳健的候选窗口。
results: 在所提出的框架内，第一个放大波瓣具有阻尼振荡的主导分量和有界非主导贡献。在单目标Grover搜索中，频率和阻尼误差的停止坐标敏感性与搜索空间大小成正比，而相位偏移则与其平方根成比例；残余模式可以独立地逆转相邻深度的排序。通过分析构造、电路仿真、有限次推断和校准导出的设备类轨迹验证了这些预测。例如，对于64元素的搜索，事后采样集检查选择深度五而非六，成功概率从0.595增加到0.626。
conclusion: 该理论将可观测频谱动态与条件整数停止保证联系起来，而无需单独的微观信道解决方案。

title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning
authors: Andreas Hermansen, Tobias Golling, Slava Voloshynovskiy
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) and explicit physical inductive biases have driven major advances in jet tagging, yet they are typically pursued along separate tracks. In this work, we unify both paradigms by integrating the Lorentz-equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) architecture with the LeJEPA framework for representation learning. Pre-training on 100 million jets from the JetClass dataset, we optimize towards a latent space, which is invariant across physics-motivated jet augmentations. We demonstrate that enforcing Lorentz symmetry in the latent space is critical for representation quality and that this can be achieved either architecturally or learned via kinematic augmentations. With a standard non-invariant Transformer backbone, LeJEPA outperforms established autoregressive, masked particle modelling, and self-distillation baselines in linear- and MLP-probe accuracy, with L-GATr-slim providing further complementary gains. Across downstream benchmarks, our pre-trained models consistently outperform baselines trained from scratch or through different pre-training objectives.
zh_title: 自监督表示学习中的洛伦兹对称性
translation: 自监督学习（SSL）和显式的物理归纳偏置是推动喷流（jet）分类取得重大进展的两个主要因素，但它们通常是沿着不同的轨迹进行的。在本研究中，我们将这两种范式统一起来，将洛伦兹等变的几何代数Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) 架构与用于表示学习的LeJEPA框架相结合。我们在JetClass数据集中对1亿个喷流进行预训练，优化目标是使潜在空间对物理启发的喷流增强操作保持不变。我们证明了在潜在空间中强制执行洛伦兹对称性对于表示质量至关重要，并且可以通过架构设计或通过运动学增强来学习实现。使用标准的非不变Transformer骨干网络，LeJEPA在線性探針和MLP探針準確度方面優於現有的自迴歸、遮罩粒子模型和自蒸餾基準，而L-GATr-slim提供了进一步的补充增益。在下游基准测试中，我们的预训练模型始终优于从头训练或通过不同预训练目标训练的基线模型。
tldr: 本研究将自监督学习（SSL）与物理归纳偏置相结合，提出了L-GATr-slim架构与LeJEPA框架的统一，并通过预训练优化了不变的潜在空间，证明了洛伦兹对称性在表示学习中的重要性。
ai_comments: 这项研究成功地将自监督学习与物理学的基本原理（洛伦兹对称性）相结合，为表示学习领域带来了创新。通过将L-GATr-slim架构与LeJEPA框架相结合，并证明了洛伦兹对称性在提高表示质量方面的关键作用，该研究为未来的物理信息机器学习模型提供了有价值的见解。然而，在实际应用中，模型的计算复杂性和可扩展性可能需要进一步考虑。
motivation: 在粒子喷注（jet）分类任务中，自监督学习（SSL）和显式的物理归纳偏置是推动进展的两个主要方向，但它们通常是分开研究的。本工作旨在将这两种范式统一起来。
method: 将洛伦兹等变的几何代数Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) 架构与LeJEPA框架相结合进行表示学习。在JetClass数据集中对1亿个喷注进行预训练，优化目标是使潜在空间对物理启发的喷注增强操作保持不变。通过架构设计或学习到的运动学增强来实现潜在空间中的洛伦兹对称性。
results: 通过强制潜在空间中的洛伦兹对称性，可以提高表示质量。在标准非不变Transformer骨干网络上，LeJEPA在線性探針和MLP探針準確度方面優於現有的自迴歸、遮罩粒子模型和自蒸餾基準。L-GATr-slim提供了进一步的补充增益。在下游基准测试中，预训练模型始终优于从头训练或通过不同预训练目标训练的基线模型。
conclusion: 本研究成功地将自监督学习与物理归纳偏置相结合，并通过L-GATr-slim架构和LeJEPA框架的统一，证明了在表示学习中强制执行洛伦兹对称性的重要性。该方法在粒子喷注分类任务中取得了优于现有基线模型的性能。

title: Sparse Hodge Preference Optimization: Fine-Tuning Language Models toward Alignment beyond Transitive Preferences
authors: Yiming Liu, Jianwei Ma, Zhongwei Xing, Tonghui Yu
abstract: The growing adoption of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which leverages pairwise preference data, reflects its great success in fine-tuning large language models to align with human expectations. It directly optimizes the policy from human preferences without explicit reward modeling or the complexities of reinforcement learning-based approaches. However, the classic DPO relies on the Bradley--Terry sampling model and cannot effectively capture intransitivity or cyclic structures in aggregated human preference data. In this article, we propose Sparse Hodge Preference Optimization (SHPO), a preference optimization algorithm that augments DPO with a sparse antisymmetric curl residual motivated by the combinatorial Hodge decomposition. We prove that SHPO strictly enlarges DPO's hypothesis class on comparison graphs containing at least one triangle, under some mild regularity conditions on the response representations. We further establish a theoretical guarantee for $\ell_1$-regularized estimation of the curl coefficients under fixed policy and representations. Qualitative studies on three preference datasets under the same QLoRA budget, SHPO-aligned LLM achieves satisfactory performances in preference accuracy, cyclic structure recovery, and GPT-4o-judged generation quality.
zh_title: 稀疏霍奇偏好优化：微调语言模型以实现超越传递性偏好的对齐
translation: 直接偏好优化（DPO）的日益普及，它利用成对偏好数据，反映了它在微调大型语言模型以符合人类期望方面取得了巨大成功。它直接从人类偏好中优化策略，而无需显式的奖励建模或基于强化学习的方法的复杂性。然而，经典的DPO依赖于Bradley-Terry采样模型，并且无法有效地捕捉聚合人类偏好数据中的非传递性或循环结构。在本文中，我们提出了稀疏霍奇偏好优化（SHPO），一种偏好优化算法，它通过引入稀疏反curl残差来增强DPO，该残差源于组合霍奇分解。我们证明，在对响应表示的一些温和正则性条件下，SHPO在包含至少一个三角形的比较图上严格扩大了DPO的假设类别。我们进一步为固定策略和表示下的curl系数的$\ell_1$正则化估计提供了理论保证。在相同QLoRA预算下的三个偏好数据集上的定性研究中，SHPO对齐的LLM在偏好准确性、循环结构恢复和GPT-4o评估的生成质量方面取得了令人满意的性能。
tldr: SHPO是一种新的偏好优化算法，它通过引入稀疏反curl残差来扩展DPO，以更好地处理人类偏好数据中的非传递性和循环结构，并在偏好准确性、循环结构恢复和生成质量方面取得了令人满意的结果。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的偏好优化算法SHPO，它通过引入基于组合霍奇分解的稀疏反curl残差来改进DPO，以解决人类偏好数据中常见的非传递性和循环结构问题。理论分析和实验结果都支持SHPO的有效性，表明它在偏好准确性、循环结构恢复和生成质量方面优于DPO。该方法在处理复杂偏好数据方面具有重要意义，为语言模型对齐提供了新的途径。
motivation: 经典的DPO方法依赖于Bradley-Terry采样模型，无法有效捕捉聚合人类偏好数据中的非传递性或循环结构。
method: 提出稀疏霍奇偏好优化（SHPO）算法，该算法通过引入稀疏反curl残差来增强DPO，该残差源于组合霍奇分解。
results: 在三个偏好数据集上的定性研究表明，SHPO在偏好准确性、循环结构恢复和GPT-4o评估的生成质量方面取得了令人满意的性能。
conclusion: SHPO成功地扩展了DPO的假设类别，并能有效处理非传递性偏好数据，在多个指标上表现出令人满意的性能。

title: InterGS+: Inter-Frame Gaussian Splatting Compression with Geometry-Aware Transformer Prediction and Adaptive Residual Coding
authors: Muhammad Talha, Zhu Li, Joel Jung
abstract: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides real-time photorealistic rendering, but representing each frame as irregular Gaussian primitives with high-dimensional attributes creates substantial storage and transmission cost. Exploiting temporal redundancy is challenging because Gaussian primitives do not preserve fixed identities across frames. We propose InterGS+, a lightweight post-hoc inter-frame codec that jointly improves temporal prediction and residual representation. Current-frame geometry is coded with G-PCC and reconstructed before prediction, enabling consistent temporal neighborhoods at encoder and decoder. Attributes are predicted using lightweight KNN and bilateral predictors together with a geometry-aware transformer for spherical-harmonic (SH) appearance, with per-Gaussian mode selection. Residual coding is adapted to each attribute: SH innovations are coded in a shared PCA domain using vector quantization with refinement, opacity and scale in activated gamma-companded domains, and rotation as canonicalized quaternion innovations using vector quantization and refinement. On MPEG dynamic sequences, InterGS+ achieves average BD-rate reductions of 45.48% over G-PCC Amd. 1 and 7.78% over InterGS-Lite, with corresponding BD-PSNR gains of 9.98 dB and 1.10 dB. Average decoding complexity is 0.049 ms/Gaussian, demonstrating efficient streamable dynamic 3DGS compression.
comment: Accepted for poster presentation at the 2027 Data Compression Conference (DCC 2027)
zh_title: InterGS+：基于几何感知Transformer预测和自适应残差编码的帧间高斯泼溅压缩
translation: 动态3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）提供了实时逼真的渲染，但将每帧表示为具有高维属性的不规则高斯基元会产生巨大的存储和传输成本。利用时间冗余具有挑战性，因为高斯基元在帧之间不保留固定的身份。我们提出了InterGS+，一种轻量级的后处理帧间编解码器，它共同改进了时间预测和残差表示。当前帧几何通过G-PCC编码并在预测前重建，从而在编码器和解码器处实现一致的时间邻域。属性使用轻量级KNN和双边预测器以及用于球谐（SH）外观的几何感知Transformer进行预测，并进行每高斯模式选择。残差编码适应于每个属性：SH创新在共享PCA域中通过矢量量化和细化进行编码；不透明度和尺度在激活的伽马压缩域中编码；旋转作为规范化的四元数创新，使用矢量量化和细化进行编码。在MPEG动态序列上，InterGS+相对于G-PCC Amd. 1实现了45.48%的平均BD-rate降低和9.98 dB的BD-PSNR增益，相对于InterGS-Lite实现了7.78%的平均BD-rate降低和1.10 dB的BD-PSNR增益。平均解码复杂度为0.049 ms/高斯，证明了高效可流式的动态3DGS压缩。
tldr: InterGS+是一种轻量级帧间编解码器，通过几何感知Transformer预测和自适应残差编码，显著提高了动态3D高斯泼溅的压缩效率，实现了高效可流式的动态3DGS压缩。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过引入几何感知Transformer预测和自适应残差编码，有效解决了动态3DGS在帧间压缩中的挑战，尤其是在高斯基元身份不固定的情况下。其创新点在于结合了几何重建和Transformer预测，以及针对不同属性的精细化残差编码策略。在压缩效率和解码复杂度方面均表现出色，对于推动动态3DGS在实际应用中的部署具有重要意义。
motivation: 动态3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）虽然能实现实时逼真的渲染，但将每帧表示为具有高维属性的不规则高斯基元会产生巨大的存储和传输成本。此外，高斯基元在帧之间不保留固定的身份，使得利用时间冗余进行压缩变得具有挑战性。
method: InterGS+是一种轻量级后处理帧间编解码器。它首先使用G-PCC编码并重建当前帧几何，以确保编解码器之间一致的时间邻域。属性预测结合了轻量级KNN和双边预测器，以及用于球谐（SH）外观的几何感知Transformer，并进行每高斯模式选择。残差编码针对每个属性进行自适应：SH创新在共享PCA域中通过矢量量化和细化进行编码；不透明度和尺度在激活的伽马压缩域中编码；旋转作为规范化的四元数创新，使用矢量量化和细化进行编码。
results: 在MPEG动态序列上，InterGS+相对于G-PCC Amd. 1实现了平均BD-rate降低45.48%和BD-PSNR增益9.98 dB。相对于InterGS-Lite，实现了平均BD-rate降低7.78%和BD-PSNR增益1.10 dB。平均解码复杂度为0.049 ms/高斯。
conclusion: InterGS+实现了高效可流式的动态3D高斯泼溅压缩。

title: GeoCANO: A Geometry-Conditioned Adaptive Neural Operator for Physical-Field Prediction on Varying Domains
authors: Biao Chen, Xinrui Zhou, Xianlin Jin, Jing Wang, Jifa Zhang, Chen Zhai, Wei Liu, Miao Zhang
abstract: Industrial design requires repeated evaluation of candidate configurations. Integral performance measures alone do not resolve critical local phenomena, while high-fidelity simulation remains costly. Existing physical-field surrogates often couple geometry representation and coordinate evaluation through prescribed mesh topologies, limiting reuse across resolutions. We propose the Geometry-Conditioned Adaptive Neural Operator (GeoCANO), which maps a sampled complete three-dimensional geometry to a coordinate-dependent field function. An attention-based encoder extracts a geometry state from unordered surface coordinates. A multiresolution axis-factorized hash encoding and query-wise sparse mixture-of-experts decoder enhance multiscale expressiveness. GeoCANO constructs the field representation before introducing output coordinates, allowing one geometry encoding to be reused across regions without rebuilding the graph for each output topology. We evaluated GeoCANO on transonic aerodynamic-field prediction over complete aircraft configurations using a Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes dataset of 10,484 wing-body-nacelle geometries. For unseen configurations within the sampled design family, GeoCANO outperformed baselines in complete-surface prediction, high-gradient pressure reconstruction, and pressure-drag recovery. It reduced pressure-coefficient mean absolute error by 77.9% relative to the strongest baseline and retained an advantage over a finite range of wall-normal distances. Ablation studies showed that geometry-modulated coordinate encoding achieved comparable accuracy with substantially fewer parameters than conventional three-dimensional hash encoding. Routing analysis indicated spatially structured, query-dependent expert specialization. These results demonstrate a reusable continuous-coordinate representation for rapid physical-field evaluation over varying geometries.
zh_title: GeoCANO：一种用于变化域上物理场预测的几何条件自适应神经算子
translation: 工业设计需要重复评估候选配置。仅凭整体性能指标无法解决关键局部现象，而高保真模拟仍然成本高昂。现有的物理场代理模型通常通过预设网格拓扑将几何表示和坐标评估耦合，限制了跨分辨率的重用。我们提出了几何条件自适应神经算子（GeoCANO），它将采样的完整三维几何映射到坐标相关的场函数。一个基于注意力的编码器从无序表面坐标中提取几何状态。多分辨率轴分解哈希编码和查询相关的稀疏专家混合解码器增强了多尺度表达能力。GeoCANO在引入输出坐标之前构建场表示，允许一个几何编码在不同区域重复使用，无需为每个输出拓扑重建图。我们在10,484个机翼-机身-短舱几何体的雷诺平均纳维-斯托克斯数据集上，评估了GeoCANO在完整飞机配置上的跨音速气动场预测。对于采样设计族中未见的配置，GeoCANO在完整表面预测、高梯度压力重建和压力阻力恢复方面均优于基线模型。相对于最强的基线，它将压力系数平均绝对误差降低了77.9%，并在有限的壁面法向距离范围内保持优势。消融研究表明，几何调制坐标编码在参数量显著减少的情况下达到了与传统三维哈希编码相当的精度。路由分析表明了空间结构化的、查询相关的专家专业化。这些结果证明了一种可重用的连续坐标表示，可用于快速评估不同几何形状上的物理场。
tldr: GeoCANO是一个新的神经网络模型，通过几何条件和自适应机制，能高效准确地预测不同几何构型上的物理场，解决了现有方法在重用性和精度上的限制。
