translation: 准确表征城市内部的温度变化对于热健康监测至关重要，然而官方监测网络过于稀疏，无法解析精细尺度的梯度，特别是对于全球南方的城市。我们提出了BRUCE，一个贝叶斯分层时空模型，利用整合嵌套拉普拉斯近似（INLA）和一个随机偏微分方程（SPDE）空间分量拟合，融合了巴西里约热内卢的四种异构温度源：官方气象站、低成本物联网传感器、公民科学个人气象站和ERA5-Land再分析数据。该模型考虑了类别和站点特定的测量偏差，并通过自回归（AR1）结构估计了逐日演变的连续空间场。独立拟合九个月度窗口（2023-2025年的1月、6月、11月）发现，海拔高度系数在所有窗口中均显著，并且在八个窗口中量级一致（每标准差－1.08至－1.38摄氏度）。在针对LCZ4r的留出区域交叉验证中，准确度具有可比性（所有三个窗口中RMSE差值均在站点级自助法不确定性之内），同时BRUCE在所有留出站点（包括LCZ4r被掩码的站点）都产生了预测，并比LCZ4r的离散分区分类保留了更精细的空间结构。应用到241个初级保健区域时，BRUCE的后验超标概率允许对96个区域进行高置信度分类（基于模型的分类），而源自LCZ4r交叉验证误差的固定宽度区间不支持对任何区域进行自信分类。该框架为数据异构环境下的城市内高温监测提供了一个统计学严谨且业务上可行的基础。
keywords: 整合嵌套拉普拉斯近似 (INLA)
tldr: 提出了一种名为BRUCE的贝叶斯时空模型，通过融合多源异构温度数据，实现了城市内部高精度、精细化的气温动态监测。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的贝叶斯分层时空模型（BRUCE），巧妙地融合了官方气象站、低成本物联网传感器、公民科学气象站以及再分析数据等多种异构数据源，有效解决了全球南方城市（如里约热内卢）气温监测网络稀疏的问题。其方法不仅考虑了测量偏差，还通过INLA和SPDE实现了高效的精确时空插值，在城市高温监测和公共卫生决策中具有极高的应用价值。
motivation: 官方监测网络过于稀疏，无法解析城市内部特别是全球南方城市的精细化温度梯度，难以满足准确的热健康监测需求。
method: 提出了一种名为BRUCE的贝叶斯分层时空模型，利用整合嵌套拉普拉斯近似（INLA）和随机偏微分方程（SPDE）空间分量，融合了四种异构温度数据源，并通过自回归（AR1）结构在时间上建模。
results: 在交叉验证中，BRUCE表现出与LCZ4r相当的准确性，但在掩码区域也能进行预测，保留了更精细的空间结构；在241个初级保健区域的应用中，基于BRUCE的后验超标概率成功高置信度地分类了96个区域，而传统方法无法实现。
conclusion: BRUCE框架为数据异构环境下的城市微气候监测提供了一个统计学严谨且业务可行的解决方案，显著提升了城市热岛效应和高温健康风险评估的精度与置信度。

title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
authors: Yin Liu, Shanshan Zhao, Didong Li
abstract: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. We further characterize the limitations of naive inference based on synthetic data, and develop a variance correction and a distribution calibration procedure to recover valid inference of original data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed generative and inferential framework with extensive simulations and two real data applications.
zh_title: 删失时间事件数据的真实生成建模：从分布保真度到统计推断
translation: 合成数据已成为数据共享、临床试验模拟和数字孪生开发的重要工具，在生物医学研究和药物开发中的应用日益广泛。然而，对于临床试验和生存分析至关重要的合成时间-事件数据，受到的关注却很有限。特别是，合成生存数据的分布保真度的理论保证在很大程度上仍未被探索。更重要的是，即使生成器实现了分布保真度，下游统计分析是否可靠仍不清楚。为了填补这些空白，我们提出了一种通用的生存数据两阶段生成框架（TSGSurv），该框架在事件状态条件下联合生成观测时间和协变量，并确立了其分布收敛速率。以广泛使用的Cox比例风险模型为重点，我们建立了生成器保真度保证模型系数估计一致性的条件。我们进一步刻画了基于合成数据的朴素推断的局限性，并开发了方差校正和分布校准程序以恢复原始数据的有效推断。我们通过大量的模拟和两个真实数据应用证明了所提出的生成和推断框架的有效性。
tldr: 本文提出了针对删失生存数据的两阶段生成框架TSGSurv，并解决了其在下游统计推断中的有效性与偏差校正问题。
ai_comments: 该论文针对带有删失的时间事件数据，创新性地提出了TSGSurv框架，不仅从理论上探讨了生成数据的分布保真度及其收敛速率，还深入研究了下游统计推断的可靠性，并开发了方差校正和分布校准方法以解决朴素生成数据的推断偏差问题。这对于医疗健康领域的合成数据共享和临床试验模拟具有重要意义。
motivation: 现有合成数据研究较少关注临床试验和生存分析中核心的删失时间事件数据，缺乏对合成生存数据分布保真度的理论保证，且即使生成器实现了分布保真度，下游统计分析的可靠性也尚不明确。
method: 提出一个通用的两阶段生存数据生成框架（TSGSurv），在事件状态条件下联合生成观测时间和协变量，建立其分布收敛速率；针对Cox比例风险模型建立保证模型系数估计一致性的条件；开发方差校正和分布 calibration 程序来恢复原始数据的有效推断。
results: 通过大量模拟实验和两个真实数据应用，证明了所提出的生成和推断框架的有效性，并揭示了基于合成数据的朴素推断的局限性。
conclusion: 论文提出的TSGSurv框架及后续的方差校正和分布校准程序，有效连接了生存数据的生成式建模与下游的统计推断，填补了该领域的理论和方法空白。

title: Causal Effect Estimation Under Uncertain Statistical Surrogacy
authors: Yi Liu, Alexander W. Levis, Shu Yang, Larry Han
abstract: Surrogate endpoints can improve the efficiency of causal effect estimation, but such gains may depend on structural assumptions. One such assumption is statistical surrogacy, which requires the primary outcome to be conditionally independent of treatment given the surrogate and baseline covariates. We study causal effect estimation with multiple candidate surrogates of uncertain validity under statistical surrogacy, considering settings where the primary outcome is either fully observed or subject to missingness. We characterize the asymptotic efficiency differences between surrogate-assisted and benchmark estimators, examine the bias induced by violations of statistical surrogacy, and identify conditions under which incorporating surrogate information leads to efficiency gains or losses. To address uncertainty in surrogate validity, we propose Surrogate-assisted Adaptive Causal effect EStimation (SACES), a procedure that anchors estimation to a robust benchmark while adaptively selecting among a finite set of surrogate-assisted estimators using an estimated mean squared error criterion. SACES aims to leverage efficiency gains when statistical surrogacy holds while preserving consistency when the assumption is violated. Simulations demonstrate that SACES achieves a favorable bias-variance trade-off across varying degrees of surrogacy violation. We illustrate the proposed methods using data from the ACTG 175 clinical trial to demonstrate how surrogate information can be adaptively incorporated into causal effect estimation.
zh_title: 不确定统计替代性下的因果效应估计
translation: 替代终点可以提高因果效应估计的效率，但这种收益可能取决于结构性假设。其中一个假设是统计替代性，它要求在给定替代指标和基线协变量的条件下，主要结果与处理条件条件独立。我们研究了在统计替代性下，具有多个有效性不确定的候选替代终点的因果效应估计，考虑了主要结果完全观测或存在缺失值的设置。我们刻画了替代辅助估计量与基准估计量之间的渐近效率差异，检查了统计替代性违背所引起的偏差，并确定了并确定了纳入替代信息会导致效率增益或损失的条件。为了解决替代有效性的不确定性，我们提出了替代辅助自适应因果效应估计（SACES）程序，该程序将估计锚定在一个稳健的基准上，同时使用估计的均方误差准则在一组有限的替代辅助估计量中进行自适应选择。SACES旨在当统计替代性成立时利用效率增益，同时在假设被违背时保持相合性。模拟表明，SACES在不同程度的替代性违背下实现了良好的偏差-方差权衡。我们使用ACTG 175临床试验的数据说明了所提出的方法，展示了如何将替代信息自适应地纳入因果效应估计中。
tldr: 本文提出了自适应因果效应估计（SACES）方法，能够在统计替代假设不确定时，安全地利用替代终点提高估计效率，同时在假设失效时保持稳健性。
ai_comments: 该论文针对因果推断中替代终点有效性不确定的问题，提出了SACES方法，在利用替代终点提升估计效率的同时，通过锚定稳健基准来保证在统计替代假设失效时的相合性，兼顾了偏差与方差的权衡。
motivation: 虽然替代终点可以提高因果效应估计的效率，但这种增益依赖于往往不确定的结构假设（如统计替代性），因此需要一种能够在假设违背时保持稳健性同时在假设成立时利用效率增益的方法。
method: 研究了替代辅助估计量与基准估计量的渐近效率差异，分析了假设违背引起的偏差，并提出了自适应因果效应估计（SACES）程序，基于估计的均方误差准则在有限的一组替代辅助估计量中进行自适应选择，同时锚定于稳健的基准。
results: 理论和模拟表明，SACES在不同程度的替代性违背下实现了良好的偏差-方差权衡；通过ACTG 175临床试验数据验证了该方法自适应纳入替代信息的有效性。
conclusion: SACES方法能够有效处理多个候选替代终点有效性不确定的问题，在统计替代假设成立时获得效率增益，在假设违背时保持一致性。

title: Geometry, Local Minimax Risk, and the Limits of Sample Average Approximation in Linear Stochastic Optimization
authors: Hanbo Yang, Ming Yuan
abstract: We study how the local geometry of a linear stochastic optimization problem determines its statistical difficulty, measured by expected decision regret. The optimal local rate is governed by how fast the support function of the feasible set grows away from its linearization at the true mean; depending on the instance, it can be $n^{-1/2}$, $n^{-1}$, $n^{-2}$, or a non-power rate, and sample average approximation (SAA) attains these rates in a Gaussian mean model. At smooth instances, SAA also attains the classical sharp local minimax constant. We then allow the data distribution to vary in a Kullback--Leibler (KL) ball of radius proportional to $1/n$ around a reference distribution $P$. The exact local minimax limit of this benchmark, which may depend on $P$, coincides with that of a Gaussian model whose local parameter set is the covariance ellipsoid of $P$. A simple coordinatewise truncated SAA rule, which does not use $P$, attains the minimax rate, and at smooth instances its constant matches the minimax constant as the neighborhood radius grows. Ordinary SAA, in contrast, can have strictly suboptimal worst-case expected regret when the local rate is fast relative to the tails of $P$, because rare tail events then dominate the expectation. The results delineate when SAA is sharply optimal, rate-optimal, or statistically suboptimal, and quantify the local price of distributional robustness.
zh_title: 线性随机优化中的几何学、局部极小极大风险与样本平均近似的极限
translation: 我们研究了线性随机优化问题的局部几何如何决定其统计难度（以期望决策遗憾衡量）。最优局部速率由可行集的支撑函数在其在真实均值处的线性化之外的增长速度决定；根据实例的不同，它可能是 $n^{-1/2}$、$n^{-1}$、$n^{-2}$ 或非幂律速率，而样本平均近似（SAA）在高斯均值模型中达到了这些速率。在平滑实例中，SAA还达到了经典的尖锐局部极小极大常数。然后，我们允许数据分布在参考分布 $P$ 周围半径与 $1/n$ 成正比的 Kullback--Leibler (KL) 球内变化。该基准的确切局部极小极大极限（可能取决于 $P$）与局部参数集为 $P$ 的协方差椭球的高斯模型的极限相吻合。一个不使用 $P$ 的简单的坐标截断 SAA 规则达到了极小极大速率，并且在平滑实例中，随着邻域半径的增长，其常数与极小极大常数相匹配。相比之下，当局部速率相对于 $P$ 的尾部较快时，普通 SAA 的最坏情况期望遗憾可能严格次优，因为罕见的尾部事件随后支配了期望。这些结果勾勒出 SAA 何时是尖锐最优的、速率最优的或统计上次优的，并量化了分布鲁棒性的局部代价。
tldr: 论文揭示了线性随机优化中局部几何如何决定统计难度，指出了样本平均近似（SAA）在处理重尾或快速局部率时的局限性，并提出了能达到极小极大率的截断SAA规则。
ai_comments: 该论文深入探讨了线性随机优化中局部几何结构对统计难度的影响，并揭示了样本平均近似（SAA）在不同几何形态和分布尾部条件下的优劣势，理论分析严谨且具有深度。
motivation: 旨在研究线性随机优化问题的局部几何结构如何决定其统计难度（由期望决策遗憾衡量），并探究样本平均近似（SAA）方法的极限及局限性。
method: 通过研究支撑函数的增长速度、局部极小极大风险、KL散度邻域内的最坏情况分析以及坐标截断的SAA规则进行理论推导。
results: 证明了SAA在平滑实例中能达到最优速率和局部极小极大常数，但在快速局部速率且尾部事件影响显著时，普通SAA可能表现出严格次优的最坏情况期望遗憾；而简单的坐标截断SAA规则则可达到极小极大速率。
conclusion: 论文阐明了SAA方法的局限性与最优性边界，并量化了分布鲁棒性的局部代价。

title: Fully Bayesian Benchmarking for Small Area Models with Count Data
authors: Soumadeep Bhowmick, Anindya Roy, Gauri S. Datta, Kyle M. Irimata, Jerry J.Maples
abstract: Small area estimates of counts are often required to conform exactly to reliable aggregates at a higher geographic level. Often the area-level model is specified on a transformed (nonlinear) scale such as a log scale. Specifying the small area model on the log-scale is common practice for positive responses. A prominent example is the production of the Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE) by the US Census Bureau. When the model is specified in a transformed scale, the benchmarking constraints, which are linear in the area means, become nonlinear in terms of the model parameters. We develop a new class of priors for Bayesian small area models under strict external benchmarking constraints when the small area model is specified in a transformed scale, and the model parameters belong to a Riemannian manifold due to the nonlinear benchmarking constraints. The prior is fully supported on the constrained parameter set, the manifold defined by the benchmarking constraints, and thereby provides a proper constrained posterior that is also supported on the restricted set. This facilitates full Bayesian analysis of the problem without the requirement of post-hoc modification to the posterior to enforce the benchmarking constraints.
zh_title: 计数数据小区域模型的全贝叶斯基准化方法
translation: 计数数据的空间小区域估计通常需要精确符合较高地理水平的可靠总体。区域级模型通常在变换（非线性）尺度（例如对数尺度）上指定。在对数尺度上指定小区域模型是正响应的常见做法。一个突出的例子是美国人口普查局制作的小区域收入和贫困估计（SAIPE）。当模型在变换尺度指定时，在区域均值上呈线性的基准化约束在模型参数方面变成非线性的。当小区域模型在变换尺度指定且模型参数由于非线性基准化约束而属于黎曼流形时，我们为严格外部基准化约束下的贝叶斯小区域模型开发了一类新的先验。该先验完全支持受约束的参数集（即由基准化约束定义的流形），从而提供了一个也支持受限集的适当约束后验。这促进了该问题的全贝叶斯分析，而无需事后修改后验来强制执行基准化约束。
tldr: 提出了一种在非线性尺度下针对小区域计数数据的全贝叶斯基准化方法，通过在黎曼流形上构建先验直接满足约束，无需事后调整。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一类针对计数数据的全贝叶斯基准化方法，特别适用于在非线性变换尺度（如对数尺度）下的小区域估计问题。通过在黎曼流形上定义先验分布，从根本上解决了非线性基准化约束下的参数估计问题，避免了事后调整。
motivation: 在变换（非线性）尺度下指定的小区域模型，其线性均值基准化约束在模型参数层面变成了非线性约束，现有的方法往往需要进行事后修改，因此需要一种能直接在约束参数集上提供正确后验分布的全贝叶斯方法。
method: 开发了一类新的先验分布，适用于在变换尺度下小区域模型面临严格外部基准化约束的情况，此时模型参数由于非线性基准化约束而属于黎曼流形。
results: 该先验完全支持受约束的参数集（即由基准化约束定义的流形），从而提供了也受限支持的适当约束后验，促进了该问题的全贝叶斯分析。
conclusion: 论文成功开发了一种在严格的外部基准化约束下适用于非线性尺度小区域模型的全贝叶斯先验及后验推断方法，无需事后修改。

title: A joint framework for SPX, VIX and VXX
authors: Martino Grasselli, Andrea Stanghellini, Sara Svaluto-Ferro
abstract: Options on VXX bring the dynamics of the VIX futures curve into the joint SPX-VIX calibration problem. We construct a common model by specifying the VIX and then recovering instantaneous SPX variance from the requirement that its risk-neutral conditional expected average over the next thirty days equals the squared VIX. With truncated signatures of time-extended polynomial diffusions, this recovery reduces to finite-dimensional linear algebra and gives explicit access to the futures underlying VXX. The same specification therefore governs equity variance and rolling volatility exposure. To accommodate flexible specifications while respecting variance nonnegativity, we develop a regularized model and quantify the pricing errors of its tractable VIX and VXX proxies. Applications to short-dated option smiles illustrate joint calibration across the three markets, with Monte Carlo estimates of the proxy error bounds well below quoted bid-ask spreads.
translation: VXX的期权将VIX期货曲线的动态引入了联合的SPX-VIX校准问题中。我们通过指定VIX并要求其在未来30天内的风险中性条件期望平均值等于VIX的平方，从而恢复瞬时SPX方差，构建了一个公共模型。利用时间扩展的多项式扩散的截断特征，这种恢复简化为了有限维线性代数，并显式地获取了VXX的基础期货。因此，相同的规范支配着股票方差和滚动波动率敞口。为了在遵守方差非负性的同时适应灵活的规范，我们开发了一个正则化模型，并量化了其易处理的VIX和VXX代理的定价误差。在短期期权微笑上的应用说明了跨这三个市场的联合校准，代理误差边界的蒙特卡洛估计远低于报价的买卖价差。
tldr: 本文提出了一种SPX、VIX和VXX市场的联合建模与校准框架，利用多项式扩散特征将方差恢复简化为线性代数，实现了极低的定价代理误差。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将VXX期权纳入SPX-VIX联合校准问题中，利用截断的多项式扩散特征，将瞬时方差恢复转化为有限维线性代数，具有高效和精确的定价优势。
motivation: VXX期权的引入将VIX期货曲线的动态带入了联合SPX-VIX校准问题中，需要一个公共模型来同时支配股票方差和滚动波动率敞口，以应对市场对灵活且无负方差规范的需求。
method: 通过指定VIX并利用风险中性条件期望等于VIX平方的要求来恢复瞬时SPX方差，结合时间扩展的多项式扩散的截断特征，将其简化为有限维线性代数，并开发了正则化模型以保证方差非负性。
results: 短期期权微笑的应用表明了跨三个市场的联合校准能力，且代理误差的蒙特卡洛估计值远低于标价的买卖价差。
conclusion: 通过构建联合框架并开发正则化模型，成功实现了SPX、VIX和VXX市场的联合校准，且代理误差远低于买卖价差。

title: Feasible sub-replicating portfolios for basket options via the block rearrangement algorithm
authors: Mohamad Hassan Abou Daya, Carole Bernard, Steven Vanduffel
abstract: We construct sub-replicating portfolios of vanilla options for a basket call when the marginal distributions of the underlying assets are known and their dependence is not. To do so, we reduce the n-asset problem to n two-asset problems of the type solved by Hobson, Laurence, and Wang (2005a), and use the Block Rearrangement Algorithm1 (BRA) to approximate the minimising dependence among the assets. The cash component of the portfolio is computed exactly, so that its price is a valid lower bound, and reassembling the BRA output with the original marginals gives an upper bound computed by quadrature; together they bracket the minimum basket-option price. In log-normal examples with three and six assets the bracket has a relative width of at most 0.1%, and the corresponding sub-replicating portfolios are sparse, using only two strikes per asset, while the resulting bounds are tighter than those obtained from a general-purpose multi-marginal optimal-transport algorithm with strikes on a grid. We also give the lower bound and an optimal portfolio in closed form in three special cases: a deep in-the-money basket, a basket with one dominant asset, and jointly mixable marginals.
zh_title: 通过块重排算法构建篮子期权的可行子复制投资组合
translation: 当底层资产的边际已知而相关性未知时，我们构建了篮子看涨期权的 vanilla 期权子复制组合。为此，我们将n资产问题简化为由 Hobson、Laurence 和 Wang（2005a）解决的n个两资产问题，并使用块重排算法（BRA）来近似资产之间的最小化相依性。组合的现金部分被精确计算，从而其价格是一个有效的下界；将 BRA 输出与原始边际重新组合，通过求积计算出一个上界；两者共同夹挤出最小的篮子期权价格。在包含三个和六个资产的对数正态示例中，夹挤区间的相对宽度最大为0.1%，并且相应的子复制组合很稀疏，每个资产仅使用两个行权价，同时所得界限比在网格上使用行权价的通用多边际最优输运算法获得的界限更紧密。我们还在三种特殊情况下以闭式给出了下界和最优组合：深度实值篮子、具有一个主导资产的篮子以及联合可混合的边际。
tldr: 本文提出了一种利用块重排算法构建篮子期权子复制投资组合的新方法，能够高效、准确地计算出极其紧密的期权价格上下界。
ai_comments: 该论文通过分块重排算法（BRA）有效解决了篮子期权无套利界限和子复制组合的计算问题，将高维问题降维，在计算效率和稀疏性上表现出色，对金融衍生品定价具有重要价值。
motivation: 在已知标的资产边际分布而未知其相关性时，如何为篮子看涨期权构建有效的 vanilla 期权子复制组合并计算其精确的无套利价格界限。
method: 将n资产问题降维为n个两资产问题，利用块重排算法（BRA）近似求解资产间的极小相依性，通过求积计算上界，并通过精确计算现金成份得出有效下界。
results: 在3资产和6资产的对数正态算例中，边界相对宽度最多为0.1%，组合非常稀疏（每个资产仅使用两个行权价），且边界比通用多边际最优输运算法更紧密；同时给出了三种特殊情况下的闭式解。
conclusion: 利用块重排算法可以高效、准确地构建篮子期权的可行子复制投资组合，并计算出紧密的上下界。

title: Statistical moments, risk weighting and percentiles of a loss distribution of a finite homogeneous credit portfolio; extending the Vasicek distribution
authors: Marco van der Burgt
abstract: The Vasicek distribution assumes an infinite portfolio of identical obligors and forms the basis of the Basel III/IV Risk Weighted Assets (RWA) calculation. We derive the central moments of the loss distribution for a finite number (n) of obligors. We use these moments to calculate percentiles of the fraction (x) of defaulted obligors, via the Cornish-Fisher expansion and via a weighting method. Both methods are based on scaling the standard deviation in x by a capital multiple. The weighting method assumes that the capital multiple is linear in the central moments and leads to an Extended Vasicek distribution. We apply this distribution in calculating an adjusted RWA for small portfolios. Simulations show that this adjustment is only relevant for small portfolios of less than 100 obligors and that the Extended Vasicek distribution allows analytical risk capital calculations for portfolios with different rating grades, even when the number of obligors per rating grade is small.
zh_title: 有限同质信贷组合损失分布的统计矩、风险加权和百分位数：扩展Vasicek分布
translation: Vasicek分布假设具有无限个相同的债务人，并构成了巴塞尔III/IV风险加权资产（RWA）计算的基础。我们推导了有限数量（n）债务人的损失分布的中心矩。我们利用这些矩，通过Cornish-Fisher展开和加权方法计算违约债务人比例（x）的百分位数。这两种方法都基于通过资本倍数对x的标准差进行缩放。加权方法假设资本倍数与中心矩呈线性关系，从而导出了扩展的Vasicek分布。我们将该分布应用于计算小型组合的调整后RWA。模拟表明，这种调整仅对少于100名债务人的小型组合相关，并且扩展的Vasicek分布允许对具有不同评级等级的组合进行解析风险资本计算，即使每个评级等级的债务人数量很少。
tldr: 本文通过推导中心矩扩展了Vasicek分布，实现了对债务人数量较少的小型信贷组合的风险加权资产（RWA）解析计算。
ai_comments: 该论文针对巴塞尔协议中Vasicek分布假设无限资产组合的局限性，创新性地推导出了有限同质信贷组合的中心矩，并提出了扩展Vasicek分布。这对于小规模信用资产组合的风险加权资产（RWA）计算具有重要的实用价值。
motivation: 传统的Vasicek分布假设债务人数量无限，构成了巴塞尔协议III/IV中风险加权资产（RWA）计算的基础，但无法精确反映具有有限债务人的实际信贷组合风险。
method: 推导有限数量债务人的损失分布中心矩，通过Cornish-Fisher展开和加权方法（假设资本倍数与中心矩呈线性关系）计算违约比例的百分位数，从而导出扩展Vasicek分布。
results: 模拟结果表明，这种调整仅对债务人少于100的小型组合相关，扩展Vasicek分布能够对小型评级组合进行精确的解析风险资本计算。
conclusion: 提出的扩展Vasicek分布允许对含有少量债务人的不同评级资产组合进行解析风险资本计算，特别适用于债务人少于100的小型组合。

title: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
authors: Aleksei Kozhevnikov
abstract: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-γ}$, $γ>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $κ$. If $r>κ$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. When the critical time falls before maturity, expected wealth at that time is finite exactly when the initial spread is zero. We also show that the suprema of the negative powers of optimal wealth and consumption are integrable on every finite horizon exactly for orders $0<m\le 1+γ$.
zh_title: 具有负幂效用的成对交易最优控制
translation: 我们在带有Ornstein-Uhlenbeck价差以及效用函数$U(x)=-x^{-γ}$（其中$γ>0$）的成对交易模型中，求解了一个有限时域的消费与投资问题。通过线性化Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman方程，我们给出了价值函数和最优反馈控制的显式公式。无需Novikov条件，利用预算不等式和凹性，我们验证了在每个有限时域内，对所有具有非负财富的容许策略而言该解的最优性。在最优反馈下，当利率$r$小于或等于均值回复率$κ$时，财富和消费承认确定性的上界。如果$r>κ$，则在起始时间之后的每个时刻，它们以正概率超过任何预设水平。如果$r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$，存在一个显式的临界时域，在此时刻及之后期望终端财富为无穷大，而最优期望效用仍然是有限的。当临界时间落在到期日之前时，恰好在初始价差为零时该时刻的期望财富才有限。我们还证明了，最优财富和消费的负幂的上确界在每个有限时域上可积的充要条件是阶数 $0<m\le 1+γ$。
tldr: 本文求解了具有OU价差和负幂效用的成对交易最优消费与投资问题，得到了显式解并分析了财富的长期行为与临界时域。
ai_comments: 该论文在成对交易模型下，利用负幂效用函数研究了有限时域内的消费与投资问题，通过线性化HJB方程得到了显式解，并对其渐近性质与期望财富的发散性进行了深入探讨，创新性地避开了Novikov条件。
motivation: 在成对交易模型（具Ornstein-Uhlenbeck价差）和负幂效用函数设定下，解决有限时域的消费与投资最优控制问题。
method: 线性化Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman方程以推导价值函数和最优反馈控制的显式公式，并利用预算不等式和凹性验证其在有限时域内所有容许策略下的最优性。
results: 给出了价值函数和最优反馈控制的显式公式，分析了利率与均值回复率大小对财富与消费确定性上界或概率超限的影响，并指出了临界时域的存在性以及某些高阶矩的积分性质。
conclusion: 通过线性化HJB方程成功求解了带有OU模型的成对交易最优控制问题，证明了解的显式形式及相关渐近与有限性性质。

title: Trading Before a Committed Rebalance
authors: Khizar Qureshi
abstract: An institution must complete a portfolio adjustment, but traders who prepare inventory for it can choose whether to participate. We study how public forecasts affect the institution's cost in a Bayesian execution game with optional activation, transient impact, and uniform-price terminal completion. The curvature of equilibrium cost as a function of the posterior target mean determines the value of information. In the scalar model, information benefits every fixed participation roster. Optional supply can reverse this ranking at entry, at full participation, and in a smooth interior with lognormal activation costs. For centered scalar targets, information weakly lowers cost relative to no information, strictly when the posterior mean is nonzero with positive probability. Centered Gaussian precision gains are always beneficial. An exact symmetric finite-population equilibrium identifies how information resolution and individual strategic size interact near entry. A portfolio extension gives a matrix criterion for the fixed-roster ranking, which can fail under general cross-impact. Even with isotropic execution, shared activation allows equally accurate signals about target magnitude and composition to have opposite execution values under one unchanged prior. Intraday ETF price data is used to characterize target uncertainty and trading conditions without identifying activation or institutional costs.
zh_title: 在承诺再平衡前进行交易
translation: 一家机构必须完成投资组合调整，但为之准备库存的交易者可以选择是否参与。我们在一个具有可选激活、瞬时冲击和统一价格终端完成的贝叶斯执行博弈中，研究了公开预测如何影响机构的成本。均衡成本作为后验目标均值函数的曲率决定了信息的价值。在标量模型中，信息有利于每一个固定的参与名单。可选供应可以在进入时、完全参与时以及具有对数正态激活成本的光滑内部逆转这种排序。对于中心化的标量目标，信息相对于无信息会微弱地降低成本，当后验均值以正概率非零时则严格降低。中心化的高斯精度增益总是有益的。精确的对称有限总体均衡确定了信息分辨率和个体战略规模如何在进入附近相互作用。投资组合扩展给出了固定名单排名的矩阵标准，这在一般的交叉冲击下可能会失效。即使在各向同性的执行中，共享激活也允许关于目标幅度和组成的同样准确的信号在未改变的先验下具有相反的执行价值。日内ETF价格数据被用于描述目标不确定性和交易条件，而无需识别激活成本或机构成本。
tldr: 本文通过建立贝叶斯执行博弈模型，研究了公开预测和可选参与对机构投资组合调整成本的影响，揭示了信息价值的复杂调节机制。
ai_comments: 本文构建了一个包含可选激活、瞬时冲击和统一价格终端完成的贝叶斯执行博弈模型，研究了公开预测对机构调整成本的影响，理论分析深入且贴近实际交易场景。
motivation: 研究在机构进行投资组合调整时，准备库存的交易者如何选择参与，以及公开预测如何影响机构的交易成本。
method: 通过构建带有可选激活、瞬时冲击和统一价格终端完成的贝叶斯执行博弈模型进行理论分析，并结合日内ETF价格数据刻画目标不确定性与交易条件。
results: 研究发现，信息通常能降低调整成本，但在标量模型的可选供应下，这一排序可能会在进入点、全参与点以及对数正态激活成本的平滑内部发生逆转；此外，共享激活允许关于目标幅度和组成的准确信号在相同先验下产生相反的执行价值。
conclusion: 信息对机构调整成本的影响取决于后验均值的曲率以及可选参与者的策略互动，信息通常有益，但在特定跨期冲击或共享激活下可能产生复杂甚至相反的价值。

title: Tracing the Messy Middle: A Runtime Transaction Schema for AI Coding Agents
authors: Yuelin Hou, Haorui Li, Lu Chen, Zhen Chen
abstract:
AI coding agents are increasingly integrated into software development, yet the field lacks a systematic feedback loop to improve their behavior in practice. Artifact datasets capture final outputs such as code patches, commits, and benchmark outcomes, but omit the messy middle of the development lifecycle: the failed retries, fallback strategies, routing decisions, and abandoned sessions that determine operational cost, reliability, and productivity.
  We propose an observability framework that captures these runtime behaviors as structured transaction records, enabling engineering coaching grounded in behavioral evidence, workflow optimization at the stages where tasks break down, and routing policy iteration measured by total task cost rather than per-request price. We define the runtime transaction schema this architecture requires and demonstrate initial feasibility through Agent Token Manager (Atm), a local-first prototype that reconciles gateway records and transcript evidence without exposing prompt content to external collectors. Finally, we identify three open research problems that must be solved to scale these feedback mechanisms: trace reconciliation without shared request identifiers, outcome linking across asynchronous systems, and intervention causality. Treating the linkage between sessions and artifacts as a fundamental infrastructure requirement provides a structured foundation for understanding and optimizing agent behavior.
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Peer-reviewed; accepted for presentation at the KDD 2026 Workshop on Agentic Software Engineering (SE 3.0), August 10, 2026, Jeju, Korea

title: A Metric for Semantic Graph Matching of No-Code Workflows
authors: Bartłomiej Matejczyk, Joao Tiago Aparicio
abstract: No-code and agentic systems increasingly produce executable workflows, but workflows cannot be compared adequately as strings because typed operations, parameters, and directed connections jointly determine the artifact. We define a semantic graph-matching distance for finite attributed workflow graphs. A partial one-to-one node matching determines node-substitution and directed labelled-edge disagreement, while unmatched nodes incur a positive null cost. Under a fixed type hierarchy, encoder, field universe, and metric-compatible primitive distances, the objective is a metric on workflow graphs up to attributed isomorphism. A padded Hungarian procedure provides a scalable feasible upper bound distinct from the exact objective. We evaluate the metric on 4,705 public n8n exports, representing 2,282 distinct normalized-graph hashes, 73,057 nodes, and 469 observed node types. Across 32,093 branch-and-bound-complete evaluations, the mean raw distance is near zero under surface-preserving transformations ($1.21 \times 10^{-5}$) and rises to $0.584$ under major type or subgraph changes. On a complete 796-hash panel, accumulated edit count has Spearman $ρ= 0.520$ with distance, while the median within-workflow correlation is $0.975$. One- and three-perturbation systems have marginal means of $0.307$ and $0.763$, and all 117,312 evaluated triangle orientations have non-negative slack. Weight ablations preserve the positive edit-count association across tested configurations. These tests support numerical consistency, near-invariance to surface-preserving transformations, graded sensitivity to semantic and structural change, and robust discrimination across controlled modifications. The metric measures artifacts and does not by itself assert behavioural equivalence under external state or runtime data.

title: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
authors: Shengxiang Lin, Jiajie Su, Pengyang Zhou, Xiang Chen, Xiaolin Zheng, Feng Tian, Chaochao Chen
abstract: LLM-enhanced recommender systems encode item side information into semantic embeddings, but these embeddings may leak sensitive textual attributes through inversion attacks. Existing input-side defenses rely on trusted collection or local token perturbation, often disrupting the inter-item semantic topology needed for recommendation. To address it, we introduce relational fidelity as the key objective, requiring semantic shift for privacy while preserving relative item relations for utility. Based on this principle, we propose prototype-guided progressive obfuscation (PGPO), which learns topology-aware obfuscation anchors for high-influence prototype words and propagates them through a static semantic graph. PGPO is optimized with GRPO using individual dissimilarity, structural consistency, and semantic constraint rewards. Experiments on two benchmarks show strong inversion defense with near-upper-bound recommendation performance. The code is available at https://github.com/Shengxiang-Lin/PGPO.

title: Neural Network-Based Modeling of Hysteretic Systems: From Prandtl and Preisach Neural Networks to Neuro-Madelung and Neuroplastic Continuous Models
authors: Mehrdad Shafiei Dizaji, Farzad Shafiei Dizaji
abstract: Hysteresis is a complex nonlinear phenomenon characterized by memory dependence, path dependence, and, in many physical systems, degradation, non-congruency, asymmetry, and rate dependence. This review examines the development and capabilities of Prandtl neural networks (PNNs), Preisach neural networks (PreisachNNs), generalized Prandtl neural networks (GPNNs), the neuro-Madelung model (NMM), extended Preisach neural networks (EPNNs), and dynamic plastic continuous neural networks (DPCNNs). Particular attention is given to their mechanisms for representing memory, network architectures, activation functions, training algorithms, treatment of deterioration and rate dependence, and applications to nonlinear structural and material systems. The PNN introduced hysteretic memory directly into neural activation through stop operators and demonstrated accurate nonlinear dynamic analysis of structures. Preisach-NNs subsequently extended this concept through an additional nonlinear hidden layer to represent non-Masing hysteresis. GPNNs introduced deteriorating-stop neurons to capture stiffness and strength degradation and non-congruent hysteresis. A different generalization was provided by the NMM, which combined Madelung's hysteresis rules with multilayer feedforward neural networks to represent diverse rate-independent and rate-dependent behaviors. These developments culminated in the EPNN, which combines deteriorating hysteretic operators, nonlinear neural mappings, and input-rate information to accommodate Masing and nonMasing, symmetric and asymmetric, congruent and noncongruent, and rate-independent and rate-dependent hysteresis.

title: Biologically-Inspired Spike Encoding and Optimization for Spiking Neural Networks
authors: Ayaan Qayyum, Bruce Yi Bu, Zicong Li, Jingfeng Zhou
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer theoretical energy-efficiency advantages over conventional deep networks, but realizing these advantages on vision tasks requires sparse spike representations that naive rate-coding methods fail to provide. We combine biologically motivated spike-encoding schemes with two training improvements: Rouser adaptive-threshold surrogate gradients and Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC) second-order optimization. The spike encoding schemes experimented with are rate coding, latency coding, DVS-style delta modulation, and Difference-of-Gaussians (DoG) filtering. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate that biologically inspired encoders yield the largest accuracy gains in capacity-constrained regimes and serve as an effective parameter-efficiency lever. DoG and delta modulation encoders produce significantly sparser spike trains than rate coding. K-FAC yields modest but consistent accuracy improvements over Adam-trained baselines, and Rouser's learnable per-neuron thresholds improve Fashion-MNIST accuracy from 87.37% to 88.13% by enabling homeostatic firing-rate regulation. Biologically grounded pre-processing methods can help close the accuracy gap between SNNs and non-spiking baselines without increasing model size.

title: GridForge: An Open Physics-Informed Digital Twin and Benchmark Suite for UK 11 kV Underground Distribution Cables
authors: Lilliane Linnet Musoke
abstract: The UK distribution-cable monitoring sector is data-rich but framework-poor: each Distribution Network Operator (DNO) collects megabytes of telemetry per asset per day, but there is no public benchmark dataset, no shared reference model, and no commonly agreed evaluation protocol for benchmarking sectoral, data-intensive models for operational decision support; notably for maintenance planning and prioritisation. We address this gap with GridForge, an open-source physics-informed digital twin and benchmark suite for fault diagnosis and prediction, integrating four building blocks: (i) a verified steady state and transient thermal model based on IEC 60287 and IEC 60853; (ii) a calibrated synthetic dataset of 64 cables (covering 320 cable-years) representing four canonical UK 11 kV thermal archetypes and four condition modes; (iii) a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate that satisfies the algebraic balance defined by IEC 60287 during training and reaches an RMSE of 0.148 °C on an independent held out set against the reference analytical oracle; and (iv) a five-task benchmark suite that includes three reference baseline models (pure physics, gradient-boosted trees, and the PINN). All numerical parameters are sourced from public standards, the code is licensed under the MIT licence, and the trained PINN converges in only two minutes (as run on the computing platform in Section 10.1), enabling independent verification by DNO engineering and research practitioners. At present only the virtual-sensor task (T4) discriminates between the reference baselines; the other tasks tie or are undefined on this test split, so extending the baselines with task-specific logic is a priority future enhancement. For open validation, the dataset, test sets and models are made available at https://github.com/mlily2024/Gridforge

title: ETA: Exit on Tool Arrival in Speculative Agent Loops
authors: Saptarshi Mitra, Xuan Zhu, Rohith Kukkala, Sitao Huang, Karthik Vijayan
abstract: Tool-using language agents in explicit thinking modes generate long chains of thought before acting, making each turn inherently serial: later tokens depend on the tool observation. Recent speculative tool dispatch methods overlap tool execution with reasoning, but offers limited benefit when reasoning dominates latency. We present ETA, that treats the speculative fork not as an actuator but as a sensor of the model's decision state, using it to terminate the reasoning of the main decode. It truncates reasoning only when the prediction is stable, agrees with the dispatched call, passes a free probe measuring whether a call will be emitted at all, and the tool result has arrived: a deadline that bounds per-turn regret by the remaining decode cost. ETA achieves speedups of 1.33x on tau2 airline/retail, 1.26x on tau2 telecom, and 1.13x on BFCL v4 multi-turn. On tau2, it decodes 24% fewer tokens at a nearly unchanged per-token rate without dropping action quality.

title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
authors: Jingwei Ge, Na Xie, Li Li, Jiayang Li
abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. Recently, Dmitry Rybin announced a seven-vertex counterexample found through an interaction with ChatGPT, which disproved this long-standing conjecture. However, the interaction did not reveal why this particular topology and its demand, fractional-flow, and cost choices work together, whether the example belongs to a broader family, or which structural features determine where counterexamples can occur. It also left unclear why the AI-assisted search succeeded where earlier human efforts had not. In this paper, we develop a forward counterexample construction pipeline. It starts from an arborescence on which failure is impossible and adds terminal-entering shortcut arcs. The resulting load constraints define a finite set of admissible route choices; their convex hull, the conflict polytope, yields exact conditions for demands, fractional flows, and costs. Starting from a simple arborescence, the pipeline selects Rybin's topology and characterizes all counterexamples it supports. Experiments further demonstrate the pipeline's transferability: when instructed to follow it while varying the initial arborescence and shortcut placement, ChatGPT produced counterexamples on topologies genuinely different from Rybin's and found valid constructions starting from 93 other rooted arborescence shapes. The theory also explains why the original example was difficult to discover through blind enumeration and suggests that Rybin's interaction lies between blind enumeration and a complete theory-guided construction.

title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence
authors: Truong Xuan Khanh
abstract: Response-relevant information is not sufficient evidence that two neural networks are in the same training state. We define training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent, relative to an intervention family and horizon, if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continues. On fresh runs of a one-layer transformer learning modular addition, response to a weight-decay pulse is highly reproducible relative to between-checkpoint differences (rho_state = 0.934 at 500 steps), establishing the target as measurable. Fifteen descriptors of weight spectra, representation geometry and optimiser geometry carry within-run response-relevant information beyond weight norm and loss on a development dataset, predicting held-out response deviation across seed blocks. But their apparent 16.1% advantage at matching checkpoints by future response does not separate from a conditional placebo preserving each descriptor's fitted dependence on the conventional observables, and a calibrated positive control makes simple insensitivity an unlikely explanation. Information a decoder can extract need not be organised in the pairwise geometry that similarity judgments require.
comment: 18 pages, 5 figures. Code and provenance verified artifacts: https://github.com/ClevixLab/training-state-equivalence

title: Chebyshev Polynomial Zonotope Abstractions for Certified Reachability of Learning-Enabled Systems
authors: Peng Xie, Amr Alanwar
abstract: Nearly all current methods for computing reachable sets of nonlinear dynamics propagate them with truncated Taylor expansions plus rigorous remainders. The expansion is pointwise: once its argument is a whole set rather than a point, one polynomial must stay accurate across that set, and it reaches only as far as its disc of convergence. The limit binds hardest on the rational terms and sigmoid gates of modern controllers: smooth as these look on the real line, in the complex plane they blow up at points just off the real axis, closer as a gate sharpens, and those points cap the set width a Taylor expansion can cover, most tightly on the switching surface where the controller decides. We prove a dichotomy: no Taylor degree certifies sets wider than that cap, while a Chebyshev abstraction of equal degree, anchored to the whole set in the same polynomial-zonotope pipeline, has no cap and gains width at a geometric rate in degree. Measured walls match the formulas to between 89 and 94 percent. We give closed-form rigorous remainders, among them the first polynomial softmax transformer; existing sound treatments are linear relaxations. On closed loops, certificates survive where the Taylor ones diverge, and specifications flip from unknown to proven; on trained classifiers up to real MNIST digits, the Chebyshev frontier certifies input territory the Taylor basis surrenders. Every certified claim passed large Monte-Carlo harnesses with zero violations, and an applicability map states in advance where the basis provably cannot matter.

title: Agent-Native Applications: A New Application Paradigm
authors: David Luo, Alberto Leon-Garcia
abstract: Traditional application architectures assume behavioral logic authored in advance, leaving reachable behavior largely bounded by explicit code and workflow rules. Large language model (LLM)-based agents challenge this assumption by enabling runtime reasoning and autonomous action to become part of application behavior, allowing applications to address situations not enumerated at design time. Extending this pattern, this paper identifies a new application paradigm in which LLM-based agents serve as central reasoning and action components responsible for the application's core logic and, where permitted, for adapting the application graph itself at runtime. We call these agent-native applications. While such applications significantly expand their possible behavioral space beyond explicit code and workflow rules, they also face a major control problem in which useful agentic reasoning should be preserved while application behavior should remain within a permissible space. We therefore propose an architectural model that represents the application as a portable graph of agents, tools, data sources, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) checkpoints, and encodes the application's permitted behavior as a behavioral envelope within a declarative application specification. At runtime, an application orchestrator serves as the control plane that coordinates tasks and governs how the graph and its permissions evolve, while an agent mesh serves as the data plane that mediates policy-relevant interactions and produces audit events. We then discuss the trust layer that makes agent-native applications governable and the supporting foundations required for practical operation. Two use cases illustrate the architecture, while Agent-Native Runtime (ANR) demonstrates selected core mechanisms in an executable prototype.
comment: 21 pages, 8 figures, 1 table, 1 code listing; published in IEEE Access

title: Budgeted Proper Loss Design for Uncertain Decision Thresholds
authors: Ankit Sharma
abstract: A binary probability estimate may be used by several decision makers with different error costs. Proper scoring rules can emphasize selected probability thresholds, but a single average threshold distribution need not give a good worst-case regret guarantee. We study the choice of a proper loss when the threshold distribution belongs to a finite specified family. Among integrable loss weights with a positive pointwise floor and a fixed total mass, we derive the weight that minimizes the sharp, distribution-free multiplier from surrogate regret to threshold-averaged decision regret. The solution clips a rescaled upper envelope of the threshold densities at the prescribed floor; its normalization is found by a one-dimensional root search. We give proofs of sharpness, optimality, and stability under density misspecification, as well as a limitation for atomic threshold laws. An exact histogram implementation and two synthetic experiments across 20 seeds verify the construction. The optimized multiplier improves over uniform and average-density weights, while fitted-model performance does not improve uniformly. The result is a loss-design guarantee under an explicit budget, rather than a general claim of predictive superiority.

title: Exploring Parkinson's Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Techniques
authors: Farhaan Qazi
abstract: In recent years, machine learning (ML) techniques have emerged as promising tools for accurate and timely diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) which is an incurable neurodegenerative disorder. This study explores the integration of ML algorithms and PD diagnosis, highlighting their potential applications in various aspects of the disease. ML methods such as support vector machines, decision trees, multilayer perceptron, k-nearest neighbours, logistic regression and random forest (with and without particle swarm optimisation) were applied on a PD dataset obtained from Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust containing data from 58 people. In terms of accuracy, the Decision Tree and Logistic Regression performed the best with scores of 72-76% while multilayer perceptron was least effective. All the models were remarkable in classifying positive PD cases with sensitivity scores going up to 97.56%, with SVM classifier at the pinnacle. However, ability to classify healthy controls from PD cases was insignificant throughout the board. Although, all the employed models delivered reasonable results in categorising PD patients in the presented dataset; access to more data, further study and advancement of these ML approaches could lead to enhanced diagnostic outcomes, supplementing to an improved understanding of Parkinson's disease.

title: The Obsolescence of High-Level Code: Agentic Generation from Semantic Artifacts
authors: Di Santi Eduardo
abstract:
This paper argues that high-level source code need not remain the primary persistent artifact of software development when AI agents can generate, validate, and regenerate executable implementations from semantic intent. We place this claim in historical context by revisiting application generators, CASE tools, model-driven development, and platforms such as GeneXus, where developers already maintained higher-level representations from which code and other artifacts were derived.
  We propose a unifying view in which generation is the fundamental operation: given a semantic specification S = (R, C, I, T, O), maintained as the semantic authority, an agent produces a generated executable artifact A. Functional requirements, contracts, and interfaces are assessed as semantic obligations, while tests and operational objectives are assessed by an explicit external oracle V(A, S). We operationalize this framework through an experiment in independent generation: multiple LLVM artifacts are generated directly from one frozen semantic authority and evaluated by the same external oracle.
  The experiment reports regeneration coherence on an evaluated domain, not a proof of absolute correctness. It provides initial evidence that independently generated executable artifacts can produce the same observable outcomes under a common semantic authority and external oracle. We conclude by discussing reproducibility, specification-centered evolution, and the implications of treating implementation representation as a deployment choice rather than the primary maintained artifact.

title: From Data Quality to Data Trustworthiness in AI-Driven Software-Intensive Embedded Systems: A Systematic Review
authors: Hariharan Gopinath, Jan Bosch, Helena Holmström Olsson
abstract: AI-driven software-intensive embedded systems (SIES) depend on data during development and operation. Poor data quality (DQ) may weaken data trustworthiness, yet evidence about its effects and lifecycle management remains fragmented. This systematic literature review synthesizes 27 primary studies published from January 2020 to February 2026. It examines DQ concerns and evidence linking them to reduced data trustworthiness, along with assessment and management methods. The review identifies 16 concerns organized as Source Quality and Content Quality. Studies provide DQ-based scores and evidence of effects on model or decision performance. Synthesis suggests upstream source or handling problems may become embedded in training baselines and remain difficult to detect at runtime. Eight method categories were identified. Runtime monitoring is the largest category, while upstream and training-time controls remain poorly integrated with runtime assurance. No study covers the full lifecycle. Data trustworthiness supports reliable SIES decisions but is one component of AI-system trustworthiness.
comment: This is a preprint version and the final version will appear in the proceedings of PROFES 2026

title: What Moves the Ceiling on Automated Audit: from General Code to Scientific Code, Results and Data
authors: Zhaohe Dong
abstract: Models increasingly check what other models write. We study one shipped arrangement, in which an auditor from a different vendor reads the work and deterministic checks verify what code can verify, and measure its limits against ground truth no model supplies. On general-purpose code with hidden tests, eight readings of the auditor reach 30.0% recall [20.0, 40.7] at 16.0% [10.1, 22.3] flags on correct code, with diminishing returns and no plateau. The reading model (confounded with its sampling), one rulebook sentence and the decision rule each move that figure, and much of what is missed is, on a post hoc rating, behaviour the specification never determined. In three preregistered science studies, checking that reported numbers trace to their sources flagged all 49 inconsistent reports and none of 25 consistent fabrications, of which the model auditor flagged 23 (21 with a sound finding, post hoc); on data, a documentation-derived validator and the auditor flagged overlapping but different faulty items, together 112 of 140 at a 2.9% [0.7, 5.7] flag rate on clean data; and on scientific code, reframing the task around one step cut flags on correct code from 68.7% to 36.0%. Where both tiers ran, the deterministic one flagged no clean item and could not see consistent error; the model saw some and erred itself. Studies making model calls were preregistered, the two unregistered analyses are named, and every quoted report passed independent cross-vendor review.

title: Who Changed the AI Agent's Rules? Measuring How AI Coding Agents Escalate Authority in CI/CD Pipelines
authors: Miroslaw Staron
abstract:
AI coding agents can modify CI/CD control-plane structures, including workflows and permission settings, thereby extending their authority beyond routine code changes. Because such modifications can affect an entire development pipeline, this study examines the trade-off between execution cost and governance risk in agentic CI/CD. We introduce a joint penalty model, P(M), that combines these two dimensions and evaluate it on all 932,791 agent-authored pull requests in the AIDev dataset, covering five autonomous coding agents. Each pull request is automatically classified by authority scope - data-plane or control-plane - and assigned a penalty score.
  We found that control-plane actions have a 2.3x higher mean joint penalty than data-plane actions (0.498 vs. 0.218) and a 3.9x higher mean governance risk (0.530 vs. 0.135), which means that they indeed increase the risk. All 775 pull requests in the extreme-risk category, defined as P(M) > 0.8, modify the control plane. Policy-violation flags occur in 46.6% of all control-plane pull requests and in 63.6% of merged control-plane pull requests. We have also found an indication that governance risk differs substantially across agent implementations, ranging from 0.166 for Cursor to 0.328 for Copilot in mean joint penalty. These differences are not explained by execution cost or merge rate, suggesting that authority policies should be calibrated for individual agents. Manual assessment of 34 pull requests yielded a Cohen's kappa of 0.72 for the authority-scope classifier.
  The results show that a single compound metric can identify and measure changes to CI/CD governance structures at scale. The proposed framework supports detecting high-risk pull requests and comparing governance behavior across agent implementations, providing a basis for authority tuning and pipeline governance in agentic software development.
comment: Accepted for publication at the Research track of PROFES (Product Oriented Software Process Improvement) 2026 conference, Karlskrona, Sweden

title: Structure-Behavior Coalescence: A Definition of Systems
authors: William S. Chao
abstract: For more than seventy years, systems engineering has developed extensive models and frameworks, yet the fundamental question of what constitutes a system remains insufficiently formalized. Existing approaches often treat structure and behavior as separate aspects, leaving their unity, system identity, and consistency conditions insufficiently defined. This paper introduces Structure-Behavior Coalescence (SBC) as a formal framework that defines a system as an integrated entity in which structure and behavior are coalesced through interaction. SBC provides a formal modeling approach with well-formedness constraints for maintaining structural-behavioral coherence, including representations for terminal, paused, and intermediate states and rules for sequential, parallel, and alternative behaviors. The framework provides a formal perspective on the question, "What is a system?", and establishes a foundation for consistent system modeling, verification, and analysis.

title: Measuring What Matters in the Age of AI: The Research Software Metrics Landscape
authors: Addi Malviya-Thakur, Reed Milewicz, Gregory R. Watson, Audris Mockus
abstract: Research software now serves as a primary instrument of science, but the methods the community uses to judge its quality, sustainability, reuse, and impact remain scattered across software engineering, open science, FAIR software, citation, and research-assessment literature. AI-assisted development sharpens the problem: code can be produced at rates that outpace human review capacity, provenance and attribution are harder to track, scholarly credit systems cannot keep pace, and existing metrics inherit assumptions about how research software gets developed that may no longer apply. To aid in navigating these challenges, we present a focused landscape synthesis of research software metrics based on 49 substantive references, organizing the recurring metrics into eight families described by data source, claimed construct, evidence of validity, automation potential, and susceptibility to misuse. Many widely cited research software metrics serve as partial signals but make weak standalone measures of scientific impact. The AI era opens or widens gaps around provenance, maintainability of generated code, reviewer effort, model and data dependencies, reuse and community-health signal inflation, and credit for human labor that AI does not perform. We argue for responsible, contextual, mixed-method use of research software metrics, and offer decision guidance for Research Software Engineers (RSEs), principal investigators, institutions, and funders selecting metrics that support better software, fairer credit, and more trustworthy science. All findings rest on the 49-reference focused review; a reproducible search-and-triage protocol and a 727-record triaged corpus accompany the paper as a transparency artifact for a future full systematic mapping study.

title: Structure-Behavior Coalescence for Model-Based Systems Engineering
authors: William S. Chao
abstract: Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) has advanced system design and analysis for decades, yet traditional approaches often treat structure and behavior separately, resulting in inconsistencies, incomplete models, and ambiguity. This paper introduces Structure-Behavior Coalescence (SBC) as a formal and unified definition of systems for MBSE. SBC defines a system as a single integrated entity in which structure and behavior are coalesced through interaction, providing both a conceptual foundation and a formal process-algebra framework. Well-formedness constraints ensure that interactions are structurally grounded and compositions are valid, enabling consistency by construction. Boundary processes, including 0 for terminal states and a checkpoint construct for paused or suspended states, allow inactive and intermediate states to be represented while preserving system unity. Illustrative examples and a Smart Healthcare IoT case study demonstrate how SBC supports sequential, parallel, and alternative behaviors while maintaining structural-behavioral coherence. SBC provides a foundation for formal verification, compositional modeling, and systematic inconsistency detection, connecting a rigorous definition of systems with practical MBSE applications.

title: Generative AI in Software Testing: Practitioners' Perspectives on the Benefits, Challenges, Opportunities, and Risks
authors: Chamari Dasanayake, Rahul Mohanani, Vladimir Mandić, Burak Turhan
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) increasingly supports software testing, yet empirical evidence on practitioners' perceptions remains limited. This study investigates perceived benefits, challenges, opportunities, and risks of GenAI in software testing through a questionnaire survey of 64 practitioners. Closed-ended responses were analyzed descriptively, while open-ended responses were qualitatively coded to contextualize the findings. Among the respondents, 34 were users (those with regular or experimental use of GenAI in testing) and 30 were non-users (those without prior use of GenAI in testing). Results show generally positive perceptions of GenAI for reducing effort, test generation, and debugging, alongside concerns about prompt dependence, trust, and incorrect outputs. Users were more positive about several concrete benefits while also more frequently prioritizing reliability-related risks, whereas non-users showed greater uncertainty about some technically specific challenges. Overall, the findings position GenAI as an assistive technology requiring human validation and highlight the importance of considering practitioners' experience with GenAI when interpreting perceptions of GenAI-assisted testing.
comment: Accepted for publication in 27th International Conference on Product-Focused Software Process Improvement (PROFES 2026)

title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
authors: Zhiyuan Peng, Wei Tao, Chenhao Ying, Yuan Luo, Yiwen Guo
abstract: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines do not expose. We introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes a checkpoint, an artifact that restores that state and can be versioned and replayed, from a natural-language functional test case and read-only access to the target's source code. The checkpoint is restored through a per-application hook that an onboarding agent binds or synthesizes once without hand-written hook code. Because a checkpoint can satisfy state checks while rendering incorrectly, checkpoints are scored by hybrid programmatic-state and visual evaluation: acceptance requires both a programmatic-state oracle and a visual oracle to pass. We calibrate the visual oracle against a blinded cross-VLM reference. We release DeepStateBench, 61 deep-state tasks across 10 interactive applications that span five language families and six rendering stacks, with source sizes from 874 to 7.2M lines. Across three registered models, a GUI agent seeded with synthesized checkpoints completes 10.4% of trials, compared with 0% without seeding under the same pixel action space, while StatePortal, which also delivers the target action through the hook, completes 27.5%. Over 1,361 replays of 112 checkpoints, 98.90% reproduce the original verdict with zero model calls, and the hybrid oracle detects 96.25% (77/80) of controlled visual faults invisible to programmatic-state checks alone. We open-source our code at https://github.com/pzy2000/State_Portal and website at https://stateportal.mineyosemite.chatgpt.site

title: Controlled Natural Language for Requirements Specification: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Ikram Darif, Ghizlane El Boussaidi, Segla Kpodjedo, Cristiano Politowski
abstract: Requirements are critical artifacts of the software development life-cycle. They express capabilities that the system should provide, guiding both the development and testing process. Given their significance, require- ments specification has attracted the interest of researchers and practitioners in recent years. Requirements specification is an activity where requirements are specified, i.e., documented. In this context, Controlled Natural Languages (CNL) were proposed as a compromise between the ambiguity of natural language and the complexity of formal languages. CNLs enable the specification of requirements using accurate statements that can be processed automatically, while remaining understandable by stakeholders. In this article, we perform a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to identify, categorize, and compare CNL approaches for requirements specification. The SLR covers 133 primary studies published between 2000 and 2024. We evaluate them accord- ing to seven dimensions: context, scope, targeted requirements types, specification technique, tool support, validation method, and adoption. We provide a categorization framework that summarizes the evaluated dimensions, and we identify directions for future research. Our main results reveal: (1) four types of CNL: standalone templates, requirement patterns, elementary templates, and linguistic rules, (2) limited support for automated tools and domain vocabulary usage, and (3) lack of validation through case studies and limited adoption for the majority of approaches.

title: Software Engineering for LLM-Based Agents: A Lifecycle-Oriented Survey
authors: Yifei Ge, Yalin Feng, Weisong Sun, Junjie Shi, Zhenpeng Chen, Chunrong Fang, Zhihong Zhao, Zhenyu Chen, Yang Liu, Zhi Jin
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based Agents perform tasks through tool use and interaction with external environments. Public engineering guidance commonly begins with a target task, selects a suitable workflow or autonomous Agent design, and refines prompts, tools, and execution strategies using task outcomes, latency, and cost. When delivered as software systems, Agents must also satisfy stakeholder requirements, action boundaries, quality checks, and maintenance needs. Model-directed execution can vary across runs, failures can span model decisions and tools, and changes to prompts, models, or interfaces can affect previously accepted behavior. This survey examines how LLM-based Agents are engineered across five software lifecycle stages: Requirements Engineering, Architecture and Design, Implementation and Integration, Testing and Assurance, and Maintenance and Evolution. Based on a main collection of 355 papers, we compare the engineering problems addressed, explain how methods and practices work, and examine their reported evaluations and limitations within each stage. We synthesize how existing research supports Agent development activities and identify open problems and research directions. The result is a lifecycle-oriented reference for understanding, selecting, and further developing methods for engineering Agent software.

title: EnvAgent: Multi-Agent Approach to Building Science Environments in the Clouds
authors: Yiming Cheng, Chris Low, Binrui Huang, Mengshi Zhang, Zihao Chen, Kate Keahey, Paul Marshall, Kexin Pei
abstract: AI agents are transforming scientific computing and software workflows, but generating and executing code requires a correctly configured execution environment. Automating environment construction remains difficult because repositories encode heterogeneous, often incomplete requirements for operating systems, toolchains, dependencies, and build procedures. Existing workflows thus rely on developer-maintained Dockerfiles and setup scripts, making preparation labor-intensive, hard to scale, and potentially biasing evaluations. We present ENVAGENT, an agentic framework that synthesizes, builds, and verifies repository-level Docker environments. ENVAGENT combines deterministic utilities for Docker execution and state management with coordinated agents for repository analysis, planning, Dockerfile synthesis, and iterative failure diagnosis and repair. We also introduce ENVBENCH, a benchmark of 54 scientific artifacts and open-source repositories spanning seven languages from Chameleon Trovi and Multi-SWE-bench. For each repository, we curate a declarative rubric of required structure, configuration, and functionality, and a shared evaluator applies 2,108 weighted checks across generated environments. Across four matched language-model settings, ENVAGENT constructs 43.5 executable environments out of 54 on average, versus 23.5 for Codex and Claude Code, and scores 62.02 versus 24.19 on a composite of executability and rubric satisfaction. These results show that environment-specific agent orchestration substantially improves automated environment construction.
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. Accepted at AI4S@SC26 (SC26 Workshop)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Finance and the Early-Career Skills Shift: A Structured Evidence Synthesis of Decision Delegation, Bank Deployments, and Business Education
authors: Prakhar Singh Sisodia
abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming a general interaction and decision-support layer across finance. Banks use AI for research retrieval, document synthesis, meeting follow-up, customer service, coding, fraud detection, risk support, and increasingly multi-step workflows. This paper asks which parts of finance work can be delegated safely, which remain human-owned, and how education should change when AI compresses the tasks through which novices traditionally build judgment. It presents a structured evidence synthesis of research and public evidence released from 2023 through October 2026 across finance, labor economics, education, bank deployments, and financial regulation. Numerical results and deployment claims remain attributed to their original sources. Four connections emerge: AI is strongest at retrieval, transformation, coding, and first-pass analysis; financial institutions are moving toward constrained rather than unrestricted autonomy; productivity assistance can weaken apprenticeship when assisted output improves faster than unaided capability; and delegation should depend jointly on consequence, reversibility, verification strength, and operational resilience. The paper develops a Finance Work Stack, Decision Delegation Matrix, AI Apprenticeship Paradox, Apprenticeship Preservation Protocol, and Career Readiness Stack. It argues that useful financial AI must improve productivity without weakening accountability, human capability, cyber resilience, or the future talent pipeline.
comment: 16 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Structured evidence synthesis of AI in finance, decision delegation, early-career work, and business education. No new experimental measurements are claimed; empirical findings and deployment claims are attributed to cited sources

title: Perceived Effectiveness of Social Debt Mitigation Measures: A Preliminary Vignette-Based Survey
authors: Philipp M. Zähl, Tom Siegel, Robin Kha, Chaitanya Chikkala, Zoé Lermusiaux, Anika Hennig
abstract: Software engineering is a socio-technical discipline in which unresolved social and organizational problems accumulate as social debt, gradually eroding collaboration and project health. The literature offers a solid vocabulary for these problems but says little about which countermeasures practitioners consider effective. We address this gap with a vignette-based survey: six social debt problem dimensions (Organizational Silo, Newcomer Isolation, Communication Breakdown, Knowledge Bottleneck, Cultural and Geographical Distance, Psychological Safety Deficit) were presented as realistic team scenarios, and 23 IT professionals and advanced students rated 41 literature-derived mitigation measures. Rankings were analyzed with paired t-tests and a hierarchical Bayesian model that accounts for the within-subject design and yields, for each measure, the probability of being the best option in its scenario. Only for Communication Breakdown is the answer unambiguous: consolidating communication into a single primary channel is almost certainly preferred (P(best)=0.91). For the other five dimensions, the model identifies favorites with moderate evidence (P(best) between 0.38 and 0.58), such as structured knowledge transfer and blameless retrospectives. Across scenarios, structural measures that change how information, decisions, and knowledge are organized were rated higher than role-based or attitudinal measures (by 0.3 to 0.4 scale points), although not in every scenario. Given the small convenience sample, the results are exploratory, but they offer software engineering managers an evidence-graded starting point for selecting mitigation measures.

title: Escaping the Anthropomorphic Trap: Resolving the Cognitive Mismatch in Future AI Software Development
authors: Yi Wang, Zheng Jiang, Gaowei Zhang, Min Zhang, Yang Feng
abstract: For more than a half-century, the foundational paradigms of software development-such as modularity, information hiding, and hierarchical labor division-have been engineered to accommodate the strict cognitive limitations of human working memory. However, the rapid emergence of multi-agent artificial intelligence exposes a fundamental cognitive mismatch. Current frameworks attempt to integrate high-dimensional, stateless neural reasoning engines by coercing them to operate within these legacy, human-centric structures, falling into an anthropomorphic trap. This friction generates a novel, highly volatile behavioral entropy defined as AI-software technical debt, wherein amnesic agents hallucinate opaque workarounds to bypass architectural blindfolds. To resolve this, we propose Invisible Software Engineering (Invisible SE), a paradigm shift from agent-centric human emulation to environment-centric stigmergic governance. By reimagining the repository as an active computational topology which utilizes topological gradients, temporally weighted memory, and representation-space regularization, Invisible SE safely guides AI behavior without classical code-level constraints, thus transcending the cognitive horizons of human developers. This environment-centric protocol offers a potential blueprint for orchestrating scalable, long-lived computational infrastructures that transcend the cognitive horizons of human developers and enable autonomous agents to work, coordinate, and scale to build future software systems.

title: f2x50: A Repository-Scale Benchmark for Fortran-to-X Software Migration
authors: Shraddha Surana, Ashwin Srinivasan
abstract: Repository-level migration requires more than translating isolated functions: it must preserve behaviour across modules, shared state, build structure, and dependencies. Existing translation benchmarks predominantly cover small programs or small repositories, or fixed and widely studied language pairs. We present f2x50, a target-independent benchmark comprising 50 public Fortran repositories pinned to exact Git revisions. It contains 12,116 Git-tracked Fortran files and 6,569,806 lines, divided into three structural-complexity tiers and paired with 561 deterministic behavioural probes. Of these probes, 446 compile pinned source files with small drivers and span 131 repository--routine pairs. Every repository has at least five direct checks that collectively execute at least two routines. f2x50 provides target-independent tools for acquisition, validation, licence review, and reproducibility, together with a reference adapter for evaluating Python targets. The remaining probes are explicitly classified as extractions, inline reimplementations, or synthetic fixtures. The benchmark therefore supports comparable evaluations across migration tools and target languages.
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
zh_title: f2x50：用于Fortran到X软件迁移的代码库级基准测试
translation: 代码库级别的迁移不仅仅是翻译孤立的函数：它必须在模块、共享状态、构建结构和依赖关系之间保持行为一致。现有的翻译基准主要涵盖小型程序或小型代码库，或者固定且经过广泛研究的语言对。我们提出了 f2x50，这是一个与目标无关的基准，包含 50 个固定在精确 Git 修订版的公共 Fortran 代码库。它包含 12,116 个 Git 跟踪的 Fortran 文件和 6,569,806 行代码，分为三个结构复杂度层级，并配有 561 个确定性行为探测器。在这些探测器中，有 446 个使用小型驱动程序编译固定的源文件，并跨越 131 个代码库-例程对。每个代码库至少有五个直接检查，共同执行至少两个例程。f2x50 提供了用于获取、验证、许可证审查和可复现性的与目标无关的工具，以及用于评估 Python 目标的参考适配器。其余的探测器被明确分类为提取、内联重新实现或合成夹具。因此，该基准支持跨迁移工具和目标语言的可比评估。
tldr: 本文推出了f2x50——一个用于Fortran代码库迁移的大规模、多目标基准测试集，包含50个真实代码库和561个行为探测器。
ai_comments: 该论文针对Fortran到其他语言的代码库级迁移任务，提出了一个大规模、多语言目标的基准测试集f2x50。其创新之处在于突破了以往基准测试局限于小规模程序或固定语言对的限制，包含了50个真实的Fortran代码库及丰富的行为探测器，为评估复杂的跨语言软件迁移工具提供了可靠的标准。
motivation: 现有的翻译基准测试大多只涵盖小型程序、小代码库或固定且研究较多的语言对，而代码库级迁移需要保持跨模块、共享状态、构建结构和依赖关系的行为一致性，缺乏一个大规模且支持多种目标语言的基准。
method: 构建了一个包含50个公共Fortran代码库（锁定在特定Git版本）的目标无关基准测试f2x50，按结构复杂度划分为三个层级，并配备了561个确定性行为探测器及获取、验证、许可证审查和可复现性的相关工具。
results: 成功创建了包含12,116个Git跟踪的Fortran文件和6,56,9806行代码的f2x50基准测试，其中包含561个确定性行为探测器（涵盖编译源文件、提取、内联重实现或合成夹具），并提供了用于评估Python目标的参考适配器。
conclusion: f2x50作为一个大规模、结构化且包含丰富行为验证的基准测试，填补了当前代码库级软件迁移评估的空白，有助于推动自动化多语言迁移技术的发展。

title: Skill Roulette: Measuring Skill Invocation Rate Across LLM Coding Agents
authors: Jin Rae Lee, Jai Lal Lulla, Sebastian Baltes, Christoph Treude
abstract: Agent skills package procedures for large language model (LLM) coding agents. An agent selects a skill from its name and description before reading the procedure. It may complete the task without invoking a relevant skill. We investigate how reliably coding agents invoke relevant skills and which factors affect that decision. We estimate invocation rates by repeating trials with identical inputs; invocation rate is the proportion of trials in which the agent invokes the relevant skill. We test 9 non-directional hypotheses about skill metadata, competing skills, contextual instructions, and task wording and composition. Eight concern invocation; the ninth tests whether making a skill available changes the occurrence of an action that the task does not request. We use tasks from 4 software engineering categories in a synthetic repository, running each of 4 coding-agent harnesses with 2 models. The planned 20,400 trials include 60 repetitions per Baseline category and configuration, 60 more per category in Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 that admit each category's task and skill, and 10 per experimental condition. Comparisons are specified before collection and evaluated within each model and harness configuration using Boschloo's exact test.
comment: Registered report, submitted to ACM TOSEM

title: An Industry Perspective on Software Vulnerability Management: A Systematic Review of Approaches, Tools, Practices, and Challenges
authors: M. Mehdi Kholoosi, Triet Huynh Minh Le, M. Ali Babar
abstract: Software vulnerability management (SVM) refers to coordinated activities to detect, assess, repair, and disclose software vulnerabilities (SVs) across a product or ecosystem. As software systems grow in scale and dependency depth, organisations must balance timely security action with limited expertise, evolving tooling, and delivery pressure. In this practitioner-centred systematic literature review, we synthesise 57 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2010 and 2025 that collect primary data directly from industry practitioners. We examine the SVM solutions (approaches, tools, and practices) proposed and evaluated with practitioners and the challenges practitioners report when adopting and using these solutions in real-world settings. We find that practice-oriented contributions, such as guidelines, recommendations, lessons learned, and shared experiences, constitute most of the evidence base, while fewer studies evaluate concrete approaches and tools in industrial environments. The solution landscape and evaluation focus are weighted toward SV detection and repair, with comparatively limited practitioner-centred coverage of SV assessment and disclosure. The most persistent challenges concern how SVM work is organised and embedded: limited security expertise and time, unclear responsibility for SV-related decisions, scattered or poorly coordinated processes, and tools that are difficult to understand, configure, or integrate into existing workflows. These findings highlight the need for more integrated socio-technical interventions, stronger coverage of under-studied SVM tasks, and evaluations that prioritise sustained workflow impact alongside technical performance.
comment: Preprint version. Submitted to ACM; under review. Online appendix included as supplementary material
zh_title: 软件漏洞管理的行业视角：方法、工具、实践与挑战的系统性综述
translation: 软件漏洞管理（SVM）是指跨产品或生态系统协调开展检测、评估、修复和披露软件漏洞（SV）的活动。随着软件系统规模和依赖深度的增长，组织必须在及时的安全行动与有限的专业知识、不断演进的工具以及交付压力之间取得平衡。在这篇以从业者为中心的系统性文献综述中，我们综合了2010年至2025年间发表的57篇直接从行业从业者那里收集一手数据的同行评审实证研究。我们考察了与从业者一起提出和评估的SVM解决方案（方法、工具和实践），以及从业者在真实世界设置中采用和使用这些解决方案时报告的挑战。我们发现，以实践为导向的贡献（如指南、建议、经验教训和共享经验）构成了证据基础的大多数，而评估工业环境中具体方法和工具的研究较少。解决方案的格局和评估重点倾向于SV的检测和修复，而对SV评估和披露的以从业者为中心的覆盖相对有限。最持久的挑战涉及SVM工作的组织和嵌入方式：有限的安全专业知识和时间、对SV相关决策的责任不清、分散或协调不周的流程，以及难以理解、配置或集成到现有工作流中的工具。这些findings突出了对更多整合的社会-技术干预的需求，对未充分研究的SVM任务的更强覆盖，以及优先考虑持续工作流影响和技术性能的评估。
tldr: 通过系统综述57项工业界实证研究，揭示了软件漏洞管理（SVM）在工业界的应用现状、工具局限性以及面临的主要组织与技术挑战。
ai_comments: 该论文通过系统性文献综述（SLR），从工业界从业者的视角审视了软件漏洞管理（SVM）的现状、方法、工具及挑战，具有很高的实用价值和现实指导意义。
motivation: As software systems grow in scale and dependency depth, organisations face challenges in balancing timely security action with limited expertise, evolving tooling, and delivery pressure, necessitating a practitioner-centred understanding of software vulnerability management.
method: A systematic literature review (SLR) synthesizing 57 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2010 and 2025 that collect primary data directly from industry practitioners.
results: Most evidence consists of practice-oriented contributions (guidelines, lessons learned) rather than evaluated concrete tools. Solutions focus heavily on SV detection and repair, neglecting assessment and disclosure. Key challenges include limited security expertise/time, unclear responsibilities, uncoordinated processes, and tools that are hard to integrate.
conclusion: 研究表明，当前SVM的解决方案多偏向实践层面的经验分享且集中于检测和修复环节，而组织和流程上的挑战（如缺乏专业知识、责任不清等）是阻碍SVM有效落地的主要瓶颈。未来需要更多关注社会-技术协同干预以及全流程的漏洞管理。

title: AI Code Review Requires Revision-Aware Evidence of Concern Resolution
authors: Mamdouh Alenezi
abstract: AI-assisted code review increasingly judges whether reported concerns have been resolved. Yet closing a thread or modifying a commented line does not establish repair, and later revisions can invalidate earlier fixes. This position paper argues that resolution requires inspectable, revision-specific evidence that is revalidated when its dependencies change. We model review concerns as persistent verification obligations, derive a sufficient condition under which dependency-gated revalidation matches exhaustive reassessment, and introduce REVAL, a lightweight procedure adapting principles from regression-test selection and build systems. We evaluate REVAL against oracle ground truth in synthetic revision histories covering 441 concerns, 1,284 assessments, and 12 defect families. A sticky outdated-line proxy falsely marked 72.9% of unresolved states as resolved, while stopping checks after initial success missed every recurrence. With three oracle-sampled witnesses, REVAL achieved a false-resolution rate of 0.11 (95% CI: 0.06-0.16) and detected 80.4% of recurrences. With witnesses derived solely from review comments and assessed using independent held-out checks, the corresponding results were 0.13 and 88.3%. Across 6,420 paired comparisons, REVAL matched exhaustive reassessment while reducing post-comment test executions by 34%. Maintenance overhead increased runtime for microsecond-scale tests; the estimated break-even test cost was 0.42 ms. These findings support revision-aware evidence maintenance in a controlled setting, while distinguishing revalidation correctness from witness adequacy. A prespecified evaluation protocol outlines how to assess generalisability in real review histories.

title: Skip-Level Meetings: Benefits, Risks, and Design Considerations Informed by Bypassed Managers' Experiences
authors: Samuel Blacher
abstract: Skip-level meetings (SLMs), bidirectional, relationship-oriented meetings between employees and managers two or more levels above, are common but not universal, and often recommended in professional outlets. They entail benefits and risks for employees, direct and skip-level managers, and organizations, with multiple factors related to shaping the value-risk balance and appropriate approach. However, SLMs have received limited scholarly attention, particularly regarding bypassed managers' views of that managerial practice. This exploratory qualitative study examined the experiences and perspectives of 25 first-tier software engineering managers from diverse personal and organizational contexts in the multicultural, dynamic, innovation-driven, and high-turnover U.S. tech sector as bypassed managers in SLMs between their direct reports and these reports' second-tier managers.
