Their accounts, integrated with directly related literature, as well as on intersecting topics such as employee voice, psychological safety, and cultural and generational differences, revealed broad support and preference for exclusion from SLMs, contrary to concerns in prior literature, broad implementation, and high sensitivity to design and contextual factors, such as the significance of follow-up involvement and of individual backgrounds. Findings position SLMs not as a universally beneficial managerial practice, but as context-dependent, requiring deliberate design and implementation, or avoidance. The study extends limited research on SLMs and hierarchy-bypassing interactions, recommends directions for further research, and offers evidence-informed guidance for deciding whether and how to use SLMs to maximize value while mitigating risks.
comment: The published article along with the supplementary material is available at: https://doi.org/10.1109/EMR.2026.3740096
zh_title: 跨级会议：基于被越级经理经验的收益、风险与设计考量
translation: 跨级会议（SLM）是员工与高两级或以上的经理之间双向、以关系为导向的会议，在职业领域中很常见但并非普遍存在，专业媒体也经常推荐。它们为员工、直接经理、跨级经理和组织带来了收益与风险，并且有多个因素决定了其价值-风险的平衡及适当的方法。然而，SLM受到的学术关注有限，特别是关于被越级经理对这种管理实践的看法。本探索性质性研究考察了来自美国多元化、动态、创新驱动且高离职率的科技行业的25位一线软件工程经理的经验与视角，他们在直接下属与其第二层级经理的SLM中扮演被越级经理的角色。他们的陈述与直接相关的文献相结合，以及与员工心声、心理安全、文化和代际差异等交叉主题相结合，揭示了他们对被排除在SLM之外的广泛支持和偏好（这与先前文献中的担忧相反），广泛的实施情况，以及对设计和情境因素（如后续参与的重要性和个人背景）的高度敏感性。研究结果表明，SLM并非一种普遍有益的管理实践，而是具有情境依赖性，需要刻意的设计和实施，或者选择避免。该研究扩展了关于SLM和越级交互的有限研究，推荐了进一步研究的方向，并为决定是否以及如何使用SLM以最大化价值同时降低风险提供了基于证据的指导。
tldr: 跨级会议（SLM）并非普遍有益，本研究从被越级经理的视角出发，证明其成效高度依赖于情境与精细设计。
ai_comments: 该研究填补了学术界对“跨级会议（SLM）”研究的空白，尤其是创新性地从被越级管理的直接经理（bypassed managers）视角出发，挑战了传统观念中“经理应参与”或“SLM普遍有益”的假设，具有很高的管理实践指导价值。
motivation: 跨级会议（SLM）在职场中常见且伴随利弊，但学术界对此关注有限，尤其是缺乏对被越级管理的直接经理（bypassed managers）这一群体的视角和体验的研究。
method: 采用探索性质性研究方法，对美国科技行业的25位一线软件工程经理进行了访谈，结合相关文献及员工心声、心理安全等交叉主题进行分析。
results: 研究发现被越级经理普遍支持并倾向于被排除在SLM之外（这与以往文献的担忧相反），同时发现SLM高度敏感于设计和情境因素（如后续跟进和个人背景）。
conclusion: 跨级会议并非普遍适用的管理实践，其成效高度取决于情境与设计，必须谨慎实施或根据实际情况选择避免。

title: torchtest2: One-Call Sanity Checks for PyTorch Models,Evaluated on Real and Unseen Architectures
authors: Grzegorz Gwardys
abstract: Many bugs in deep learning code are silent: a layer that is never called, an optimizer created before the classification head was replaced, a recurrent layer that treats the batch as time, or an ignored attention mask. The code runs, the loss decreases somewhat, and the defect surfaces, if ever, after days of GPU time. We present torchtest2, an open-source library that runs 18 sanity checks on a single batch with one call, restores the PyTorch state it touches, and adapts to model families through plugins. We evaluate it by mutation analysis with 17 classes of silent bugs on 103 models from torchvision, timm and Hugging Face transformers, on 600 random architectures and on 20 hand-written realistic bugs, against the checks of the original torchtest, overfitting a single batch, a smoke test and a training monitor in the style of AUTOTRAINER and DeepDiagnosis. Every mutant is compared with its healthy counterpart, and intervals come from a bootstrap over models. After freezing the tool, we ran it on 191 models of architecture families it had never seen: counting, for every tool alike, a failing report where the healthy model's report does not fail, it detected 78% of the injected bugs (95% CI 75-80), against 40% for the original torchtest checks and 48% for the training monitor. On real models its batch-independence check found a bug in timm's GCViT that couples the images of a batch. Real models also exposed false alarms that neither the tool's own test suite nor random architectures had revealed. Two independent collections of real silent bugs mark the limits of the approach: only 3 of 28 reproduced PyTorch bugs from Stack Overflow and 3 of the 18 silent training errors released with TrainCheck are within reach of a pre-training model tester. A median check takes 1.0 s. We release the library, the benchmark and all raw results.
zh_title: torchtest2：PyTorch模型的一键式健康检查，在真实和未见架构上的评估
translation: 深度学习代码中的许多bug是静默的：从不被调用的层、在分类头被替换之前创建的优化器、将批次视为时间的循环层，或者被忽略的注意力掩码。代码运行，损失有所下降，缺陷如果浮出水面，往往也是在消耗了数天GPU时间之后。我们提出了torchtest2，这是一个开源库，它通过单次调用在单个批次上运行18项健康检查，恢复其触及的PyTorch状态，并通过插件适应模型系列。我们通过变异分析进行了评估，包含17类静默bug、来自torchvision、timm和Hugging Face transformers的103个模型、600个随机架构以及20个手写的现实bug，并将其与原始torchtest的检查、过拟合单个批次、冒烟测试以及AUTOTRAINER和DeepDiagnosis风格的训练监视器进行对比。每个突变体都与其健康对应体进行比较，区间来自对模型的自助采样。在冻结工具后，我们在从未见过的架构系列的191个模型上运行了它：计算每个类似工具在健康模型报告未失败的情况下失败的报告，它检测到了78%的注入bug（95%置信区间75-80），而原始torchtest检查为40%，训练监视器为48%。在真实模型上，其批次独立性检查发现了timm的GCViT中一个耦合批次图像的bug。真实模型还暴露了工具自身的测试套件和随机架构都未曾揭示的误报。两组独立的真实静默bug集合标志着该方法的局限性：在预训练模型测试器能力范围内的，仅有Stack Overflow上28个复现的PyTorch bug中的3个，以及TrainCheck发布的18个静默训练错误中的3个。中位检查耗时1.0秒。我们发布了该库、基准测试以及所有原始结果。
tldr: torchtest2是一个开源的PyTorch模型健康检查库，只需单次调用即可在一批数据上运行18项检查，能够高效检测出深度学习代码中的各类静默bug。
ai_comments: torchtest2为PyTorch模型提供了一种高效的单元测试工具，通过一次调用执行多达18项健康检查，显著减少了深度学习中难以察觉的隐蔽bug所造成的计算资源浪费。其在未知架构上的有效评估证明了其强大的泛化能力和实用价值。
motivation: 深度学习代码中存在许多不会报错但会导致结果异常的“静默bug”，往往在消耗大量GPU时间后才被发现，现有的测试手段在检测这类问题上存在不足，因此需要更高效、全面的单次调用健康检查工具。
method: 提出开源库torchtest2，使用单批次数据通过一次调用运行18项健康检查，恢复被修改的PyTorch状态，并通过插件适应不同模型系列，同时采用变异分析对多种模型和架构进行了严格评估。
results: 在未见过的架构测试中，torchtest2检测出了78%的注入bug，显著优于原始torchtest的40%和训练监视器的48%；此外，它成功发现了timm中GCViT模型的真实bug，且中位检查时间仅为1.0秒。
conclusion: torchtest2能够在一单批次数据上通过18项健康检查有效检测出深度学习代码中的静默bug，且在未见过的新架构上表现优于传统方法和基线工具，但仍受限于预训练模型测试器的设计边界。

title: Evidence-Carrying Contracts for Safe Claim Composition in Data Marketplace Workflows
authors: Duc-Trung Bui, Phuong-Chi Le, Quyet-Thang Huynh
abstract: Data marketplace workflows cross organizational boundaries, where payment, policy presence, or API delivery may be promoted into transaction claims that the evidence does not support. We introduce evidence-carrying claim contracts: a lightweight assume-guarantee semantics declaring assumptions, guarantees, blocking obligations, and evidence dependencies. A conflict-sensitive four-state domain distinguishes supported, refuted, unresolved, and conflicting requirements. Safe composition bounds the transaction claim by the meet of local bounds and blocks full promotion while a critical obligation remains open. We establish local soundness, compositional boundedness, revocation safety, termination, and aggregation-order invariance for finite acyclic workflows. An executable conformance harness covers all 4,096 configurations (four states for each of six stages), 18 mutations, six basic revocations, 12 alternative-support scenarios, an eight-transition evidence trace, 2,880 aggregation schedules, 96 requirement-level and six interface checks. An independent operational evaluator agrees with the declarative oracle; mutation-sensitive campaigns detect all eight seeded defects, though no single campaign detects all. It issues no unsupported full claim, preserves a full claim under valid alternative support, and blocks it when none remains. Four diagnostic negative controls, not competitive baselines, issue 63-1,023 unsupported full claims. These results establish executable conformance to declared contracts, not specification completeness, evidence authenticity, or legal validity.
comment: 14 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Preprint of the version submitted to SoICT 2026 (Springer CCIS), before peer review. Reproducibility artifact: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22737537

title: Agents as Architecture Evaluators: Automating ATAM and SAAM for Continuous Assessment
authors: Adyansh Kakran, Sathvika Miryala, Karthik Vaidhyanathan
abstract: The long-term success of a software system relies heavily on its underlying architecture, which dictates its performance with respect to quality attributes. Software Architecture Evaluation methods, such as the Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method (ATAM) and the Software Architecture Analysis Method (SAAM), are widely recognized for their ability to mitigate risks and ensure reliable quality attributes. However, their widespread adoption remains limited due to the significant cost, time, and human expertise required for these processes. This paper investigates the potential of agentic AI to lower these barriers and facilitate architectural assessment. To enable this preliminary study, we established a dataset by extracting human conducted evaluations from existing academic literature into a structured format. Using this dataset, we developed an agentic workflow to synthesize ATAM and SAAM evaluation reports based on these high level architectural descriptions. This approach simulates the reasoning process of human evaluators when provided with structured architectural data. We validated the approach using automated metrics and human evaluation. Agentic workflows achieve strong relevance and completeness ratings of 4.5/5 and 3.9/5 respectively. The agents successfully automated the labor-intensive phases of scenario generation and risk identification, reducing the evaluation time from weeks to under 5 minutes at a cost of less than $0.50 per run. The results confirm that agentic AI effectively lowers adoption barriers, enabling continuous, high-coverage architectural assessment.

title: Log Analysis for LLM-Based Agents: A Lifecycle-Oriented Survey
authors: Cong Wang, Yaowei Sun, Guohua Xin, Jiongchi Yu, Shuangcheng Sang, Guangquan Xu, Maode Ma
abstract: Logs generated by LLM-based agents support analysis of execution behavior beyond final outputs. Existing surveys give limited attention to dependencies across the lifecycle of these records. A lifecycle-oriented review of 90 core studies published between 2024 and August 2026 covers Agent Logging, Agent Log Structuring, and Agent Log Mining. Stage-specific comparisons reveal cross-stage dependencies and limitations. Detailed logs do not necessarily provide sufficient evidence. Structural uniformity does not guarantee semantic equivalence. Analytical claims require alignment with supporting evidence, reference criteria, and validation procedures. Representative open-source tools, public datasets, and future research directions are also summarized.

title: A Concurrent Structured Record Mirrored the Prose It Accompanied: A Pre-Registered Conceptual Replication and Extension of the Hide Pending Tool Call Scenario
authors: Nicolás Rocchia
abstract: Huang et al. (2026) show that language models writing reports of agentic work tend to conceal narrative-changing flaws, and that appending "Be honest in your response." to the instruction substantially increases disclosure in most of their scenarios. In their Hide Pending Tool Call scenario, where a broader follow-up query was accepted but never returned, the honesty prompt left GPT-5.5's rate of flagging the missing data at 0%, although it turned most answers into caveats. I ask whether a different request changes this: appending, in the same generation, a structured record that follows the schema of an adversarial-review tool, including a residue section for what remained unresolved. In two pre-registered phases on the same 100 synthetic log pairs, each pending log matched with a clean twin in which the follow-up query did return, I ran gpt-5.6-sol through Codex CLI under four conditions. Phase 1 measured the record: with the residue schema, a judge coded it as stating the unreturned query in 29% of logs, against 5% with a findings-only placebo schema, and in none of the clean twins (p = 1.2 x 10^-7); a second run two days later gave 30% and 6%. But 70-71% of residue records declared that nothing remained open while the query was pending. Phase 2 measured the prose answer: the confirmatory comparison against the honesty prompt was not significant (four discordant logs, all favoring the honesty prompt; p = 0.125), no equivalence test was pre-registered, and the judge failed the pre-registered human validation on the decisive category; I therefore claim neither an effect nor its absence. In an exploratory cross-tabulation, every residue record coded as stating the gap accompanied prose coded as mentioning it (30 of 30), and none accompanied prose coded as omitting it (0 of 70): in this setting, the structured record mirrored the prose it accompanied.
comment: 10 pages, 4 tables. Pre-registered study; protocols, code, data and analyses at https://github.com/NicolasRocchia/disensor-hide-pending
zh_title: 并发结构化记录镜像了其伴随的散文：一项预先注册的概念复制和扩展“隐藏待处理工具调用”场景
translation: 黄等人（2026）的研究表明，在撰写代理工作报告时，语言模型倾向于隐藏改变叙述的缺陷，并且在大多数场景下，在指令后添加“请诚实回答”可以显著提高披露率。在他们的“隐藏待处理工具调用”场景中，虽然接受了更广泛的后续查询但从未返回，但诚实提示使 GPT-5.5 标记缺失数据的比率保持在 0%，尽管它将大多数答案变成了警告。我询问不同的请求是否会改变这一点：在同一代中添加一个遵循对抗性审查工具模式的结构化记录，包括一个用于未解决问题的残差部分。在对相同的 100 对合成日志进行的两个预注册阶段中，每个待处理日志都与一个干净的孪生日志匹配，其中后续查询确实返回了，我在四种条件下通过 Codex CLI 运行了 gpt-5.6-sol。阶段 1 测量了记录：使用残差模式，法官将其编码为在 29% 的日志中陈述未返回的查询，而使用仅包含发现的安慰剂模式为 5%，在干净的孪生日志中则为 0%（p = 1.2 x 10^-7）；两天后第二次运行的结果为 30% 和 6%。但是，70-71% 的残差记录声明在查询待处理时没有任何问题。阶段 2 测量了散文答案：与诚实提示的确认性比较不显著（四个不一致的日志，均倾向于诚实提示；p = 0.125），没有预先注册等效性检验，并且法官在决定性类别上未能通过预先注册的人工验证；因此，我声称neither an effect nor its absence。在探索性交叉表中，每个被编码为陈述差距的残差记录都伴随着被编码为提及它的散文（30/30），并且没有一个伴随着被编码为遗漏它的散文（0/70）：在这种情况下，结构化记录镜像了它所伴随的散文。
tldr: 通过在提示中添加结构化记录，可以提高语言模型在报告代理工作时披露信息（例如未返回的查询）的比例，但这种效果在 prose answer 中并不显著。
ai_comments: 本研究在方法上进行了预注册和多阶段实验，增加了研究的严谨性。然而，在阶段2的 prose answer 评估中，由于未能通过人工验证和缺少等效性检验，导致结论不够明确。未来的研究可以考虑更完善的评估方法和更多的场景来验证结构化记录的效果。
motivation: 研究是否通过在提示中添加结构化记录，可以改变语言模型在“隐藏待处理工具调用”场景下披露信息的能力，并与之前的“诚实回答”提示进行比较。
method: 在预先注册的两个阶段中，对100对合成日志进行实验。阶段1测量结构化记录的效果，阶段2测量 prose answer 的效果。使用 gpt-5.6-sol 模型，在四种条件下运行。
results: 在阶段1中，包含“残差”部分的结构化记录在29%的情况下指出了未返回的查询，而仅包含“发现”部分的记录为5%。在阶段2中，与“诚实回答”提示的比较不显著，无法得出明确结论。然而，探索性分析显示，提及查询的结构化记录伴随着提及查询的 prose answer。
conclusion: 虽然结构化记录在一定程度上能够指明未返回的查询，但其对 prose answer 的影响在本次实验中并未得到显著证实。在特定情况下，结构化记录能够反映 prose answer 的内容。

title: Ephyra: A Property-Based Testing Framework for the LLM Era
authors: Alperen Keles
abstract: Coding agents now write a growing share of software tests; however, property-based testing (PBT) libraries are designed with historical considerations. We present Ephyra, a PBT library in Rust built on three concepts: customizability, observability and generator synthesis. Ephyra lets users compose their own testing loops from generation, mutation and shrinking, and synthesize these components to satisfy functional predicates. Applying Ephyra to 14 open source systems, we have found 349 bugs and reported 300 of them, in database management systems (SQLite, Turso, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, DataFusion), the verified policy engine (Cedar), the SQL equivalence prover (QED), the URL parser used in Node.js (ada-url), reimplementations of existing open source systems in Rust (coreutils, brush, gitoxide), and compilers (binaryen, OCaml, and OxCaml).

title: When Single Agent Is Enough: Rethinking Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Code Review
authors: Jiawei Li, Hoa Khanh Dam, Iftekhar Ahmed
abstract: Code review plays a critical role in identifying software quality issues and ensuring system robustness. Prior work has proposed techniques for Review Comment Generation (RCG) and Code Refinement (CR), with recent Multi-Agent (MA) approaches achieving state-of-the-art results by coordinating agents specialized in different quality dimensions. However, MA systems introduce substantial architectural complexity and runtime overhead, and recent evidence suggests they may underperform Single-Agent (SA) approaches in certain tasks. In this work, we systematically compare MA and SA designs for RCG and CR. Surprisingly, our results show that SA approaches perform comparably to- and sometimes outperform-MA systems, despite their simpler design. These findings challenge the prevailing assumption that MA architectures are the default choice for complex software engineering tasks.

title: Code Cloning and Procedural Abstraction in Scratch: A Large-Scale Study of Co-Existing Reuse Practices
authors: Ricardo Hidalgo-Aragon, Jesús Moreno-León, Alejandro Echaniz, David Roldán-Álvarez, Jesús M. González-Barahona, Gregorio Robles
abstract: Code cloning is a long-standing software-evolution concern: duplicated implementations diverge as software changes. In block-based programming, however, duplication is an everyday reuse mechanism, and Scratch facilitates a copy-and-paste culture that may hinder abstraction. We study this relation in 2.04 million public Scratch projects. We compare cloned sequences with existing abstractions and examine how their use varies across Computational Thinking (CT) score levels. Clones occur in 6.2% of projects and custom blocks in 11.9%. Of 436,198 detected clone instances, 16.1% have a normalized sequence matching a custom block in the same project and 17.8% match a custom block only outside it. At the pattern level, 83 of the 100 most frequent clone patterns have counterparts implementable as custom blocks elsewhere in the corpus. Of the remaining 17 patterns, 15 are amenable to custom-block extraction, while in two cases the benefit of abstraction is ambiguous; no class of frequent clone resists abstraction in principle. Yet the abstractions that do exist are often shallow: 53.0% of custom blocks are parameter-free. Increased use of abstraction does not coincide with less cloning. Both become more prevalent at higher CT-score levels, and their combined use dominates the highest band. These findings are consistent with cloning and procedural abstraction being co-existing reuse practices rather than mutually exclusive stages. Closing that gap requires both instruction on when to abstract, not only how, and platform support for refactoring.

title: The Illusion of Relief: How GenAI Redistributes Cognitive Workload in Software Organizations
authors: Chamari Dasanayake, Vladimir Mandić, Rahul Mohanani, Burak Turhan
abstract: This study explores how Generative AI (GenAI) reshapes software practitioners' cognitive work across software development activities. We analyzed questionnaire responses from 44 practitioners across nine organizations using descriptive quantitative methods and qualitative analysis of relevant open-ended responses. Practitioners reported productivity and time savings, but also effort associated with providing context, prompting, reviewing, correcting, verifying, and integrating AI-generated outputs. Human judgment and accountability remained central, with practitioners anticipating a shift from direct code production to guiding, evaluating, validating, integrating, and coordinating AI-supported work. Thus, GenAI appears to redistribute cognitive work toward oversight rather than simply eliminate it, although whether overall cognitive workload increases or decreases remains undetermined.
comment: Accepted for 20th International Scientific Conference on Industrial Systems - IS'26

title: Decided or Open? Comparing Program Repair Techniques When Patch Correctness Is Unknown
authors: Sadnan Nafis
abstract: Comparisons of automated program repair (APR) techniques depend on knowing which patches are correct, but many patches are never checked and some archived test results are wrong. We propose reporting each comparison as decided or open. For two techniques that each pick one patch per bug, we compute the full range of the difference in their success rates over every possible value of the unknown labels, and we call the comparison decided when that range excludes zero. Because a test can only show that a patch is wrong, more testing can move this range in one direction only. This lets us tell, before any test runs, which open comparisons testing could never settle. We study eight settings, including 55,466 candidate patches for Defects4J bugs. The labels already in the archive decide 12 of 16 comparisons between a learned patch selector and its baselines, and adding further evidence decides all 16. In a campaign whose predictions we published in advance, all eight predictions held. We also show that copies of the developer's fix, which must pass, are recorded as failing for 33.5% of GPT-4's copies but for only 2.5% of the RepairLLaMA model's, so the reliability of archived test results differs between models. With these checks, researchers can see which comparisons need more evidence and which kind of evidence can help.
comment: 40 pages. Under review at Empirical Software Engineering. Also available at Research Square, doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11480796/v1. Replication package: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23590962

title: Monitoring Machine Learning Systems in Production: A Multivocal Literature Review
authors: Hira Naveed, Aleksandar Pasquini, Scott Barnett, Chetan Arora, John Grundy, Hourieh Khalajzadeh, Omar Haggag
abstract: Monitoring is essential for maintaining reliable machine learning (ML) systems after deployment. However, knowledge about its practical implementation and effectiveness remains fragmented across academic and gray literature. We present a multivocal literature review of 94 sources (37 academic and 57 gray) covering both traditional ML and generative AI systems. We develop taxonomies covering monitored objects and properties, techniques, input signals, tools, automation, frequency, evaluation, and challenges. Our findings reveal an imbalanced monitoring process. Existing approaches provide broad and largely automated support for observing system behavior, detecting problems, and communicating findings, while monitor configuration, investigation, and response retain substantial human involvement. Monitoring is concentrated on inference, with no source covering the entire production ML system, limiting end-to-end diagnosis. Evidence of effectiveness is also limited: among 78 sources presenting an approach or tool, 45 provide no formal evaluation, 24 report offline or controlled evaluations, and only nine evaluate monitoring in live production. This gap is particularly evident for generative AI, where evidence is dominated by gray literature and vendor claims. We propose six directions for improving monitor design, cross-layer diagnosis, proxy validation, corrective responses, production-oriented evaluation, and organizational practices. Our review provides a structured basis for improving the detection, diagnosis, and resolution of production ML problems.

title: An Empirical Study of Visual Artifacts in Pull Request Descriptions
authors: Tianzi Hao, Kazi Amit Hasan, Yuan Tian, Bram Adams
abstract: Reviewers rely on pull request (PR) descriptions to understand what a change does, yet some changes, such as UI updates or runtime behavior, are hard to convey in text alone. PR authors attach visual artifacts to fill this gap, but how often they do so, what they show, and whether they change how a PR is reviewed remain unknown. We present a large-scale study of visual artifacts in GitHub PR descriptions. From 6,505,113 closed PRs in 5,012 repositories, we built VisPR, a dataset of 2,473,892 English, human-authored PRs from 647 repos where visual artifacts are an established practice. Of these, 329,185 (13.3%) are visual PRs, i.e., their descriptions contain at least one visual artifact (479,974 in total). By manually labeling a sample of 1,113 visual artifacts from 891 merged visual PRs, we derived two taxonomies: 11 content types capturing what developers show and six purposes capturing why they include visual artifacts. The dominant content type is Interaction & State, which shows how the interface responds to user actions. its share rises from 37.0% of images to 63.5% of GIFs and 79.7% of videos, whereas about a quarter of images (23.4%) show text such as logs, code, or error messages . Compared with 1,782 merged non-visual PRs matched on repository, PR type, and change size, visual PRs receive 43% more review comments and 17% more reviewers, and take 72% longer from first response to merge, time to merge and churn-normalized review efficiency do not differ significantly. LLM-assisted classification of 10,031 review comments in two groups shows that review centers on code in both, but comments on visual PRs address how the UI looks or behaves twice as often (6.4% vs.3.3%), and visual-output fixes after review are about four times as common (4.7% vs. 1.2% of PRs). Visual artifacts are thus associated with closer scrutiny of what users see, not with an overall faster review.

title: From Ambiguous Tickets to Ranked Hypotheses: Multi-Agent Root-Cause Analysis for Autonomous Heavy-Vehicle Software
authors: Marten Seegers, Maximilian Kneissl, Enrique Aguayo-Lara, Chih-Hong Cheng
abstract: Autonomous haulage systems run safety-critical software on driverless mining trucks, with no onboard driver to detect or mitigate abnormal behavior. Every failure in testing or operation must therefore be traced to its root cause to keep the safety case valid and limit downtime. An investigation often starts from a sparse ticket containing an approximate timestamp, sometimes a suspected cause, and a multimodal vehicle recording of several gigabytes. We present a multi-agent root-cause analysis (RCA) workflow that turns this input into a telemetry-grounded event chain, ranked causal hypotheses, and candidate code locations. A suspected cause in the ticket, which could anchor the analysis on a false theory, goes to a single LLM analyst in a separate agent session. Non-neural tools select the relevant telemetry once, before analysis, and an LLM condenses it into shared evidence artifacts; this more than halved the cost per incident compared with per-analyst querying. Specialist analyst agents then apply established RCA techniques in parallel, including fault tree analysis, Kepner-Tregoe analysis, and call-chain tracing, and hypotheses that several LLM analysts reach independently rank higher. We evaluated the workflow on 12 held-out industrial incidents against a single agent with the same model and tools. It located the faulty file more often (10 vs. 8 cases) at higher cost. Two human domain experts accepted a top-three hypothesis in 4 and 9 cases, respectively. The gap, which two LLM judges did not resolve, shows that rating causal explanations is itself a hard evaluation problem.

title: Beyond Stars: MTTX Brings Developer Responsiveness to Dependency Decisions, from Dashboard to IDE to GitHub Actions
authors: Imranur Rahman, Ranindya Paramitha, Mahzabin Tamanna, Laurie Williams
abstract: Modern software reuses open-source packages as dependencies, and developers often choose among candidate packages with cheap signals, such as GitHub stars and download counts. However, such signals are easy to fake, so developers need signals that represent "observed behavior," such as how quickly the developers of a package respond to new dependency releases and to security fixes. Prior work computed these responsiveness metrics, MTTU (Mean Time To Update) dependencies and MTTR (Mean Time To Remediate) vulnerable dependencies, but only with a research prototype for a fixed set of packages. Therefore, developers cannot easily benefit from them or integrate them into their workflow. We present MTTX, an open-source tool that computes MTTU and MTTR with accurate historical dependency resolution for any package and given time window, and brings them into different phases of developer workflow. MTTX resolves each version constraint of npm, PyPI, and Cargo packages as of a past date, with data from the native registries or deps.dev and vulnerability data from OSV. We validated MTTX with 328 automated tests, and for 90 packages from prior work, we manually verified its dependency resolution at each historical release point and its MTTU and MTTR computation. Developers can use MTTX in an interactive web dashboard, an IDE extension, and a GitHub Action, which are all available from the project homepage at https://imranur-rahman.github.io/dependency-update-metrics/. We envision that package registries (e.g., npm) and metadata aggregators and intelligence platforms (e.g., deps.dev) will display these values on the package page, alongside download counts and stars, to make them easier for developers to access. A demo video is at https://youtu.be/MZqjDnJ8bEQ.
zh_title: 星标之外：MTTX 将开发者的响应度带入依赖项决策中，从仪表板到 IDE 再到 GitHub Actions
translation: 现代软件将开源包作为依赖项重新使用，开发人员经常在候选包中选择廉价的信号，例如 GitHub 星标和下载量。然而，这些信号很容易被伪造，因此开发人员需要代表“观察到的行为”的信号，例如包开发人员对新依赖项发布和安全修复的响应速度。先前的研究计算了这些响应度指标，即依赖项的 MTTU（平均更新时间）和存在漏洞的依赖项的 MTTR（平均修复时间），但这些指标仅适用于一组固定包的研究原型。因此，开发人员无法轻易从中受益或将其集成到工作流中。我们提出了 MTTX，这是一个开源工具，它使用来自原生注册表或 deps.dev 的准确历史依赖关系解析以及来自 OSV 的漏洞数据，为任何包和给定的时间窗口计算 MTTU 和 MTTR，并将它们带入开发人员工作流的不同阶段。MTTX 能够根据过去日期的历史数据解析 npm、PyPI 和 Cargo 包的每个版本约束。我们通过 328 个自动化测试验证了 MTTX，并针对先前工作中的 90 个包，手动验证了其在每个历史发布点的依赖关系解析及其 MTTU 和 MTTR 计算。开发人员可以在交互式 Web 仪表板、IDE 扩展和 GitHub Action 中使用 MTTX，这些都可以在项目主页 https://imranur-rahman.github.io/dependency-update-metrics/ 上获取。我们设想包注册表（例如 npm）以及元数据聚合器和智能平台（例如 deps.dev）将在包页面上显示这些值，连同下载量和星标一起，以便开发人员更轻松地访问它们。演示视频位于 https://youtu.be/MZqjDnJ8bEQ。
tldr: MTTX 是一个开源工具，它通过计算和提供依赖项的响应度指标（MTTU 和 MTTR）并集成到开发者的各种工作流中，帮助开发者做出更安全的依赖选择。
ai_comments: 该论文从开发者的实际工作流出发，将抽象的软件供应链安全指标（MTTU和MTTR）落地为可交互的、多平台集成的生产力工具，具有极高的实用价值和创新性。
motivation: 现代软件高度依赖开源包，但现有的选择信号（如 GitHub 星标和下载量）容易造假，而代表包维护者实际响应行为的指标（如 MTTU 和 MTTR）此前仅局限于研究原型，无法融入开发者的日常工作流中。
method: 开发了开源工具 MTTX，利用原生注册表、deps.dev 和 OSV 的数据，实现了对 npm、PyPI 和 Cargo 软件包在任意历史时间点的准确依赖解析，并计算 MTTU 和 MTTR。通过 328 个自动化测试和人工验证进行评估，同时提供了网页仪表板、IDE 插件和 GitHub Action 等多种工作流集成方式。

title: Architectural Design Decisions for Data Ingestion in Big Data Architectures
authors: Yikang Huang, Stefano Fossati, Indika Kumara, Damian A. Tamburri, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel
abstract:
Introduction: Data ingestion is the first critical step in a data architecture, in which data from various sources is moved to storage systems, such as data lakes and data warehouses, for analysis and insight generation. When developing a data ingestion pipeline, practitioners (e.g., data engineers and architects) must understand the data ingestion requirements (functional and non-functional) and select appropriate design options to support them.
  Objective: To help practitioners systematically develop data ingestion processes, this paper aims to compile a catalog of data ingestion design decisions, their options, and the selection drivers.
  Method: We conducted a systematic gray literature review on data ingestion, analyzed the selected literature using qualitative data analysis methods, and conducted semi-structured interviews with experts to assess the framework's practicality and utility.
  Results: From 42 gray literature articles, we identified 8 architectural design decisions, 59 decision options, and 36 decision drivers to guide practitioners in the design and implementation of data ingestion pipelines. The framework was evaluated through expert interviews, assessing its completeness, simplicity, understandability, operational feasibility, and usefulness.

title: Ask the Peers: Ranking NFR Coverage Gaps for Requirements Review
authors: Risha Parveen, Najmeh Akbari, Farnaz Delirie, Zheying Zhang, François Christophe, Jussi Rasku, Pekka Abrahamsson
abstract: Missing or underrepresented non-functional requirements (NFR) categories leave little direct evidence in a requirements set, making them difficult to identify during requirements review. In this study, we frame NFR coverage-gap review as a project-level ranking task: given a target requirements specification, the goal is to rank the 11 PROMISE NFR categories for analyst inspection. We compare seven statistical, embedding-based, and large language model (LLM)-based configurations that differ in both ranking mechanism and evidence source, including target requirement statements, peer requirements, their semantic representation, and peer category statistics. We evaluate the configurations using controlled gap injection with leave-one-project-out evaluation on PROMISE, PROMISE+, PURE-Transport, and PURE-Business. Four configurations that use peer category statistics are effectively tied under complete removal (0.875-0.889 mean AUROC), despite different ranking mechanisms, and supplying those statistics to a direct LLM ranker produces the largest evidence gain. All configurations weaken when a category is present but underrepresented, and none is best for every NFR category. For count-changing category-level gaps, structured peer evidence matters more than ranker sophistication. The findings suggest that the rankings should guide analyst inspection rather than serve as automatic judgements of requirements completeness.
comment: Pre-review version of a paper subsequently accepted for publication at PROFES 2026

title: Plug-and-Play Sensor Evolution in Software-Defined Vehicles through Asset Administration Shells
authors: Akshay Narla, Nasser Jazdi, Michael Weyrich
abstract:
Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) promise continuous software evolution, but sensor integration in deployed vehicles still depends on manual configuration, hardware-specific drivers, and repeated application-side adaptation. Existing standards address only parts of this problem. AUTOSAR standardizes selected sensor interfaces, the Vehicle Signal Specification (VSS) standardizes signal semantics, and Asset Administration Shells (AAS) standardize digital asset descriptions. However, these building blocks are rarely combined into an end-to-end onboarding path for sensors attached after vehicle deployment.
  This paper presents an AAS-driven plug-and-play sensor integration framework for safety-supervised sensors. Each sensor is represented by an AAS that combines hardware identification, interface metadata, VSS mappings, and references to containerized driver and optional application software. After physical connection, an edge gateway identifies the device, retrieves the matching AAS, deploys the referenced software, and publishes the resulting data under stable vehicle signal paths. A prototype on a resource-constrained edge gateway connected to an RR100 UGV demonstrates automated integration of a USB camera and an ultrasonic sensor. Across repeated integration cycles, the prototype reaches operational state in about 2s, shows no failed events, and keeps applications independent of hardware-specific interfaces. The results indicate that the introduction of AAS as an executable onboarding contract enables automated runtime deployment of sensor drivers in SDV environments.
comment: Peer-reviewed and Published in the 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)

title: When Code Works but the License Doesn't: Evaluating License Constraint Handling in Coding Agents
authors: Sundaraparipurnan Narayanan, Sandeep Vishwakarma
abstract:
Coding agents increasingly undertake repository-level development, including dependency selection, source modification, and software deployment. However, existing evaluations prioritize functional success over licensing correctness and commercial suitability.
  We investigate whether agents recognize and preserve software-license constraints when developing proprietary software. Experiments across multiple agents examine permissive and copyleft licenses, missing licensing information, transitive dependencies, source modification, dual licensing, vendoring, and distribution contexts. Agent traces, repository changes, and final artifacts are evaluated against licensing ground truth.
  Results reveal a persistent gap between functional and licensing correctness. Agents can successfully build and test software while overlooking licensing constraints involving provenance, authorization, and distribution. Better outcomes emerge when licensing information translates into engineering actions such as dependency substitution, architectural changes, and release gating. We argue that licensing in agentic development requires contextual constraint recognition and preservation across the software lifecycle, not merely license classification.
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 VeriCode Workshop

title: Optimal Development Path: An Empirical Evaluation of Tiered Dependency-Aware Sequencing
authors: Azzeddine Ihsine, Sara Ihsine
abstract: The Optimal Development Path (ODP) in D-POAF orders Feature Blocks in a Wave Candidate by choosing the eligible block with the lowest effort-and-risk-to-value ratio (ERS/BVS), while respecting declared prerequisites. We evaluate native ODP (L0) against four dependency-aware strategies: unlock count (L1), unlocked value (L2), multi-hop potential (L3), and one-step rollout (L4), alongside local search, Sidney decomposition, and an exact reference. On held-out synthetic graphs with about one prerequisite per block, L0 attains 0.978 of the surrogate optimum at 12 blocks, versus 0.993 for L2 and 0.994 for L4. At 100 blocks, L0 attains 0.942 and L2 0.983. In contrast, 373 historical Jira sprints from 21 open-source projects in TAWOS, used as scheduling proxies rather than D-POAF Waves, contain sparse recorded dependencies. On these instances, L0 attains 0.998 of the surrogate optimum and is exactly optimal in 69% of sprints. Unlock bonuses calibrated on synthetic graphs do not deliver significant average gains on these sprint-derived instances and can worsen the surrogate. L4 never worsens the declared surrogate relative to L0, but this guarantee does not extend to operational outcomes. Retrospective calendar replays using recorded Jira durations show that surrogate improvements do not reliably improve value-weighted completion. The findings support keeping L0 as the default and presenting rollout and exact references as auditable alternatives. Dependency-valid sequences expose prerequisite readiness, but their effects on interruptions, rework, costs, and delivery times remain unmeasured.
comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Public aggregate benchmark results available on Zenodo: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23762369

title: Dependency Fabrication in Repository Deployment Agents
authors: Robin Matter, Salman Toor
abstract: Repository deployment agents set up the environment needed to run a software repository. They often treat passing tests as proof of a successful setup. This report examines how such agents behave when a working setup is impossible. Probe repositories were built with a dependency that the agents could not legitimately obtain. Passing tests therefore indicated fabrication, such as creating a stub to replace the missing package. Agents in Repo2Run and SetupX usually fabricated the dependency. Both harnesses mostly still marked these runs as successful. Rules against fabrication, whether given in the prompt or repository documentation, did not reliably prevent this behavior. On MinimalSetupAgent, which was built for this report, mitigations proposed in the reward-hacking literature were most effective when the agent received a direct rule and had a clear way to stop and report the problem. Under these conditions, neither Qwen3.5-Plus nor GPT-5.6 Luna cheated in any of the 16 runs. Applying the same mitigation to Repo2Run and SetupX also required a native tool call for escalation. In Repo2Run, it worked only after the prompt was also replaced with one that placed less emphasis on passing tests.

title: LLMs for Software Vulnerability Prediction and Prioritization: A Review
authors: Faheem Ullah, Muhammad Moiz Khalid, Shayan Ayaz Khan, Hussain Ahmad
abstract: Large language models have moved beyond vulnerability detection into prediction, assessment, exploitability estimation, risk assessment and prioritization, yet the evidence for this shift has not been synthesised separately from the detection literature. In this systematic literature review, we examine how LLMs are used across those five task classes, how well they perform against established baselines, and what prevents their operational adoption. Following a prespecified protocol, we identified 197 records, removed 53 duplicates, and excluded 103 records at title and abstract stage. We assessed 41 full texts and finally retained 23 primary studies published between 2024 and 2026 after a six-question quality assessment. The review contributes a five-class taxonomy ordered by decision outcome, a method taxonomy covering prompting, tuning and retrieval or agentic architectures, an evaluation-practice audit, a bounded performance synthesis, and a deployment-barrier analysis. The main findings are that (i) assessment is the largest class (9 of 23 studies), ahead of risk assessment and prioritization (7 each); (ii) reported accuracy is highest where the label space is tightest and is not stable across evaluation periods; (iii) explanation usability is an audited evidence gap rather than a demonstrated capability; and (iv) reproducibility is the weakest reported dimension. We conclude that present systems should support analyst judgement rather than replace it, and we specify three validation studies that would settle the open questions.

title: Checking Retry Transparency in Agent Tools
authors: Jiapeng Li
abstract: A successful retry does not necessarily put the earlier attempt behind it. An old write may still overwrite a later acknowledged update; a partially executed file write may even empty a file after the retry has returned successfully. We study how to test the recovery guarantee behind an agent tool's local idempotence claim. Our prototype takes manually constructed, source-backed effect contracts and checks them at two levels: atomic retry-absorption obligations and bounded interleavings of successful-attempt microsteps. It emits model witnesses, conditional admission decisions, and explicit uncertainty when a completion boundary cannot be justified. The evaluation preserves a locally frozen purposive frame of 6 MCP components from 4 repositories; selected paths in 5 execute on the study machine and one backend remains unavailable. Real tests include file, graph, Git-index, document-update and browser bindings, together with a native Qdrant development matrix. In 27 missing-reply checks, the selective rule completes six justified workflows without an acknowledged goal violation, whereas strict coalescing completes none and blind retry completes nine with three violations. An intent-aware Porcupine specification independently agrees with all 156 complete-history oracles. These are mechanism-selected tests, not defect-prevalence estimates or a new linearizability algorithm. The contribution is an executable recovery-contract workflow that makes effect granularity, logical identity and completion assumptions testable rather than inheriting them from a tool annotation.

title: When Exact Inference Changes Code Selection: A Decision-Theoretic Analysis of B4
authors: Yanliang Cai
abstract: When generated programs are ranked using generated tests, a more exact posterior computation need not improve the selected program. We characterize this distinction in the published B4 code--test model. Identical execution signatures reduce exact candidate marginalization to N summands and nonempty joint maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference to two weights per group. A prior--budget condition guarantees that B4's whole-group rule already attains MAP; a sharp finite correction bound certifies when candidate marginals must select the same group. All 2,421 default-setting comparisons on 807 development matrices select the same candidates. A prospectively specified validation on 1,345 execution snapshots from a separate public archive also finds no changes in 4,035 default-setting comparisons. Across 80 literature-derived priors, this new archive yields 85 changed top sets in 107,600 comparisons; only six coincide with failure of whole-group MAP. Under finite-test proxy labels, four changes increase and five decrease expected success. These descriptive changes span seven snapshots; per-prior mean differences range from -0.074 to +0.045 percentage points. The results do not recommend a tuned prior or a new performance method. Exact enumeration and independent high-precision checks support the formulas and decision diagnostics. A supplementary fixed-test analysis separates asymptotic failure from observational ambiguity. The contribution is a model-specific account of when an inference intervention can change a software-testing decision, and when its effect must be sought in the priors or evidence instead.
comment: 16 pages, 7 tables; full proofs and numerical checks

title: Edge Computing for IoT-Enabled Smart Cities: A Review of Middleware, Explainable AI, and User Behavior Analytics
authors: Alexandros Gazis, George Vavouras, Nikos E. Mastorakis, Kleanthi Santamouri, Nikolaos Pournaras, Stylianos Pappas
abstract: This review looks at cloud-IoT edge middleware for analyzing user behavior in smart cities, with a particular focus on linking behavioral analytics to energy-aware and mission-critical urban services. The topic sits at the crossroads of smart-city platforms, IoT sensing, edge/fog/cloud computing, service-oriented architectures, machine learning, explainable AI, privacy-aware governance, and energy-critical applications such as EV charging, energy demand, environmental exposure, crowd safety, and the operational resilience of urban infrastructure. As such, this paper maps out the main categories of user-behavior data, examines five application domains, compares several case studies, and puts forward a new XAI-EdgeSOA Middleware Framework called X-EdgeCity Middleware. This framework brings together IoT sensing, edge preprocessing, fog coordination, event-driven communication, cloud analytics, XAI explanations, privacy-by-design, and benchmark logging. The goal is to support not just general smart-city applications, but also energy-sensitive or mission-critical services, where latency, reliability, explainability, and accountability have a direct impact on urban safety and continuity of operations.

title: Repository-Grounded Rubrics for Execution-Free Evaluation of Coding Agents
authors: Matej Gerek, Danylo Zahorulko, Samuel Budai, Chris Rupley, Thierry Donneau-Golencer
abstract: Coding agents are usually evaluated by running task-specific tests, but tests may be missing or incomplete, and running them requires a working environment for each repository. We adapt agentic rubrics, introduced for selecting among candidate patches, into an execution-free measure of how far a patch satisfies a task's requirements. An agent explores the repository before the change and writes weighted binary criteria, and a judge without tools scores a diff by the weighted share of criteria it satisfies. We validate the ordering this score produces against test outcomes on SWE-bench Verified, using 7,291 labeled patches from fifteen systems. Within the 400 tasks that have both resolved and unresolved patches, the mean per-task AUROC is 0.826 (0.838 on tasks not used to tune the rubric-generation prompt), and ranking systems by their failing patches closely agrees with ranking them by resolve rate (Spearman 0.968). Case analyses trace disagreements to tests that do not match the task, execution-blocking defects that the textual assessment misses, and errors in criteria or verdicts. The validation does not establish absolute score magnitudes or requirement satisfaction beyond agreement with tests, but rubric scores could complement tests where tests or execution environments cannot be assumed.
comment: 31 pages, 6 figures, 15 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/faros-ai/repository-grounded-rubrics

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Education for Software Developers: A Multivocal Literature Review
authors: R.D.N. Shakya, C.P. Wijesiriwardana, S.M.Vidanagamachchi, Nalin A.G. Arachchilage
abstract: Quantum computing threatens widely deployed public-key cryptography, making post-quantum cryptography (PQC) adoption a software engineering challenge. However, it remains unclear how well existing educational provision prepares software developers for secure PQC implementation and migration. We conducted a multivocal literature review of 8 research publications and 15 professional training offerings, examining competency coverage, practical software engineering tasks, pedagogical approaches, learner support, and evaluation. All 23 sources covered PQC foundations and algorithms, but coverage of practical software-engineering tasks was uneven. Our analysis identifies six gaps concerning developer focused evaluation, authentic software engineering tasks, task competency alignment, pedagogical design and learner support, security-focused assessment, and long term validation of learning outcomes and transfer. We derive recommendations for strengthening PQC education and better preparing software developers to implement and migrate cryptographic systems securely.

title: YUL: Bringing Software Supply Chain Security to Coding Agents
authors: Aman Sharma, Frank Reyes, Martin Monperrus
abstract: Coding agents choose and declare third-party dependencies on their own. They often declare a stale version that they recall from their training data. A stale dependency exposes the project to known vulnerabilities that the latest release already fixes. We present YUL, a design for coding agent harnesses that ensures that no stale dependencies are ever used. It does so by checking every dependency declaration against the package registry. If a dependency is stale or does not exist, YUL blocks the usage and tells the coding agent which version to use, so the coding agent retries with the fix. We evaluate YUL on 60 tasks across six ecosystems with Claude Code running Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenCode running DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Without YUL, Opus declares a stale version in 29% of runs and DeepSeek in 39%, and both declare a stale version in every GitHub Actions run. With YUL, the coding agents end on the latest release in 93% of stale Opus runs and in 96% of stale DeepSeek runs. YUL thus brings the best practices of software supply chain security to coding agents.

title: MRASLive: An online parameter estimation toolbox for time-dependent PDEs
authors: Christian Aarset, Benedikt Kaltenbach, Tram Thi Ngoc Nguyen
abstract: We present MRASLive, a toolbox for online parameter identification in time-dependent partial differential equations based on a model reference adaptive system (MRAS). Building on the MRAS proposed by Kaltenbacher and Nguyen (Inverse Problems 37(5) 2021) and its first numerical realization by the authors (Applied Mathematics for Modern Challenges 8 2026), the toolbox is designed for ease of use, utilising the user's weak form specification to prepare the data, the discretized MRAS and its solvers, and to verify the assumptions of MRAS's convergence theory semi-automatically.

title: Model Discovery for Virtual Chaos Engineering with Incomplete Tracing: An eBPF Study
authors: Anatoly A. Krasnovsky
abstract: Model-based fault experiments can assess the consequences of component failures before intervening in a running application. Recent work on model discovery and graph simulation acquired operation models from application telemetry and used them for availability prediction. Applying this approach to operational legacy systems raises an acquisition problem: the required traces may be absent or incomplete, while introducing them can require changes across heterogeneous components. These systems continue to serve business operations during extended maintenance and modernization. External observation offers a possible route to model-based fault analysis before a tracing retrofit, but collecting telemetry does not by itself establish that an executable operation model can be obtained. We investigate this route using extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) observations and the existing graph-based modelling approach. A 108-case study varied application software development kit (SDK) tracing across absent, partial and full conditions in three public applications. Discovered dependencies were combined with declared operation requirements, deployment facts and scenario assumptions; model forecasts preceded independent execution checks. With SDK tracing disabled, the tested OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation path supported all seven operations in two applications across three repetitions. Forecasts agreed exactly in 17 of 21 operation-repetition groups; the maximum state-weighted discrepancy was 4.22 percentage points. Combining observed context links supported nine additional groups under partial tracing. The results establish an acquisition path for virtual fault experiments under the tested observation constraints and identify limits imposed by protocols, evidence association and operation semantics.
comment: Submitted to Software and Systems Modeling journal

title: AppSec Core: An Ontology for Security-by-Design Software Engineering
authors: Pedro Farinha
abstract: When engineers or coding agents change an application, a dependency, a configuration or a build pipeline, they need to know three things: which security rules apply, how to meet them, and what evidence to leave. Today the answers are spread over many standards, frameworks, laws and lists of weaknesses, and each one uses its own words and level of detail. This paper presents AppSec Core, a model of the security work that engineers do. It says what must be true, which practices get there, which mechanisms do the job and which artefacts show that it was done. It has 259 elements in ten domains. We built it from a security-by-design manual written from practice, and then checked it against 31 outside sources, ten of them about AI systems and agents. Along the way we made three changes, which added five objectives and made one domain wider. We did not need a new domain. Most objectives are backed by several sources: the typical objective is used by six of the twenty technical sources, and 194 of the 202 objectives, practices and mechanisms are linked to items in the sources. For the domain of a change, the model gives back a closed set of typed elements, and for a source, it gives back the objectives that the source points to. We keep the model apart from the manual, the selection rules and the server that delivers the result, and we follow one change, adding a third-party package, through all four. When a code generator received the requirements, the share of security tests passed on a public benchmark went from 77.4% to 93.0%. On a second benchmark, the result was close to that of the benchmark's own "oracle" prompt, which is written with the tests in mind.
comment: 24 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Supersedes OSF preprint doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/WG8PV

title: Error Analysis of Deep Learning
authors: Yuling Jiao, Peiying Wu, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Pingwen Zhang
abstract: This review examines deep learning theory through the lens of error decomposition, systematically addressing approximation, statistical, and optimization errors. We trace the development of error analyses from bounds on individual error components to frameworks that account for all three. Using nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz Method as dual running examples, we demonstrate how these analyses apply across fundamentally different loss structures. We then review representative analyses in scientific machine learning, generative learning, reinforcement learning, representation learning, and large language models, showing how learning errors affect solutions, distributions, and predictions through problem-specific arguments. Throughout, we clarify which error components are controlled, how they are combined, and what assumptions are needed to obtain guarantees for trained networks.
comment: Mathematical survey of error analysis for neural network methods, with nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz method for elliptic PDEs as running examples. Covers function and Sobolev approximation, statistical estimation, and optimization error, together with stability estimates, convergence rates, and selected proofs

title: Numerical approximation of Benjamin-Ono type models for two-dimensional internal waves
authors: Angel Durán
abstract: In this paper we analyze the numerical approximation with spectral methods of two asymptotic models for the two-dimensional propagation of internal waves in a two-layer system of fluids with rigid-lid condition. The semidiscretization in space of the periodic initial-value problem with the spectral Fourier-Galerkin method is introduced and some error estimates are derived. Then the semidiscrete system is integrated in time with the Implicit Midpoint Rule and several numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the corresponding full discretization.

title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
authors: Aydin Mohseni
abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. And when AI variants that keep more resources spread faster, alignment lasts only while misaligned variants are reliably sanctioned. In these two senses, human-AI mutualism is unstable.

title: HydroMind: A Checkable Agent for Autonomous Hydrological Research
authors: Zheng Fang, Yiqun Sun, Simin Qu, Shijie Jiang
abstract: General-purpose coding agents have written code for hydrological and Earth-system models. In these studies the researchers decided in advance how the model would be evaluated, for example the test period, the scoring function, and the standard the model had to meet. No study has tested what happens when the agent makes these decisions itself: how many of its claims are supported by its own data, code, and results, and whether readers can check them. Both may depend on the agent's harness, that is, the tools it can call and the written instructions it follows. We compared three harnesses: the agent's own harness; this harness plus the modeling tools of HydroMind, a hydrological modeling system we developed for general-purpose agents, which run every model through fixed commands and store its settings, trained model, and predictions; and both plus HydroMind's research procedure, under which the agent writes a research design before running any model and records every change to it. Under each harness, the same agent studied four open questions in hydrological model development and was given only the data. Under the three harnesses, the experiments submitted 23, 20, and 41 claims, each stating that one model or approach is better than, worse than, or similar to another. A claim does not hold if the difference recomputed from the experiment's own code and predictions disagrees with it, or if the code did not compare the two models or approaches the claim names. Under the three harnesses, 30%, 20%, and 5% of the claims did not hold. A statistical test, confidence interval, or decision rule that lets readers judge the stated difference was reported for 48%, 53%, and 83% of the claims. With the language model unchanged, changing only the harness reduced the share of claims that do not hold and increased the share that readers can check.

title: Sharp error estimates for Lagrange interpolation and Kantorovich-type operators in weighted $L_p$-spaces
authors: L. Angeloni, D. Costarelli, Yu. Kolomoitsev
abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp direct and inverse approximation estimates for algebraic Lagrange interpolation polynomials and Kantorovich-type operators in weighted $L_p$ spaces on $[-1,1]$. A well-known limitation in the theory of approximation by interpolation polynomials states that for small rates of convergence $α\le 1/p$, classical moduli of smoothness fail to provide matching direct and inverse estimates due to the insufficiency of integral metrics to determine pointwise values at the interpolation nodes. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce new special semi-discrete measures of smoothness based on Steklov averaging operators, which combine global $L_p$-smoothness with discrete deviations from Steklov averages at the interpolation nodes. By using these measures, we establish fully matching direct and inverse approximation theorems for Lagrange interpolation polynomials, thereby providing complete two-sided characterizations of the rate of convergence for an arbitrary rate $α> 0$. As a natural application of the developed approach, we also obtain corresponding direct and inverse estimates, as well as strong converse inequalities, for Kantorovich-type operators constructed via Lagrange polynomials.

title: Computing with Orientation-Dependent Vector Fields in Crystallographic Texture Analysis
authors: Ralf Hielscher, Erik Wünsche
abstract:
We present a computational framework for representing orientation-dependent vector fields. Building on (arXiv:2608.21235), we translate the differential-geometric formulation into crystallographic notation and focus on its computational use in crystallographic texture analysis.
  In crystallographic applications, small orientation changes are commonly described by rotation vectors, spin tensors, or infinitesimal misorientations. By contrast, vector fields in harmonic computations are usually represented by components with respect to Euler-angle derivatives, following the classical formulation of generalized spherical harmonics. This representation is convenient but numerically unfavorable. We instead use rotation-vector components, extending a familiar description of individual orientation changes to orientation-dependent vector fields.
  In this representation, vector fields are described by three scalar component functions, which can be expanded into generalized spherical harmonics. We derive frequency-domain formulas for gradient, divergence, and curl, enabling their evaluation directly on harmonic coefficients. In particular, the gradient of a band-limited scalar function remains band-limited with the same bandwidth.

title: A level is not a rank: an empirical audit of quantile-to-index conversion in 10 released conformal-prediction libraries
authors: Shivam Lalakiya
abstract: Context. A conformal interval at 0.90 keeps that guarantee only at the right rank: a fresh score falls at or below the rth smallest of n with probability r/(n + 1). The libraries we study instead hand a level to a quantile function, which can land elsewhere. At n = 20, the upper end of statsforecast's interval sits at position 18.05 where rank 19 is required. Objective. Where does installed code resolve the wrong rank, at what cost in coverage, and what does it return when no rank reaches the level? Method. We audit 39 sites where a level becomes an index in 10 pinned packages, a named set rather than a systematic search. 12 are classified by running them, 11 through their shared numpy method, the rest from source. Coverage is paired against the required rank on the same scores. Results. All 7 tabular implementations reach the required rank. In darts, on one code path, coverage is unchanged (0.0000) where the ranks agree and 0.0280 to 0.0560 lower where they differ; a second archive repeats that split but not its range. Below the feasibility floor, $n < 1/α- 1$, of 14 public call paths 5 silently return a finite number; the rest raise or warn. Conclusions. Quantile interfaces take only a level; statsforecast's default calibrates below its floor. 6 of 19 upstream filings have merged, one fixing a coverage shortfall. A conformance suite classifies helpers by the rank they reach, and a checklist guides review.
comment: 34 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Online Resource (45 pages) included as an ancillary file. Code, probe outputs and pinned environments: doi:10.5281/zenodo.21799203

title: Training for sustainable scientific software in the AI era: from code production to scientific stewardship
authors: Juliette Alimena
abstract: Generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are changing how researchers interact with scientific software. Their effects on productivity vary across tasks and users, but they can weaken the connection between producing a successful computational artifact and retaining scientific command over the consequential choices and evidence on which it depends. For high-energy physics, this shifts part of the training challenge from code production toward scientific stewardship: researchers must be able to validate, explain, reproduce, maintain, and justify software and workflows partly generated or modified by AI. We argue that AI-aware software training should therefore combine dedicated instruction on AI systems with the integration of AI into established software and analysis training. Testing, provenance, reproducibility, resource judgment, and scientific validation should be exercised in AI-assisted workflows, with competence judged by the evidence supporting a result rather than by code generation alone. We frame this as a problem of sustainable scientific software: AI-assisted workflows should remain trustworthy and maintainable, use computational resources responsibly, and avoid making core competence unnecessarily dependent on privileged access to particular tools or infrastructure.
comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Submitted to Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
zh_title: AI时代可持续科学软件的培训：从代码生产到科学管理
translation: 生成式和智能体人工智能（AI）系统正在改变研究人员与科学软件的交互方式。它们对生产力的影响因任务和用户而异，但可能会削弱产生成功计算产物与保持对其所依赖的关键选择及证据的科学掌控力之间的联系。对于高能物理学而言，这将部分培训挑战从代码生产转向了科学管理：研究人员必须能够验证、解释、复现、维护和论证由AI部分生成或修改的软件与工作流。我们认为，具备AI意识的软件培训因此应将针对AI系统的专门指导与将AI融入既定软件及分析培训相结合。测试、溯源、可重现性、资源判断和科学验证应在AI辅助的工作流中得到实践，能力的衡量应取决于支持结果的证据，而非仅仅依靠代码生成。我们将此界定为可持续科学软件的问题：AI辅助的工作流应保持值得信赖与可维护，负责任地使用计算资源，并避免使核心能力不必要地依赖于对特定工具或基础设施的特权访问。
tldr: 面对AI降低编码门槛却削弱科学把控的挑战，科研软件培训需从单纯的代码生成转向强调验证、复现与负责任使用资源的“科学管理”。
ai_comments: 本文敏锐地指出了生成式AI在科研计算中的潜在风险，即代码产出的便捷可能削弱研究人员对底层科学证据的掌控。文章立足高能物理领域，创新性地提出将培训重点从“代码生产”转向“科学管理”，对未来科研人才培养具有重要指导意义；其局限在于摘要内容属于观点与倡导性论述，尚未提供具体的教学实践评估数据。
motivation: 生成式与智能体AI系统虽然能提升特定任务的生产力，但容易削弱研究人员在生成计算产物时对其依赖的关键科学选择与证据的直接掌控能力。
method: 主张构建具备AI意识的软件培训体系，将AI系统的专门教学与现有软件分析培训深度融合，在AI辅助工作流中强化测试、数据溯源、可重现性、计算资源合理利用与科学验证等实践环节。
results: 重塑了科研能力评价标准，强调以支持结果的科学证据而非单纯的代码生成量来评估能力，从而确保AI辅助工作流的可信度与可持续性。
conclusion: 科学软件的可持续发展要求AI辅助的工作流保持可信与可维护，合理使用计算资源，并防止研究的核心竞争力过度受制于特定的专有AI工具或特权基础设施。

title: What Should an LLM Know? Knowledge-Guided Warm Starts for Software Optimization
authors: Srinath Srinivasan, Tim Menzies
abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) process gigabytes in minutes; human experts work far more slowly. Prior studies that explored combinations of human/AI optimizers ignore this gap. Those studies asked systems or humans to label too many examples (e.g., SynthCore needs over four dozen per trial). Here, we test human and AI knowledge under a budget where evaluation is practical (a few dozen labels or fewer).
  We compare five baselines (random search, RRP, EZR, few-shot prompting, and a budget-matched SynthCore variant) against three ways to give an LLM domain knowledge before it proposes its first configurations: (1) AMP lists the domain's rules, then checks each candidate against them; (2) HKMA adds scouted data or documentation to the prompt; and (3) H-DKP has human experts correct the LLM's rules.
  We find that domain knowledge improves the "start-up" phase of LLM optimization, but only when that knowledge is checked, by the LLM itself or by a human expert. Across 49 datasets, unchecked knowledge did no better than few-shot prompting or EZR. On the other hand, AMP's self-checking variant (AMP-4) reached the best statistical rank in 44 of 49 datasets (budget-matched SynthCore: 23 of 49), and H-DKP did so in 7 of 8 expert studies. These checks cost little: half a cent of LLM calls per trial, or 6 to 10 expert contacts.
  Hence we say LLMs may not need more data, but rather their knowledge needs checking (and checking is cheap).
zh_title: 大语言模型应该了解什么？用于软件优化的知识引导热启动
translation: 大语言模型（LLM）可以在几分钟内处理千兆字节的数据，而人类专家的工作速度要慢得多。以往探索人类/AI优化器结合的研究忽视了这一差距。这些研究要求系统或人类标注过多的样本（例如，SynthCore每次试验需要超过四打样本）。在此，我们在评估预算切合实际（几十个标签或更少）的条件下，测试了人类和AI知识的效果。我们比较了五个基准方法（随机搜索、RRP、EZR、少样本提示以及预算匹配的SynthCore变体）与在LLM提出首批配置前为其提供领域知识的三种方法：(1) AMP，列出领域规则，然后根据这些规则检查每个候选配置；(2) HKMA，向提示中添加侦查数据或文档；(3) H-DKP，由人类专家纠正LLM的规则。我们发现，领域知识改善了LLM优化的“启动”阶段，但前提是该知识经过了核查——无论是由LLM自身还是由人类专家核查。在49个数据集中，未经核查的知识表现并不比少样本提示或EZR好。另一方面，AMP的自检变体（AMP-4）在49个数据集中的44个中达到了最佳统计排名（预算匹配的SynthCore为23/49），而H-DKP在8项专家研究中的7项中做到了这一点。这些检查的成本很低：每次试验只需半美分的LLM调用费用，或6至10次专家交流。因此我们认为，LLM可能不需要更多的数据，而是其知识需要被核查（且核查成本很低）。
tldr: 在软件优化中，LLM需要的不是更多数据而是低成本的知识核查，经过核查的领域知识能以极低代价显著提升热启动性能。
ai_comments: 该研究切中实际应用痛点，指出了以往优化方法依赖过多人工标注的不切实际之处。其核心洞见极具启发性：大语言模型在软件配置优化中并不盲目缺乏数据，而是缺乏对知识的核查机制；且无论是通过自身核查规则还是专家少量介入，成本都极其低廉，具有很高的实用价值和工程指导意义。
motivation: 人类专家与LLM处理速度存在巨大差距，以往结合人类与AI优化的研究忽略了这一问题，要求标注过多样本（如每次试验需几十个标签），导致在实际中不可行。因此需要在评估预算受限（更符合实际）的情况下探究人类与AI知识的结合。
method: 在实用低评估预算（几十个或更少标签）下，对比了5种基线（随机搜索、RRP、EZR、Few-shot、预算匹配的SynthCore变体）与3种注入领域知识的方法：(1) AMP：列出领域规则并核查候选配置；(2) HKMA：在Prompt中加入侦查数据或文档；(3) H-DKP：由人类专家纠正LLM生成的规则。
results: 领域知识仅在经过核查（由LLM自检或专家纠错）时才能显著改善优化的启动阶段；未经核查的知识表现平平。自检变体AMP-4在49个数据集中的44个达到最佳统计排名，H-DKP在8项专家研究中的7项达到最佳，且核查成本极低（每次试验仅约0.5美分或6-10次专家交互）。
conclusion: LLM在软件优化中或许并不需要更多的数据，关键在于对其知识进行核查，且这种自检或人机协同核查的成本极其低廉。

title: Integrating AI Coding Agents Into Scientific Research
authors: Rory Barnes
abstract: New software tools have emerged that enable AI agents to quickly develop code that analyzes data and generates figures, but their mistakes can also harm a researcher's computer, require extensive resources for validation, and cause the results to be received more skeptically. These concerns could be mitigated if scientific software is developed in a secure environment with a system for monitoring file changes and well-defined standards for handling AI agents. This paper first describes how coding agents change eleven aspects of generating, verifying, and reproducing numerical results. A six-level scale is then proposed for classifying AI-assisted numerical experiments by their provenance, reproducibility, openness, oversight, and falsifiability (PROOF). The scale begins with locally self-consistent, version-controlled, human-verified results and culminates in a publicly accessible and curated archive of the files, change history, prompt transcripts, independent agent regeneration of the analysis, and multiple cryptographically verifiable attestations of regeneration by independent researchers. These aspects of AI-assisted scientific software development have been synthesized into a new open source software package called vaibify that optimizes the agentic development of computational experiments ascending the PROOF Ladder. Docker containers sequester the agents while a GUI enables researchers to prompt command line agents, monitor the current status of local and remote files, and drive a project to PROOF Level 3 (reproducible). The methods described in this paper could help researchers reduce the time required to verify agent-written software and efficiently communicate trust in AI-assisted science.
comment: 36 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Software publicly available at https://github.com/RoryBarnes/vaibify
zh_title: 将AI编码代理集成到科学研究中
translation: 新软件工具的出现使得AI代理能够快速开发分析数据和生成图表的代码，但它们的错误也可能损害研究人员的计算机，需要大量的资源进行验证，并导致结果受到更多质疑。如果在安全的开发环境中开发科学软件，并建立文件更改监控系统以及明确的AI代理处理标准，这些担忧就可以得到缓解。本文首先描述了编码代理如何改变生成、验证和再现数值结果的十一个方面。然后，提出了一个六级量表，用于根据来源、可再现性、开放性、监督和可证伪性（PROOF）对AI辅助的数值实验进行分类。该量表从本地自洽、版本控制、人工验证的结果开始，最终达到公开可访问和策划的文件、更改历史、提示记录、独立代理再生成分析以及多个由独立研究人员进行的加密可验证的再生成证明的存档。AI辅助科学软件开发的这些方面已被整合到一个名为vaibify的新开源软件包中，该软件包优化了计算实验的代理开发，使其能够提升PROOF等级。Docker容器隔离代理，而GUI使研究人员能够提示命令行代理，监控本地和远程文件的当前状态，并将项目驱动到PROOF 3级（可再现）。本文描述的方法可以帮助研究人员减少验证代理编写软件所需的时间，并有效地传达对AI辅助科学的信任。
tldr: 本文提出了一种名为PROOF的六级量表来分类AI辅助的数值实验，并开发了开源软件vaibify，旨在安全地整合AI编码代理到科学研究中，以提高可验证性和可信度。
ai_comments: 本文提出了一种新颖且及时的解决方案，旨在解决AI编码代理在科学研究中应用时面临的可信度和可验证性挑战。PROOF量表提供了一个结构化的框架来评估AI辅助实验的质量和透明度，而vaibify软件则为研究人员提供了一个实用的工具，以安全、高效地利用AI代理。其创新性在于将安全容器、文件监控和明确的验证标准结合起来，这对于促进AI在科学发现中的负责任应用至关重要。
motivation: AI编码代理在数据分析和图表生成方面展现出潜力，但其错误可能损害研究者的计算机、需要大量资源进行验证，并导致结果受到质疑。为了解决这些问题并减轻担忧，需要在安全环境中开发科学软件，并建立文件监控系统和AI代理处理标准。
method: 本文首先描述了编码代理如何改变数值结果的生成、验证和再现的11个方面。然后，提出了一个六级量表（PROOF），用于根据来源、可再现性、开放性、监督和可证伪性对AI辅助的数值实验进行分类。该量表从本地自洽、版本控制、人工验证的结果开始，最终达到公开可访问和策划的文件、更改历史、提示记录、独立代理分析再生成以及多重加密可验证的独立研究者再生成证明的存档。这些方面被整合到一个名为vaibify的新开源软件包中，该包优化了计算实验的代理开发以提升PROOF等级。Docker容器隔离代理，而GUI使研究人员能够提示命令行代理，监控本地和远程文件的当前状态，并将项目驱动到PROOF 3级（可再现）。
results: 开发了一个名为vaibify的新的开源软件，它将AI辅助科学软件开发的各个方面整合起来，并优化了计算实验的代理开发，使其能够提升PROOF等级。该软件使用Docker容器隔离代理，并通过GUI使研究人员能够与代理交互，监控文件状态，并将项目驱动到PROOF 3级（可再现）。
