An ego-trajectory query conditions DINOv3-aligned BEV predictions from shared planner representations. Training combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with one-sided feature separation under an unlabeled perturbed trajectory. Together, these objectives train the shared planner to generate driving waypoints. Native inference directly generates waypoints and bypasses the auxiliary future-prediction branch. On all 220 Bench2Drive routes, TrajWAM achieves 91.53 Driving Score and 75.45% Success Rate, exceeding a schedule-matched planning-only fine-tuning baseline by 5.31 Driving Score points and eight successful routes.
comment: 22 pages, including supplementary material. Code and model weights: https://github.com/FangWD520/TrajWAM

title: High-Precision Docking of Differential-Drive Mobile Robots Through LiDAR and Vision Collaboration
authors: Zaide Zhang, Zheyuan Zhang
abstract: Precise docking requires a differential-drive robot to correct lateral offset through coupled rotation and translation within a short approach distance. We combine global navigation with terminal control using complementary LiDAR and visual observations. A line fitted to the cabinet front gives normal distance and heading. An AprilTag identifies the workstation; intersecting its center ray with the LiDAR plane determines tangential position. Taught observations define the docking reference and can cancel repeatable fixed biases under unchanged mounting and geometry. Lateral pre-alignment and continuous visual servoing coordinate the approach, with predictive stopping to account for low-speed actuation lag. Across two sessions using the same navigation and docking code at five workstations on Robot 2, all 111 tasks completed, including 101 on the first attempt. Relative to the taught observations, onboard longitudinal, lateral and heading residual root-mean-square values were 1.51 mm, 5.93 mm and 0.238 degrees, respectively. Joint acceptance within plus or minus 10 mm per position axis and plus or minus 1 degree heading was 96.4% (107/111), or 95.5% (106/111) with a plus or minus 0.5 degree heading limit.

title: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
authors: Baiang Li, Enze Xie, Jincheng Yu, Jin Wang, Haozhe Liu, Yitong Li, Juanxi Tian, Felix Heide
abstract: Video world models keep the world in the context of a generator, so a revisit is synthesized again and earlier edits can drift or disappear. We present WM^MLLM, the first interactive world model built on multimodal large language models (MLLMs), for persistent, editable world generation from a single image. WM^MLLM keeps the world state outside every generator, as a panorama with a revision history, and lets the MLLMs write it: they turn each request into operations on this state, select where a local edit is written, and check every candidate before it becomes the next state. Image generators only propose views, and video only presents them. Users can walk to new places and return, edit objects through text or a box, place subjects, and change lighting, weather or season. By construction, a revisit at the same revision reproduces the earlier view exactly, a local edit leaves every panorama pixel outside its region unchanged, and each request starts from the result of the previous one. Against six world model baselines on MBench-A, WM^MLLM has the highest mean on all four environment-recovery metrics (Epipolar 91.5 versus 0.1 to 74.0) and completes the most camera round trips (85.3% versus at most 50.9%). It has the best value in all 15 CompBench columns against 15 baselines. On 112 local edits judged blind, selecting the region to write after generation raises completion from 34.8% to 83.0%. On 258 WBench and MBench-A items, all 46 revisits recover their earlier views, and all 97 local edits that pass the check leave panorama pixels outside their region unchanged.
comment: 25 pages, 14 figures, 8 tables; project page: https://ztmotalee.github.io/wmmllm/

title: From Neural Tokens to Language: Dual-View EEG Semantic Bridging for Brain-to-Text Generation
authors: YaoYang Liu, Jun Dai, ZhuoShi Tang, Weijun Sun, Xiaozhao Fang, Jie Wen
abstract: Visually evoked EEG-to-text generation aims to produce natural-language descriptions from neural responses elicited by visual stimuli. Existing approaches typically compress EEG signals into a single global representation and directly project it into the hidden space of a large language model (LLM), which may limit the preservation of complementary visual semantics under noisy and subject-dependent EEG signals. We propose a dual-view semantic token bridging framework that exploits raw images and sketch images as complementary visual supervision to learn raw-oriented and sketch-oriented EEG semantic token streams. To interface these structured neural representations with an LLM, we introduce a branch-specific semantic query bridge that aggregates each token stream into compact semantic slots and converts them into LLM-compatible soft prompts. A progressive adaptation strategy further transitions the learned visual-semantic interface from image-supported training to image-free EEG-conditioned generation. Experiments demonstrate strong subject-wise EEG classification performance and competitive EEG-to-text generation across multiple LLM backbones. Ablation, branch-level representation, and EEG-label disentanglement analyses further show that the two EEG streams learn complementary view-oriented representations and that EEG-derived prompts provide sample-specific information beyond category labels.

title: A (12/11+eps)-Approximation for Nonpreemptive Throughput Maximization
authors: Mikhail Cherniavskii, Mikhail Koshelev, Andrey Kupavskii, Stanislav Moiseev, Fedor Ozhegov, Alexander Shekhovtsov
abstract: We study unweighted nonpreemptive throughput maximization on an arbitrary number of identical machines: each job has a processing time and a release--deadline window, and the goal is to schedule as many jobs as possible. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, we give a randomized $(12/11+\varepsilon)$-approximation. This improves the recent $(4/3+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Alexander Armbruster, Fabrizio Grandoni, Antoine Tinguely, and Andreas Wiese and the $(17/13+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Tong and Xu. For binary-encoded integral inputs, our algorithm runs in time $n^{O_\varepsilon(1)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$, where $N$ is the input length.

title: Large-Scale Tensor Trace-Ratio Problem: Randomized Algorithm and Sparse Multilinear Discriminant Analysis via Closed-Form Solution
authors: Yuhang Li, Gang Wu
abstract: Trace-ratio optimization problems from high-dimensional tensor data appear across numerous research domains including machine learning, signal processing, as well as pattern recognition. Up to now, analytical closed-form expressions remain unavailable for tensor trace-ratio tasks; prevailing techniques mostly adopt inner-outer iterative schemes to tackle such optimization tasks. However, when dealing with high-dimensional tensor data sets, existing multilinear discriminant analysis methods often encounter limitations such as heavy computational costs, insufficient memory space, and interference from redundant features. This paper yields two core contributions.First, we present a closed-form solution under the full row rank condition, and construct a randomized solver targeting large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization. In contrast to prior approaches, the devised algorithm achieves substantial computational speedup.Its core mechanism is to reformulate the original large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization into a tensor least-squares formulation, instead of the much more complicated (generalized) tensor eigenproblems. We derive theoretical error-bound results which verify the reliability of the newly developed algorithm. Second, we build a sparse multilinear discriminant analysis model leveraging the above closed-form result combined with tensor \ell_{2,0}-norm regularization, and propose a sparse multilinear discriminant method for tensor feature selection. The sparse method can identify key discriminative features from high-dimensional data and suppress redundant information. Comprehensive numerical evaluations are conducted over multiple publicly available real-world benchmarks.The proposed methods demonstrate significant advantages in computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale problems, while achieving competitive classification accuracy on some datasets.

title: SpiderMark: Hybrid Watermarking for Generative AI via Algorithmic Injection and Learning-Based Verification
authors: Chihcheng Hsieh, Yang Song, Flora Salim, Martin Bell, Jacinto C. Nascimento, Catarina Moreira
abstract: The proliferation of diffusion-based generative models has intensified the need for reliable methods to trace and verify the provenance of AI-generated images. Existing watermarking approaches for diffusion models typically rely on isotropic frequency patterns and handcrafted detection metrics, which are prone to directional vulnerability and threshold instability across diverse image transformations. We propose SpiderMark, a hybrid watermarking framework that combines algorithmic frequency-domain injection with learning-based probabilistic verification, requiring no modifications to pretrained diffusion model weights. SpiderMark embeds a structured spider-web pattern, comprising radial spokes and concentric polygonal rings, into the Fourier representation of the initial latent noise, and trains a lightweight ResNet-18 verifier augmented with auxiliary similarity cues (PSNR and L1) to produce a continuous watermark confidence score for watermark detection. Across nine evaluation conditions, SpiderMark achieves the highest fixed-threshold Accuracy in eight, while retaining strong detection on unseen COCO prompts without verifier retraining. CLIP similarity and FID measurements show that these detection gains are accompanied by small measured differences in prompt alignment and distributional image quality. SpiderMark establishes that structured watermark geometry and learned probabilistic verification can be unified into a single, practical framework, bridging the gap between imperceptibility, robustness, and real-world verifiability for generative AI content attribution.

title: Learning with Unlearning: Synaptic Role Partitioning for Simultaneous Continual Learning and Machine Unlearning
authors: Mohammad Ali Vahedifar, Behzad Bozorgtabar, Qi Zhang
abstract: Continual Learning (CL) asks a model to acquire new knowledge without forgetting what it already knows. Machine Unlearning (MU) asks it to destroy specific knowledge without damaging the rest. The challenge is integrating them in the same system; the two objectives pull on the same weights, and an edit made for one harms the other. To address this, we propose Learning with Unlearning (LwU), a unified framework that resolves the conflict where it occurs: at the individual synapse. LwU scores every weight twice, once against the data to keep and once against the data to delete, and partitions the network into four zones with separate update rules. Weights that only require retention are frozen. Weights that only require deletion are cleared and returned to the network as free capacity. Contested weights take a gradient-ascent step projected orthogonally to the retention gradient. The remaining capacity learns the incoming task by a privileged teacher via self-distillation. Deletion is served post hoc, and no retraining is required. Across both CL and MU jobs, LwU outperforms or matches the strongest baseline. Its real-world practicality has been demonstrated on the Physical Artificial Intelligence (PAI) dataset we conducted. Additionally, in the image generation task and in removing dangerous content, it outperformed the closest baseline, as shown in Fig.1.

title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors
authors: Yoobin Shin, Jaeyoung Lee, Jieun Kang, Hyun Song, Woojin Kim, Andrew Jaeyong Choi
abstract: 3D object reconstruction is essential for robotic perception and manipulation, yet conventional approaches predominantly rely on visual observations that can be limited by occlusion or unavailable in visually constrained environments. In this work, we propose a vision-free, training-free, and category-agnostic framework for reconstructing 3D object meshes from sparse tactile contacts without relying on pretrained shape models. A 6-DoF robotic arm equipped with a 20-DoF multi-finger robotic hand collects tactile observations using 3x3 pressure sensor arrays mounted on the finger pads. The acquired tactile measurements are transformed into 3D contact constraints through robot kinematics and integrated into a multi-scale Gaussian Process Implicit Surface (GPIS). To address sparse and incomplete surface observations, the proposed method incorporates contact confidence weighting, weak pseudo-surface constraints, and an observation-driven geometric prior to preserve local surface geometry and provide structural guidance in unobserved regions. Real-world experiments on six objects achieve a Chamfer Distance (CD) of 1.610, an Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) of 7.738, and an F-Score of 95.00, with reconstruction completed in an average of 49.99 s per object. These results demonstrate that sparse tactile sensing can provide sufficient geometric information for continuous 3D object reconstruction without visual or semantic information.

title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
authors: Philippe Forest, Giulia Lioi, Mai Pham Quyen, Alix Lamouroux, Javen Shi, Adrien Merlini
abstract: Neural decoding of visual experience from electroencephalography (EEG) has achieved strong performance in intra-subject settings, but current methods fail to generalize across individuals: on the standard 200-way benchmark THINGS-EEG-2, top-1 accuracy drops from above 80% within subjects to about 32% for an unseen subject. Adapting a pre-trained encoder to new subjects and sessions typically requires labeled data, a bottleneck whose collection time severely limits practical device deployment. In a practical Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), however, the possible outcomes are known in advance and form a gallery of candidates, and the unlabeled EEG of the user accumulates as soon as the device is used. We propose a new setting, incremental transductive calibration, in which the decoder is calibrated regularly on all the unlabeled EEG received so far and on the known gallery, without any labels. This setting is closer to the conditions of a deployed BCI than the zero-shot and batch evaluations in current use. We evaluate it with a protocol in which queries arrive one at a time, with unknown and possibly unequal frequencies, and each query is decoded before it is used for calibration. In this setting, we introduce GALA : GAllery-Level Alignment, a label-free calibration method which registers the unlabeled EEG embeddings onto the gallery through shrinkage whitening, hubness correction and a Sinkhorn--Procrustes alignment with query frequencies estimated from the buffer, updated after every query. On THINGS-EEG-2, with a gallery of 200 images, it raises the top-1 accuracy on a new subject from 28% to 67% over 53 minutes of use. Across 60 evaluation settings that vary the gallery size, the query frequencies and the number of repetitions averaged per query, GALA is the most accurate label-free method in every setting, 6.6 points above the best competing method on average at the end of the stream.

title: OmegaHyper: Explicit-State HyperLTL Model Checking on an omega-Automaton Diet
authors: Hugo Pacheco
abstract: HyperLTL extends LTL with quantification over traces. AUtoHyper is the de facto explicit-state model checker for HyperLTL, complete for an arbitrary quantifier prefix: it eliminates quantifiers through products of the formula's omega-automaton with the systems, complementing on quantifier alternations. However, it suffers from state explosion, as it fully materializes input systems and intermediate automata. We present OmegaHyper, an overhaul of AutoHyper that keeps its algorithm but decomposes and reduces the size of the processed automata, and integrates the Kofola omega-automaton complementation tool. We compare OmegaHyper with existing explicit-state and symbolic HyperLTL model checkers, on 120 benchmarks from their published suites. OmegaHyper improves the performance of explicit-state HyperLTL model checking by up to orders of magnitude; bounded symbolic tools still reach further on violated instances with short counterexamples, as expected.

title: Conditional What-If Generation for Radio Access Network Energy under Rare and Unseen Contexts
authors: Kevin Wardakhan, Marie Line Alberi-Morel, Jérémie Leguay, Afef Feki, Adrien Sardi, Sébastien Archeveque, Claudiu Mihailescu
abstract: Energy-saving mechanisms in RANs must balance energy reduction and network performance under varying traffic conditions. Conditional generative models support what-if analysis by generating plausible power-consumption trajectories for radio configurations and operating scenarios, helping operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment. However, representative measurements are costly and operationally constrained, so historical data cover only limited configurations and conditions, leaving some contexts poorly represented or unseen during training. In this paper, we study conditional generation of RAN power-consumption trajectories under decreasing training coverage, from well-represented to rare and unseen configurations. We first introduce a context-normalized conditional generator combining temporally aligned conditioning with configuration-dependent target normalization. It improves generation for well-represented configurations but becomes less reliable as training exposure decreases because target consumption is harder to estimate. We therefore introduce a prediction-based generative framework that decomposes power consumption into global prediction, residual level and scale correction, and temporal residual generation. Experiments on a commercial 5G RAN and a public dataset show that hardware metadata provides transferable information about residual scale, while limited target observations at inference improve generation through residual-level correction without retraining. An ablation study confirms that residual-level correction provides most of the gain. Both approaches outperform state-of-the-art methods for well-represented configurations, while the prediction-based approach also generalizes to rare and unseen contexts and, with one target observation, reduces median MAE by about 50% compared with TimeWeaver.
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Submitted for publication

title: DetailScale-SR: Decoupling Restoration and Continuous Detail Control for Real-World Super-Resolution
authors: Shengchuan Gao, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen, Jingjing Chen
abstract: Real-world image super-resolution often seeks the most detailed plausible reconstruction, although more detail is not always desirable. The same degraded image may require restrained restoration, faithful reconstruction, or enhanced visual detail according to user intent. We present DetailScale-SR, a preference-conditioned framework that continuously controls reconstructed detail for a fixed low-resolution input without altering the scene being restored. Rather than relying on post-processing or repeatedly rewriting prompts, it learns a continuous family of reconstructions while separating content recovery from detail preference. This enables a smooth transition from conservative restoration to richly textured results under consistent input and semantic constraints. Its controllable range also extends beyond conventional restoration: DetailScale-SR can enhance high-frequency structures and generate perceptually richer textures than the paired high-resolution reference. Text restoration is another distinct strength. For text-rich scenes, especially Chinese posters and signs, it recovers more legible and character-faithful text than prior generative SR methods under matched textual guidance. DetailScale-SR therefore unifies continuous detail control, beyond-reference enhancement, and reliable recovery of semantically important content. Our model is available at https://modelscope.cn/models/DiffSynth-Studio/Qwen-Image-2.1-SR

title: Continuous Noisy-Loop Models
authors: An T. Le
abstract: Efficient learning and inference need not imply a compact probabilistic circuit. We quantify this distinction for continuous noisy readings of agreement between adjacent latent spins on a known square grid with $d$ edges. With known margins and bounded Lipschitz channels, minimax squared Hellinger risk is $Θ(\min\{1,dN^{-2/3}\})$ from $N$ independent vectors, without a reliability lower bound. A spline estimator reaches this rate in polynomial arithmetic time given a fixed positive reliability bound; an exponential-size mixture removes that requirement. At fixed positive reliability, nonnegative decomposable circuits need $\exp(Θ(\sqrt d))$ nodes for fixed total-variation error below one, even when each leaf uses at most $αd$ coordinates, $0<α<1$. Optimal Kullback--Leibler (KL) approximation error is $Θ(d/\max\{\log d,\sqrt\ell\})$ in either direction with at most $d^r$ nodes and leaf scopes $\ell\leqαd$, for fixed $r>1$ and $0<α<2/3$. Node counts exclude leaf computation. For three fixed masks, optimal joint conditional KL has order $d/\log d$ when $\ell\leq(\log d)^2$. Local cycle identities relate joint divergence to identifiable channel products and separate weak-channel recovery from density estimation. Factorized evidence preserves a planar zero-field Ising model: given local integrals, exact queries cost $O(d^{3/2})$ arithmetic operations and one root extraction.

title: Expand & Reduce: a Framework Bridging Branch-and-Reduce and Dynamic Programming
authors: Martin Vatshelle, Kenneth Langedal, Ernestine Grossmann
abstract: We introduce expand-and-reduce, a framework that augments classical reduction rules with a new type of optimality-preserving operation, called an expansion rule. While a reduction rule in practice typically makes the instance smaller, an expansion rule may enlarge the instance yet still making progress towards a solution. We present a simple expansion rule called edge expansion for the Maximum Weighted Independent Set (MWIS) problem. It encodes the joint choice of two non-adjacent vertices by adding an edge between them and creating a new vertex representing their union. We prove that the number of edge expansions needed to transform a graph into a clique equals the number of independent sets in the graph minus the number of vertices. We demonstrate that expand-and-reduce, using edge expansion and just two well-known reduction rules, has greater reduction power than a set of 22 commonly used reduction rules for MWIS. Therefore, it can significantly simplify methods that depend on reduction rules. To highlight the practical potential of the expand-and-reduce framework further, we provide an implementation and preliminary results showing that a simple implementation outperforms a far more advanced method for MWIS preprocessing. Moreover, expand-and-reduce can simulate both branching and dynamic-programming-style state construction, yielding exact and fixed-parameter algorithms with matching asymptotic running times. By that, expand-and-reduce offers a unified and conceptually clean perspective on techniques that are usually considered incompatible.
comment: 18 pages, 5 figures. Code and data links included in paper

title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
authors: Johannes Hog, Neeratyoy Mallik, Steven Adriaensen, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Tom Viering, Danny Stoll, Frank Hutter
abstract: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few evaluation datasets leads to systematically over-optimistic performance estimates. We further demonstrate that compute-optimal scaling requires expanding the range of synthetic pretraining dataset sizes alongside model size and training compute. Increasing the maximum numbers of rows and features sampled during pretraining improves performance and produces more predictable scaling trends. These insights guide the training of more efficient TabPFNv2-like models, using the open-source training pipeline of nanoTabPFN.

title: TableControl: Gesture Interaction Through Surface Vibrations
authors: Florian Hettstedt, Andreas Erbslöh, Gregor Schiele
abstract: Integrating gesture sensing into furniture offers a way to interact with digital applications and physical devices through familiar surfaces. We present TableControl, an interactive demonstration of continuous surface-vibration-based gesture recognition with the complete processing pipeline running on a microcontroller. Using four concealed piezoelectric sensors, the system combines signal acquisition and preprocessing with neural event detection and gesture classification. The resulting labels for knock, swipe-up, and swipe-down gestures are transmitted to a host computer without streaming the underlying sensor signals. Visitors explore two example applications through hands-on interaction: an endless runner game and a physical table lamp with on/off and brightness control. A dashboard displays recognized gestures, class probabilities, and processing times.
comment: 4 pages, 3 figures, accepted as demo paper on the ACM ISS

title: The Partially Saturated Cells Method for Complex Moving Geometries in Turbulent Flow Conditions
authors: Philipp Suffa, Harald Koestler, Ulrich Ruede
abstract: We present four application cases to test and validate fluid-structure-interaction models based on the Lattice Boltzmann and the Partially Saturated Cells method (PSM) for turbulent flow conditions. For a flow around a stationary sphere we compare the PSM with direct mapping boundary conditions and achieve good agreement to reference data for Reynolds numbers up to one million. In particular, the model predicts the drag crisis for this case with good accuracy. For a three dimensional airfoil simulation at a Reynolds number of 150000, the PSM predicts the stall angle for a NACA0018 profile with excellent accuracy. For a geometry-resolved stirred tank simulation at a Reynolds number of 29000 the PSM produces the time averaged velocity profiles around the impeller with excellent fidelity. Finally, a wind turbine geometry is resolved with the PSM for a tip Reynolds number of 40000, where thrust and mean velocity in the turbine wake shows excellent agreement with reference data from literature.

title: The Comprehension Gap in LLM-Assisted Software Development: An Experiment
authors: Julian Oertel, Jil Klünder, Regina Hebig
abstract: When LLM tools are pushed beyond their capabilities for software development tasks, developers must be able to step in. However, the comprehension that developers acquire during development might be negatively impacted due to excessive code generation. This could create a cognitive debt that needs to be resolved before tasks can be solved efficiently again. We explore how well developers understand code they generated by prompting in comparison to self-written and unseen code and how they reflect on their comprehension. We conduct a crossover experiment and interviews with 35 participants consisting of students, academic personnel, and software developers. After completing two programming tasks with or without LLM chat usage, respectively, participants are tasked with finding introduced mutations in the produced and additional unseen code. We use insights from interviews and screen recordings to supplement our results. Regarding the experiment, 36% of participants report a better understanding of self-written code compared to their generated code. On average, participants solved the comprehension task 20% faster for self-written code than for generated code and found 11% more mutations. Participants needed significantly less time to solve programming tasks when working with the LLM. However, participants with high reliance on the LLM chat and low task engagement showed significantly decreased comprehension. Our qualitative results show great variability in individual perspectives on comprehension differences and strategies to mitigate issues. Strategies for dealing with comprehension differences range from accepting comprehension differences to adapting their LLM interactions or avoiding the tools altogether. Our results warrant further investigation into cognitive debt in larger systems and developer practices to mitigate issues.

title: Erased but Recoverable: On the Fragility of Concept Erasure Under Fine-Tuning
authors: Jun Li, Lizhi Xiong, Ziqiang Li, Yu Liu, Zenglin Shi
abstract: Existing concept erasure methods for text-to-image diffusion models primarily focus on suppressing target concepts while preserving non-target generation quality. However, in practical applications, open-source diffusion models are often further adapted through DreamBooth, LoRA, or Custom Diffusion. Such adaptations can reshape internal representations, thereby weakening or even reversing the erasure effects achieved by existing methods. We identify erasure persistence as a key yet underexplored dimension of concept erasure and analyze how downstream fine-tuning reshapes internal representations. Our analysis reveals that fine-tuning of the original model does not uniformly modify the model, but preserves certain high-contribution structures, particularly attention heads with stable output subspaces and response magnitudes. We also observe that, after downstream fine-tuning of concept-erased models, these heads' output representations more readily realign with their pretrained counterparts. Motivated by this observation, we propose Stable-Head-Aware Concept Erasure (SHACE), which improves erasure persistence by preserving stable attention structures during concept erasure. SHACE identifies stability-critical attention heads through Attention-Head Stability Profiling and keeps their corresponding parameter blocks unchanged during erasure via Stable-Head Gradient Preservation. Extensive experiments show that SHACE improves resistance to concept recovery across diverse fine-tuning settings while maintaining strong suppression and non-target generation quality.

title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming
authors: Xiaoyang Xing, Wenyu Dai, Xiaoliang Gong, Asoke K Nandi, Anthony Cohn
abstract: Automated red teaming is essential for identifying safety failures in large language models (LLMs), but its practical scalability depends on the resources required to discover those failures. Multi-agent systems can combine complementary capabilities, yet repeated planning, redundant exchanges, and ineffective information routing can make their coordination expensive. Moreover, a target model's response indicates the outcome of a test without identifying which collaboration decision should change. We present Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided framework that evolves an executable multi-agent workflow for each red-teaming case. L2C represents agent responsibilities, execution dependencies, and input bindings in a versioned graph, and associates each graph with records of the information actually delivered and produced. A controller trained through supervised fine-tuning integrates these records with target responses, evaluator verdicts, and remaining budget to retain the workflow, refine instructions, restructure collaboration, or lock further editing. This design connects feedback to explicit changes in subsequent execution while allowing a useful organization to continue without repeated controller intervention. The evaluation protocol covers HarmBench with three execution backbones and two target models, together with component ablations, dataset transfer, and evaluator checks. Across the six executor-target configurations, L2C improves ASR over EvoSynth by 1.4 to 4.5 percentage points while reducing mean online tokens by 35.6% to 37.3%. L2C connects adaptive collaboration to the resource requirements of automated security evaluation.

title: Training Denoising Models of Any Architecture Without Stored Images
authors: Christos Koutlis, Ioannis Kompatsiaris, Symeon Papadopoulos
abstract: Can a pretrained denoising model replace the dataset used to train it? We investigate this question through teacher-supervised training, showing for the first time that continuous-time diffusion and flow models of any architecture and size can be trained from random initialization without stored images. Our students regress the teacher's velocity on a rolling pool of noisy samples, advanced along trajectories of random step counts to obtain independent, dense and approximately continuous noise levels. This saves considerable storage for large datasets and applies even when the data are unreleased or private. Our experiments include 12 teachers of 6 families and 6 datasets. Our method outperforms standard training of the same network on CIFAR-10 for students 4x smaller than the teacher, comes within 0.75 to 1.92 FID of it at the teacher's size and surpasses training on teacher-generated images and step reduction methods without teacher-based initialization. Our code is available at https://github.com/mever-team/ddm.

title: Target-Consistent Action Guidance via Semi-Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Drifting World Models
authors: Md Abtahi Majeed Chowdhury, Md Rifat Ur Rahman, Md Sakib Hossain Shovon, Jaesik Choi, Minhyuk Sung
abstract: Action-conditioned world models let robots imagine the outcomes of their actions for planning and offline policy evaluation, but these uses need many rollouts, which multi-step diffusion makes expensive. Drifting models move the iteration from inference to training and generate samples in one network pass. DriftWorld brought this paradigm to action-conditioned world models; to strengthen action following, it repels predictions from the current frame, a construction borrowed from classifier-free guidance. We show that this accentuation has a target bias: the push persists even when a prediction matches the recorded future, in kernel, balanced, and unbalanced Wasserstein drifting fields alike. We introduce Mass-Share Accentuation (MSA) to remove this bias. MSA treats the current frame as a counterfactual destination competing with the recorded future in a semi-relaxed optimal transport problem; subtracting the closed-form share of the correct future makes the guidance vanish at the target, and the remainder is shared by all predictions. We prove that the recorded future is the unique fixed point along the motion direction for collapsed predictions, and that the guidance fades with prediction error. On Push-T, Robomimic, and BridgeV2, where trained models under-react rather than overshoot, MSA improves action ranking, response slope, and moving-region error over latent-space baselines at no inference cost, though these benchmarks do not isolate bias removal as the cause.

title: ProbeShare: Probing a Few, Sharing Across Many for Fast World-Model Planning
authors: Zejian Kang, Xiantao Lin, Zekai Chen, Boyang Shen, Mingyu Ma, Shengwen Zheng, Chengtai Guo, Xiangru Huang
abstract: Visual planning with a frozen joint-embedding world model supports robotic reaching and object manipulation by evaluating candidate action sequences against an image goal before execution. Standard cross-entropy method (CEM) planners roll out every candidate independently through a billion-parameter predictor, even when nearby actions induce similar scene changes. This redundant computation grows with population size and search rounds, slowing closed-loop replanning. We observe that candidates within a planning step share an observation history and thus a common action-to-feature map. Based on this insight, we propose ProbeShare, which measures local responses with a few representative probes and reconstructs each candidate's feature grid through scene-conditioned, geometry-aware weighting. When promising candidates move beyond existing probe coverage, ProbeShare evaluates a new probe to rescore nearby candidates. Across four RoboCasa tasks, ProbeShare accelerates episode planning by 43.8--128.9 times over dense RoboJEPA and at least $14.2\times$ over competitive baselines, with greater mean goal progress in a matched-time comparison.

title: Neural Network-Based In-Contact Task Segmentation of Demonstrated Robot Motions via Hand Guiding
authors: Johannes Hartwig, Marcello Kögler, Dominik Henrich
abstract: Intuitive robot programming approaches, such as Programming by Demonstration, enable non-experts to teach robots tasks through hand-guided demonstrations. However, for in-contact tasks requiring force control for parts of the motion, automated segmentation of motion types is crucial for improving usability. Considering the related work, this work proposes a neural network-based segmentation method categorizing motion into three fundamental types using input data of cartesian twists and wrenches at the end effector. We collect demonstration data using a 7-axis robot with a wrist-mounted force torque sensor and generate ground truth labeling by hand. While still in development, our research direction aims to enable non-experts to program in-contact tasks more intuitively.
comment: Extended abstract, accepted and presented at the 1st German Robotics Conference (GRC 2025), Nuremberg, 13-15 March 2025; no official proceedings, not peer-reviewed; see also https://eref.uni-bayreuth.de/id/eprint/94264

title: Canonical Proof Nets for Intuitionistic Multiplicative Linear Logic
authors: Matteo Acclavio, Willem Heijltjes, Dominic J. D. Hughes
abstract:
We study the problem of finding canonical representations of proofs in the multiplicative fragment of intuitionistic linear logic with units.
  We show that, contrary to the classical case, it is possible to define a notion of proof nets for this fragment which is provided with a polynomial-time sequentialization procedure and is both canonical and efficient. In particular, we show that sequent calculus derivations differing only by a permutation of independent rule applications are translated to the same proof net, and that the translations between sequent calculus and proof nets are inverse to each other.

title: Psychometrics-Inspired Coreset Selection for Image Quality Assessment
authors: Susu Jiang, Xuelin Shen, Baoliang Chen
abstract: Collecting large-scale subjective annotations remains a critical bottleneck in training accurate image quality assessment (IQA) models. Coreset selection reduces this burden by selecting representative images before annotation. However, diversity in a visual feature space does not necessarily reflect diversity in perceptual quality, raising a fundamental question about which quality-related factors the representation should encode. We propose GRAM, a quality-aware representation learning framework inspired by the graded response model (GRM) from psychometrics. GRM describes how an individual's latent ability determines the probabilities of reaching successive assessment grades, with response sensitivity and grade thresholds governing this relationship. In this paper, we find that this principle naturally aligns with perceptual quality assessment, where the impact of image degradation depends on image content and distortion characteristics. Building on this connection, GRAM models quality judgments through three complementary factors: latent quality, content-dependent response sensitivity, and distortion-dependent grade thresholds. These factors jointly determine the probabilities of attaining different quality grades and the resulting expected quality score. The learned parameters provide a structured quality-aware representation that complements general visual features for coreset selection. Experiments on nine datasets demonstrate improvements across different selection strategies, downstream IQA models, and annotation budgets. The code will be made publicly available.

title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
authors: Haoyang Liu, Yinong Xu, Zhe Lang, Zhenyu Guan, Qianyun Zhang
abstract: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-borne replacement at 77.96\%. Protection also depends on target type, rendering settings, wording, and repetition, and a search over eight fixed attack candidates largely closes the image deficit in appending and formatting for Qwen and Gemini, though not for GPT-5-nano. Utility ratios on original questions range from 93.31\% to 101.61\%, but Qwen falls to 61.99\% when answers combine two evidence spans. Illegibility cannot explain all failed attacks: models often transcribe and identify image-borne commands they do not execute, and trusted user authorization raises execution on unchanged pages. Inside Qwen, patching early attack-region states induces all three operations, more weakly in images. Attention blocking suggests why: a text command acts through its own positions, whereas visual encoding spreads an image command and its target across the instruction page. Rendering thus offers conditional protection, motivating evaluations that report security by model, operation, and attack budget alongside utility.

title: Hardware Acceleration of Vision-Language-Action Models with Weight Precision Rising over the Flow Steps
authors: Robin Geens, Simon Haepers, Jonas Crols, Chao Fang, Marian Verhelst
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models such as GR00T control robots through an action head: a diffusion transformer that turns noise into a chunk of actions in a few flow-matching steps. Every step re-reads all of the head's weights from DRAM but applies each weight to only about fifty tokens. Inference is therefore memory-bound, and its latency and energy are largely determined by the total number of transferred weight bits. We show that later flow steps attenuate the quantization errors of earlier steps, so the weight precision of an action head should rise over the steps. With plain per-channel rounding and without calibration or training, widths rising over the steps from 2 to 4 bits preserve the closed-loop success of robot policies. These widths transfer 25% fewer bits than 4-bit weights at every step. However, we show that on Jetson AGX Thor, current GPU kernels cannot exploit this per-step precision due to fixed overheads. We therefore present a programmable accelerator whose latency and energy both scale with the transferred weight bits. It decodes entropy-coded weights for bit-serial sub-arrays at the DRAM rate. Because the width changes per step, a run-time allocator divides these sub-arrays between the linear layers and the attention to balance their workloads. The same sub-arrays are thus capable of running action heads of different families and sizes, as well as a vision-language model. On the DRAM side, a requantizer and an entropy encoder at each bank let one stored 8-bit copy replace the copies of all widths. Simulated with LPDDR5X timing, our RTL implementation runs the GR00T N1.6 action head in 8.02 ms per inference with 2, 3, 3 and 4 bits in its four flow steps. With a copy per width and 50% of Thor's memory bandwidth, the accelerator runs this schedule 1.7x faster than Thor in NVFP4, at 9.1x less energy and equal closed-loop success.

title: Approximation Algorithms for Product Query Optimization
authors: Macéo Ottavy, Avijeet Ghosh, Pascal Koiran, Alantha Newman, François Schwarzentruber, Blair D. Sullivan, Stéphan Thomassé
abstract: We study database query optimization for Cartesian products. This problem is equivalent to finding an optimal plan for multiplying non-negative integers. We call this problem multiplication ordering. We show that the problem has an FPTAS when the cost of a plan is the sum of all intermediate products; both in the case when the overall final product is counted and when it is not. We show that using the optimal solution to the well-known product partition problem does not always lead to an optimal plan, but we establish connections between the product partition and multiplication ordering problems. Finally, we prove that multiplication ordering is in PTIME (resp. \NP-complete) when integers are powers of a same base where the exponents are written in unary (resp. in binary).
zh_title: 乘积查询优化的近似算法
translation: 我们研究了笛卡尔积的数据库查询优化。该问题等价于寻找非负整数相乘的最优计划，我们称该问题为乘法排序。我们证明了当计划的成本为所有中间乘积之和时（无论最终总乘积是否被计入），该问题均存在完全多项式时间近似方案（FPTAS）。我们证明了使用著名的乘积划分问题的最优解并不总能得到最优计划，但我们建立了乘积划分与乘法排序问题之间的联系。最后，我们证明了当整数为同一基数的幂时，若指数以一进制表示，则乘法排序属于PTIME；若以二进制表示，则该问题是NP完全的。
tldr: 本文研究了笛卡尔积查询优化（乘法排序问题），提出了FPTAS近似算法，并刻画了其在不同指数编码下的多项式时间与NP完全性复杂度。
ai_comments: 本文将数据库中基础的笛卡尔积查询优化问题形式化为整数相乘的乘法排序问题，具有很强的理论创新性与形式化美感。论文不仅给出了强有力的FPTAS近似算法，还深刻揭示了数字编码方式（一进制与二进制）对计算复杂度界限的影响，为查询执行计划生成理论提供了坚实的计算复杂性基础。
motivation: 研究数据库中笛卡尔积的查询优化，该问题在数学上等价于寻找非负整数相乘的最优执行计划（即乘法排序问题）。
method: 将笛卡尔积查询优化规约为乘法排序问题；针对中间乘积和成本设计FPTAS算法；建立乘积划分问题与乘法排序的联系；利用同底数幂及其指数编码（一进制与二进制）进行计算复杂度分析。
results: 证明了在成本为中间乘积总和（无论是否包含最终乘积）时存在FPTAS；指出乘积划分问题的最优解不总能得出乘法排序的最优解，但证明了二者的内在联系；证明了当整数为同底数的幂且指数用一进制（unary）表示时属于PTIME，用二进制（binary）表示时为NP完全。
conclusion: 乘法排序问题在以中间乘积之和为成本度量时具备FPTAS近似算法；同时，其精确求解复杂度在输入指数采用一进制和二进制表示时分别属于PTIME和NP完全。

title: ViLFlow: Parallel Vision-Language Generation with Continuous Latent Flows
authors: Kevin Zhai, Bian Sun, Zhenyi Wang, Song Wang
abstract: Vision-language generation has predominantly relied on autoregressive and discrete diffusion models. Autoregressive models generate tokens sequentially, while discrete diffusion models typically predict tokens independently within each denoising step. We propose ViLFlow (Vision-Language Flow), a continuous-flow vision-language model that combines joint modeling of output embeddings with parallel token decoding. ViLFlow adapts pretrained continuous language generation to visual question answering and image captioning through learned image guidance and prediction-aware token decoding. A visually adapted teacher provides image-guided predictions as additional denoising supervision. The denoiser learns to reproduce these predictions directly, retaining one image-conditioned prediction per generation step. We train the token decoder on denoiser predictions and paired reference text to improve the conversion of continuous outputs into words. The decoder can be adapted independently, improving answering and captioning without further denoiser training. For captioning, it also supplies text feedback during late denoising, allowing decoded words to inform subsequent refinement. ViLFlow outperforms autoregressive and masked-diffusion baselines by up to 8.46 percentage points on VQAv2 and 4.50 points on GQA without GQA training. On COCO Karpathy test, it improves CIDEr by 16.25 over masked diffusion and 17.81 over sampled autoregression.
zh_title: ViLFlow：基于连续潜在流的并行视觉-语言生成
translation: 视觉-语言生成主要依赖于自回归模型和离散扩散模型。自回归模型按顺序逐个生成词元，而离散扩散模型通常在每个去噪步骤内独立预测词元。我们提出了 ViLFlow（视觉-语言流），这是一种连续流视觉-语言模型，它将输出嵌入的联合建模与并行词元解码相结合。ViLFlow 通过学习到的图像引导和预测感知词元解码，将预训练的连续语言生成适配到视觉问答和图像描述任务中。一个视觉自适应的教师模型提供图像引导的预测作为额外的去噪监督。去噪器学习直接复现这些预测，并在每个生成步骤中保留一个基于图像条件的预测。我们在去噪器预测和成对参考文本上训练词元解码器，以改善连续输出向词语的转换。该解码器可以独立进行调整，无需进一步训练去噪器即可改善问答和描述性能。对于图像描述，它还在去噪后期提供文本反馈，允许解码后的词语指导后续的细化。ViLFlow 在 VQAv2 上比自回归和掩码扩散基线高出多达 8.46 个百分点，在未经 GQA 训练的情况下在 GQA 上高出 4.50 个百分点。在 COCO Karpathy 测试集上，其 CIDEr 得分比掩码扩散提高了 16.25，比采样自回归提高了 17.81。
tldr: ViLFlow 提出了一种基于连续潜在流的并行视觉-语言生成模型，通过联合建模连续表征与预测感知解码，在 VQA 和图像描述任务上大幅超越自回归与离散扩散模型。
ai_comments: 该研究的创新之处在于突破了传统的自回归与离散扩散范式，首次将连续流生成模型应用于视觉-语言多模态任务，通过输出嵌入联合建模实现了高效的并行生成。此外，教师去噪监督与后期文本反馈机制的设计进一步强化了图文多模态特征的对齐。其局限在于摘要未提供推理延迟和采样步数的具体比较，连续流迭代的实际计算开销仍有待结合实际场景评估。
motivation: 现有的视觉-语言生成模型主要受限于两类范式：自回归模型需要严格串行生成词元导致效率受限，而离散扩散模型在每个去噪步骤中通常独立预测词元，难以充分对输出嵌入进行联合建模。
method: ViLFlow 基于连续流架构实现输出嵌入的联合建模与并行词元解码。主要方法包括：1）利用视觉自适应教师模型提供图像引导的预测作为额外的去噪监督，使去噪器直接复现该预测；2）构建预测感知词元解码器，利用去噪预测和参考文本进行训练，该解码器支持独立适配与微调；3）在图像描述任务中，解码器在去噪后期提供文本反馈，利用已解码词元指导后续特征细化。
results: 在 VQAv2 数据集上，ViLFlow 比自回归和掩码扩散基线高出最多 8.46 个百分点；在未经 GQA 训练的情况下，在 GQA 上提升 4.50 个百分点；在 COCO Karpathy 测试集上，其 CIDEr 得分比掩码扩散模型提高 16.25，比采样自回归模型提高 17.81。
conclusion: ViLFlow 证明了通过结合连续潜在流建模、并行词元解码、图像引导监督以及预测感知解码器，能够在无需自回归逐词生成的情况下大幅提升多模态文本生成质量，显著超越现有自回归和掩码扩散基线。

title: From a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$:$C_2$ leads to a Holant dichotomy
authors: Yuxuan Zhou
abstract:
Counting complexity within the Holant framework has been extensively studied through complexity dichotomy theorems. While substantial progress has been achieved for various restricted settings, the general complex-valued even-arity case without auxiliary unary signatures remains largely open. This paper studies a fundamental case in this program where the binary signatures induce a group structure satisfying \(M(B(\mathcal{F}))\cong C_2\). It is observed that projective equivalence classes of binary signature matrices naturally embed into finite subgroups of \(SO(3)\), providing an algebraic viewpoint for structural classification. This paper further identifies two fundamentally different regimes for the \(C_2\) case, namely the normal and isotropic cases, and analyzes their complexity behavior separately.
  Combining gadget constructions, decomposition techniques, interpolation arguments, and a realnumberization approach that transforms the complex-valued setting into an equivalent real-structured framework, this paper establishes a complete dichotomy theorem: for every even-arity signature set \(\mathcal{F}\) satisfying \(M(\B(\mathcal{F}))\cong C_2\), the problem \(\mathrm{Holant}(\mathcal{F})\) is either polynomial-time computable or \#P-hard. A Pauli-basis representation for signatures is further introduced as an algebraically natural language for organizing realizable signatures and revealing structural relations that are less transparent in the standard basis.

title: End-to-End Landsat Land Surface Temperature Reconstruction with AlphaEarth Embeddings
authors: Shengjie Liu
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) data at Landsat's 30 m resolution is important for many applications, but cloud contamination prevents its spatially continuous observations. Here, we propose A$^2$E$^2$, an end-to-end U-Net that integrates annual temperature cycle (ATC), coarse LST from Earth system modeling, and AlphaEarth embeddings for Landsat LST reconstruction. The ATC supplies a physics-guided thermal prior, the coarse LST provides a temporal background, and the U-Net converts the embedding field into day-specific fine-scale correction using observed pixels. Experimental results on four seasonally distributed Landsat 8/9 scenes over New York City in 2022 show that A$^2$E$^2$ achieves 0.78 K mean absolute error and 1.01 K root mean squared error, reducing error by 60.1% relative to baseline method without spatial correction and by 3.7% relative to the same U-Net guided by annual mean spectral reflectance. Sensitivity analysis shows stable performance regardless of distance to clear pixels and percentage of blocked pixels. Independent validation with ECOSTRESS LST shows that Earth foundation model embeddings have better performance than annual mean spectral bands for LST reconstruction.
zh_title: 基于AlphaEarth嵌入的端到端Landsat地表温度重建
translation: Landsat 30米分辨率的地表温度（LST）数据对于许多应用非常重要，但云层污染阻碍了其空间连续观测。在此，我们提出了A^2E^2，这是一个端到端的U-Net，它集成了年温度循环（ATC）、来自地球系统建模的粗分辨率LST以及用于Landsat LST重建的AlphaEarth嵌入。ATC提供了物理引导的热先验，粗分辨率LST提供了时间背景，U-Net利用观测像素将嵌入场转换为特定日期的精细尺度校正。对2022年纽约市四个季节分布的Landsat 8/9场景的实验结果表明，A^2E^2实现了0.78 K的平均绝对误差和1.01 K的均方根误差，与没有空间校正的基线方法相比，误差减少了60.1%，与由年平均光谱反射率引导的相同U-Net相比，误差减少了3.7%。敏感性分析表明，无论距离清晰像素的距离和受阻像素的百分比如何，性能都保持稳定。与ECOSTRESS LST的独立验证表明，地球基础模型嵌入在LST重建方面比年平均光谱波段具有更好的性能。
tldr: 本文提出了一种名为A^2E^2的端到端深度学习方法，利用AlphaEarth嵌入和物理先验实现了高分辨率Landsat地表温度的无云重建。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将AlphaEarth嵌入（Earth foundation model embeddings）与物理驱动的年温度循环（ATC）和粗分辨率LST相结合，通过端到端的U-Net架构实现了高分辨率Landsat地表温度的无云重建。实验证明其在精度和鲁棒性上均有显著提升。
motivation: Landsat 30米分辨率的地表温度（LST）数据对许多应用至关重要，但云层污染导致其无法进行空间连续观测，因此需要高精度的LST重建方法。
method: 提出了一种名为A^2E^2的端到端U-Net模型，整合了年温度循环（ATC）提供的物理热先验、来自地球系统建模的粗分辨率LST作为时间背景，以及AlphaEarth嵌入，利用观测像素将嵌入场转换为特定日期的精细尺度校正。
results: 在纽约市2022年四个季节分布的Landsat 8/9场景上的实验表明，A^2E^2实现了0.78 K的平均绝对误差和1.01 K的均方根误差，较无空间校正的基线方法误差减少了60.1%，较基于年平均光谱反射率的U-Net误差减少了3.7%。同时，敏感性分析显示出对不同遮挡比例和距离的稳定性能。
conclusion: A^2E^2模型能够有效利用AlphaEarth嵌入和物理先验进行Landsat地表温度重建，表现出极高的准确性和对缺失像素的鲁棒性，优于传统的基于光谱反射率的方法。

title: CommDreamer: Radio-Geometric World Models for Mapless Cellular-Connected UAV Trajectory Planning
authors: Yuqi Ping, Tianhao Liang, Tingting Zhang
abstract: Reliable cellular connectivity and collision-free flight are essential for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations in low-altitude urban canyons, where dense 3D buildings obstruct flight clearance, shadow serving base stations, and create strong co-channel interference at street intersections. Existing planners either require prior 3D city meshes and channel knowledge maps unavailable onboard, or rely on model-free reinforcement learning with low sample efficiency and poor cross-city generalization. We propose CommDreamer, a mapless radio-geometric world model that fuses raw onboard 3D LiDAR scans, multicell cellular reports, and shift-invariant relative kinematics to jointly infer local obstacle clearance and directional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) dynamics. Using a categorical recurrent state-space model, CommDreamer compresses multimodal measurement histories into a coordinate-invariant latent belief, enabling the UAV to foresee deep shadow zones and train a lightweight online policy purely via multi-step latent imagination without prior maps or antenna patterns. Zero-shot evaluations across unseen urban morphologies in our open-source ray-tracing simulator, AeroCity-RT, show that CommDreamer converges within 150 episodes where model-free reinforcement learning fails to complete flights, achieving 100.0% mission success with zero collisions while lifting median route SINR to 8.02 dB and cutting effective SINR outage by over 50% relative to radio-blind world-model and reactive LiDAR baselines.
zh_title: CommDreamer：用于无地图蜂窝连接无人机轨迹规划的无线电几何世界模型
translation:
**CommDreamer：用于无地图蜂窝连接无人机轨迹规划的无线电几何世界模型**

在低空城市峡谷中，可靠的蜂窝连接和无碰撞飞行对于无人机（UAV）操作至关重要，这些区域密集的3D建筑会阻碍飞行、遮蔽服务基站，并在街道交叉口产生强烈的同频干扰。现有的规划器要么需要机载不可用的预先3D城市网格和信道知识图，要么依赖于样本效率低且跨城市泛化能力差的模型无关强化学习。我们提出了CommDreamer，一个无地图的无线电几何世界模型，它融合了原始机载3D LiDAR扫描、多小区蜂窝报告和平移不变相对运动学，以联合推断局部障碍物清除和定向信号干扰加噪声比（SINR）动态。CommDreamer使用分类递归状态空间模型，将多模态测量历史压缩成坐标不变的潜在信念，使无人机能够预见深层阴影区域，并纯粹通过多步潜在想象训练轻量级在线策略，无需预先地图或天线模式。在我们的开源光线追踪模拟器AeroCity-RT中，对未见城市形态进行零样本评估显示，CommDreamer在150个回合内收敛，而模型无关强化学习未能完成飞行，实现了100.0%的任务成功率和零碰撞，同时将中位路线SINR提升至8.02 dB，并将有效SINR中断降低了50%以上，优于无线电盲世界模型和反应式LiDAR基线。
tldr: CommDreamer是一个无地图的无线电几何世界模型，通过融合激光雷达扫描和蜂窝报告来预测障碍物和信号质量，从而实现蜂窝连接无人机在城市峡谷中的碰撞避免和可靠通信轨迹规划，表现优于现有方法。
ai_comments: CommDreamer的创新之处在于其构建了一个无地图的无线电几何世界模型，能够联合感知障碍物和预测无线电信号质量，这对于在复杂城市环境中运行的蜂窝连接无人机至关重要。通过利用潜在想象进行在线策略训练，它避免了对预先地图和大量样本的需求，解决了现有方法的关键局限性。其在零样本评估中的出色表现证明了其在实际应用中的潜力和泛化能力。
motivation: 现有无人机轨迹规划器在城市峡谷中面临挑战，因为需要预先的3D城市网格和信道知识图（通常不可用），或依赖于样本效率低、泛化能力差的模型无关强化学习。在低空城市峡谷中，可靠的蜂窝连接和无碰撞飞行对于无人机操作至关重要，但密集的3D建筑会阻碍飞行、遮蔽基站并产生强干扰。
method: 本文提出了CommDreamer，一个无地图的无线电几何世界模型。它融合了原始机载3D LiDAR扫描、多小区蜂窝报告和平移不变相对运动学，以联合推断局部障碍物清除和定向信号干扰加噪声比（SINR）动态。CommDreamer使用分类递归状态空间模型，将多模态测量历史压缩成坐标不变的潜在信念，使无人机能够预见深层阴影区域，并通过多步潜在想象训练轻量级在线策略，无需预先地图或天线模式。
results: 在开源光线追踪模拟器AeroCity-RT中，对未见城市形态进行零样本评估显示，CommDreamer在150个回合内收敛，而模型无关强化学习未能完成飞行。它实现了100.0%的任务成功率和零碰撞，同时将中位路线SINR提升至8.02 dB，并将有效SINR中断降低了50%以上，优于无线电盲世界模型和反应式LiDAR基线。
conclusion: CommDreamer通过其无地图的无线电几何世界模型，显著提高了蜂窝连接无人机在复杂城市环境中的轨迹规划能力，实现了高任务成功率、零碰撞和优化的蜂窝连接，解决了现有方法的局限性。

title: PMKPIR: Parallel Multi-Keyword PIR with Interleaved Batching for Private Boolean Retrieval
authors: Rongxi Wang, Guanxiong Ha, Chunfu Jia, Minfen Gao, Hanmiaomiao Wang
abstract: Keyword Private Information Retrieval (Keyword PIR) allows users to retrieve data associated with specific keywords from a database while protecting query privacy. However, existing Keyword PIR schemes supporting boolean retrieval either incur high computational overhead due to multiple database traversals, or fail to support universal boolean computation. We propose PMKPIR, a novel keyword PIR scheme supporting both parallel multi-keyword queries and universal boolean computation. We utilize the single instruction multiple data (SIMD) capability of BFV homomorphic encryption to propose an interleaved batching method, and design IBPIR based on this method, achieving the private matching of multiple keywords in a single database traversal. Furthermore, we design a boolean query processing method, extending the parallel capability of interleaved batching from keyword querying to boolean query computation, to support universal boolean computation and accelerate boolean operations. Building upon IBPIR, we integrate this method to further design PMKPIR. To the best of our knowledge, PMKPIR is the first Keyword PIR scheme to support multi-keyword batch matching within boolean queries. Security analysis demonstrates that, consistent with existing PIR schemes supporting boolean retrieval, PMKPIR preserves the core security guarantees of classic PIR. Compared with state-of-the-art schemes, PMKPIR reduces query time, communication overhead, storage overhead, and peak memory by up to 79.06%, 75.00%, 97.92%, and 80.26%, respectively.
zh_title: PMKPIR: 采用交错批处理的并行多关键词PIR，用于私有布尔检索
translation: 关键词私有信息检索（Keyword PIR）允许用户在保护查询隐私的同时从数据库中检索与特定关键词相关的数据。然而，现有的支持布尔检索的关键词PIR方案要么由于多次数据库遍历而产生高计算开销，要么无法支持通用的布尔计算。我们提出了PMKPIR，一种新颖的关键词PIR方案，支持并行多关键词查询和通用布尔计算。我们利用BFV同态加密的单指令多数据（SIMD）能力，提出了一种交错批处理方法，并在此方法的基础上设计了IBPIR，实现了单次数据库遍历中的多个关键词的私有匹配。此外，我们设计了一种布尔查询处理方法，将交错批处理的并行能力从关键词查询扩展到布尔查询计算，以支持通用布尔计算并加速布尔操作。在IBPIR的基础上，我们整合此方法进一步设计了PMKPIR。据我们所知，PMKPIR是第一个在布尔查询中支持多关键词批量匹配的关键词PIR方案。安全分析表明，与现有支持布尔检索的PIR方案一致，PMKPIR保留了经典PIR的核心安全保障。与最先进的方案相比，PMKPIR在查询时间、通信开销、存储开销和峰值内存方面分别降低了高达79.06%、75.00%、97.92%和80.26%。
tldr: PMKPIR是一种新的关键词PIR方案，利用BFV同态加密的SIMD能力和交错批处理，实现了单次数据库遍历中的多关键词私有匹配和通用的布尔查询计算，显著降低了查询时间、通信、存储和内存开销。
ai_comments: PMKPIR的创新点在于结合了BFV同态加密的SIMD能力和独创的交错批处理方法，实现了多关键词的单次遍历私有匹配，并首次将这种并行能力扩展到通用布尔查询中。这不仅解决了现有方案的效率瓶颈，也拓宽了关键词PIR的应用范围，特别是在隐私保护的数据检索领域具有重要意义。其显著的性能提升证明了该方法的有效性。
motivation: 现有的支持布尔检索的关键词PIR方案要么由于多次数据库遍历导致高计算开销，要么无法支持通用的布尔计算。
method: 提出PMKPIR方案，其核心是利用BFV同态加密的SIMD能力和交错批处理方法。设计了IBPIR，通过单次数据库遍历实现多关键词私有匹配。进一步设计了布尔查询处理方法，将交错批处理的并行能力扩展到布尔查询计算，以支持通用布尔计算并加速布尔操作。将此方法集成到IBPIR中以设计PMKPIR。
results: PMKPIR是第一个支持布尔查询中多关键词批量匹配的关键词PIR方案。安全分析表明它保留了经典PIR的核心安全保障。相比现有方案，PMKPIR在查询时间、通信开销、存储开销和峰值内存方面分别降低了高达79.06%、75.00%、97.92%和80.26%。
conclusion: PMKPIR通过引入交错批处理和并行布尔查询处理，显著提高了关键词PIR方案的效率，同时支持多关键词和通用布尔检索，填补了现有方案的空白。

title: Allocentric Memory, Egocentric Acting: A Dual-Frame VLA for Urban Aerial Navigation
authors: Haotian Xu, Yue Hu, Zhengqiu Zhu, Tuo Feng, Wenguan Wang, Quanjun Yin
abstract: Language-goal aerial navigation requires a UAV to reach a destination specified in natural language using observations collected during flight. A key challenge is linking changing egocentric perception with spatial evidence anchored to stable locations for long-range navigation. We propose CityNav-VLA, a dual-frame vision-language-action model for urban navigation integrating dynamic egocentric context with persistent allocentric spatial memory. The UAV incrementally accumulates visual observations on a fixed north-up map initialized with geographic and landmark priors, preserving evidence across viewpoint changes. A dynamic query conditioned on the instruction, current observations, UAV state, and motion history retrieves relevant memory evidence to predict a map-frame target. A deterministic controller converts this target into body-frame commands using the UAV's current pose, connecting global reasoning with egocentric execution. To reduce target fluctuations over long horizons, early goal commitment (EGC) fixes the execution target to the coordinate-wise median of the first $K$ predictions without extra trainable parameters. On Test Unseen, CityNav-VLA reduces NE by 21.2% and improves SR and SPL by 15.8% and 30.9%, respectively. It also reduces NE by 6.2% and improves SR and SPL by 5.6% and 23.2%, respectively, relative to the former SOTA after dataset refinement. Cumulative ablations show that navigation-map features yield the largest gains, while metric coordinates further improve endpoint accuracy. With a 4B-scale backbone, inference averages 0.68 s per decision with 8.6 GB peak memory on a single A100, presenting remarkable model efficiency.
zh_title: 以自我中心行为进行异位记忆：一种用于城市空中导航的双帧VLA
translation: 语言目标空中导航要求无人机使用飞行中收集的观测数据到达自然语言指定的目标。一个关键挑战是如何将变化的自我中心感知与锚定在稳定位置的空间证据联系起来，以实现长距离导航。我们提出了CityNav-VLA，一个用于城市导航的双帧视觉-语言-动作模型，它整合了动态自我中心上下文和持久的异位空间记忆。无人机在一个初始化有地理和地标先验知识的固定北向上地图上逐步积累视觉观测，从而在视角变化时保留证据，即使在视点变化时也能保持证据。一个根据指令、当前观测、无人机状态和运动历史动态查询的模块，检索相关的记忆证据以预测地图坐标系目标。一个确定性控制器利用无人机当前姿态将此目标转换为机体坐标系指令，连接全局推理与自我中心执行。为减少长距离目标波动，早期目标承诺（EGC）机制将执行目标固定为前K个预测的坐标中位数，无需额外可训练参数。在Test Unseen数据集上，CityNav-VLA将NE降低了21.2%，SR和SPL分别提高了15.8%和30.9%。相对于数据集精炼后的前SOTA，它还分别将NE降低了6.2%，将SR和SPL提高了5.6%和23.2%。累积消融实验表明，导航地图特征带来了最大的增益，而度量坐标进一步提高了端点精度。采用4B规模骨干网络时，在单个A100上，每次决策的推理平均耗时0.68秒，峰值内存为8.6 GB，模型效率显著。
tldr: CityNav-VLA是一个双帧视觉-语言-动作模型，通过结合异位记忆和自我中心执行，显著提高了城市空中导航的性能和效率。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一个双帧VLA模型，有效地解决了城市空中导航中自我中心感知与异位空间记忆的融合问题，这对于长距离和复杂环境下的导航至关重要。其引入的早期目标承诺（EGC）机制，无需额外训练参数即可稳定长期目标，是一个巧妙且高效的设计。模型在性能提升和效率方面表现出色，特别是在推理速度和内存占用上，使其具有较高的实际应用潜力。
motivation: 语言目标空中导航要求无人机使用飞行中收集的观测数据到达自然语言指定的目标。主要挑战在于如何将变化的自我中心感知与锚定在稳定位置的空间证据联系起来，以实现长距离导航。
method: 本文提出了CityNav-VLA，一个用于城市导航的双帧视觉-语言-动作模型。它整合了动态自我中心上下文和持久的异位空间记忆。无人机在一个初始化有地理和地标先验知识的固定北向上地图上逐步积累视觉观测，从而在视角变化时保留证据。一个根据指令、当前观测、无人机状态和运动历史动态查询的模块，检索相关的记忆证据以预测地图坐标系目标。一个确定性控制器利用无人机当前姿态将此目标转换为机体坐标系指令，连接全局推理与自我中心执行。为减少长距离目标波动，采用早期目标承诺（EGC）机制，将执行目标固定为前K个预测的坐标中位数，无需额外可训练参数。
