title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
authors: Guoqing Wang, Pin Tang, Xiangxuan Ren, Chao Ma
abstract: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VLA model reason over to support planning beyond pixel-level prediction? We argue that planning-oriented world modeling should focus on a compact and structured agent-centric latent state that captures the interactions between objects in the driving scene over time. As such, we introduce AgentWorld, an agent-centric VLA world model that uses discrete agent tokens jointly for reasoning and trajectory planning. Each token is dynamically grounded to a surrounding agent associated with its object's state, such as semantic identity, 3D geometry, motion, and interaction context. AgentWorld learns these tokens through three key processes: explicit geometric grounding, reasoning-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and agent-oriented reinforcement learning. Extensive open-loop and closed-loop experiments under diverse driving scenarios show that AgentWorld enhances planning capabilities, fully exploits visual evidence and agent dynamics, and yields interpretable agent-centric world states.

title: The Whole Warps the Parts: Attentional Certainty Modulates Ensemble-Induced Bias in Visualizations
authors: Jennifer E. Corbett, Brian W. Anthony
abstract: Data visualizations often require viewers to extract both ensemble statistics and individual values from collections of graphical marks. Yet individual items embedded within an ensemble can be systematically biased by that context. Prior studies have reported both repulsion away from and attraction toward ensemble statistics, but these effects have been observed across different conditions. We test whether task or attentional certainty explains these opposing forms of ensemble-induced bias. In Study 1, observers briefly viewed ensembles of differently sized circles and then judged the size of an individual circle embedded within the ensemble. Using a common stimulus generation framework, we tested both identification and discrimination when the target was specified before or after the ensemble, and an additional no-cue identification condition without a specified target. Under the shared cued conditions, effects were predominantly repulsive or near zero in both identification and discrimination. In contrast, eliminating target-specific information reversed ensemble-induced bias from repulsion to attraction. Identification precision also decreased systematically from pre-cue to post-cue to no-cue conditions. Study 2 replicated this cue-dependent pattern in graphical displays of startup valuations and precinct vote contributions. Our findings isolate attentional certainty as a key determinant of whether ensemble context repels or attracts individual-item representations, extending the design question beyond precision to how attention directing choices determine which bias the viewer will be operating under.
zh_title: 整体扭曲局部：注意确定性调节可视化中由整体引起的知觉偏差
translation: 数据可视化通常要求观察者从图形标记集合中同时提取整体统计信息与单个数值。然而，嵌入在整体中的单个项目可能会被其所处的上下文系统性地产生知觉偏差。以往研究分别报道了远离整体统计值的排斥效应和朝向整体统计值的吸引效应，但这些效应是在不同条件下观察到的。我们测试了任务类型或注意确定性是否能解释这些形式相反的整体诱发偏差。在研究1中，观察者短暂浏览大小不一的圆形集合，然后判断集合中某个圆的大小。在一个通用的刺激生成框架下，我们测试了在整体呈现之前或之后指定目标时的识别与辨别任务，以及未指定目标的无提示识别任务。在相同的有提示条件下，识别和辨别中的效应主要表现为排斥或接近于零。相反，消除目标特异性信息后，整体诱发的偏差从排斥逆转为吸引。识别精度也从前提示、后提示到无提示条件系统性地下降。研究2在初创公司估值和选区投票贡献的图形展示中复现了这种依赖于提示的模式。我们的研究结果明确了注意确定性是决定整体背景排斥还是吸引单个项目表征的关键因素，将可视化设计问题从单纯的精度考量延伸至注意引导策略如何决定观察者所面临的偏差类型。
tldr: 研究发现注意确定性决定了整体环境对局部项估计是产生“排斥”还是“吸引”偏差，为图表设计中的注意力引导提供了新依据。
ai_comments: 该研究的重要创新在于统一并解释了以往研究中整体背景对局部估计产生“排斥”与“吸引”这一对立现象的矛盾，证明注意确定性是决定偏差方向的关键变量。其重要性在于将可视化评估从单纯的“读图精度”拓展到了“知觉偏差方向”的层面，对如何通过提示或高亮等注意力引导手段优化图表设计具有重要指导意义。局限性在于测试主要集中在静态简单标记和二维气泡图/散点图式场景，未来需在更复杂、多变量或动态交互的可视化中进一步验证。
motivation: 在数据可视化中，整体环境常常系统性地扭曲局部项的估计，但以往研究在不同条件下分别观察到了局部向整体统计值“吸引”或被其“排斥”的矛盾现象。本研究旨在探究任务类型或注意确定性是否能解释这种相反的整体诱发偏差。
method: 研究包含两个实验：研究1采用大小不一的圆形刺激集合，通过前线索（pre-cue）、后线索（post-cue）和无目标线索（no-cue）操纵注意确定性，测试被试在识别和辨别任务中对特定圆大小的判断；研究2将该范式复制并推广到初创公司估值和选区投票贡献的实际数据可视化图表中。
results: 在线索提示条件下（前线索和后线索），被试在识别和辨别任务中主要表现出排斥效应或近零偏差；而在消除目标特异性信息的无提示条件下，整体诱发的偏差由排斥逆转为吸引。同时，识别精度从前线索到后线索再到无提示呈系统性下降。研究2在实际图表场景中成功复现了这一依赖于线索的模式。
conclusion: 注意确定性是决定整体背景对单个项目表征产生排斥还是吸引偏差的关键决定因素；图表设计不仅要考虑感知精度，还需关注注意力引导方式如何决定用户所受偏差的类型。

title: RoadAnnoter: An AI-Assisted Desktop Tool for Semantic Segmentation Annotation of Road-Scene Images
authors: Nazmul Haque, Arnob Protim Roy
abstract: Accurate semantic segmentation of road-scene images is essential for road safety research; however, polygon-level annotation remains labor-intensive and limits labelled dataset development. This study presents RoadAnnoter v1.0, an open-source desktop application integrating six human-in-the-loop annotation modes: manual polygon delineation, SAM Prompt, Smart Select, Edge Fill, pretrained semantic segmentation using Cityscapes-trained SegFormer models, and task-specific segmentation using TinySegNet, a lightweight MobileNetV3-Small-based network trained with accumulated annotator-generated labels. SAM-based modes use promptable segmentation with SAM and MobileSAM, while Edge Fill combines Canny edge detection with colour-similarity-based flood filling in CIELAB colour space. SegFormer generates suggestions for common road-scene categories, whereas TinySegNet supports adaptation to project-specific features through iterative training. All six modes use a shared mask-to-polygon pipeline comprising morphological processing, Gaussian smoothing, contour extraction, and Douglas-Peucker simplification; annotations are exported in YOLO segmentation format. RoadAnnoter was used to annotate Google Street View images from recorded road accident locations in Bangladesh for a vision-language model-based investigation of free-flow speed estimation. Qualitative assessment across representative scenes demonstrated the complementary applicability of the annotation modes to diverse feature geometries. Visual comparison with Roboflow indicated similar qualitative boundary characteristics for principal road-scene regions, although no quantitative accuracy assessment was conducted. RoadAnnoter provides a locally operated framework for developing road-scene segmentation datasets for transportation engineering and road safety research.
zh_title: RoadAnnoter：用于道路场景图像语义分割标注的AI辅助桌面工具
translation: 道路场景图像的精确语义分割对道路安全研究至关重要；然而，多边形级别的标注仍然属于劳动密集型工作，限制了带标签数据集的发展。本研究提出了RoadAnnoter v1.0，这是一款开源桌面应用程序，集成了六种人机协同（human-in-the-loop）标注模式：手动多边形勾勒、SAM Prompt、Smart Select、Edge Fill、利用基于Cityscapes训练的SegFormer模型进行的预训练语义分割，以及使用根据标注者累积生成的标签训练的轻量级MobileNetV3-Small网络（TinySegNet）进行的任务特定分割。基于SAM的模式使用SAM和MobileSAM进行提示式分割，而Edge Fill结合了Canny边缘检测与CIELAB颜色空间中基于颜色相似度的泛洪填充。SegFormer为常见的道路场景类别生成建议，而TinySegNet通过迭代训练支持对特定项目特征的自适应。所有六种模式均采用共享的“掩膜转多边形”流水线，包括形态学处理、高斯平滑、轮廓提取和Douglas-Peucker多边形简化；标注结果以YOLO分割格式导出。RoadAnnoter被用于标注孟加拉国记录在案的交通事故地点的谷歌街景图像，以支持基于视觉-语言模型的自由流速度估计研究。对代表性场景的定性评估表明，这些标注模式对多样化的特征几何形态具有互补的适用性。与Roboflow的视觉对比表明，两者在主要道路场景区域具有相似的定性边界特征，尽管尚未进行定量准确性评估。RoadAnnoter为交通工程和道路安全研究提供了一个用于开发道路场景分割数据集的本地运行框架。
tldr: RoadAnnoter是一款集成了SAM、SegFormer和自适应TinySegNet等六种人机协同模式的开源本地桌面道路场景语义分割标注工具。
ai_comments: 该工具将基础分割模型（SAM/MobileSAM）、预训练模型（SegFormer）、轻量级自适应微调网络（TinySegNet）与传统CV算法（Canny边缘检测与泛洪填充）集成在本地桌面端，实用性强且保护数据隐私。局限在于摘要中明确指出尚未进行定量准确性评估，仅依赖定性分析与对比。
motivation: 道路场景图像的高精度语义分割对道路安全研究至关重要，但多边形级别的精细标注极其耗时费力，限制了标注数据集的构建与扩展。
method: 开发了开源桌面工具RoadAnnoter v1.0，集成了六种人机协同标注模式（手动多边形勾勒、SAM Prompt、Smart Select、基于Canny和CIELAB泛洪填充的Edge Fill、基于Cityscapes的SegFormer预训练分割、以及基于MobileNetV3-Small构建的TinySegNet任务特定分割网络）。所有模式共用一套掩膜转多边形流水线（包括形态学处理、高斯平滑、轮廓提取与Douglas-Peucker简化），并支持导出为YOLO分割格式。
results: 利用该工具对孟加拉国事故多发地的谷歌街景图像进行了标注，定性评估证明了六种模式针对不同几何特征的互补适用性；与Roboflow进行视觉对比显示主要道路区域具有相似的定性边界特征（注：未进行定量准确率评估）。
conclusion: RoadAnnoter 为交通工程与道路安全研究提供了一个本地运行的道路场景分割数据集标注框架，能有效支持相关领域的数据构建。

title: Beyond Attribute-Centric Fairness: Modelling and Mitigating Unified Bias Representation in Omni-modal Large Language Models
authors: Runqi Lin, Suqin Yuan, Zihao Fu, Chris Russell
abstract: Omni-modal large language models (OLLMs) provide joint multimodal understanding and generation capabilities, making them well-suited to complex environments and promising backbones for next-generation AI. Despite these advances, the harmful stereotypes encoded in such models manifest in increasingly diverse forms, leading to broader and more severe societal consequences. Existing debiasing methods typically impose separate fairness objectives for each sensitive attribute and modality to minimise demographic-dependent variations. However, in omni-modal settings, this attribute-centric paradigm struggles to jointly address diverse social biases with distinct fairness objectives and to generalise beyond predefined attributes. To this end, we propose OmniDebias, one of the first methods for promoting fairness in OLLMs, which employs a bias-centric formulation to extract and mitigate a shared bias representation across attributes and modalities while preserving attribute-related knowledge. Specifically, we exploit activation inconsistencies of a given attribute (e.g., gender) across semantic contexts (e.g., occupations) to disentangle bias from legitimate knowledge. We further consolidate multiple extracted biases into a shared representation, formulating a unified objective that captures the underlying structure across social biases and generalises to unseen attributes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that eliminating unified bias with both post-hoc editing and fine-tuning can consistently improve fairness across diverse attributes and modalities in OLLMs while maintaining favourable utility.
zh_title: 超越以属性为中心的公平性：在全模态大语言模型中建模与缓解统一偏见表征
translation: 全模态大语言模型（OLLM）具备联合的多模态理解与生成能力，使其非常适合复杂环境，并成为下一代人工智能的有前景的基座。尽管取得了这些进展，但此类模型中编码的有害刻板印象表现出日益多样的形式，导致了更广泛且更严重的社会后果。现有的去偏方法通常针对每个敏感属性和模态施加单独的公平性目标，以最小化依赖人口统计学特征的差异。然而，在全模态环境中，这种以属性为中心的范式难以通过各异的公平性目标协同解决多样化的社会偏见，也难以泛化到预定义属性之外。为此，我们提出了OmniDebias，这是首批促进OLLM公平性的方法之一，它采用以偏见为中心的表述，提取并缓解跨属性和模态的共享偏见表示，同时保留与属性相关的知识。具体而言，我们利用给定属性（如性别）在不同语义上下文（如职业）中的激活不一致性，将偏见与合理知识解耦。我们进一步将提取出的多种偏见整合为一个共享表示，构建了一个能够捕捉跨社会偏见的底层结构并可泛化至未见属性的统一目标。大量实验表明，通过事后编辑和微调来消除统一偏见，可以在保持良好实用性的同时，持续提升OLLM在多样化属性和模态下的公平性。
tldr: 针对全模态大模型难以兼顾多属性与跨模态去偏的问题，本文提出OmniDebias，通过解耦偏见与有效知识并构建统一共享偏见表示，实现了跨模态、可泛化的公平性提升且不损模型效用。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地突破了传统的“以属性为中心”的去偏偏见范式，针对全模态大语言模型（OLLM）提出了“以偏见为中心”的统一表示建模方法。其重要性在于能够跨模态、跨属性捕获共享偏见结构，并泛化至未预定义的属性，同时保留了模型的实用性与合法知识。局限在于摘要中未明确说明该方法在极端多模态或全新模态（如音频、视频等多源异构输入）下的计算开销与性能边界。
motivation: 全模态大语言模型中编码的刻板印象形式愈发多样。现有的去偏方法多针对特定敏感属性和特定模态设置独立的公平性目标（以属性为中心），难以在全模态场景下协同处理多类社会偏见，且无法泛化至未预先定义的属性。
method: 提出OmniDebias方法，采用“以偏见为中心”的构想：1）利用特定属性在不同语义上下文中的激活不一致性，将有害偏见与合法属性知识解耦；2）将提取出的多种偏见整合为跨属性与跨模态的共享统一偏见表示；3）构建统一优化目标，支持通过事后编辑（post-hoc editing）或微调（fine-tuning）来消除该统一偏见。
results: 大量实验表明，在后处理模型编辑和微调中消除该统一偏见表示，能够持续提升OLLM在多种属性与模态上的公平性，并保持良好的模型实用效用。
conclusion: OmniDebias通过建模统一偏见表示并在后处理编辑与微调中予以消除，能够有效提升全模态大语言模型在多模态与多属性上的公平性，并具备向未知属性泛化的能力，同时兼顾了模型原有的效用。

title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
authors: Deokhyung Kang, Minjae Gwon, Sangdon Park
abstract: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retaining impossibility judgments about unachieved capabilities. To test whether context management can elicit further capability, we propose SCoRe, which compacts context at stop bursts and marks these judgments as unproven. SCoRe improves verified capability over summary-based continuation and other evaluated context-management baselines. With SCoRe, MiMo reaches a capability coverage score of 67.0% at 2,000 turns, exceeding both 32.4% under the original stopping policy and the 58.6% computed for GPT-5.5 from ExploitBench's 300-turn reference results on the same tasks. These findings show that stopping need not mark an agent's exploitation limit, and that continued execution with context management can elicit substantial further capability.
zh_title: 停止并非终点：理解与激发智能体在长程漏洞利用中的能力
translation: 漏洞利用旨在测试语言模型智能体是否能根据已知软件缺陷构建出可行的利用程序。顺序测试时扩展可以提高漏洞利用性能，但更大的计算预算并不一定能保证持续的探索：智能体通常会在预算尚有剩余时就停止。然而，当执行超越停止点继续进行时会发生什么，目前仍缺乏充分研究。我们在ExploitBench上使用DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731和MiMo-V2.6-Pro对这一空白进行了调查。我们发现，在首次给出停止响应之后仍可获得经验证的额外增益，但随着执行时间的延长，增益会出现递减。我们指出了与低效延续相关的两种模式：同一上下文中停止响应的比例不断增加，以及摘要中保留了对未实现能力的“不可能”判断从而导致提前停止。为了测试上下文管理是否能激发更多能力，我们提出了SCoRe，该方法在停止集中爆发时压缩上下文，并将这些不可能判断标记为“未被证实”。相比于基于摘要的延续策略及其他评估的上下文管理基线，SCoRe提升了经验证的能力。借助SCoRe，MiMo在2,000轮次时的能力覆盖得分达到67.0%，既超过了原始停止策略下的32.4%，也超过了相同任务下ExploitBench 300轮参考结果中为GPT-5.5计算出的58.6%。这些发现表明，停止并不必然标志着智能体的漏洞利用能力极限，通过上下文管理继续执行可以激发巨大的潜在能力。
tldr: 论文发现LLM智能体在漏洞利用任务中提前停止并不等于达到能力上限，通过提出的SCoRe上下文管理策略纠正错误停滞判定，可大幅提升智能体的长程利用能力。
ai_comments: 该研究敏锐地抓住了长程智能体任务中‘过早停止（premature stopping）’这一核心痛点，指出了模型由于上下文记忆中的‘不可能判断’而产生探索停滞的机制。所提出的SCoRe方法通过上下文压缩和纠正确定性认知，有效释放了模型的潜在探索能力，对提升长上下文/复杂决策场景下的Agent推理能力具有重要的启发意义。
motivation: 在漏洞利用任务中，顺序测试时扩展（test-time scaling）虽能提升性能，但更大的预算无法保证持续探索，智能体往往在预算未耗尽时就提前停止，而停止之后继续执行会带来何种影响目前尚未得到深入探究。
method: 在ExploitBench基准上评估模型（DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731和MiMo-V2.6-Pro）在首次停止后的表现，分析导致低效延续的模式（同上下文内停止响应比例增加、摘要中保留未达成能力的‘不可能’判定）。进而提出SCoRe方法，在停止爆发点压缩上下文，并将既有的‘不可能’判定标记为‘未被证实’，以此打破探索僵局。
results: 首次停止后继续执行能带来经检验的额外增益，但增益会随执行增长而递减；SCoRe在经检验能力上优于基于摘要的延续策略及其他基线。在2000轮交互下，MiMo结合SCoRe使能力覆盖得分达到67.0%，远超原始停止策略下的32.4%，并超越了同任务下GPT-5.5在300轮参考结果中的58.6%。
conclusion: 智能体的主动停止并不代表其能力极限；在停止后通过有效的上下文管理继续执行，可以充分激发智能体更深层次的漏洞利用能力。

title: You Only Encode Once: Sub-Pixel-Shifted Frames for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution with 2D Gaussian Splatting
authors: Canjie Liu, Liuqian Wang, Qi Ming, Wei Lu, Xiaohan Hao, Yuefei Wu, Wentao Chao, Lei Shi
abstract: Arbitrary-scale super-resolution (ASSR) of remote sensing images remains challenging due to the limited high-frequency information in a single low-resolution (LR) observation. While multi-frame SR can exploit complementary sub-pixel information, existing approaches often require real multi-frame training sequences and repeated feature encoding, increasing data acquisition demands and computational costs. To address these limitations, we propose SPS-GS (Sub-Pixel-Shifted Gaussian Splatting), an encode-once framework that learns from multi-phase LR observations synthesized from individual high-resolution images, without requiring real multi-frame training sequences. Specifically, Phase-Coherent Aliasing Demodulation (PCAD) exploits shift-dependent aliasing through Fourier-based alignment, phase-aware residual fusion, and least-squares aliasing estimation, enabling multi-frame information to be integrated before a single deep encoding pass. Gaussian Projection Alignment (GPA) then iteratively refines Gaussian centers and colors using multi-observation back-projection to promote observation consistency. The refined Gaussians support continuous rendering at arbitrary scales. Extensive experiments on five remote sensing datasets demonstrate strong reconstruction performance against single-image and multi-frame SR baselines, while maintaining competitive inference efficiency at common scales. The code will be publicly released.
zh_title: 你只编码一次：结合2D高斯泼溅的亚像素偏移帧用于任意尺度遥感超分辨率
translation: 遥感图像的任意尺度超分辨率（ASSR）仍然具有挑战性，原因在于单个低分辨率（LR）观测中高频信息有限。尽管多帧超分辨率可以利用互补的亚像素信息，但现有方法通常需要真实的多帧训练序列和重复的特征编码，这增加了数据采集需求和计算成本。为了解决这些限制，我们提出了SPS-GS（亚像素偏移高斯泼溅），这是一个一次编码的框架，它从由单个高分辨率图像合成的多相LR观测中学习，而无需真实的多帧训练序列。具体来说，相位相干混叠解调（PCAD）通过基于傅里叶的对齐、相位感知残差融合和最小二乘混叠估计来利用与位移相关的混叠，从而实现在单个深度编码过程之前整合多帧信息。然后，高斯投影对齐（GPA）使用多观测反向投影迭代地细化高斯中心和颜色，以促进观测一致性。细化后的高斯支持任意尺度的连续渲染。在五个遥感数据集上进行的广泛实验表明，与单幅图像和多帧超分辨率基线相比，该方法表现出强大的重建性能，同时在常见尺度下保持了具有竞争力的推理效率。代码将公开发布。
tldr: 该论文提出了SPS-GS，一个用于遥感图像任意尺度超分辨率的一次编码框架，它通过合成亚像素偏移的低分辨率观测和2D高斯泼溅来解决现有方法的局限性，实现了卓越的重建性能和效率。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新之处在于其“一次编码”框架，通过利用合成的多相低分辨率观测，避免了对真实多帧训练数据和重复编码的需求。将PCAD和GPA与2D高斯泼溅结合以实现任意尺度渲染，是一种新颖的方法。这项工作对于解决遥感图像处理中的关键挑战具有重要意义，为高质量图像放大提供了一种更数据高效和计算有效的方法。
motivation: 遥感图像的任意尺度超分辨率（ASSR）面临挑战，因为单个低分辨率（LR）观测中的高频信息有限。现有的多帧超分辨率方法需要真实的多帧训练序列和重复的特征编码，这导致数据采集需求和计算成本增加。
method: 本文提出了SPS-GS（亚像素偏移高斯泼溅），一个一次编码的框架，它从由单个高分辨率图像合成的多相LR观测中学习，无需真实的多帧训练序列。具体而言，相位相干混叠解调（PCAD）通过基于傅里叶的对齐、相位感知残差融合和最小二乘混叠估计来利用与位移相关的混叠，从而在单个深度编码过程之前整合多帧信息。随后，高斯投影对齐（GPA）利用多观测反向投影迭代地细化高斯中心和颜色，以促进观测一致性。细化后的高斯支持任意尺度的连续渲染。
results: 在五个遥感数据集上进行的广泛实验表明，与单幅图像和多帧超分辨率基线相比，SPS-GS表现出强大的重建性能，同时在常见尺度下保持了具有竞争力的推理效率。
conclusion: SPS-GS通过利用合成的多相低分辨率观测和一次编码框架，有效解决了遥感图像任意尺度超分辨率的挑战，实现了强大的性能和效率。

title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
authors: Haozhi Han, Junjie Yang, Ruge Zhang, Zihe Huang, Pengyi Xu, Bo Zhang, Yunquan Zhang, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu, Yifeng Chen, Kun Li
abstract: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce BORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. BORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, BORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, BORN finishes in 1.41h on a single CPU node, 77$\times$ faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline and still 9.8$\times$ faster with development time included. On a single GPU, BORN completes the ubiquitin calculation in 2.1,h, the same order of runtime as the GPU-accelerated package Mako on 64 GPUs, and shortens the B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1,h (173$\times$).
zh_title: 为任务而生：通过前瞻性智能体计算重新思考量子化学
translation: 量子化学依赖于通用软件，但其通用性使得许多大规模计算超出了实际的资源预算。编程智能体虽然降低了编写任务特定程序的成本，但要找到高效程序并不容易：一种计算策略是否足够精确和快速，往往只有在它实际于目标规模下运行后才能明朗。我们提出了BORN，一个前瞻性智能体计算框架，可按需合成高性能量子化学程序。BORN在执行前预判每种策略的表现，从小规模代表性系统中推演其误差，并根据目标规模的工作负载与实测硬件吞吐量预测其运行时间。基于这些预测，BORN将现有软件包的预设方案解构为可独立配置的算法组件，从预测的精度-耗时帕累托前沿中选择误差容限内最快的策略，并通过组件级性能预测指导编程智能体完成编译。对于包含50,024个基函数的Hartree-Fock计算，BORN在单CPU节点上耗时1.41小时完成，比通用基准的预估运行时间快77倍，即使计入开发时间仍快9.8倍。在单GPU上，BORN在2.1小时内完成了泛素计算，与GPU加速软件包Mako在64块GPU上的运行时间处于同一量级，并将B-DNA双螺旋计算从预计的两个月缩短至8.1小时（加速173倍）。
tldr: BORN是一个结合了事前误差与耗时预测的前瞻性智能体计算框架，能按需自动合成专用量子化学程序，实现超百倍的计算加速。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地将性能/误差前瞻预测机制与代码生成智能体相结合，解决了在未实际运行前难以评估定制程序在大规模任务下精度与效率的核心痛点。实验表明其在单CPU/单GPU上的表现可匹敌甚至大幅超越传统集群计算，对AI for Science中特定科学计算软件的自动化、高性能定制具有重要的应用价值。
motivation: 通用量子化学软件因其通用性难以在实际资源预算内完成大规模计算；而代码智能体虽易于编写专用程序，却无法在目标规模实际运行前预知该策略是否具备足够的精度与速度。
method: 提出前瞻性智能体计算框架BORN：1）在执行前从小系统推演误差，结合目标规模工作负载和实测硬件吞吐量预测策略耗时；2）将现有软件包的方案解构为可独立配置的算法组件，从预测的精度-耗时帕累托前沿中选取满足误差容限的最优策略；3）基于组件级性能预测引导编程智能体按需编译并生成高效程序。
results: 在50,024个基函数的Hartree-Fock计算中，单CPU节点耗时1.41小时，比通用基线估计快77倍（含开发时间快9.8倍）；在单GPU上，泛素计算耗时2.1小时（达到GPU加速包Mako在64卡上的耗时量级），并将B-DNA双链计算从预计的2个月缩短至8.1小时（加速173倍）。
conclusion: BORN通过前瞻性性能与精度预测指导智能体按需合成专用程序，成功突破了传统通用量子化学软件在大规模计算中的资源与耗时瓶颈。

title: Wear and Go: Calibration Free Sparse Inertial Motion Capture via Online Sensor Setup Estimation
authors: Yuanshuo Tan, Licheng Zhong
abstract: Sparse inertial motion capture typically assumes that each sensor's anatomical identity and mounting orientation are known. We present MOSAIC (Motion-based Sensor Assignment and Inertial Calibration), a framework that recovers this setup from ordinary motion without a calibration pose. Our central insight is that body pose changes continuously while the sensor setup persists, allowing movements that are individually ambiguous to provide complementary evidence over time. A setup network processes unordered sensor streams with temporal and cross-sensor attention, then accumulates assignment and rotation evidence into a session-level estimate. The recovered setup canonicalizes measurements for frozen pretrained pose estimators, separating sensor configuration from motion reconstruction. For sensors worn at prescribed body sites, evaluation on real inertial recordings with randomized setups shows near-calibrated pose accuracy for bounded offsets and substantial benefits from accumulation under arbitrary orientations. Transfer across pose networks supports setup recovery as a reusable interface between interchangeable sensors and pretrained pose models.
zh_title: 即戴即用：基于在线传感器配置估计的免标定稀疏惯性动作捕捉
translation: 稀疏惯性动作捕捉通常假设每个传感器的解剖学身份和安装朝向是已知的。我们提出了MOSAIC（基于运动的传感器分配与惯性标定），这是一个无需标定姿势、直接从日常运动中恢复该配置的框架。我们的核心洞见在于：身体姿态是连续变化的，而传感器配置保持稳定，从而使原本单帧下具有歧义的运动能够随时间提供互补证据。配置网络利用时序与跨传感器注意力处理无序的传感器数据流，随后将分配和旋转证据累积为会话级别的估计。恢复出的配置可规范化测量数据并输入到冻结的预训练姿态估计器中，从而将传感器配置与动作重建解耦。对于佩戴在预定身体部位的传感器，在带有随机配置的真实惯性记录上的评估表明，在有界偏移下其姿态精度接近已标定状态，且在任意朝向下时序累积带来了显著增益。在不同姿态网络间的迁移能力，支持将配置恢复作为可互换传感器与预训练姿态模型之间的可复用接口。
tldr: 提出MOSAIC框架，无需标定姿势，仅通过普通运动在线推断无序传感器的佩戴部位与朝向，实现免标定的稀疏惯性动作捕捉。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地摆脱了传统惯性动作捕捉对特定标定姿态（如T-pose）的依赖，提出了“即戴即用”的范式；通过将传感器配置估计与姿态重建解耦，使其具备高度模块化和可迁移性。局限在于目前实验仍然假定传感器佩戴在预定的解剖学身体部位集合中，对于非预定部位的泛化能力仍待进一步探索。
motivation: 传统的稀疏惯性动作捕捉依赖预先已知的传感器解剖学身份（佩戴部位）与安装朝向，通常需要用户做出特定的标定姿势，使用体验繁琐且限制了便捷性。
method: 提出MOSAIC框架，利用身体姿态持续变化而传感器配置固定的特性，使用结合时序与跨传感器注意力机制的网络处理无序传感器流，将各时刻的部位分配与旋转证据累积为会话级配置估计，并将数据规范化后输入冻结的预训练姿态估计器中。
results: 在具有随机配置的真实惯性数据评估中，对于预定部位的传感器，在有界偏移下取得了接近标定水准的姿态估计精度；在任意朝向下时序累积机制优势显著，并展现了在不同姿态网络间的良好迁移能力。
conclusion: MOSAIC证明了无需特定标定姿势，仅凭自然日常运动即可在线准确估计传感器的分配与朝向，可作为通用、可互换的接口赋能各类预训练惯性姿态估计模型。

title: Impact of Pretraining Length, Model Size, and Annotation Budget on Downstream Clinical Tasks of Foundation Models in Radiotherapy
authors: Alejandro Cortina Uribe, Sidsel Højklint Poulsen, Ivan Richter Vogelius, Jens Petersen
abstract: Cone-beam CT (CBCT) scans acquired during radiotherapy capture changes such as tumor shrinkage and radiation-induced tissue changes, offering great potential for foundation models that help monitor individual treatment responses. However, to our knowledge, no large-scale pretrained models for radiotherapy CBCT exist, and evaluating modeling choices is difficult since downstream tasks are not known in advance. We examine how pretraining length, model size, and finetuning strategy relate to downstream clinical performance, and how metrics tracked during pretraining correlate with it. We pretrain vision transformer encoders with masked image modeling on about 150,000 raw 3D radiotherapy CBCT scans, tracking representation quality via validation loss, effective rank, and linear probing. Downstream tasks are classification of feeding tube presence ($n=51,135$ CBCTs, $1,562$ patients) and clinical characteristics (T-, N-stage, sex, age, tumor site; $n=1,278$ patients) in head and neck cancer. We compare low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and full finetuning against no pretraining, varying annotated dataset size. Pretext validation loss was the most consistent predictor of downstream performance; effective rank and linear probing were also associated, but not consistently across model sizes and finetuning methods. LoRA performed comparably to full finetuning while training only 0.5-2.5% of the parameters. Fully finetuned models consistently outperformed models without pretraining across all sizes, with AUROC 0.91-0.97 vs. 0.58-0.85 for feeding tube classification and 0.99-1.00 vs. 0.71-0.97 for sex classification. Model size had only a small, inconsistent effect, suggesting smaller models suffice at lower computational cost. Code and pretrained models (non-commercial license): https://github.com/alexCortinaU/RT-CBCT_SSL
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Supplementary Material included
zh_title: 预训练时长、模型大小和标注预算对放疗基础模型下游临床任务的影响
translation: 放射治疗期间采集的锥形束CT（CBCT）扫描能够记录肿瘤缩小以及辐射引起的组织变化等，在构建协助监测个体治疗反应的基础模型方面蕴含巨大潜力。然而，据我们所知，目前尚不存在针对放疗CBCT的大规模预训练模型，且在下游任务未知的情况下评估建模选择较为困难。我们研究了预训练时长、模型大小和微调策略与下游临床性能之间的关系，以及预训练阶段追踪的指标与下游性能的相关性。我们在约150,000例放疗3D CBCT原始扫描上，使用掩码图像建模预训练了视觉Transformer编码器，并通过验证损失、有效秩和线性探测评估表征质量。下游任务为头颈癌患者的鼻饲管存在性分类（n=51,135例CBCT，1,562位患者）和临床特征分类（T分期、N分期、性别、年龄、肿瘤部位；n=1,278位患者）。我们通过改变标注数据集大小，对比了低秩自适应（LoRA）、全参数微调与从头训练的表现。前置任务验证损失是下游性能最一致的预测指标；有效秩和线性探测也具有相关性，但在不同模型尺寸和微调方法间表现并不一致。LoRA仅训练0.5%-2.5%的参数便取得了与全参数微调相当的性能。全微调模型在所有尺寸下均显著优于无预训练模型，鼻饲管分类的AUROC达到0.91-0.97（对比0.58-0.85），性别分类达到0.99-1.00（对比0.71-0.97）。模型尺寸的影响较小且不一致，表明较小的模型即可在更低的计算成本下满足需求。代码和预训练模型（非商业许可）开源于：https://github.com/alexCortinaU/RT-CBCT_SSL。
tldr: 研究在15万例放疗CBCT上训练了首个3D基础模型，证明预训练可大幅提升临床下游任务性能，且轻量ViT结合LoRA即可达到顶尖效果。
ai_comments: 该论文填补了放疗CBCT领域缺乏大规模自监督基础模型的空白，具有很强的临床实用价值。其系统性评估了预训练监控指标与下游性能的相关性，并证实了参数高效微调（LoRA）与轻量化ViT模型在医疗影像落地中的可行性与高性价比，为资源受限场景下的放疗AI开发提供了重要依据。
motivation: 放疗中的锥形束CT（CBCT）能够追踪肿瘤及组织的动态变化，具备构建基础模型的巨大潜力，但目前尚无针对放疗CBCT的大规模预训练模型，且在下游任务未知的情况下难以有效评估预训练和建模方案的选择。
method: 基于掩码图像建模（MIM）在约15万例放疗3D CBCT原始扫描上预训练视觉Transformer（ViT）编码器；在预训练过程中通过验证损失、有效秩和线性探测跟踪表征质量；在头颈癌鼻饲管分类及多项临床特征预测下游任务中，对比了LoRA微调、全参数微调与从头训练在不同标注量下的表现。
results: 预训练验证损失是下游表现最稳定一致的预测指标；LoRA微调仅需更新0.5%-2.5%的参数即可取得与全参数微调相当的表现；预训练模型显著优于无预训练模型（鼻饲管分类AUROC 0.91-0.97 vs. 0.58-0.85，性别分类 0.99-1.00 vs. 0.71-0.97）；模型尺寸对性能影响较小且不一致，轻量模型即可满足需求。
conclusion: 自监督预训练显著提升了CBCT下游临床任务的预测性能；预训练验证损失是预测下游效果的最佳代理指标；结合小模型与LoRA微调能够在极低计算资源下实现高精度的临床任务预测。

title: A Dichotomy for Exact Quantum Circuit Amplitudes
authors: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng
abstract: We classify the complexity of exactly computing computational-basis amplitudes for circuits over any fixed finite library of unitary qubit gates, with each gate allowed to act on any ordered tuple of distinct wires. Exact evaluation is polynomial-time computable if all gates permute the computational basis up to phases, all preserve product states, or all become Clifford under a common diagonal one-qubit unitary change of basis on every wire. For every other library, the problem is $\#\mathrm P$-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. Our proof connects circuit amplitudes to the Boolean Holant classification of tensor contractions on arbitrary graphs. For an algebraic library containing a nonmonomial gate and an entangling gate, we show how to simulate the joint use of a symmetric maximally entangled state and its adjoint at polynomial cost, using only amplitude queries over the original library. This lets us evaluate unrestricted contractions of the resulting gate and boundary tensors. Unitarity and the computational-basis boundaries then restrict the tractable cases to the three forms above. Algebraic specialization extends the dichotomy to arbitrary fixed complex gate entries under a symbolic exact-output convention.

title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
authors: Zerui Yang, Quan Xue, Miaomiao Dong, Chaorui Zhang, Xuanyu Zheng, Xiyuan Wang, Haolin Ruan, Xueyan Niu, Guangcheng Song, Weixi Zhang, Wei Han, Bo Bai
abstract: Coding agents often continue working after their own tests pass. Does this additional work improve the patch, and how much could be saved by stopping earlier? We study these questions through anytime evaluation: replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and measuring the cost incurred at each step. For policies that only stop a run or select an earlier patch, this allows paired comparisons without generating new trajectories, provided replay preserves the relevant states. Across about 6,000 runs of eight open models in two scaffolds on SWE-bench Verified, we find substantial differences in the value of continued work. The hindsight saving available at passing self-tests ranges from under 1% to 57%, depending on the model and scaffold. A rule that stops after the same patch passes twice saves 23% in a preregistered replication, but the preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority. We explain these differences by measuring how often a rule fires, how often the patch changes afterwards, and whether those changes repair or break it. Fine-tuning agents to imitate the rule saves 30% over six seeds, while quality preservation remains uncertain. Our results help identify both the opportunities and the risks of early stopping.

title: BRepA: Graph-Based B-Rep Pretraining for Unified CAD Understanding and Generation
authors: Dekai Zhu, Zhaiyu Chen, Stefan Gavranovic, Slobodan Ilic
abstract: Boundary representation (B-Rep) of CAD models encodes geometric primitives and their relations as a graph structure, enabling efficient shape modeling within CAD software. Learning on B-Reps for downstream tasks, such as segmentation and novel shape generation, requires specialized neural network designs. Moreover, performance improvements and accelerated training can be achieved with effective pretraining strategies, which is particularly important for tasks with limited labeled B-Rep data. In this paper, we introduce BRepA, a unified self-supervised pretraining framework that explicitly reconstructs both the geometry and topology of B-Rep objects via graph-based modeling. By learning from large-scale unlabeled CAD data only once, BRepA produces representations that generalize across tasks and significantly enhance both discriminative and generative learning. On segmentation tasks, BRepA demonstrates remarkable data efficiency. For instance, with only 1% labeled samples, BRepA pretraining improves mIoU by 32.52% compared to models trained from scratch. On generative tasks, aligning diffusion model representations with pretrained BRepA features substantially accelerates convergence, achieving nearly 2 times faster training while improving generation quality under the same computational budget, despite the diffusion model being roughly 20 times larger than BRepA. Overall, our results show that geometry- and topology-aware B-Rep pretraining provides a powerful foundation for both understanding and generating CAD structures, serving as a versatile representation backbone for diverse downstream applications. We will release the code to facilitate future research.

title: blaris: Windowless Random-Access LZSS for Constrained Microcontrollers
authors: Ihor Lukianov
abstract: Embedded LZ77 decompressors (such as heatshrink and tamp) require an in-RAM sliding window that couples memory usage to compression ratio and incurs high latency on random-access reads. We present blaris, a lightweight, windowless LZSS decompressor for execute-in-place (XIP) random access on constrained microcontrollers. By partitioning tokens into bidirectionally traversable streams with power-of-two checkpoints, blaris resolves back-references directly in the compressed payload, achieving compression ratios comparable to high-window heatshrink and tamp configurations without allocating a RAM window. Targeting compress-on-host, decompress-on-device workflows, blaris assumes trusted build-time payloads and omits runtime error and bounds checks. On RV32IMC, it requires just 548-784 B of Flash and 104-112 B of total RAM, achieving orders-of-magnitude faster small-slice random reads than ratio-matched, block-indexed heatshrink and tamp.
comment: 4 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Source code and benchmark suite available at https://github.com/lis05/blaris
zh_title: blaris：面向受限微控制器的无滑动窗口可随机访问LZSS解压缩器
translation: 嵌入式LZ77解压缩器（例如heatshrink和tamp）需要占用RAM的滑动窗口，这使得内存占用与压缩率强相关，并在随机访问读取时导致较高的延迟。我们提出了blaris，这是一种轻量级、无滑动窗口的LZSS解压缩器，适用于受限微控制器上的就地执行（XIP）随机访问。通过将标记（token）划分为带有2的幂次检查点的双向可遍历流，blaris能够直接在压缩有效负载中解析后向引用，从而在不分配RAM窗口的情况下，获得了与大窗口配置下的heatshrink和tamp相当的压缩率。blaris针对主机端压缩、设备端解压的工作流程设计，假定构建时的有效负载是受信任的，因而省略了运行时错误和边界检查。在RV32IMC架构上，它仅需要548至784字节的Flash和104至112字节的总RAM，与压缩率相匹配的块索引heatshrink和tamp相比，其小切片随机读取速度提升了数个数量级。
tldr: blaris是一种专为受限微控制器设计的无RAM滑动窗口LZSS解压缩器，可在极低内存占用下实现出色的压缩率和极速的XIP随机读取。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新之处在于打破了传统LZ77/LZSS系算法在解压端必须在RAM中保留滑动窗口的限制，通过带有检查点的双向数据流直接在Flash/压缩载荷中回溯解析引用，极为契合RAM资源仅有几KB的超受限MCU及XIP（就地执行）场景。其局限性在于去除了运行时的错误与边界检查并假定数据可信，因此只适用于“主机端离线压缩、设备端部署”的受信场景，无法直接用于处理不受信的外部输入数据。
motivation: 现有的嵌入式LZ77解压缩器（如heatshrink和tamp）需要片上RAM滑动窗口，导致内存占用与压缩率耦合，并在执行随机访问读取时产生较高的延迟。

results: 在RV32IMC架构上，blaris仅占用548-784字节的Flash和104-112字节的RAM；其压缩率与采用大窗口配置的heatshrink及tamp相当；在小切片随机读取速度上，比同等压缩率且采用分块索引的heatshrink和tamp快数个数量级。

title: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness When Only a Few Hospitals Collaborate
authors: Adnan Malkani
abstract:
Clinical federated learning (FL) collaborations typically connect only three to six hospitals, yet Byzantine-robust aggregation rules are designed and benchmarked on synthetic partitions across dozens of equal-sized clients. We conduct an empirical audit of eight standard aggregation rules: FedAvg, coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, Krum, Multi-Krum, Bulyan, geometric median (GeoMed), and Centered Clipping (CC). We evaluate both unweighted and sample-size-weighted variants across three cross-silo medical datasets from the FLamby benchmark: Fed-Heart-Disease ($n = 4$ hospitals), Fed-TCGA-BRCA ($n = 6$ regions), and Fed-ISIC2019 ($n = 6$ centres). We execute 54,214 training runs across enumerated attacker coalitions ($f \in \{1, 2\}$) paired with exact-twin leave-out controls that decompose performance drops into honest data loss versus adversarial attack damage.
  We report three findings. First, client-count validity checks fail to capture breakdown in skewed medical consortia: while $n = 6, f = 1$ satisfies every count condition except Bulyan's, assigning sample-size weights turns median and GeoMed into a clean-model dictatorship whenever a single hospital holds more than half the training data, and causes weighted median, GeoMed, and CC to collapse when that dominant centre attacks. Second, exact-twin leave-out controls reveal that when the largest hospital attacks, the apparent failure of count-based robust rules is predominantly caused by the loss of honest training data (7.5 to 10.4 points on ISIC) rather than adversarial perturbation (2.3 to 3.8 points on ISIC). Conversely, weight-dependent rules suffer large true attack damage (16.1 to 25.1 points on ISIC). Third, unweighted robust rules consistently discount whichever institution generates the most atypical parameter updates, penalizing the smallest hospital on Heart but penalizing larger institutions on TCGA and ISIC.

title: Think Before You Code: A Benchmark for Testing LLMs on Software Engineering Deliberation
authors: Ashman Mehra
abstract: Think Before You Code (TBYC) is a benchmark pipeline for studying whether code-focused language models can reason about software issues in ways that resemble human engineering deliberation. The benchmark curates GitHub issue discussions into structured records, extracts human discussion artifacts such as problems, solutions, constraints, rationales, and trade-offs, and then prompts models to generate issue-level "thoughts" using retrieved code context and few-shot examples. It converts model responses back into the same artifact space and evaluates them against human annotations using complementary metrics for artifact type detection, metadata matching, tag overlap, and semantic summary similarity. Beyond scoring, this study includes visualization, leaderboard, and baseline tools that make it possible to compare models, prompting strategies, and extraction methods across repositories and issues. Think Before You Code is an end-to-end evaluation environment for measuring how closely LLM software reasoning aligns with human strategic judgment.

title: Arboreus: A Realistic Boreal Forest Simulator with Topographic Terrain and Satellite-Informed Parametric Tree Distributions
authors: F. Labra Caso, A. Saradagi, A. Koval, G. Nikolakopoulos
abstract: This work presents Arboreus, a realistic Boreal forest simulator, developed to support statistical validation of robotic autonomy algorithms in Boreal forest environments. Arboreus presents an automated methodology for synthesizing large-scale, data-informed, plausible forest worlds from parametric trees, height-variant terrain, and satellite-informed tree density distributions. The parametric generation of dominant Boreal tree species such as Birch, Spruce, and Pine is guided by trunk, canopy, and foliage parameters, extracted from growth studies in the Nordic areas. Tree distribution in an area of interest is guided by the Copernicus satellite dataset, which provides tree cover density and dominant species type at up to 10m raster resolution. The forest floor generation is guided by topographic data from the Swedish cadastral agency to produce realistic data-informed terrains. Given coordinates and extents of forested areas of interest, Arboreus synthesizes data-informed plausible forests, while offering flexibility to inject user observations of real forests (detail, age, dimensionality and tree count), which is critical for realistic synthetic data generation and for the testing of feature-sensitive autonomy algorithms. The applicability of Arboreus for benchmarking and validation of robot autonomy for different robot mobilities is demonstrated in Gazebosim, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim physics engines. The applicability of Arboreus as a source of synthetic forest data and its potential to support downstream forest resource mapping research (volume estimation, tree instance segmentation and stem attribute estimation) is also demonstrated. Arboreus has been open-sourced along with a dataset comprising 25 Boreal forest worlds of size 1000m2 corresponding to three real forest sites.

title: Can Verifiable PIR Match the Online Efficiency of SimplePIR?
authors: Xinxuan Zhang, Ruida Wang, Zirui Wang, Yuming Guo, Jikang Bai, Yuanju Wei, Yi Deng, Xianhui Lu
abstract: Verifiable Private Information Retrieval (vPIR) ensures that a malicious server cannot return tampered database records, but it traditionally incurs significant overhead compared to classical PIR.Recent advancements, notably VeriSimplePIR, approach the online efficiency of SimplePIR by introducing a proof preprocessing phase and requiring only lightweight client-side online verification. However, this scheme relies on an additional Short Integer Solution (SIS) assumption and SIS-based commitments, which only support relaxed range proofs. Consequently, these schemes are forced to adopt significantly weaker parameter choices, resulting in additional online overhead. In this paper, we propose a novel vPIR protocol that employs a newly designed error-correcting code-based commitment scheme as the database digest. This approach (i)supports efficient proofs of linear relations, (ii) achieves precise range proofs and (iii) eliminates the reliance on the SIS assumption. Thus, our scheme successfully adopts parameter choices identical to those of SimplePIR. As a result, our vPIR protocol is the first to achieve exactly the same online communication and server computation costs as SimplePIR, while keeping online client computation nearly identical. Additionally, compared to VeriSimplePIR,our protocol reduces online communication and client-side computation by approximately 20%, and decreases online server-side computation by over 35%.
comment: Accepted for publication at the 2027 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (IEEE S&P 2027)

title: A 4.542-approximation for the Small Cuts Cover problem via a multi-rate primal-dual algorithm
authors: Zeev Nutov, Elazar Koren
abstract: In the Small Cuts Cover problem we seek to cover by a min-cost edge-set the set-family of cuts of size $<k$ of a graph. Bansal, Cheriyan, Grout, and Ibrahimpur [ICALP 2023: 15:1-15:19] showed that the classic primal-dual algorithm with reverse delete of Williamson, Goemans, Mihail, and Vazirani [STOC 1993: 708-717] achieves approximation ratio $16$ for this problem. The analysis of the approximation ratio was then improved in a sequence of papers, culminating in the $5$-approximation by Simons, Bansal, and Cheriyan. A matching example of Nutov shows that this bound is tight for the classic algorithm. We improve the approximation ratio to $(3+\sqrt{37})/2<4.542$ using a multi-rate primal-dual algorithm (that applies for strongly pliable set-families) in which the dual variables of the inclusion-minimal violated sets are not raised uniformly, but with different rates. We also provide a tight example. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example in network design where for the standard LP, an efficiently computable choice of growth rates improves on the tight guarantee of uniform growth.

title: Action-outcome coupling: a pre-investment feasibility audit for offline reinforcement learning in supply chain operations
authors: Tung Dang, Hung Phung, Son Lam Nguyen, Tu Nguyen
abstract: Prescriptive analytics initiatives in logistics, such as offline reinforcement learning and next-best-action systems, are often funded before anyone verifies that the available historical logs can support an improved decision policy. We formalise this pre-investment feasibility question via action-outcome coupling: a total-effect variance index measuring how much expected outcomes change with the logged action. Coupling provides an algorithm-independent upper bound on any policy's achievable value, expressed in monetary units per decision for both single-step and discounted sequential objectives. We also analyse the asymptotic false-licensing risk of an invalid workflow: fitting a value model and evaluating the model's greedy policy on the same data. The false-licence rate is driven mainly by the number of state cells over which selection is performed, rising from the nominal test level with one cell to near certainty with a few dozen, while overlap has a smaller effect. We then propose an audit that assigns logs to four tiers of decision support, separately for fixed and contextual policies, and returns an explicit stopping rationale. On a randomised e-commerce log, the audit endorses a fixed recommendation policy, certifying gains equal to 30 per cent of the theoretical ceiling; the remaining gap reflects bound looseness under an 80-action design. Two public logistics logs fail at different checkpoints: one because the target is an accounting identity of the action, and another because, with 27 clusters, estimated coupling stays below the design's detectability threshold even though a conservative offline learner certifies an improvement in 29 of 30 seeds.

title: A short proof of the 1-1/e performance of RANKING on the complete upper triangular instance
authors: Giovanni Montanari, Nadav Merlis, Simon Mauras, Vianney Perchet
abstract: The randomized online bipartite matching algorithm RANKING of Karp, Vazirani and Vazirani (1990) matches, asymptotically, a fraction $1-1/e$ of the vertices of the complete upper triangular (CUT) instance. We give a short proof of this fact that looks at the final matching from the offline side. A single observation drives the argument: the first $k$ arrivals can distinguish the offline vertices $v_k,\ldots,v_n$ only through their ranks. As a consequence, whether $v_k$ is matched is decided by a uniform draw among the remaining ranks, and the number of matched vertices among $v_1,\ldots,v_k$ is a Markov chain with explicit transition probabilities. A linear differential equation, solved by hand, gives the limiting profile of this chain, and the constant $1/e$ appears where the matching probability reaches one.

title: SWIR-cGAN: Synthesizing SWIR Bands Using VNIR Imagery from CBERS and AMAZONIA-1
authors: Alisson Cleiton de Oliveira, Rennan de Freitas Bezerra Marujo, Thales Sehn Körting
abstract: Spectral band synthesis is an important research topic in remote sensing. The Brazilian satellites CBERS-4, CBERS-4A, and AMAZONIA-1 provide high temporal resolution (1-3 days) visible and near-infrared (VNIR) imagery through the Wide-Field Imager (WFI), but lack short-wave infrared (SWIR) bands. Recent deep learning methods have shown promising results for spectral synthesis, but challenges remain for cross-satellite generalization and spectrally distant bands. This paper presents a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) with an attention-enhanced U-net generator and a multi-loss objective to synthesize Sentinel-2/MSI SWIR bands 11 (SWIR-1) and 12 (SWIR-2) from WFI VNIR inputs. Experiments used 4,125 patches for training and cross-validation and 1,026 unseen patches for testing, with hyperparameters optimized using a subset of the training data. On SWIR-1, the model achieved SSIM of 0.900, PSNR of 31.44 dB, and MAE of 0.019 in TOA reflectance. On SWIR-2, it achieved SSIM of 0.917, PSNR of 33.35 dB, and MAE of 0.015. Benchmarking was performed on the test dataset, with each model optimized separately prior to evaluation. SWIR-cGAN outperformed the baselines, particularly for SWIR-2. The ablation study identified the multi-loss as the main performance contributor, while the attention and residual modules provided additional improvements. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of synthesizing SWIR bands from WFI imagery. The SWIR-cGAN is available at https://github.com/marujore/swir-cgan.

title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
authors: Ruoyu Wang, Hao Zhong, Yanming Yang, Jiahao Tian, Lin Liu, Biao Gong, Guoshan Lu, Yiding Tian, Chunhua Shen, Zhenzhong Lan, Chi Zhang
abstract: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.

title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
authors: Hongyang Zhang, Boyuan Deng, Siyuan Feng, Kai Chen, Junbo Zhang
abstract: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses. Their low inference cost and response latency make them attractive for transportation problems with predefined alternatives. This paper investigates their effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency in two representative transportation tasks: individual travel-mode choice prediction and sequential traffic signal control. We systematically evaluate TypeSafe Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions against conventional transportation methods, reinforcement learning algorithms, and four chat-based large language models. Experiments on the Swissmetro dataset show that typed decision models achieve lower prediction accuracy than traditional discrete choice models and the strongest chat-based baseline, while their performance varies substantially with input representation and question framing. In closed-loop traffic signal control experiments, typed decision models demonstrate competitive performance against established controllers in several scenarios, but exhibit performance degradation under more challenging network conditions. Furthermore, the typed models achieve lower inference latency and computational cost than the evaluated chat-based large language models, highlighting their potential for efficient, zero-shot transportation decision-making. Overall, these findings demonstrate both the potential and limitations of typed decision models, emphasizing the importance of input design, task characteristics, and robustness evaluation for their effective application in transportation systems.

title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
authors: Yanjie Dong
abstract: We investigate communication-efficient federated learning over heterogeneous datasets in the presence of Byzantine adversaries capable of uploading arbitrary information. Penalty-based methods bound the influence of each worker through the bounded gradient of a penalty function; however, the bound is lost once the uploads are compressed, since a Byzantine worker can accumulate an unbounded state at the server. To retain the Byzantine resilience under compressed uploads, we propose a projected penalty-gradient tracking framework, where each honest worker uploads a compressed residual of its penalty gradient and the server projects each reconstructed state onto the known penalty-gradient ball. The framework accommodates any contractive compressor and yields two algorithms: fault-resilient proximal gradient with consistent sparsification (FRPG-CS), whose shared mask is protected by freshly drawn reserve rows, and lazily aggregated FRPG (LAG-FRPG), whose uploads are event-triggered. For smooth and strongly convex losses, we establish a finite-time bound on the expected objective gap, where the Byzantine error floor is independent of the compressor and the compression error decays faster than the optimization error. We also bound the expected number of lazy uploads and derive certificates that separate the finite-penalty model bias from the optimization error. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST show that the proposed algorithms attain the highest accuracy among twelve methods under the Min-Max attack, whereas a compressed-momentum benchmark and a local-update benchmark remain preferable in attack-free accuracy and total traffic, respectively.

title: Sideslip-Conditioned Drift Trajectory Planning with Flow Matching and Control Barrier Functions
authors: Seokjun Lee, Seung-Hyun Kong
abstract: Drifting, the deliberate control of a vehicle at large sideslip angles, is relevant to both motorsport and recovery from unexpected oversteer. Existing autonomous drifting methods typically determine drift intensity through predefined reference trajectories, optimization objectives, or learned policy rewards, rather than accepting a desired sideslip angle as an explicit input. We propose, to the best of our knowledge, the first generative drift trajectory planner explicitly conditioned on a requested peak sideslip angle. A conditional flow matching model is trained on demonstrated drift laps with hindsight-derived sideslip labels and refined through reinforcement fine-tuning. A control barrier function (CBF) correction is then applied to satisfy model-based road, tire friction, and actuator constraints at the planning waypoints. In closed-loop experiments in the racing simulator Assetto Corsa, a nonlinear model predictive controller tracks the generated plans for six requested sideslip angles from 20 deg to 45 deg, with 30 laps (approximately 75 km) per request. The median peak sideslip angle measured across drift-corner passes follows the requested angle, with a mean absolute error of 1.2 deg across the six conditions. Ablation experiments show that reinforcement fine-tuning improves conditioning accuracy, while CBF correction substantially reduces off-road and spin events.
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Under review. Demonstration video: https://youtu.be/nskukDD1MFg

title: LASH-PAT: Deadlock-Free Adaptive Shortest-Path Routing for Inter-Chiplet Interconnects
authors: Patrick Iff, Torsten Hoefler
abstract: With the slowdown of transistor scaling, chipletbased systems, and in particular chiplet-based wafer-scale integration, have emerged as a promising approach to sustain growth in computing capability per cost for modern processors and accelerators. In recent years, many specialized inter-chiplet interconnect topologies have been proposed. In these topologies, the simple, well-established, and deadlock-free dimension-order routing scheme is not applicable due to its reliance on regular mesh structures. In this work, we study routing in these recently proposed inter-chiplet interconnect topologies by categorizing and evaluating nine deadlock-free routing functions for irregular topologies known from data center networking in this new context. This reveals a trade-off between turn-based routing, which enables path diversity, and layered routing, which ensures shortest-path delivery. To resolve this trade-off, we propose LASH-PAT, a routing function that extends layered shortestpath routing with adaptive path diversity. LASH-PAT supports multiple shortest paths and dynamically selects among them based on local congestion while preserving deadlock freedom. When compared to the best-performing baseline routing function for each combination of topology, traffic pattern, and evaluated metric, LASH-PAT improves throughput by 21.15% and reduces energy per packet by 12.77%, while providing latency comparable to the lowest-latency baseline routing function.

title: The Shared Word: Evaluating Language Models on Dutch Word Puzzles
authors: Rik van Noord, Maurice Voors
abstract: Many LLM benchmarks for languages other than English are translated, multiple-choice, or difficult to score automatically. We introduce The Shared Word (TSW-NL), a Dutch benchmark built around four core principles: it is language-specific, open-vocabulary, human-curated, and deterministically scored. Each puzzle gives three clues that describe different senses or uses of the same Dutch word. The clues are individually ambiguous, requiring the solver to combine evidence across multiple clues. We construct the benchmark from Dutch Wikipedia disambiguation pages, followed by automatic filtering and extensive manual curation. The final dataset contains 222 instances, with three independent human answers per test item. The task is clearly challenging: scores in our human study range from 49.5% to 61.0% and the highest-scoring open-weight model we tested reaches only 39.3%. Many others even score below 20%. At the same time, closed-source models show great progress: GPT-4.1 (April 2025) scores 59.2%, whereas GPT-5.6 Sol with max reasoning scores 88.8%. We believe this task provides a useful addition to Dutch model evaluation, plus a clear recipe that can be applied to construct a similar benchmark for other languages.

title: Binary Affine Optimization with Nearly-Graphic Constraint Matrices
authors: Qiming Fang, Sihong Shao, Yuxuan Wu
abstract: We present a polynomial-time algorithm for binary affine optimization with a linear objective when every column of the constraint matrix has Hamming weight at most 2, and prove that the problem is NP-hard when every column of the constraint matrix has Hamming weight exactly 3. We obtain fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms for the unrestricted problem provided that a nearly-graphic certificate is given, where the certificate roughly measures how far the constraint matrix is from having columns of Hamming weight at most 2. We apply our FPT algorithm to Max-Lin$_2$ on graphs and obtain FPT algorithms parameterized by the contraction distance and contraction rank of the graph, utilizing the concept of Eulerian-spanning set. In the case of contraction distance, another FPT algorithm can be used to find the corresponding certificate; that is, we obtain an FPT algorithm that requires no information beyond the problem instance itself.

title: A Transformer-Derived Iterative Preconditioner
authors: Patrick Lutz, Themistoklis Haris, Aditya Gangrade, Venkatesh Saligrama
abstract:
Transformers trained on in-context prediction problems can learn known numerical algorithms, e.g., gradient descent. We go further, showing that their internal computations can reveal new algorithms with provable guarantees. A softmax-attention transformer trained to solve linear systems $Xw=y$ implicitly improves matrix conditioning. Tracing $XX^\top$ reveals an iterative preconditioning primitive, which we develop into RAPID, a standalone algorithm requiring no learned components.
  RAPID is an anytime preconditioner for symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices, using randomized mixing and sparse local corrections to improve conditioning. Proof-of-concept experiments on synthetic and real-world problems consistently improve conditioning and reduce conjugate gradient iterations needed to reach a target accuracy. For a Haar-mixing idealization, we prove convergence to any fixed target condition number regardless of spectral distribution, with only logarithmic dependence on initial conditioning. Together, these results show how a transformer can discover a broadly applicable numerical algorithm.

title: The Kernel Reality Check: Benchmarking and Distilling Efficient Attention at Scale
authors: Fırat Öncel, Cem Subakan, Mirco Ravanelli, Çağatay Yıldız
abstract: Kernelized attention methods, which aim to replace the $O(N^2)$ complexity of softmax attention with $O(N)$ alternatives, have been the focus of intense research in the last five years. Despite growing interest, systematic evaluations and fair comparisons across approaches and scales are still missing. We analyze kernelized attention in two halves and highlight prominent limitations on each. On efficiency, FlashAttention achieves lower memory consumption and faster wall-clock time than SOTA kernelized methods during training and in vision transformers across most sequence lengths (with inference-time memory in causal language models the only clear exception), contradicting the core assumption for pure kernelized attention used as a drop-in replacement for softmax. We also discover that reported efficiency gains often fail to reproduce against modern baselines. On quality, current kernelized methods leave gaps of 2-10 points relative to softmax under a unified distillation protocol, and model scala alone does not close these gaps. We show this gap is not intrinsic to kernelization: LARA++, a principled extension of LARA that approximates softmax via importance sampling with adaptive proposal distributions, recovers up to 99% of softmax accuracy. We establish that the gap is closable; however, the computational overhead remains substantial, leaving the efficiency wall intact. Code is available at https://github.com/firatoncel/KernelRealityCheckNeurIPS2026

title: Sim2CBF: From Forward Simulations to Implicit Control Barrier Function Safety Filtering without Model Derivatives
authors: Luzia Knoedler, Yihan Liu, Shaohang Han, Yifei Dong, Jana Tumova
abstract: Failure avoidance in complex robot-environment interactions is challenging because the underlying dynamics are difficult to model accurately, and available predictive models may not provide reliable derivatives. We present Sim2CBF, a failure-avoidance framework that solves the Control Barrier Function (CBF)-Safety Filter (SF) optimization problem using only forward-model evaluations, thereby avoiding differentiation of the predictive model. Specifically, we approximate the CBF constraint using finite differences and local linear interpolation over sampled control inputs while preserving failure-avoidance guarantees. The underlying CBF is implicit and constructed from backup-policy rollouts, enabling the use of expressive predictive models such as physics-based simulators and learned world models. Compared with purely sampling-based SFs, our formulation requires fewer control samples and yields less conservative behavior than direct nominal-backup blending. We evaluate Sim2CBF in simulation, hardware box-toppling, and vision-based control tasks, demonstrating its applicability to contact-rich and learned dynamics, as well as its adaptability to changes in the predictive model.

title: Can Decision Models Replace LLMs in Real-World Contact Center Classification and Judging Tasks?
authors: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Xue-Yong Fu, Shashi Bhushan TN
abstract: Contact center systems often need to make bounded decisions, such as identifying a caller's intent, retrieving the knowledge-base article that answers a query, assessing agent compliance, or judging the output of AI models used in production. Decision models return a typed answer and its probability directly, making them a promising cost-effective alternative to generative Large Language Models (LLMs) in such bounded conversational tasks. However, their effectiveness in real-world contact center applications remains unclear. In this paper, we compare nine decision models against thirteen generative LLMs in zero-shot settings across eight contact center use cases: six classification tasks and two judging tasks. Our experiments demonstrate that many decision models can match the performance of frontier LLMs on contact center classification, and API-based closed decision models achieve this at the lowest per-request cost among the API models we evaluate. We further observe that their confident predictions are more accurate, enabling selective routing in real-world production scenarios. Across classification tasks, the main weakness of most decision models is abstention: they rarely choose the no-answer option, which accounts for most of their gap to the strongest LLMs (although Gemini-Decision-1 is the notable exception in this regard). We also find that the judging quality of decision models drops sharply for smaller models, and they are also more prone to position bias. In short, our findings provide practical guidance for selecting decision models based on abstention behavior, confidence, and deployment cost, rather than overall accuracy alone.

title: Fiberpose: state-of-the-art fiber morphometry and instance segmentation with a distance-transform neural network
authors: Viktor A. Balashov, Daniil S. Antonenko
abstract: Analysis of fibrous structures in SEM images is a routine task in biomedical engineering and materials science. However, most available methods for fiber quantification still rely on classical image binarization followed by simple post-processing. These approaches often produce unreliable results in images with weak boundaries, heterogeneous contrast, and densely packed fibers. Here, we introduce Fiberpose, a framework that reformulates fiber analysis as direct regression of a smooth distance-transform (DT) field, together with a novel set of geometry-based algorithms specifically adapted to this representation. The predicted field directly encodes fiber geometry, while the accompanying algorithms enable instance reconstruction and measurement of diameter and orientation within a unified workflow. The framework is implemented as a standalone Python desktop application and a web tool https://fiberpose.org. On an independent dataset of fibrous SEM images, Fiberpose achieved state-of-the-art instance-segmentation accuracy in comparison with SAM2 and Cellpose-SAM, and more accurate diameter measurements than DiameterJ, Fibar and GIFT. The method remains effective in dense and weakly contrasted regions and shows qualitative generalization across microscopy modalities not represented in the training data. Fiberpose therefore provides an interpretable geometric representation and an automated pipeline for reproducible quantitative characterization of fibrous materials.

title: ResoLUT: Distilling Residual Networks into Lookup-Table Networks
authors: Katarzyna Fojcik, Aidas Mikalauskas, Matthias Kampa, Renaldas Zioma, Jogundas Armaitis
abstract: Logic networks built from Boolean gates or lookup tables (LUTs) promise efficient hardware inference, but training them at depth and learning their connectivity remain difficult. We do not train logic as logic. Instead, ResoLUT distills a trained residual network (ResNet) layer by layer into LUT trees, preserving its multi-bit residual stream and BatchNorm while extracting connectivity from the teacher rather than learning it. To our knowledge, ResoLUT is the first convolutional logic network in computer vision to retain a ResNet-style multi-bit residual stream. Hard LUT decisions are used throughout training and inference, avoiding a discretization gap in the logic. ResoLUT-20 reaches 95.66% on CIFAR-10 with twice the trees, and ResoLUT-56 reaches 78.87% on CIFAR-100 and 53.69% on ImageNet at 64px, the best results of logic and lookup-table networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, showing that LUT networks can scale in depth. We explore and quantify the role of the residuals and the tree budget and shape. The most optimized model, a ResoLUT-8 with one eighth of the trees and further optimizations, fits on an FPGA and reaches 90.04% at 189k images per second, the highest throughput among the compared models above 85% on CIFAR-10.

title: Is model self-assessment enough for diverse LVLM ensembles?
authors: Michael Smith, Frank P. Ferrie
abstract: Ensembles of diverse Large Vision Language Models have demonstrated performance beyond that of single models across multiple datasets and tasks. However, the necessary aggregation process usually relies on training, parameter fitting, or complex task-specific pipelines. Furthermore, evaluation is limited, making a fair comparison difficult. We create a unified pipeline where we perform candidate response selection: we build an ensemble by selecting the best answer from a set provided by different models. We comprehensively evaluate across 34 different means of confidence estimation, 24 ensemble configurations, 20 datasets, and two prompt specifications. We show that simple training and parameter-free approaches can be sufficient, even for ensembles of different architectures. These simple self-assessment approaches rely solely on each constituent model's confidence, without explicit calibration, yet are able to perform better than said constituent models. They are also competitive with more involved alternatives on standard metrics such as accuracy, including on open-ended problems. However, we also discover that dataset, ensemble composition, and prompt wording are key confounding variables insufficiently explored by prior work that significantly affect ensemble performance, such that the ensemble can perform worse than its best constituent model. These must be optimized for to get the most out of ensembles, at the cost of limiting their generalizability. We recommend that practitioners consider training-free ensembles only if deployment conditions can be precisely characterized, with Best-of-N configurations of strong models being a good starting point.

title: Smoothing Bias and Direction Recovery at Boundary Minima of the Nuclear Norm along Matrix Lines
authors: Haocheng Wang, Yuanqi Zhang, Yi Xu
abstract: We study optimal matrix directions associated with minimizing $\|G+λΘ\|_*$, the nuclear norm along a fixed affine line of real matrices with scalar multiplier $λ$. At a rank-deficient minimum, the compact polar factor can violate the tangency constraint even at the minimizing multiplier. Spectral smoothing gives a continuous scalar equation for tangency. We quantify its bias at a unique boundary minimum, where exactly one one-sided derivative vanishes. An orthogonal block decomposition shows that pseudo-Huber smoothing with scale $δ$ shifts the multiplier by exact order $δ^{2/3}$ as $δ\to0$. The Frobenius error relative to the minimum-Frobenius-norm optimal direction has exact order $δ^{1/3}$ when some singular values vanish at exactly second order in the multiplier displacement, and $δ^{2/3}$ otherwise. A sharp rank bound rules out the slower rate when $Θ$ has rank at most two. Huber smoothing gives an error of exact order $δ$ for the same limiting direction. Convergent expansions in powers of $δ^{1/3}$ also yield a three-scale extrapolation with $O(δ)$ error after restoring feasibility.

title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
authors: Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Weihang Guo, Chen Wei, Lydia E Kavraki, Niloofar Mireshghallah, Steven Wu
abstract: Pixel-space diffusion learns visual representations and image generation jointly in a single end-to-end training stage, without a separately pretrained visual encoder. However, plain pixel-space Transformers still trail leading two-stage latent diffusion models in generation quality and training efficiency. We hypothesize that part of this gap arises from retaining one token per patch throughout the backbone, which does not explicitly encourage a visual hierarchy that summarizes related content at progressively coarser levels. To address this, we introduce Hierarchical Diffusion Transformers (HiT), which progressively group related tokens and represent each group with a single token. The main Transformer bottleneck processes these compact group tokens, and ungrouping restores features to their original image positions. A compression budget regulates the average compression ratio across the batch, allowing group memberships and counts to vary across images and diffusion timesteps during both training and generation. The model exhibits emergent semantic structure, learning to group coherent objects and object parts without segmentation labels. In text-to-image generation, HiT further learns to group caption words with image patches depicting the same concepts, without region annotations. HiT achieves 1.48 FID on ImageNet $256\times256$ and reaches comparable generation quality to JiT using approximately 40\% of its cumulative training FLOPs. For text-to-image generation, HiT exceeds UniLiP's average score across five benchmarks with roughly $6\times$ fewer denoiser parameters and $3\times$ fewer forward FLOPs. These results suggest that learning a visual hierarchy within the generator breaks down the barrier to stronger image generation without external visual pretraining.

title: DDSL: Iterative Self-Labeling for Financial Market States
authors: Xianbin Gu, Qingyue Zhu, Yuhong Geng
abstract: Financial market states lack a unique ground truth and must therefore be constructed from price data. Conventional labeling methods typically define states independently of the downstream classifier, leaving unresolved whether the resulting labels can be recovered from information available at prediction time. We propose DDSL, an iterative self-labeling framework that couples a price- and grammar-guided Viterbi labeler with a Transformer classifier through model feedback. DDSL constructs a nine-state representation that jointly encodes current and future market trends while retaining structured price emissions and temporal constraints throughout refinement. Experiments on SSE50, CSI300, CSI500, and NASDAQ100 show that DDSL increases held-out joint-state macro F1 by 78%-96% over single-pass dynamic-programming labeling. An independent GRU classifier that never participates in the labeling loop reproduces the same trend, while label entropy and class coverage remain stable, indicating that the gain transfers across architectures and is not caused by label collapse. We further show that learnability is controlled by both iteration and the model-feedback weight $β_{\mathrm{model}}$. Iterative gains diminish as successive label systems converge, whereas stronger feedback increasingly widens the performance gap between the feedback Transformer and the independent GRU. Increased learnability is accompanied by declining segment-level price-feature separation after an initial improvement. Finally, a non-anticipative event study provides partial external validation: refinement strengthens a conditional BEAR$\rightarrow$BULL reversal signal on the three A-share datasets, while the corresponding effect has the opposite sign on NASDAQ100. These results position DDSL as a structured framework for constructing market-state labels whose learnability can be explicitly controlled and evaluated.
comment: 17 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Conference version published in ICAIF 2026. Code available at https://github.com/hogwild/DDSL

title: Training-Free Building Change Detection with Example-Induced Discriminants
authors: Zhi Lu, Bin Hong, Zhenming Peng
abstract: Building change detection (BCD) relies on dense annotations that are costly to collect across regions. A few annotated examples offer a more economical way to specify the target, but change maps provide incomplete building supervision: they label only changed buildings and leave the building-containing date unspecified. Our key observation is that these annotations nevertheless reveal features that recognize buildings in other images, including unchanged ones. We present Linear INduced Discriminants (LIND), a training-free framework that turns regional feature contrasts into a reusable linear building classifier. Using a single frozen vision transformer, it unifies building recognition and temporal comparison in the same feature space. This approach requires neither text prompts nor an auxiliary segmentation model. Only one parameter is tuned on a single validation dataset and then kept fixed across datasets and shot settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong detection accuracy, cross-dataset transfer, and efficient inference, with extensions to other semantic classes and broader land-cover changes. Change annotations thus provide a compact visual specification for detection in new scenes. Code: https://github.com/lzcn/lind

title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models
authors: Xiaoyan Hu, Rohit Sonker, Jalal Butt, Jiayu Chen, Egemen Kolemen, Jeff Schneider
abstract: Many real-world optimization problems involve optimizing black-box objectives for which only a limited number of evaluations are available. Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for such problems, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in high-dimensional spaces. Recent work leverages diffusion models for black-box optimization, often through pre-training a reward-conditioned score network to steer generation towards high-reward samples. Alternatively, gradient-based guidance methods assume access to a differentiable reward function from which guidance gradients are queried. However, these approaches either require large amounts of labeled data for offline training or access to exact reward gradients, limiting their applicability in black-box settings. We propose BReaD (Black-box Reward-guided Sampling of Diffusion Model), a guidance sampling framework for optimizing black-box rewards without assuming access to a labeled dataset or reward gradients. The proposed method uses a Gaussian process (GP) as a differentiable surrogate for the unknown objective and actively queries labels for the generated samples. We provide a theoretical analysis of the total-variation distance between the generated distribution and the target distribution. Using Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) as guidance signals, our method balances exploration and exploitation during generation and enables the discovery of high-reward regions in the data space. Numerical experiments on scientific discovery and image generation tasks demonstrate that our framework can effectively optimize black-box rewards in low-data scenarios.

title: MI-Hyper: Generating Multiple Instance Models for Weight Space Transfer Learning in Histopathology via Mixed Tasks Pretrained HyperNetwork
authors: Xitong Ling, Yousef Kotp, Weiming Chen, Yining Li, Jiawen Li, Minxi Ouyang, Xinyi Guo, Mingxi Fu, Yizhi Wang, Tian Guan, Lianghui Zhu, Yonghong He
abstract: Zero-shot whole-slide image (WSI) prediction aims to generalize to new pathology tasks without parameter updates at deployment. MI-Zero makes these predictions by pooling patch-text similarities. Conditional weight generation, combined with supervision from diverse pathology tasks, offers an alternative: learning to construct predictive rules from task descriptions. We introduce MI-Hyper, a hypernetwork pretrained across mixed tasks to generate the aggregation and classification weights of multiple instance learning (MIL) models. We first train the generator and a shared MIL basis jointly using source labels. We then freeze the basis and refine the generator. The generated task weights are reused across cases. Across 308 tasks from 52 pathology datasets, MI-Hyper improves mean AUC, balanced accuracy and macro-F1 over MI-Zero by 1.85, 1.17 and 0.57 percentage points, respectively. On some molecular prediction tasks, both AUC and balanced accuracy improve by more than 20 points. These results support task-conditioned weight generation as a promising approach to weight-space transfer for long-sequence modeling.

title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
authors: Junyi Shen, Yao Lu
abstract: Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent. We find that much of this time is avoidable, for two reasons. First, 37.5% of the frames of a session's later films were drawn before, many shifted in time or inside an edited scene. Second, half of the builds stop at a check, where the agent needs only the verdict, but which builds stop is unknown until the checks finish. We present CodeReel, a training-free execution layer behind agents' existing commands. Exact frame reuse keys each frame by its drawing commands, regardless of its position in time, and reuses each frame whose key recurs. Blocking-aware scheduling runs the checks first and starts the render alongside them, at idle priority, unless the session's recent builds make a pass unlikely. Scheduling spends CPU to answer sooner and reuse returns it; exact keys let later versions use frames rendered for a failed one as the agent thinks. We introduce EditLoop, a benchmark of replayable agent sessions whose films are checked against renders from scratch.
