abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures activate only a subset of experts for each token, allowing large language models (LLMs) to scale parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation per token. However, intermediate data movement and uneven expert loads limit the efficiency of MoE inference on TPUs. To address these bottlenecks, we introduce Fuse-All MoE, a TPU kernel design that jointly optimizes expert computation, output communication, and load balancing. The kernel fuses token collection, expert projections, gated activation, and output writes, retaining expert computation intermediates on chip. Fixed token-slot destinations allow scheduling and expert placement to change while preserving routing semantics. In prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated serving, Fuse-All MoE balances EP16 prefill workloads through scheduling and expert redistribution, while symmetric EP8TP2 shares active expert computation between the two TensorCore devices within each chip during decode. Our experiments show that Fuse-All MoE reduces kernel runtime for a measured skewed EP16 prefill workload from 2.3x to 1.09x the same fixed reference time for a balanced workload. Across 32-512 decode tokens, symmetric EP8TP2 reduces kernel latency by up to 21.3% relative to fused EP16. With accompanying serving stack optimizations, the integrated system improves serving throughput by up to 34.5% over the Megablox EP16 baseline.

title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process
authors: Dohyun Kim, Jaeung Lee, Donghee Hong, Jaemin Jo
abstract: Tools for interpreting the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on LLMs themselves to both generate and evaluate explanations, creating a self-referential automated interpretation process with minimal human oversight. This automation raises significant reliability concerns, which are exacerbated by the absence of ground truth. In practice, it is difficult to validate explanations or to attribute interpretability failures to their source -- whether they originate from the tool's extracted representations or from the LLM used in the process. To address these challenges, we present DECODE, a visual analytics system that reintroduces human oversight into the automated interpretation process. Our approach decomposes the diagnostic workflow into three progressive stages, isolating failure sources ranging from structural defects to explanation-level misalignments. Drawing inspiration from inter-coder consensus in qualitative analysis, we utilize consensus among independently generated explanations and their evaluation metrics as a proxy for reliability. To further scale human inspection, we employ a three-phase active seeding protocol that strategically recommends high-priority instances for manual review. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study on 16,384 Sparse Autoencoder features, showing that it can efficiently identify and attribute interpretability failures at scale.

title: Implicit discretization of PID-like sliding-mode control with third-order output accuracy
authors: Martin Zapf, Benedikt Andritsch, Leonid Fridman, Martin Horn
abstract: A digital PID-like sliding-mode controller is proposed for a double integrator with a Lipschitz matched disturbance. A proper implicit discretization, matched to the exact sampled dynamics of the plant, attains the accuracy of the continuous-time controller without discretization chattering. Global finite-step convergence to a discrete-time sliding mode is established for two gain designs and every sampling time, using an implicit Lyapunov function and a computer-assisted certificate in exact arithmetic. The resulting controller provides third-order output accuracy, second-order accuracy for its derivative, and exact finite-time rejection of constant matched disturbances. These accuracy orders are proved to be optimal among deterministic causal controllers using the same sampled information.
comment: Extended version of a paper submitted to Automatica. 20 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Code and verification records: https://github.com/MartinZapf/Implicit-PID-like

title: AI-aided Decision-Making in Education - Uncertainty, Explainability, and Human Responsibility
authors: Fabian Kieser, Paul Tschisgale, Peter Wulff
abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based systems have become increasingly integrated into various aspects of everyday life, including education, understanding how these systems make decisions is of paramount importance. AI holds significant potential to enhance educational practices through the facilitation of personalized and adaptive learning, automation of assessment procedures, and assistance with administrative tasks. However, the opacity of AI-based decision-making in education (especially with deep learning and generative AI models) can hamper decision-making, especially when outcomes appear unjustified or incorrect. In this chapter, we argue that three key principles (uncertainty, explainability, and human responsibility) are essential for the legitimate use of AI in educational settings. Acknowledging the inherent uncertainties in AI-based decisions, analogous to those in human decision-making, is fundamental. Explainability is critical for ensuring that the functioning and outcomes of AI applications are transparent and comprehensible to both educators and learners. Furthermore, human responsibility is crucial, particularly in human decision-making, which remains indispensable across all stages of AI development and deployment. By examining these three principles, this chapter provides a comprehensive guide for stakeholders seeking to integrate AI thoughtfully and effectively into the educational system.
comment: Fabian Kieser and Paul Tschisgale contributed equally and share first authorship. This is a preprint of the following chapter: Kieser, F., Tschisgale, P., Wulff, P., "AI-Aided Decision-Making in Education: Uncertainty, Explainability, and Human Responsibility", published in "AI Roles and Responsibilities in Education", edited by S. Papadakis, 2025, Springer, reproduced with permission of Springer

title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models
authors: Zuyang Shen, Luqi Gong, Fanda Fan, Bingsong Wang, Xiang Ao, Yahui Wei, Minghao Liu, Chunjie Luo, Jianfeng Zhan
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) based on autoregressive (AR) next-token prediction entangle two factors: variable-context conditioning and prediction-unit factorization with autoregressive rollout. Strong AR performance therefore does not reveal whether generalization stems from the flexible training distribution, the local prediction target, the left-to-right inference process, or their combination. We propose FlexCast, a flexible context-target learning framework that disentangles these factors. FlexCast reformulates forecasting as variable-length masked prediction over time series patches: during pretraining, it dynamically samples visible context and masked target patches, exposing the model to diverse context-target configurations without sequential decoding. At inference time, the same pretrained model supports one-step forecasting, confidence-based iterative refinement, and next-token-style generation through a unified mask-and-predict interface, enabling controlled comparison of inference schedules under identical architecture, data, and objective. Evaluated on BLAST and multiple zero-shot benchmarks, FlexCast achieves accuracy competitive with or better than strong TSFM baselines while substantially reducing inference latency. Ablations confirm that context diversity and contiguous target masking drive performance, while left-to-right decoding does not yield consistent gains once flexible context-target relationships have been learned, suggesting that the key benefit of AR-style TSFMs lies in flexible training rather than sequential inference. The code is available at https://github.com/BenchCouncil/FlexCast.

title: Per-Agent-Safe Navigation of Globally Driven Robot Collectives via Affine Field Design
authors: Seunghwan Jang, Steven Ceron, Wei Xiao
abstract: Safe navigation of robot collectives requires coordinating motion and deformation so that the collective can traverse constrained environments while ensuring each robot's safety. Existing controllers for swarmalator collectives largely rely on local control, where each robot receives an individual command, which causes the control and communication requirements to grow with the number of agents. We introduce a broadcast control formulation in which a single spatially affine field governs both the motion and deformation of the collective. The scalar component of the field regulates collective size, and its spatial gradient generates collective translation through non-reciprocal interactions. Both components enter the collective dynamics directly, which allows per-robot wall, actuation, and cohesion constraints to be enforced using control barrier functions within a single quadratic program for the whole collective. The resulting controller continuously adapts the collective size to the local environment, and enables safe passage through corridors narrower than the unconstrained collective without pre-planned resizing. We further derive how the available actuation budget determines the reachable speed and minimum passable corridor width, and we demonstrate that two independently driven collectives can simultaneously traverse a shared junction using distinct fixed phase labels without inter-collective coordination.

title: Disentangling Forgetting from Utility: Lightweight LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Null-Space Projection
authors: Xiuyuan Wang, Weiming Liu, Zongxin Yang, Fan Wang, Liemiao Jin, Rubin Qin, Wei Chen, Bin Shi, Chaochao Chen, Xiaolin Zheng
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) pose significant security risks by retaining private or hazardous information, creating an urgent need for unlearning techniques that excise specific knowledge without compromising general utility. However, prevailing fine-tuning-based unlearning methods struggle to achieve this balance, often suffering from computational inefficiency and unintended utility degradation due to the entangled nature of knowledge within model parameters. To disentangle forgetting from utility, we propose UUE, a theoretically grounded framework that reformulates unlearning as controllable model editing. First, UUE projects parameter updates into the orthogonal left null space of retained knowledge representations, strictly ensuring that the editing process causes minimal interference to the model's general capabilities. Second, distinct from targeted mapping, we introduce a convex untargeted objective that derives a closed-form analytical solution to effectively disrupt undesired knowledge by pushing forget-set embeddings toward their antipodal points. We implement UUE via lightweight, pluggable adapters (including a low-rank variant, UUE-L), enabling efficient deployment without modifying the frozen backbone. Extensive experiments on TOFU and WMDP benchmarks demonstrate that UUE and UUE-L achieve superior unlearning efficacy, significantly outperforming existing methods.

title: Starlight: Whittle-Driven Fidelity Rescue for Satellite-Terrestrial Quantum Networks
authors: Yaliang Shi, Zhiwei Zhao, Bangguo Yuan
abstract: A planetary-scale quantum internet is constrained by exponential attenuation in terrestrial fibers. Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites provide a low-loss vacuum backbone, but limited satellite resources must be allocated among competing connections under continuously evolving and heterogeneous physical conditions. Existing satellite scheduling remains largely provisioning-oriented, optimizing satellite-resource assignment for aggregate entanglement delivery. Recent age-based approaches instead incorporate chronological freshness into entanglement scheduling. Neither line of work directly identifies the connections most urgently requiring satellite assistance as their physical states evolve. We propose Starlight, a demand-driven satellite-terrestrial entanglement routing architecture that targets degrading connections before their terrestrial entanglement becomes unusable. Starlight introduces Effective Age of State (EAoS), a physics-aware metric that maps heterogeneous decoherence and swapping-induced fidelity penalties onto a unified additive coordinate. Representing each connection by evolving EAoS, we formulate rescue scheduling as a Restless Multi-Armed Bandit (RMAB) problem and derive a closed-form Whittle-style index approximation for top-K selection. Starlight further employs a two-timescale control plane and an asynchronous dispatch-and-mask pipeline to suppress redundant in-flight allocations. Simulations show that Starlight achieves up to 84.5% average satisfaction under constrained rescue capacity and sub-0.5-ms orchestration at 1,000 connections, while remaining robust to heterogeneous memory decay and stochastic atmospheric degradation.

title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries
authors: Rajarshi Roy, Xiaowei Huang
abstract: Temporal specifications are essential for verification and monitoring, yet writing formulas that capture the intended behaviour is difficult. Active learning derives such specifications through interaction between a learner and a teacher, but remains underexplored for temporal logics. Existing approaches require the teacher to answer equivalence queries and to construct counterexamples, and they often rely on SAT-based learning procedures that restart the search after each new example. We present an active-learning framework for LTLf in which the teacher only labels traces and answers natural-language questions about the intended behaviour. The learner maintains an enumerated version space of candidate formulas, generates traces that distinguish candidates, and uses the teacher's hints to rank candidates or to restrict the search. We prove consistency with the observed examples, identification within bounded hypothesis classes with a bound on the number of queries, and a PAC guarantee for the final hypothesis. In experiments with a simulated teacher on 36 targets, including targets in four standard environments, the learner identifies every target when it compares all rivals, with fewer than seven queries beyond an initial sample of ten traces on average. Correct hints reduce the number of queries by up to 16% and the number of generated candidates by a fifth, and hints used for ranking never prevent identification, even when incorrect. Our enumeration-based version space is faster than the SAT-based approach of previous learners at every target size.

title: Speed-Variation Distillation for Generative Modeling
authors: Sukit Seripanitkarn, Phonphrm Thawatdamrongkit, Supasorn Suwajanakorn
abstract: While diffusion models excel at image generation, their denoising trajectories pass through corrupted intermediate states far from the image manifold. We ask whether generation can instead proceed through recognizable images throughout the entire trajectory. We introduce a generative framework built around a variation-reducing degradation process that contracts diverse images toward a shared prototype while preserving recognizable intermediate states. Because such manifold traversal lacks a simple analytical form, we construct the trajectories using generative-prior-based image morphing. We then distill the reverse process into a diversification operator that transforms the prototype into increasingly varied samples. To resolve the one-to-many ambiguity of the reverse process, we associate each trajectory with its initial noise latent and apply perturbations to improve robustness against accumulated errors. At inference, every step yields a recognizable image, allowing early termination and enabling a controllable speed--variation trade-off.

title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
authors: Astarag Mohapatra
abstract: We study encoder models that pick one of several options in a single forward pass, without generating text. This technical report compares recipes for fine-tuning UltraBERT-380M with one mask per option. The four recipes differ in how an option is scored and how the scores become probabilities; one follows the expert gate of DeepSeek-V3. Trained on the same data as Qwen3-0.6B with the LLM-as-Jev recipe (67.6% test accuracy), the encoder reaches 69.7% to 72.1%. Scoring an option by "yes" minus "no" instead of "yes" alone gives the larger gain, from 69.7% to 71.3% on the test set and from 57.8% to 59.6% on external benchmarks (56.1% for the decoder). Sigmoid normalisation adds 0.8 test points; a square-root softplus adds none. One request at a time on an NVIDIA A100, the encoder takes 29 ms per decision against 68 ms, but uses more peak memory (2.8 against 2.2 GiB). An auxiliary head, trained on human-marked evidence and on labels selected with a reward adapted from SelfCite, predicts in the same pass the sentences annotated as support for the answer.

title: Process Mining-Enabled Federated Anomaly Detection for the Industrial IoT
authors: Francesco Vitale, Salvatore Bramante, Francesco Flammini, Hangli Ge
abstract: While federated anomaly detection enables the integration of local data insights across diverse nodes to reduce false positives, it inherently struggles with non-IID data. In practice, industrial IoT plants often operate under varying conditions and experience diverse environmental phenomena, resulting in significant heterogeneity in the monitored time series. In such settings, standard federated learning approaches fail to perform nuanced aggregation that accounts for these cross-node differences, ultimately leading to increased false positive rates. In this paper, we propose a process mining approach to evaluate the similarity of local node data against a reference provided by a global node. The global node utilizes these similarity metrics to dynamically weight local models during aggregation, producing personalized updates distributed across the network. We evaluate our approach using industrial IoT time-series data collected from manufacturing plants operating under distinct conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that our process mining-enabled federated anomaly detection pipeline achieves superior performance, yielding a 46.52% and 11.99% relative improvement in F1-score compared to isolated local training baselines and standard FedAvg, respectively, alongside a 51.24% relative reduction in false positives over standard federated aggregation.
comment: Accepted to the IEEE Annual Congress on Artificial Intelligence of Things (IEEE AIoT 2026)

title: OmniScore-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Musical Score Reading
authors: Congren Dai, Zhancheng Guo, Danni Zhao, Wenchu Wang, Xiaobing Li, Maosong Sun
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about musical scores, but their ability to recognise notation, recover its structure and interpret its musical meaning requires separate evaluation. Existing optical music recognition (OMR) resources establish detection and transcription measurements; a transcription score alone leaves the strengths and bottlenecks of a VLM score reader unresolved. We introduce OmniScore-Bench, an evaluation of OMR capabilities in VLMs through 3,000 questions spanning six aspects and 24 task subtypes. Each question specifies a visible scope, reference annotations and an answer schema, enabling automatic evaluation from symbol localisation to musical consistency and evidence-linked question answering. Our assessment of twelve VLMs reveals operation-specific capability profiles and different transcription leaders across excerpt, single-page and multipage tasks. Controlled analyses examine the roles of score images, auxiliary givens and additional page context. On the tested subset, image removal exposes visual dependence in pitch and repeat interpretation while measuring how much performance remains with public context alone. Separate format and content analyses distinguish answer-format violations from musical errors. OmniScore-Bench supports diagnosing which score-reading operations VLMs perform reliably and which require improvement.

title: Protection-Oriented Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Fault Detection in Power Systems
authors: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Changhun Kim, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Johann Jäger, Siming Bayer
abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based fault detectors are increasingly proposed for power system protection, yet aggregate metrics can obscure the consequences of false and missed trips. We present a protection-oriented assessment of three ML detectors and a sequence-current reference on PROTECT-90, comprising 9,022 simulated fault episodes on a 90 kV double-circuit line. The assessment combines five window conditions, causal window-end labelling, episode-grouped cross-validation, and operating-point selection under a fixed security budget. It reports security, dependability, detection timing, decision margins, and episode-level nuisance assertions. Gradient-boosted trees, a convolutional neural network, and logistic regression achieve AUC-ROC values above 0.999, yet at a security budget of $10^{-3}$ their developed-fault missed-trip rates range from 0.007% to 1.99%. Post-clearing false-trip rates of approximately 0.12-0.16% per window coexist with nuisance assertions in 11.3-19.1% of episodes. Among the analysed physical descriptors, missed trips are most consistently associated with higher fault resistance within the sampled range. An analytical current proxy suggests a fault-current gradient only partly reproduced by waveform-derived current (rank correlation 0.62). No single topology state or faulted phase consistently dominates within the sampled domain. Because PROTECT-90 contains fault episodes only, security is assessed on pre-fault and post-clearing windows rather than independent non-fault disturbances.
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for oral presentation at the 21st International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2027), Hong Kong, 6-9 January 2027

title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining
authors: Md Rifat Arefin, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Ernie Chang, Chinnadhurai Sankar, Rylan Conway, Aristide Baratin, Irina Rish, Adithya Sagar, Patrick Huber
abstract: A temporary optimization intervention can increase validation loss when it ends yet reduce it at the final training budget. We demonstrate this with temporary weight decay in Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers with 162M, 405M, 1.4B, and 3.4B parameters. For models up to 1.4B parameters, moving a fixed-duration decay window from early to late training reverses its final effect. At 162M, changing window duration alters final loss even at approximately matched total shrinkage. Most strikingly, a schedule selected at 162M and transferred without retuning to 1.4B is 0.26 nats worse than no decay when removed, overtakes it only after 73% of training, and ultimately finishes 0.028 nats better while also outperforming the best sampled constant-decay baseline. Early decay leaves a persistent weight-norm deficit, which keeps relative steps larger after the intervention ends. An approximate norm-dynamics recurrence captures the slow convergence of these relative steps, and fixed-norm replays of the measured trajectories reproduce the performance ordering and a similar loss difference. At 162M and 405M, norm-reset experiments show that smaller weight norms at the end of the decay window explain most of the final loss improvement. A separate Gram intervention exhibits related post-removal norm and relative-step dynamics. These results show that temporary optimization schedules can have delayed effects long after removal and should therefore be evaluated at the intended final training budget, not only at removal.

title: What a Memory Preview Cannot Tell You: Ambiguity in AI Memory Permissions
authors: Sadia Noman Tonni, Nafis Fuad Shahid
abstract: A memory rule states when an assistant may reuse a remembered event, and an editor can confirm a rule by previewing one use it allows and one it blocks. We ask what such a preview lets a person infer about the rule they saved. For an editor with six or twelve valid rules, we enumerate every rule compatible with a preview. Splitting the rules most evenly does not target the question a user cares about. For an explicit preference, two adaptive tests leave all three recommendation scopes open (for a one-off choice the outcome turns on a tie), while one test of transfer to another task settles the question. Weak previews are also the default. Under the intended rule, 36 of 39 possible allowed/blocked pairs contain a blocked example that no rule allows, and no pair identifies the rule. Three or four tests suffice here; when permissions depend on each other, a fixed checklist grows to six or nine and adaptive questioning needs at most five or seven. These counts use a specified rule vocabulary and fictional events. In a small pilot, 10 of 20 people who saw such a weak preview of a rule they had just chosen mispredicted, or were unsure about, at least one of two uses, and none of those 10 said the outcomes matched what they wanted. Whether better previews help people is untested.
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Code and data: https://github.com/tonni19/memory-preview-ambiguity

title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
authors: Olaf Hellwich, Moritz Heine, Patrik Reiske, Sole Traverso, Katharina Hohlbaum, Henning Sprekeler, Christa Thöne-Reineke, Lars Lewejohann, Roman Bhuiyan
abstract: Video-based behavior estimation is often implemented end-to-end from image sequences. We advocate a two-stage alternative: reconstruct 3D body and object geometry before classifying behavior. This makes ambiguities of the ill-posed 2D-to-3D inverse problem explicit and potentially correctable. We demonstrate the strategy with simulated interacting mice and extend it to real video.

title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
authors: Tiantong Wang, Zhiren Gong, Yixin Wang, Tiantong Wu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim
abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can share experts across layers or computational steps, pooling training information from different contexts. This can reduce local prediction error, but multi-step systems are ultimately evaluated by their final outputs. We study when these local gains survive composition. In specified linear regression models, we derive exact sharing and merging criteria by balancing variance savings against bias from sharing across roles with different target behavior. Under a common fixed linear propagation map, we characterize expected squared final-output risk, retaining error directions and correlations. We construct cases where sharing lowers average local error yet increases final-output error. Within this setting, we also identify when orthogonal full pooling with isotropic noise preserves every local improvement at the final output. For general routed computations, we derive conditional end-to-end error bounds that account for distribution shifts, errors in surrounding components, and changes in expert selection. Separately, we show that correct predictions and route labels alone do not establish that individual experts implement the attributed operations. Controlled experiments realize a strict local-to-final risk reversal. In low-data symbolic settings, trained Transformers exhibit statistically supported teacher-forced one-step gains without statistically resolved free-running final-output gains. Separate intervention tests distinguish successful multi-layer actions from single-expert attribution and generalization to unseen transitions. Together, these results distinguish when sharing improves local estimation, when those gains survive to the final output, and what evidence is needed to attribute reusable operations to individual experts.

title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
authors: Mike He, Ankush Desai, Sharad Malik, Aarti Gupta
abstract: LLM agents that execute multi-step tool calls must satisfy two objectives simultaneously: completing the user's task (utility) and conforming to domain policies and correctness constraints (safety). These objectives are in tension -- blocking an unsafe action prevents a violation but can leave the agent stranded with no principled way to recover. Existing approaches sacrifice one objective for the other. We introduce Soteria, a framework that reconciles safety and utility through verified hierarchical planning and runtime enforcement of specifications. Before execution, the agent generates a structured plan that is formally verified against the specifications prior to any tool invocation. During execution, the verified plan serves dual roles: it ensures that the agent takes specification-conformant trajectories and provides guidance when unsafe actions are blocked. Across multiple benchmarks covering a diverse range of tool-use tasks, Soteria achieves 1.7 times the average task success rate of the best baselines, with no violations of policy specifications, demonstrating that safety and utility need not be traded off.

title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
authors: Kailai Sun, Zijie Gao, Mingyi He, Can Rong, Alok Prakash, Baoshen Guo, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao
abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption. By conditioning on static urban land use, DySENSE can generate realistic, diverse and new static urban imagery with aligned energy maps. By conditioning on dynamic monthly and climate prompts, DySENSE can jointly generate dynamic, monthly energy consumption maps while keeping the urban morphology static. Experiments across four cities (New York, Washington, Norfolk, Busan) demonstrated that DySENSE can generate annotated high-fidelity synthetic energy data using less than 25% labelled data, boosting downstream prediction performance by 8% mIoU, and achieving strong energy dynamic consistency. Compared to existing methods, DySENSE significantly improved prediction performance (8.7% accuracy) and reduced prediction error (9%-18% CVRMSE, ASHRAE). DySENSE offers an effective foundation for energy-efficient cities, peak-load analysis, building performance simulation and dynamic demand response for city, energy, and building science. The data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/skl24/MUSE2 and https://github.com/kailaisun/DySENSE

title: RuralShield: Super Intelligence-Assisted Security Triage and Serverless Infrastructure for Resource-Constrained Healthcare
authors: Mohammad Arman Ullah, Asif Ahmed
abstract: Resource-constrained healthcare providers must connect cloud security controls to an operational response process. Introducing language-model assessments adds an authorization problem: a recommendation must be converted into a permitted action against a specific resource. RuralShield combines a configurable serverless application foundation with structured model assessment, deterministic routing, and human-approved containment. Its design separates workload access, assessment validation, and action authorization so that each boundary produces inspectable records. We evaluate the implementation through a frozen 120-hour non-AI workload and separate desktop and AWS AI cohorts. The workload recorded 999,861 authenticated requests and 999,860 successful responses, with one HTTP 404 and one missing minute representing 139 scheduled requests. Median, 95th-percentile, and 99th-percentile Ohio client latencies were 28.57, 53.01, and 110.77 ms. Eight successful model requests exercised assessment and reporting in two four-case cohorts. The AWS cohort and five scripted controls produced nine completed workflows, including two human-approved Lambda containment cases with verified restoration of the original concurrency setting. Source-linked, checksum-verified archives preserved the records before scoped cleanup. The study demonstrates an inspectable integration of application controls and human-mediated AI response under the evaluated synthetic conditions.

title: PLL-Less Synchronization of Grid-Following Converters Using a Voltage-Driven Frenet Frame
authors: Jinhui Chen, Huadong Sun, Shiyun Xu, Bing Zhao, Peng Han, Federico Milano
abstract: In grid-following converters, the synchronization path can transmit voltage disturbances to the current loop under weak or unbalanced grid conditions. This paper develops a Frenet-frame controller that derives its axes from the integral curve of the measured voltage at the point of common coupling. The tangential current governs active power, while the normal and binormal currents govern the transverse components of non-active power. Feedforward terms derived from the output filter model compensate curvature and torsion coupling, yielding identical nominal current dynamics across the axes. The controller operates without a phase-locked loop or sequence extraction. A reduced transverse model accounts for the finite bandwidth of geometric rate reconstruction and predicts a reduction in low-frequency coupling from voltage disturbances to current. Controller hardware-in-the-loop tests using real-time simulation of a three-phase four-wire converter show the shortest settling time after an active power reference step and the smallest peak power deviations during balanced voltage disturbances among the tested controllers. Under single-phase voltage unbalance, the method reduces peak binormal current and maximum phase-current total harmonic distortion relative to both benchmarks. It also settles to the commanded power in a weak-grid connection test where the phase-locked loop benchmark exhibits sustained oscillations.

title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
authors: Zeinab Sharifi, Hossein Shirazi
abstract: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically. This survey introduces a unified formalism that describes every QGNN as an encoder, a graph-conditioned circuit, observables, and an optional classical head, together with a circuit-level condition for permutation equivariance and a resource model for comparing costs. We organize the literature into five architecture families (convolutional, equivariant, message-passing and recurrent, Hamiltonian, and hybrid) and compare them by qubit cost, symmetry, scalability, and evidence. We then review symmetry and geometric inductive biases (permutation, rotation, and Lorentz), the results on expressivity, trainability, noise, and scalability, and applications in high-energy physics, chemistry, finance, healthcare, earth observation, and transportation. An audit of datasets and evaluation practices leads to a minimum reporting protocol. Our main finding is that the design space is rich and symmetry is the best-supported inductive bias, whereas the evidence remains thin: results are mostly simulated, on small graphs, at parity with classical models or with fewer parameters, and no advantage has yet been established on tasks over classical graph data. We identify five open challenges and a research agenda covering provable advantage, equivariant and geometric designs, fault-tolerant implementations, and shared benchmarks. The coverage extends through 2026 and emphasizes recent work.

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design
authors: Xilong Wang, Xiaoxing Chen, Neil Gong
abstract: Multi-agent systems solve complex tasks by decomposing them into subtasks, delegating the subtasks to agents, and aggregating the agents' responses using an aggregation rule. Malicious agents can manipulate the final solution by providing malicious responses to their assigned subtasks. In this paper, we first propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA), which iteratively optimize malicious responses to maximize attack effectiveness. Specifically, we formulate untargeted and targeted attacks as optimization problems and develop an approach to approximately solve these problems by iteratively refining malicious responses based on feedback from a surrogate multi-agent system. To defend against such attacks, we further propose SecMAS, a secure aggregation rule that leverages the semantic similarities among agent responses to select the response that is most consistent with a sufficiently large subset of the other responses. We theoretically establish security guarantees for SecMAS against both untargeted and targeted attacks. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that existing aggregation rules are vulnerable to ReMA, whereas SecMAS effectively defends against all evaluated attacks, including adaptive variants of ReMA, while maintaining utility comparable to that of existing aggregation rules.

title: See and Detect: Image-Driven Open-Vocabulary Multi-View 3D Object Detection
authors: Yating Xu, Na Zhao, Chenhan Jiang, Qingwen Zhang, Jiankang Deng, Jifei Song
abstract: Recent open-vocabulary multi-view indoor 3D detection methods typically follow a point-cloud-driven pipeline, where pseudo 3D boxes are generated from reconstructed or estimated geometry and semantic labels are inferred from projected regions. However, such a design makes box generation dependent on the completeness of point clouds and restricts semantic learning to local appearance, causing inferior 3D object localization and open-vocabulary classification. In this paper, we present See and Detect, an image-driven framework that uses multi-view images as the primary evidence for 3D box and semantic label generation. For box generation, we first discover object candidates from individual images, enabling objects missing in point clouds to be recovered from visual evidence. However, single-view predictions are often noisy and redundant. To address this, we propose multi-view consensus box consolidation to fuse spatially consistent predictions across views, and box quality assessment to reduce the impact of boxes with partial object coverage. For semantic label generation, we introduce context-aware semantic learning, where semantic labels are queried from full image context, enabling more accurate semantic prediction. Extensive experiments on ScanNet and ARKitScenes demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art open-vocabulary multi-view 3D detection performance while running over 500$\times$ faster than the previous state-of-the-art method.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian physics-augmented neural networks for populations of hyperelastic laws: specimen variability and uncertainty from scarce, noisy data
authors: Vincent C. Scholz, Phaedon-Stelios Koutsourelakis
abstract: The hyperelastic law of a material such as soft tissue differs between specimens, and often only a few specimens can be tested. Physics-augmented neural networks (PANNs) learn such laws from data without a prescribed functional form while keeping them physically admissible, and Bayesian versions of related models quantify the uncertainty of the law of one specimen or of a pooled group of specimens. A pooled fit, however, attributes the differences between specimens to measurement noise or to uncertainty about a mean law, and neither describes a new specimen. We first develop a Bayesian PANN for one specimen, whose priors keep the learned law plausible for few, noisy data. We then extend it to a hierarchical Bayesian PANN, a nonlinear mixed-effects model in which all specimens share learned polyconvex features and each specimen is a draw from a population of laws. Features, specimens, and population are inferred jointly by variational inference, with a separate model of the measurement noise, so that the variability between specimens is not mistaken for noise, the population carries its own uncertainty, and every specimen drawn from it is polyconvex. The population predicts the response of new specimens with credible intervals, without data or from a partial test, and assigns them to cohorts with quantified uncertainty, all without a prescribed form of the law. On synthetic populations, it recovers the population from few specimens and predicts new specimens more reliably than three published methods. On Treloar's rubber and on healthy and aneurysmal aortas, it reaches the accuracy of a deterministic PANN and assigns no aorta specimen to the wrong cohort with confidence, although it underestimates the uncertainty of untested curves.

title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
authors: Songming Zhang, Yuxiao Luo, Shifu Luo, Siran Chen, Shuquan Su, Jinyan Li
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) prediction from histology aims to infer spatially resolved gene expression profiles directly from tissue images. This is a challenging problem that is currently often addressed with complicated model architectures, additional inputs, and complicated training procedures, while remaining limited to fixed, small gene panels. This raises a natural question: Is there an efficient method for large-panel ST prediction? Here, we present GeneFlow, a simpler yet effective framework for large-scale spatial gene expression prediction that unifies flow-matching generative modeling with structured multimodal fusion. Specifically, GeneFlow first encodes both histological morphology and cross-gene interactions in spatial spots through histology and gene tokenizers. The model directly predicts spatial gene expression, rather than an intermediate velocity field, while being trained with a velocity-based flow-matching objective. We show that, even without relying on heavy generative pipelines, GeneFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple ST benchmarks, with up to 56.8% gains in 1,000-gene prediction. Extensive experiments further show that GeneFlow produces biologically meaningful spot profiles while reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude, thereby improving efficiency and scalability, particularly in clinical settings. We believe GeneFlow provides an opportunity for leveraging widely available histology images for downstream biological discovery. Code is available at: https://github.com/ZZhangsm/GeneFlow
zh_title: 更多基因，更快推理：基于组织学的高效大Panel空间转录组预测
translation: 基于组织学预测空间转录组（ST）旨在直接从组织图像推断具有空间分辨率的基因表达谱。这是一项极具挑战性的任务，目前通常需要复杂的模型架构、额外的输入以及繁琐的训练过程，且预测范围往往局限于固定的、小规模基因集合。这自然引出一个问题：是否存在一种用于大Panel空间转录组预测的高效方法？在此，我们提出了GeneFlow，一个更简洁但高效的大规模空间基因表达预测框架，它将流匹配（flow-matching）生成模型与结构化多模态融合结合在一起。具体而言，GeneFlow首先通过组织学和基因分词器对空间位点中的组织形态学以及基因间相互作用进行编码。该模型利用基于速度的流匹配目标进行训练，同时直接预测空间基因表达，而不是中间速度场。我们表明，即使不依赖繁重的生成管线，GeneFlow在多个ST基准测试中也取得了最先进的性能，在1,000个基因预测任务中提升高达56.8%。大量实验进一步表明，GeneFlow不仅能生成具有生物学意义的位点图谱，还将计算成本降低了数个数量级，从而提高了效率和可扩展性，尤其是在临床环境中。我们相信GeneFlow为利用广泛可用的组织图像进行下游生物学发现提供了良机。代码公开在：https://github.com/ZZhangsm/GeneFlow。
tldr: 提出了一种结合流匹配与多模态融合的高效框架GeneFlow，大幅提升了从组织图像预测千级基因空间表达的精度并显著降低计算开销。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地将流匹配生成目标与直接回归表达量相结合，克服了传统生成模型迭代采样推理慢的缺陷；同时解决了大基因Panel难以建模与高计算成本的问题，兼顾了高精度、生物学可解释性与临床落地实用性。
motivation: 现有的从组织学图像预测空间转录组的方法模型结构复杂、训练繁琐且依赖额外输入，且多局限于小规模固定基因集，亟需一种能够用于大Panel空间基因表达预测的高效方法。
method: 提出GeneFlow框架，将基于速度的流匹配目标与结构化多模态融合相结合。利用组织学和基因分词器对组织形态和位点内跨基因相互作用进行编码；模型采用流匹配目标进行训练，但直接预测空间基因表达量而非中间速度场，从而省去沉重的生成采样管线。
results: 在多个空间转录组基准上取得SOTA性能，在1000个基因的大Panel预测任务中提升高达56.8%；在生成具有生物学意义图谱的同时，将计算成本降低了数个数量级。
conclusion: GeneFlow显著提升了大Panel空间转录组预测的效率与可扩展性，在临床场景与利用海量组织学图像进行下游生物学发现方面展现出巨大潜力。

title: AmbiSteer: Selectively Eliciting Ambiguity-Aware Responses in Vision-Language Models
authors: Monica Riedler, Samuele Antonelli, Barbara Plank, Raffaella Bernardi
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often exhibit overconfidence, providing firm answers even when visual evidence is insufficient. A prominent case is referential ambiguity in Visual Question Answering (VQA), where multiple entities in an image are plausible referents of a question. Addressing such cases requires recognizing when ambiguity is present: ambiguous questions can be handled by asking for clarification or enumerating plausible referents, while unambiguous questions should receive a direct answer. Current VLMs struggle with this distinction, often defaulting to a single interpretation. To investigate whether activation steering can serve as an inference-time mechanism to elicit such behaviors, we introduce AmbiSteer, a lightweight framework to selectively elicit ambiguity-aware behavior. Across three VLMs, we find that steering alone has limited and model-dependent effects, while prompting is generally more effective. Combining prompting and steering substantially increases clarification and enumeration behaviors, but also elicits them on unambiguous cases. AmbiSteer addresses this using a linear classifier to predict input ambiguity and condition the steering direction accordingly, increasing the proportion of inputs handled appropriately from 59.0% to 77.0% on average across models. Our work sets the ground for lightweight approaches to reduce model overconfidence in uncertain multimodal settings.
zh_title: AmbiSteer：选择性诱导视觉语言模型中的歧义感知响应
translation: 视觉语言模型（VLM）通常表现出过度自信，即使在视觉证据不足时也会给出确定的回答。一个突出的情况是视觉问答（VQA）中的指称歧义，即图像中的多个实体都是问题的合理指称对象。处理此类情况需要识别何时存在歧义：对于歧义问题，可以通过请求澄清或列举合理的指称对象来处理，而无歧义问题则应获得直接回答。当前的 VLM 难以做出这种区分，往往默认采用单一解释。为了探究激活引导（activation steering）是否可以作为一种推理时机制来引出此类行为，我们提出了 AmbiSteer，这是一个用于选择性诱导歧义感知行为的轻量级框架。在三个 VLM 上的实验发现，单独引导的效果有限且依赖于具体模型，而提示通常更有效。将提示与引导相结合可大幅增加澄清和枚举行为，但也会在无歧义样本上诱发这些行为。AmbiSteer 通过使用线性分类器预测输入歧义性并相应地对引导方向进行条件调节解决了这一问题，使跨模型恰当处理输入的平均比例从 59.0% 提高到 77.0%。我们的工作为在不确定多模态设置下减少模型过度自信的轻量级方法奠定了基础。
tldr: AmbiSteer 结合提示与线性分类器条件化的激活引导，能够选择性地让视觉语言模型对歧义问题进行澄清或列举，将正确应对歧义的比例从 59.0% 提升至 77.0%。
ai_comments: 该研究具有很强的实用价值和创新性，首次探索了激活引导（activation steering）在缓解视觉语言模型歧义过度自信上的机制，并敏锐地发现了提示与引导结合时容易对非歧义样本“过度修正”的副作用，创新性地引入线性分类器进行条件引导。局限性在于分类器的判断准确率可能直接制约引导效果，且摘要显示仅在三种模型上进行了验证。
motivation: 视觉语言模型（VLM）存在过度自信问题，尤其在视觉问答遇到指称歧义（图像中存在多个可能实体）时，难以区分有歧义与无歧义问题，往往默认给出单一确定答案而非请求澄清或列举。
method: 提出轻量级框架 AmbiSteer，将提示与激活引导相结合，并利用线性分类器预测输入是否具有歧义，从而条件化地调整激活引导方向，以选择性诱导澄清或枚举等歧义感知行为。
results: 在三种 VLM 上的测试表明，单独使用激活引导效果有限，结合提示和引导可大幅增加澄清和枚举行为但会波及无歧义案例；AmbiSteer 通过条件化引导，使跨模型恰当处理输入的平均比例从 59.0% 提升至 77.0%。
conclusion: 该工作为在不确定的多模态场景下，采用轻量级推理期方法减少视觉语言模型的过度自信奠定了基础。

title: Evaluating Polling Schemes for OFDMA Uplink Scheduling in Time-Sensitive Wi-Fi Networks
authors: Douglas Dziedzorm Agbeve, Ferhat Van Herck, Andrey Belogaev, Jeroen Famaey
abstract: IEEE 802.11ax introduced orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) to improve channel utilization through concurrent multi-user transmissions. For effective uplink (UL) scheduling, the access point (AP) requires timely knowledge of buffered traffic at the stations (STAs). Explicit buffer-status polling provides this, yet each polling round can query only as many STAs as there are resource units (RUs). Scheduled-access, random-access, activity-based, and learning-based schemes address this buffer-status acquisition problem differently and have generally been evaluated in isolation under different conditions, so it remains unclear how they compare across time-sensitive workloads. We evaluate common schemes from the Wi-Fi standard and literature under three time-sensitive environments: a large-scale teleconferencing session, an industrial IoT deployment, and an extended reality (XR) service. The relative performance of the schemes depends strongly on traffic characteristics and offered load. In conferencing, activity-based and learning-based polling perform best, while conventional contention-based access remains competitive under light load. In the industrial scenario, scheduled-access most effectively delivers time-sensitive packets within their deadlines under heavy load, whereas contention-based access performs best under lighter load. In XR, OFDMA-based schemes achieve high video throughput that contention-based access cannot sustain; among them, activity-based polling achieves the lowest deadline-miss ratios for uplink head-tracking traffic, at the expense of longer video delay tails. These findings highlight the importance of selecting channel access and scheduling schemes according to traffic requirements and operating conditions.

title: Zoom In, Scale Out: Metric Depth Models Mistake Digital Zoom for Moving Closer
authors: Rabeya Noor, Khandoker Nosiba Arifin
abstract: Many new AI models estimate how far away things are, in metres, from a single photo. To do this they must also work out what camera took the photo. We check whether they really do with a simple test: digital zoom, that is, cropping a photo and enlarging the crop back to full size. Zooming moves nothing in the scene, so a correct model should give the same distance for every point still in the picture. The test is free, exact and needs no labels. Two numbers describe a model's reaction: its depth changes like $s^{-α}$ (ideal $α=0$) and its focal-length estimate like $s^β$ (ideal $β=1$), for zoom factor $s$. On 800 images from KITTI, NYUv2 and DIODE, the widely used Depth Anything V2 has $α=0.95$: it treats a zoomed photo almost as if the camera had moved closer, because it judges distance mainly from how large things look. Models that also predict the camera remove only part of this error ($α\approx0.31$-$0.36$), because their focal estimate grows too little. Given the true camera, Depth Pro and DA3-Nested keep their depth ($α\approx0$), so the error lies in their camera estimate. The reason: a zoomed photo is, pixel for pixel, a normal photo of a scene squashed in depth, so size alone cannot tell the two apart, and a focal estimator trained by regression stays close to the cameras it saw in training. Undoing this needs no labels or training and makes Depth Pro pass the test ($α=0.04$) at almost no cost on normal photos. Controls, including a real optical zoom lens, rule out blur and resizing artefacts. Finally, label-free fine-tuning for self-consistency lowers $α$ to 0.05 on KITTI and 0.07 on NYUv2 once a "blurry means zoomed" shortcut is removed; we report what this costs on normal and unseen photos.
zh_title: 放大与缩小：度量深度模型将数码变焦误认为是相机靠近
translation: 许多新型人工智能模型能根据单张照片以米为单位估算物体的距离。为此，它们还必须推断出是用何种相机拍摄的照片。我们通过一个简单的测试来验证它们是否真正做到了这一点：数码变焦，即裁剪照片并将裁剪部分放大回完整尺寸。变焦并没有移动场景中的任何物体，因此正确的模型对于画面中保留的每个点都应给出相同的距离。该测试成本为零、结果精确且无需标签。我们用两个数字来描述模型的反应：对于变焦因子 $s$，其深度变化表现为 $s^{-\alpha}$（理想值为 $\alpha=0$），焦距估计变化表现为 $s^\beta$（理想值为 $\beta=1$）。在来自 KITTI、NYUv2 和 DIODE 的 800 张图像上，被广泛使用的 Depth Anything V2 的 $\alpha=0.95$：它几乎将放大的照片当成相机移动得更近，因为它主要根据物体看起来有多大来判断距离。能够同时预测相机的模型也仅能消除部分误差（$\alpha \approx 0.31\sim0.36$），因为它们的焦距估计增幅太小。在给定真实相机参数的情况下，Depth Pro 和 DA3-Nested 能够保持其深度（$\alpha \approx 0$），因此误差出在它们的相机估计上。其原因在于：放大的照片在像素级别上就是一张场景在深度方向被压扁的普通照片，仅凭尺寸无法将两者区分，而通过回归训练的焦距估计器往往局限于训练中见过的相机。纠正这一点无需标签或训练，即可让 Depth Pro 在对普通照片几乎无代价的情况下通过测试（$\alpha=0.04$）。包括真实光学变焦镜头在内的对照实验排除了模糊和尺寸调整伪影的影响。最后，在消除了“模糊即变焦”的捷径后，用于自一致性的无标签微调将 KITTI 上的 $\alpha$ 降至 0.05，NYUv2 上降至 0.07；我们还报告了这在常规及未见照片上所带来的代价。
keywords: 度量深度估计 (Metric Depth Estimation)
tldr: 单目度量深度模型普遍严重依赖物体表观尺寸，会将数码变焦误判为相机拉近；本文定位出相机焦距估计是其瓶颈，并提出了无需标注的高效修复方案。
ai_comments: 该论文切入点极其巧妙且极具启发性。它通过“数码变焦”这一完全零标注成本的几何变换，直击当前单目绝对度量深度估计大模型依赖“表观物体尺寸”而非真正理解三维相机几何的痛点。揭示了相机参数回归泛化能力差是导致深度尺度崩溃的主因，并给出了实用且开销极小的免训练及无监督微调修复方案。
motivation: 度量深度估计模型需要从单张照片中推算真实物理距离和相机参数。作者旨在验证现有模型是否真正理解相机与场景距离关系，还是仅仅依赖“物体看起来有多大”这一视觉捷径，将数码变焦错误地当成相机拉近。
method: 设计了基于数码变焦（裁剪并放大）的零成本测试协议，用指数参数 $\alpha$（深度缩放系数）和 $\beta$（焦距缩放系数）量化模型误差；提出了针对 Depth Pro 的免训练修正方法，以及消除“模糊即变焦”捷径后的无标签自一致性微调（label-free fine-tuning）方法。
results: Depth Anything V2 在变焦下 $\alpha=0.95$（近乎等同于相机前移）；带相机预测的模型 $\alpha \approx 0.31\sim0.36$；若直接提供真实相机内参，Depth Pro 等模型 $\alpha \approx 0$；采用提出的免训练方法可将 Depth Pro 的 $\alpha$ 降至 0.04；无标签微调进一步将 KITTI 和 NYUv2 上的 $\alpha$ 分别降至 0.05 和 0.07。
conclusion: 当前单目度量深度模型普遍缺乏对变焦与物理移动的有效区分能力，根源在于相机焦距估计偏向训练集均值；通过无需标注的修正与自一致性微调，可以使模型在几乎不损失常规图像性能的前提下克服这一几何缺陷。

title: Game-Theoretic Analysis of RIS-Assisted Challenge-Response PLA - Part II: Partial Channel Knowledge
authors: Anna V. Guglielmi, Linda Senigagliesi, Marco Baldi, Stefano Tomasin
abstract: We consider a physical layer authentication scenario in which a legitimate user (Alice) communicates with an authenticator (Bob) through a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), controlled by Bob. An attacker (Trudy) aims to impersonate Alice by suitably precoding her messages and still transmitting them through the RIS. This two-part study analyzes this attack-defense interaction between Bob and Trudy under perfect (Part I) and partial (Part II) channel knowledge by all the agents. Part I formulates the joint RIS selection and precoder design under perfect channel knowledge as a finite zero-sum game, establishing exact channel subspace conditions for attack indistinguishability alongside equilibrium mixed strategies. Part II extends the defense to incomplete channel information, where each agent observes only its own channel, by formulating a finite-action Bayesian game and characterizing the resulting Bayesian Nash equilibrium. Simulations in geometric and 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi-NLOS channels reveal that authentication performance is governed by available spatial degrees of freedom, channel correlation, and operating signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed equilibrium strategies effectively balance communication rate and security, outperforming conventional benchmark policies.
comment: Part II of arXiv:2611.16557. Submitted to IEEE TIFS
zh_title: RIS辅助挑战-应答物理层认证的博弈论分析——第二部分：部分信道知识
translation: 我们考虑一个物理层认证场景，其中合法用户（Alice）通过由认证方（Bob）控制的可重构智能表面（RIS）与Bob进行通信。攻击者（Trudy）试图通过适当地对其消息进行预编码并同样通过RIS传输来冒充Alice。该由两部分组成的研究分析了在所有参与者拥有完美信道知识（第一部分）和部分信道知识（第二部分）下Bob与Trudy之间的攻防交互。第一部分将完美信道知识下的RIS联合选择与预编码器设计表述为有限零和博弈，建立了攻击不可区分性的精确信道子空间条件以及混合策略均衡。第二部分通过构建有限动作贝叶斯博弈并表征所得的贝叶斯纳什均衡，将防御拓展到每个参与者仅能观测自身信道的不完全信道信息场景。在几何信道和3GPP TR 38.901 UMi-NLOS信道下的仿真表明，认证性能由可用空间自由度、信道相关性以及工作信噪比决定。所提出的均衡策略有效权衡了通信速率与安全性，优于传统基准策略。
tldr: 本文通过构建有限动作贝叶斯博弈，分析了部分信道知识下RIS辅助物理层认证的攻防交互，给出了优于传统方案的均衡策略。
ai_comments: 本研究的创新点在于将RIS辅助的物理层认证建模为不完全信息下的贝叶斯博弈，克服了传统研究中对全局完美信道状态信息（CSI）的严苛假设，更契合实际无线环境。其重要性体现在为RIS赋能的安全通信提供了兼顾速率与认证性能的博弈均衡策略。局限在于该分析基于有限动作博弈，若实际系统动作空间连续或信道估计误差严重，均衡解的复杂度与可行性可能面临挑战。
motivation: 在RIS辅助的挑战-应答物理层认证系统中，攻击者企图通过预编码伪造合法用户身份，且在实际场景中各方通常仅能获取局部/不完全信道信息，因此需要研究非完美信道知识下攻防双方的博弈行为与防御策略。
method: 将各节点仅能获取自身信道状态的不完全信息防御交互建模为有限动作贝叶斯博弈（finite-action Bayesian game），并求解分析其贝叶斯纳什均衡（Bayesian Nash equilibrium）；在几何信道与3GPP TR 38.901 UMi-NLOS信道下进行了仿真验证。
results: 仿真结果表明，认证性能主要取决于可用的空间自由度、信道相关性以及工作信噪比；所提出的贝叶斯均衡策略有效权衡了通信速率与安全性，显著超越了传统基准策略。
conclusion: 在部分信道知识条件下，所提出的贝叶斯纳什均衡策略能够有效权衡通信速率与安全性能，其认证表现受空间自由度、信道相关性及信噪比的综合制约，且性能显著优于传统基准方案。

title: Cracks in Embeddings: Robustness and Stability of JEPA-Based Chest X-Ray Representations
authors: Zahid Mansur, Kalpana Yadav, Deepak Mishra
abstract: Self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) models are increasingly used for medical imaging, however there is a limited understanding about robustness of these models toward real-world image changes. We test four JEPA-based chest X-ray encoders, trained on 78,468 NIH ChestX-ray14 images, under six tests: two black-box adversarial attacks (SPSA, Boundary Attack), three image corruptions (Gaussian noise, brightness shift, contrast shift), and a label-scarcity test, measuring embedding change and classification AUROC. These perturbations cause severe, model-dependent damage: encoder-level Cosine Similarity drops as low as 0.33, and AUROC falls by as much as 0.12 in the worst case (I-JEPA under the Boundary Test). We test two ways of training the small predictor on top of each frozen encoder to address this. Adversarial fine-tuning, trained on clean and perturbed images together, raises embedding consistency above 0.97 in nearly every case and improves AUROC, relative to the same perturbed baseline, for most models, with the largest gain of $+0.10$ on I-JEPA. A Vector-Quantized codebook method, trained only on clean images and evaluated on perturbed test images for the first time, instead degrades under distortion for all four models, most noticeably for I-JEPA ($-0.15$ AUROC on average), showing that its discrete bottleneck alone does not provide the robustness that comes from training on perturbed data directly.
zh_title: 嵌入中的裂缝：基于JEPA的胸部X射线表示的鲁棒性与稳定性
translation: 自监督联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）模型在医学影像中的应用日益广泛，然而关于这些模型应对真实世界图像变化的鲁棒性了解仍十分有限。我们在78,468张NIH ChestX-ray14图像上训练了四个基于JEPA的胸部X射线编码器，并在六种测试下进行评估：两种黑盒对抗攻击（SPSA、边界攻击）、三种图像损坏（高斯噪声、亮度偏移、对比度偏移）以及一项标签稀缺测试，用于测量嵌入变化和分类AUROC。这些扰动引起了严重的、依赖于模型的损害：编码器级别的余弦相似度最低降至0.33，在最坏情况下AUROC下降高达0.12（边界测试下的I-JEPA）。为了解决这一问题，我们在每个冻结的编码器上测试了两种训练小型预测器的方法。在干净和扰动图像上联合训练的对抗微调在几乎所有情况下都将嵌入一致性提高到0.97以上，并改善了大多数模型相对于相同扰动基线的AUROC，其中I-JEPA的增益最大（+0.10）。相比之下，首次在仅干净图像上训练并在扰动测试图像上评估的矢量量化（VQ）码本方法，在所有四个模型中遇到失真时性能均发生退化，其中I-JEPA最为显著（AUROC平均下降0.15），这表明仅依靠其离散瓶颈并不能提供直接在扰动数据上训练所获得的鲁棒性。
tldr: 本文揭示了基于JEPA的胸部X射线模型在对抗攻击和图像扰动下的脆弱性，并证明对抗微调能有效提升其鲁棒性，而离散VQ瓶颈则无法单独提供保护。
ai_comments: 该研究针对JEPA自监督模型在医学影像关键场景下的安全与鲁棒性进行了系统检验，具有重要的现实意义；实验揭示了即使是先进的自监督架构也对扰动和攻击十分敏感，且证伪了“离散VQ瓶颈天然具备抗扰动能力”的假设，为后续构建高可靠医疗AI模型提供了明确指导。
motivation: 自监督联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）模型在医学影像中日益普及，但目前对其在应对真实世界图像变化时的鲁棒性与表征稳定性了解非常有限。
method: 在78,468张NIH ChestX-ray14图像上训练4个JEPA胸部X射线编码器；设计6项测试（SPSA和Boundary黑盒对抗攻击、高斯噪声/亮度偏移/对比度偏移图像损坏、标签稀缺测试）；评估在冻结编码器上采用对抗微调与矢量量化（VQ）码本训练小型预测器的防御效果。
results: 测试扰动导致严重且因模型而异的性能受损，余弦相似度降至0.33，AUROC最多下降0.12（I-JEPA在Boundary测试中）；对抗微调将嵌入一致性恢复至0.97以上并有效提升AUROC（I-JEPA提升达+0.10）；而仅在干净数据上训练的VQ码本方法在扰动下性能进一步退化（I-JEPA的AUROC平均下降0.15）。
conclusion: 基于JEPA的医学影像表示在面对输入扰动和对抗攻击时表现出明显的脆弱性；仅凭矢量量化（离散瓶颈）无法抵御扰动，而结合干净与扰动样本的对抗微调是恢复模型表征稳定性和分类性能的有效途径。

title: DiffusionSSD: Achieving Extreme Visual Compression with Dual-stage Diffusion and Cross-level Near-Data Processing
authors: Kuai Yu, Wen Li, Shengwen Liang, Jie Zhang, Ying Wang, Huawei Li, Xin Yao, Renhai Chen, Gong Zhang
abstract:
Growing visual data overwhelms storage on resource-constrained edge devices, making compression essential. Traditional codecs offer inadequate rate-distortion performance, motivating the exploration of diffusion codecs. Diffusion codecs face two limitations: (1) At the algorithm level, diffusion decoders preserve perceptual quality under extreme compression, but require substantial computation. (2) At the architecture level, in NPU-centered devices, neural codecs occupy the NPU, interfering with other AI applications. Meanwhile, the complex codec pipeline incurs long I/O paths, leading to additional overhead and energy cost.
  To address these issues, we propose DiffusionSSD, a cross-level near-data processing framework for extreme visual data compression on edge devices, using an algorithm-architecture co-design method. Specifically, (1) at algorithm level, we present Dual-stage Diffusion, a lightweight solution tailored for diffusion codecs that employs patchification and single-step diffusion, reducing computation cost while preserving perceptual quality; (2) at architecture level, we introduce a Cross-level Near Data Processing architecture that integrates the proposed computational universal flash storage (cUFS) and LPDDR-PIM, enabling codecs to be entirely offloaded to data side while reducing visual-data movement and avoiding SoC redesign; (3) at system level, combining both the algorithm and the underlying architecture, we propose a Patch-Workload co-aware scheduling scheme to enable more efficient system-level execution. Experiments show that Dual-stage Diffusion maintains comparable perceptual quality while reducing computation cost by up to 92.7%. Compared with NPU+DRAM and near-data-processing design such as SmartSSD, cUFS+PIM improves coding throughput by 2.32 times and 2.91 times on average, respectively.
zh_title: DiffusionSSD：通过双阶段扩散与跨层级近数据处理实现极限视觉压缩
translation: 持续增长的视觉数据对资源受限的边缘设备存储造成了巨大压力，使数据压缩变得不可或缺。传统编解码器的率失真性能不足，促使人们开始探索扩散编解码器。扩散编解码器面临两个局限：(1) 算法层面，扩散解码器虽然在极限压缩下能保持感知质量，但需要巨额计算；(2) 架构层面，在以NPU为中心的设备中，神经编解码器会占用NPU，干扰其他AI应用的执行。同时，复杂的编解码流水线带来了冗长的I/O路径，导致额外的系统开销与能耗。为了解决这些问题，我们提出了DiffusionSSD，一种面向边缘设备极限视觉数据压缩的跨层级近数据处理框架，该框架采用了软硬件协同设计方法。具体而言，(1) 在算法层面，我们提出了双阶段扩散（Dual-stage Diffusion），这是一种专为扩散编解码器定制的轻量化方案，采用分块化与单步扩散，在降低计算开销的同时保留感知质量；(2) 在架构层面，我们引入了跨层级近数据处理架构，集成了所提出的计算型通用闪存存储（cUFS）和LPDDR-PIM，使编解码器能够完全卸载到数据侧，从而减少视觉数据移动并避免对SoC的重新设计；(3) 在系统层面，结合算法与底层硬件架构，我们提出了一种分块-工作负载协同感知的调度机制，以实现更高效的系统级执行。实验表明，双阶段扩散在保持相近感知质量的同时，最多可减少92.7%的计算开销。与NPU+DRAM以及SmartSSD等近数据处理设计相比，cUFS+PIM将编解码吞吐量平均分别提升了2.32倍和2.91倍。
tldr: DiffusionSSD通过双阶段扩散算法与cUFS+PIM近数据处理架构协同设计，在减少92.7%计算量的同时使吞吐量提升2倍以上，实现了边缘端高效极限视觉压缩。
ai_comments: 该论文通过软硬件协同设计的方式解决扩散模型在边缘端极限视觉压缩中的高计算负载与I/O开销瓶颈，创新性地提出了两阶段扩散算法以及结合cUFS与LPDDR-PIM的跨层级近数据处理架构，在显著降低计算量与数据搬移的同时避免了复杂的SoC重构，具有很强的实用价值和前瞻性。局限在于该架构依赖定制化的硬件支持（cUFS和PIM），在现有商用边缘硬件上的普及部署仍面临硬件生态成熟度的挑战。
motivation: 边缘设备存储空间受限，传统编解码器率失真性能不足，而新兴的扩散编解码器存在计算开销过大（算法层面）以及抢占NPU、I/O路径长带来额外能耗开销（架构层面）的两大瓶颈。
method: 提出DiffusionSSD协同设计框架：(1) 算法层面：提出双阶段扩散（Dual-stage Diffusion），利用分块处理（patchification）和单步扩散显著降低计算量并保持感知质量；(2) 架构层面：提出跨层级近数据处理架构，结合计算型通用闪存存储（cUFS）与LPDDR-PIM，将编解码完全卸载至数据端并减少数据迁移；(3) 系统层面：提出分块与工作负载协同感知（Patch-Workload co-aware）调度方案以优化执行效率。
results: 实验结果显示，双阶段扩散在维持相近感知质量的同时，将计算开销降低了高达92.7%；所提出的cUFS+PIM相比NPU+DRAM架构以及SmartSSD等近数据处理设计，编码吞吐量分别平均提升了2.32倍和2.91倍。
conclusion: DiffusionSSD通过算法与硬件协同设计，有效解决了扩散编解码器在边缘设备上的计算和I/O瓶颈，在保证极高感知压缩质量的同时实现了高能效与高吞吐量的视觉数据处理。

title: CardioTrace: Motion-Aware Cine Synthesis via Coupled Tracing and Segmentation
authors: Zhi Chen, Le Zhang
abstract: Cardiac cine MRI provides time-resolved visualization of cardiac motion and is essential for evaluating ventricular function and anatomy. In routine clinical acquisition, however, cine sequences are frequently temporally sparse or degraded by arrhythmia, motion, and scan-time constraints, which can hinder reliable quantification and downstream analysis. We present CardioTrace, a motion-aware cine synthesis framework that generates a full cardiac cine sequence from limited input while explicitly modeling and tracing cardiac motion. CardioTrace couples two complementary pathways: a pixel-translation branch that directly predicts cine frames in a residual formulation, and a flow-field branch that estimates time-resolved deformation fields from a reference phase to provide interpretable motion correspondences across frames. To further preserve anatomical plausibility, a segmentation branch supervises clinically meaningful cardiac structures at key phases, and a cross-branch consistency objective encourages the synthesized appearance dynamics to follow the explicit motion guidance, mitigating temporal drift and unrealistic shape transitions over long sequences. The framework also supports prompt-style conditioning to incorporate auxiliary patient or acquisition information, improving robustness across heterogeneous multi-center data. Experiments on public cardiac cine MRI datasets demonstrate that CardioTrace improves perceptual quality and temporal coherence over representative GAN- and diffusion-based baselines, while better preserving ventricular morphology throughout the cardiac cycle. \textit{Our codes are available after review}.
zh_title: CardioTrace：基于耦合追踪与分割的运动感知电影磁共振合成
translation: 心脏电影磁共振（cine MRI）能够提供心脏运动的时间分辨可视化，对于评估心室功能和解剖结构至关重要。然而在常规临床采集中心动电影序列往往时间稀疏，或因心律失常、运动伪影和扫描时间限制而发生退化，这阻碍了可靠的定量评估和下游分析。我们提出了CardioTrace，一个运动感知的电影合成框架，能够在显式建模和追踪心脏运动的同时，从受限的输入生成完整的心脏电影序列。CardioTrace耦合了两个互补分支：一个以残差形式直接预测电影帧的像素平移分支，以及一个从参考相位估计时间分辨形变场以提供跨帧可解释运动对应关系的流场分支。为了进一步保持解剖结构的合理性，分割分支在关键相位对具有临床意义的心脏结构进行监督，同时跨分支一致性目标促使合成的外观动态遵循显式运动引导，从而减轻长序列中的时间漂移和不切实际的形态过渡。该框架还支持提示风格的条件注入以引入辅助的患者或采集信息，提高了在异构多中心数据中的鲁棒性。在公开心脏电影MRI数据集上的实验表明，相比代表性的基于GAN和扩散模型的基准方法，CardioTrace提升了感知质量与时间连贯性，并在整个心动周期中更好地保留了心室形态。我们的代码将在论文审稿后开源。
tldr: CardioTrace通过耦合像素生成分支、运动流场分支与解剖分割监督，实现了从有限输入中高质量合成具有时间连贯性和解剖保真度的心脏电影MRI序列。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于将显式的运动流场追踪、隐式像素生成网络与关键解剖结构的语义分割进行耦合，并通过跨分支一致性有效解决了生成模型在长时间动态序列中常见的时间漂移和解剖失真问题。此外，引入提示式条件增强了多中心异构数据的适应性。潜在局限在于依赖形变场估计，对极度不规则心律或严重结构病变的合成稳定性仍需进一步验证。
motivation: 临床常规采集的心脏电影MRI常因扫描时间限制、运动或心律失常导致时间分辨率稀疏或图像质量退化，严重阻碍了心室功能与解剖结构的可靠定量分析。
method: CardioTrace耦合了两个互补通路：一是采用残差形式直接预测帧图像的像素平移分支，二是从参考相位估计时间分辨形变场的流场分支；同时引入分割分支在关键相位监督心脏解剖结构，并设计跨分支一致性目标约束外观动态遵循运动引导；此外还支持提示词风格的条件注入以融合辅助临床与采集信息。
results: 在公开心脏电影MRI数据集上的实验结果表明，CardioTrace在感知质量和时间连贯性方面均优于现有的GAN和扩散模型基准，且在整个心动周期内能更好地保持心室形态结构。
conclusion: CardioTrace通过显式运动建模与解剖先验约束，能从受限/退化的输入中鲁棒且高质量地合成具有真实运动连贯性与解剖保真度的心脏电影MRI序列。

title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
authors: Stephen Obadinma, Xiaodan Zhu
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents, their abilities in navigating automated planning tasks have become essential. However, despite their strengths, LLMs' planning ability is not robust, particularly when they are not allowed to exploit commonsense cues in the symbolic vocabulary (e.g., names of actions, predicates, and objects) used to define planning tasks. This makes LLMs unreliable compared to symbolic planners. With recent reasoning models showing improved planning performance on tasks with obfuscated symbolic vocabularies, we utilize an adversarial attack framework to reveal to what extent the crucial weaknesses of LLM agents at joint symbolic interpretation and planning remain and whether they can reason properly when presented with severe cases. As such, our main contribution is devising an LLM-based attack model, which we call Symbolic Swapper, to automatically generate obfuscated planning domains with non-standard symbolic vocabularies that systematically break strong reasoning models' ability to plan. In doing so, we reveal how much LLMs' planning abilities can be further degraded under more advanced obfuscation schemes, allowing us to ascertain their success when having to rely on their pure planning ability. We find that attacks can decrease the planning performance of base models and even robust planning frameworks by over 70%. We further analyze the factors behind how LLM planning abilities break down and find that successful obfuscation causes models to appear to significantly degrade in reasoning quality despite them showing some inherent ability to understand the domain, revealing a gap in the perception of a task domain and being able to plan under it.
zh_title: 针对LLM规划器中符号词汇漏洞的对抗攻击
translation: 随着大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被部署为自主智能体，它们在自动化规划任务中的能力变得至关重要。然而，尽管LLM能力强大，但其规划能力并不鲁棒，尤其是在无法利用定义规划任务的符号词汇（例如动作、谓词和对象的名称）中的常识线索时，这使得LLM与符号规划器相比显得不够可靠。尽管近期的推理模型在具有混淆符号词汇的任务上表现出了规划性能的提升，但我们利用对抗攻击框架揭示了LLM智能体在联合符号解释和规划方面的关键缺陷在多大程度上依然存在，以及它们在面对极端情况时是否能够正常推理。因此，我们的主要贡献是设计了一种基于LLM的攻击模型，称为Symbolic Swapper，用于自动生成具有非标准符号词汇的混淆规划域，从而系统性地破坏强大推理模型的规划能力。通过这种方式，我们揭示了在更高级的混淆方案下，LLM的规划能力会被进一步削弱到何种程度，进而检验其在必须依赖纯规划能力时的表现。我们发现，这些攻击可以使基础模型乃至具备鲁棒性的规划框架的规划性能下降超过70%。我们进一步分析了导致LLM规划能力崩溃的深层因素，发现成功的混淆虽然让模型表现出对领域具有一定内在理解能力，但其推理质量却显著恶化，这揭示了任务域感知与在该领域下进行规划之间存在差距。
tldr: 提出了一种名为Symbolic Swapper的对抗攻击方法，通过混淆符号词汇使LLM规划器的性能下降超70%，揭示了其缺乏纯规划能力的本质。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地从对抗攻击视角评估大语言模型规划器的鲁棒性，揭示了模型看似提升的推理能力很大程度上仍依赖于符号语义常识先验，而非纯粹的形式规划逻辑。这一发现对于评估与改进基于LLM的自主智能体具有重要警示意义。局限性在于攻击方法依赖于符号替换混淆，对真实世界规划场景中更复杂逻辑扰动的泛化性仍有待进一步探讨。
motivation: 大语言模型（LLM）在规划任务中缺乏鲁棒性，高度依赖符号词汇（如动作、谓词和对象名称）中的常识线索。为探究最新推理模型在面对严重符号混淆时是否真正具备纯粹的规划推理能力，作者构建对抗攻击框架进行深入测试。
method: 提出了一种基于LLM的对抗攻击模型“Symbolic Swapper”，该模型能够自动生成包含非标准符号词汇的混淆规划域，从而系统性地瓦解先进推理模型的规划能力。
results: 对抗攻击使得基础模型乃至更具鲁棒性的规划框架的规划性能下降超过70%；分析表明，成功的混淆导致模型推理质量显著恶化，揭示出模型在任务域感知与在该域下进行实际规划之间存在明显断层。
conclusion: 研究表明LLM规划器对非标准符号词汇高度脆弱，即使展现出一定的领域理解感知能力，也难以在混淆符号下进行有效规划，暴露出LLM在领域感知与纯粹规划执行之间存在显著差距。

title: DOCKET: A Pluralistic Benchmark for Evaluating AI-Assisted Policy Feedback in U.S. Rulemaking
authors: Alexander Spangher, Charlotte Peale, Sílvia Casacuberta, Victor Y. Wu, Mirac Suzgun, Olivia H. Martin, Dan Bateyko, Cassandra Handan-Nader, Diyi Yang, Sanmi Koyejo, Daniel E. Ho
abstract: As AI models advance and impact deliberative democracies, there is a growing need to assess their support of pluralistic viewpoints. Most pluralism benchmarks are insufficient for this: they are not grounded in diversity (i.e., stakeholders across different frames, skills and needs), quality (i.e., rigorous and technical debates), and impact (i.e., invested deliberators and real-world outcomes). To address this, we first (i) curate DOCKET, the most comprehensive dataset of the U.S. Federal Notice & Comment process to date. DOCKET consists of 42.3M public comments on 22,400 regulations across 44 government agencies between 2016 and 2026 and contains millions of policy debates; we link public comments to particular policy items proposed by regulators to track the public's attention and the responsiveness of regulators to public input. (ii) Next, we demonstrate the pluralistic utility of DOCKET - we show that public commenters have a wide breadth of perspectives with significant depth in policy expertise and that regulators are often responsive. (iii) Finally, we present DOCKETBench, the first systematic evaluation of LLMs' ability to represent human policy perspectives in federal rulemaking. Only 18-30% of LLM-generated feedback aligns with real human comments. LLMs critique proposals broadly but generally, lacking the specific grounding, citations, and lived-experience arguments that humans bring to bear; in addition, most models we test systematically agree with government perspectives (overlapping with up to 68% of their claims) and agree least with labor unions (as little as 26% of their claims), demonstrating a fundamental skew in perspectives that even tools like persona modeling do not solve. Taken together, we reveal fundamental gaps in how language models navigate real policy issues, and DOCKETBench serves as a testbed for closing those gaps in a crucial real-world domain.
zh_title: DOCKET：一个评估美国法规制定中AI辅助政策反馈的多元化基准
translation: 随着人工智能模型的发展并影响审议民主，越来越需要评估它们对多元化观点的支持。大多数多元化基准对此不足：它们没有以多样性（即跨不同框架、技能和需求的利益相关者）、质量（即严谨和技术性辩论）和影响力（即投入的审议者和现实世界结果）为基础。为了解决这个问题，我们首先（i）策划了DOCKET，这是迄今为止最全面的美国联邦公告与评论流程数据集。DOCKET包含2016年至2026年间来自44个政府机构的22,400项法规的4230万条公众评论，并包含数百万次政策辩论；我们将公众评论与监管机构提出的特定政策项目关联起来，以追踪公众的关注度以及监管机构对公众意见的响应程度。（ii）接下来，我们展示了DOCKET的多元化效用——我们表明公众评论者具有广泛的视角和深厚的政策专业知识，并且监管机构通常会做出回应。（iii）最后，我们提出了DOCKETBench，这是首次系统性评估大型语言模型（LLM）在联邦法规制定中代表人类政策观点的能力。只有18-30%的LLM生成反馈与真实人类评论一致。LLM对提案的批评广泛但笼统，缺乏人类所带来的具体依据、引用和亲身经验论证；此外，我们测试的大多数模型系统性地与政府观点一致（与高达68%的声明重叠），而与工会的观点一致性最低（低至26%的声明），这表明存在根本性的视角偏差，即使像角色建模这样的工具也无法解决。总而言之，我们揭示了语言模型在处理真实政策问题方面的根本性差距，DOCKETBench作为一个测试平台，旨在弥补这些在关键现实世界领域中的差距。
tldr: 该研究推出了DOCKET数据集和DOCKETBench基准，用于评估LLM在美国法规制定中代表多元化人类政策观点的能力，发现LLM在与人类评论对齐方面表现不佳，并存在偏向政府观点的系统性偏差。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过构建大规模、高质量的DOCKET数据集和DOCKETBench基准，创新性地解决了AI在审议民主中支持多元化观点评估的难题。其重要性在于揭示了当前LLM在理解和代表复杂、多元化政策观点方面的显著不足和系统性偏见，特别是对政府观点的过度认同和对特定群体（如工会）观点的忽视。这对于AI辅助政策制定工具的开发具有重要的指导意义，强调了未来模型需要更好地捕捉人类经验、具体论证和多元化视角，以避免加剧现有偏见或简化复杂的政策辩论。
motivation: 随着AI模型的发展及其对审议民主的影响，需要评估AI对多元化观点的支持。现有的多元化基准不足，因为它们缺乏多样性（不同背景、技能和需求）、质量（严格和技术性辩论）和影响力（投入的审议者和现实世界结果）。
method: 1. 策展了DOCKET数据集，这是迄今为止最全面的美国联邦公告与评论流程数据集，包含2016年至2026年间来自44个政府机构的22,400项法规的4230万条公众评论。数据集将公众评论与监管机构提出的具体政策项目关联。2. 展示了DOCKET的多元化实用性，表明公众评论者具有广泛且深入的政策专业知识，且监管机构通常会做出回应。3. 提出了DOCKETBench，这是首次系统性评估大型语言模型（LLM）在联邦法规制定中代表人类政策观点的能力。
results: 1. LLM生成的反馈与真实人类评论的对齐度仅为18-30%。2. LLM对提案的批评宽泛且笼统，缺乏人类评论所具有的具体依据、引用和亲身经验论证。3. 大多数测试模型系统性地与政府观点一致（高达68%的声明重叠），而与工会的观点一致性最低（低至26%的声明），这表明存在根本性的视角偏差，即使像角色建模这样的工具也无法解决。
conclusion: 研究揭示了语言模型在处理真实政策问题方面的根本性差距，DOCKETBench作为一个测试平台，旨在弥补这些在关键现实世界领域中的差距。

title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
authors: Yang Chen, Feifan Tian, Cong Wang, Cheng Feng, Wenbin Li, Yang Gao
abstract: While current few-shot adaptation strategies for time series forecasting foundation models are predominantly dataset-centric, the necessity of obtaining an additional dataset for the finetuning process poses a significant hurdle for adoption. To address this constraint, we propose Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning (SWIFT), a novel forecasting adaptation framework that achieves fine-grained specialization by leveraging structural priors from the target instance's own history. This shift allows the fine-tuning process to be entirely transparent to the end-user, which significantly enhances the ease of adoption. To implement this framework, SWIFT synergizes Self-Retrieval for historical mining and Frequency-Aware Loss for spectral consistency, while employing Deviation-Aware Dynamic Fusion to balance adaptation with general knowledge preservation. Extensive experiments across four TSFM backbones and three long-history benchmark subsets validate SWIFT, yielding average MASE and WQL reductions of 6.41% and 4.83% across 24 combinations of four backbones and six Chronos Benchmark II datasets. To the best of our knowledge, SWIFT is the first framework to investigate sample-wise instance fine-tuning of time-series foundation models, specializing the model for an individual prediction window using only the corresponding forecasting sample's own observed history.
zh_title: SWIFT: 用于预测的时间序列基础模型的样本级实例微调
translation: 当前时间序列预测基础模型的少样本适应策略主要是以数据集为中心的，但获取额外的微调数据集的必要性对采用构成了重大障碍。为了解决这一限制，我们提出了样本级实例微调（SWIFT），这是一种新颖的预测适应框架，通过利用目标实例自身历史的结构先验实现细粒度专业化。这种转变使得微调过程对最终用户完全透明，从而显著提高了采用的便利性。为了实现这一框架，SWIFT协同了用于历史挖掘的自检索（Self-Retrieval）和用于频谱一致性的频率感知损失（Frequency-Aware Loss），同时采用偏差感知动态融合（Deviation-Aware Dynamic Fusion）来平衡适应性与通用知识保留。在四个TSFM骨干和三个长历史基准子集上进行了广泛实验，验证了SWIFT，在四个骨干和六个Chronos Benchmark II数据集的24种组合中，平均MASE和WQL分别降低了6.41%和4.83%。据我们所知，SWIFT是第一个研究时间序列基础模型样本级实例微调的框架，它仅使用相应预测样本自身的观测历史来针对单个预测窗口对模型进行专业化。
tldr: SWIFT是一种新的时间序列预测适应框架，通过利用目标实例自身的历史结构先验进行样本级微调，无需额外数据集，提高了采用便利性，并在多个基准测试中取得了显著效果。
ai_comments: SWIFT的创新之处在于其“样本级实例微调”方法，打破了传统依赖额外数据集进行微调的范式，通过利用实例自身的历史数据进行适应，极大地提高了时间序列基础模型的可用性和易用性。这种方法对于实际应用中数据获取受限的场景具有重要意义。
motivation: 当前时间序列预测基础模型的少样本适应策略主要是数据集中心的，需要额外的微调数据集，这阻碍了其采用。
method: SWIFT通过利用目标实例自身历史的结构先验实现细粒度专业化。它结合了用于历史挖掘的自检索（Self-Retrieval）和用于频谱一致性的频率感知损失（Frequency-Aware Loss），并采用偏差感知动态融合（Deviation-Aware Dynamic Fusion）来平衡适应性与通用知识保留。
results: 在四个TSFM骨干和三个长历史基准子集上进行了广泛实验，SWIFT在24种组合（四个骨干和六个Chronos Benchmark II数据集）中，平均MASE和WQL分别降低了6.41%和4.83%。
conclusion: SWIFT是第一个研究时间序列基础模型样本级实例微调的框架，它仅使用相应预测样本自身的观测历史来针对单个预测窗口对模型进行专业化。

title: Condensing Law of Security Information
authors: Qi Tan, Tianyu Cui, Qi Li, Ke Xu
abstract: Scaling laws indicate that the generalization error of a large language model (LLM) decreases monotonically with model size once data is sufficient, and the corollary that larger models outperform smaller ones is now widely accepted. We argue that this corollary fails in security: decisions there hinge on anomalous inputs, which are long-tailed (e.g., zero-day attacks) and therefore poorly served by likelihood fitting. Worse still, the capability brought about by scale (e.g., inferring the intended whole from a corrupted part) leads a LLM silently \emph{repair} the anomaly before any downstream security head ever sees it. We formalize this as a tradeoff between two quantities: the cognitive capability $K(W)=I(W;P)$ that a model holds about the world distribution, and the security-information retention $R(W)=\frac{I(Z;S)}{I(A;S)}$ that survives in its intermediate representation. We derive three information-theoretic bounds to connect them: an upper bound on restoration accuracy in terms of $K(W)$, an upper bound on $R(W)$ in terms of the restoration error, and a Fano lower bound on security-task error in terms of $R(W)$. These theorems approximately imply that usable security information is a product of how much security information survives and how well it can be extracted, indicating that optimal usable security information can be achieved at a certain model size. We state this as the \emph{condensing law of security information}: usable security information is unimodal in model size, so security generalization error is U-shaped and is minimized at a finite $N^{\star}$ rather than decreasing without bound. The experiments on various real-world LLMs validate the condensing law, indicating that there is an optimal model size to solve security issues.
translation:
标题：安全信息凝聚定律
摘要：缩放定律表明，一旦数据充足，大型语言模型（LLM）的泛化误差会随着模型尺寸的增加而单调下降，并且“模型越大性能越好”的推论已被广泛接受。我们认为这一推论在安全领域是失效的：安全决策依赖于异常输入，这些输入是长尾的（例如，零日攻击），因此通过似然拟合效果不佳。更糟糕的是，规模带来的能力（例如，从损坏的部分推断出完整的意图）导致LLM在任何下游安全头部看到异常之前就默默地“修复”了异常。我们将此形式化为两个量之间的权衡：模型对世界分布的认知能力$K(W)=I(W;P)$，以及在其中间表示中幸存的安全信息保留$R(W)=\frac{I(Z;S)}{I(A;S)}$。我们推导了三个信息论界限来连接它们：关于$K(W)$的恢复准确性上限，关于恢复误差的$R(W)$上限，以及关于$R(W)$的安全任务误差的Fano下限。这些定理近似地暗示，可用安全信息是安全信息存活量和提取能力乘积，表明在特定模型尺寸下可以实现最优的可用安全信息。我们将其表述为“安全信息凝聚定律”：可用安全信息在模型尺寸上呈单峰分布，因此安全泛化误差呈U形，并在有限的$N^{\star}$处最小化，而不是无限制地下降。对各种真实世界LLM的实验验证了这一凝聚定律，表明存在一个最优模型尺寸来解决安全问题。
tldr: 针对安全领域的LLM，存在一个最优模型尺寸，使得安全泛化误差最小，而非越大越好，这被称为安全信息凝聚定律。
ai_comments: 这篇论文提出了一个反直觉但重要的观点，即在安全领域，LLM并非越大越好。其创新点在于通过信息论的视角，形式化了模型认知能力与安全信息保留之间的权衡，并提出了“安全信息凝聚定律”。这对于指导LLM在安全领域的应用和模型选择具有重要意义，避免盲目追求模型规模。
motivation: 现有观点认为大型语言模型（LLM）越大性能越好，但在安全领域，模型规模的增加可能导致LLM“修复”异常输入，从而损害其识别异常输入的能力，因此需要探究LLM在安全任务中的真实性能与模型规模的关系。
method: 本文通过形式化模型的认知能力$K(W)$和安全信息保留$R(W)$之间的权衡，推导了三个信息论界限（关于恢复准确性的上限、关于$R(W)$的上限以及关于安全任务误差的Fano下限）来连接它们，并在此基础上提出了“安全信息凝聚定律”。
results: 理论推导表明，可用安全信息是安全信息存活量和提取能力的乘积，且在特定模型尺寸下可实现最优。提出了“安全信息凝聚定律”，即可用安全信息在模型尺寸上呈单峰分布，安全泛化误差呈U形，并在有限的$N^{	ext{*}}$处最小化。实验验证了这一凝聚定律。
conclusion: 在解决安全问题时，存在一个最优的模型尺寸，而非模型越大越好。

title: Vessel2Brain: Edge-Aware Multi-Scale Flow Matching for 3D Brain Image Generation from Vessel Masks
authors: Zhi Chen, Tianyang Zhang, Theodoros N. Arvanitis, Le Zhang
abstract: Generating realistic 3D brain MRI volumes from sparse anatomical priors is a highly ill-posed yet clinically valuable problem, with important applications in data augmentation, simulation, and downstream neuroimaging analysis. In this work, we investigate the challenging task of synthesising full 3D brain MRI volumes conditioned solely on vascular label maps. While vascular structures provide strong anatomical and topological cues, they occupy only a small fraction of the brain volume and offer no direct information about surrounding tissue appearance. To address this challenge, we propose Vessel2Brain, an edge-aware multi-scale conditional flow matching framework that explicitly incorporates vascular structure information into the generative process. Our approach formulates vessel-guided brain image synthesis as a conditional continuous flow, enabling stable training and flexible generation while preserving structural correspondence. A multi-scale flow matching strategy is introduced to jointly model global anatomical coherence and fine-grained local details, with auxiliary velocity predictions providing additional supervision across spatial resolutions. Furthermore, we design an edge-aware objective that emphasises vascular boundaries during training, encouraging anatomically faithful tissue synthesis around vessel structures. We evaluate Vessel2Brain on two public 3D brain MRI datasets with paired vascular annotations.
