Obaleth plans completions around buffer lifetimes and optimizes memory ordering, synchronization, and batching across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On H100 GPUs, Obaleth sends small messages up to 3.3$\times$ faster, and on 256 GPUs runs all-to-all 1.25$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ faster than NVSHMEM and NCCL GIN, with much smaller memory and register use. In vLLM, it serves Qwen3-235B on 16 B200 GPUs and answers requests up to 1.29$\times$ faster than with DeepEP.
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, 6 tables. Equal contribution from first two authors. Code: https://github.com/ParCoreLab/aboleth
zh_title: 编译专用 GPU 发起的网络
translation: 机器学习系统会针对工作负载和硬件对计算进行专门化，但通信部分仍然依赖于通用的库，这些库的设备代码和传输决策对高级编译器来说是不可见的。我们提出了 Obaleth，一个编译器，它将 GPU 发起的通信作为内核的中间表示的一部分，并与计算一起进行共同优化，然后将其降低到专用的传输代码。Obaleth 围绕缓冲区生命周期规划完成，并优化跨 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 的内存排序、同步和批处理。在 H100 GPU 上，Obaleth 发送小消息的速度提高了 3.3 倍；在 256 个 GPU 上，其 all-to-all 操作比 NVSHMEM 和 NCCL GIN 快 1.25 倍和 2.3 倍，同时内存和寄存器使用量也大大减少。在 vLLM 中，它在 16 个 B200 GPU 上服务 Qwen3-235B，响应速度比 DeepEP 快 1.29 倍。
tldr: Obaleth 是一个编译器，它将 GPU 发起的通信纳入内核的中间表示，并与计算一起进行优化，最终生成专用的传输代码。它围绕缓冲区生命周期规划完成，并优化跨 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 的内存排序、同步和批处理。
ai_comments: 这项工作通过将通信纳入编译器的优化范围，解决了机器学习系统中一个长期存在的瓶颈。将 GPU 发起的通信与计算共同优化是一个重要的进步，有望在未来的 GPU 计算系统中带来更高的性能和效率。未来工作可以探索 Obaleth 在更广泛的通信模式和异构计算环境中的应用。
motivation: 机器学习系统通常会针对工作负载和硬件对计算进行专门化，但通信部分仍然依赖于通用的库，这些库的设备代码和传输决策对高级编译器来说是不可见的。
method: Obaleth 将 GPU 发起的通信作为内核的中间表示的一部分，并与计算一起进行共同优化，然后将其降低到专用的传输代码。它通过围绕缓冲区生命周期进行规划，并优化跨 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 的内存排序、同步和批处理来实现这一点。
results: 在 H100 GPU 上，Obaleth 发送小消息的速度提高了 3.3 倍；在 256 个 GPU 上，其 all-to-all 操作比 NVSHMEM 和 NCCL GIN 快 1.25 倍和 2.3 倍，同时内存和寄存器使用量也大大减少。在 vLLM 中，它在 16 个 B200 GPU 上服务 Qwen3-235B，响应速度比 DeepEP 快 1.29 倍。
conclusion: Obaleth 成功地将 GPU 发起的通信集成到编译过程中，实现了与计算的共同优化，并在各种 GPU 架构和实际应用中取得了显著的性能提升。

title: STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels
authors: Jihoon Kim, Jun Hyeok Song, Wonho Ha, Namwoo Kang
abstract: Generative design of formed sheet panels must preserve geometric manufacturing conditions while exploring layouts and improving performance. STAMP embeds these conditions directly in the shape representation. Each panel is described by its material layout and a reference surface with one height at each occupied position in a plane perpendicular to the drawing direction. Nominal thickness is prescribed along the normal. The representation allows curved surfaces, ribs, and openings. It excludes reference-surface undercuts and keeps nominal thickness fixed without manufacturing penalty terms. Because these conditions belong to the representation, every generated and optimized panel satisfies them regardless of training-set size. Boundary-conditioned diffusion generates alternative layouts, and predictor gradients guide a surface optimization that retains outlines, openings, and designated fixed regions. We demonstrate STAMP on automotive hood inner panels using CarHoods10k. With a comparable number of stored values, depth maps reconstruct surfaces more accurately than point-cloud and voxel baselines. From only five training designs, one of three training runs yields novel and varied layouts. A generator trained on 500 designs, 6.5% of the training set, already reaches the layout variety of the full-data model. Across 11 held-out design families, predictor-based selection among existing dataset designs yields an average gap of 0.18 mm to the best available FEA deformation, versus an expected 1.59 mm for random selection. It does better than random selection in all 11 families. At a 10% depth-change bound, a network not used in the search predicts an average deformation reduction of 24.8% for six generated and existing panels, with a 3.2% average mass increase computed from geometry. Engineers can thus explore and optimize panels within this manufacturing-informed design space.
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, 7 tables, including supplementary material
zh_title: 片状面板的制造信息生成设计与形状优化
translation: 生成式设计的成形板材面板必须在探索布局和提高性能的同时，保持几何制造条件。STAMP将这些条件直接嵌入形状表示中。每个面板由其材料布局和一个参考表面描述，在绘图方向垂直的平面上的每个占用位置都有一个高度。标称厚度沿法线指定。该表示允许曲面、肋骨和开口。它排除了参考表面的底切，并保持标称厚度固定，没有制造惩罚项。由于这些条件属于表示的一部分，因此每个生成的和优化的面板都满足它们，而与训练集大小无关。边界条件扩散生成替代布局，预测器梯度引导表面优化，以保留轮廓、开口和指定的固定区域。我们在汽车引擎盖内面板上使用CarHoods10k演示了STAMP。在存储值数量相当的情况下，深度图比点云和体素基线更准确地重建表面。仅用五个训练设计（占训练运行的三分之一），就能产生新颖多样的布局。在500个设计（占训练集的6.5%）上训练的生成器，已经达到了全数据模型的布局多样性。在11个保留的设计系列中，基于预测器的选择在现有数据集设计中，与最佳可用有限元分析变形相比，平均差距为0.18毫米，而随机选择的预期差距为1.59毫米。在所有11个系列中，它的表现都优于随机选择。在10%的深度变化限制下，一个未用于搜索的网络预测了六个生成和现有面板的平均变形减少24.8%，几何计算的平均质量增加为3.2%。因此，工程师可以在这个制造信息设计空间内探索和优化面板。
tldr: STAMP是一种新的生成设计方法，它将制造约束直接嵌入到形状表示中，用于优化片状面板。它使用边界条件扩散生成布局，并利用预测器梯度进行表面优化，在汽车引擎盖内面板的案例研究中表现出色，能够生成新颖多样的布局，并在变形和质量方面优于传统方法。
ai_comments: 该方法将制造约束整合到形状表示中，解决了传统生成设计方法在处理复杂制造条件时的挑战。利用深度图作为形状表示，提高了重建精度。在小样本数据下表现出色，具有良好的泛化能力。预测器梯度引导的优化方法有效平衡了性能和设计空间。该研究为制造导向的生成设计提供了有价值的见解和实用的解决方案。
motivation: 需要一种生成设计方法，能够生成具有制造约束（如保持几何制造条件）的成形板材面板，同时探索布局并提高性能。
method: STAMP将制造条件嵌入形状表示中，使用边界条件扩散生成布局，并使用预测器梯度进行表面优化。面板由其材料布局和参考表面描述，参考表面在每个平面位置有一个高度。该方法排除了参考表面的底切，并保持标称厚度不变，无需制造惩罚项。
results: STAMP能够生成满足制造条件的新颖多样的布局。在汽车引擎盖内面板的案例研究中，与点云和体素基线相比，深度图能更准确地重建表面。仅用少量训练数据就能达到接近全数据模型的布局多样性。与随机选择相比，STAMP在变形预测方面表现更好，差距更小。在给定深度变化限制下，STAMP生成的面板在减小变形的同时，质量增加也较少。
conclusion: STAMP是一种制造信息生成设计和形状优化方法，能够有效地为工程师探索和优化片状面板，在保持制造约束的同时，实现优异的性能。

title: Evidence-Carrying Transport Across Effects
authors: Félix Castro, Liron Cohen, Ariel Grunfeld, Étienne Miquey
abstract: A program logic proved sound against one effectful semantics need not remain sound when the effect is re-implemented, yet the semantic relationship between reasoning before and after a change of effect is usually left implicit and re-established by hand. This paper provides a uniform, proof-relevant account of it. Working in realizability, where a notion of computation determines a model whose entailments carry explicit program evidence, we introduce simulations between effectful realizability cores, generalizing Longley's applicative morphisms to computation over an arbitrary strong monad. A single simulation transports the source logic along a ladder: it induces a morphism of the associated evidenced frames and, functorially, of the induced triposes. These passages are $2$-fully-faithful, so the three levels agree and a change of effect carries the entire higher-order program logic together with the evidence witnessing each derivation. A computationally dense simulation moreover computes a modality on the source logic, a nucleus through which the transport factors and which marks exactly the reasoning stable under the change, read off from the translation rather than postulated. This recovers known examples such as the double-negation modality of classical realizability, and examples such as sheafification arise from a modal refinement of the construction. Overall, the framework makes a change of effect a first-class object, one that can be composed, factored through its modality, and shown in cases not to exist, opening a path to transporting verified reasoning across effects.
zh_title: 跨副作用的承载证据迁移
translation: 在一种副作用语义下证明为健全的程序逻辑，当该副作用被重新实现时并不一定会保持健全，然而副作用改变前后推理之间的语义关系通常是不明确的，且需要手动重新建立。本文为此提供了一种统一的、与证明相关的解释。在可实现性理论（其中计算概念决定了一个蕴涵关系携带显式程序证据的模型）框架下，我们将Longley的应用态射推广到任意强单子上的计算，引入了副作用可实现性核心之间的模拟。单个模拟即可沿着阶梯迁移源逻辑：它诱导了相关证据框架的态射，并函子式地诱导了相应三元基（triposes）的态射。这些传递过程是2-全忠实的，因此这三个层次保持一致，副作用的改变承载了整个高阶程序逻辑以及见证每次推导的证据。此外，计算稠密模拟还会在源逻辑上计算出一个模态（核），迁移过程通过该模态分解，并且它精确标记了在改变下保持稳定的推理，这一模态是从翻译中直接读取而非人为假设的。这涵盖了已知示例（例如经典可实现性的双重否定模态），且层化（sheafification）等示例可由该构造的模态精化得出。总体而言，该框架使副作用的改变成为一等对象，能够对其进行组合、通过其模态进行分解，并在某些情况下证明其不存在，从而为在不同副作用之间迁移经验证的推理开辟了道路。
tldr: 基于可实现性理论与强单子推广，提出了一种在不同副作用语义之间迁移高阶程序逻辑及其程序证据的一等对象形式化框架。
ai_comments: 该工作创新性地将范畴逻辑中的三元基（tripos）可实现性理论与单子副作用语义相结合，把Longley的应用态射推广至强单子，建立了证明相关的逻辑迁移机制。其2-全忠实性确保了推理证据的严格保持，并将副作用改变本身提升为可组合、可分析的一等对象，理论深度极高。局限在于其构造高度抽象，具体验证工具链的工程化集成与实用性仍待实践检验。
motivation: 在一种副作用语义下证明健全的程序逻辑，当副作用被重新实现或改变时往往无法直接保持健全，而现有工作通常对副作用变化前后的语义关联处理模糊且需大量手工重新证明，缺乏统一的、证据相关的形式化迁移框架。
method: 在可实现性理论背景下，将Longley的应用态射推广到任意强单子上的计算，引入了副作用可实现性核心之间的模拟；利用2-全忠实的传递在证据框架和三元基（tripos）层次上承载源逻辑与推导证据；进一步通过计算稠密模拟在源逻辑上计算出核模态以刻画稳定推理。
results: 证明了从模拟到证据框架及三元基态射的传递是2-全忠实的，确保了整个高阶程序逻辑连同见证证据的无损迁移；计算稠密模拟能够直接从翻译中提取出标记稳定推理的模态（涵盖经典可实现性的双重否定模态和层化等已知案例）。
conclusion: 该框架成功将副作用的改变转化为一等对象，不仅支持组合与模态分解，还能判定某些逻辑迁移的不存在性，为跨副作用环境迁移经验证的高阶程序逻辑与推导证据开辟了坚实的范畴论路径。

title: Forget the Lineage: Forward-Secure, Lineage-Complete Cryptographic Erasure for LLM-Agent Memory
authors: Yulliwas Ameur, Billal Mokhtari, Samia Bouzefrane
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents keep a long-term memory that the model itself writes: summaries, extracted facts and embeddings derived from what users said. Deleting a message is therefore not enough: its derivatives, storage residue and backups survive. We define lineage-complete forward-secure erasure: after a forget request, an adversary that later obtains all storage and the agent's current keys learns nothing about the forgotten input or any memory derived from it. We present LinEra, which encrypts each memory under a key derived from its parents' keys along the derivation graph; source keys come from a puncturable pseudorandom function, so forgetting is a single puncture and every descendant becomes unreadable without being located. A sound lineage rule records as parents everything the writer saw, which confines all influence of a source to its descendants. We prove security and lineage integrity and integrate LinEra with mem0. With real LLMs from two families (1.5B to 7B parameters) writing the memory of LoCoMo conversations, an attacker holding every file and the current keys recovers, on all ten conversations written by the largest model, 70 of 71 forgotten secrets after logical deletion, 67 with per-object or epoch keys, and none with LinEra; the same holds for every writer tested. The price is a larger forgetting radius, which follows a simple law in the writer's fan-in: forgetting 1% of turns erases 73.0% of derived memories with session-level summaries but only 3.8% with four-turn windows, which also answer better; re-deriving restores what is lost.
comment: 14 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Code and LLM-call logs: https://github.com/yulliwasameur/linera (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24166476)
zh_title: 遗忘谱系：针对大语言模型智能体记忆的前向安全、谱系完备密码学擦除
translation: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体保留由模型自身写入的长期记忆：从用户输入中提取的摘要、事实及嵌入向量。因此，仅仅删除消息本身并不足够：其派生物、存储残留与备份依然存在。我们定义了谱系完备的前向安全擦除：在收到遗忘请求后，随后获取所有存储介质和智能体当前密钥的攻击者，无法了解任何有关被遗忘输入或由此派生的记忆信息。我们提出了LinEra，它沿派生图使用从父节点密钥派生出的密钥对每条记忆进行加密；源密钥来自可穿孔伪随机函数，因此遗忘仅需一次穿孔操作，所有后代记忆无需被逐一定位即可全部变为不可读。完备的谱系规则将写入者看到的所有内容记录为父节点，从而将源的影响严格限制在其后代中。我们证明了其安全性和谱系完整性，并将LinEra与mem0集成。使用两个系列（1.5B至7B参数）的真实LLM写入LoCoMo对话记忆，在持有所有文件和当前密钥的攻击者面对最大模型写入的全部十场对话时，逻辑删除后可恢复71个被遗忘机密中的70个，按对象或纪元密钥方案可恢复67个，而LinEra恢复数为零；测试的所有写入模型均呈现相同结果。其代价是更大的遗忘半径，这遵循写入者扇入的简单规律：遗忘1%的轮次在会话级摘要下会擦除73.0%的派生记忆，但在4轮窗口下仅擦除3.8%（且回答质量更佳）；重新推导可恢复丢失的内容。
tldr: 提出LinEra系统，利用基于派生图的密钥派生与可穿孔伪随机函数，实现即使存储全泄露也能使被遗忘信息及其所有派生记忆完全无法恢复的前向安全加密擦除。
ai_comments: LinEra针对大语言模型智能体记忆遗忘的痛点，创新性地将谱系追踪与可穿孔伪随机函数（PPRF）相结合，实现了即使存储和当前密钥全部泄露也无法恢复遗忘信息的前向安全密码学擦除。其主要权衡在于遗忘半径受输入扇入大小影响，但通过优化上下文窗口切分和重新推导，能够在保证完全安全的同时将过度擦除控制在极低水平。
motivation: 大语言模型智能体会自行写入摘要、提取事实及向量嵌入等长期记忆，单纯删除原始消息无法清除其派生记忆、存储残留和备份，容易导致敏感信息泄露。亟需一种在发生遗忘请求后，即使敌手获得全部存储和当前密钥也无法推断出被遗忘内容及其派生记忆的安全擦除机制。
method: 提出了LinEra系统：1）沿记忆派生图，使用由父节点密钥派生出的密钥对各级记忆进行加密；2）源密钥由可穿孔伪随机函数（PPRF）生成，遗忘操作只需进行单次穿孔即可使该源及所有后代记忆全部不可读且无需定位目标；3）采用完备谱系规则记录写入者所见的所有内容作为父节点，将源影响严格限制在后代中；4）在mem0上进行了集成。
results: 在LoCoMo对话数据集及1.5B至7B参数的LLM实验中，敌手持有所有存储和当前密钥时，逻辑删除下泄露了71个被遗忘机密中的70个，每对象/时期密钥方案泄露67个，而LinEra完全没有泄露（0个）。在遗忘代价方面，遗忘1%的轮次在会话级摘要下擦除73.0%的派生记忆，而在4轮窗口切分下仅擦除3.8%，且短窗口回答质量更佳，遗失记忆可通过重新推导恢复。
conclusion: LinEra实现了前向安全且谱系完备的LLM智能体记忆加密擦除机制，在不依赖物理定位或破坏底层备份存储的前提下，可彻底阻断敌手从残留和派生数据中恢复被遗忘机密的可能性。

title: Which Model, For Which Variable? Per-Variable Forecast Combination in Sparse ICU Time Series
authors: Marius Fracarolli, Stefan Riezler
abstract: Clinical forecasting papers typically report a single best architecture. We show that on multivariate ICU physiology this question conceals variable-specific differences: no architecture is best on every variable, and which model wins changes from variable to variable. Across five ICU databases (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, eICU, HiRID, and UMM (University Medicine Mannheim), a German single-center ICU) we forecast 94 channels over a 24-hour horizon with a pool of 14 models, and combine them with weights fitted per variable. On test, the combination beats the best single model on all five databases by 6.1-11.0% mean squared error (mean 8.7%). The gain is concentrated where clinical data is thinnest: the sparsest third of channels improves by 11.9% and laboratory values by 7.5%, against 3.1% for the densest third. Rank-based harmonic weighting of the best five models per variable, with no fitted weights at all, recovers about four-fifths of the gain. Extending the pool afterwards with a per-channel gradient-boosted tree, ARIMA and ETS makes the tree the validation-selected best single model on all five databases; per-variable combination still improves on it by 2.9-5.9% (significant on four of five), while equal weighting of the same members does not. As on univariate benchmarks, learned combination beats simple averaging - but only once the weights are constrained. We also report which model to prefer when, and show that the ordering changes with database size.
comment: Accepted at Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026 Findings Track, Sydney

title: Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models
authors: Konstantinos Dovelos
abstract: Computational models of pulsed field ablation predict the lesion as the tissue where the electric field exceeds a lethal threshold. Their numerical error is rarely bounded, and automated pipelines increasingly run them without an expert checking each result. To verify each run, we separate the question "was the stated model solved correctly?" from the solver that answers it. An untrusted solver returns with its answer a certificate, consisting of a potential with the correct electrode and ground values and an exactly charge-conserving current. A small independent checker verifies the certificate against a written specification of the physics. Using the Prager-Synge hypercircle theorem evaluated in ball arithmetic, it turns the certificate into guaranteed two-sided bounds on the impedance and on the root-mean-square field of every tile of a lesion map, also over a range of blood/tissue conductivity ratios. A vectorized version of the checker takes about a tenth of the solve time. For a focal electrode in contact, the tile-resolved depth at 1000 V and 700 V/cm is proven to lie in 3.50-3.75 mm for every ratio from 1.7 to 3.75. For a bipolar catheter, certified depths overlap published in-vivo depths. Where they differ from a published reference model, the certificates prove that the difference is not numerical error in our computation. We compare the certificate with a grid convergence study on the same solver. On graded grids the study is sharper for local fields but remains an estimate. On uniform grids it fails to converge at the electrode edge, where the certificate still gives a valid bracket. Solvers that deliberately solve equations other than the specified ones pass the grid convergence study, but the certificates refute their claims or leave them unsupported.

title: The Complexity of Traffic Engineering in Segment Routing Networks
authors: Matthias Bentert, Stefan Schmid
abstract:
Segment routing is a modern variant of source routing which has recently become popular in the Internet. It allows operators to equip network packets with an additional header which specifies segments: a list of waypoints the packet needs to traverse on its way to the destination. This is reminiscent of Valiant routing in parallel computing and introduces an additional degree of freedom in traffic engineering. This flexibility can be exploited to minimize congestion in the network.
  This paper sheds light on the computational complexity of traffic engineering in segment routing networks. We consider two problem variants: a fixed-length variant where link weights are given and only waypoints can be chosen, and a variable-length variant where additionally the network operator can also choose the link weights, which then define the shortest paths taken between the waypoints. We prove that the first variant is NP-hard even if the network graph is planar and if all demands and link weights are 1. We also show that the second variant is NP-hard already for planar network graphs with all demands being 1. On the positive side, we present a compact and general mixed integer linear program to compute exact solutions for the first variant.

title: Hamming and Johnson-Type Bounds for Joint Error Correction and Detection
authors: Yulin Chen, Raymond W.Yeung
abstract: We derive upper bounds on the size of codes for joint error correction and detection over classical $q$-ary Hamming spaces. A $(c,c')$ joint error correcting and detecting code corrects every error of weight at most $c$ and detects every error whose weight lies between $c+1$ and $c+c'$. We establish equivalent conditions for this decoding requirement using Hamming balls and Hamming rings, and derive a joint bound that reduces to the Hamming bound when $c'=0$. We introduce joint perfect codes and show that binary repetition codes attain the joint bound whenever $n=2c+c'+1$. For codes satisfying $d_{\min}=2c+c'+1$, we investigate an alternative joint bound based on ring multiplicity and constant-weight code bounds. A further argument using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and pairwise ring intersections yields a refined joint bound that is always at least as strong as the original joint bound. We then incorporate an additional outer Hamming shell to obtain a Johnson-type extension. This extension provides a strict improvement for binary codes with $c'=1$, $d_{\min}=2c+2$, $c\geq2$, and $d_{\min}+2\leq n\leq3d_{\min}/2-1$. These results connect sphere-packing bounds with the geometry of joint error correction and detection.
comment: This manuscript is a preliminary draft and is currently being revised. The final version will be posted once the revisions are complete. Comments and suggestions are welcome

title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
authors: Alexandru Rancea, Ionut Anghel, Tudor Cioara, Ovidiu Anchidin, Ancuta Nemes
abstract: The automated transformation of unstructured natural language process descriptions into Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams remains a challenging task, due to linguistic ambiguity and the difficulty to detect non-adjacent control-flow relationships. This paper proposes a solution for generating BPMN models from natural language descriptions through a multi-layered pipeline that integrates transformer-based architectures, Large Language Models and ontology population. The proposed method starts with natural language descriptions and separates textual processing, control-flow relation extraction, and structural validation into dedicated components. Entity extraction is performed using a fine-tuned RoBERTa-based transformer model while a control-flow engine captures non-adjacent relationships through LLM-based inference. To improve generalization under limited available data, the approach uses a dynamic few-shot strategy with con- trolled template input construction, enabling improved generalization under limited data availability. Additionally, an ontology population mechanism is introduced to represent the generated process models as semantic knowledge structures. For evaluation purposes we have used from the literature and industry reference processes. Additionally, we have validated the proposed method on a real-world heart disease patients transitional care process, capturing practical constraints and multi-actor collaboration, and serving as an expert-defined benchmark scenario. Experimental results demonstrate strong performance in the relation extraction task, achieving an accuracy of 90.7%, as well as maintaining structural alignment between the generated and reference BPMN models across multiple evaluation scenarios scenarios.

title: On the Limits of Sufficient Explanations
authors: Klaus Weinbauer, Peter F. Stadler, Thomas Gärtner, Sagar Malhotra
abstract: We formally characterize the conditions under which sufficient explanations exist for classifiers on structured data such as graphs and strings. We focus on post-hoc explainers that select parts of the input as sufficient explanations. An explanation is sufficient if the selected part alone ensures the predicted label. Sufficient explanations have been widely adopted across data modalities, including graphs, strings, and images. However, a unified formal analysis of sufficient explanations remains missing. We bridge this gap with four main contributions: (i) We define a general explanation formalism consisting of an instance space, a classifier, and a select relation. The select relation specifies which potential sub-instances or feature subsets can be selected as explanations from each instance; (ii) We show that the existence of sufficient explainers is fully characterized by the interplay between the classifier and the select relation; (iii) We extend this analysis to practically relevant variants of sufficiency, including probabilistic sufficiency and deletion sufficiency; (iv) Based on the formal analysis, we devise statistics that bound the maximum achievable sufficiency for a given task. We evaluate these statistics on language, protein, and molecular classification datasets and find that full sufficiency is unattainable on most of them. Since these bounds hold for every explainer, they provide a task-level reference against which any explainer's sufficiency can be judged in absolute terms.

title: An entropy-stable splitting strategy for a hyperbolic dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes
authors: Frédéric Couderc, Arnaud Duran, Maria Kazakova, Bastien Lombard, Pascal Noble, Rémy Baraille, Jean-Paul Vila
abstract: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the \textit{slow} gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the \textit{fast} acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.

title: The QBF Gallery 2026
authors: Cynthia Peyrer, Luca Pulina, Martina Seidl
abstract:
The QBF Gallery 2026 is the latest evaluation event of (dependency) quantified Boolean formula (QBF) solving technology. Its goal is to assess the current state-of-the-art, enable the evaluation of novel solvers on newly curated benchmark instances and present the progress made since the previous competition. This report discusses the solvers, instances and tools submitted by the community and introduces new benchmark collections for evaluation. We evaluate solvers in three tracks, reflecting most common input formats in (dependency) QBF solving. In addition to those main evaluations, we investigate effects of preprocessing and include a track of new crafted benchmark families.
  The results are analyzed using various metrics and complementary statistics on solver similarities, different memory limitations and performance across formula families. Finally, the dedicated benchmarks for each track are made available as an artifact to support future research and reproducible evaluation.

title: ALoMa: Affine Correspondences Beyond Patches
authors: David Nordström, Georg Bökman, Viktor Larsson, Fredrik Kahl, Jonathan Ventura
abstract: Affine correspondences (ACs) enable robust and efficient solvers for multiple-view geometry by constraining the local geometry of point correspondences (PCs). Despite their utility in minimal solvers, AC estimation remains understudied. We revisit AC estimation beyond local image patches, extending it to the image and image-pair levels. Rather than estimating the components of the affine transformation separately, we learn the full 4-DoF matrix jointly. Building on this formulation, we introduce ALoMa, an AC estimator using LoMa keypoint descriptions, demonstrating consistent improvements across a wide range of downstream tasks. Code at https://github.com/davnords/loma.

title: Who Counts as Exposed? Measurement Choices in an Open, Re-estimable Index of Occupational AI Exposure
authors: Luca Mouchel, Pierre Bouquet, Yossi Sheffi
abstract: Occupational AI exposure indices are used as inputs to economic analysis, workforce planning, and policy, and the choices built into them decide which workers are described as exposed. We build an open, re-estimable task-level index and vary its two main design decisions, context and calibration, to show how much the answer depends on them. For each of the 18,796 occupation--task pairs in \onet, seven open-weight reasoning models rate exposure under a common rubric. Each model rates with or without a context of retrieved news and research passages, workplace descriptors, and a bottleneck-based reasoning protocol, and the ensemble is combined with or without simplex-constrained calibration to observed Claude usage. The largest difference from the dominant 2023 benchmark is not a disagreement about what AI can do but about how much credit to give exposure that depends on software integrations not yet built, a choice that no data can settle. At the benchmark's own weight, the calibrated index counts fewer exposed workers than the benchmark, and when only direct exposure counts it counts more. At full score resolution, the ensemble ranks tasks better than the benchmark against observed usage and an independent physical-task classification. Adding context mainly shifts the level of exposure rather than improving the ranking. Context and calibration both relocate exposure toward higher-wage occupations, and calibration, which anchors the index to one platform's users, does more of it, so we also release the uncalibrated arm. Exposure indices used as policy inputs should state such choices, report their numbers under the alternatives, and be re-estimated as systems change.

title: Safety Analysis of Parameterized Networks with Shared Counters
authors: June Roupin, Arnaud Sangnier
abstract: We study networks with an unbounded number of processes sharing some natural counters that can be decremented, incremented and tested to zero. We look at two safety problems: the first one asks whether there is a network with an execution bringing a process in a given final state and the other one asks the execution to bring all the processes in the final state. In their full generality, these two problems are undecidable, but we show that decidability can be regained by either using a single counter or by forbidding the use of zero-tests (as it is is the case in Vector Addition Systems with States). For these decidable cases, we obtain low complexity results, the problems being solvable either in non-deterministic logarithmic space or in polynomial time.

title: STaG: Human-Annotation-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Text-Based Person Retrieval
authors: Ji Yucheng, Bai Yang, Li Yang, Zhou Xinyu, Cao Min
abstract: Real-world deployment of Text-Based Person Retrieval (TBPR) is bottlenecked by the absence of textual annotations in new domains. Existing Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA-TBPR) methods still assume access to target-domain human-written annotations (albeit unpaired with images), limiting their practicality. We consider a more practical setting: human-annotation-free UDA-TBPR, with labeled image-text data in the source domain and annotation-free, unlabeled images in the target domain. This setting introduces two core challenges: the absence of cross-modal alignment in the target domain, and visual domain shifts from source to target. To tackle these, we propose STaG, a dual-path framework comprising Style-Agnostic Text Alignment (SATA) and Heterogeneous Graph Memory Alignment (HGMA). Specifically, SATA leverages source-domain data to decouple identity-discriminative semantics from machine-generated stylistic artifacts, establishing robust cross-modal alignment for the target domain. Meanwhile, HGMA exploits cross-domain semantic neighborhoods via a memory-based graph to learn domain-invariant visual features. Ultimately, STaG achieves state-of-the-art performance across three benchmarks under this realistic setting.

title: Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders
authors: Diane Bouchacourt, Gaëtan Brison
abstract: Medical AI systems that answer users' queries rely on retrieving medical knowledge from large document collections. In this context, finetuning general models on medical datasets can improve retrieval relevance. Yet the dense embeddings underlying modern retrieval systems remain largely opaque, making it difficult to understand the mechanics behind their results. Moreover, adapting to a specific medical dataset risks losing transferability to new clinical corpora. In this work, we tackle these issues by applying Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to medical information retrieval, transforming dense text embeddings into semantically interpretable representations. To do so, our model combines a reconstruction objective with an InfoNCE contrastive loss that directly preserves query-document relevance. We evaluate three embedding models across six medical retrieval datasets, both in-domain and out-of-domain. Trained on a medical corpus, our sparse codes improve in-domain retrieval over the original embeddings, and lose less out-of-domain performance than their dense counterparts, especially when the target corpus is distant from the training one. Importantly, our experiments show that the method yields interpretable features whose semantic content can be inferred from the queries and documents that activate them most strongly. The interpretation of these features sheds light on why a particular document was retrieved, and transfers beyond the training distribution.

title: PTMTD: A Topology-Aware Temporal-Graph Attention Network for Joint Cyber-Attack Detection and Relay-Level Localization in Power System Protection Networks
authors: Shahin Razazni, Mohammad Ali Alirezapouri
abstract: The digitization of protection relays exposes power grids to sophisticated cyberattacks, yet existing GNN detectors omit temporal encoding, rely on static topologies, and lack relay localization. We propose PTMTD-a Pearson-driven Temporal Multimodal Topology-aware Detection Network-coupling a dilated TCN with multi-head GATv2 in a dual-head architecture for simultaneous 37-class detection and four-relay localization. PTMTD constructs its graph from measurement correlations (no impedance data) and is trained with a composite loss jointly optimizing both tasks. On the MSU-ORNL benchmark (78,377 samples, 37 classes), it achieves 99.27% accuracy, 99.25% macro F1, and 95.98% localization, outperforming GraphKAN, LSTM, GCN, and Random Forest by 5.64-11.15 percentage points (p < 0.05). Ablations confirm gains from temporal encoding (+2.38%), graph attention (+2.69%), residuals (+2.07%), and correlation-driven supervision. With 639k parameters and 2.5 ms CPU inference, PTMTD is lightweight and deployment-ready. While validated on a transmission testbed, the architecture applies to microgrids with similar relay structures. Code and models are publicly available.

title: When Should a Virtual Patient Ask? RISP-Guided Proactive Information Seeking in Multi-Agent Patient Simulation
authors: Jingyao Cai, Shuaijun Liu, Abdul Rehman, Xiaowan Li, Qintian, Thomas Dolby, Sue M Green, Xiaosong Yang
abstract: Virtual patient (VP) systems support nursing communication training by providing simulated encounters in which learners practise explaining care and responding to patient concerns. Although large language models (LLMs) support flexible dialogue, current approaches give less explicit attention to how patients' information needs develop and guide the content and timing of their questions. We draw on the Risk Information Seeking and Processing (RISP) model, which relates information seeking to perceived risk and the gap between perceived knowledge and desired understanding. Guided by this perspective, we propose the RISP Multi-Agent System (RISP-MAS), a VP system for patient-initiated information seeking. The system links ongoing assessment of the patient's perceptions and information needs to coordinated decisions about whether to seek information, when to ask and which uncertainty to address. Evaluation of nursing student-VP interactions suggested that RISP-MAS exhibited plausible patient information-seeking behaviour, as indicated by expert assessments, while student feedback reflected positive interaction experiences. This work extends patient simulation by connecting a psychological account of information needs to explicit decisions about question initiation. The approach offers nursing students opportunities to practise recognising unresolved patient concerns and tailoring explanations to patients' information needs.

title: ESI: An Embodied Self-Improvement Flywheel for LLM-VLA Agents
authors: Yundi Cai, Zihan Wang, Chenxi Han, Yi Cheng, Houde Liu, Zilei Wang
abstract: Independently pretrained language models and vision-language-action (VLA) policies provide complementary building blocks for embodied agents, but connecting them does not automatically produce coordinated behavior. The VLA may generate actions that diverge from the LLM's intended subtask and, upon regaining control after a correction, undo the promising state restored by the LLM. We introduce ESI (Embodied Self-Improvement), an automated flywheel that uses environmental interaction to align reasoning and action. ESI treats the modular agent as the unit of post-training, repeatedly refining the prompts that guide the LLM, the shared skill interface that expresses its intent, and the VLA parameters that realize that intent, then redeploying these components together. Our key insight is that collaboration itself can supply supervision for improving this interface. The LLM's subtask decisions provide semantic supervision for what the policy should execute, while its effective corrections and subsequent student continuations provide action-level supervision for recovery and handoff. The student also learns from its own effective execution, allowing locally useful experience to contribute even when the overall episode fails. On ten selected RoboDojo tasks, ESI achieves a mean Score of 62.03 and a mean success rate of 49.41% using an LLM-VLA agent without generating task-specific control code. On both metrics, it outperforms the published reference results of all hybrid embodied agents, including the Agent+WAM system GO-3 Nano Preview (47.27 Score and 36.60% success), as well as all compared code-based methods.
comment: Technical report. 25 pages, 7 figures. Code: https://github.com/ZERITH-ZLab/ESI

title: SemRAG: Semantic-Guided Sentence-Level Retrieval-Augmented Sign Language Production
authors: Xiao Liu, Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Peishuo Liu, Bowen Guo, Kuizhuang Liu, Cong Wang, Lei Xie
abstract: Sign language production (SLP) aims to generate sign pose sequences that faithfully express spoken-language text while preserving the rhythm and coordination patterns of signing. Common SLP methods learn text-to-pose mappings from training data but often suffer from semantic inaccuracies in long or complex sentences. Retrieval augmentation offers a way to introduce realistic signing priors to provide more explicit guidance for text-to-pose generation. However, existing retrieval-based SLP methods typically operate at the gloss or word level, relying on gloss-pose dictionaries or isolated sign segments that require costly annotations and fail to preserve continuous sentence-level dynamics. To bridge this gap, we propose SemRAG, a semantic-guided sentence-level retrieval-augmented framework that retrieves full-sentence signing templates as priors without constructing gloss/word-level sign dictionaries. While such templates preserve local motion patterns and global rhythm, they also introduce a semantic mismatch problem: irrelevant motions in the retrieved sentence may interfere with the target semantics. To address this issue, we introduce an SLT-guided template semantic localization module that identifies target-relevant temporal regions within the retrieved template while suppressing irrelevant signing content. To adaptively incorporate the template features into the generator, we further introduce layer-specific learnable gates that regulate their contribution across generator layers. Extensive experiments show that SemRAG improves semantic consistency and motion quality over baselines under both back-translation and motion accuracy metrics.

title: NPU-Accelerated GNSS Signal Acquisition
authors: Taro Suzuki
abstract: On small single-board computers (SBCs), GNSS signal acquisition is a major CPU load. This paper proposes using the neural processing unit (NPU) of an SBC not for machine learning but as an accelerator for the parallel code search in GNSS signal acquisition. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) used in acquisition is decomposed by the four-step DFT into matrix products of small DFTs and expressed by $1\times1$ convolutions, element-wise products, and transposes, which NPUs execute efficiently. Furthermore, we propose a method that divides the DFT, the non-coherent integration, and the peak detection between the CPU and the NPU according to the configuration of the NPU (an NPU with its own memory connected via PCIe, or an NPU sharing memory with the CPU). The proposed method is implemented in the open-source software GNSS receiver Pocket SDR and evaluated on a Raspberry Pi 5 combined with the external AX8850 NPU and on the NPU built into the SoC (RK3588) of the ROCK 5C, a small SBC of comparable size. Compared with acquisition by an optimized CPU implementation, the acquisition of short codes on the Raspberry Pi 5 with the AX8850 is 3.0-3.8 times faster. In the evaluation of the whole receiver, the number of tracking channels that reach their first lock within 30 s with the NPU is 1.5 times that with the CPU, and the time until 90% of the channels are locked is reduced from 66 s to 26 s. Furthermore, because the CPU load of acquisition is reduced, the number of tracking channels that can be processed in real time increases from about 175 to about 230. These results show that using the NPU on SBCs with limited CPU resources is effective for achieving both GNSS signal acquisition and tracking. The implementation is publicly available as open source under the name PocketSDR-NPU.

title: MarathonTS: a benchmark of long synthetic time series from window assembly and long-series generators
authors: Ilyas Varshavskiy, Sergey Shulgin, Shuhrat Khalilbekov, Bonu Boboeva, Azizjon Azimi
abstract: Many applications of synthetic time series require a series that is much longer than the windows on which a generative model is trained. Such a series can be assembled from a pool of short generated windows, which requires deciding which windows are taken, in what order, and how their seams are processed, or it can be produced directly by a long-series generator. This study presents MarathonTS, to our knowledge the first open benchmark that compares both families under one protocol. Every method produces a series of the same length on 9 open hourly datasets with 10 seeds. The series is evaluated by its fidelity to the real data (83 metrics in 12 groups, against three real references: train, validation and an out-of-time split), by its utility (models are trained on the synthetic series only and tested on real data, TSTR against TRTR, in 14 classification and regression tasks), by its memorisation of the training data and by its computational cost. The statistical analysis is carried out as a separate stage that reads the published tables and gives the rankings of every method in every slice, the answers to the research questions with tests and uncertainty, and the results of a pre-specified confirmatory family. In the main run, the methods differ in both confirmatory cells; the choice of windows matters more than the processing of their seams, which does not improve the series, and no method trains the downstream models as well as the real series. The top tier of the leaderboard is reproduced on other hardware, whereas the exact places within it are not. For the reproducibility of the study, the code, the data hashes and all results are publicly available (links below).

title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
authors: Yue Xu, Kaiyun Wei, Wenying Duan, Zichen Xu, Shuai Ma, Xiaoxi He
abstract: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect. Since observations at each location form a time series, this motivates a natural question: can abundant time-series data enhance STFMs when spatio-temporal observations are scarce? To bridge this gap, we propose T2ST, a data-efficient training framework that augments limited spatio-temporal observations with selected auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model. Our key insight is that temporal pattern learning can benefit from abundant external time series, while spatial dependency learning remains grounded in real spatio-temporal observations. Guided by this insight, T2ST retrieves matched sequences to reinforce sparsely observed temporal patterns and selects reliable complementary sequences to broaden temporal coverage. Temporal relation distillation aligns relationships among historical patches, while multi-scale prediction distillation transfers forecasting behavior at fine and coarse temporal resolutions, enabling knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. Using only 10\% of the original spatio-temporal data, T2ST enables STFMs to achieve overall forecasting performance competitive with or superior to their full-data counterparts across six long-term and twelve short-term forecasting datasets. These results establish a new paradigm for data-efficient training of spatio-temporal foundation models. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/T2ST-65F3/.

title: Movable Antenna-Aided ISAC: A Time- and Frequency-Division Framework
authors: Yuyan Zhou, Haocheng Hua, Jie Xu, Rui Zhang
abstract: This paper investigates movable-antenna (MA)-enhanced integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) under time division duplex (TDD) and frequency division duplex (FDD) protocols, where sensing and communications occupy orthogonal time and frequency resources, respectively. A wideband target-position Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) is derived under a pulse-radar framework with pulse compression, incorporating delay and angle estimation error bounds in Cartesian coordinates. Both bounds depend on sensing power; the delay bound also depends on sensing bandwidth, while the angle bound depends on the effective aperture determined by the antenna position vector (APV). A worst-case position CRB over a prescribed target region ensures robust sensing performance. For multiuser downlink communication, joint APV and resource-allocation problems are formulated for TDD and FDD to maximize the minimum achievable user rate subject to the sensing requirement. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed for FDD, while TDD is addressed by searching over feasible sensing pulse numbers combined with APV optimization. Representative scenarios clarify how MA improves channel orthogonality and enlarges the sensing aperture, and how these effects shape the TDD/FDD rate comparison. Numerical results show that APV optimization enlarges the communication-sensing tradeoff region over fixed-position antenna benchmarks. The optimized configurations exhibit distinct tendencies: TDD favors a larger antenna position variance, whereas FDD favors better channel orthogonality among users.

title: Data-Driven Sparse Identification and Robust Tube-Based Predictive Control for Multivariable Chaotic Systems
authors: Shahin Razani
abstract: This paper addresses the data-driven synchronization and robust control of multivariable chaotic systems subject to strict actuation constraints, modeling uncertainties and bounded input disturbances. Using empirical data collected from a four-dimensional chaotic Rossler response system, Sequentially Thresholded Least Squares (STLSQ) sparse regression is employed to recover a nominal control-affine model, achieving an identification accuracy of R^2 = 1.0000 across all channels with root-mean-square error within [4.15e-6, 8.33e-4]. To establish a mathematically rigorous bridge between data-driven identification and robust synthesis, all structural discrepancies in the drift vector field and input matrix are unified into a single lumped uncertainty field delta(x,u). A computable scalar bound delta_bar is established based on library truncation error, regression residuals, input bounds, and Lipschitz constants (Lemma 1). We subsequently prove that input-output feedback linearization maps delta(x,u) into a state- and control-dependent additive disturbance d(z,nu) in Brunovsky canonical coordinates, bounded by ||d(z,nu)||_2 <= alpha_1 delta_bar + alpha_2 delta_bar ||nu||_2 with closed-form expressions for alpha_1 and alpha_2 (Theorem 1). This certified bound, together with a bounded input disturbance and a zero-order-hold margin, yields a compact disturbance set that seeds a robust tube-based model predictive controller. We prove that the resulting tightened quadratic program is recursively feasible, that the physical actuator limit (|u_i| <= 1100) remains inactive under an explicit sufficient condition, and that the closed-loop tracking error is Input-to-State Stable (ISS) with an asymptotic gain that is linear in delta_bar plus a term due to the exogenous input disturbance (Theorems 2 and 3).

title: Go under Chinese Rules with a Succinct Game History is Complete for Exponential Space
authors: Markus Bläser, Felix Czerner
abstract:
The complexity of games is a central topic in combinatorics, algorithms, and computational complexity theory. It asks how difficult it is to determine the winner of a combinatorial game under optimal play. Many games, such as Hex or Othello, are PSPACE-complete: the game tree has polynomial depth, so the game can be decided in PSPACE. However, some games allow exponentially long plays, for instance Chess (without a generalized 50-move rule) or Go under Japanese rules; these are complete for exponential time. To prevent infinite games, some games employ a no-repetition rule (super-ko rule), for instance Go under Chinese rules. Robson (1984) proved that Chess and Checkers with a no-repetition rule are even harder: deciding whether the first player has a winning strategy is EXPSPACE-complete. Since then, it has been an open problem whether Go with a no-repetition rule is EXPSPACE-complete, too.
  The complexity of a game under a no-repetition rule is typically interpreted as follows: given a board position, decide whether the first player has a winning strategy such that no repetition occurs from that position on. We introduce the concept of a succinct game history: a Boolean circuit that, given a board position, outputs 1 if the position is in the game history and 0 otherwise. It serves as a "judge" that tells the players whether a move is illegal because it creates a repetition. We prove that deciding whether Black has a winning strategy in Go with a no-repetition rule is EXPSPACE-complete when the game history is given succinctly. Moreover, the starting position in our hardness proof is reachable by legal gameplay, which has not always been the case in prior proofs.
comment: A preliminary version of this paper appears in the Proceedings of the ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA 2027)

title: Who sets the consent signal? Platform defaults and crawl coverage in measuring opt-outs from AI training
authors: Marcin Lawenda
abstract: Web data used in social research and in the training of AI models increasingly carry consent signals, but who sets these signals is rarely measured. This paper attributes opt-outs from AI training to the party that set them. The complete lists of Polish, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian and German domains recorded by Common Crawl, with 3,445,751 reachable sites, were crawled in October 2026 together with a random sample of 10,000 Slovak registry domains. Each signal was matched against vendor templates and identical files. Four exploratory hypotheses were examined with logistic models. Between 0.70% and 3.82% of the listed sites opt out. Platform and hosting defaults set 15% to 78% of the opt-outs. Settings active by default reach 60% to 95% of a vendor's sites, while settings that owners switch on reach at most 2.1%. Most of the higher Czech and Slovak rates compared with Germany are statistically attributable to platforms. Lists derived from Common Crawl miss about a third of the Slovak opt-outs because they exclude sites that block its crawler. The results describe delegated consent, a signal that a platform sets on behalf of its users, which measurements of consent on the web must consider.

title: New Results on the Subfield Metric
authors: Ana Kosovac, Jeanette Plechinger, Nikola Spirovski, Violetta Weger
abstract:
In this paper, we further develop the theory of the recently introduced $λ$-subfield metric. We investigate extremal codes, classical bounds and asymptotic densities in this setting.
  We first study codes attaining a Singleton-type bound, called Maximum $λ$-subfield Distance (M$λ$D) codes. We establish structural restrictions on their parameters and extend the theory to sublinear codes. We then investigate the asymptotic density of M$λ$D codes in several parameter regimes and compare their behavior with that of MDS and MRD codes.
  We then turn to a Plotkin-like bound, where we construct a family of constant-weight codes attaining the bound and classify all non-degenerate linear constant-weight codes for $λ>1$.
  Finally, we complement the collection of classical coding-theoretic bounds available for the $λ$-subfield metric by deriving Griesmer-, Elias- and Johnson-type bounds.
translation:
在本文中，我们进一步发展了最近引入的λ-子域度量理论。我们在此背景下研究了极值码、经典界限和渐近密度。
我们首先研究了达到Singleton型界限的码，称为最大λ-子域距离（MλD）码。我们确定了其参数的结构限制，并将该理论扩展到次线性码。然后，我们研究了MλD码在几个参数范围内的渐近密度，并将其行为与MDS和MRD码进行了比较。
然后，我们转向了Plotkin型界限，在此基础上我们构建了一族达到该界限的常重码，并分类了所有λ>1的非退化线性常重码。
最后，我们通过推导Griesmer、Elias和Johnson型界限，补充了适用于λ-子域度量的经典编码理论界限集合。
tldr: 本文进一步发展了λ-子域度量理论，研究了极值码、经典界限和渐近密度，包括MλD码、常重码以及Griesmer、Elias和Johnson型界限。
ai_comments: 本文在λ-子域度量这一新兴领域取得了重要进展，通过系统地研究极值码、渐近密度和多种经典编码界限，极大地丰富和完善了该度量下的编码理论框架。其创新性在于将经典的编码理论概念和工具应用于λ-子域度量，并取得了具体的理论成果。
motivation: 进一步发展最近引入的λ-子域度量理论。
method: 研究了达到Singleton型界限的MλD码，包括其参数的结构限制和对次线性码的扩展。调查了MλD码在不同参数范围内的渐近密度。构建了一族达到Plotkin型界限的常重码，并分类了λ>1的非退化线性常重码。推导了Griesmer、Elias和Johnson型界限。
results: 建立了MλD码的结构限制，并将其理论扩展到次线性码。研究了MλD码的渐近密度，并与MDS和MRD码进行了比较。构建了一族达到Plotkin型界限的常重码，并分类了λ>1的非退化线性常重码。推导了Griesmer、Elias和Johnson型界限，补充了λ-子域度量的经典编码理论界限。
conclusion: 本文通过研究MλD码、常重码和推导新的编码理论界限，进一步发展了λ-子域度量理论，丰富了该度量下的经典编码理论框架。

title: From Pen-and-Paper to Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean for System Identification
authors: Manas Mejari, Dario Piga, Marco Forgione
abstract: Mathematical proofs in scientific papers are often long and intricate, relying on chains of references to earlier results. This makes it difficult for readers and reviewers to verify each and every step. Interactive theorem proving offers a complement: the theorem and its proof are written as code, and every inference is checked by a small, trusted piece of software called the kernel. This paper serves as an introduction to the Lean 4 proof assistant for a system identification and control audience, assuming no prior exposure to formal methods. We first show how a Lean proof is read using two elementary examples: the first on identifiability, the second on set invariance. We then illustrate how Lean can be used to analyse results from the literature, taking as example a classic lemma on the inversion of the noise filter in prediction-error identification (Ljung, 1999, Lemma 3.1). Since in Lean every step must be justified, the formalization brings to light a subtle point: the original claim of that lemma holds almost surely, although not for every realisation, as its statement may suggest. A simple counterexample makes this concrete. Finally, the paper discusses guidelines and perspectives on the use of Lean in system identification research.
zh_title: 从手写证明到机器验证：Lean在系统辨识中的应用
translation: 科学论文中的数学证明通常冗长而复杂，依赖于对早期结果的引用链。这使得读者和审稿人难以验证每一步。交互式定理证明提供了一个补充：定理及其证明被写成代码，并且每一个推论都由一个小型、受信任的软件（称为内核）进行检查。本文旨在向系统辨识与控制领域的读者介绍Lean 4证明助手，假设读者之前没有接触过形式化方法。我们首先通过两个基本示例展示了如何阅读Lean证明：第一个是关于可识别性，第二个是关于集合不变性。然后，我们以预测误差辨识中噪声滤波器反演的一个经典引理（Ljung，1999，引理3.1）为例，说明了Lean如何用于分析文献中的结果。由于在Lean中每一步都必须有依据，形式化过程揭示了一个微妙之处：该引理的原始主张“几乎必然”成立，尽管不像其陈述可能暗示的那样对每个实现都成立。一个简单的反例使其具体化。最后，本文讨论了在系统辨识研究中使用Lean的指导方针和前景。
tldr: 本文向系统辨识与控制领域的读者介绍了Lean 4证明助手，通过实例展示了如何使用Lean进行数学证明的机器验证，并发现了一个经典引理的微妙之处：它仅在“几乎必然”的条件下成立，而非在所有情况下都成立。
ai_comments: 本文创新性地将交互式定理证明工具Lean 4引入系统辨识领域，展示了其在提高数学证明严谨性和发现现有理论中潜在细微差别方面的巨大潜力。通过对经典引理的验证，揭示了其适用条件的精确性，这对于确保科学研究的准确性具有重要意义。该工作为系统辨识领域的理论验证提供了一种强大的新工具和方法论。
motivation: 科学论文中的数学证明通常冗长复杂，依赖于对早期结果的引用链，这使得读者和审稿人难以验证每一步。
method: 本文介绍了Lean 4证明助手，假设读者没有形式化方法的经验。首先通过两个基本示例（可识别性和集合不变性）展示了如何阅读Lean证明。然后，以一个关于预测误差辨识中噪声滤波器反演的经典引理为例，说明了Lean如何用于分析现有文献结果。
results: 通过Lean的形式化验证，发现了一个微妙之处：该经典引理的原始主张“几乎必然”成立，但并非如其陈述可能暗示的那样对每个实现都成立，并通过一个简单的反例具体化了这一点。
conclusion: Lean在系统辨识研究中可以揭示数学证明中的细微差别，并有助于提高证明的严谨性和可验证性。论文最后讨论了在系统辨识研究中使用Lean的指导方针和前景。

title: Large language models put existential risk from artificial intelligence at 10%
authors: Julian Kauk
abstract: How likely is it that advanced artificial intelligence (AI) will cause human extinction or a similarly permanent disempowerment of humanity? Humans, including AI experts, frequently disagree on this question. Yet one important perspective is missing from this debate: that of AI systems themselves. We put the question to 241 large language models (LLMs) at every available reasoning setting. The models converged on a median risk of 10.0%, with the middle 90% of their estimates between 3.5% and 15.8%, far narrower than the spread among human experts. More expensive, and typically more capable, models stated higher risks; newer models showed more uniform, but not higher, risks. More reasoning barely changed the models' estimates but widened their uncertainty, mostly toward higher risk. Almost all models named loss of control over AI as the most likely cause. These answers are not independent judgments; they likely echo training data, including published expert polls, and choices made in aligning the models. Still, they document the position that current AI systems state on the risks of their own technology. Whether this position reflects any genuine understanding of the systems' own capabilities remains open. Repeated measurements can show whether it shifts as AI systems advance, and how training and alignment shape it is a question for both research and public debate.
zh_title: 大型语言模型将人工智能带来的生存风险评估为10%
translation: 先进人工智能（AI）导致人类灭绝或类似永久性人类权力丧失的可能性有多大？包括AI专家在内的人类经常在这个问题上存在分歧。然而，这场辩论中缺少一个重要的视角：AI系统本身的视角。我们将这个问题抛给了241个大型语言模型（LLMs），在所有可用的推理设置下。模型将风险中位数估计为10.0%，其估计值的中间90%在3.5%到15.8%之间，远窄于人类专家的估计范围。更昂贵、通常更强大的模型报告了更高的风险；更新的模型显示出更统一但并未更高的风险。更多的推理能力几乎没有改变模型的估计，但扩大了其不确定性，主要倾向于更高的风险。几乎所有模型都将对AI失去控制列为最可能的原因。这些答案并非独立的判断；它们可能反映了训练数据，包括已发布的专家调查，以及模型对齐时所做的选择。尽管如此，它们记录了当前AI系统对其自身技术风险的立场。这种立场是否反映了对系统自身能力的真正理解仍有待观察。重复测量可以显示它是否随着AI系统的进步而变化，以及训练和对齐如何塑造它，是研究和公共辩论的问题。
tldr: 研究向241个大型语言模型提问，它们将人工智能导致人类灭绝的生存风险中位数估计为10.0%。更强大的模型报告了更高的风险，且模型普遍认为失控是主要原因。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新之处在于它直接向大型语言模型提问，获取了AI系统对自身技术风险的“自我评估”，这在以往的讨论中是缺失的视角。其重要性在于，它记录了当前AI系统对生存风险的立场，为理解AI的“思维”和潜在风险感知提供了初步数据。然而，论文也明确指出了局限性，即这些回答可能并非AI的“真实”理解，而是训练数据和对齐选择的回声，这提示我们需要谨慎解读这些结果，并进一步研究AI的理解能力和偏见来源。
motivation: 人类专家对先进人工智能（AI）导致人类灭绝或类似永久性权力丧失的可能性存在分歧，而AI系统本身的视角在这一辩论中缺失，因此本研究旨在获取AI系统对自身技术风险的看法。
method: 研究向241个大型语言模型（LLMs）在所有可用的推理设置下提出了关于AI生存风险的问题。
results: 模型对生存风险的估计中位数收敛于10.0%，90%的估计范围在3.5%到15.8%之间，远窄于人类专家的估计范围。更昂贵、通常更强大的模型报告了更高的风险；更新的模型显示出更统一但并未更高的风险。增加推理能力几乎没有改变模型的估计，但扩大了其不确定性，主要倾向于更高的风险。几乎所有模型都将对AI失去控制列为最可能的原因。
conclusion: 本研究记录了当前AI系统对其自身技术风险的立场。这些答案可能反映了训练数据和模型对齐的选择，但它们仍然提供了AI系统自我评估的视角。AI的这种立场是否反映了对其自身能力的真正理解，以及它如何随AI进展而变化，仍有待进一步研究和公共辩论。

title: Characterisation of the DQsym Framework Against Harmonic State-Space and Dynamic Phasor Models for Modular Multilevel Converters
authors: Saif Alsarayreh, Robert Dimitrovski, Aleksandra Lekic'
abstract: Modern power systems rely on power converters that exhibit multifrequency periodic dynamics, such as modular multilevel converters (MMCs). Such converters are commonly analysed using harmonic state-space (HSS) and dynamic phasor (DP) representations. Both approaches rely on building state matrices based on the system topology, whose size grows with the number of harmonics retained in the model. This paper shows that a symmetrical direct-quadrature (dq) dynamic phasor formulation for time-domain simulation, named DQsym, has a smaller solver state matrix than HSS and DP, and whose size is independent of the truncation order K. This reduction results from evaluating harmonic coupling outside the state matrix, in the nonlinear signal blocks. The open-loop MMC model used in this paper is derived in three harmonic-domain (HD) formulations and validated against a three-phase time-domain reference model. The models are compared in terms of state-space size and sparsity, harmonic content, steady-state accuracy and eigenvalues. For truncation at K = 4, the DQsym solver has 45 states against 135 for HSS and DP, stays within about 4% of the reference, and, once closed with its coupling blocks, yields eigenvalues identical to those of HSS and DP.
comment: Submitted to the 25th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission
zh_title: 模块化多电平换流器中DQsym框架与谐波状态空间和动态相量模型的特性分析
translation: 现代电力系统依赖于表现出多频率周期性动态的电力转换器，例如模块化多电平换流器（MMC）。这类转换器通常使用谐波状态空间（HSS）和动态相量（DP）表示进行分析。这两种方法都依赖于基于系统拓扑构建状态矩阵，其大小随模型中保留的谐波数量而增长。本文表明，一种用于时域仿真的对称直交（dq）动态相量公式，命名为DQsym，其求解器状态矩阵比HSS和DP小，并且其大小与截断阶数K无关。这种缩减是由于在非线性信号块中评估谐波耦合，而不是在状态矩阵内部。本文使用的开环MMC模型是在三种谐波域（HD）公式中推导出来的，并通过一个三相时域参考模型进行了验证。这些模型在状态空间大小和稀疏性、谐波含量、稳态精度和特征值方面进行了比较。对于截断阶数K = 4，DQsym求解器有45个状态，而HSS和DP有135个状态，与参考模型保持在约4%的误差范围内，并且一旦与耦合块闭合，其特征值与HSS和DP的特征值相同。
tldr: DQsym框架在分析模块化多电平换流器时，相比谐波状态空间和动态相量模型，拥有更小的求解器状态矩阵，且其大小与截断阶数无关，同时保持了高精度和相同的特征值。
ai_comments: DQsym框架的创新点在于将谐波耦合的评估从状态矩阵中分离出来，从而显著减小了状态矩阵的规模，并且使其大小与谐波截断阶数无关。这对于复杂电力电子系统（如MMC）的高效动态仿真具有重要意义，因为它能够降低计算成本，同时保持对系统多频率动态的准确捕捉。这项工作为现代电力系统的建模和分析提供了一种更优化的工具。
motivation: 现代电力系统中的模块化多电平换流器（MMC）表现出多频率周期性动态。常用的谐波状态空间（HSS）和动态相量（DP）表示方法在分析此类换流器时，其状态矩阵大小随模型中保留的谐波数量而增长，导致计算效率低下。
method: 本文提出了一种用于时域仿真的对称直交（dq）动态相量公式，命名为DQsym。通过在非线性信号块中评估谐波耦合，将谐波耦合从状态矩阵中分离。DQsym模型与两种谐波域公式（HSS和DP）进行了比较，并通过一个三相时域参考模型进行了验证。比较指标包括状态空间大小、稀疏性、谐波含量、稳态精度和特征值。
results: DQsym求解器的状态矩阵比HSS和DP模型小，且其大小与截断阶数K无关。这种缩减是由于在状态矩阵之外的非线性信号块中评估谐波耦合。在截断阶数K=4时，DQsym求解器有45个状态，而HSS和DP有135个状态。DQsym模型与参考模型的误差保持在约4%以内，并且在与耦合块闭合后，其特征值与HSS和DP模型的特征值相同。
conclusion: DQsym框架为模块化多电平换流器提供了一种更高效（状态矩阵更小）且同样准确的分析方法，其状态矩阵大小不受谐波截断阶数的影响，同时能准确捕捉系统的动态行为。

title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery
authors: Ze Guo, Mingyue Cheng, Xiaoyu Tao, Shuo Yu, Shangtong Ye
abstract: Developing effective forecasting models for diverse time-series domains requires substantial expert knowledge, evidence from scientific literature on the web, and iterative experimentation. However, translating this knowledge and research experience into model designs requires preserving source context and testing applicability under task-specific assumptions. In this paper, we propose NeoResearch, a literature- and experience-guided autonomous research framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) as researchers to discover lightweight, domain-specific forecasting models. Specifically, NeoResearch establishes an expert-inspired dual-loop research workflow, coupling hypothesis-driven architecture exploration with iterative training and hyperparameter optimization through experimental feedback. To enable knowledge-grounded discovery, the agent autonomously mines scientific literature from the Web, extracting modeling mechanisms, empirical evidence, and applicability conditions to formulate task-grounded, testable architecture hypotheses. Furthermore, a hierarchical experience memory links literature findings to experimental outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons, guiding architecture discovery and training optimization while supporting reuse across forecasting tasks. Experiments on ten datasets show competitive performance and support dual loops, literature extraction, and memory reuse. Our code is available.
zh_title: NeoResearch：文献和经验指导的自主时间序列模型发现
translation: 开发针对不同时间序列领域的有效预测模型需要大量的专家知识、网络上的科学文献证据以及迭代实验。然而，将这些知识和研究经验转化为模型设计需要保留来源上下文并在任务特定的假设下测试适用性。在本文中，我们提出了NeoResearch，一个文献和经验指导的自主研究框架，它利用大型语言模型（LLMs）作为研究员来发现轻量级、领域特定的预测模型。具体来说，NeoResearch建立了一个专家启发的双循环研究工作流，将假设驱动的架构探索与通过实验反馈进行的迭代训练和超参数优化相结合。为了实现知识驱动的发现，该代理自主挖掘网络上的科学文献，提取建模机制、经验证据和适用条件，以制定任务驱动、可测试的架构假设。此外，分层经验记忆将文献发现与实验结果联系起来，并巩固条件经验，指导架构发现和训练优化，同时支持跨预测任务的重用。在十个数据集上的实验显示出竞争性能，并支持双循环、文献提取和记忆重用。我们的代码已提供。
tldr: NeoResearch是一个利用大型语言模型（LLMs）作为研究员，通过文献挖掘和实验反馈，自主发现轻量级、领域特定时间序列预测模型的框架。
ai_comments: NeoResearch的创新性在于将LLMs的能力与文献挖掘和迭代实验反馈相结合，构建了一个能够自主发现时间序列预测模型的智能框架。其双循环研究工作流和分层经验记忆机制是核心亮点，有望显著降低时间序列模型开发的专家门槛和提升效率。该方法为利用AI进行科学研究和模型自动化设计提供了新的思路。
motivation: 开发有效的时间序列预测模型需要大量的专家知识、科学文献证据和迭代实验。将这些知识和研究经验转化为模型设计，并测试其在特定任务假设下的适用性，是一个复杂且需要保留源上下文的挑战。
method: NeoResearch是一个文献和经验指导的自主研究框架，利用大型语言模型（LLMs）作为研究员来发现轻量级、领域特定的预测模型。它建立了一个专家启发的双循环研究工作流，将假设驱动的架构探索与通过实验反馈进行的迭代训练和超参数优化相结合。该代理自主挖掘网络上的科学文献，提取建模机制、经验证据和适用条件，以制定任务驱动、可测试的架构假设。此外，一个分层经验记忆将文献发现与实验结果联系起来，巩固条件经验，指导架构发现和训练优化，并支持跨预测任务的重用。
results: 在十个数据集上的实验表明，NeoResearch具有竞争性能，并支持其双循环工作流、文献提取能力和记忆重用机制的有效性。
conclusion: NeoResearch成功地展示了一个文献和经验指导的自主研究框架，能够利用LLMs有效发现高性能、领域特定的时间序列预测模型，并通过实验验证了其方法的有效性和组成部分的贡献。

title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
authors: Mateusz Wozniak, Qi Gao, Agnieszka Wykowska
abstract: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified. Current alignment practice steers a single model toward an aggregate of human values, ignoring that individual users may prefer a robot whose value profile differs from their own. We administer parallel self- and robot-targeted versions of three established psycho-metric instruments - the simplified Schwartz Values Survey (SVS), the Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-21), and the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) - to potential future users (N=22), capturing both their personal values and the values they would want an assistant robot to embody. We compare the three instruments as personalization tools using the UEQ-S and benchmark fifteen contemporary LLMs against the resulting profiles. Participants wanted their robot to score markedly lower than themselves on personal-focus values and higher on social-focus values; moral profiles were nearly identical. LLMs prompted to act as robots shifted only weakly toward the desired profile, indicating that default model behaviour and prompt engineering are no substitute for explicit value personalization.
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures. Version accepted for publication in: Value Engineering in Artificial Intelligence: Fourth Inter-national Workshop, VALE 2026, Bremen, Germany, August 15, 2026, Proceedings.
