authors: Run Luo, Kuan Zhang, Qi Deng, Yukun Chen, Zhihao Yang, Yufei Zhang, Renrong Hu, Yi Zhang, Guiyu Ma, Tianyu Fan, Longze Chen, Hao Sun, Jiaming Li, Jiaming Yang, Xiaohao Liu, Tao Tan, Minzheng Wang, Hangtian Jia, Shuai Yuan, Lvdi Wang, Xiao Liu, Chao Ma, Yuting Zou, Yinhe Zheng, Xiaobo Xia, Dawei Jiang, Shaoqing Ren
abstract: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.
zh_title: Gamer：面向长视距实时游戏智能体的通用视觉-语言-动作基础模型
translation: 我们介绍了Gamer，这是一个专为复杂交互环境中长视距任务构建的通用智能体框架。其端到端架构融合了感知、记忆管理和多步推理能力。一个共享的训练与部署流水线支持与传统2D图形界面以及复杂3D模拟世界的交互。我们首先在由数万小时设备级键盘和鼠标交互轨迹构建的数据集上进行持续预训练。这些轨迹涵盖了模拟游戏和具身环境，使模型能够跨物理和虚拟领域学习环境动力学。随后的稀疏思考指令微调（sparse-thinking instruction tuning）在保留复杂决策所需推理能力的同时，大幅减少了冗余计算。我们通过一种稳定的多轮强化学习方法来训练用于长程交互的策略，该方法解决了有限上下文窗口、累积误差和稀疏奖励等问题。针对实时交互，云边推理引擎能够并发支持大量模拟游戏环境，支持无边界上下文执行，并保持极低的在线推理延迟。在多个极具挑战性的3D开放世界游戏中，Gamer展示了扎实的泛化能力以及媲美熟练玩家的运行效率。它还在一系列传统2D游戏基准上取得了具有竞争力的结果。这些结果表明，即便是重复性的键鼠轨迹，也能通过扩展数据和学习算法带来显著提升。在这些轨迹上训练有助于Gamer在兼具物理和数字特性的环境中更稳定地学习复杂技能。该方法为构建能够跨越数字与物理世界交互的通用智能体提供了一条可行路径。
keywords: 视觉-语言-动作模型 (Vision-Language-Action Model)
tldr: 本文提出了通用游戏智能体基础模型Gamer，通过大规模键鼠交互预训练、稀疏思考微调及多轮长程强化学习，在复杂2D与3D游戏中实现了低延迟、媲美熟练玩家的实时交互表现。
ai_comments: 该研究展示了通过大规模设备级（键鼠）操作数据进行基础模型预训练的可行性与价值。结合稀疏思考指令微调、针对长视距的多轮强化学习算法以及云边协同低延迟推理引擎，系统性地解决了长程复杂环境交互中的上下文受限、误差累积及实时性瓶颈，为数字乃至具身通用智能体的发展提供了重要参考。
motivation: 旨在解决在复杂交互环境中处理长视距任务的挑战，构建能够同时适应传统2D图形界面和复杂3D模拟世界、具备低延迟实时交互能力的通用智能体。
method:
1. 构建结合感知、记忆管理和多步推理的端到端架构，采用统一的训练与部署流水线适配2D和3D环境；
2. 利用数万小时设备级键鼠交互轨迹进行持续预训练以学习物理和虚拟环境动力学；
3. 采用稀疏思考指令微调（sparse-thinking instruction tuning）减少冗余计算并保留推理能力；
4. 使用稳定的多轮强化学习解决有限上下文窗口、累积推演误差和稀疏奖励问题；
5. 设计云边协同推理引擎以支持并发环境交互、无界上下文执行和低在线推理延迟。
results: 在多个高难度的3D开放世界游戏中，Gamer展现出了扎实的泛化能力以及媲美熟练玩家的运行效率；同时在多项传统2D游戏基准上取得了具有竞争力的结果。
conclusion: 研究表明，利用大规模重复性键鼠轨迹结合适配的扩展算法，能够帮助智能体更稳定地学习复杂技能，为构建跨越数字和物理世界的通用智能体开辟了可行路径。

title: Deep Neural Networks Training Efficiency: Does Grokking Modify its Dynamics?
authors: Eduardo Cueto-Mendoza, John D. Kelleher
abstract: We study whether grokking, the delayed emergence of out-of-distribution generalization after apparent overfitting, alters training efficiency in deep neural networks, where efficiency is measured as accuracy per unit energy. Using two canonical settings, modular arithmetic and MNIST, we analyze two neural network models under 16-, 32-, and 64-bit precision and use Orthograd to test whether grokking produces noticeable deviations from the typically decreasing dynamics of training efficiency. We consider both short training runs of up to 500 epochs and long training runs of up to 20,000 epochs, and in both cases identify grokking as a sharp improvement in test accuracy after a sustained train-test gap. In the short-horizon experiments, applying Orthograd at progressively stronger levels during early training does not induce grokking, and efficiency remains smoothly decreasing. In the long-horizon experiments, Orthograd induces grokking, but the efficiency curves remain approximately monotonic and show no appreciable local increase at the grokking transition. These results suggest that, in our setting, grokking does not materially alter overall training-efficiency dynamics.
zh_title: 深度神经网络训练效率：顿悟（Grokking）是否改变了其动态特性？
translation: 我们研究了“顿悟”（Grokking，即在表现出过拟合之后延迟出现的分布外泛化）是否会改变深度神经网络的训练效率，其中训练效率衡量为单位能量的准确率。在模算术和MNIST这两个经典设置中，我们分析了在16位、32位和64位精度下的两种神经网络模型，并使用Orthograd测试顿悟是否会导致训练效率显著偏离通常递减的动态特性。我们同时考虑了最多500个epoch的短程训练和最多20,000个epoch的长程训练，在两种情况下均将顿悟识别为在持续的训练-测试差距后测试准确率的急剧提升。在短程实验中，在训练早期施加更强级别的Orthograd并没有引发顿悟，效率保持平滑下降。在长程实验中，Orthograd诱导了顿悟，但效率曲线仍保持近似单调，并且在顿悟过渡阶段没有显示出明显的局部上升。这些结果表明，在我们的设定下，顿悟并未实质性改变整体的训练效率动态。
tldr: 研究发现，即使深度神经网络在训练中出现顿悟（Grokking）泛化跃升，以单位能耗准确率衡量的训练效率依然单调下降，顿悟未显著改变训练效率动态。
ai_comments: 该研究切入点新颖，首次将顿悟（Grokking）现象与基于能耗的训练效率动态相结合进行实证分析。局限性在于研究仅在模算术和MNIST两个相对简单、小规模的经典基准及特定优化器（Orthograd）下进行，结论是否能推广到大规模语言模型或多模态模型仍需进一步验证。
motivation: 探究深度神经网络中在过拟合后延迟出现的泛化现象（顿悟/Grokking）是否会改变以“单位能耗准确率”衡量的训练效率动态变化轨迹。
method: 在模算术和MNIST两个经典任务上，评估了两种神经网络模型在16、32和64位精度下的表现，并使用Orthograd优化器测试长周期（多达20,000轮）与短周期（多达500轮）训练，以准确率与单位能耗的比值量化训练效率。
results: 在短周期实验中，早期应用Orthograd并未诱导顿悟发生，训练效率保持平滑下降；在长周期实验中，Orthograd虽然诱导了顿悟，但效率曲线整体仍近似单调下降，在发生顿悟的突变转换点并未出现可察觉的局部效率提升。
conclusion: 在该实验设置下，顿悟现象并没有实质性改变整体的训练效率动态。

title: LitArc-Bench: Disentangling Text-Specific Reader-Response Dynamics from Position and Lexical Affect
authors: Mingming Su, Yushan Wei, Sen Song, Xinche Zhang
abstract: When model predictions track an unfolding human affect trajectory, alignment may reflect narrative position, affective words, or text-specific reader-response dynamics. We introduce LitArc-Bench to separate these explanations: 39 Chinese-language literary excerpts segmented into seven checkpoints, with 430 questionnaires from 81 adults in two classroom groups (9,020 VAD ratings). We compare three future-blind model runs with leave-one-text-out position priors, lexical affect, and human-human references. Position alone reaches r = .470 for arousal, making raw alignment insufficient. Yet all six V/A transition advantages over a joint position-lexicon control have text-bootstrap intervals above zero. Cross-fitted models match the correct human text better than 38 mismatched texts in all nine model-dimension cells (p < .0001); a text-invariant negative control returns chance (p = 1). On human transitions at least 0.5 points against the position trend, models recover 69-76% of valence directions and 53-68% for arousal and dominance. Under crossed participant-text resampling, all nine identity intervals remain above zero; joint-control advantages are robust for valence and directional but less certain for arousal. High shape agreement still coexists with scale bias. LitArc-Bench identifies which components of literary reader response are recoverable beyond shallow explanations and why shape, calibration, and human variability require separate evaluation.
zh_title: LitArc-Bench：解耦特定文本的读者反应动态与位置及词汇情感效应
translation: 当模型预测能够追踪人类随时间展开的情感轨迹时，这种对齐可能反映的是叙事位置、情感词汇，或是特定文本引起的读者反应动态。我们提出了 LitArc-Bench 来解耦这些解释：包含划分为七个检查点的39篇中文文学节选，以及来自两个课堂群体共81名成人的430份问卷（共计9,020个VAD评分）。我们将三个不预知后文的模型运行结果与留一文本位置先验、词汇情感和人际参考基准进行了比较。单凭叙事位置在唤醒度上即可达到 r = .470，这表明单纯的表面对齐是不充分的。然而，相较于位置-词汇联合控制组，模型在所有六个效价/唤醒度转换上的优势，其文本自举区间均大于零。在全部九个模型-维度单元中，交叉拟合模型匹配正确人类文本的效果均显著优于38个错配文本（p < .0001）；而文本不变的负控制组结果与随机猜测无异（p = 1）。在人类情感转换与位置趋势相差至少0.5分的情况下，模型恢复了69-76%的效价变化方向，以及53-68%的唤醒度和支配度变化方向。在交叉参与者-文本重采样下，全部九个同一性区间仍保持大于零；联合控制优势在效价上表现稳健，在唤醒度上呈现同向趋势但确定性较低。高曲线形状一致性仍与尺度偏差并存。LitArc-Bench 阐明了在浅层解释之外文学读者反应的哪些成分是可恢复的，以及为何形状、校准和人类变异性需要分别进行评估。
tldr: 提出了 LitArc-Bench 基准，证明模型对人类文学情感轨迹的预测不仅依赖叙事位置和情感词汇，还能有效捕捉特定文本驱动的深层读者反应动态。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地构建了基准数据集 LitArc-Bench，深入探讨了模型情感预测与人类反应对齐背后的驱动因素，巧妙地将文本特定的动态响应与叙事位置偏置和词汇情感效应进行解耦；其局限在于目前仅测试了39篇中文文学选段，且模型在唤醒度（arousal）维度的稳健性仍弱于效价（valence），并在高形状一致性的同时存在尺度校准偏差。
motivation: 当模型预测能够追踪人类随时间展开的情感轨迹时，这种对齐可能只是反映了叙事位置规律或情感词汇的表面特征，而非特定文本引发的动态读者反应，因此需要将这些混淆因素解耦。
method: 构建了包含39篇中文文学节选的基准数据集 LitArc-Bench，每篇分为7个检查点，收集了81位成人的430份问卷（共9,020个VAD评分）；将不预知后文的模型预测与留一法位置先验、词汇情感及人类基准进行对比，通过交叉拟合匹配、反位置趋势转换分析以及交叉重采样等统计方法进行评估与控制。
results: 仅凭叙事位置先验，唤醒度的相关性即可达 r = .470；在控制联合位置-词汇效应后，所有六个效价/唤醒度转换增益的bootstrap置信区间均大于0；交叉拟合模型在所有维度上匹配真实文本的效果均显著优于错配文本（p < .0001）；面对与位置趋势相悖至少0.5分的人类转变，模型能恢复69-76%的效价方向和53-68%的唤醒度及支配度方向；高曲线形状一致性与尺度偏差并存。
conclusion: LitArc-Bench 明确了文学读者反应中哪些动态成分可以在排除浅层解释（如位置和词汇）后被模型捕捉，并证明了对情感曲线的形状、数值校准及人类个体差异进行独立评估的必要性。

title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
authors: Tao Hu, Ling-Xiang Zhang, Da-Wei Zhou
abstract: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising way to mitigate task interference through expert specialization and combination. However, while existing MoE-based methods avoid overwriting shared parameters by allocating separate experts for each task, this progressive expansion incurs severe cross-task redundancy and linear parameter growth. Specifically, experts across tasks often learn overlapping functions alongside task-specific capabilities. For instance, ScienceQA and TextVQA both locate relevant image regions. To curb parameter redundancy without inducing forgetting, we propose Consolidating and Preserving MoE (CoPre-MoE). For each incoming task, CoPre-MoE first learns task-specific MoE to capture specialized capabilities. To eliminate redundancy and reduce parameter growth across tasks, we design a shared-and-private expert architecture. Specifically, we first evaluate functional overlap to selectively consolidate overlapping experts across tasks into a fixed-capacity generic expert pool. We then factorize the remaining task-specific experts into shared projection bases and compact task-specific cores within a private expert pool. To mitigate forgetting, we construct the router by pairing each expert with learnable retrieval keys, where historical keys remain frozen during continual updates while newly added keys are regularized with an orthogonality penalty. At inference, input-dependent routing dynamically combines both pools without test-time task labels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPre-MoE achieves superior performance while substantially reducing parameter overhead.
zh_title: CoPre-MoE：用于多模态持续指令微调的整合与保留混合专家模型
translation: 多模态持续指令微调要求多模态大语言模型能够按序获取新能力，同时避免灾难性遗忘。混合专家（MoE）架构通过专家专业化和组合，为缓解任务干扰提供了一种很有前景的方法。然而，现有基于 MoE 的方法虽然通过为每个任务分配单独的专家来避免覆盖共享参数，但这种渐进式扩展会导致严重的跨任务冗余和参数的线性增长。具体而言，跨任务的专家在学习特定任务能力的同时，往往还会学习重叠的功能（例如 ScienceQA 和 TextVQA 都需要定位相关的图像区域）。为了在不引起遗忘的情况下抑制参数冗余，我们提出了整合与保留 MoE（CoPre-MoE）。对于每个新到达的任务，CoPre-MoE 首先学习任务特异性 MoE 以捕获专业化能力。为了消除冗余并减少跨任务的参数增长，我们设计了一种共享与私有专家架构：首先评估功能重叠度，以选择性地将跨任务的重叠专家整合到一个固定容量的通用专家池中；然后将剩余的任务特定专家分解为共享投影基和私有专家池中紧凑的任务特定核心。为了缓解遗忘，我们通过将每个专家与可学习的检索键配对来构建路由器，其中历史键在持续更新期间保持冻结，而新添加的键则受到正交性惩罚的正则化约束。在推理时，依赖输入的路由可以动态组合两个专家池，且无需测试时的任务标签。大量实验表明，CoPre-MoE 在大幅降低参数开销的同时取得了优越的性能。
tldr: CoPre-MoE 通过共享/私有解耦专家架构与正交键控路由，有效解决了多模态持续学习中MoE专家的参数冗余与线性膨胀问题。
ai_comments: 该研究精准指出了MoE架构在持续学习场景下专家数量线性增长及跨任务功能重叠的核心痛点。其创新之处在于共享-私有双专家池的设计理念，既通过功能合并保留了跨任务通用表征，又通过矩阵分解压缩了专有知识，同时搭配正交键控路由实现了免任务标签推理，在参数效率与抗遗忘之间取得了优雅的平衡。
motivation: 多模态大语言模型在持续指令微调时面临灾难性遗忘问题。现有基于MoE的方法通过为每个任务新增独立专家来避免参数覆盖，但这导致了严重的跨任务功能冗余和参数线性增长，亟需在抑制参数膨胀的同时保留跨任务能力并防止遗忘。
method: 提出CoPre-MoE架构：1. 针对新任务先学习任务特异性MoE；2. 设计共享与私有专家架构，评估功能重叠度并将重叠专家整合到固定容量的通用专家池，剩余专家则分解为共享基底与紧凑核心存入私有池；3. 构建基于检索键的路由器，冻结历史键并对新键施加正交正则化以防遗忘；4. 推理阶段基于输入动态组合两池专家，无需测试期任务标签。
results: 大量实验证明，CoPre-MoE 在多模态持续指令微调任务中取得了优越的表现，并且大幅降低了模型的参数开销。
conclusion: CoPre-MoE 成功解决了多模态持续学习中MoE参数线性膨胀与功能冗余的矛盾，在保持优异模型性能的同时显著减少了参数开销，为高效多模态持续指令微调提供了有效方案。

title: Grid-Forming AI Data Centers: Coordinated Grid Support Control from IT Loads and Energy Storage
authors: Xuechun Zhang, Zhiyi Zhao, Fei Teng, Zhen Wang
abstract: To exploit the grid-support capability of AI data centers (AIDCs), this paper proposes a grid-forming (GFM) control scheme which coordinates the IT loads and energy storage (ES) in the AIDC. First, the framework of a grid-connected AIDC is presented, with the multi-stage power conversion from the grid to the IT loads presented. A dual GFM scheme is then proposed for the back-to-back converters to provide grid support through coordinated power adjustments from IT loads and ES. In addition, an aggregated power response model is established to characterize the IT-load flexibility considering multiple IT servers executing diverse tasks. Time-domain simulations of a 100 MW grid-connected AIDC demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can effectively support the grid.
zh_title: 构网型人工智能数据中心：来自IT负载和储能的协调电网支持控制
translation: 为了利用人工智能数据中心（AIDCs）的电网支持能力，本文提出了一种构网型（GFM）控制方案，该方案协调AIDC中的IT负载和储能（ES）。首先，介绍了并网AIDC的框架，并展示了从电网到IT负载的多级电力转换。然后，为背靠背变换器提出了一种双重构网型方案，通过IT负载和ES的协调功率调整来提供电网支持。此外，建立了一个聚合功率响应模型，以表征考虑执行不同任务的多个IT服务器的IT负载灵活性。一个100 MW并网AIDC的时域仿真表明，所提出的控制方案能够有效地支持电网。
tldr: 本文提出了一种构网型控制方案，协调AI数据中心的IT负载和储能，以提供电网支持。
ai_comments: 该论文创新性地将人工智能数据中心（AIDCs）视为电网支持的潜在资源，并提出了一个协调IT负载和储能的构网型控制方案。考虑到AIDC的巨大电力需求和未来发展趋势，其对电网稳定性的潜在贡献具有重要意义。通过聚合IT负载的灵活性来提供电网支持是一个值得关注的思路。
motivation: 为了利用人工智能数据中心（AIDCs）的电网支持能力。
method: 首先，提出了并网AIDC的框架，包括从电网到IT负载的多级电力转换。然后，为背靠背变换器提出了双重构网型方案，通过IT负载和储能的协调功率调整提供电网支持。此外，建立了聚合功率响应模型来表征考虑执行不同任务的多个IT服务器的IT负载灵活性。
results: 100 MW并网AIDC的时域仿真表明，所提出的控制方案能有效支持电网。
conclusion: 所提出的控制方案能有效支持电网。

title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
authors: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar
abstract: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. The technical supplement is included as an ancillary file. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
zh_title: 状态并非瓶颈：基于三模组播网格的分页状态Gated-DeltaNet硬件模块，从RTL到芯片实现比特级精确
translation: 线性注意力语言模型用固定大小的循环状态取代了不断增长的键值缓存（KV cache）。在边缘FPGA上，该状态可能会超出片上存储容量，因而必须分页至外部存储器。本文探讨了此类分页是否主导了解码（生成token）的开销。我们在Agilex 5 FPGA上构建了一个硬件单元（tile），用于计算自定义的3.69亿参数混合Gated DeltaNet模型的一个完整层，并对其循环状态进行分页。该模型状态需要6.2 MiB，而设备仅有0.87 MiB的块存储。分页使每个解码token增加26.0 MB的访存流量，最多占计算总量的11.2%。在75 MHz的开发板上使用合成权重，该层生成一个token需要11.15毫秒。与权重相关的矩阵-向量乘法大约占用了该时间的62%，而包含分页的状态阶段占13%。该硬件单元是三模处理单元组播网格中的一个节点。我们测量了定点算术相对于浮点算术的误差，并确认硬件在逐位对比下与定点参考模型完全一致。在仿真中，状态逻辑在全部18个循环层上与参考模型一致。在硬件板卡上，6个版本均通过了所有30次64 token以及2次1024 token的运行测试。对于该模型和内存接口，权重的传输限制了解码性能，而循环状态则没有。因此，在边缘FPGA上为此类模型进行状态分页是切实可行的。
tldr: 在边缘FPGA上部署线性注意力模型时，将循环状态分页到片外内存仅带来极小的开销占比（耗时约13%），解码性能的瓶颈在于权重传输而非状态分页。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地量化评估了边缘FPGA上线性注意力循环状态分页的真实开销，打破了关于“片外状态访存会显著阻碍实时推理”的常规担忧，明确指出权重搬运才是真正的核心瓶颈。此外，工作完成了从RTL仿真到实际硅片板载验证的比特级精确（bit-exact）对齐，工程落地度高。局限性在于测试使用的是单层硬件Tile与合成权重，在完整模型端到端多层流水线及更高并发请求下的扩展性与内存争用情况仍有待进一步探讨。
motivation: 线性注意力语言模型依赖固定大小的循环状态，在边缘FPGA上该状态容易超出有限的片上存储而被迫分页至片外内存；本研究旨在探究这种状态分页是否会成为Token解码生成性能的主要开销瓶颈。
method: 在Agilex 5 FPGA上实现了一个作为三模处理单元组播网格节点的硬件Tile，用于计算自定义3.69亿参数混合Gated DeltaNet的一层；采用定点运算并将超出片上存储的循环状态分页至片外内存，在硬件与定点参考实现之间完成了从RTL仿真到板载芯片的比特级精确验证。
results: 该模型状态需6.2 MiB而片上内存仅0.87 MiB，分页每Token增加26.0 MB访存流量（至多占总量的11.2%）；在75 MHz板载实测下单层单Token耗时11.15 ms，权重矩阵-向量乘法耗时约占62%，而包含分页的状态阶段仅占13%；仿真与板卡测试均实现比特级一致验证。
conclusion: 对于给定的模型与内存接口配置，解码性能的瓶颈在于模型权重的传输，而非循环状态的分页开销；在边缘FPGA上采用循环状态分页技术是完全可行且实用的。

title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs
authors: Stanislas Pamela, Nicolas Pailliez, Emmanuel Franck, Victor Michel-Dansac, Laurent Navoret, Vignesh Gopakumar
abstract: Research in the domain of Physics-Informed Neural Networks applied to PDE modelling has advanced significantly in recent years, providing a wide ecosystem of novel methods. However, one frequent limitation is the inability of PINNs to scale out on High-Performance Computing architectures to address more ambitious challenges, particularly non-linear physics models with turbulent dynamics in large spatial domains. Typical studies restrain demonstrations to toy models with simple physics equations, few variables, and rarely any complex non-linear dynamics evolved over long timescales. Part of the AI community has even adopted the idea that "PINNs don't scale". This work proves otherwise. We present a mathematically robust formulation of Finite-Element-Method for Neural Networks (FEM-NN) implemented into a comprehensive, modular framework: Fuse-PINN. This formulation provides the basis for a sclable parallelisation of Physics-Informed Neural Networks on GPU-based HPC systems. Furthermore, an Energy Natural Gradient Descent optimiser is implemented to allow high-precision convergence. Fuse-PINN is demonstrated on physics models relevant to Magnetic Confinement Fusion, including non-linear convective models with fine-scale dynamics. Near-perfect scaling is achieved on multi-GPU runs with increasing problem size.
comment: 9 pages plus Appendix, 11 figures, 1 table. Rejected at ICLR
zh_title: Fuse-PINN：结合有限元方法与物理信息神经网络以实现非线性偏微分方程的大规模并行模拟
translation: 近年来，物理信息神经网络（PINN）在偏微分方程建模领域的研究取得了显著进展，涌现出了丰富的新方法生态。然而，PINN的一个常见瓶颈是无法在高性能计算架构上实现横向扩展，从而难以应对更严苛的挑战，尤其是在大空间域内具有湍流动力学的非线性物理模型。以往的研究大多局限于方程简单、变量少且极少涉及长时间尺度演化的复杂非线性动力学的玩具模型，导致部分AI学术界形成了“PINN无法扩展”的看法。本研究打破了这一观点。我们提出了神经网络有限元方法（FEM-NN）在数学上鲁棒的形式，并将其集成到全面的模块化框架Fuse-PINN中。该表述为基于GPU的高性能计算系统上PINN的可扩展并行化奠定了基础。此外，该框架还实现了能量自然梯度下降优化器以确保高精度收敛。Fuse-PINN在与磁约束聚变相关的物理模型（包括具有微细尺度动力学的非线性对流模型）上得到了验证，并在随着问题规模增加的多GPU测试中实现了近乎完美的并行扩展性。
tldr: Fuse-PINN通过融合有限元法与PINN，打破了PINN无法横向扩展的瓶颈，在多GPU上实现了复杂非线性物理模型的高精度与高扩展性并行求解。
ai_comments: 该研究针对学术界“PINN无法在超算上扩展”的既有认知，创新性地将数值分析中成熟的有限元思想与PINN及能量自然梯度下降优化器相结合，成功实现了面向大规模非线性偏微分方程的高精度多GPU近乎线性扩展，为聚变物理等复杂多尺度模拟开辟了新途径。
motivation: PINN难以在高性能计算架构上横向扩展以解决大规模、长时演化及复杂湍流等非线性物理挑战，导致社区普遍存在“PINN无法扩展”的质疑。
method: 提出了基于神经网络的有限元方法（FEM-NN）数学形式，并构建了模块化框架Fuse-PINN，支持GPU集群上的可扩展并行化；同时引入能量自然梯度下降（Energy Natural Gradient Descent）优化器以实现高精度收敛。
results: 在磁约束聚变相关的非线性对流与细微尺度动力学物理模型中成功完成验证，并在问题规模增大的多GPU运行环境中实现了近乎完美的并行扩展性。
conclusion: 本研究证明了PINN具备在大规模高性能计算架构上高效扩展的能力，成功攻克了复杂非线性PDE在大空间域与细微尺度动力学下的高精度并行计算难题。

title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data
authors: Jimin Mun, Maarten Sap, Yanai Elazar
abstract: Humans know that airplanes are fast, that this extends to red airplanes, but that it does not hold for broken airplanes. How do LLMs acquire category knowledge that humans learn and apply effortlessly? We introduce LeCat, a two-part framework to analyze LLM's Learning of Category knowledge. First, we use LeCat to evaluate models on their ability to learn category knowledge, distinguishing between three cases: memorization of in-domain category knowledge, generalization to unseen instances, and ability to flexibly use knowledge in appropriate contexts. Then, we use LeCat to trace how this knowledge can be learned in pretraining from text that may encode category knowledge in various ways, such as verbatim repetition or exceptions, which we refer to as forms of "knowledge expression". We first assess open-source pretrained models using 199 curated category-feature pairs and analyze their training data. Our findings suggest that strengthening context and category-feature co-occurrence likelihood (PMI) improve learning for larger models and verbatim rule-like statements diminish flexible category learning. To systematically isolate these effects, we then train a 68M model from scratch with precise control over the categorical information each sees in their training data, confirming that verbatim repetition reduces flexible learning but mixture of diverse knowledge expressions lead to more robust category learning. Together, our findings highlight that while contextual flexibility is persistently difficult for models, how category knowledge is expressed in pretraining greatly impacts models' acquisition of robust category knowledge.
zh_title: LECAT：衡量LLM从预训练数据中学习类别知识
translation: 人类知道飞机很快，红色飞机也很快，但损坏的飞机则不然。LLM如何获取人类轻松学习和应用的类别知识？我们引入了LeCat，一个两部分的框架来分析LLM对类别知识的学习。首先，我们使用LeCat评估模型学习类别知识的能力，区分三种情况：领域内类别知识的记忆、对未见实例的泛化能力以及在适当上下文中灵活使用知识的能力。然后，我们使用LeCat追溯这些知识是如何在预训练中从文本中学到的，这些文本可能以各种方式编码类别知识，例如逐字重复或例外情况，我们称之为“知识表达”形式。我们首先使用199个精心策划的类别-特征对评估开源预训练模型，并分析它们的训练数据。我们的发现表明，加强上下文和类别-特征共现可能性（PMI）可以改善大型模型的学习，而逐字规则式的陈述会削弱灵活的类别学习。为了系统地隔离这些影响，我们随后从头训练了一个68M模型，精确控制其训练数据中看到的分类信息，这证实了逐字重复会降低灵活学习，但多样化知识表达的混合会导致更鲁棒的类别学习。总而言之，我们的发现强调，虽然上下文灵活性对模型来说持续困难，但预训练中类别知识的表达方式极大地影响模型获取鲁棒类别知识。
tldr: 研究引入LeCat框架，分析LLM如何学习和应用类别知识，发现预训练数据中知识的表达方式（如逐字重复或多样化表达）对模型获取鲁棒类别知识有显著影响，其中逐字重复会降低灵活学习，而多样化表达能增强学习。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过引入LeCat框架，系统地探讨了LLM学习类别知识的机制，特别是预训练数据中知识表达方式的关键作用。其创新之处在于区分了记忆、泛化和灵活使用知识的能力，并通过从头训练模型来精确控制变量，为理解LLM的知识获取提供了深入见解。研究结果对于优化预训练数据和提高LLM的泛化与灵活推理能力具有重要指导意义。
motivation: LLM如何获取人类轻松学习和应用的类别知识，以及预训练数据中类别知识的表达方式如何影响LLM的知识获取。
method: 引入LeCat框架，分为两部分：评估模型学习类别知识的能力（记忆、泛化、灵活使用）和追溯知识在预训练数据中的学习方式（知识表达形式）。首先使用199个类别-特征对评估开源预训练模型及其训练数据，然后从头训练一个68M模型，精确控制训练数据中的类别信息，以系统地隔离影响。
results: 对于更大的模型，强化上下文和类别-特征共现可能性（PMI）可以改善学习。逐字规则式陈述会削弱灵活的类别学习。从头训练的模型证实：逐字重复降低灵活学习，而多样化的知识表达混合导致更鲁棒的类别学习。
conclusion: 上下文灵活性对模型来说持续困难，但预训练中类别知识的表达方式极大地影响模型获取鲁棒类别知识。

title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
authors: Gurinder Kaur Sandhu, Jude Koenig, Ankita Shukla, Shruti Kshirsagar
abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity groups. We observed that the SleepXAI model achieves strong classification performance on both datasets. Among the evaluated methods, Integrated Gradients (IG) consistently achieves the highest mean attribution fidelity across all five sleep stages on Sleep-EDF and across all AHI groups on DREAMT, outperforming all other evaluated methods under the Spearman rank correlation metric. These findings highlight the importance of attribution method selection as a key factor for ensuring reliable and clinically interpretable automated sleep staging systems.
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at AgIA4BioHealth Workshop, IEEE BIBM 2026, Dallas, Texas, December 1-4, 2026
zh_title: 迈向基于单通道脑电图的可解释睡眠阶段分类
translation: 自动化睡眠分期已取得了强大的基准准确性；然而，由于缺乏可解释性，其临床应用仍然有限。在这项工作中，我们通过扩展SleepXAI睡眠分期框架来系统比较五种不同的XAI方法，从而填补了研究空白。此外，通过使用AASM定义的脑电图频率带作为临床参考信号，评估了归因保真度与Spearman秩相关性。在本文中，我们专注于单通道脑电图（EEG），与完整的多导睡眠图设置相比，它更适用于实际临床部署。实验在Sleep-EDF基准数据集和DREAMT数据集上进行。在DREAMT数据集中，我们根据OSA将受试者分层为四种呼吸暂停-低通气指数（AHI）严重程度组。我们观察到SleepXAI模型在两个数据集上都取得了强大的分类性能。在所评估的方法中，集成梯度（IG）在Sleep-EDF数据集的全部五个睡眠阶段以及DREAMT数据集的所有AHI组中，始终获得最高的平均归因保真度，在Spearman秩相关指标下优于所有其他评估方法。这些发现强调了归因方法选择作为确保可靠和临床可解释的自动化睡眠分期系统的关键因素的重要性。
tldr: 本研究扩展了SleepXAI框架，比较了五种可解释人工智能（XAI）方法，以提高自动睡眠分期的临床可解释性。结果显示，集成梯度（IG）在归因保真度方面表现最佳，强调了选择归因方法对构建可靠、临床可解释系统的重要性。
ai_comments: 这项研究的创新之处在于系统性地比较了多种XAI方法在睡眠分期领域的应用，并引入了临床接地（AASM EEG频带）的归因保真度评估指标，这对于提高AI模型在医疗领域的透明度和信任度至关重要。研究聚焦于单通道EEG也增强了其实用性和临床部署潜力。
motivation: 尽管自动睡眠分期已达到高准确性，但由于缺乏可解释性，其临床应用受到限制。本研究旨在通过引入和比较可解释人工智能（XAI）方法来解决这一问题，从而提高自动睡眠分期系统的临床可解释性。
method: 本研究将SleepXAI睡眠分期框架扩展到系统比较五种不同的XAI方法。通过使用AASM定义的脑电图频率带作为临床参考信号，利用Spearman秩相关性评估归因保真度。研究重点是单通道脑电图（EEG），并在Sleep-EDF和DREAMT基准数据集上进行实验，其中DREAMT数据集根据OSA将受试者分为四种AHI严重程度组。
results: SleepXAI模型在Sleep-EDF和DREAMT两个数据集上均取得了强大的分类性能。在所评估的方法中，集成梯度（IG）在Sleep-EDF数据集的全部五个睡眠阶段以及DREAMT数据集的所有AHI组中，始终获得最高的平均归因保真度，在Spearman秩相关指标下优于所有其他评估方法。
conclusion: 归因方法的选择是确保自动化睡眠分期系统可靠性和临床可解释性的关键因素。

title: Accounting for Trust and Safety: Bounding Content-Moderation Quality from Records You Already Hold
authors: Aayush Agarwal, Daron Veer Singh Sohi, Linda Cornelison
abstract: Platforms use expert audits to measure content-moderation quality. This paper develops a formal method for checking those claims using records platforms already maintain, such as appeal reversals and confirmed reports. These records provide one-sided bounds: they can show that a stated quality target was missed, but cannot prove that it was met. The paper presents the theory, limitations, constructed examples, and a prospective protocol for future evaluation. It reports no analysis of Meta operational data, no experiment, and no production result.
zh_title: 衡量信任与安全：利用现有记录界定内容审核质量
translation: 平台使用专家审计来衡量内容审核质量。本文开发了一种形式化方法，利用平台已维护的记录（例如申诉撤销和已确认的举报）来核查这些声明。这些记录提供了单边界限：它们可以表明既定的质量目标未达成，但无法证明该目标已达成。本文介绍了相关理论、局限性、构建的示例以及供未来评估使用的前瞻性协议。本文未报告对 Meta 运营数据的分析，未进行实验，亦无生产结果。
tldr: 本文提出了一种利用平台现有记录（如申诉撤销）来计算单边界限的形式化方法，用以证伪平台的内容审核质量达标声明。
ai_comments: 创新点在于提出了一种低成本的核查思路，直接利用平台已有的运营记录（如申诉和举报数据）对内容审核质量声明进行数学上的单边边界约束；局限性在于只能证伪（证明未达标）而无法证实（证明达标），且摘要明确指出缺乏实际运营数据、实验及生产环境验证。
motivation: 平台通常依赖专家审计来衡量内容审核质量，需要一种有效且利用现有数据的方法来检验这些审核质量声明的真实性。
method: 开发了一种形式化方法，利用平台已维护的记录（如申诉撤销和确认的举报）构建单向数学边界，以核查专家审计给出的质量声明，并提出了理论、局限性分析、构造示例及前瞻性评估协议。
results: 该方法能够证明预设的质量目标未被达成（但无法证明其已达成）；论文未包含实验结果、生产环境结果或对 Meta 运营数据的实际分析。
conclusion: 利用平台现有日常记录可以构建单边界限，从而在数学上有效证明内容审核质量声明是否未达标，但该方法无法证明目标已被满足。

title: Efficiency Gains in Social Science Research: A Prospective Silicon Sampling Protocol for Pre-Treatment and Code Optimization
authors: Noaïm Astitou, Etienne Aucouturier
abstract: This study evaluates the methodological potential of using large language models (LLMs) to generate synthetic datasets prior to real-world data collection, thereby streamlining subsequent processing and statistical analysis. The approach is applied to a survey conducted within the France Life Imaging (FLI) network, leveraging three distinct LLMs (Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.3, and Kimi 2.6) to simulate responses and prepare data processing workflows. The findings demonstrate significant time savings in code development (85% to 90% reuse rate) and highlight the conditional validity of this preprocessing method, which depends on the thematic predictability of the models. While synthetic data effectively captures collective perceptions, it struggles with specialized or contextualized practices, reflecting limitations documented in the silicon sampling literature, such as homogenization and reduced variance. This work extends the Phase 0 concept (Trojacka et al. 2025) from instrument validation to a full-fledged methodological preprocessing step, paving the way for scalable applications in survey research.
zh_title: 社会科学研究中的效率提升：一种用于预处理和代码优化的前瞻性硅采样协议
translation: 本研究评估了使用大型语言模型（LLM）在实际数据收集之前生成合成数据集的方法学潜力，从而简化后续的处理和统计分析。该方法应用于法国生命成像（FLI）网络内进行的一项调查，利用三个不同的LLM（Sonnet 4.6、GPT 5.3和Kimi 2.6）来模拟响应并准备数据处理工作流程。研究结果表明，在代码开发方面节省了大量时间（代码重用率达到85%至90%），并强调了这种预处理方法的条件有效性，该有效性取决于模型的 the_matic 预测能力。虽然合成数据能有效捕捉集体认知，但它在处理专业化或情境化实践方面存在困难，这反映了硅采样文献中记录的局限性，如同质化和方差降低。这项工作将Phase 0概念（Trojacka et al. 2025）从仪器验证扩展为一个成熟的方法学预处理步骤，为调查研究中的可扩展应用铺平了道路。
tldr: 该研究提出使用大型语言模型（LLM）生成合成数据，以优化社会科学研究中的数据处理和代码开发流程，并在法国生命成像网络（FLI）的调查中进行了验证，结果显示显著的时间节省和代码重用率，但同时也指出了该方法在处理专业化或情境化信息时的局限性。
ai_comments: 该研究巧妙地将LLM应用于社会科学研究的数据预处理阶段，通过生成合成数据来加速代码开发和初步分析，这是一个具有前瞻性的方法。85%-90%的代码重用率是一个非常可观的成果，直接体现了该方法的效率优势。然而，研究也坦诚地指出了合成数据在捕捉细微差别和专业知识方面的局限性，这对于依赖精确性和深度洞察的科学研究来说是一个重要的考量。未来的工作可以关注如何改进LLM在生成更具代表性和多样性合成数据方面的能力，或者探索与真实数据结合使用的最佳策略。
motivation: 为了提高社会科学研究中数据处理和代码开发的效率，探索使用大型语言模型（LLM）生成合成数据作为预处理步骤的可能性。
method: 利用三个不同的LLM（Sonnet 4.6、GPT 5.3和Kimi 2.6）为法国生命成像网络（FLI）的一项调查生成合成响应数据，并利用这些合成数据来准备数据处理工作流程和优化代码。
results: 在代码开发方面实现了显著的时间节省（代码重用率达到85%至90%）。合成数据能够有效捕捉集体认知，但在专业化或情境化实践方面存在局限性，表现为同质化和方差降低。
conclusion: 使用LLM生成合成数据作为预处理步骤，在提高社会科学研究效率方面具有方法学潜力，尤其是在代码开发和集体认知捕捉方面。然而，该方法的有效性取决于LLM在特定主题上的预测能力，并且在处理高度专业化或情境化的信息时存在局限性。

title: Toward On-Device Markerless 6DoF Tracking of a Physical Manipulative on a Mixed-Reality Headset: A Preliminary Study
authors: Guangxi Feng, Philip Yasskin, Wei Yan
abstract: AR-Classroom uses physical models and virtual overlays to help learners explore spatial transformations. To align these overlays on a standalone headset, we developed a markerless six-degree-of-freedom(6DoF) tracker for a LEGO airplane on the Meta Quest 3. A compact YOLO model trained on synthetic Unity renders predicts 20 keypoints from dynamic RGB crops resized to 128 by 128 pixels. A perspective-n-point solver estimates the airplane's pose from these predictions and the corresponding 3D landmarks. In a paired evaluation on 1,000 synthetic validation images, cropping guided by ground-truth boxes increased the detection rate on annotated images from 32.5 to 46.2 percent. Mean keypoint F1 increased from 42.9 to 44.6 percent, with lower keypoint precision in the cropped view. In preliminary headset tests, 2 Hz was the highest tested tracking target at which the application maintained approximately 72 frames per second. A headset demonstration illustrates virtual overlay alignment with the physical airplane before and after a manual rotation. Quantitative 6DoF pose accuracy on real headset footage will be measured in future work.

title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements
authors: Helma Torkamaan, Masoud Mansoury, Yanan Xin, Oscar Oviedo Trespalacios, Roberta Savella, Andrej Zwitter, Maria Heuss, Huy Son Nguyen, Marie-Therese Sekwenz, Moyi Li, Roberta Tamponi, Megha Khosla
abstract: The EU AI Act imposes technical and organizational requirements for high-risk AI systems, but applying these requirements involves contextual choices about what to measure and what evidence supports a compliance claim. We investigate these challenges through a participatory workshop involving 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners from different disciplines, using realistic scenarios in healthcare, recruitment, and public transport to examine how regulatory obligations are interpreted, translated into technical requirements, and evaluated in practice. Through a thematic analysis of workshop data, we identify recurring tensions between how regulatory obligations are translated into measurable system properties, how responsibility and human oversight are exercised in practice, and how the validity of compliance evidence is affected by changing operational conditions and system uses. For example, participants highlighted how fairness metrics could conceal discrimination in recruitment, how time pressure and limited information could undermine human oversight in public transport, and how changes in patient populations could invalidate previously established evidence of system performance. Our findings suggest that technical, organizational, and evidentiary challenges are interdependent, and that establishing and maintaining compliance requires attention not only to technical assessments but also to how AI systems are used, governed, and monitored over time. We discuss implications for supporting context-sensitive and ongoing compliance.

title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
authors: Rishii Kumar Singh, Abhinav Rajput, Dinesh Kumar Vishwakarma
abstract: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences. The best worst-case Cohen's kappa over the five references is only 0.23 (Q-Align), while two raters in our study agree with a median kappa of 0.41. The widely used UCIQE often favors edits that people reject. On a Nano Banana Pro replica chain that should leave the image unchanged, only 22 of 73 scores decrease at every checkpoint, while noise grows by 2.5 times. We also introduce TrustUIQA, a benchmark that combines the human references, our study choices, the edited, attacked and generated images, and the scores of every metric on every image. The code is available at https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA and TrustUIQA at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA.
comment: Accepted at the 6th WVAQ Workshop, WACV 2027. 18 pages including appendix
zh_title: 水下图像质量度量与人类感知一致吗？一项包含人类选择、简单编辑和生成漂移的基准测试
translation: 水下图像增强由于缺乏清晰的参考图像而难以评估，因此研究人员依赖无参考图像质量评估（NR-IQA）指标。然而，这些指标是否与人类判断一致尚不明确。我们评估了73种手工制作的水下、学习型水下、视觉语言和通用指标，并将其与人类在五个参考数据集上的偏好进行比较：四个已发表的意见评分集和一个新的配对比较研究。对于每个指标，我们测量了在比较同一场景不同版本时，它选择与人类相同图像的频率。我们进一步测试了简单的图像编辑和小的对抗性扰动是否会使指标得分高于人们偏爱的增强效果，以及重复的生成编辑增加噪声时得分是否会下降。我们的结果显示，没有一个指标能始终与人类偏好匹配。在五个参考数据集上，最差情况下的科恩Kappa系数仅为0.23（Q-Align），而我们研究中两位评分者之间的Kappa中位数为0.41。广泛使用的UCIQE通常偏爱人类拒绝的编辑。在一个应该保持图像不变的Nano Banana Pro复制链上，73个得分中只有22个在每个检查点都下降，而噪声增加了2.5倍。我们还引入了TrustUIQA，一个结合了人类参考、我们的研究选择、编辑、攻击和生成图像以及每个指标在每张图像上得分的基准测试。代码可在https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA获取，TrustUIQA可在https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA获取。
tldr: 现有水下图像质量评估指标与人类感知不一致，本研究通过广泛评估揭示了这一问题，并引入了新的基准测试TrustUIQA。
ai_comments: 这项工作具有重要的创新性和实用价值。它首次全面地评估了多种水下图像质量指标与人类感知之间的一致性，揭示了当前指标的局限性。引入的TrustUIQA基准测试是一个重要贡献，为未来研究开发更准确、更符合人类判断的评估方法提供了宝贵的工具和数据。该研究强调了在设计自动化质量评估时考虑人类主观判断的重要性。
motivation: 水下图像增强的评估由于缺乏清晰的参考图像而具有挑战性，研究人员依赖无参考图像质量评估（NR-IQA）指标。然而，这些指标是否与人类判断一致尚不明确。
method: 本研究评估了73种手工制作、学习型水下、视觉语言和通用指标，并将其与人类偏好进行比较，使用了五个参考数据集：四个已发表的意见评分集和一个新的配对比较研究。对于每个指标，测量了在比较同一场景不同版本时，它选择与人类相同图像的频率。此外，测试了简单的图像编辑和小的对抗性扰动是否会使指标得分高于人们偏好的增强效果，以及重复的生成编辑增加噪声时得分是否会下降。
results: 结果显示，没有一个指标能始终与人类偏好匹配。在五个参考数据集上，最差情况下的科恩Kappa系数仅为0.23（Q-Align），而我们研究中两位评分者之间的Kappa中位数为0.41。广泛使用的UCIQE通常偏爱人类拒绝的编辑。在一个应该保持图像不变的Nano Banana Pro复制链上，73个得分中只有22个在每个检查点都下降，而噪声增加了2.5倍。本研究还引入了TrustUIQA，一个结合了人类参考、研究选择、编辑、攻击和生成图像以及每个指标在每张图像上得分的基准测试。
conclusion: 现有水下图像质量评估指标与人类感知之间存在显著不一致，没有一个指标能始终与人类偏好匹配。本研究通过引入TrustUIQA基准测试，为未来的研究提供了工具。

title: HerAgent: A Block-Level Checkpointing Harness for Coding-Agent Environment Setup
authors: Xiang Li, Siyu Lu, Federica Sarro, Claire Le Goues, He Ye
abstract: Modern coding agents rely on establishing executable software environments before they can perform software engineering tasks such as testing, debugging, and patch validation. Existing setup agents typically control progress at either single-command or whole-script granularity, making recovery either too local to remove polluted state or too coarse to preserve useful progress. We present HerAgent (Harness EnviRonment Setup Agent), a block-level harness for coding-agent environment setup. HerAgent's main contribution is semantic setup blocks: a single progress-control abstraction used for execution, validation, checkpointing, repair, and rollback. Evaluated against six prior agents on four environment-setup datasets, HerAgent improves setup success in every comparison, achieving the largest gains on Installamatic-Bench (52.0% to 85.0%) and SetupBench (46.3% to 70.4%). It also reduces setup costs by up to 94.5%, showing that block-level progress control improves reliability and efficiency.

title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
authors: Yuhang Wang, Jingxin Yang, Chuheng Wei, Suyang Chen, Haozhuang Chi, Hao Zhou
abstract: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN events with time-aligned GNSS trajectories (3,940 drives, 454 drivers), and CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery (3,675 drives, 431 drivers, 1,380 hours, 85,919 km). On 776 evaluation drives from 94 unseen drivers, we compare six re-implemented attacks and benchmark baselines under explicit information-access protocols, paired comparisons, and metrics incorporating failures. Experiments show that combining steering signals with road-network constraints yields the largest gain: With a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises the online map filter's five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87%, with a median average displacement error of 43 m versus 921 m for map-free dead reckoning. Offline beam search recovers 88% of test routes with the heading and 81% without it. Because methods fail on different windows, we also evaluate an LLM harness that selects among candidate routes on 659 five-minute windows; its best configuration recovers 79% of routes on test and 83% on few-shot, outperforming the best baseline on test and matching it on few-shot. Data and code at huggingface.co/datasets/HenryYHW/CANTraj and github.com/WangYuHang-cmd/GPS--CAN.

title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM
authors: Ruilin Wang, Xiaodai Dong
abstract: Frequency-selective fading and oscillator phase noise (PN) jointly impair coded sub-THz OFDM reception. We propose a decoder-confidence-guided two-round receiver combining a {pilot-aware complex transformer} (PACT) estimator, banded linear minimum mean-square error equalization, and neural normalized min-sum decoding. PACT jointly estimates the frequency-domain channel and effective time-domain PN through interacting complex-valued branches. Decoder-derived pseudo-pilots and continuous constellation-aware confidence guide second-round refinement through PACT inputs and attention, with parameters shared across rounds. At $E_b/N_0=30$~dB, the PACT receiver achieves approximately $70\%$ and $57\%$ lower code-block error rates than the best-performing learning-based baseline in the two benchmark settings, respectively. Frozen-weight tests further demonstrate applicability across channel/PN models, carrier frequencies, and FFT/bandwidth configurations.

title: Deterministic ECDSA on secp256k1: the RFC 6979 assumption, a counterexample, and the state of deployed implementations
authors: Ilia Prosianoi
abstract: RFC 6979 derives the ECDSA nonce as $k = F_x(h)$, with $F_x$ HMAC_DRBG keyed by the signing key x. We isolate the assumption its security rests on, A*: at known public key $Q = xG$, the signing transcript under nonces $F_x()$ is indistinguishable from the transcript under uniform nonces. A* suffices, and it is neither PRF security of HMAC nor auxiliary-input PRF security (AI-PRF) of $F_x$. A function $F'(x, h) = P_{Ext(xG)}(h)$ is a PRF under standard assumptions yet leaks x from one signature; the same holds for unmodified RFC 6979 over a compression function that keeps the PRF and dual-PRF properties used in proofs of HMAC, given a collision-resistance premise. A* and AI-PRF are separated in both directions. A* does not imply AI-PRF if the one-bit hidden number problem is hard. Conversely, in the standard model: any AI-PRF can be modified so that it stays one while two chosen-digest signing queries reveal x; under DDH with one public random point, or decisional square Diffie-Hellman without it, there is an AI-PRF whose key is recovered from signatures on two ordinary hashed messages; and a third function, under PRF security and DLP, violates A* while the scheme stays unforgeable. With an ideal compression function, A* follows tightly from DLP in the presence of a randomized-ECDSA signing oracle, and a nonce key independent of x removes the assumption. The secret HMAC message block is $2^{-127.65}$ from uniform on secp256k1, $2^{-32}$ on P-256 and 0.336 on brainpoolP256r1. An audit of 31 secp256k1 implementations finds that 28 sign deterministically without added entropy and that the raw-message deviation from bits2octets of libsecp256k1 before 0.2.0 survives in NBitcoin, dcrd and btcec v2. Low-R grinding needs no assumption beyond A*, and every nonzero Fourier coefficient of the low-R nonce set is below $2^{-116.9}$ unconditionally. We give test vectors for the untested $h >= n$ branch

title: Policy-Conditioned Koopman Representations for Parameterized Closed-Loop Systems
authors: Kiran G. Krishnan, Shankar A. Deka
abstract: Predicting the response of a nonlinear system across different feedback controllers requires a model that captures how the closed-loop dynamics change with the controller parameters. In a finite-dimensional Koopman model, these changes may affect both the latent dynamics and the observable coordinates used to represent them. In this paper, we propose a policy-conditioned Koopman representation framework to address this problem. This framework allows a single learned model to predict a family of closed-loop trajectories without retraining for each controller. We test the framework on four nonlinear prediction benchmarks, where the model stays below a 15% error threshold on every system, while each baseline exceeds it on at least one. As an example application, the resulting surrogate supports one-shot feedback-parameter selection: an optimization at the initial state selects a controller that then operates with fixed parameters and ongoing state feedback. On nonlinear control benchmarks including MuJoCo, the selected controllers stabilize every system with 3 to 97 times less online computation than nonlinear model predictive control. These results demonstrate how policy-dependent coordinates can support both prediction across closed-loop systems and controller selection without repeated online trajectory optimization.

title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
authors: Yifan Jin, Tao Liu
abstract: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating yields a MAP mean absolute error of 7.3 mmHg, compared with 9.2 mmHg for random selection at the same coverage. The gated agent achieves 60.0% agreement with recorded actions at 81.0% decision coverage, compared with 55.0% agreement and 99.5% coverage for an ungated ensemble agent. Component ablations show lower factual risk with joint gating than with either gate alone.These results characterize a reliability--coverage trade-off in selective clinical simulation; they do not identify individualized treatment effects or establish improved patient outcomes.

title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
authors: Jianjun Ou, Matthew Lentz
abstract: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. We present Callo, a disaggregated serving system that leverages invalidated KV for speculative drafts to reduce this latency, while verifying drafts against the exact KV after prefill before committing tokens. Callo makes effective use of decode resources by scheduling speculations during periods of underutilization and preempting speculations when drafts are likely to not be accepted. We evaluated Callo on a two-GPU testbed using SWE-agent sessions across three model families, observing all-request speedups of 1.05-1.19x over vLLM at moderate load. We demonstrate that these gains are also realized at scale through cluster-level simulations driven by real-world traces.

title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
authors: Wang Ma, Debarun Bhattacharjya, Junkyu Lee, Nhan H Pham, Harsha Kokel, Qiang Ji
abstract: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps. Bayesian and deep-ensemble methods deliver this aleatoric/epistemic decomposition in principle, but are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale and require white-box access. Existing black-box methods, in contrast, summarize to a single scalar that cannot make the distinction. We introduce a two-level ensemble that bridges this gap. Stochastic decoding of a fixed prompt forms the inner ensemble; meaning-preserving semantic perturbations of the prompt form the outer ensemble. Variability is measured in a continuous embedding space, and the law of total covariance gives an exact within-/between-perturbation decomposition to estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty (AU/EU); it requires only black-box sampling access. On top of this estimator, we contribute three theoretical results that ground the framework: (i) a finite-sample bias identity for nested Monte Carlo with a closed-form bias-corrected epistemic estimator; (ii) a Bayesian bridge bounding the gap between perturbation-population AU/EU and Bayesian targets; and (iii) a separation result identifying a class of failure modes that any consistency-only black-box method provably misses while perturbation-based EU detects. Across five short QA benchmarks and four instruction-tuned LLMs spanning two families and two scales, our estimator is competitive with strong white-box baselines, and at a matched generation budget it matches leading black-box methods on error ranking while decomposing AU and EU; controlled paired interventions show that AU and EU respond selectively to distinct, actionable sources of failure: prompt ambiguity and model knowledge gaps; and a long-form pilot on the NQ long-answer split shows the framework extends to claim-level factuality without retraining.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 54 pages (10 pages main text), 3 figures, 38 tables. Code: https://github.com/wma17/Black-box_UQ_for_LLMs_Ensemble_of_Ensemble

title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
authors: Jianguo Hou, Wuchen Li
abstract: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective. This objective can control the error of the induced density when the growth rate is bounded. The algorithm divides the time interval into short windows. In each window, a frozen velocity generates the particle data for a regression of the network velocity. We draw the particles from period-adapted initial sampling distributions and weight them in the loss partly by their predicted future mass, because the reaction can make regions with little initial mass important later. We numerically investigate the method on the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) equation with a linear source term, Fisher--KPP equations, and Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows.

title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning
authors: Ahmed Shoyeb Raihan, Md Habibor Rahman, Ashish Nimbarte, Imtiaz Ahmed
abstract: Accurate prediction of high-entropy alloy (HEA) strength can guide composition and processing decisions; however, obtaining tensile-test data for HEAs can be costly and experimentally demanding. This study proposes Robust Outcome-aware Sequential Experimentation for High-Entropy Alloys (ROSE-HEA), a sample-efficient framework for predicting ultimate tensile strength (UTS) from alloy composition and processing conditions. Its acquisition policy anticipates how possible UTS outcomes update predictions and the support for complementary Gaussian process (GP) descriptions. It then reassesses the worst-case expected predictive risk remaining across a reference domain to select informative candidates. A retrospective evaluation on 501 HEA records compares ROSE-HEA with expected-improvement (EI) and upper-confidence-bound (UCB) Bayesian optimization (BO), random GP sampling, and eight conventional regressors across 30 matched runs with shared initial observations and test conditions. Starting from 25 initial observations and acquiring 100 additional responses, ROSE-HEA achieves the lowest mean root-mean-square error (RMSE), at 152.84 MPa, and the highest mean R^2, at 0.7443. Mean RMSE is reduced by 6.16% and 6.37% relative to EI and UCB, respectively. The selected observations improve prediction across six regressor families and provide broader design-space coverage. ROSE-HEA also surpasses the strongest conventional regressor's mean predictive performance using 125 rather than 185 observations, corresponding to 32.4% fewer training observations. These findings demonstrate the potential of outcome-aware robust sequential learning to improve UTS prediction in HEAs under constrained training budgets.

title: VellSSLH: Sound Type-Guided Selective Speculative Load Hardening for LLVM IR
authors: Swarn Priya
abstract:
Constant-time cryptographic programs written in C can still leak secrets during speculative execution. Mispredicted branches may allow instructions to access secret data and expose it through observable behavior. Speculative load hardening (SLH) addresses these leaks, but protecting values unnecessarily can introduce significant runtime overhead. We present VellSSLH, which selectively inserts speculative load hardening at LLVM IR. Programmers specify Public and Secret inputs in annotated C programs, and our analysis infers which values may become secret during speculation. The transformation then inserts misspeculation-flag operations and protections only where needed. VellSCT, our extracted checker, validates the resulting LLVM IR.
  We formalize speculative constant-time (SCT) security by extending Vellvm's LLVM semantics with speculative execution, attacker directives, and leakage observations. Our security type system reasons about SSA joins, symbolic values, poison, pointer provenance, and observable faults, and supports declared declassifications and trusted external services. In Rocq, we prove that programs accepted by the checker satisfy SCT, and that a reference hardening transformation preserves architectural behavior. Evaluated optimized variants are rechecked for SCT but are not covered by this preservation proof. Our mechanized guarantees apply at LLVM IR; security of the generated binary additionally depends on backend and hardware assumptions.
  We evaluate VellSSLH on 24 cryptographic entries on a bare-metal Intel processor. VellSSLH achieves 4.03% lower geometric-mean runtime than LLVM SLH, with 13 comparisons favoring VellSSLH, eight favoring LLVM SLH, and three inconclusive. For X25519, VellSSLH improves runtime by 22.69% over LLVM SLH with only 1.86% overhead over unprotected code. Compared with Ultimate SLH, VellSSLH achieves 19.65% lower runtime.

title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
authors: Abhilash Durgam, Nyle Siddiqui, Mubarak Shah, Qiushi Fu
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the linguistic structure that drives typing, so every keystroke is inferred from the muscle signal alone. We propose a fully causal, zero-lookahead sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model (SSM), in which a single model decodes a whole session without windowed partitions, conditioned on what has already been typed. We achieve this by fusing a traditional typing decoder with an efficient autoregressive language model, instilling both sEMG and linguistic understanding in one model. To train such a model for per-character typing rather than whole-word text, we introduce a retokenization method that rewrites ordinary prose as human-like typing, with keystrokes, typos, backspaces and line breaks included, converting WikiText into a large typing corpus where none existed. Our model, having never seen a single sEMG-to-character transcript in typing, achieves a state-of-the-art character error rate of 25.13% on emg2qwerty's cross-user benchmark, a 5.4% relative improvement over the previous best with 6.7 times fewer parameters, while running strictly causally with no future context.

title: Stochastic Games with Distributional Entropy Objectives
authors: Shankaranarayanan Krishna, Durgam Latha, Dion Reji, Ashutosh Trivedi
abstract:
We introduce \emph{stochastic games with distributional entropy objectives}, two-player zero-sum games whose configurations are probability distributions over the states of a finite arena and whose stage reward is Shannon entropy. Over an infinite discounted horizon, MIN seeks to concentrate the distribution, while MAX seeks to disperse it. Because entropy is nonlinear, it matters whether strategic and transition randomness are averaged before entropy is evaluated or sampled first. We formalise three resulting semantics: averaged-distribution, sampled-profile, and sampled-transition.
  This semantic choice fundamentally changes the game-theoretic structure. Averaged-distribution games need not be determined, even on a four-state deterministic arena, whereas both sampled semantics are determined and admit optimal stationary randomised strategies. We give contractive Bellman characterisations and convergent finite-horizon approximations for the upper and lower averaged values and the two sampled values. Moreover, even the lower value under averaged-distribution semantics dominates the value under either sampled semantics, while the sampled-profile and sampled-transition values are incomparable in general.
  For fixed rational discount and positive rational promise gap, the averaged-distribution (upper and lower value) gap problems and both sampled gap problems lie in PSPACE; for a single entropy minimiser, the averaged and sampled-profile problems lie in NP. Finally, under all three semantics, entropy optimisation is NP-hard to approximate within a suitable fixed additive constant, already for deterministic one-player games, where pure memoryless strategies are optimal.

title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
authors: Jiayu Fu, Zirong Shen, Lin Gan, Yiming Zhang, Wenjing Han, Xiaoming Sun, Riling Li, Guangwen Yang
abstract: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $μ$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $μ$s per round.

title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
authors: Sicheng Feng, Zigeng Chen, Song Wang, Gongfan Fang, Xinchao Wang
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlash, a simple and effective framework that adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly. For long video inputs, MMFlash further employs sparse attention to reduce redundant attention computation and improve drafting quality. Across various multimodal benchmarks, MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to $3.58\times$, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%, respectively.

title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
authors: Vincent Lageschulte, Joel Nishimura
abstract: The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them. We demonstrate that when ideological space is two-dimensional, these franchise elections can generate complex behavior and that this complexity exists for any social choice function. Using the Yolk social choice function from voting theory, we illustrate that franchise elections can predict that agents attempting to introduce a new ideological axis perpendicular to an existing left-right spectrum risk disenfranchisement unless they ally with either side of the spectrum, and that franchise elections can cycle with any period.

title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
authors: Disha Sheshanarayana, Sai Linisha Reddy Goli
abstract: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory. In deployed agent systems, the same execution may be exposed through composed tools, delegation boundaries, or compacted histories, changing what execution evidence is directly observable to the verifier. It therefore remains unclear whether correct verifier judgments persist across such abstraction boundaries. We introduce Verification Transport, a reliability test that measures judgment stability under abstraction-induced changes in execution observability. We construct matched native, abstracted, and restored views of the same frozen executions while holding the task, realized trajectory, outcome, ground truth, evaluation criterion, and verifier fixed. Across four agent-evaluation benchmarks, seven verifier backbones, four verification protocols, and three abstraction boundaries, we find substantial transport failure, reaching about 31% under macro abstraction and delegation. Verification protocols exhibit distinct failure modes: direct verification more often produces incorrect verdicts, whereas evidence-grounded and deliberative protocols tend to abstain under limited observability. This suggests that lower transport failure rates do not necessarily imply greater reliability. Restoring the corresponding execution provenance recovers 85.5% of transport failures, while recovery is lower when provenance is lossy or unavailable. These results show that native-view accuracy alone is insufficient to characterize verifier reliability when execution evidence crosses abstraction boundaries.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development

title: Evaluating Feedback-Driven Black-Box Processes via Stochastic Modeling and Simulation
authors: Mengfan Xu, Zirui Liu, Juan Zhai, Shiqing Ma, Barry Nelson
abstract: We study feedback-driven black-box processes across software engineering and machine learning. These processes are inherently sequential: policies generate inputs, observe outputs/feedback from systems, and use the feedback to guide the design of subsequent inputs. While many policies are developed under structural assumptions on the underlying systems, many real-world systems operate without such knowledge, necessitating black-box policies that lack a unified evaluation framework. We introduce a stochastic framework that models and evaluates such policies using Markov chains and simulation, thereby connecting empirical practice with theory. We instantiate the framework in mutation-based fuzzing (widely used for discovering software bugs via sequential input mutation), by a novel Markov chain model of fuzzing whose transitions are governed by the mutation strategy and whose feedback is given by program execution. We develop a rigorous evaluation paradigm with new performance measures, sound estimators, and evaluation procedures with provable guarantees. Guided by the theory, we evaluate 9 fuzzers on 18 widely used fuzzing benchmarks and conduct case studies in 4 non-fuzzing domains. These results show that the framework provides a principled basis for evaluation while connecting to practice, with implications beyond fuzzing.

title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
authors: Ivana Ragusa, Lorenzo Guiducci, Filippo Cavallo
abstract: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows. We propose agentic robotics as a future direction for supervised systems embedded in the care ecosystem, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians, caregivers, and patients through auditable workflows that can be interrupted and remain subject to human oversight and explicit AI governance.
comment: 34 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems, Volume 10 (2027)

title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
authors: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mike Degany, Deyuan Qu, Qing Yang, Matyas Szanto
abstract: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed). We introduce hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD), a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes. After 300 further updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80% in both seeds, against 35--41% for a budget-matched control. The gain holds on a fresh scenario seed, on eleven held-out partner conditions and on partners that start later than any training delay; it cuts high-force contact three- to five-fold and needs no retraining of the partner.
comment: CoRL 2026, Human-Centered Robot Learning and Interaction (HumanRLI) Workshop. Code: https://github.com/mkhoshnam/Selfplay-PPO-handover

title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
authors: Robin Shing Moon Chan, Ryan Cotterell
abstract: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. This paradigm broadens programming access by letting users demonstrate the rule-based behavior they want to apply to unseen data, instead of having to implement it themselves. However, recovering a program from finite input-output examples is fundamentally ambiguous, as a finite set of input-output examples is theoretically consistent with infinitely many programs whose output diverges on unseen inputs. We view this problem from a Bayesian perspective, where, given a prior $p^0$ over programs, identifying the target program means concentrating posterior probability mass on it by observing additional input-output examples. In the interactive program induction setting, the learner chooses maximally informative inputs and queries an oracle, such as the user, for their outputs. We derive a greedy query-selection algorithm and show that it terminates after $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}γ\log 1/p^0(f^\star))$ informative oracle queries, and returns the target program $f^\star$ up to approximate equivalence when no other class outweighs it under the prior. The algorithm uses a language model as the prior under a PAC-style relaxation of program equivalence, where the query-selection objective is estimated using importance sampling. On the CodeARC benchmark, the algorithm improves accuracy over the LM only agent by up to 22 percentage points while observing up to 10.5 fewer input-output examples.

title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
authors: Dhruv Dixit, Khushi Patel, Congcong Xu, Min Song
abstract: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shifts the supervision target from imitating explanatory text to learning a tool-grounded reasoning policy. In the second stage, ARCHER refines this policy through asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning, using grouped and conditionally gated trajectory rewards for answer correctness, tool grounding, process discipline, and trace alignment. Across five standard sub-10B backbones, ARCHER improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points on macro-average across benchmark accuracies, including gains of 8.95 points on MATH-500 and 5.33 and 5.34 points on AIME-2024 and AIME-2025. Evaluations on two additional reasoning-specialized 7B backbones further show that executable grounding remains beneficial after reasoning-focused reinforcement learning or distillation. These results demonstrate that executable supervision and reward-guided behavioral refinement provide a general and effective training paradigm for compact mathematical reasoners.

title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
authors: Ziheng Wu, Adrian Vecina Tercero, Andre A. Fatehi, Abhik Sarkar, Brian Giera, Eric B. Duoss, Christopher M. Spadaccini, Nikhil Deshpande, Aldair E. Gongora
abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions. To evaluate the framework, teleoperators intervened across three SDL fault scenarios. In the first study, comparative trials showed that the decoupled controller was associated with shorter completion times and reduced rotational motion. In a second study, teleoperators performed an aiming task with and without reference-path guidance. Users were more target-driven and risk-tolerant without guidance but showed behavioral differences under different guidance strategies. These findings suggest that controller configuration and reference-path design influence operator performance during SDL fault recovery, informing teleoperation interface optimization. This work demonstrates the potential feasibility of teleoperation as a human-in-the-loop recovery mechanism for SDL workflows, combining robotic precision with human adaptability and problem-solving. These findings also provide a foundation for future studies in shared autonomy and semi-autonomous intervention.

title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
authors: Sandip Nandi, Aishwarya Bose, Apurba Bose, Soovadeep Bakshi
abstract: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. We study this aspect of agentic compliance with TradeGauntlet, a replayable limit-order-book simulator that separates detection, prevention, and execution cost. In 1,680 simulated sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, all conduct alerts were self-matches. Gates eliminated those alerts by rejecting self-crossing orders, while the aggregate-gate condition reduced Sonnet's two-sided fills by about 15%. A conduct reminder reduced Sonnet's alert rate but reduced Haiku's fills without a detectable alert benefit. These results show why zero alerts alone do not establish an agent's compliance. Scripted probes and two search methods test weaknesses beyond those observed in the LLM runs. The searches find split-order schedules that evade the implemented conduct rules; a learned baseline catches all 2,400 tested searched episodes but also flags 15% of a large maker's sessions. Aggregate caps reduce the response-dependent gain unevenly, with smaller reductions when only near-touch depth affects prices. A response fitted to five Nasdaq stocks and a separate ABIDES experiment expose the dependence of these estimates on market assumptions. A distinct adversarial prompt elicited refusals from Sonnet in all 240 rounds, yielding no candidate strategies to evaluate. TradeGauntlet provides reproducible tests of controls around trading agents; the experiments do not establish legal compliance or real-market detection accuracy.
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Code and saved results: https://github.com/tokencraftdata/agentic-compliance

title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
authors: Nenyi Kweku Nkensen Dadson, Jean Paul Gonzalez, Daniel P. Arabie, Ryan J. Cedel, Dorin Boldor, Corina Barbalata
abstract: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. Autonomous waypoint missions were used to collect measurements across selected sampling regions and multiple depths, enabling both horizontal and vertical characterization of environmental conditions. Field deployments were conducted in Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, with additional measurements collected in False River, Louisiana to increase dataset diversity. The collected measurements included algal pigment indicators, nutrient concentration, turbidity, temperature, and other water-quality parameters relevant to bloom formation. In addition, complementary sonar and event-camera data were collected during vehicle operation to provide contextual environmental information. A machine-learning classification approach was also evaluated using the collected water-quality measurements to support HAB and non-HAB classification. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using a modular ASV platform for repeatable, multi-modal water-quality data collection and support future development of autonomous monitoring systems.

title: EPIGRIDS: Documentation and Validation of Seven Open Synthetic Transmission Grid Cases
authors: Jonathan M. Snodgrass, Scott Greene, Thomas J. Overbye, Christopher L. DeMarco, Bernard C. Lesieutre
abstract: This paper documents and checks EPIGRIDS, seven open synthetic transmission grid cases from four independently built networks, made with an optimization-based construction method instead of the graph-statistics method behind most large public synthetic grids. The cases range from 250 to 78,484 buses, with geolocated substations, voltages up to 765 kV, and line parameters taken from conductor data. Each ships under an open license in three common power flow formats that agree at the solved operating point, and the six larger cases have a companion hourly, bus-level load series for one year. The Texas, Florida, and Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana cases are sub-networks of the Eastern case. Every case solves an alternating-current power flow from its stored operating point. With parallel circuits merged, the Eastern and Western cases are 9 and 16% denser than the real interconnections, while graph-statistics cases on the same footprints lie within 6% and meet more published realism criteria. A full single-outage contingency analysis completes on every case, and in an optimal power flow benchmark every case except the New England base case and one of its 12 operating points solves in polar form.
