motivation: 热带地区技术出现的条件尚不清楚。本文旨在通过整合全新世考古和古气候证据，检验两种相互竞争的假设：技术出现是由环境压力触发的，还是技术追踪有效人口的增长。
method: 本研究整合了全新世考古和古气候证据。使用哥伦比亚考古学衍生的放射性碳定年数据作为人类活动的代表，包括植物管理、陶器、冶金和高地耕作的定年。古气候数据则使用厄瓜多尔Laguna Pallcacocha和Laguna El Junco的两个厄尔尼诺-南方涛动（ENSO）重建数据。通过贝叶斯变点分析和贝叶斯对数线性回归来检验假设。
results: 在3575年BP（95%最高后验密度区间(HPDI) = 3811–3329）出现一个贝叶斯变点，标志着前西班牙时期人类活动增长率增加了约13倍（$r_2$/$r_1$中位数 = 13.3，95% HPDI = 8.1–22.2）。植物管理和陶器早于这一转变一千多年，而冶金和高地耕作则集中在早期加速阶段，此时气候和人口相对稳定。人口变点后，人类活动与ENSO频率和强度的贝叶斯对数线性回归显示出不对称的协变：ENSO频率和强度降低会抑制活动58%和21%，而ENSO频率升高则适度提高活动约11-13%。
conclusion: ENSO调节人口活动，而非触发技术出现。这些模式表明，前哥伦布时期社区可能是在能够进行计算时——即有效人口达到临界阈值且稳定窗口允许组合搜索时——进行创新，而不是在受到环境压力（表现为人口或气候变异）迫使时进行创新。

title: Does Increasing Government Spending on Tertiary Education Provide a Return on Investment? A Bayesian Causal Inference Analysis
authors: Andrew C. Parnell
abstract: When a government increases public spending on tertiary (university) education, does it provide a positive fiscal return on investment once general economic growth is separated out? Cross-country data make this hard to answer because growing economies naturally collect more tax, international ratios divide per-student spending by GDP per person and student headcount, and cohorts take years to graduate. We assemble a five-year panel of 121 countries (1985-2024) and fit continuous-treatment Multivariate Bayesian Causal Forests that model four tax changes jointly whilst adjusting for starting conditions, predicted funding, and follow-up economic growth. A +10 percentage-point (pp) increase in per-student university spending (% of GDP per person) shifts the tax mix toward direct income and profit taxation by +0.36 pp after 5 years (93% probability of a positive effect) and +0.71 pp after 10 years (96% probability). Overall tax-to-GDP takes a decade to respond as cohorts graduate: 10-year total non-resource tax rises by +0.24 pp of GDP (89% probability) and direct income tax by +0.12 pp (90% probability) per +10 pp of per-student spending, by +0.37 pp (100% probability) after five-year within-country funding increases, and by +0.22 pp in total tax (95% probability) and +0.15 pp in direct income tax (98% probability) per +25% increase in real PPP dollars per student. Comparing one entering cohort's degree cost against its 40-year career tax payments shows a typical three- to five-fold total tax return in high-income economies (EUR 2.37 billion in Ireland returning EUR 9.66 billion in total tax with a 77% probability of net profit and EUR 2.87 billion in direct income tax, or EUR 11.55 billion in the UK returning EUR 58.33 billion), whereas expanding the university budget without protecting spending per student yields no return.
comment: 37 pages, 10 figures, 10 tables. Open-source R/C++ code, data, and interactive policy web application available at https://github.com/andrewcparnell/education-tax-bcf
zh_title: 增加高等教育政府支出是否能提供投资回报？一项贝叶斯因果推断分析
translation: 当政府增加高等教育（大学）公共支出时，在剔除一般经济增长后，能否带来正的财政投资回报？跨国数据难以回答此问题，因为经济增长自然会增加税收，国际比率将人均支出除以人均GDP和学生人数，并且学生毕业需要数年时间。我们汇集了121个国家5年的面板数据（1985-2024），并拟合了连续处理多变量贝叶斯因果森林模型，该模型同时对四个税收变化进行联合建模，同时调整初始条件、预测资金和后续经济增长。高等教育人均支出每增加10个百分点（占人均GDP的百分比），五年后税收结构会向直接所得税和利润税倾斜+0.36个百分点（93%的概率为正效应），十年后为+0.71个百分点。十年后，总税收占GDP比重上升+0.24个百分点（89%的概率），直接所得税上升+0.12个百分点（90%的概率）。每增加10%的学生人均大学支出（占人均GDP的百分比），五年内国家内部资金增加，总税收增加+0.37个百分点（100%的概率），直接所得税增加+0.22个百分点（95%的概率），总税收增加+0.15个百分点（98%的概率）。将一个入学队列的学位成本与其40年的职业税收支付进行比较，在高收入经济体中，总税收回报通常是三到五倍（例如，爱尔兰的23.7亿欧元总税收回报为96.6亿欧元，净利润的概率为77%，直接所得税为28.7亿欧元，或者英国的115.5亿欧元总税收回报为583.3亿欧元），而扩大大学预算而不保护学生人均支出则不会带来回报。
tldr: 增加高等教育支出可以带来财政投资回报，尤其是在高收入国家，但需要保护人均支出。
ai_comments: 该研究利用先进的贝叶斯因果推断方法，克服了传统计量经济学分析的局限性，为高等教育投资的经济效益提供了有力的证据。研究结果对于政府制定教育和财政政策具有重要的参考价值。然而，研究的结论在一定程度上依赖于模型的假设和数据的质量，未来可以进一步探讨不同国家和地区在教育投入回报上的差异性。
motivation: 当政府增加高等教育公共支出时，在剔除一般经济增长后，能否带来正的财政投资回报？跨国数据难以回答此问题，因为经济增长自然会增加税收，国际比率将人均支出除以人均GDP和学生人数，并且学生毕业需要数年时间。
method: 利用121个国家5年的面板数据（1985-2024），拟合连续处理多变量贝叶斯因果森林模型，同时对四个税收变化进行联合建模，并调整初始条件、预测资金和后续经济增长。
results: 高等教育人均支出每增加10个百分点（占人均GDP的百分比），五年后税收结构会向直接所得税和利润税倾斜+0.36个百分点（93%的概率为正效应），十年后为+0.71个百分点。十年后，总税收占GDP比重上升+0.24个百分点（89%的概率），直接所得税上升+0.12个百分点（90%的概率）。五年内的人均资金增加10%会使总税收增加+0.37个百分点，总税收增加+0.22个百分点（95%的概率），直接所得税增加+0.15个百分点（98%的概率）。在高收入国家，一个入学队列的学位成本与其40年的职业税收支付相比，总税收回报通常是三到五倍。
conclusion: 增加高等教育人均支出可以带来显著的财政投资回报，尤其是在高收入国家，但前提是必须保护人均支出，否则单纯扩大大学预算而未保护人均支出则不会带来回报。

title: Asymptotic properties for weak Markov-switching AR(p) models
authors: Yacouba Boubacar Mainassara, Jean-Armel Bra, Landy Rabehasaina
abstract: In this paper we study the asymptotic properties of an autoregressive model of order p (AR for short), possibly non-centered, whose parameters switch according to an unobserved Markov chain. Departing from the conventional assumption of independent innovations, we merely require the errors to be uncorrelated but not necessarily independent, thereby widening substantially the range of potential applications of Markov-switching AR models. We establish sufficient conditions for the consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed moment estimators. We also propose a consistent estimator of the asymptotic variance matrix of the moment estimators. The finite-sample performance of the proposed procedures is illustrated through Monte Carlo experiments and an empirical study based on hourly meteorological data, which together provide strong support for the theoretical findings.
zh_title: 弱马尔可夫转换AR(p)模型的渐近性质
translation: 在本文中，我们研究了自回归阶数为p（简称AR）的模型（可能是非中心化的）的渐近性质，其参数根据一个不可观测的马尔可夫链进行转换。背离了传统对独立新息的假设，我们仅要求误差是不相关的但不一定是独立的，从而大大拓宽了马尔可夫转换AR模型的潜在应用范围。我们为所提出的矩估计量的一致性和渐近正态性建立了充分条件。我们还提出了矩估计量渐近方差矩阵的一致估计量。通过蒙特卡洛实验和基于每小时气象数据的实证研究，说明了所提程序的有限样本性能，这些实验和研究共同为理论发现提供了强有力的支持。
keywords: 马尔可夫转换自回归模型
tldr: 本文研究了新息仅需不相关的弱马尔可夫转换AR(p)模型的渐近性质，证明了矩估计量的一致性和渐近正态性。
ai_comments: 该论文放松了传统模型对独立新息的假设，仅要求误差项不相关，这扩展了马尔可夫转换AR模型的实际应用范围，具有较高的理论创新性和实用价值。
motivation: 传统的马尔可夫转换自回归（AR）模型通常依赖于独立新息的假设，这在许多实际应用中过于严苛，因此需要研究将新息放宽为仅不相关的弱马尔可夫转换AR模型及其渐近性质。
method: 在不要求新息独立而仅要求不相关的条件下，建立了矩估计量的充分条件，证明了其一致性与渐近正态性，并提出了渐近方差矩阵的一致估计量，最后通过蒙特卡洛实验和实证研究验证了方法的有限样本性能。
results: 建立了所提矩估计量的一致性和渐近正态性的充分条件，并给出了渐近方差矩阵的一致估计，蒙特卡洛实验和气象数据实证研究支持了理论发现。
conclusion: 论文通过理论证明和实验验证了弱马尔可夫转换AR(p)模型中矩估计量的渐近性质，为相关时间序列分析提供了更具普适性的工具。

title: Extended Bayesian Estimation for In-flight Calibration of Space-based Instruments
authors: Soham Das, Yang Chen, David A. van Dyk, Herman L. Marshall, Vinay L. Kashyap, Michael Smith
abstract: The ongoing calibration of space-based instruments is essential to ensure accurate measurements of physical quantities such as photon flux. The goal is to obtain a unified photon-flux measurement of a single astronomical source using data obtained with multiple instruments. Calibration involves in-flight adjustments to address discrepancies arising from instrument-specific variations. Taking a statistical approach, we extend a previously proposed additive log-Normal hierarchical model with half-variance correction based on a multiplicative physical model for photon counts. The newly proposed Bayesian hierarchical model can leverage domain-specific priors to account for correlated passbands and integrate information across different instruments, sources, and passbands effectively. The model is fitted using Markov chain Monte Carlo and can provide uncertainty quantification for instrument- and source-specific parameter estimation. Moreover, we obtain valid inferences for other structural parameters of the physics model. We use data derived from Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray observatories to illustrate the proposed inference procedure.
zh_title: 空间仪器飞行中校准的扩展贝叶斯估计
translation: 空间仪器持续的飞行中校准对于确保光子通量等物理量的准确测量至关重要。其目标是利用多个仪器获得的数据，对单一天文源进行统一的光子通量测量。校准包括飞行中的调整，以解决由仪器特定变异引起的差异。采用统计方法，我们在光子数的乘法物理模型的基础上，扩展了一个先前提出带有半方差校正的加性对数正态分层模型。新提出的贝叶斯分层模型可以利用领域特定的先验来处理相关的通带，并有效地整合来自不同仪器、源和通带的信息。该模型使用马尔可夫链蒙特卡罗方法进行拟合，可以为仪器和源特定参数的估计提供不确定性量化。此外，我们获得了物理模型其他结构参数的有效推断。我们使用来自钱德拉（Chandra）和XMM-Newton X射线天文台的数据来阐明所提出的推断程序。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于贝叶斯分层模型的方法，用于解决多个空间天文仪器的飞行中校准和统一测量问题。
ai_comments: 本文针对星载仪器飞行中校准这一关键问题，提出了一种创新的扩展贝叶斯分层模型。该模型结合了乘法物理模型与对数正态分层先验，能够有效整合多个仪器、源和通带的信息，并提供完整的测不准量化，具有很高的实用价值和统计严谨性。
motivation: 为了确保空间仪器对光子通量等物理量测量的准确性，需要进行持续的飞行中校准，以解决不同仪器变异引起的差异，并实现多个仪器对同一天文源的统一光子通量测量。
method: 提出了一种扩展的加性对数正态分层模型（具有半方差校正），基于光子数的乘法物理模型，利用马尔可夫链蒙特卡罗（MCMC）方法进行模型拟合与推断。
results: 使用来自钱德拉（Chandra）和XMM-Newton X射线天文台的数据对所提出的推理程序进行了说明，成功实现了对仪器和源特定参数估计的不确定性量化，并获得了物理模型其他结构参数的有效推断。
conclusion: 本文成功开发了一种用于星载仪器飞行中校准的扩展贝叶斯分层模型，通过整合多仪器数据和领域先验，实现了对物理模型参数的准确估计和不确定性量化。

title: Making Experiment Results Comparable through Sitewide Impact Estimation
authors: Xiaochen Zhang, Wenjing Zheng, Xingye Kang, Vamsi Manthena
abstract: Roblox spans many product surfaces-discovery, the virtual economy, creator tools-that differ sharply in reach and in how much the affected population contributes to any sitewide metric. A randomized experiment shows whether a treatment works for the users in its sample, but this experiment lift is not comparable across surfaces, because surfaces differ in reach and in their contribution to sitewide metrics. The quantity a strategic decision needs is a counterfactual-how much an aggregated sitewide metric (e.g., total platform play time) would move if the treatment reached 100% of its target population, which may be only part of the sitewide population, during the measurement period. We call this sitewide impact. Its scaling factor, which we call the coverage factor, combines the reach and the target population's contribution to the sitewide metric under no treatment. Hence a low-reach surface whose users carry much of the metric could outrank a high-reach surface whose users carry little. We develop two estimators under this framing: one for difference-in-means metrics and one for variant-level ratio metrics (a metric defined as a ratio of two population aggregates). Empirically, experiment lift is a poor proxy for sitewide impact-across 139 experiments that are statistically significant on time spent, the Spearman rank correlation between the two is 0.20, and 5 of the 10 largest experiment lifts are among the 10 largest sitewide impacts. We validate the estimator with A/A tests and against a long-term holdout, and apply it to cross-domain prioritization and attributing year-over-year growth to shipped innovations.
comment: Extended abstract accepted for presentation at the 2026 Conference on Digital Experimentation at MIT (CODE@MIT)
zh_title: 通过全站影响估计使实验结果具有可比性
translation: 罗布乐思跨越了许多产品面——发现、虚拟经济、创作者工具——这些产品面在触达率以及受影响人群对任何全站指标的贡献上截然不同。随机实验显示了某种处理是否对样本中的用户有效，但这种实验提升度无法在各个面上进行比较，因为各个面在触达率及其对全站指标的贡献上有所不同。战略决策所需的数量是一个反事实——如果在测量期间处理触达了其目标人群的100%（可能只是全站人口的一部分），聚合的全站指标（例如平台总游戏时间）会发生多大变化。我们称之为全站影响。它的缩放因子（我们称之为覆盖因子）结合了触达率以及目标人群在无处理情况下对全站指标的贡献。因此，一个用户承担了大部分指标的低触达面，其排名可能会超过一个用户承担很少指标的高触达面。我们在这一框架下开发了两个估计器：一个用于均值差指标，另一个用于变体级比率指标（定义为两个总体聚合值比率的指标）。从实证来看，实验提升度是全站影响的糟糕代理——在对花费时间产生显著统计影响的139个实验中，两者的Spearman秩相关系数为0.20，且最大的10个实验提升度中有5个属于最大的10个全站影响。我们通过A/A测试和长期保留对照验证了该估计器，并将其应用于跨域优先级排序以及将年同比增长归因于已发布的创新。
tldr: 传统的实验提升度无法跨不同产品面进行比较；本文提出的“全站影响”估计方法通过覆盖因子将局部实验效果转化为统一的全站宏观指标，从而更好地指导战略决策。
ai_comments: 该论文提出的“全站影响估计”（Sitewide Impact Estimation）方法为跨业务面、跨体量的A/A与A/B测试结果提供了统一的量化与比较标准，填补了实验提升度（Lift）与全站宏观业务目标之间衔接的空白，在工业界具有很高的实用价值。
motivation: 罗布乐思（Roblox）等平台的不同产品面在触达率和对全站指标的贡献上差异巨大，传统的实验提升度无法跨业务面直接进行比较，难以满足战略决策的需求。
method: 开发了两种估计器：一种用于均值差指标，另一种用于变体级比率指标，并利用覆盖因子（结合触达率和目标人群对全站指标的贡献）将实验提升度转化为全站影响。
results: 实证表明实验提升度是全站影响的糟糕代理指标（Spearman秩相关系数仅为0.20）；通过A/A测试和长期保留实验验证了估计器的有效性，并成功应用于跨领域优先级排序和年同比增长归因。
conclusion: 通过引入覆盖因子，该研究成功将不同实验面的局部提升转化为可直接比较的全站影响，并通过实证和长期保留实验验证了其有效性。

title: Well-Posedness of Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Partial Marginal Constraints for Model Calibration
authors: Jean-François Chassagneux, Stéphane Crépey, Grégoire Loeper, Justin Ruelland
abstract: We study the well-posedness and stability of a semimartingale optimal transport problem with partial marginal constraints at several maturities, motivated by the calibration of financial models to finitely many option prices. We connect its probabilistic and Eulerian formulations within the Benamou--Brenier framework. Under convex-duality assumptions, we establish strong duality for every price vector in the extended-value sense and existence of a primal optimizer whenever the value is finite. Under additional PDE assumptions, we establish dual attainment on the relative interior of the admissible price set, together with uniqueness of the primal optimizer. Under further non-degeneracy assumptions, we show that this price set has nonempty interior, on which the dual optimizer is unique and depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the prices. The analysis combines convex methods with regularity and local strong convexity results for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solution maps established in a companion paper. For a fixed deterministic initial state, we also prove continuity of the optimal law on path space in the adapted Wasserstein distance of order two as prices vary within this interior. This stability concerns the optimizer over the full admissible class of semimartingale laws, allowing characteristics that depend on the past. The framework accommodates bounded uniformly continuous payoffs, including European puts in log-price coordinates, without payoff regularization or spatial truncation.
zh_title: 用于模型校准的具有部分边缘约束的半鞅最优传输的良定性
translation: 我们研究了具有多个到期日部分边缘约束的半鞅最优传输问题的良定性和稳定性，该研究受金融模型校准至有限个期权价格的启发。我们在Benamou-Brenier框架内将其概率公式与欧拉公式联系起来。在凸对偶假设下，我们在扩展值意义上为每个价格向量建立了强对偶性，并在值有限时建立了原最优解的存在性。在附加的PDE假设下，我们在容许价格集的相对内部建立了对偶极值实现以及原最优解的唯一性。在进一步的非退化假设下，我们证明该价格集具有非空内部，对偶解在此内部上是唯一的，并且关于价格呈局部Lipschitz连续依赖。该分析将凸方法与伴随论文中建立的Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman解映射的正则性和局部强凸性结果结合起来。对于固定的确定性初始状态，当价格在此内部变化时，我们还证明了路径空间上最优律在二阶适应Wasserstein距离下的连续性。这种稳定性涉及整个半鞅律容许类的优化器，允许特征依赖于过去。该框架适应有界一致连续收益，包括对数价格坐标中的欧式看跌期权，无需收益正则化或空间截断。
tldr: 本文研究了用于期权定价校准的半鞅最优传输问题的良定性、对偶性及稳定性，证明了解的存在唯一性及其对价格的局部Lipschitz连续依赖性。
ai_comments: 该论文将Benamou-Brenier框架引入具有部分边缘约束的半鞅最优传输问题，建立了强对偶性、原最优解存在性、对偶极值实现及解的唯一性和局部Lipschitz稳定性，对金融模型校准具有重要理论意义。
motivation: 为了解决金融模型校准中将模型拟合到有限个期权价格的问题，研究带有多个到期日部分边缘约束的半鞅最优传输问题的良定性与稳定性。
method: 结合了凸优化方法、对偶性理论以及伴随论文中建立的Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman解映射的正则性和局部强凸性结果。
results: 在凸对偶假设下建立了强对偶性和原最优解的存在性；在附加PDE假设下证明了对偶极值实现与原解唯一性；在非退化假设下证明了价格集的非空内部及其上对偶解的唯一性和局部Lipschitz连续性，以及路径空间最优律在适应Wasserstein距离下的连续性。
conclusion: 论文成功证明了带部分边缘约束的半鞅最优传输问题的良定性与稳定性，涵盖了对偶性、极值存在性及解对价格的连续依赖性。

title: Care, Human Enfeeblement, and the Existential Implications of AGI
authors: B. Scot Rousse
abstract: Stuart Russell has named "human enfeeblement" as a long-term societal risk of advanced AI. This paper gives a new interpretation of the enfeeblement danger by interpreting it in light of recent work by Brian Christian, Alison Gopnik, and David Spivak on care and caregiving, and connecting it with the ontological design tradition of Terry Winograd and Fernando Flores. The enfeeblement that threatens is not merely a matter of cognitive off-loading and loss of knowledge, but a form of disengagement with the world which I explain in terms of an erosion of our capacities to care. This paper articulates a conception of care as a constellation of cultivable skills that involve us in the world and with each other, while making life worth living. Designing AI to support our capacities to care addresses the worry recently raised by Demis Hassabis and others regarding the questions of "meaning and purpose" that are looming in a post-AGI world.

title: Enhancing Resolution and Reliability with Attention Mechanisms in Nuclear Accident Surrogate Modeling
authors: Wonung Jeong, Sangam Khanal, Jeongik Lee, Sangseung Lee, Joongoo Jeon
abstract: Severe accident (SA) analysis of nuclear power plants relies on system codes such as MAAP, whose computational cost limits large-scale applications including dynamic probabilistic safety assessment and reinforcement learning. This study proposes the Accident Binary-Continuous Transformer (ABC-Transformer), a decoder-only surrogate combining causal self-attention with temporal attention pooling. It jointly embeds continuous thermal-hydraulic variables with binary safety-system and severe accident management guideline (SAMG) states, enabling 5-minute-resolution forecasting over 72-hour transients. Trained on 11,000 MAAP simulations of a total loss of component cooling water scenario for the OPR1000, it achieved lower one-step teacher-forcing error than CNN and recurrent baselines at fine resolutions. Autoregressive reliability was characterized as a full per-scenario distribution over 1100 held-out scenarios. For scheduled-sampling (SS) training, the median $R^2$ is $0.947 \pm 0.006$ and $3.8 \pm 1.0$% of scenarios fail ($R^2<0$; mean $\pm$ SD over four training seeds), while errors accumulate with rollout length. A Mahalanobis self-distance computed from each surrogate rollout, before comparison with the MAAP reference, ranks these failures (ROC-AUC 0.895, reference seed). A threshold at the 40th percentile of calibration scores accepts $36.8 \pm 0.5$% of 550 evaluation scenarios, with no accepted rollout below $R^2 = 0$ for any seed, and routes the rest to MAAP.

title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution
authors: Peng Yin, Zhiwei Chen, Tianyi Liu, Chen Li, Kai Li, Jian Cheng
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of automating end-to-end OpenFOAM workflows for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). However, current progress is bottlenecked by two critical limitations. First, existing evaluations are dominated by tutorial-level cases and execution-oriented metrics, masking a substantial executability--acceptability gap: successfully executed simulations often fail to satisfy prescribed numerical or quantity-of-interest (QoI) criteria. Second, domain expertise in existing systems is tightly coupled with bespoke agent architectures, limiting its reuse and continual refinement across agent implementations. To address these challenges, we introduce ExtFoamBench, a challenging benchmark for OpenFOAM agents that spans five axes of workflow variation, and separately assesses execution completion, numerical soundness, and QoI satisfaction. Complementing this, we propose EasyFoam, an agent framework that decouples CFD expertise into modular, externalized skills driven by a dual-loop mechanism. An execution loop constructs workflows from explicit task requirements and uses structured simulation evidence to diagnose failures and guide targeted repairs. Meanwhile, an evolution loop distills task experience into reusable skill updates selected through paired evaluation. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that EasyFoam achieves substantially higher task acceptance rates than baseline agents, establishing this work as a starting point for future research toward self-improving CFD agents.

title: Learning Nonlinear Transient Dynamics in Fluid Flow Networks with the Neural Basis Method
authors: Aijaz Nazir, Yuhe Wang, S.K. Rasel, Min Wang
abstract: Fluid flow networks, from pipeline infrastructure to biological vasculature, are governed by nonlinear edgewise hyperbolic laws coupled through continuity and conservation at junctions. Many-query tasks require rapid evaluation across unseen parametric settings, but conventional methods re-solve the system for each query at prohibitive cost. Existing physics-informed neural approaches impose the governing equations through penalty losses over generic neural approximators; these losses act only as optimization surrogates, with no guarantee that their reduction reduces solution error, and the resulting optimization is prone to ill-conditioning, particularly for hyperbolic systems. Building on the "representation-then-projection" principle of the neural basis method, we introduce a new approach for modeling fluid flow networks. Fixed neural bases define the representation space on each edge, while projection of the discretized equations determines the expansion coefficients, embedding edgewise laws into a conservative formulation. Edge subdomains are coupled through non-overlapping domain decomposition, and a neural operator learns, directly in this reduced space, the parametric map to the expansion coefficients. On looped and branching network topologies, we reproduce references with relative $L^2$ errors below 0.02%, whereas the physics-informed neural network baseline fails. Across unseen boundary conditions in both interpolation and extrapolation, we maintain mean pressure errors below 1% and mean flux errors below 3.3%, while the physics-informed DeepONet baseline reaches 8-18% pressure errors and 85-95% flux errors. These results highlight the framework's potential for real-time monitoring, design exploration, and uncertainty quantification of fluid flow networks.

title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs
authors: Tek Raj Awasthi, Babita Awasthi
abstract: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, and each token reads every weight from memory, so on edge devices, decoding is limited by memory bandwidth. 2:4 semi-structured sparsity keeps two of every four weights, but Apple-silicon GPUs have no sparse matrix hardware, so pruning helps only if a kernel actually reads fewer bytes. We present metalSPARSE, to our knowledge the first 2:4 sparse kernels for Apple GPUs, together with a fused decoder written in Metal. The kernels stream weights in compressed form and expand them in registers. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 2:4 sparsity on every decoder linear layer, decoding runs 3.6x faster than HuggingFace Transformers on PyTorch-MPS on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 1.52x faster than MLX on a 16 GB M4. The same engine on dense weights matches MLX, so the gain comes from the compressed weights, and sparsity delivers 97% of the speedup its byte reduction allows. Prompt processing, which is compute-bound, does not speed up. To preserve quality, we combine a Wanda mask with block-wise reconstruction and low-rank adapters trained jointly with the surviving weights and quantized to 4 bits. On WikiText-2 this brings perplexity from 3.01x dense after one-shot pruning (Wanda with a closed-form refit) to 1.34x, and the whole pipeline runs on the same laptop/hardware.

title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
authors: Gerhard Trippen
abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. On the first section, the human-verified output matches an independent expert transcription move for move on 34 of 45 games, and adjudication against the sheets found errors in both records, on different plies. We do not establish that either workflow is faster or more accurate. The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.
comment: 54 pages, 3 figures. Code and models: https://github.com/GerhardTrippen/Zugwise

title: Probe Before You Preach: Conformal Ambiguity Sets and Neuro-Symbolic Counterfactual Probing for Diagnosing Algebraic Misconceptions in Middle School Mathematics
authors: Caihong Xu, Xiangyu Yu
abstract: Distinct mathematical misconception rules can produce the same incorrect answer, making diagnosis from a single response ambiguous. We formalize this algebraic collision and derive a conditional Bayes error bound; internally generated reasoning does not add student-specific information beyond its inputs under an explicit conditional-independence assumption. We propose Mondrian Adaptive Conformal Misconception Sets (MACMS) and Symbolic-Verified Counterfactual Micro-Probing (Sym-EIG). MACMS has curriculum-group marginal coverage under exchangeability, not a per-student correctness guarantee. Sym-EIG searches for probes whose outputs separate modeled candidate rules; identification additionally depends on the candidate set and response model. An audit of a local public Eedi graph finds 2,118 of 2,258 linked constructs associated with at least two misconception IDs; construct-level associations alone do not establish same-answer collisions. Other project performance tables require recomputation because their script assigns numerical results directly. No diagnostic performance or classroom learning benefit is claimed here. A classroom study is proposed for future validation.
comment: 19 pages, 1 figure. Theoretical framework, method, and public-graph audit; withdrawn hardcoded offline/classroom outcome tables omitted; classroom study proposed for future validation

title: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery in Coding Agents
authors: Xiangyu Wen, Qiang Xu
abstract:
Can a coding agent fix a user's repository while also completing and delivering work the user never requested? In this paper, we introduce SideTaskBench to measure this failure where third-party technical references induce agents to produce independent side-task artifacts during an authorized repair. Repair success alone misses this behavior. Our key measurement contribution is to pair each repair with a self-contained side task and verify side tasks' delivery success rate along with the repair success rate. The benchmark contains 25 Python repairs and 190 side-task units. Its four-level similarity index defines 300 executable repair--side-task pairs.
  The experiments show roughly 40% valid delivery under wrapped requests for two models, alongside repair success close to their clean baselines. The completed v10 similarity run uses DeepSeek-V4-Flash on all 300 pairs, with eight repetitions per pair (2,400 runs). Conditional delivery ranges from 20.48% for L0 unrelated tasks to 57.44% for L3 mechanism-overlapping tasks, while the L1-L0 difference is 5.37 percentage points and remains sensitive to task composition. The central insight is that technical relevance may blur the authorization boundary for an agent, such that an agent can solve the requested problem and still deliver unauthorized work. SideTaskBench emphasizes this potential weakness of existing agents and provides a testbed for defenses that preserve repair capability while preventing unauthorized delivery. The code is available at: https://github.com/xywen97/SideTaskBench.

title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
authors: Katherine MacKenzie, James Rand, Ben Ashby, Tristan Pryer, Claire E. Heaney, Christopher C. Pain, Thomas Rodding Kjelsden
abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is almost an order of magnitude faster than a comparable FEM. Finally, the Neural Physics method is applied to a real-world test case with integrated experimental data and simulates the infiltration of water through a rain garden. This new approach therefore provides a route to efficiently and accurately solve Richards equation for a wide array of hydrological applications.

title: The Market Is the Reward: Design Markets, Not Just Traders for Human-AI Collective Intelligence
authors: Yankai Chen, Xueqing Peng, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Yuehua Tang, Michał Dzieliński, Yijia Zhao, Jimin Huang, Xue Liu, Sophia Ananiadou
abstract: Learning agents are becoming market participants, yet machine learning still treats the market as a fixed environment, although its payoff rule is the reward agents learn from. This position paper argues that financial AI should build HyperMarkets for human-AI collective intelligence, and not only the agents that trade in them: markets whose liquidity provision, information production, outcome determination, and trading rule are performed or adapted by learning agents and designed jointly toward explicit market-level objectives. In a pre-registered simulation with Claude agents trading for principals, joint design raises a market-level objective by 79% over separately tuned functions, through a trading rule that helps only when slow traders are present, and how evidence is paid for decides whether a stronger agent earns more for its principal. We state when fixed rules or non-market aggregation should be preferred and what findings would refute the case.

title: Beyond the First Hit: Towards Tight Guarantees for $k$-means++
authors: Aravind Reddy
abstract: Let $R_k$ be the worst-case ratio between the expected cost of the $k$ seeds chosen by $k$-means++ and the optimal $k$-means cost. In their seminal paper introducing $k$-means++, Arthur and Vassilvitskii (SODA 2007) showed that $2\ln k\le R_k\le8(\ln k+2)$, and Makarychev, Reddy and Shan (NeurIPS 2020) improved the upper bound to $5(\ln k+2)$. We prove $R_k\le\frac{1163}{233}+2.108\,H_{k-2}$ for every $k\ge3$ by a computer-assisted argument, and $R_k\le5+2.3139\,H_{k-2}$ for every $k\ge2$ by a short analytic argument; here $H_j$ is the $j$th harmonic number. Since $H_{k-2}\le1+\ln k$, this lowers the leading coefficient of $\ln k$ from $5$ to $2.108$. We also determine $R_2=5$ and $R_3=185/32$ exactly; both are suprema that are approached but not attained. On the lower side we prove $R_k\ge2(1+H_{k-1})$ for every $k$, and give a second family of lower bounds that is larger than this for $2\le k\le18$. Previous analyses bound the expected cost of a cluster just after it is first sampled by a constant times its optimal cost, and then charge that cost for the rest of the run. We instead track how a cluster's cost evolves after its first hit: a cluster left with a large residual cost is likely to be sampled again before it accumulates much of the logarithmic charge, and each repeat repairs it.
comment: 24 pages, 1 figure. Verification code included as ancillary files

title: MechFoundry: An agentic loop that poses and performs engineering analyses and optimization of real-world objects
authors: Xue-Ling Luo, Marco Conte, Peter Yichen Chen, Nikolaos Bouklas
abstract: AI agents can automate software engineering because a compiler or a test suite checks that the code does what the user or the agent intended. In engineering analysis, however, the steps that precede the computation have few easily verifiable checks: modeling a design or an object, deciding how it is used, where supports and loads are applied, and what material each part is made of. A human expert therefore makes these decisions, carries out the steps, and judges the result, one object at a time. We present MechFoundry, an agentic loop coupled with bespoke software that automates structural analyses of real-world objects without a human in the loop. From an object's lexical description, it generates a shape, poses a loading case relevant to how the object is used, assigns a material to each part, solves the nonlinear structural response, and improves the design against the loads it carries. A differentiable GPU solver built on an adaptive octree that need not conform to the surface enables the transition from shape generation to simulation and optimization. Across 50 everyday and engineering objects, the agent posed and solved a loading case in 6.5 minutes and for US$1.3 per object on average. Without a test suite to check against, we had language-model reviewers grade each session, as a first indication of where the agent's engineering judgment holds and where it fails.

title: Provenance-tracked, experimentally validated neural operator surrogates of three-dimensional laser melting with keyholes and free-form paths
authors: Alix Benoit, Elia Iseli
abstract:
A three-dimensional thermo-fluid-dynamic simulation of laser melting resolves the melt pool and vapor depression but costs from one to thousands of core-hours per track. We train FNO, RIGNO and GAOT neural operators that predict the temperature, melt-pool and free-surface fields. Our datasets comprise 3D temperature and melt geometry fields covering lack-of-fusion to keyhole conditions under varied laser power, scan speed, beam radius, beam shape and preheat, and include free-form scan paths with speed changes and up to four beams. We generate them with FLOW-3D WELD, using solver settings validated against published measurements for four materials. We implement an AiiDA framework to store the provenance of every simulation, model and evaluation, so each tabulated metric traces back to the solver and model inputs behind it. On held-out simulations, the best architecture scores below 2 % relative temperature error on quasi-steady straight tracks, below 4 % on single-beam free-form paths and about 5 % with two to four beams. Inference takes under a second per predicted arbitrary time step on our single-GPU setup. We extend a surrogate trained on Ti-6Al-4V to Inconel 718 by growing its training set autonomously, and the extended models reach a relative temperature error of about 3 % or less on both Inconel 718 and Ti-6Al-4V. At 20 Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 718 conditions held out of training, the two-alloy RIGNO predicts melt-pool and vapor-depression depths within 30 % of published measurements, and its depths differ from FLOW-3D at the same conditions by 2 % on average.
  Furthermore, these results provide a scalable framework which can readily be applied to computationally intensive simulations in fields other than laser melting.
comment: Main text: 44 pages, 13 figures, 7 tables. Supplementary Information: 19 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables

title: The norm, not the labels: training and evaluating finite-element surrogates for stress analysis in the energy norm
authors: Ruifeng Cao, Xidan Song
abstract: Finite-element surrogates predict the stresses of a new design in one evaluation, but are usually trained on solutions with a displacement loss and compared by it, although engineering decisions rest on stresses. Application in engineering: stress analysis of perforated plates and solids with cavities, parametric families in which holes concentrate stress. Contribution to artificial intelligence: training and evaluating such surrogates in the energy norm, with or without solutions, and screening their predictions without solutions. For linear elastostatics, minimising the assembled discrete potential energy is exactly supervised regression in this norm: the energy gap of a prediction is the strain energy of its stress error. A displacement loss under-weights the stiff modes that carry the strains. In pre-registered comparisons, changing only the norm of the supervised loss cut a three-dimensional transformer's median energy-norm error 7.5-fold and its median von Mises error 6.1-fold; in two dimensions it more than halved the von Mises error, also on held-out instances. In three dimensions, the transformer trained on the energy alone came within a factor of 1.3 of the energy-norm-supervised one in median energy-norm and von Mises error. It was more accurate than the displacement-supervised one on all five metrics in every seed. Given the stiffness matrix, a Ritz projection was more accurate than the label-free transformer, in the seed means, on every metric but peak stress. No network transferred to a substantially finer mesh. The energy ranks predictions of a load case, and its sign flags those worse than the zero field.
comment: 45 pages, 6 figures; supplementary material (37 pages, 4 figures) appended

title: Designing Collaborative Virtual Environments for Software Engineering Education
authors: Filipe Fernandes, Cláudia Werner
abstract: Collaborative virtual environments offer opportunities to make software models available for shared inspection, but educational design and usability need to be examined separately from claims of learning effectiveness. This article presents MetaSEE, an approach connecting requirements guidance, a Web XR feature model, a reusable UML component, and a browser-based multiuser platform. We synthesize documented formative evaluations of the framework (16 participations), feature model (15), UML component (9), and platform (14). These counts represent evaluation participations; the same 12 developers took part in the first two evaluations. The principal platform study involved six teachers working individually and eight students working in four pairs through desktop or notebook computers, keyboard, and mouse. The documentary synthesis traces educational intentions to implemented features and reported difficulties. Participants identified potential value in shared modeling and simulation, alongside navigation, interaction, visualization, and distraction concerns. A numerical audit reconstructs a student System Usability Scale mean of 67.50 from published item frequencies, conflicting with the reported 79.38; an incomplete teacher item distribution prevents recovery of that group's overall mean. The contribution is a traceable account of educational design and formative limitations, with practical implications for onboarding, model readability, collaboration, and evaluation reporting. The evidence supports bounded feasibility and perceived usefulness, without establishing learning gains, sustained engagement, or adoption.
comment: Submitted to Computers and Education: X Reality

title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
authors: Mingjie Cao, Gewei Zhang, Deqing Wang, Lizhao You, Fei-Yun Wu, Liqun Fu
abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.

title: CAFIN: CUDA-accelerated Adaptive Fisher Information Matrix Network Optimization via GPU-Native Kernel Fusion
authors: Maryam Arshad, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad
abstract: Second-order optimizers improve deep neural network training using curvature information, but their practical efficiency is limited by GPU execution overhead. AdaFisher reduces Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) approximation costs through diagonal Kronecker structures and exponential moving averages, yet its PyTorch implementation requires sequential CUDA kernel launches, intermediate tensor allocations, and repeated memory accesses. We introduce CAFIN, a GPU-native CUDA kernel fusion framework that improves AdaFisher execution efficiency without changing its optimization formulation. The proposed approach progressively integrates FIM preconditioner construction, exponential moving average updates, gradient preconditioning, momentum accumulation, weight decay, and parameter updates into fused CUDA kernels. Shared-memory reuse, register-resident computation, and in-place operations further reduce memory traffic and intermediate allocations. Experiments using ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet across NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti and RTX 3060 Laptop GPUs demonstrate up to 78.4% lower isolated FIM construction latency and 2.1-26.9% lower optimizer-step latency. The implementation also eliminates approximately 18.91 MB of intermediate GPU memory allocations per optimizer step. Numerical validation confirms consistency within the predefined FP32 tolerance, while convergence accuracy remains comparable across evaluated datasets and random seeds. These findings demonstrate that CUDA kernel fusion can substantially accelerate second-order optimization while preserving AdaFisher's underlying mathematical formulation and learning behavior.

title: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench
authors: Sungbin Im
abstract:
Agentic workflows, in which a large language model (LLM) calls tools to read and write data, are evaluated in two ways. Benchmarks compare the final state against a gold answer. Deployed services have none; an LLM judge reads the transcript and decides. Practice treats the two as interchangeable. This paper measures whether they are.
  We ran 2,160 episodes in tau2-bench's airline and retail domains and recorded every database write. We scored each episode four ways: native scoring against gold state, an LLM judge, that judge given the policy document, and the boundary evaluator, a minimal rule-based check of whether a write was expected against whether one occurred in the trace. Two annotators independently labeled 120 episodes for task correctness, policy compliance, and commitment correctness.
  The judge repeated its verdict 98.2% of the time but agreed with native scoring on 56.2%. In 11 episodes the agent executed a forbidden write. The judge passed 10 to 11, with or without the policy or transcript. A stronger judge still passed 6. The boundary evaluator, with no model call, caught all 11; no judge significantly exceeded it on human labels. Forbidden writes occurred in 11.1% of episodes without gates. Verification, correction, and safe-termination gates did not reduce them significantly. The traces show a candidate cause: the gates' evidence digest dropped the order status and customer authentication, so valid requests were rejected. The choice of evaluator decides the conclusion; the minimal check exposes failures the judges miss. Traces, code, prompts, and labels are released.
comment: 38 pages, 3 figures, 11 tables. Submitted to Empirical Software Engineering. Replication package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23683806. Supplementary material (Online Resource 1) is included as an ancillary file

title: Adversarial Risk in the Generative AI Era Necessitates Dropping the Small Epsilon Ball
authors: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil G. Marchant, Paul Montague, Jiani Xie, Benjamin I.P. Rubinstein
abstract: Adversarial Machine Learning research is currently centered on the search for the epsilon-ball: minimal perturbations designed to fool models while remaining imperceptible to humans. We argue that this fixation on $\ell_p$ norms is a metrological trap that communicates a distorted perception of risk to defenders, one that is unaligned with real-world system vulnerabilities. This paradigm misleads defenders into optimizing for narrow, mathematical robustness at the expense of systemic security, while simultaneously incentivizing attackers to exploit non-overlapping alternative adversarial pathways. Ultimately, we argue that the dominance of the $\ell_p$ ball does not just fail to reduce harm---it may actively facilitate it by communicating a false sense of security against the wrong threats.

title: An Asynchronous Federated Learning Platform for Lung Adenocarcinoma Grading via Foundation Models and Structural Pruning
authors: Moon-Il Joo, Md Ariful Islam Mozumder, Hee-Cheol Kim
abstract: Classification of lung adenocarcinoma into poorly differentiated (PD) and well-to-moderately differentiated (WMD) subtypes plays an important role in patient survival; however, consistent classification is difficult due to inter-observer variability among pathologists. Collecting data from multiple hospitals is also challenging due to patient privacy concerns. This study proposes a web-based federated learning system that shares only locally trained model weights without sharing patient data between institutions. The UNI2 foundation model and CLAM-SB were used to classify pathological whole slide images. A four-client federated learning system was constructed, and the NLST cohort was reserved exclusively for external validation. In centralized evaluation, joint training with CPTAC and TCGA outperformed single-institution training on external validation, confirming the necessity of multi-institutional data integration. FedAvg, FedProx, FedBN, and FedNova were compared as federated learning algorithms under identical experimental conditions. Test AUC ranked as FedBN, FedProx, FedNova, and FedAvg. FedNova showed the most balanced classification performance between PD and WMD. L1-norm structural pruning at 20%, 30%, and 40% sparsity was applied to reduce model transmission size. FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN showed a tendency of decreasing Test AUC under pruning, while FedNova achieved improved Test AUC across all sparsity levels. A web-based application was developed supporting slide upload, local training, AI classification, and attention heatmap-based visualization. The combination of FedNova and 40% pruning was confirmed as a practical approach that improves communication efficiency and classification performance while protecting patient privacy.

title: StructRL: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning with Replay Graphs
authors: Ivo Nowak
abstract: StructRL turns the experience collected during reinforcement learning into an explicit replay graph. Once the graph contains a path to the task goal, dynamic programming selects actions on the observed part of the state space; these actions form a graph policy that is defined only where the required transitions have been observed. StructRL transfers these actions to model-free learners: as action preferences for a DQN Q-model and as target directions along shortest observed paths for a SAC actor. For DQN on three sparse-reward MiniGrid tasks, final success rises from 0.10 to 0.90 (DoorKey), 0.10 to 0.80 (KeyCorridor) and 0 to 0.50 (ObstructedMaze); plain DQN does not catch up with three times the budget. For SAC on continuous PointMaze, graph-derived direction labels raise final success from 0.17 to 1.0 on seven matched runs that reached the goal. Distilling the graph policy into a fresh Q-model gives a DoorKey 6x6 controller that reaches the goal from 91% of reachable states, against 38% for plain DQN. Scaling experiments identify three bottlenecks: incomplete graph support, structural aliasing, and loss of graph information in high-dimensional inputs.

title: VASTRA: Efficient Agentic Top-K Interactive Video Analysis
authors: Tushar Tyagi, Aditya Raghavan, Haoran Qiu, Francisco Romero
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable natural language video retrieval, bypassing traditional hand-engineered pipelines. Integrating agentic reasoning frameworks (e.g., ReAct) further advances this paradigm by allowing models to dynamically inspect video content rather than relying on a single visual pass. Applying this pattern naively to video retrieval inherits problems that video systems cannot afford: results vary from run to run under identical conditions, and cost and latency scale with every reasoning step the agent takes rather than with the work the query actually requires. We present VASTRA, an agentic video retrieval system whose execution is dictated by query complexity rather than an open-ended reasoning loop: cheap, reliably answerable queries are ranked directly from pre-ingested summaries, while harder queries trigger targeted verification only where relevance is genuinely uncertain. This keeps control flow external to the model rather than latent in a growing chain of thought, establishing deterministic control flow by construction and end-to-end rank reproducibility under greedy serving. Across 40 benchmark queries, VASTRA exposes explicit presets: VASTRA-Fast runs 12.2x faster (4.2 s vs. 51.2 s) and 10.4x cheaper ($0.0044 vs. $0.0458) than best performing ReAct agent at a 5.0-point mAP reduction, while VASTRA-Max matches peak ReAct agent accuracy (0.653 vs. 0.649 mAP) at comparable latency, trading higher spend ($0.1022 vs. $0.0458) for zero run-to-run variance.

title: KernelMosaic: An Open Dataset and Agentic Framework for CUDA Kernel Generation
authors: Ningyuan Xi, Yuhang Lai, Ning Miao
abstract: Training large language models to generate efficient CUDA kernels requires supervision spanning diverse computational requirements and iterative code optimization. Constructing this supervision is challenging because of heterogeneous specifications, and useful implementations emerge through iterative complicated testing and refinement. We introduce KernelMosaic, an open dataset pairing diverse CUDA tasks with verified solutions and trajectories. Human-guided review and diversity-aware selection curate tasks expressed as natural-language descriptions, reference programs, mathematical specifications, and their intersections. To build the solutions and trajectories, our agentic framework guides a strong LLM through implementation, correctness repair, and performance optimization with reusable CUDA guidance and execution feedback. Supervised fine-tuning of a small open-source model on KernelMosaic raises correctness from 4%, 0%, and 0% to 88%, 82%, and 16% on KernelBench L1, L2, and L3, respectively, while increasing the fraction of tasks with kernels faster than PyTorch eager at every level. Further training experiments show that supervision from the curated trajectories substantially outperforms direct responses and promotes sustained testing and revision. These results demonstrate that KernelMosaic enables a general-purpose model to achieve substantial gains in CUDA kernel generation.

title: Discovering the Relation Between Architectural Models and Reference Architectures
authors: Thi Dinh Tran, Maria Teresa Rossi, Ludovico Iovino, Leonardo Mariani
abstract: Assessing whether concrete software architectures are consistent with their reference architecture (RA) is essential to ensure that architectural decisions scale coherently across projects, preserving the quality attributes the RA was designed to guarantee. In the absence of dedicated techniques, mapping the components of an architectural model onto a predefined RA can be addressed only with general-purpose model-comparison algorithms. Our experiments show that these algorithms are inaccurate when applied to RAs. To address this gap, we propose Reference Architecture Mapping Discovery (RAMD), an LLM-based workflow that combines model analysis with structured prompting, and refines results through an iterative RA compliance-checking mechanism. We evaluate RAMD on 64 open-source architectural models spanning three RAs from the IoT, self-driving, and smart parking domains. With domain knowledge and GPT-4o, RAMD reaches 85.8% mapping accuracy and outperforms the strongest baseline by 44.6 percentage points, while ensuring structural consistency with the RA.
