title: Neuromorphic Camera for Multi-Target Pointing Acquisition and Tracking in Free Space Optical Communication
authors: Francesco Nardo, Nigitha Selvaraj, Klaus Schertler, Peter Krötz, Ricardo Barrios, Sebastian Houben, Sebastian Randel
abstract: Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT) in Free-Space Optical Communication (FSOC) applications must achieve both low jitter and a large Field of View (FoV) to support beacon acquisition and multi-target tracking. While conventional frame-based sensors provide the necessary angular coverage, their performance is limited by latency, available frame-rate, and motion blur. This work explores and demonstrates the application of an event-based vision sensor for PAT tasks in FSOC. The system employs a neuromorphic sensor that asynchronously records brightness changes (events) with microsecond-level temporal resolution. The main contribution of this paper is a comparative analysis of event-based tracking algorithms for the simultaneous acquisition and tracking of multiple optical beacons that operate directly on this asynchronous stream. The performance of these strategies is validated on an experimental dataset representing realistic operational conditions for dynamic High-Altitude Platform (HAP) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. The analysis compares key metrics, such as tracking accuracy and processing latency, under various signal-to-background conditions.

title: A Diffusive T-Matrix Unifying the Electric and Magnetic Polarizability Tensors in Conducting Layered Media
authors: Fraser Williams, Dhammika Jayalath, Clinton Fookes, Ajay Pandey
abstract: Electromagnetic induction is used to detect and classify buried and submerged objects, such as unexploded ordnance in soil and on the seabed. A small object is commonly described by its magnetic polarizability tensor (MPT), which is independent of its position and of the sensor. The MPT assumes that the surrounding medium does not conduct. In seawater at extremely low frequency, or in clay at kilohertz frequencies, this assumption fails at depths comparable to the skin depth. The object then also diverts the current induced in the medium, a galvanic response that the MPT omits. We describe the object instead by its transition matrix (T-matrix), which keeps the independence from position and sensor and includes both responses. It is computed once per medium and frequency from a single finite element problem, for any shape and materials. Its inductive block reduces to the MPT when the medium conducts weakly, and its galvanic block reduces to the electric polarizability tensor in the static limit. We test the model against full finite element solutions for a conducting box, non-magnetic and permeable, in a layered sea and in clay over bedrock. Two orders beyond the dipole, it is accurate to within 1.4% over two decades of frequency and for sizes up to 0.7 of the depth, whereas the error of the MPT carried into the conducting medium reaches 91%. Blocks coupling the two responses, contained in neither tensor, contribute up to 13%.
zh_title: 一种统一导电分层介质中电极化率张量和磁极化率张量的扩散T矩阵
translation: 电磁感应用于探测和分类埋藏及水下物体，例如土壤和海床中的未爆弹药。小物体通常由其磁极化率张量（MPT）描述，该张量独立于物体位置和传感器。MPT假设周围介质不导电。在极低频海水或千赫兹频率粘土中，当深度与趋肤深度相当时，此假设失效。此时，物体还会分流介质中感应的电流，这是一种MPT忽略的电偶响应。我们转而用过渡矩阵（T矩阵）来描述物体，它保持了与位置和传感器的独立性，并包含了两种响应。它针对每种介质和频率，通过单一的有限元问题计算一次，适用于任何形状和材料。当介质弱导电时，其感应块简化为MPT；其电偶块在静态极限下简化为电极化率张量。我们针对在分层海水和粘土基岩中的导电盒子（非磁性和可渗透）的完整有限元解测试了该模型。在偶极子两阶之外，它在两个频率十年区间内，对于尺寸高达深度的0.7倍时，精度可达1.4%，而MPT在导电介质中的误差高达91%。耦合两种响应的块（在任一张量中均未包含）贡献高达13%。
tldr: 传统磁极化率张量（MPT）在导电介质中失效，无法准确描述埋藏或水下物体。本文提出了一种扩散T矩阵，它统一了电感应和电流响应，在导电分层介质中能提供高精度描述。
ai_comments: 这篇论文在电磁感应建模领域取得了重要进展，特别是在处理导电环境中的物体探测问题上。通过引入扩散T矩阵，该研究成功地统一了电极化率张量和磁极化率张量，并有效地纳入了传统方法所忽略的电偶响应。这种方法显著提高了在复杂分层导电介质中描述物体行为的准确性，对于未爆弹药探测等实际应用具有重要的理论和实践价值。
motivation: 电磁感应技术用于探测和分类埋藏及水下物体。然而，传统用于描述小物体（如未爆弹药）的磁极化率张量（MPT）假设周围介质不导电，这在海水或粘土等导电介质中，当深度达到趋肤深度时会失效。MPT无法解释物体在介质中引起的电流分流（电偶响应）。
method: 本文提出用过渡矩阵（T矩阵）来描述物体，该矩阵保持与位置和传感器的独立性，并包含电感应和电偶响应。T矩阵通过单一的有限元问题对每种介质和频率计算一次，适用于任何形状和材料。其感应部分在介质弱导电时简化为MPT，其电偶部分在静态极限下简化为电极化率张量。
results: 模型通过与导电盒子在分层海水和粘土基岩中的完整有限元解进行对比测试。结果显示，在偶极子两阶之外，该模型在两个频率十年区间内，对于尺寸达到深度的0.7倍时，精度可达1.4%。相比之下，MPT在导电介质中的误差高达91%。T矩阵中耦合两种响应的块（在MPT或电极化率张量中均不包含）贡献高达13%。
conclusion: 扩散T矩阵为导电分层介质中的物体提供了一种统一且准确的描述方法，克服了传统MPT的局限性，成功整合了电感应和电偶响应。

title: Hierarchical Empirical-Bayes Forecasting of Sparse Counts with Exposure: An Application to Airline Demand and Premium-Cabin Capacity Sharing
authors: Irakli Gudavadze
abstract: Sparse count forecasting arises when events are rare, exposure varies across observational units, and short histories contain many zeros. Using thin-market airline demand as a motivating application, this paper develops a hierarchical exposure-adjusted Poisson-Gamma (HEPG) framework for probabilistic forecasting. Conditional counts follow a Poisson model with an exposure offset and pooled calendar effects, while unit specific baseline intensities receive a Gamma prior whose hyperparameters are estimated empirically across the population. The resulting posterior is Gamma and the posterior predictive distribution is negative binomial, providing closed-form partial pooling and explicit propagation of parameter uncertainty. This is especially useful for zero-history or low-exposure units, where independent maximum-likelihood estimates are unstable or collapse to zero. An adaptive extension, A-HEPG, adds a moment-matched negative-binomial variance correction when residual extra-Poisson variation remains. In synthetic experiments with 400 heterogeneous markets, HEPG improves average negative log predictive probability relative to complete pooling and independent route-level Poisson estimation. At a mean latent rate of 0.15 requests per exposure unit, the score is 0.525 for HEPG, compared with 0.585 for pooled Poisson and 0.731 for route-level Poisson maximum likelihood. Under strong overdispersion, A-HEPG reduces the score from 0.552 to 0.529. A downstream cabin-capacity example links the predictive distribution to a seat-protection rule based on predictive survival probabilities and fare ratios. The study emphasizes coherent probabilistic inference, partial pooling, and diagnostic model escalation for sparse applied count data.

title: Time-Domain and Spectral Decomposition of Dynamic Coupling with Instantaneous and Time-Lagged Causality: Methodological Evaluation and Application to Cardiovascular Variability
authors: Gorana Mijatovic, Marta Iovino, Michal Javorka, Luca Faes
abstract: The quantification of dynamic interactions in coupled physiological time series is a central question in biomedical signal processing. A critical issue is the presence of instantaneous dependencies, often neglected in conventional Granger causality (GC) analyses despite potentially reflecting physiologically meaningful effects. We investigate time- and frequency-domain measures of causality within the linear autoregressive (AR) framework, treating instantaneous dependencies according to three formulations: (i) the classical strictly causal AR model, providing spectral measures of time-lagged GC and instantaneous interaction; (ii) the Geweke approach, assigning instantaneous dependencies to the direction opposite to that under investigation; (iii) a single extended AR model incorporating causally-oriented instantaneous dependencies, yielding spectral GC measures accounting for both instantaneous and time-lagged causality. The three approaches are evaluated in simulated Gaussian systems, where dynamic measures can be derived analytically and compared with the expected coupling structure. The single extended AR model emerges as the most consistent formulation when instantaneous dependencies have a physiologically meaningful causal direction and is then applied to cardiovascular interactions between heart period (HP) and systolic (SAP) or diastolic arterial pressure (DAP) in healthy subjects during postural and mental stress. Accounting for instantaneous dependencies substantially affects HP-SAP and HP-DAP interactions, enabling better quantification of baroreflex and cardiac run-off mechanisms and characterization of their responses to stress and of low- and high-frequency dynamics. Overall, the framework provides consistent representation of causal interactions across time and frequency and highlights the importance of accounting for instantaneous dependencies in physiological coupling.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
authors: Bisheshwor Neupane
abstract: This study benchmarks 24 forecasting configurations on ESHED-38, daily smart-meter consumption for 38 homes in Erbil, Iraq, collected from May 2020 to June 2025 with station weather and a household survey. The configurations span five base families, plus two cross-family ensembles: naive baselines, per-house statistical models, global gradient-boosted trees, global deep networks, and zero-shot time-series foundation models. All are evaluated on the same 54,720 forecasts from 48 weekly origins over a 359-day held-out period, at lead times up to 30 days, using scaled absolute error, the continuous ranked probability score, calibration, and Friedman, Nemenyi and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests. The best configurations cut the scaled error of a seasonal-naive forecast by 20 to 25 percent, and the leading models beat it in all 38 houses. Chronos-2, used without training, is significantly the most accurate model one day ahead; at one week it is statistically tied with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and a pre-specified ensemble, and the two ensembles lead at 30 days. Deep networks trained from scratch do not outperform exponential smoothing on average, and the household survey adds negligible skill. Metered demand peaks in winter and falls as temperature rises. Recorded weather did not improve any model run with and without it. A quality screen helps explain why: on 68 percent of dates a temperature value recurs exactly on other dates, in three annual blocks covering almost all of the test period, suggesting that much of the weather record reuses one annual sequence. The value of weather information is therefore treated as unresolved, and the protocol is released as a baseline.

title: A Hidden Markov Analysis of Wet-Weather Tyre Crossover in Formula One
authors: Bo-Yi Lin, Michka Sharpe
abstract: Detecting a wet-weather regime and deciding when to replace slick tyres are distinct tasks. This study examines their relationship through a retrospective analysis of the 2024 British Grand Prix. A three-state hidden Markov model (HMM) represents normalized lap time and precipitation, while an entry rule requires both a high filtered Wet-state probability and sufficient pace deterioration. The analysis includes 642 car-laps and 33 complete lap-bin observations within the available precipitation record. Each completed-lap signal takes effect on the following lap. The combined rule enters on lap 27, matching the team-weighted modal reference; removing the pace or state condition advances entry to laps 25 and 20, respectively. The combined entry is retained in all 10 team-exclusion refits, but refitting a specification with larger off-diagonal transition probabilities produces entry on lap 20. These comparisons illustrate how state inference can contextualize a performance criterion while exposing dependence on model assumptions. Because estimation and rule development use the same event, the correspondence establishes neither prospective accuracy nor a race-time advantage.

title: Strategic Causal Policy Learning with Manipulable Eligibility
authors: Suhwan Bong
abstract: The standard rule in unconstrained causal policy learning is simple: treat individuals with nonnegative CATEs. But this rule can fail when treatment eligibility is strategically manipulable. After a policy is announced, individuals may change the covariates used for assignment without changing their underlying treatment effects. We study how such responses affect treatment allocation and welfare. Using an access-burden representation, we characterize strategic treatment and decompose welfare loss into missed beneficial treatment and harmful treatment. For linear CATEs and quadratic manipulation costs, we derive closed-form threshold corrections. When manipulation costs are homogeneous, a single correction recovers the ideal positive-CATE allocation. With heterogeneous costs, welfare maximization, pointwise safety, and minimax group welfare regret can favor different thresholds. Simulations illustrate these tradeoffs and examine the effects of estimating treatment effects and behavioral responses.
comment: Accepted to the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

title: Bayesian Evidence Fusion for Capability Tracking-A Simulation Study and Historical CI Pilot
authors: Taimoor Ahmad
abstract: SaaS capability assessments can become stale between questionnaires, while delivery telemetry offers incomplete and correlated evidence. Continuous assessment and Bayesian delivery analysis already exist, leaving uncertainty about how biased surveys and missing observations should influence capability estimates.We implement SAAS-MATURITY-TWIN, an anchored Gaussian state model that jointly filters capability proxies and persistent survey offsets. Source covariance prevents correlated observations from being counted independently. Conditional uncertainty supports forecasting and budgeted intervention screening, with action effects estimated from randomized synthetic cohorts. Ten seeds generate forty paired worlds spanning reference observations, extensive missingness, informative missingness, and increased noise. Reference latent root mean squared error is 0.1261, compared with 0.1452 for a tuned moving average; nominal ninety percent intervals cover 90.3 percent. Improved state recovery produces only small incident forecasting differences. Adaptive conformal inference and an adapted conformal PID controller are evaluated separately for observed telemetry, where noise shifts expose calibration limitations. A licensed TravisTorrent pilot evaluates build prediction on 13 074 held out builds from 224 projects. Logistic regression achieves a Brier score of 0.1289, close to random forests. These results support reproducible methodological testing, but do not establish real organizational maturity, intervention effectiveness, or production readiness. Independent calibration and longitudinal validation remain necessary.

title: Where Does EEG Sleep-Onset Forecasting Skill Arise? A State-Conditioned Evaluation
authors: Ali Amini, Mohammad Alijanpour Shalmani, Kaare B Mikkelsen, Robertas Damaševičius
abstract: Sleep is scored afterwards in 30-second epochs as wake (W), the transitional stage N1, or N2. We study EEG forecasts, issued every 30 s from the preceding 30 s of EEG alone, of whether the first scored N2 epoch will begin within five minutes, on Sleep-EDF. A Brier score pooled over decisions made before and after the input is scored N1 does not show when the gain arose. In our own prespecified one-shot held-out comparisons, the spectral model SpecLR-18 improved on a training prevalence constant by 18.3% in the internal test, whereas its prespecified external result was inconclusive. Joining the retrospectively scored stage of each input epoch to the same frozen predictions, almost all of that internal-test Brier difference was attributed to N1-scored decisions; a diagnostic reference told only the scored stage reached 26.3% in the internal test and 29.5% in the external cohort, above the spectral forecasts in point estimate though not every difference excluded zero; and within-stage EEG advantages seen in single cohorts were not consistent across cohorts, with no consistent wake-stratum improvement. These references use labels unavailable online and cannot reveal what a model represents; they show why pooled forecasting scores need state-conditioned interpretation before being read as early anticipation.

title: Methodological Pitfalls in Predicting Ship Turnaround Time at Brazilian Ports: An Empirical Audit and a Reproducible Pipeline
authors: Eduardo Caruso Barbosa Pacheco, Reynaldo Pereira Martins, Alexandre dos Santos Gualberto, Joao Vitor Souza Germano, Milton Miranda Neto, Francisco Louzada
abstract: Two recent studies on ship turnaround time at Brazilian ports report models with R-squared scores above 0.80 on data from the national waterway transportation agency. We audit their published datasets and reveal these results are inflated by structural data leakage. Specifically, 97 percent of berthing events in their random row-level split appear in both training and testing partitions. We demonstrate that a model's R-squared drops from 0.82 to 0.20 when the data is properly split at the berthing level. We further document additional methodological flaws, including survivorship bias, undocumented target truncation, and the retention of variables that algebraically reconstruct the target. To address these issues, we propose a reproducible pipeline that aggregates cargo to the berthing level, utilizes conditional imputation, and represents high-cardinality cargo variables through weighted averages of multilingual sentence embeddings. Evaluating six time targets and thirty seeds, our pipeline reveals that cargo embeddings yield statistically significant improvements on four operational targets, while administrative waiting times remain unaffected. Prior works missed this per-target heterogeneity by conflating genuine signal with leaked identity.

title: Empirical Bayes mirror testing for persistent widening of achievement gaps in U.S. school districts
authors: Bowen Gang, Yin Xia
abstract: Unequal recovery from pandemic learning losses raises concerns about widening achievement gaps between economically disadvantaged students and their peers. This study seeks to identify districts whose mathematics gaps widened in every annual interval from 2022 to 2025. The analysis uses estimates from the Stanford Education Data Archive (SEDA) for 5,600 U.S. school districts. Identifying such districts requires accounting for correlated errors and differing precision in the estimated annual changes, as well as multiplicity. The true annual gap changes in each district form an effect vector, and persistent widening means that every component is positive. To address this class of multiple testing problems, we propose an empirical Bayes mirror procedure. It uses an estimated distribution of effect vectors to guide ranking and covariance-adjusted mirror observations to calibrate selection. The procedure achieves finite-sample false discovery rate (FDR) control under a Gaussian observation model, without requiring accurate estimation of the posterior null probabilities used for ranking. Simulations demonstrate power gains from incorporating information about the distribution of effect vectors. At a target FDR of 25%, the SEDA analysis identifies eight districts in five states with evidence of widening gaps in every annual interval.

title: GrAFT-PDX: Growth and Failure-Time Modeling of Patient-Derived Xenograft Experiments
authors: Nihar Mauskar, Sebastian Salazar, Aaron Schein, Wesley Tansey
abstract: Cancer drugs are often evaluated for efficacy in mice before proceeding to human clinical trials. To do this, human tumors are engrafted onto immune-incompetent mice to create a patient-derived xenograft (PDX). Engrafted tumors can be propagated to evaluate multiple drugs, but the time and costs involved in PDX studies limit high throughput drug screens in mice. Here we present GrAFT-PDX, a Bayesian model of PDX drug screens that aims to reduce the PDX screening burden by enabling imputation of missing experiments and early stopping of likely unsuccessful drugs. Unlike conventional survival or growth models, GrAFT-PDX jointly predicts tumor growth and survival outcomes using a learned latent function decomposition. In experiments on a large-scale PDX dataset, GrAFT-PDX outperforms Cox proportional hazards models at predicting time of death, outperforms machine learning baselines at predicting tumor growth, and recovers known gene-treatment relationships without genomic input.

title: Is generative AI really changing public sector work? Evidence from a multi-country survey
authors: Saba Esnaashari, Tvesha Sippy, Youmna Hashem, Sukankana Chakraborty, Jonathan Bright
abstract: Artificial intelligence has the potential to transform how public services are delivered, with important implications for public service productivity. But how widely is the technology actually being used - and is it making any difference? Our survey of 3,362 public sector workers across the UK, the USA, South Africa and the EU finds widespread use of AI in every region. Our findings suggest that this spread is being driven by bottom-up individual adoption rather than top-down institutional adoption. In the EU, for example, 65\% of respondents use AI, while only 19\% say their organisation has formally adopted it. Most users are positive about its effects, with 79\% saying AI has improved their productivity. However, only 29\% say it has increased what is expected of them at work, raising questions about how truly transformative the technology is so far. Across regions, South Africa is a clear outlier, with the highest levels of use, organisational adoption, optimism and awareness of guidelines.

title: Regularized trimmed Factorial and Reduced K-means for contaminated high-dimensional data: separating geometry, search and selection
authors: Cinzia Di Nuzzo, Matteo Farnè
abstract: Factorial and Reduced K-means estimate a partition and a low-dimensional clustering subspace jointly, which makes them attractive when the variables that separate groups are not those that dominate total variance. On contaminated high-dimensional data they face three linked problems: trimming can make the scatter matrices singular, the criterion has many local optima, and the rank, number of groups and trimming proportion are unknown and interact. We propose REG-HD-TFKM and REG-HD-TRKM, regularized trimmed versions of the two methods, together with a selection procedure that handles these problems as separate decisions. A ridge-stabilized spectral step keeps every fit well defined; heterogeneous multistart search explores alternative solutions; method-specific agreement and reproducibility scores choose among them; and trimming is applied only when a radial diagnostic or the path over trimming levels supports it. A simulation study with 41 design cells shows why the separation matters. Two representations of euro-area bank balance sheets show that similar partitions can rest on nearly orthogonal subspaces, and that the same selected structure can describe different retained samples.

title: Clustering professional football players using Gaussian mixture models: A case study of the English Premier League 2024/25
authors: Harry O'Donnell, Antony M. Overstall
abstract: The increasing availability of detailed football performance data has created new opportunities for identifying player archetypes and informing recruitment and tactical decision-making. Most existing clustering approaches assign each player to a single group, despite the reality that many modern footballers perform hybrid roles spanning multiple stylistic categories. Performance data for 314 outfield players from the 2024/25 English Premier League season are analysed using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) applied to principal component representations of player statistics. Unlike hard-assignment methods such as k-means, the GMM provides probabilistic cluster memberships, allowing uncertainty and role hybridity to be quantified. Seven player archetypes are identified in the full dataset. Posterior membership probabilities reveal a subset of players whose profiles span multiple clusters, providing an objective measure of tactical flexibility and stylistic ambiguity. Further analyses within defender, midfielder, and forward groups recover position-specific sub-archetypes and highlight exceptional outliers. The results demonstrate that model-based clustering provides a flexible and interpretable framework for identifying latent structure in high-dimensional performance data while explicitly quantifying uncertainty in cluster membership. More broadly, the approach is readily transferable to other sports and domains in which individuals exhibit overlapping characteristics and cannot be adequately represented by hard cluster assignments alone.

title: Bayesian modeling of predictive stability under generalized Arrhenius non-linear kinetics
authors: Lorenzo Mauri, Samantha Gleich, Michael Johnson, Andy Liaw, Daniel Skomski, Federico Ferrari
abstract: Predictive stability modeling is widely used in pharmaceutical development to establish product shelf-life by identifying the kinetic parameters that govern degradation behavior and using these parameters to extrapolate out in time. Recent approaches typically assume linear degradation dynamics and rely on the Arrhenius equation to model temperature-specific reaction rates. However, observed degradation profiles may reflect nonlinear reaction dynamics and more complex temperature-specific reaction rates, potentially leading to reduced accuracy in long-term predictions and motivating a more flexible approach. We propose a novel Bayesian framework which extends predictive stability modeling beyond simple Arrhenius low-order kinetic dynamics and accommodates complex degradation mechanisms. The degradation process is modeled through the Sestak-Berggren kinetic formulation, a flexible ordinary differential equation encompassing many classical degradation models as special cases. To facilitate model interpretability and model exploration, probabilistic model selection on kinetic parameters automatically determines whether nonlinear reaction components are supported by the data, allowing the model to adaptively collapse to simpler dynamics when appropriate. To address departure from classical Arrhenius kinetics, we develop a generalized temperature reaction rate formulation in which temperature-specific reaction rates are shrunk toward Arrhenius predictions through a hierarchical shrinkage prior while allowing departures when supported by the data. This approach yields robustness to misspecification and reduces sensitivity to potentially influential high-temperature observations commonly encountered in accelerated stability experiments. The resulting framework provides a principled and flexible statistical tool for model-informed shelf-life determination.
comment: 28 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables; includes supplementary material

title: Functional Regression with Interacting Latent Mean and Variance Processes
authors: Ching-Chia Chou, Jeng-Min Chiou
abstract: In many applications, variability itself carries important predictive information beyond the mean, and its association with an outcome may further depend on the underlying mean trajectory. However, existing functional regression approaches primarily rely on mean-based representations of functional predictors, while variability is often ignored or reduced to scalar summaries. We propose a functional regression framework that incorporates latent mean and variance processes as predictors, together with their mean-variance interaction, allowing the predictive contribution of variability to depend on the underlying mean trajectory. We establish consistency and convergence rates for the estimated coefficient functions and interaction surface, accounting for reconstruction errors, increasing observation frequency, and diverging truncation dimensions without requiring independence between the latent processes. Applications to real data demonstrate substantial gains in predictive accuracy from incorporating the variance process, with the proposed approach outperforming competing functional regression methods in the Tecator application and revealing localized mean-variance interaction patterns.

title: Introducing and Repealing an EV Subsidy: Evidence from New Zealand's Clean Car Discount
authors: Fabian Dunker, Jyotsna Garg
abstract: New Zealand's Clean Car Discount (CCD) was a feebate scheme that offered rebates for low-emission vehicles from July 2021, added fees for high-emission vehicles from April 2022, and was abolished at the end of December 2023. Shortly afterwards, road user charges were introduced for electric vehicles (EVs). We study how EV adoption responded to the introduction and the abrupt repeal of the scheme, using monthly vehicle registration data from 2014 to 2024. A structural break analysis following Bai and Perron, combined with a regression discontinuity in time, shows that breaks in the registrations of battery electric, plug-in hybrid and conventional vehicles coincide with the policy dates. To estimate causal effects, we apply a difference-in-differences approach with Queensland, Australia, as a comparison region and Newey-West standard errors. Because the New Zealand market was about four times larger, the analysis uses log-transformed registrations, so that parallel trends refer to equal growth rates. The results are asymmetric. After the introduction of the rebates, EV registrations in New Zealand rose strongly, but by a similar proportion as in Queensland, and the average effect relative to Queensland is not statistically significant. A specification allowing for a change in slope suggests a gradual acceleration of EV uptake. After the repeal, EV registrations fell by about 72% relative to Queensland, and the decline persisted in 2025. Both policy dates were preceded by a rush of purchases. The average CO2 emissions of newly registered vehicles fell markedly during the scheme and rebounded after its end. The results suggest that an abrupt end of EV purchase incentives can cause a large and lasting drop in EV uptake, and that a gradual, pre-announced phase-out may be preferable.

title: Improving Algorithmic Trading for BESS on Intraday Electricity Markets through Distributional Price Forecasts
authors: Simon Hirsch, David Schaurecker, David Wozabal
abstract: Grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) are becoming increasingly important in short-term energy markets, where they help balance fluctuations in variable renewable generation. In many countries, the continuous intraday market is the most important wholesale market for BESS to monetize their flexibility. In this paper, we propose an extension to the myopic rolling intrinsic policy that incorporates intraday price forecasts tailored specifically to the BESS trading problem. While a large literature addresses intraday price forecasting, most existing work focuses on volume-weighted prices during the last hours of trading and consequently fails to capture the features most relevant to BESS trading. Our approach addresses this gap by introducing a novel target variable derived from the limit order book and its dynamics. The resulting forecasts are designed to inform the optimization about future profit opportunities while preserving computational efficiency and avoiding the burden of full stochastic optimization. In a realistic high-frequency simulation setting covering 2023 and 2024, our method improves profits by up to 42% over the naive rolling intrinsic formulation. We further analyze the relationship between forecast accuracy, stability, and financial performance, establishing a clear inverse relationship between accuracy and stability. Finally, we find evidence that BESS size and duration jointly influence both overall profitability and the marginal benefit of incorporating forecasts.

title: A Family-Level Graphical Gatekeeping Procedure with Iterative Retesting
authors: Zhiying Qiu, Wenge Guo, Sanat Sarkar
abstract: Confirmatory clinical trials often involve multiple objectives grouped into families according to scientific priorities. At the intersection of graphical multiple testing and gatekeeping methods, we develop a Bonferroni-based family-level graphical procedure with partial-rejection-based transfers and iterative re-testing. Families are tested sequentially within each stage, using fixed component tests and a prespecified transition matrix. The updating rule combines current-stage forward contributions based on current family levels with previous-stage backward contributions based on initial allocations. We establish strong global familywise error rate control at a prespecified level under arbitrary dependence. The construction permits backward feedback while retaining fixed component tests and transition coefficients, distinguishing its implementation from forward-only family-level procedures and the specified superchain algorithm. Simulations demonstrate gains over the corresponding No-retest procedure, while identifying an efficiency cost relative to a hypothesis-level graphical comparator with matched initial allocations and edge weights. Clinical illustrations show how the procedure implements family-level priorities and feedback, and an extension accommodates a two-layer structure with multiple families per layer.
comment: 42 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Includes proofs in the appendix

title: Gatheral's Conjecture: General sufficient conditions for refutation
authors: Elisa Alòs, Òscar Burés, Vladimir Lucic
abstract: In this paper we give general sufficient conditions for a stochastic volatility model to be a counterexample for Gatheral's conjecture. The conditions, achieved by asymptotic properties of integrated variance derivatives and Wiener chaos expansions, show that a general class of rough volatility models are generally counterexamples to Gatheral's conjecture. For stochastic volatility models with Markovian variance, the conjecture fails under a relationship on the coefficients of the SDE defining the variance process. Particular examples are provided.

title: Idiosyncratic Market Effects in Global Time Series Momentum
authors: Andrew Butler, Maciej Zawadzki, Adam Butler
abstract: Time series momentum is a pervasive explanatory factor in financial markets whereby a market's recent historical average return positively predicts future returns. Recent applications of statistical learning augment the traditional linear model definition with a more descriptive global nonlinear factor model. We extend the work of \citet{MoskowitzNonlinear} and demonstrate that models fit at the individual market level exhibit response curves that are distinct from the global factor model. We highlight the heterogeneity of forward market returns as a function of time series momentum and provide a framework that enables each feature-market pair to express its unique prediction behaviour. Empirical results demonstrate that, despite substantially smaller sample sizes, fitting nonlinear models to individual markets is a robust and often overlooked modelling approach that can result in a marginal improvement in out-of-sample performance.

title: Aproximación práctica a los métodos de selección de portafolios de inversión
authors: Carlos Minutti-Martinez
abstract:
This paper explores the practical approach to portfolio selection methods for investments. The study delves into portfolio theory, discussing concepts such as expected return, variance, asset correlation, and opportunity sets. It also presents the efficient frontier and its application in the Markowitz model, which employs mean-variance optimization techniques. An alternative approach based on the mean-semivariance model is introduced. This model accounts for the skewness and kurtosis of the asset return distribution, providing a more comprehensive view of risk and return. The study also addresses the practical implementation of these models, including the use of genetic algorithms to optimize portfolio selection. Additionally, transaction costs and integer constraints in portfolio optimization are considered, demonstrating the applicability of the Markowitz model.
  --
  Este documento explorar la aproximación práctica a los métodos de selección de portafolios para inversiones. El estudio profundiza en la teoría de los portafolios, discutiendo conceptos como el rendimiento esperado, la varianza, la correlación entre activos y los conjuntos de oportunidades. También presenta la frontera eficiente y su aplicación en el modelo de Markowitz, que utiliza técnicas de optimización media-varianza. Se introduce un enfoque alternativo basado en el modelo media-semivarianza. Este modelo tiene en cuenta la asimetría y la curtosis de la distribución de retornos de los activos, proporcionando una visión más completa de riesgo y rendimiento. El estudio también aborda la implementación práctica de estos modelos, incluyendo el uso de algoritmos genéticos para optimizar la selección de portafolios. Además, se consideran los costos de transacción y las restricciones enteras en la optimización del portafolio.

title: Global Seasonality Factor Investing
authors: Andrew Butler, Adam Butler, Maciej Zawadzki
abstract: We study seasonality as a factor for predicting risk-adjusted returns across global futures markets. We document five seasonality anomalies that, in aggregate, are pervasive across bond, commodity and equity markets. We demonstrate that each seasonality factor produces excess returns that are not reasonably explained by established global time series carry, momentum and skewness factors. We apply recent innovations in statistical learning and fit nonlinear seasonality models at the individual market level, thereby allowing each feature-market pair to express its unique seasonal prediction pattern. We discuss candidate economic rationales for the existence and persistence of each seasonality anomaly. Walk-forward out-of-sample testing demonstrates that fast-moving seasonal patterns, such as day-of-week and day-of-month, produce strong gross performance but with extremely high turnover, resulting in negative performance net of transaction costs. In contrast, slower-moving seasonal patterns, such as day-of-quarter, day-of-half-year and day-of-year, produce positive gross performance and, with the exception of day-of-quarter, positive net performance. An equal-weight ensemble of seasonality models produces an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio that is competitive with, and uncorrelated to, established global time series factor portfolios. Empirical results demonstrate that adding seasonality to a global factor portfolio increases the out-of-sample Sharpe ratio by approximately $30\%$ over the full evaluation period.

title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Shuoqing Deng, Daxin Huang, Dominykas Norgilas
abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

title: Media Trading with Censored Auction Prices: A Stochastic Control and Reinforcement Learning Approach
authors: Yun-Ithry Gamrani, Huyên Pham
abstract: In real-time bidding, marketing agencies must balance campaign performance, transaction margins and the use of a finite advertising budget. A key difficulty is that market-clearing prices are typically observed only when bids are successful, so the information available for subsequent decisions depends on the bidding policy. We formulate this problem using a continuous-time stochastic control model with a latent price process. To construct a price signal, we consider parallel exploratory subcampaigns in which bids are randomized subject to an upper bound. Under a stylized cross-sectional sampling model, the resulting price estimator is consistent and satisfies a mean-square error bound of order $N^{-1}$, where $N$ is the number of exploratory observations. We then describe a model-based approach combining forward-equation calibration with Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman policy iteration and a physics-informed neural network, alongside an entropy-regularized actor-critic approach based on observable information in a model-free setting. Synthetic experiments illustrate the estimator and the computational procedures. The framework clarifies the decision and information trade-offs faced by the agency, while distinguishing full-information benchmarks and estimated-price policies from the genuinely partially observed control problem.

title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
authors: Eduardo Abi Jaber, Dorinel Bastide, Ronan Pécheul, Clément Rey
abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

title: Novel Esscher concepts for informational risks and valuation in market models under random horizon
authors: Tahir Choulli, Ella Elazkany
abstract: This paper considers the setting constituted by the triplet $(S,\mathbb{F},τ)$. The pair $(S,\mathbb{F})$ is the initial model where $S$ is the discounted price process of risky assets (Stocks) and $\mathbb{F}$ is the ``public" flow of information that is available to all agents over time. $τ$ is an arbitrary random time, which might not be seen through the flow $\mathbb{F}$, and it represents a default time in credit risk and a death time of an insured in life insurance where mortality and/or longevity risks present serious challenges. For simplicity, we suppose $S$ follows a geometric jump-diffusion model with stochastic volatiles and $\mathbb{F}$ is generated by a Brownian motion and Poisson process. In this setting, we address how the Esscher densities and/or measures notions can evolves with the informational risk induced by $τ$. In fact, we introduce the notion of Esscher with degrees-of-freedom associated to the informational risks generated by $τ$. On the one hand, we give various and complete characterizations of these Esscher notions in our informational setting. On the other hand, we fully characterize the Escher-prices bounds, for vulnerable claims (claims built on the occurrence of $τ$), using constrained backward stochastic differential equations (CBSDEs for short hereafter) that appear to be novel as well.

title: On the continuity of martingale optimal transport in higher dimensions
authors: Francesco Mattesini, Johannes Wiesel
abstract: We investigate qualitative and quantitative continuity of martingale optimal transport under perturbations of both marginals in dimensions $d\geq2$. We assume that each pair of marginals admits a reference martingale coupling whose density relative to the product of its marginals is bounded above and away from zero, uniformly along the sequence. If the limiting target measure is not carried by a hyperplane, we prove continuity under $W_1$-convergence for continuous costs of at most linear growth, assuming only finite first moments. For Lipschitz costs, a uniform $p$-moment bound on the targets, $p>1$, yields an explicit stability estimate with exponent $(1-1/p)/2$; uniformly bounded target supports give exponent $1/2$. The proof constructs a correction of couplings with small martingale bias while preserving both marginals. Truncated moment corrections allow the target measure to have unbounded support. The construction also shows that every martingale coupling of the limiting marginals can be approximated in $W_1$ by martingale couplings of the approximating marginals. We also discuss counterexamples showing that neither the uniform density condition nor non-degeneracy of the limiting target measure can be omitted in general.

title: Incomplete-market CAPM equilibria in continuous time
authors: Christoph Czichowsky, Martin Herdegen, David Martins
abstract: We study continuous-time CAPM equilibria with general mean-variance preferences of the form $U(μ,σ)$, where $U$ is strictly quasiconcave, increasing in the mean $μ$ and decreasing in the volatility $σ$ of terminal wealth. Our framework accommodates both financial and productive assets with nontradeable endowments. We allow for equilibria driven by general semimartingales in the case of linear mean-variance preferences and by continuous semimartingales in the case of general mean-variance preferences. The key insight is a connection between mean-variance efficiency and quadratic utility maximisation. We first characterise quadratic equilibria through an explicit family of equilibrium price processes indexed by the aggregate risk tolerance. We then show that each agent's optimal mean-variance strategy corresponds to a quadratic optimum with an endogenously determined risk tolerance. This correspondence reduces the mean-variance equilibrium problem to a one-dimensional fixed-point problem, whose solvability we establish using fine properties of (dynamic) mean-variance hedging and a novel stability result for quadratic BSDEs with BMO growth at the origin. Finally, examples illustrate how unspanned stochastic-volatility risk interacts with aggregate endowments to affect equilibrium asset prices, and how nonlinear mean-variance preferences influence equilibrium risk tolerance and asset-price comparative statics.

title: We Used It Anyway: Low Trust and High Adoption of Large Language Models in Requirements Engineering Education
authors: Riccardo Coppola, Giacomo Garaccione, Stefano Mancini, Luca Ardito
abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping how students approach Software Engineering activities, particularly those centered on textual artifacts. This paper reports on the experience of integrating a non-restrictive LLM use within a first-year Master's course in Software Engineering, in which students completed a semester-long Software Engineering project divided in a Requirements Engineering (RE) phase and a software testing phase. Following the completion of the RE phase of the project, we administered a 12-question survey to 43 students to investigate which LLM tools they used, for which activities, how they evaluated AI-generated outputs, and how they envisioned the role of LLMs in future SE curricula. Our findings show that LLM use was nearly universal among respondents and concentrated primarily on text-intensive activities such as use-case narratives, consistency checking, brainstorming, and refinement of existing artifacts. Despite this widespread adoption, most students perceived AI-generated outputs as inferior to their own work, frequently reporting issues related to incorrect or incomplete content, mismatches with course-specific conventions, over-engineering, and limitations in diagram generation. Nevertheless, students continued to rely extensively on LLM as a reviewer, critic, and productivity aid rather than as a fully autonomous artifact generator. We also observe that students' choice of models was strongly influenced by access to premium subscriptions available for free for student accounts, highlighting the role of economic accessibility in shaping educational AI ecosystems. The results suggest that the most significant challenge in the adoption of LLMs within Requirements Engineering education is not whether students use these tools, but whether they possess the skills required to critically evaluate, contextualize, and correct its outputs.

title: From Relevant Posts to Attributable Spans: Explicit Symptom Evidence for Depression Questionnaire Inference
authors: Sumanth Manduru, Carlotta Domeniconi
abstract: Longitudinal social-media histories offer an opportunity to assess depression, potentially supporting the inference of standardized depression questionnaire responses. However, this task requires evidence that is semantically relevant to a symptom and attributable to the user, while being sufficiently specific to support an individual questionnaire item. Existing approaches rely on semantic similarity to retrieve posts, which can introduce misleading or non-attributable evidence, particularly in multi-symptom posts and discussions of others' experiences. We propose SREE (Symptom Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded InfErence), an evidence-grounded pipeline that extracts first-person and symptom-specific text spans, selects a representative subset using a Facility Location-inspired objective, and performs Evidence-Gated Inference over the selected evidence. We evaluate evidence retrieval on BDI-Sen and evidence-conditioned questionnaire inference on eRisk 2019-2021. Compared with state-of-the-art retrieval approaches, SREE achieves relative improvements of 70% in post-level precision and 59% in F1, while retaining at least 30% fewer posts. On multi-symptom sentences, it also outperforms dense retrieval in precision and F1 even with twice the retrieval budget. Across all three eRisk collections, SREE achieves the highest exact item-level agreement while remaining competitive on ordinal and aggregate metrics. These results highlight the importance of localizing attributable evidence and controlling its composition before inferring depression questionnaire responses.

title: Efficient Conversion of Algorithms to Linear Programs
authors: Shermin Khosravi, David Bremner
abstract: The expressiveness of Linear Programming (LP) has motivated research on an LP compiler that generates polynomial-size LPs for polynomial-time solvable problems, including those having exponential extension complexity. By automating modeling from high-level algorithmic descriptions, the compiler offers a promising alternative to algebraic modelling languages. However, the resulting LPs are extremely large, posing challenges for existing solvers. Recently, we have introduced two LP compiler optimizations, namely Hierarachical Synchronization Barriers (HSB) and Constraint Sharing (CS), that address this challenge by exploiting structural and similarity-based patterns derived from the source code and the design of compiler-generated LPs, beyond what conventional compiler and presolve techniques can achieve in isolation. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive evaluation of these optimization methods on fundamental combinatorial algorithms and introduce the Execution Domain Aware (EDA) optimization framework to address a limitation revealed by this analysis. The framework reinterprets structural synchronizations as a time abstraction layer within which other optimizations can target localized reductions while remaining agnostic to time-step transitions. Across a broad suite of benchmarks, HSB and CS consistently generate smaller LPs, achieving LP file-size reductions of up to 96% and 53%, respectively, while also improving numerical conditioning, solver performance, and solution quality. HSB provides the strongest and most robust overall gains. The EDA framework further broadens the range of benchmarks that can benefit from HSB when its underlying structural assumptions are less effective. We view this work as a step toward systematic generation of Compact Integer Programming formulations for problems with exponential-size Integer Programs having polynomial-time separation oracles.
comment: Full version with experimental data in appendices

title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
authors: Zhongxing Xu, Zhonghua Wang, Zhe Qian, Shiyan Su, Ming Hu, Xiaocheng Zou, Wei Feng, Mingquan Lin, Yuyin Zhou, Yifan Peng, Hamid Rezatofighi, Zongyuan Ge
abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.

title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
authors: Wentao Lei, Li Liu
abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. We also build SEL-Pairs, a benchmark of length-matched evidence and control deletions from three question-answering datasets. Quantitative and qualitative experiments with five reader models on it show that SELD consistently outperforms strong and recent baselines across compressors, compression rates and models, identifying the evidence-removing edit in 83% of matched pairs with unchanged answers, against 70% for the strongest baseline. These results show that evidence loss in compressed contexts can be detected even when the answer is unchanged.

title: TimeOmni-o1: Bidirectionally Coupling Time Series Foundation Models and LLMs for Multimodal Reasoning and Forecasting
authors: Ziyang Zhang, Shenyi Li, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang
abstract: Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. Moreover, understanding outputs text while forecasting outputs a time series, so serving both requires a model that reads and generates both modalities. Large language models (LLMs) read time series as digit tokens and handle long series poorly. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast well from large-scale pretraining but typically neither read nor generate text. Time series language models add a time series modality to the LLM but forecast on the LLM side, leaving the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability unused. We present TimeOmni-o1, which couples a pretrained TSFM and an LLM bidirectionally. In one direction, the TSFM encodes the series in compressed form for the LLM, which reasons over it together with the text. In the other, the LLM's reasoning is fed back into the TSFM, which produces the forecast conditioned on it. One model architecture thus reads and generates both series and text, reasons in text, and draws on the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability. To train it, we build MMTR, a multimodal time series reasoning dataset with annotated reasoning traces, covering both tasks across 12 domains with 500k+ samples. On MMTR, TimeOmni-o1 outperforms existing models on both understanding and forecasting across most domains, as well as the LLM and the TSFM inside it when used individually. The gains carry over to three open benchmarks, where it outperforms the dedicated time series models.

title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models
authors: José Roberto Homeli da Silva, Felipe Jorge do Nascimento, Lucas Coutinho Freitas, William Alberto Cruz Castañeda, Marcellus Amadeus
abstract: This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. We introduced Brasilidade, an assessment methodology comprised of standardized tasks distributed across four different domains, and we are making available the tasks from its first domain, which address nuances of the language, grammar, and variations of Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Different task levels revealed significant nuances: while some tasks proved easy for most models, others posed extreme challenges, and some yielded mixed results, with wide variations in performance. This clearly illustrates the need for benchmarks that address the limitations of the models in Brazilian Portuguese, allowing future training cycles to seek to overcome them. Project repository https://github.com/soberania-oficial/brasilidade

title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
authors: Daniel P. Jeong, Yewon Byun, John Giorgi, Peng Xu, Zachary C. Lipton, Michael Oberst
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In practice, not all edits represent actionable feedback: for instance, on data drawn from real-world deployment of an AI clinical documentation product, our review suggests that over 45% of edited outputs contain user-added information that is not directly supported by the inputs to the model. Naively fine-tuning on such edits risks teaching the model to hallucinate. In this paper, we develop a method to address this challenge. Given that real clinician edits on deployed documentation tools are not publicly available, we first develop a taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors, informed by data from a deployed AI clinical documentation product. Then, we develop a method for generating semi-synthetic clinician-edit data, informed by our taxonomy, on a discharge-summary generation task based on MIMIC-III, a public dataset. Finally, we introduce simple filtering methods for identifying actionable edits, with accuracy evaluated by expert review. We show empirically, on our semi-synthetic dataset, that naive fine-tuning on raw edited output increases ungrounded content, while our approach of progressively filtering toward grounded edits enables improvement on clinician-alignment metrics while retaining faithfulness to the input context.

title: 51 Additions per Recursive Step for Rank-23 $3\times3$ Matrix Multiplication, Machine-Checked over Arbitrary Rings
authors: Greg Sidebottom
abstract: We present a rank-23 bilinear scheme for $3\times3$ matrix multiplication that uses 51 additions per recursive step in the alternative-basis (Karstadt-Schwartz) cost model, one below Nielsen's 52 (arXiv:2609.06588). The count 51 itself was first posted, on a different scheme, by Stapleton and Perminov (arXiv:2609.32388), found by heuristic sparse-basis search; the present work is independent and complementary: exactness and breadth rather than a single construction. The scheme is valid over every ring, so it recurses on block matrices, and its correctness is machine-checked in Lean 4/Mathlib. The count is exactly optimal for the scheme's equivalence class: we introduce an exact free-basis minimization procedure whose negative answers are exhaustion proofs, and use it to show that 51 is the minimum for this class, that 52 is exactly optimal both for Nielsen's class and for the class of the current flat-model record, and to sweep the complete Heule-Kauers-Seidl database of rank-23 classes. The sweep is complete: exactly four classes attain 51, all in a single HKS invariant family. We machine-check Stapleton and Perminov's scheme as well, and prove in Lean that their 51 is optimal for its class. Separately, we document a systematic gap between $\mathbb{F}_2$ and signed optima: the $\mathbb{F}_2$-optimal chains of a class typically admit no sign assignment under most of the class's integer sign models, and certificate lifting fails where a direct signed search succeeds.
comment: 14 pages. Artifacts (certificates, exact searcher, Lean 4 proofs): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23305910; source: https://github.com/gsidebottom/logic

title: Uncovering the Blind Spots of OKS-mAP: A Unified Protocol for Occlusion, Joint-Angle, and Temporal Evaluation of 2D Pose Estimators
authors: Yifan Fan
abstract: The dominant metric for 2D human pose estimation, OKS-mAP, has three blind spots: it does not distinguish visible from occluded keypoints, does not measure joint-angle error, and is silent on the temporal stability of tracking-free per-frame inference. We propose a supplementary protocol with three modules: (M1) OKS-mAP stratified by ground-truth visibility, with Delta_occ = mAP(v=1) - mAP(full), quantifying how much the aggregate metric masks occlusion-specific differences; (M2) joint-angle error (RMSE/MAE/P95) plus knee-valgus detection consistency; (M3) frame-to-frame displacement, median-filter residual jitter, and jump rate, before and after OneEuro smoothing. We ran it on four datasets (COCO val2017, CrowdPose, OCHuman, PoseTrack18) and four models from two architecture families (YOLO11s-pose, an occlusion-domain fine-tuned variant, ViTPose-B/L), under a common detector-free oracle protocol and an open-source harness. Delta_occ is negative in every combination (-0.19 to -0.47): aggregate mAP overestimates occluded-scene performance in every tested combination. Joint-angle error is amplified in occluded layers; angle metrics reveal differences mAP cannot localize, e.g., the smaller occlusion-trained model significantly outperforming a larger transformer in occluded elbows. On PoseTrack18 val, raw jitter matched between the two YOLO models; pixel-domain OneEuro smoothing cut jump rates 9-10% at no matched-scope AP cost; residual jitter persists after detector removal; the transformer pair's jump rate is significantly lower; smoothing benefits replicate across architectures. Stratified mAP tracks full mAP closely (sign-consistency 1.0, 12/12), serving magnitude diagnosis rather than re-ranking; angle-metric difference vectors (especially knee) partially diverge, suggesting independent information. The protocol and harness are open-sourced, complementing rather than replacing OKS-mAP.

title: Möbius Interaction Filtering: Order-Selective Spectral Regularization for Multimodal Humor Detection
authors: Jiahao Qin, Yiwen Wang
abstract: Multimodal humor detection requires interpreting language, vocal delivery, and visual behavior jointly. Expressive fusion must also regulate how interactions of different orders enter the final judgment. We propose Möbius Interaction Filtering (MoIF), which learns a modality-subset prediction function and imposes order-selective spectral regularization through its aggregation structure. Private temporal encoders and balanced reciprocal interaction construct supervised unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal predictors. Their uniform aggregate is exactly a Möbius-domain filter with a geometrically decreasing interaction-order response. This formulation retains higher-order representations while regulating their contribution to prediction. Controlled UR-FUNNY perturbations reveal a pronounced decline in label-aligned signal-to-noise ratio across interaction orders. The induced filter improves the final ratio by 1.62-2.79 times relative to the co-trained trimodal predictor while preserving its own clean class-aligned signal under perturbation. Five-seed experiments achieve 70.6% accuracy and weighted F1 on UR-FUNNY, exceeding thirteen reproduced methods on these detection metrics. CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI evaluations establish applicability to sentiment prediction, and cross-seed analyses show more stable estimates on all three datasets. MoIF connects the organization of multimodal interactions to their statistical reliability through an executable spectral constraint. Code is available at https://github.com/D-ST-Sword/MoIF.

title: Large-area Spatially Aligned Anchors
authors: Joni Vanherck, Brent Zoomers, Lode Jorissen, Isjtar Vandebroeck, Eric Joris, Nick Michiels
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) technologies, including Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR), offer immersive experiences merging digital content with the real world. Achieving precise spatial tracking over large areas is a critical challenge in XR development. This paper addresses the drift issue, caused by small errors accumulating over time leading to a discrepancy between the real and virtual worlds. Tackling this issue is crucial for co-located XR experiences where virtual and physical elements interact seamlessly. Building upon the locally accurate spatial anchors, we propose a solution that extends this accuracy to larger areas by exploiting an external, drift-corrected tracking method as a ground truth. During the preparation stage, anchors are placed inside the headset and inside the external tracking method simultaneously, yielding 3D-3D correspondences. Both anchor clouds, and thus tracking methods, are aligned using a suitable cloud registration method during the operational stage. Our method enhances user comfort and mobility by leveraging the headset's built-in tracking capabilities during the operational stage, allowing standalone functionality. Additionally, this method can be used with any XR headset that supports spatial anchors and with any drift-free external tracking method. Empirical evaluation demonstrates the system's effectiveness in aligning virtual content with the real world and expanding the accurate tracking area. In addition, the alignment is evaluated by comparing the camera poses of both tracking methods. This approach may benefit a wide range of industries and applications, including manufacturing and construction, education, and entertainment.

title: One Rater to Score Them All: Frozen Large Language Model Anchoring for Video Quality of Experience
authors: Parsa Hassani Shariat Panahi, Amir H. Jalilvand, M. Hassan Najafi
abstract: Quality of Experience results for video streaming cannot be compared across studies, because public databases share neither test material nor subjects. This work introduces a common reference rater: an open-weights large language models with a fixed rubric and greedy decoding that scores the delivery events of every session and supplies the shared items that score equating requires. The rater is used without training, and it reads only the playback event log of startup delay, stalls and quality switches, which most delivery databases retain even when they share nothing else. A monotonic curve then maps each study's native scale onto the common scale. On 3{,}552 sessions from four studies covering four rating scales, the rater attains a Spearman correlation of 0.809 on VL04 of the ITU-T P.1203 collection, exceeding P.1203 mode~0 on the same sessions, with a Krippendorff alpha of 0.974 over repeated scoring and 0.951 across three serving providers. Sessions from three further laboratories give correlations from 0.756 to 0.787. After calibration, the four studies are placed on a single 0 to 100 scale with a held-out error between 7.8 and 13.3 points, and a mean VMAF of 60 corresponds to positions 17 points apart in two of the studies.
zh_title: 一个评估器评分所有：用于视频体验质量的冻结大型语言模型锚定
translation: 视频流媒体的体验质量（QoE）结果无法在不同研究之间进行比较，因为公共数据库既不共享测试材料也不共享受试者。这项工作引入了一个通用的参考评估器：一个具有固定规则和贪婪解码的开源大型语言模型，它对每次会话的交付事件进行评分，并提供评分均衡所需的共享项目。该评估器无需训练即可使用，它只读取启动延迟、卡顿和质量切换等播放事件日志，这些日志是大多数交付数据库即使不共享其他内容也会保留的。然后，通过单调曲线将每个研究的原始量表映射到通用量表上。在来自四个研究（涵盖四种评分量表）的3,552个会话中，该评估器在ITU-T P.1203集合的VL04上达到了0.809的Spearman相关性，超过了P.1203模式0。重复评分的Krippendorff alpha为0.974，跨三个服务提供商的Krippendorff alpha为0.951。来自另外三个实验室的会话相关性在0.756到0.787之间。校准后，四个研究被置于一个0到100的单一量表上，保留误差在7.8到13.3点之间，平均VMAF为60在其中两个研究中对应相差17点的位置。
tldr: 本文提出一个冻结的大型语言模型作为通用的视频体验质量（QoE）参考评估器，用于标准化不同研究间的QoE评分，使其能够进行比较。
ai_comments: 这项工作的创新之处在于首次提出使用“冻结”的大型语言模型作为视频QoE的通用锚定评估器。其重要性在于提供了一种标准化不同QoE研究结果的有效途径，解决了现有研究数据无法直接比较的长期问题。通过仅依赖常见的播放事件日志，该方法具有高度的普适性和实用性。
motivation: 视频流媒体的体验质量（QoE）结果无法在不同研究之间进行比较，因为公共数据库既不共享测试材料也不共享受试者。
method: 本研究引入了一个通用的参考评估器：一个具有固定规则和贪婪解码的开源大型语言模型，它对每次会话的交付事件进行评分。该评估器无需训练，只读取启动延迟、卡顿和质量切换等播放事件日志。然后，通过单调曲线将每个研究的原始量表映射到通用量表上。
results: 在来自四个研究的3,552个会话中，该评估器在ITU-T P.1203集合的VL04上达到了0.809的Spearman相关性，超过了P.1203模式0。重复评分的Krippendorff alpha为0.974，跨三个服务提供商的Krippendorff alpha为0.951。来自另外三个实验室的会话相关性在0.756到0.787之间。校准后，四个研究被置于一个0到100的单一量表上，保留误差在7.8到13.3点之间，平均VMAF为60在其中两个研究中对应相差17点的位置。
conclusion: 通过引入一个冻结的大型语言模型作为通用参考评估器，本文成功地解决了视频QoE研究结果无法跨研究比较的问题，并提供了一种将不同研究的QoE评分标准化到通用量表的方法。

title: Two-Sided Amortized Resource Analysis: Verifying Resource Lower Bounds via Ill-Typing
authors: Zimu Chen, Di Wang
abstract:
We present a two-sided type system with potential for verifying resource lower bounds of functional programs. Automatic amortized resource analysis (AARA) verifies upper bounds: types carry potential, and typing certifies sufficient resources. A lower bound, however, is a necessity statement---the program evaluates only if enough resources are available---and prior type-based approaches obtain it by switching the substructural discipline of potential, so that upper and lower bounds live in separate type systems. Matching upper and lower bounds characterize a program's cost exactly.
  Our system combines AARA-style potential with the two-sided type systems of Ramsay and Walpole, whose central guarantee is that ill-typed programs do not evaluate. Typing formulas may constrain arbitrary terms and appear on both sides of the turnstile; the judgment $t : A \vdash q$ states that if $t$ evaluates to a result of type $A$, then at least $q$ units of resource must be available---that is, $q$ is a lower bound. Because potential makes typing formulas non-replicable, our system follows an affine discipline instead of the replicable contexts of the original framework. We interpret types by semantic typing over value states, pairs of values and remaining resources, and we prove soundness on a safety fragment; corollaries recover the classical two-sided guarantees and the soundness of both kinds of bounds in a single proof system. A prototype type checker in OCaml verifies, on a suite of 19 benchmarks, matching pairs of bounds that characterize costs exactly, as well as lower bounds for programs whose upper bounds are unavailable. In a parallel exploration, we study a two-sided linear type system in which every value is a non-replicable resource; there, closures that capture linear resources call for dual typing formulas, and the exact accounting explains the affine design of the main system.

title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction
authors: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Daren Zha
abstract: Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. We show that this protocol can create a candidate-support confound: when the target is outside training support while all distractors are sampled from that support, support membership identifies the gold action without modeling behavior. We formalize this effect with support-identifiability rate (SIR), construct support-balanced candidate sets, and evaluate a target-free dual-path proposer that combines support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals. On filtered OPeRA (4,282/469/992 train/dev/test steps), the original protocol has SIR 1.0000 on target-OOV rows and a support-only rule reaches 1.0000 OOV Exact@1. Support balancing reduces SIR to 0.0000; the strongest conditional reranker obtains 0.7214 overall Exact@1, 0.7988 on IV rows, and 0.5668 on OOV rows. The target-free dual-path system reaches Proposal Recall@16 0.6915 and end-to-end Exact@1 0.5212, compared with oracle conditional Exact@1 0.7450. On Mind2Web, the same audit yields SIR 0.2380 and an oracle-to-proposal gap of 0.2125. A 200-row semantic audit labels 0.7150 of exact-key OOV targets as semantically novel, 0.2450 as locator/string variation, and 0.0400 as ambiguous (Cohen's $κ=0.8173$). These measurements show why support composition must be controlled alongside candidate accuracy when offline results are used to reason about deployment.
zh_title: 意图孪生：解决离线网页行为预测中候选支持混淆和预言机到部署差距
translation: 离线网页行为基准测试通常将演示动作插入有限的候选集中，然后测量重新排序效果。我们发现这种协议会产生候选支持混淆：当目标超出训练支持范围，而所有干扰项都从该支持中采样时，支持成员身份可以在不建模行为的情况下识别出正确动作。我们通过支持可识别率（SIR）来形式化这种效应，构建了支持平衡的候选集，并评估了一个无目标的双路径提议器，该提议器结合了支持检索和开放词汇DOM/LM提议。在过滤后的OPeRA数据集（4,282/469/992训练/开发/测试步骤）上，原始协议在目标-OOV（超出词汇表）行上的SIR为1.0000，并且仅基于支持的规则达到了1.0000 OOV Exact@1。支持平衡将SIR降低到0.0000；最强的条件重排序器在整体上获得了0.7214的Exact@1，在IV（词汇内）行上获得0.7988，在OOV行上获得0.5668。无目标双路径系统达到了Proposal Recall@16 0.6915和端到端Exact@1 0.5212，而预言机条件Exact@1为0.7450。在Mind2Web数据集上，相同的审计产生了0.2380的SIR和0.2125的预言机到提议差距。一项200行的语义审计将0.7150的精确键OOV目标标记为语义新颖，0.2450标记为定位器/字符串变体，0.0400标记为模糊（Cohen's κ=0.8173）。这些测量结果表明，当使用离线结果来推断部署情况时，必须同时控制支持构成和候选准确性。
tldr: 该论文揭示了离线网页行为预测基准测试中存在的候选支持混淆问题，并提出了支持可识别率（SIR）指标、支持平衡候选集以及无目标双路径提议系统来解决此问题，强调了在评估离线结果时控制支持构成的重要性。
ai_comments: 该论文深入分析了离线网页行为预测基准测试中一个被忽视但关键的问题——候选支持混淆，这对于确保评估的公正性和模型在实际部署中的有效性至关重要。通过引入SIR这一量化指标和提出支持平衡的候选集，论文为解决这一根本性评估缺陷提供了明确的工具和方法。此外，无目标双路径提议系统的设计思路也具有创新性，它尝试从根本上解决开放词汇场景下的挑战。这项工作对于推动网页行为预测领域的研究和实际应用具有重要意义，因为它提醒研究者和开发者必须警惕离线评估与真实世界性能之间的潜在偏差。
motivation: 离线网页行为基准测试中，将示范动作插入有限候选集并测量重排序的协议，会产生候选支持混淆。当目标不在训练支持范围内，而所有干扰项都从该支持中采样时，支持成员身份可以在不建模行为的情况下识别正确动作。
method: 通过支持可识别率（SIR）来形式化这种效应，构建支持平衡的候选集，并评估一个无目标的双路径提议系统，该系统结合了支持检索和开放词汇DOM/LM提议。
results: 在过滤后的OPeRA数据集上，原始协议在目标-OOV行上的SIR为1.0000，支持专用规则达到了1.0000 OOV Exact@1。支持平衡将SIR降至0.0000；最强的条件重排序器在整体上获得0.7214 Exact@1，在IV行上获得0.7988，在OOV行上获得0.5668。无目标双路径系统达到了Proposal Recall@16 0.6915和端到端Exact@1 0.5212，而预言机条件Exact@1为0.7450。在Mind2Web数据集上，相同审计的SIR为0.2380，预言机到提议的差距为0.2125。一项200行的语义审计将0.7150的精确键OOV目标标记为语义新颖，0.2450标记为定位器/字符串变体，0.0400标记为模糊（Cohen's κ=0.8173）。
conclusion: 这些测量结果表明，当使用离线结果来推断部署情况时，必须同时控制支持构成和候选准确性。

title: Using LLM Agents to Evaluate Prosocial Interventions on Social Media Platforms
authors: Lucen Li, Erin Wertz, Muhammad Haroon, Anshuman Chhabra, Magdalena Wojcieszak
abstract: Social media platforms are a primary source of information for many users. Although research explores various interventions to promote prosocial content or demote harmful content on platforms, there are few systematic methods for evaluating competing intervention designs before conducting costly human-subject experiments. We develop a simulation-based evaluation pipeline built on the OASIS framework. We generate 13,835 LLM-based agents, each with a unique profile. Over 20 time steps, we expose them to real-world Twitter/X posts and let them comment, like, repost, or follow. We use those agents to systematically evaluate three interventions that increase exposure to verified news: adding content, upranking content, and celebrity source cues. All interventions significantly increase news engagement, with upranking news to prominent feed positions producing the largest effects. These effects hold across agents' gender, age, and education levels. We validate our injection treatment results against a comparable human-subject study and find strong directional alignment and similar dose-normalized efficiency. Our results suggest that LLM-based agent simulations can support early-stage evaluation of platform interventions before human-subject deployment, and upranking may be more effective than news volume or source.
zh_title: 使用LLM代理评估社交媒体平台上的亲社会干预措施
translation: 社交媒体平台是许多用户获取信息的主要来源。尽管研究探索了各种干预措施来促进平台上的亲社会内容或抑制有害内容，但在进行昂贵的人体实验之前，缺乏系统性的方法来评估相互竞争的干预设计。我们开发了一个基于OASIS框架的模拟评估管道。我们生成了13,835个基于LLM的代理，每个代理都有一个独特的配置文件。在20个时间步长内，我们让他们接触真实的Twitter/X帖子，并允许他们评论、点赞、转发或关注。我们使用这些代理系统地评估了三种增加认证新闻曝光的干预措施：添加内容、提升内容排名和名人来源提示。所有干预措施都显著增加了新闻参与度，其中将新闻提升到显著信息流位置的干预效果最大。这些效果在代理的性别、年龄和教育水平上均成立。我们针对一项可比较的人体研究验证了我们的注入治疗结果，并发现了强烈的方向一致性和相似的剂量标准化效率。我们的结果表明，基于LLM的代理模拟可以支持在人体部署之前对平台干预措施进行早期评估，并且提升排名可能比新闻量或来源更有效。
tldr: 本文开发了一个基于LLM代理的模拟评估管道，用于在昂贵的人体实验之前评估社交媒体上的亲社会干预措施。研究发现，提高新闻内容排名比增加新闻量或来源更能有效提高新闻参与度，并且LLM代理模拟可以支持早期干预评估。
ai_comments: 这项研究的创新之处在于利用LLM代理构建了一个大规模的社交媒体模拟环境，为在进行昂贵的人体实验之前评估平台干预措施提供了一种经济高效且系统化的方法。其重要性在于为社交媒体平台改进内容推荐和干预策略提供了实用的见解，特别是发现提升内容排名比增加内容量或提示来源更有效。通过与人体研究的验证，增加了模拟结果的可信度。未来的工作可以探索更多复杂的代理行为模型和更广泛的干预类型。
motivation: 现有研究探索了各种促进亲社会内容或抑制有害内容的干预措施，但在进行昂贵的人体实验之前，缺乏系统性的方法来评估相互竞争的干预设计。
method: 本文基于OASIS框架开发了一个模拟评估管道，生成了13,835个具有独特配置文件的LLM代理。这些代理在20个时间步长内接触真实的Twitter/X帖子，并进行评论、点赞、转发或关注。研究使用这些代理系统地评估了三种增加认证新闻曝光的干预措施：添加内容、提升内容排名和名人来源提示。研究还将注入治疗结果与可比较的人体研究进行了验证。
results: 所有干预措施都显著增加了新闻参与度，其中将新闻提升到显著信息流位置的干预效果最大。这些效果在不同性别、年龄和教育水平的代理中均成立。与人体研究的验证结果显示出强烈的方向一致性和相似的剂量标准化效率。
conclusion: LLM代理模拟可以支持在人体部署之前对平台干预措施进行早期评估。提升新闻排名可能比增加新闻量或来源更有效。

title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
authors: Gunik Luthra, Ronald J. Pandolfi, Benjamin T. Diroll, Ricky Ronquillo, Ruipeng Li, Christopher B. Murray, Marcus M. Noack, Kevin G. Yager, Esther H. R. Tsai
abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored.
